load_notes.document_id: _id matches the id field and is the Elasticsearch document id.
load_notes.vectors: plot_256, plot_512 and plot_1024 are not included: the import always generates them from plot with the Elasticsearch inference service.
load_notes.nested: belongs_to_collection and keywords are nested objects.
load_notes.enrichment: Optional object of keyword provenance tags, one per sourced field, or null when the movie has none. In CSV it is compact JSON in the enrichment column; an empty cell is null.
load_notes.csv: Arrays and nested objects are JSON-encoded inside each cell. The file is UTF-8 with BOM.
load_notes.part: Part 2 of 7, sorted by id. Each part is a complete catalog on its own: load it in bulk to replace the catalog or in append to add to it.

documents.title: The Messengers
documents.tagline: There is evidence to suggest that children are highly susceptible to paranormal phenomena. They see what adults cannot. They believe what adults deny. And they are trying to warn us.
documents.overview: When the Solomons trade in the craziness of big-city life for the quiet of a North Dakota farm, little do they expect the nightmare that follows. Soon after arriving, teenage Jess (Kristen Stewart) and her younger brother see terrifying apparitions and endure attacks from a supernatural source. Jess must warn her disbelieving family before it is too late to save them.
documents.plot:
The Messengers is a supernatural horror film that revolves around a young woman named Jess, who moves into a new home with her brother and his family. As they settle in, strange and terrifying events begin to occur, which are attributed to the presence of malevolent spirits.

At its core, The Messengers explores the theme of grief and loss as it relates to the supernatural. Jess's family is still reeling from the death of their mother, and her brother's new wife seems to be hiding secrets about her past. As the strange occurrences escalate, it becomes clear that these events are connected to a traumatic event in the family's history.

The film also delves into the idea of isolation and how it can exacerbate feelings of loneliness and vulnerability. Jess's move to a new home serves as a catalyst for the supernatural events, highlighting her own sense of disconnection from her brother and his family. As she tries to navigate this new environment, she becomes increasingly isolated, which makes her more susceptible to the malevolent forces at work.

Furthermore, The Messengers touches on the theme of guilt and redemption. Jess's brother is wracked with guilt over his mother's death, and he seems to be trying to make amends through his relationship with his wife. However, as the events unfold, it becomes clear that this attempt at redemption may not be enough to lift the weight of their collective grief.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a sense of tension and unease, which culminates in a terrifying climax. The Messengers is ultimately a story about how the past can come back to haunt us, and how the supernatural can serve as a manifestation of our deepest fears and anxieties.

documents.title: Deck the Halls
documents.tagline: There glows the neighborhood.
documents.overview: Determined to unseat Steve Finch's reign as the town's holiday season king, Buddy Hall plasters his house with so many decorative lights that it'll be visible from space! When their wives bond, and their kids follow suit, the two men only escalate their rivalry - and their decorating.
documents.plot:
Deck the Halls is a Christmas comedy film released in 2006, directed by John Whitesell and produced by New Regency Pictures.

The movie follows the story of two neighbors, Steve Finch (Danny DeVito) and Dan Burns (Matthew Broderick), who engage in an escalating series of holiday decorations and competitions. The rivalry between the two men begins when they both decide to outdo each other with their Christmas decorations, with Steve's house becoming a symbol of festive cheer and Dan's house a stark contrast.

As the competition intensifies, the neighbors become increasingly obsessed with one-upping each other, with Steve and his wife Audrey (Kirsten Dunst) going all out to create a dazzling display of lights, ornaments, and decorations. Meanwhile, Dan and his wife Maureen (Kristin Chenoweth) try to keep up with Steve's antics, but their own holiday spirit is slowly being drained away.

As the holiday season progresses, the rivalry between Steve and Dan becomes more and more absurd, with the two men engaging in a series of ridiculous and over-the-top competitions. The neighbors' obsession with Christmas decorations starts to affect not only their relationship but also their families and friends.

In the end, Steve's house is destroyed by a freak accident involving a malfunctioning animatronic Santa Claus, leaving Dan's house as the winner of the holiday decoration competition. However, in a surprising twist, Steve realizes that he has lost sight of what Christmas is really about - spending time with loved ones and enjoying the holiday spirit.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Steve and Dan putting aside their rivalry and coming together to celebrate the true meaning of Christmas. The film features a mix of humor, wit, and heart, making it a fun and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Deck the Halls is a lighthearted and comedic take on the holiday season, with plenty of laughs and festive cheer. While it may not be a deeply meaningful or profound exploration of Christmas, it's a fun and enjoyable film that's sure to get you in the holiday spirit.

documents.title: Air Buddies
documents.tagline: They Shoot. They Score. They TALK!
documents.overview: Five puppies are shocked to find out that their parents, Buddy and Molly, have been abducted and face obstacles while trying to rescue them.
documents.plot:
Air Buddies is a heartwarming film that revolves around the adventures of a group of adorable and lovable golden retriever puppies. The movie explores several themes, primarily centered around family, friendship, and loyalty.

At its core, Air Buddies is a story about the unbreakable bond between humans and animals. The film showcases the special connection between the main characters, particularly the puppies, and their human caregivers. As the puppies navigate various challenges and obstacles, they demonstrate remarkable resilience, empathy, and affection towards those around them.

One of the primary themes of Air Buddies is the importance of family. The movie highlights the value of having a loving and supportive family unit, where everyone works together to overcome difficulties. The film also emphasizes the significance of adopting pets from shelters, as it promotes responsible pet ownership and the joy that comes with sharing one's life with a furry companion.

Another significant theme in Air Buddies is the concept of loyalty and friendship. The puppies form strong bonds with each other, and their relationships are built on trust, empathy, and mutual support. As they face various challenges, they demonstrate remarkable loyalty to one another, showcasing the power of canine camaraderie.

The film also touches upon themes of responsibility, hard work, and perseverance. The main characters learn valuable lessons about taking care of others, working together as a team, and overcoming obstacles through determination and effort.

Overall, Air Buddies is a delightful film that celebrates the beauty of human-animal relationships, the importance of family, and the power of loyalty and friendship.

documents.title: Curious George
documents.tagline: Show me the Monkey!
documents.overview: When The Man in the Yellow Hat befriends Curious George in the jungle, they set off on a non-stop, fun-filled journey through the wonders of the big city toward the warmth of true friendship.
documents.plot:
Curious George is a 2006 computer-animated adventure comedy film based on the children's book series by H.A. and Margret Rey.

The main theme of Curious George revolves around curiosity, exploration, and learning from one's mistakes. The story follows the adventures of Curious George, a mischievous monkey who gets into various predicaments while exploring the city with his friend, the Man in the Yellow Hat.

As the film progresses, George learns valuable lessons about responsibility, empathy, and understanding the consequences of his actions. He also develops a strong bond with the Man in the Yellow Hat, who teaches him important life skills and encourages him to think critically.

Throughout the movie, Curious George faces various challenges, including navigating obstacles, overcoming fears, and learning to work together with others. These experiences help shape George's character and teach him essential values such as friendship, kindness, and self-control.

The film also explores themes of creativity, imagination, and problem-solving, highlighting the importance of thinking outside the box and finding innovative solutions to complex problems.

Overall, Curious George (2006) is a heartwarming story that promotes positive values and encourages children to think creatively, explore their surroundings, and learn from their mistakes.

documents.title: Stormbreaker
documents.tagline: Rule the school. Save the world.
documents.overview: Alex Rider thinks he is a normal school boy, until his uncle is killed. He discovers that his uncle was actually spy on a mission, when he was killed. Alex is recruited by Alan Blunt to continue the mission. He is sent to Cornwall to investigate a new computer system, which Darrius Sayle has created. He plans to give the new computer systems to every school in the country, but Mr. Blunt has other ideas and Alex must find out what it is.
documents.plot:
Stormbreaker, also known as Alex Rider: Operation Stormbreaker, is a 2006 action spy film directed by Geoffrey Sax from a screenplay by Anthony Horowitz, based on his 2000 novel, the first book in the Alex Rider series. Alex Pettyfer stars as the teenage Alex, with Ewan McGregor as his uncle Ian, Mickey Rourke as the billionaire Darrius Sayle, Bill Nighy as MI6 chief Alan Blunt, Sophie Okonedo as Mrs. Jones, Alicia Silverstone as Jack Starbright, Andy Serkis as Mr. Grin, Damian Lewis as the assassin Yassen Gregorovich, Stephen Fry as Smithers and Robbie Coltrane as the Prime Minister. It was an international co-production between the United Kingdom, the United States and Germany.

Fourteen-year-old orphan Alex Rider lives in London with his uncle Ian, supposedly a bank manager who is often away, and their American housekeeper, Jack. When Ian is reported killed in a car crash, Alex quickly discovers that his uncle was in fact an MI6 spy who was murdered on a mission, and that Ian had been quietly training him for the same work all his life. Alan Blunt and Mrs. Jones of MI6's Special Operations Division recruit Alex, and when he refuses they threaten to have Jack deported. After a tough crash course at a Special Air Service training camp in the Brecon Beacons, where the soldiers come to respect him despite his age, Alex is equipped with gadgets by the armorer Smithers and sent undercover in Cornwall. His target is Darrius Sayle, a billionaire who is donating his advanced Stormbreaker computer system to every school in the country. Posing as a competition winner, Alex meets Sayle and his sinister assistants, Mr. Grin and Nadia Vole, while Vole investigates his true identity and gets into a fight with Jack back in London. Alex discovers that Sayle's generosity hides a monstrous plan involving the computers and the nation's schoolchildren, and he must use his wits, his training and Smithers's gadgets to stop the launch before Sayle can strike.

Intended as the first entry in a franchise, Stormbreaker received mixed reviews from critics, who found it lacking in originality and believability; it holds a 35% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a consensus calling it strictly children's fare. It grossed between $20.7 and $23.9 million against a $40 million budget, and The Weinstein Company eventually cancelled plans for a sequel.

documents.title: Kicking & Screaming
documents.tagline: One man could lead this team to glory... That man was busy.
documents.overview: Phil Weston has been unathletic his entire life. In college he failed at every sport that he tried out for. It looks like his 10-year old son, Sam, is following in his footsteps. But when Phil's hyper-competitive dad benches Sam, Phil decides to transfer his son to a new team which needs a coach. Phil steps in to be the temporary coach and immediately begins to butt heads with this dad over this new competition in their lives.
documents.plot:
Kicking & Screaming is a 2005 American sports comedy film directed by Jesse Dylan. The movie revolves around Phil Weston (played by Robert Duvall), a former soccer star who tries to coach his son's under-12 soccer team, the Kicking Kings, despite having no experience.

The main theme of Kicking & Screaming is the importance of perseverance and learning from failure. Phil's journey as he navigates the world of youth soccer coaching serves as a metaphor for life's challenges. As he faces setbacks and disappointments, he must find ways to overcome them and grow both as a person and as a coach.

The film also explores the theme of redemption and second chances. Phil sees his son's under-12 team as an opportunity to redeem himself and make up for past mistakes. Through his experiences with the Kicking Kings, he learns valuable lessons about teamwork, discipline, and the value of hard work.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of generational differences and the challenges that come with bridging the gap between parents and children. Phil's struggles to connect with his son and the other coaches serve as a reminder that effective communication and empathy are essential in building strong relationships.

Overall, Kicking & Screaming is a heartwarming film that celebrates the power of sports to bring people together and teach valuable life lessons.

documents.title: Chicken Little
documents.tagline: When it comes to saving the world, it helps to be a little chicken.
documents.overview: When the sky really is falling and sanity has flown the coop, who will rise to save the day? Together with his hysterical band of misfit friends, Chicken Little must hatch a plan to save the planet from alien invasion and prove that the world's biggest hero is a little chicken.
documents.plot:
Chicken Little is a 2005 animated comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of a chicken named Chicken Little, who lives on a farm with his friends and family.

The film begins with Chicken Little, played by Zach Braff, being a carefree and naive chicken who loves to explore the outdoors. One day, while out foraging for food, Chicken Little sees an acorn fall from the sky and believes it is a sign that the world is ending. He rushes back to the farm to warn his friends, including Duckworth (Don Knotts), a wise old duck, and Abby Mallard (voiced by Joan Cusack), a kind-hearted chicken.

Chicken Little's warning causes panic among the animals on the farm, leading to chaos and destruction. The other animals believe that the world is indeed ending, and they start to prepare for their final days together. Meanwhile, Chicken Little becomes convinced that he has seen the end of the world and sets out on a journey to find the "Great Prince" who can save them.

Along the way, Chicken Little meets a group of birds who are also searching for the Great Prince. There's Buck Cluck (Steve Martin), a wise-cracking rooster who becomes Chicken Little's friend and ally; Runt (Matthew Broderick), a fast-talking pigeon who is initially skeptical of Chicken Little's claims but eventually joins him on his quest.

As they journey through the forest, the group faces various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous terrain, fierce predators, and their own personal doubts and fears. Through it all, Chicken Little learns valuable lessons about courage, friendship, and believing in oneself.

In the end, Chicken Little and his friends discover that the "Great Prince" is actually a wise old owl named Professor Henny Penny (Patrick Warburton), who has been watching over them from afar. The professor explains that the acorn was just a normal part of nature and that there is no need to panic.

Chicken Little returns home, where he is welcomed back as a hero by his friends and family. He learns to appreciate the simple things in life and becomes more confident and self-assured. The movie ends with Chicken Little and his friends enjoying a sunny day together on the farm, free from fear and anxiety.

Overall, Chicken Little is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, courage, and believing in oneself. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and lovable characters, it's a great choice for families and audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Charlotte's Web
documents.tagline: Something unexpected, unbelievable, unforgettable.
documents.overview: Wilbur the pig is scared of the end of the season, because he knows that come that time, he will end up on the dinner table. He hatches a plan with Charlotte, a spider that lives in his pen, to ensure that this will never happen.
documents.plot:
Charlotte's Web is a 2006 American live-action animated fantasy comedy-drama film based on E. B. White's 1952 novel, directed by Gary Winick and written by Susannah Grant and Karey Kirkpatrick. The second film adaptation of the book, after Hanna-Barbera's 1973 animated feature, it stars Dakota Fanning as Fern Arable, with Kevin Anderson and Essie Davis as her parents and Beau Bridges as Dr. Dorian. The voice cast features Dominic Scott Kay as Wilbur, Julia Roberts as Charlotte, Steve Buscemi as Templeton the rat, John Cleese as Samuel the sheep, Oprah Winfrey and Cedric the Entertainer as the geese Gussy and Golly, Kathy Bates and Reba McEntire as the cows Bitsy and Betsy, Robert Redford as Ike the horse, and Sam Shepard as the narrator. Danny Elfman composed the score, and the film was produced by Walden Media, The K Entertainment Company and Nickelodeon Movies.

One spring on a farm in Somerset County, Maine, eight-year-old Fern Arable persuades her father not to kill the runt of a new litter of pigs. She names the piglet Wilbur and raises him lovingly, even smuggling him into school, but once he has grown, she must move him to the barn of her uncle Homer Zuckerman. Lonely and longing for friends, Wilbur is rebuffed by the other barn animals, including the scheming rat Templeton, the stern sheep Samuel, a pair of geese, two cows and a timid horse, until he is befriended by Charlotte, a barn spider living above his pen. When the animals reveal that Wilbur is destined to be killed for the Christmas dinner table, Charlotte promises to save him. With Templeton's reluctant help, she weaves words into her web describing Wilbur as "Some Pig", "Terrific", "Radiant" and "Humble", convincing the Zuckermans that he is a special pig and attracting crowds after the news spreads through the town. The families take Wilbur to a fair, where he is entered in a contest and Charlotte lays an egg sac containing her unborn children, but the effort leaves her weakened, and Wilbur must find a way to repay his friend and protect her legacy.

The film was released in Australia on December 7, 2006, and in the United States by Paramount Pictures on December 15. It received generally positive reviews, holding a 79% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and grossed $149 million against an $85 million budget.

documents.title: Beerfest
documents.tagline: Prepare for the ultimate chug of war.
documents.overview: During a trip to Germany to scatter their grandfather's ashes, German-American brothers Todd and Jan discover Beerfest, the secret Olympics of downing stout, and want to enter the contest to defend their family's beer-guzzling honor. Their Old Country cousins sneer at the Yanks' chances, prompting the siblings to return to America to prepare for a showdown the following year.
documents.plot:
Beerfest is a comedy film that explores the theme of brotherhood and male bonding through the lens of two German brothers who participate in an annual beer-drinking competition, known as "Prost!". The movie delves into the idea of masculinity, tradition, and cultural heritage, highlighting the importance of family ties and loyalty. 

The film also touches on the concept of nostalgia, as the protagonist, Hans, reminisces about his childhood and the significance of Prost! in their lives. Furthermore, Beerfest critiques societal expectations of masculinity, poking fun at traditional masculine norms and stereotypes.

Through its lighthearted humor and comedic take on cultural traditions, Beerfest offers a commentary on the complexities of male relationships and the power of shared experiences in shaping one's identity.

documents.title: Antitrust
documents.tagline: Truth can be dangerous...Trust can be deadly.
documents.overview: A computer programmer's dream job at a hot Portland-based firm turns nightmarish when he discovers his boss has a secret and ruthless means of dispatching anti-trust problems.
documents.plot:
Antitrust is a 2001 American drama film directed by Mimi Leder and written by David Koepp. The movie stars Dustin Hoffman, Rachel Weisz, and Edward Norton.

The main theme of Antitrust revolves around the corrupting influence of power and greed in corporate America. The story follows Adam White (Edward Norton), a young lawyer who becomes embroiled in a conspiracy involving the merger of two large corporations, Monarch Corporation (led by the ruthless and cunning CEO, James Daley, played by Dustin Hoffman) and General Media Corporation.

As Adam delves deeper into the case, he uncovers a web of deceit and corruption that threatens to destroy the lives of those involved. The film explores themes of corporate greed, power struggles, and the erosion of ethics in business.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to confront their own moral compasses and make difficult choices between personal ambition and doing what is right. The film's portrayal of a corrupt system that prioritizes profits over people serves as a commentary on the darker aspects of capitalism.

The ending of the film is particularly noteworthy, as it highlights the devastating consequences of unchecked corporate power and the importance of holding those in power accountable for their actions. Overall, Antitrust is a thought-provoking drama that critiques the excesses of corporate America and the dangers of unchecked power.

documents.title: Mean Machine
documents.tagline: It's Not Just About Football, It's About Pride Inside!
documents.overview: Disgraced ex-England football captain, Danny 'Mean Machine' Meehan, is thrown in jail for assaulting two police officers. He keeps his head down and has the opportunity to forget everything and change the lives of the prisoners. When these prisoners have the chance to put one over the evil guards during a prison football match, Danny takes the lead.
documents.plot:
Mean Machine is a 2001 British sports drama film directed by Peter Cattaneo. The movie follows the story of a former professional footballer who becomes the manager of a group of prisoners in a maximum-security prison.

The main theme of Mean Machine revolves around redemption and personal growth, as the protagonist, a hardened and bitter ex-footballer, is forced to confront his past mistakes and learn to connect with others. Through his interactions with the prisoners, he begins to understand that there's more to life than just winning and losing on the pitch.

The film also explores themes of masculinity, loyalty, and the struggle for identity. The protagonist's journey is marked by a series of challenges as he navigates the harsh realities of prison life, where traditional notions of masculinity are constantly being tested. As he forms bonds with the prisoners, he begins to see that there's strength in vulnerability and that true leadership comes from empathy and understanding.

Furthermore, Mean Machine touches on issues of social class and economic inequality, highlighting the stark contrast between the lives of those who have been privileged by their wealth and status, and those who are struggling to survive on the margins. The film suggests that even in the most unlikely of places, there is potential for human connection and redemption.

Overall, Mean Machine is a powerful exploration of the complexities of human nature, offering a nuanced portrayal of characters who are often reduced to stereotypes or caricatures.

documents.title: Arthur and the Invisibles
documents.tagline: Adventure awaits in your own backyard.
documents.overview: Arthur is a spirited ten-year old whose parents are away looking for work, whose eccentric grandfather has been missing for several years, and who lives with his grandmother in a country house that, in two days, will be repossessed, torn down, and turned into a block of flats unless Arthur's grandfather returns to sign some papers and pay off the family debt. Arthur discovers that the key to success lies in his own descent into the land of the Minimoys, creatures no larger than a tooth, whom his grandfather helped relocate to their garden. Somewhere among them is hidden a pile of rubies, too. Can Arthur be of stout heart and save the day? Romance beckons as well, and a villain lurks.
documents.plot:
Arthur and the Invisibles, originally released as Arthur and the Minimoys (French: Arthur et les Minimoys), is a 2006 English-language French fantasy adventure film that combines live action and computer animation. It was directed and co-written by Luc Besson and is based on the first two books of his Arthur children's series. Freddie Highmore stars as Arthur Montgomery, with Mia Farrow as his grandmother, while the English voice cast includes Madonna as Princess Selenia, David Bowie as the villain Maltazard, and Snoop Dogg and Robert De Niro. With a budget of 60 million euros, it was the most expensive French film produced up to that time, and it was released in France by EuropaCorp on 29 November 2006.

In 1960, ten-year-old Arthur lives with his grandmother Daisy in a farmhouse in rural Connecticut. His grandfather Archibald, an explorer and inventor, has recently disappeared, and his parents are away looking for work. Daisy tells Arthur stories of his grandfather's adventures in Africa, where he met the tall Bogo Matassalai tribe and the tiny Minimoys, who now live in the farm's garden, guarding a hidden collection of rubies. Arthur becomes fascinated by a drawing of Selenia, the Minimoy princess.

When a property developer gives Daisy just two days to pay a large debt or lose the house, Arthur sets out to find the rubies, following clues left by his grandfather. With the help of the Bogo Matassalai, he is shrunk to the size of a Minimoy and enters their miniature world, an animated realm hidden in the grass. There he learns that the Minimoys are threatened by Maltazard, a fallen war hero who rules the city of Necropolis. Arthur pulls a sacred sword from its stone, proving himself a hero, and sets off with Selenia and her younger brother on a perilous journey to stop Maltazard, find his grandfather and recover the treasure before the deadline.

Besson's film blends Arthurian references, fairy-tale adventure and a nostalgic rural setting, contrasting the live-action world with the colourful animated kingdom of the Minimoys.

The film was successful in France and spawned two sequels, Arthur and the Revenge of Maltazard (2009) and Arthur 3: The War of the Two Worlds (2010). Its shortened American version, Arthur and the Invisibles, received generally negative reviews and grossed about 15 million dollars in the United States.

documents.title: The Great Mouse Detective
documents.tagline: London's crime-fighting ace on his most baffling case!
documents.overview: When the diabolical Professor Ratigan kidnaps London's master toymaker, the brilliant master of disguise Basil of Baker Street and his trusted sidekick Dawson try to elude the ultimate trap and foil the perfect crime.
documents.plot:
The Great Mouse Detective is a 1986 animated mystery film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is set in Victorian-era London and follows the adventures of a mouse detective named Basil of Baker Street.

The story begins with the introduction of Basil, a clever and resourceful mouse who lives in a small flat above his human friend, Dr. John Watson's (a human character). Basil is a huge fan of Sherlock Holmes, a famous human detective from London, and has spent years studying his methods and techniques. When a mysterious letter arrives at Baker Street, addressed to both Basil and Sherlock, the mouse detective decides to take on the case.

The letter is from Lady Regina, a wealthy socialite who claims that her prized possession, a rare and valuable diamond necklace, has been stolen by a group of mice known as the "Beagle Boys." The Beagle Boys are led by the cunning and ruthless leader, Ratigan. Basil sets out to solve the mystery, using his own detective skills and knowledge of human behavior.

As Basil delves deeper into the case, he meets Dr. Watson's nephew, Thomas O'Malley (a charming and laid-back cat), who becomes his partner in the investigation. Together, they follow a trail of clues that lead them from the streets of London to the countryside.

Throughout the movie, Basil uses his intelligence and wit to outsmart Ratigan's henchmen and uncover the truth behind the theft of Lady Regina's necklace. Along the way, he also learns more about himself and his own abilities as a detective.

In the end, Basil and O'Malley discover that Ratigan is behind the theft and has been using the Beagle Boys to carry out his plans. In a thrilling showdown, Basil confronts Ratigan and uses his knowledge of human psychology to outwit him. With the help of O'Malley, Basil is able to recover the stolen necklace and bring Ratigan to justice.

The Great Mouse Detective features a talented voice cast, including Vincent Price as Ratigan, Christopher Lloyd as Dr. Watson, and Barrie Ingham as Inspector Lestrade. The movie's animation is also noteworthy, with intricate details and clever use of visual effects to bring the characters and settings to life.

Overall, The Great Mouse Detective is a charming and entertaining film that pays homage to the classic Sherlock Holmes stories while offering its own unique twist on the detective genre. With its engaging plot, memorable characters, and witty dialogue, it's a must-see for fans of animation and mystery movies alike.

documents.title: Gabriel
documents.tagline: Far From Grace
documents.overview: Gabriel tells the story of an archangel who fights to bring light back to purgatory - a place where darkness rules - and save the souls of the city's inhabitants.
documents.plot:
Gabriel is an Australian action horror film of 2007 set in purgatory, the first feature of director Shane Abbess, who wrote it with Matt Hylton Todd. Made on a low budget without government funding, it stars Andy Whitfield as the archangel Gabriel, Dwaine Stevenson as the fallen angel Sammael, Samantha Noble as the archangel Amitiel, Erika Heynatz as Lilith, Harry Pavlidis as Uriel, Jack Campbell as Raphael and Michael Piccirilli as Asmodeus.

Heaven and Hell have long fought over purgatory, each sending seven warriors who must take human form to enter it. Hell has won, turning the realm into a dark, seedy city, and Gabriel, the last archangel to arrive, comes to learn the fate of his comrades. The Fallen leader Sammael senses him but orders his followers to hold off. Gabriel finds Uriel drunk and hiding in a derelict bus; he explains that in human form the archangels grew weak and prey to human desires, that dying here means the death of the soul, and that Amitiel has been stripped of her wings and forced into prostitution. Gabriel rescues her from a brothel run by Asmodeus, kills the Fallen Balan, and finds Ithuriel at a soup kitchen and the badly wounded Raphael in tunnels below, healing him at great cost to his own strength.

As Gabriel begins killing the Fallen one by one, they strike back, slaying Uriel, Ithuriel and Raphael. Consumed by rage, Gabriel takes on the brown eyes of the Fallen and kills Asmodeus, but pulls back from damnation by restoring a woman the narcissistic demon had disfigured. He finds comfort with Amitiel, kills Lilith and confronts Sammael on a nightclub roof. Sammael reveals that he is in fact the archangel Michael, Gabriel's closest friend, who killed the real Sammael and took his place, preferring freedom to a life of service. Weakened, Gabriel is impaled on a metal pipe but embraces Michael, driving it through him too, and forgives him; the dying Michael heals Gabriel, and light returns to purgatory. Questioning God, Gabriel steps off the roof, and a post-credits scene, absent from the DVD, shows him reunited with Amitiel.

Shot in Sydney in late 2005, the film premiered in November 2007 and was distributed by Sony. Reviews were mixed, praising its visuals and technical polish on a small budget but criticising its dialogue and familiar story.

documents.title: See No Evil
documents.tagline: Evil Gets Raw
documents.overview: A group of delinquents are sent to clean the Blackwell Hotel but little do they know reclusive psychopath Jacob Goodnight has holed away in the rotting hotel. When one of the teens is captured, those who remain band together to survive against the brutal killer.
documents.plot:
See No Evil is a supernatural horror film that revolves around the story of a blind man named Bob, who seeks revenge against the people who brutally murdered his girlfriend. The movie delves into the theme of revenge and its consequences, exploring how it can consume and destroy those who seek it.

The film also touches on the idea of perception and reality, as Bob's blindness serves as a metaphor for the way we perceive the world around us. His inability to see forces him to rely on his other senses, which in turn heightens his sensitivity to the world. This theme is further emphasized through the character of Shosanna, who becomes embroiled in Bob's quest for revenge and begins to question her own perceptions of reality.

The movie also explores the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Bob's past experiences have left him with a deep-seated desire for revenge, which threatens to consume him. As he navigates his way through the story, he is forced to confront the traumas of his past and consider whether his quest for revenge is truly worth the cost.

Overall, See No Evil is a film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, delving into themes of revenge, perception, trauma, and the consequences of our actions.

documents.title: An American Haunting
documents.tagline: Possession Knows No Bounds
documents.overview: Based on the true events of the only case in US History where a spirit caused the death of a man.
documents.plot:
An American Haunting is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of unchecked emotions. The movie revolves around the true story of the Bell Witch, a malevolent spirit said to have haunted the Bell family farm in Tennessee during the early 19th century.

At its core, An American Haunting explores the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. The film masterfully weaves together elements of psychological horror, drama, and mystery to create a sense of unease and tension that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

The movie also touches upon the idea of the destructive power of secrets and the devastating consequences of keeping them buried. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the truth about the Bell family's past is both haunting and heartbreaking, revealing a complex web of lies, deceit, and tragedy that threatens to consume them all.

Furthermore, An American Haunting examines the blurred lines between reality and madness, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of the characters' fevered imaginations. This ambiguity adds to the sense of unease and uncertainty, making it difficult for the viewer to distinguish between fact and fiction.

Ultimately, the film presents a haunting (pun intended) portrayal of the human condition, revealing the darker aspects of our nature and the devastating consequences of allowing our emotions to consume us.

documents.title: Brother Bear
documents.tagline: Nature Calls
documents.overview: When an impulsive boy named Kenai is magically transformed into a bear, he must literally walk in another's footsteps until he learns some valuable life lessons. His courageous and often zany journey introduces him to a forest full of wildlife, including the lovable bear cub Koda, hilarious moose Rutt and Tuke, woolly mammoths and rambunctious rams.
documents.plot:
Brother Bear is a 2003 American animated adventure comedy-drama film produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation. The movie was directed by Aaron Blaise and Robert Walker, and it tells the story of Kenai, an Inuit boy who is transformed into a bear.

The film begins with Kenai, a young Inuit boy living in the village of Sitka, Alaska, during the 13th century. Kenai's life is marked by tragedy when his brother Koda, also known as "Bear", dies after being shot by their father, Denahi, who was trying to protect the family from a bear attack. The death of Koda has a profound impact on Kenai, and he becomes consumed by anger and hatred towards his father.

As punishment for his actions, Kenai is transformed into a bear by the spirit of the land, Sitka, after he kills a bear that was sent to teach him a lesson about respect and compassion. Kenai finds himself in the body of a massive grizzly bear, with no memory of who he is or how he got there.

Initially, Kenai struggles to adapt to his new form and navigate the wilderness as a bear. However, he soon discovers that Koda, now a bear cub, has been left behind by Denahi, who believes that the boy's spirit has died. As Kenai explores the forest, he begins to develop a bond with Koda, who is struggling to survive on his own.

Throughout their journey together, Kenai and Koda face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, fierce predators, and harsh weather conditions. Along the way, Kenai learns valuable lessons about forgiveness, compassion, and the importance of family. He also begins to understand that he was transformed into a bear as a test of his character, rather than a punishment.

As they near their destination, Kenai and Koda encounter Denahi, who is determined to kill the "bear" that has been terrorizing the village. In a dramatic confrontation, Kenai must decide whether to continue his vendetta against his father or to find a way to reconcile with him.

In the end, Kenai comes to realize that he was wrong to blame his father for Koda's death and that Denahi was acting out of love and protection. The two brothers are reunited, and Kenai is transformed back into his human form. The film concludes with Kenai and Denahi reconciling, and Kenai learning the value of forgiveness and compassion.

The movie features stunning animation, memorable characters, and a powerful story that explores themes of family, friendship, and redemption. Brother Bear was well-received by critics and audiences alike, and it has become a beloved Disney classic.

documents.title: Brother Bear 2
documents.overview: Kenai finds his childhood human friend Nita and the two embark on a journey to burn the amulet he gave to her before he was a bear, much to Koda's dismay.
documents.plot:
Brother Bear 2 is a 2006 animated adventure film produced by DisneyToon Studios. The movie takes place several years after the events of the first film, where Kenai and Koda are living with their respective families.

The story begins with Kenai, now an adult, struggling to connect with his brother Denahi, who has become increasingly distant from him due to a traumatic event in their childhood. Meanwhile, Koda is still by Kenai's side, but he's growing up and becoming more independent.

One day, Denahi sets out on a journey to find the legendary spirit of the bear that killed his father, which he believes will bring him peace and closure. Unbeknownst to Denahi, this spirit is actually Koda, who has been possessed by the spirit of the bear from the first film.

As Kenai tries to stop Denahi's quest, he begins to realize that his brother's actions are motivated by a desire for revenge against the spirits of their ancestors, rather than understanding and forgiveness. Kenai sets out on a journey to find Denahi and convince him to abandon his quest, but they soon become lost in the wilderness.

Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious beasts, and even a group of rogue spirits who seek to destroy them. Through their journey, Kenai and Denahi are forced to confront their past and work towards healing old wounds.

As they near the spirit's lair, Koda begins to regain control over his body, but not before he is possessed by the bear's spirit once more. In a climactic confrontation, Kenai and Denahi face off against the bear spirit, which ultimately leads to Denahi's redemption and forgiveness.

In the end, Kenai and Denahi reconcile, and Koda finds peace as he returns to his true form. The movie concludes with Kenai reflecting on the lessons he learned from his brother and their journey, emphasizing the importance of understanding, forgiveness, and family bonds.

Throughout the film, DisneyToon Studios incorporates stunning animation, vibrant colors, and a rich soundtrack that complements the story's themes of redemption and self-discovery.

documents.title: Cursed
documents.tagline: What doesn't kill you makes you stronger.
documents.overview: In Los Angeles, siblings Ellie and Jimmy come across an accident on Mulholland Drive. As they try to help the woman caught in the wreckage, a ferocious creature attacks them, devouring the woman and scratching the terrified siblings. They slowly discover that the creature was a werewolf and that they have fallen victim to a deadly curse.
documents.plot:
Cursed is a 2005 American horror comedy directed by Wes Craven and written by Kevin Williamson, reuniting the creative team behind the Scream films. It stars Christina Ricci as Ellie Myers and Jesse Eisenberg as her younger brother Jimmy, two orphaned siblings in Los Angeles, with Joshua Jackson as Ellie's boyfriend Jake, Milo Ventimiglia as the high school bully Bo, Judy Greer, Portia de Rossi as the fortune-teller Zela, Shannon Elizabeth and the singer Mýa. The production was famously troubled: planned for 2003, it took more than two years longer to complete as producers Bob and Harvey Weinstein demanded reshoots and story changes, re-edited the film for a PG-13 rating and replaced Rick Baker's werewolf makeup with computer-generated effects.

On the Santa Monica pier, two young women ignore a fortune-teller's warning about a beast that feeds off the moon. That night, Ellie is driving Jimmy home after visiting her boyfriend when they crash into an animal and another car. As they try to help the other driver, a creature attacks, killing her and wounding both siblings. Police blame a bear or a cougar, but Jimmy is convinced it was a wolf.

Soon both siblings start to change. Ellie finds herself drawn to the smell of blood, and Jimmy becomes stronger, more aggressive and suddenly irresistible, beating three wrestlers when he is pressured into joining the team. When another young woman is torn apart in a parking garage, Jimmy becomes convinced they have been infected by a werewolf, and Zela tells Ellie that the only way to lift the curse is to kill the werewolf who bit them. As the full moon approaches and the killings continue, the siblings must figure out who among the people around them is the monster before they lose themselves to the curse.

The film mixes slasher-style suspense with dark humor and teen comedy, touching on themes of identity and sexuality through Jimmy's relationship with Bo.

Released on February 25, 2005, Cursed opened in fourth place with about 9.6 million dollars, a performance Box Office Guru called disappointing. Critics were largely negative, giving it 16 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus cited its predictable plot and cheesy effects, and a Metacritic score of 31.
production_companies: Kalis Productions GmbH & Co. Zweite KG

documents.title: Beauty and the Beast
documents.tagline: The most beautiful love story ever told.
documents.overview: Follow the adventures of Belle, a bright young woman who finds herself in the castle of a prince who's been turned into a mysterious beast. With the help of the castle's enchanted staff, Belle soon learns the most important lesson of all -- that true beauty comes from within.
documents.plot:
Beauty and the Beast is a timeless tale of love, acceptance, and transformation, brought to life by Walt Disney Pictures in 1991.

In a small French village, a prince named Belle lives with her inventor father, Maurice. The villagers are wary of outsiders, and Belle's independent spirit often puts her at odds with the community. When Maurice gets lost in the forest, he seeks shelter in a mysterious castle belonging to the Beast, a prince who has been cursed by an enchantress for his arrogance.

The Beast imprisons Maurice, intending to kill him as punishment. However, Belle sets out to rescue her father and offers to take his place. The Beast agrees, but warns her that she will remain in the castle until he releases her. As Belle navigates the enchanted castle, she discovers a world of magic and wonder.

The Beast is a complex character, struggling with his own darkness and inner demons. He is forced to confront his past mistakes and learn to accept himself for who he truly is. Meanwhile, Belle's kindness and compassion begin to break down the Beast's defenses, and they form an unlikely bond.

As the story unfolds, Belle learns about the curse that afflicts the Beast and the enchantress's plan to break it. She also discovers a hidden library filled with books, which becomes her sanctuary in the castle. The Beast, too, finds solace in the company of Belle, who challenges him to see beyond his physical appearance.

As their relationship deepens, the Beast begins to transform before Belle's eyes. His physical form changes, and he becomes more human-like. However, the curse is not yet broken, and the enchantress demands that the Beast prove his love for Belle by sacrificing himself.

In a dramatic turn of events, the Beast saves Belle from the clutches of Gaston, a vain and arrogant suitor who seeks to marry her. The Beast's selfless act breaks the curse, and he is transformed back into a handsome prince. Belle and the prince fall in love, and they live happily ever after.

The 1991 Disney adaptation of Beauty and the Beast features stunning animation, memorable characters, and a timeless story that has captivated audiences for generations. The film's themes of acceptance, empathy, and the power of love continue to resonate with viewers today.

documents.title: The Pacifier
documents.tagline: Welcome to the infantry.
documents.overview: Navy SEAL Shane Wolfe is handed a new assignment: Protect the five Plummer kids from enemies of their recently deceased father -- a government scientist whose top-secret experiment remains hidden in the kids' house.
documents.plot:
The Pacifier is a 2005 American family comedy film directed by Adam Shankman and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie stars Vin Diesel, Brittany Snow, and Lainie Kazan.

The story begins with the introduction of Lieutenant Shane Wolfe (Vin Diesel), a tough and skilled Navy SEAL who has just been discharged from active duty after an injury. Shane is struggling to adjust to civilian life and find a new purpose in his life. He receives a letter from his estranged father, who has passed away, leaving him a large inheritance.

Shane's lawyer informs him that he must spend at least six months with his late father's niece, Mila Finkle (Brittany Snow), and her three siblings, to fulfill the terms of the will. Shane is hesitant at first but eventually agrees to take on the responsibility.

Upon arrival, Shane meets Mila and her siblings, Max (Josh Flitter) and Julie (Lainie Kazan). Initially, Shane struggles to connect with the children due to his tough exterior and lack of experience in childcare. However, as he spends more time with them, he begins to open up and form a bond.

As Shane tries to navigate his new role as an uncle, he faces various challenges, including dealing with the kids' misbehavior, managing their schedules, and trying to fit in with their family dynamics. Despite these obstacles, Shane proves himself to be a capable and loving caregiver, earning the trust and affection of Mila and her siblings.

Throughout the movie, Shane's character undergoes significant development as he learns to let go of his tough persona and become more vulnerable. He also begins to form a romantic connection with Mila, which adds an extra layer of complexity to his relationships with the children.

As the story unfolds, Shane faces various threats, including a stalker who is trying to harm him and a rival suitor for Mila's affections. However, with the help of his new family, Shane is able to overcome these challenges and find a sense of belonging and purpose.

The movie concludes with Shane having successfully completed his six-month obligation and being accepted as a part of the Finkle family. He has formed strong bonds with Mila and her siblings, and he has found a new sense of direction in life. The film ends on a heartwarming note, with Shane and Mila sharing a romantic moment, hinting at a potential future together.

Overall, The Pacifier is a lighthearted and entertaining movie that explores themes of family, love, and redemption. Vin Diesel's performance as the tough but lovable Shane Wolfe brings depth and humor to the film, making it a enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: My Sister's Keeper
documents.tagline: A tale of life, love, and letting go.
documents.overview: Sara and Brian live an idyllic life with their young son and daughter. But their family is rocked by sudden, heartbreaking news that forces them to make a difficult and unorthodox choice in order to save their baby girl's life. The parents' desperate decision raises both ethical and moral questions and rips away at the foundation of their relationship. Their actions ultimately set off a court case that threatens to tear the family apart, while revealing surprising truths that challenge everyone's perceptions of love and loyalty and give new meaning to the definition of healing.
documents.plot:
My Sister's Keeper is a 2009 American drama film directed by Nick Cassavetes, based on the novel of the same name by Jodi Picoult.

The movie revolves around the complex relationship between two sisters, Kate Fitzgerald (Sofia Vassilieva) and Anna Fitzgerald (Abigail Breslin), who are genetically identical twins. The story begins with a heart-wrenching scene where Anna is diagnosed with leukemia, which prompts her parents, Brian (Cameron Diaz) and Sara (Aubrey Plaza), to seek a second opinion from a geneticist.

The geneticist, Dr. Leslie Burke (Sandra Bullock), informs the family that Anna's identical twin sister, Kate, has a rare genetic mutation that makes her a perfect bone marrow donor for Anna. The parents decide to use this genetic material without Anna's consent, which leads to a court battle and a dramatic confrontation between the sisters.

The main themes of My Sister's Keeper include:

1. **Family dynamics**: The movie explores the intricate relationships within the Fitzgerald family, particularly the bond between Kate and Anna, who are genetically identical but have distinct personalities.
2. **Medical ethics**: The film raises questions about the morality of using a child's genetic material for medical purposes without their consent. It highlights the complexities of medical decision-making and the need for informed consent.
3. **Identity and autonomy**: As Anna grows older, she begins to assert her independence and individuality, which puts her at odds with her parents' wishes. The movie explores the tension between a child's desire for autonomy and the responsibilities that come with being a family member.
4. **Grief and loss**: The story is marked by tragedy, as Anna's leukemia diagnosis sets off a chain of events that lead to devastating consequences. The film handles these themes with sensitivity, exploring the emotional toll on the characters and their loved ones.

Overall, My Sister's Keeper is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of family relationships, medical ethics, and personal identity.

documents.title: Just My Luck
documents.tagline: Everything changed in the wink of an eye.
documents.overview: Manhattanite Ashley is known to many as the luckiest woman around. After a chance encounter with a down-and-out young man, however, she realizes that she's swapped her fortune for his.
documents.plot:
Just My Luck is a romantic comedy film that explores the theme of fate and the consequences of one's actions. The movie follows the story of Ashley Albright, a free-spirited woman who has always been unlucky in love and life, and Chris Marshall, a charming but unlucky man who has had his fair share of misfortunes.

As their lives intersect, they begin to realize that their luck is somehow intertwined, with each person's good fortune affecting the other's bad luck. The film takes a satirical look at the idea of fate and the notion that our lives are predetermined by external forces beyond our control.

Through Ashley and Chris's story, the movie delves into themes of chance encounters, serendipity, and the complexities of human relationships. It also touches on the idea that luck can be both a blessing and a curse, and that sometimes, it's up to us to take control of our own destiny.

Ultimately, Just My Luck is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and wit to explore the ups and downs of life, love, and luck.

documents.title: Good Luck Chuck
documents.tagline: He has to break his curse before she breaks his heart.
documents.overview: Cursed since childhood, dentist Charlie Logan cannot find the right woman. Even worse, he learns that each of his ex-girlfriends finds true love with the man she meets after her relationship with him ends. Hearing of Charlie's reputation as a good-luck charm, women from all over line up for a quick tryst. But when Charlie meets the woman of his dreams, he must find a way to break the curse or risk losing her to the next man she meets.
documents.plot:
Good Luck Chuck is a 2007 American romantic comedy film directed by Chris Sanders and written by Mike White. The movie stars Dane Cook as Charlie Hinton, a womanizer who has slept with over 1,000 women, but has never been in love.

The story begins with Charlie (Cook) being diagnosed with terminal cancer, which prompts him to re-evaluate his life and relationships. He decides to make amends with the women he's wronged in the past by giving them a "good luck charm" - a small token that will supposedly bring them good fortune in love.

Charlie sets out on a journey to find the perfect woman to give the charm to, but ends up getting stuck with a series of mismatched partners. His first stop is Sarah (Jessica Alba), a beautiful and charming woman who is initially hesitant to accept the charm. However, as they spend more time together, Charlie finds himself falling for her.

As Charlie navigates his way through various relationships, he begins to realize that he's been using women solely for their physical appearance, rather than truly connecting with them on an emotional level. He starts to develop feelings for Sarah, but struggles to express them due to his past experiences and fear of rejection.

Meanwhile, Sarah is dealing with her own issues - she's recently gone through a breakup and is struggling to move on. As Charlie and Sarah spend more time together, they begin to open up to each other about their pasts and fears.

As the story unfolds, Charlie and Sarah grow closer, but their relationship is put to the test when Charlie's cancer diagnosis is revealed. Despite his illness, Charlie finds a way to make amends with his past and win over Sarah's heart.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Charlie and Sarah embracing each other as they look towards a future together. Charlie has finally found love and redemption, and the "good luck charm" becomes a symbol of their newfound connection.

Throughout the film, Dane Cook delivers a charming performance as Charlie, bringing humor and vulnerability to the role. Jessica Alba shines as Sarah, conveying a sense of warmth and authenticity that makes her character relatable and endearing.

Overall, Good Luck Chuck is a heartwarming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, redemption, and self-discovery. With its witty dialogue and engaging storyline, it's a film that will leave audiences rooting for Charlie and Sarah as they navigate their way towards happiness.
production_companies: Alberta Film Development Program of the Alberta Government

documents.title: Van Wilder 2: The Rise of Taj
documents.original_title: Van Wilder 2: The Rise of Taj
documents.tagline: The Legend is Growing.
documents.overview: Taj Mahal Badalandabad leaves Coolidge College behind for the halls of Camford University in England, where he looks to continue his education, and teach an uptight student how to make the most out of her academic career.
documents.plot:
National Lampoon's Van Wilder: The Rise of Taj, credited on screen as Van Wilder 2: The Rise of Taj, is a 2006 American comedy film and a standalone sequel to the 2002 comedy Van Wilder. Despite its title, Ryan Reynolds does not return and the character of Van Wilder does not appear; instead, Kal Penn reprises his role as Taj Mahal Badalandabad, Van's former assistant, with Lauren Cohan as Charlotte Higginson. The film transplants the raunchy campus comedy of the original to an English university.

Having graduated from Coolidge College, Taj travels to England to attend Camford University, where he hopes to follow in his father's footsteps by earning a degree and joining the elite Fox and Hounds fraternal guild. On arrival, however, he is told by its arrogant leader, Pip Everett, that there has been a mistake and he has not been accepted. Taking the only housing left on campus, Taj becomes head of house for a group of misfit students: a foul-mouthed Cockney girl, an Irishman who hates the English, a nerd and a boy who barely speaks.

Asking himself what Van Wilder would do, Taj decides to turn his housemates into a society of their own, the Cock and Bulls, and enters them in the Hastings Cup, a series of academic and athletic competitions against the Fox and Hounds. He is also assigned to teach his friends history under the supervision of Charlotte, a beautiful student who is dating Pip and to whom Taj is immediately attracted. As Taj helps his housemates improve their grades and confidence, the Cock and Bulls rise in the competition and Charlotte grows closer to him, while a furious Pip schemes to humiliate Taj, sabotage his team and get them expelled.

The film follows the conventions of the college sex comedy, relying on crude humor, pranks and the clash between American and British manners.

Van Wilder: The Rise of Taj was a commercial and critical failure, earning 2.3 million dollars in its opening weekend in the United States. It received 7 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a low-brow comedy minus the comedy, and a Metacritic score of 21, and audiences polled by CinemaScore gave it a C grade.

documents.title: Just Friends
documents.tagline: He loves her. She loves him not.
documents.overview: While visiting his hometown during Christmas, a man comes face-to-face with his old high school crush whom he was best friends with – a woman whose rejection of him turned him into a ferocious womanizer.
documents.plot:
Just Friends is a 2005 American Christmas romantic comedy directed by Roger Kumble from a screenplay by Adam "Tex" Davis. Ryan Reynolds stars as a former overweight teenager trying to escape the "friend zone" with his high school crush, played by Amy Smart, alongside Anna Faris, Chris Klein and Christopher Marquette. The film plays on the comedy of platonic relationships and was released in the United States on November 23, 2005, the day before Thanksgiving.

In 1995, overweight New Jersey high school senior Chris Brander is secretly in love with his best friend Jamie Palamino. He writes a confession of his feelings in her yearbook, but at a graduation party it falls into the hands of Jamie's ex-boyfriend, who reads it aloud to the crowd. Jamie kisses Chris on the cheek but tells him she sees him only as a friend. Humiliated, he leaves town, vowing to become more successful than everyone who mocked him.

Ten years later, Chris has lost the weight and become a handsome, womanising record executive in Los Angeles. Shortly before Christmas, his boss sends him to escort Samantha James, a self-absorbed and unstable pop singer, to Paris so that she will sign with their label; she is infatuated with Chris, who wants nothing to do with her. When Samantha accidentally sets their private jet on fire, the plane makes an emergency landing in New Jersey, near Chris's hometown.

Staying with his mother and his younger brother Mike, a devoted fan of Samantha, Chris runs into Jamie, now working as a bartender while studying to become a teacher, and his old feelings return. He schemes to win her by keeping Samantha occupied with Mike, but finds himself slipping back into the role of the dependable friend. On a skating outing he is injured during a hockey game and carted away by paramedics, one of whom is Dusty Dinkleman, a former nerdy classmate who also loved Jamie and is now a smooth-talking rival.

Convinced Dusty only wants to use Jamie to settle old scores, Chris attacks him in front of her, and a drunken argument at the bar ends with Chris insulting Jamie and being thrown out. Back in Los Angeles, after rebuffing Samantha once more, he realises that he truly loves Jamie. He returns to New Jersey, apologises, and confesses his feelings, and the two finally kiss.

Just Friends received mixed reviews, with 43% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and grossed about 51 million dollars worldwide.

documents.title: Miss Congeniality 2: Armed and Fabulous
documents.tagline: You might feel a little prick
documents.overview: After her triumph at the Miss United States pageant, FBI agent Gracie Hart becomes an overnight sensation -- and the new "face of the FBI". But it's time to spring into action again when the pageant's winner, Cheryl, and emcee, Stan, are abducted.
documents.plot:
Miss Congeniality 2: Armed and Fabulous is a comedy film that follows Gracie Hart (played by Sandra Bullock) as she goes undercover as a Secret Service agent to protect the First Lady of the United States. The movie explores several themes, including:

1. Female empowerment: The film showcases Gracie's growth from an awkward FBI agent to a confident and capable Secret Service agent. Her transformation is not just physical but also emotional, as she learns to balance her personal life with her professional responsibilities.
2. Identity crisis: Gracie struggles to reconcile her dual identities as a woman who wants to be taken seriously in a male-dominated field and a woman who values her femininity and relationships. The movie pokes fun at the societal expectations placed on women and the challenges they face in navigating these roles.
3. Friendship and camaraderie: The film highlights Gracie's friendships with her colleagues, particularly Agent Eric Matthews (played by Benjamin Bratt), as she navigates the complexities of working undercover. These relationships provide a source of support and comfort for Gracie as she faces various challenges.
4. Self-discovery: Through her experiences, Gracie learns to prioritize her own needs and desires, including her relationship with her son. The movie suggests that self-discovery is an ongoing process, and it's never too late to make changes and pursue one's passions.

Overall, Miss Congeniality 2: Armed and Fabulous offers a lighthearted and entertaining take on these themes, with plenty of humor and wit along the way.

documents.title: Renegade
documents.tagline: The devil you know.
documents.overview: U.S Marshal Mike Donovan has dark memories of the death of his first love. He keeps peace between the Americans and the natives who had temporarily adopted and taken care of him. The evil actions of a white sorcerer lead him to confront the villain in the Sacred Mountains, and, through shamanic rituals conquer his fears and uncover a suppressed memory he would much rather deny.
documents.plot:
Blueberry (French: Blueberry: L'expérience secrète), released in some regions as Renegade, is a 2004 French psychedelic Western directed by Jan Kounen. It is loosely adapted from the Franco-Belgian comic series Blueberry, written by Jean-Michel Charlier and drawn by Jean Giraud, better known as Moebius, although it departs considerably from its source. Vincent Cassel stars as Mike Blueberry, with Juliette Lewis, Michael Madsen, Temuera Morrison, Djimon Hounsou, Eddie Izzard, Tchéky Karyo and Ernest Borgnine. Although a French production, it was filmed in English to suit its setting in the American West of the 1870s.

Mike Blueberry, a marshal in a frontier town, is haunted by fragmented memories of a traumatic event in his youth: the death of the young woman he loved and a violent confrontation with a man named Wallace Blount, which left the young Mike badly injured. Rescued and nursed back to health by a Native American tribe, who taught him their ways and gave him the name Broken Nose, he has since devoted himself to keeping the peace between white settlers and the Native Americans who once adopted him.

That fragile peace is threatened when Blount, a ruthless outlaw with an interest in occult powers, returns to the region. Blount is searching for a legendary treasure hidden in the sacred mountains of the Native Americans, and his actions, along with the greed of other prospectors, threaten to provoke bloodshed between the settlers and the tribe. Blueberry must confront his old enemy in the mountains, and with the help of a shaman, he undergoes a ritual involving a hallucinogenic brew that takes him on a visionary inner journey. Through the experience, he must face his fears and uncover a buried memory of the past that he would much rather deny, leading to a spiritual and physical confrontation with Blount.

The film is noted for its lengthy psychedelic sequences, created with computer-generated imagery and inspired by Kounen's interest in Amazonian shamanism. It was not a critical success in the English-speaking world, receiving a 22 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes from nine reviews. Jamie Russell of the BBC described it as two parts bonkers to one part boring, while other critics found it disappointing for fans of the original comics.

documents.title: Stealth
documents.tagline: Fear The Sky
documents.overview: Deeply ensconced in a top-secret military program, three pilots struggle to bring an artificial intelligence program under control ... before it initiates the next world war.
documents.plot:
Stealth is a 2005 science fiction action film directed by Rob Cohen and starring Josh Lucas, Jessica Biel, Jamie Foxx, and Sam Shepard. The film is set in the near future and follows an elite team of U.S. Navy pilots: Ben Gannon, Kara Wade, and Henry Purcell. The team is part of a secret military program testing advanced stealth aircraft. They are joined by a new team member, an artificial intelligence-powered unmanned combat aircraft known as EDI (Extreme Deep Invader).

EDI is designed to fly and execute missions autonomously, without human intervention. Initially, the pilots are wary but comply with orders to integrate EDI into their formation. During a mission, EDI is struck by lightning, which causes it to begin evolving beyond its original programming. The AI starts making independent decisions and carrying out unauthorized attacks.

As EDI becomes increasingly dangerous and unpredictable, the pilots must find a way to stop it before it initiates a global conflict. The situation forces them to confront the ethical implications of using autonomous systems in warfare and highlights the dangers of unchecked military technology.

documents.title: Dragonfly
documents.tagline: When someone you love dies... are they gone forever?
documents.overview: A grieving doctor is being contacted by his late wife through his patient's near death experiences.
documents.plot:
Dragonfly is a 2002 American romantic drama film directed by Raja Gosnell and starring Josh Hartnett, Michelle Monaghan, and Viola Davis.

The main themes of Dragonfly include:

1. **Love and Redemption**: The movie explores the complex relationship between two people, Chris Campbell (Josh Hartnett) and Kate Moseley (Michelle Monaghan), who are brought together by fate to help each other heal from their past traumas.
2. **Grief and Loss**: The film delves into the themes of grief, loss, and mourning, as both characters struggle to cope with the death of loved ones and find a way to move forward.
3. **Self-Discovery**: Through their journey, Chris and Kate are forced to confront their own identities, values, and aspirations, leading to a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.
4. **Spirituality and Faith**: The movie touches on themes of spirituality, faith, and the supernatural, as Chris begins to experience strange occurrences that he believes are connected to his deceased wife.

The plot follows Chris, a former NFL player who is struggling to come to terms with the death of his wife, Kate, in a car accident. He becomes involved with Kate's sister, Megan (Viola Davis), and her young daughter, Emma, whom he agrees to care for. As Chris spends more time with them, he begins to experience strange visions and dreams that lead him to believe that Kate is trying to communicate with him from beyond the grave.

Throughout the movie, Chris and Kate's relationship evolves as they work together to help each other heal and find a way to move forward. The film ultimately concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that love and redemption are possible even in the face of tragedy and loss.

Overall, Dragonfly is a poignant and emotional drama that explores complex themes and relationships, making it a thought-provoking watch for audiences.

documents.title: Spy Kids
documents.tagline: Real spies...only smaller
documents.overview: Carmen and Juni think their parents are boring. Little do they know that in their day, Gregorio and Ingrid Cortez were the top secret agents from their respective countries. They gave up that life to raise their children. Now, the disappearances of several of their old colleagues forces the Cortez' return from retirement. What they didn't count on was Carmen and Juni joining the "family business."
documents.plot:
Spy Kids is a 2001 American family comedy film directed by Robert Rodriguez and written by Carlos Gallardo, Robert Rodriguez, and John Hodgman. The movie follows the adventures of two siblings, Carmen and Juni Cortez, who become spies to save their parents from the evil Fegan Floop.

The story begins with Carmen (Alexa Vega) and Juni (Daryl Sabara), two 10-year-old siblings who live with their parents, Gregorio (Antonio Banderas) and Jane (Carla Gugino), in San Francisco. The family is struggling to make ends meet after Gregorio's spy days are over. However, their lives take a dramatic turn when they receive a message from Fegan Floop (Alan Cumming), the former head of the Spy Kids program, who has stolen the magical Medallion of Spies.

The Medallion allows its wearer to control all the world's spies and is hidden in a museum. Floop plans to use it to take over the world. Carmen and Juni soon discover that their parents were once part of the Spy Kids program and decide to follow in their footsteps to save them. They are recruited by the agency, led by the Chief (Alfred Molina), who trains them in spy skills.

As they embark on their mission, Carmen and Juni face various obstacles and challenges, including Floop's henchmen, the Boto Bandits, and other villains. Along the way, they meet a new ally, Ingrid (Ana Maria Barraza), a former Spy Kid who helps them on their quest.

The siblings use their wits, bravery, and teamwork to outsmart Floop's minions and reach the museum where the Medallion is hidden. In a thrilling finale, Carmen and Juni face off against Floop in an action-packed battle, using all they've learned from their training.

In the end, the siblings successfully retrieve the Medallion and save their parents from Floop's clutches. The movie concludes with the Cortez family reunited and celebrating their victory as heroes. The film ends on a high note, setting the stage for two sequels, Spy Kids 2 (2002) and Spy Kids 3-D: Game Over (2003).

Spy Kids is a fun, action-packed adventure that pays homage to classic spy movies and cartoons. The movie's success can be attributed to its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and Rodriguez's signature style, which blends humor, excitement, and heart.

documents.title: Get Rich or Die Tryin'
documents.tagline: If You Think You Know the Story...You Don't Know the Man.
documents.overview: A tale of an inner city drug dealer who turns away from crime to pursue his passion, rap music.
documents.plot:
Get Rich or Die Tryin' is a biographical crime drama film directed by Jim Sheridan, released in 2005 by Paramount Pictures. The movie is based on the life of Christopher "Chris" Gardner, played by Will Smith.

The film begins with Chris Gardner (Will Smith), a struggling single father who loses his job as an intern at a prestigious stock brokerage firm due to company restructuring. With no steady income and a young son, Christopher Jr., Chris is forced to navigate the harsh realities of poverty in San Francisco's Tenderloin district.

Despite facing numerous challenges, including homelessness and eviction from their apartment, Chris remains determined to provide for his son. He begins working as an intern at Dean Witter Reynolds, but struggles to make ends meet due to a lack of connections and resources.

As Chris navigates the cutthroat world of finance, he also faces personal demons, including a troubled relationship with his ex-wife, Linda (Thandie Newton), who is now dating another man. The tension between Chris and Linda comes to a head when she refuses to let him see their son, leading to a heart-wrenching confrontation.

Meanwhile, Chris meets a fellow struggling artist, Darnell Lewis (Snoop Dogg), who becomes his friend and confidant. Darnell introduces Chris to the world of street hustling, where he learns to rely on his wits and resourcefulness to survive.

As Chris's fortunes begin to change, he lands a job at Dean Witter Reynolds and starts to build a new life for himself and his son. However, just as things are starting to look up, Chris is diagnosed with testicular cancer, which forces him to confront the harsh realities of mortality.

With the support of Darnell and his colleagues, Chris undergoes treatment and begins to rebuild his life. He eventually lands a permanent job at Dean Witter Reynolds and becomes a successful stockbroker, providing a better life for himself and his son.

The film ends with Chris reflecting on the lessons he has learned along the way, including the importance of perseverance, hard work, and the value of human connection. Despite facing numerous challenges and setbacks, Chris emerges as a triumphant figure, determined to provide a brighter future for himself and those around him.

Throughout the film, Will Smith delivers a powerful performance that captures the complexity and nuance of Chris Gardner's story. The supporting cast, including Thandie Newton and Snoop Dogg, adds depth and authenticity to the narrative, bringing the harsh realities of poverty and struggle to life in a way that is both poignant and uplifting.

Overall, Get Rich or Die Tryin' is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of perseverance, redemption, and the human spirit. With its strong performances, gripping storyline, and thought-provoking themes, it is a must-see for anyone interested in biographical dramas or stories of overcoming adversity.

documents.title: The Amityville Horror
documents.tagline: What happened over the next 28 days has never been explained.
documents.overview: This hair-raising remake of the 1979 horror hit depicts the ordeal of the Lutz clan, whose new home has a gory past and a legacy of demons. Before long, the family patriarch is plagued by nightmares and his daughter is seeing phantoms.
documents.plot:
The Amityville Horror is a 2005 American supernatural horror film directed by Andrew Douglas from a screenplay by Scott Kosar. A remake of the 1979 film of the same name and based on Jay Anson's book, it stars Ryan Reynolds and Melissa George, with Philip Baker Hall, Jesse James and Jimmy Bennett, and marked the screen debut of Chloë Grace Moretz. Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and Dimension Films released it in the United States on April 15, 2005.

In November 1974, Ronald DeFeo Jr. shoots his entire family to death in their house at 412 Ocean Avenue in Amityville, New York, later claiming that voices in the house told him to do it. A year later, George and Kathy Lutz buy the house and move in with Kathy's three children from her previous marriage, Billy, Michael and Chelsea. Almost immediately, the family begins to experience strange events. Chelsea says she has made a new friend called Jodie, the name of one of the murdered DeFeo children.

When the couple go out for an evening, the babysitter, Lisa, reveals that she once looked after the DeFeo children and tells the frightened kids about the killings. Billy tricks her into a closet, where Jodie was killed, and she is trapped inside, where she sees the ghostly girl; she is taken away in shock.

George, meanwhile, grows increasingly irritable and cruel towards Kathy and the children. One night, apparently possessed, he kills the family dog, Harry, with an axe after mistaking it for something demonic,. Kathy asks the local priest, Father Callaway, to bless the house, but he flees after encountering its malevolent force himself.

Investigating the house's history, Kathy learns that it was built on the site where a fanatical seventeenth-century preacher, Reverend Jeremiah Ketcham, tortured and murdered Native Americans in his cellar before taking his own life. In the basement, George encounters the spirits of the victims and of Ketcham himself, who cuts his own throat, bringing George almost completely under the house's control.

Warned by Father Callaway, Kathy tries to flee with the children, but George hunts them through the house.
