documents.title: Shrek Forever After
documents.tagline: It ain't Ogre... Til it's Ogre
documents.overview: A bored and domesticated Shrek pacts with deal-maker Rumpelstiltskin to get back to feeling like a real ogre again, but when he's duped and sent to a twisted version of Far Far Away—where Rumpelstiltskin is king, ogres are hunted, and he and Fiona have never met—he sets out to restore his world and reclaim his true love.
documents.plot:
Shrek Forever After is a 2010 animated fantasy comedy film directed by Mike Mitchell, produced by DreamWorks Animation, and based on the Shrek franchise. The movie takes place after the events of Shrek the Third.

The story begins with Shrek (Mike Myers) feeling unappreciated and overworked as an ogre. He is constantly surrounded by fairy tale creatures, including Donkey (Eddie Murphy), who never shuts up. Shrek longs for a simpler life, free from his royal duties and responsibilities. One day, while sitting in a swampy bar with Donkey, Shrek meets Rumpelstiltskin (Conrad Vernon), a mischievous imp who offers him a deal: if Shrek signs the charter of his kingdom over to Rumpelstiltskin for one day, he will be granted any wish he desires.

Shrek, tempted by the promise of freedom and adventure, agrees to the deal. However, things don't go as planned. On the designated day, Shrek finds himself in a parallel universe where he is married to Fiona (Cameron Diaz) and has three children with her. He also meets his alternate self, who is a more confident and successful ogre.

As Shrek navigates this new reality, he realizes that being an ogre isn't all it's cracked up to be. His wife and children are not as happy with him as they seem, and he begins to question the choices he made in his life. Meanwhile, Rumpelstiltskin is using Shrek's kingdom to gain power and control over both worlds.

Shrek must find a way to return to his own world and break the curse that has been cast upon him. Along the way, he teams up with Donkey, who has also become trapped in this parallel universe. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to rescue Shrek's family and restore balance to both worlds.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges and obstacles, including the villainous Rumpelstiltskin and his minions. The film features plenty of humor, action, and heartwarming moments as Shrek learns valuable lessons about being true to oneself and appreciating what one has.

Overall, Shrek Forever After is a fun and entertaining addition to the Shrek franchise, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers engaged until the very end.

documents.title: The Last Airbender
documents.tagline: Four nations, one destiny.
documents.overview: The story follows the adventures of Aang, a young successor to a long line of Avatars, who must put his childhood ways aside and stop the Fire Nation from enslaving the Water, Earth and Air nations.
documents.plot:
The Last Airbender is a 2010 American fantasy action-adventure film written and directed by M. Night Shyamalan, based on the first season of the animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender. Noah Ringer stars as Aang, with Nicola Peltz as Katara, Jackson Rathbone as Sokka, Dev Patel as Prince Zuko, Shaun Toub as Iroh, Aasif Mandvi as Commander Zhao and Cliff Curtis as Fire Lord Ozai.

For a century, the Fire Nation has waged war on the Air Nomads, the Water Tribes and the Earth Kingdom. In the Southern Water Tribe, the siblings Katara and Sokka break open an iceberg and free a twelve-year-old boy, Aang, and his flying bison Appa. The exiled Fire Nation prince Zuko sees the burst of light and arrives demanding the Avatar, the only person who can "bend" all four elements. Aang surrenders to protect the village but escapes. At the Southern Air Temple he learns he has been frozen for a hundred years and that the Fire Nation has wiped out his people, including his mentor Monk Gyatso. His grief sends him into the Avatar State, where he meets a Dragon Spirit. After freeing an occupied Earth Kingdom village, Aang admits he has mastered only airbending, and the group heads north so he can learn waterbending.

Aang is captured by Commander Zhao but rescued by the masked Blue Spirit, who turns out to be Zuko. Zuko survives Zhao's attempt on his life. At the Northern Water Tribe, Master Pakku teaches Aang and Katara, until the Fire Nation attacks. Zuko captures Aang, who returns to the Avatar State and receives the Dragon Spirit's advice to show the power of water. Katara freezes Zuko in ice. Zhao kills the Moon Spirit to rob the waterbenders of their power, but Iroh drives him away, and Princess Yue gives her life to restore the spirit. Zhao is drowned by waterbenders, and Aang raises the ocean into a towering wall that drives back the Fire Nation fleet. Fire Lord Ozai orders his daughter Azula to stop the Avatar before Sozin's Comet returns.

Filmed in Greenland and Pennsylvania in 2009, the film drew protests over the casting of white actors as characters from Asian- and Native-influenced cultures. Paramount released it on July 1, 2010. It grossed about $319.7 million worldwide but was almost universally panned for its script, acting, effects and 3D conversion. Rotten Tomatoes reported just 5% approval, the lowest for any Nickelodeon Movies production. Roger Ebert gave it half a star. It won five Golden Raspberry Awards, including Worst Picture and Worst Director.

documents.title: The Princess and the Frog
documents.tagline: Every love story begins with a kiss...
documents.overview: A waitress, desperate to fulfill her dreams as a restaurant owner, is set on a journey to turn a frog prince back into a human being, but she has to face the same problem after she kisses him.
documents.plot:
The Princess and the Frog is a beautifully crafted animated film set in New Orleans during the 1920s jazz era. The story follows Tiana, a hardworking and ambitious young African-American woman who dreams of opening her own restaurant. She is determined to succeed and make a name for herself in the culinary world.

One day, while walking through the bayou, Tiana meets Prince Naveen, a charming but arrogant prince who has been turned into a frog by the villainous Dr. Facilier (also known as Shadow Man). The only way to break the curse is for Naveen and Tiana to kiss each other, which leads to an unlikely partnership between the two.

As they embark on their journey together, Tiana and Naveen face numerous challenges, including navigating the magical world of voodoo and encountering a cast of colorful characters. Along the way, Tiana learns valuable lessons about perseverance, friendship, and the importance of following her dreams.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with vibrant colors and intricate details that bring the city of New Orleans to life. The music is equally impressive, featuring a range of jazz and blues classics that perfectly capture the spirit of the era.

One of the standout aspects of The Princess and the Frog is its strong female protagonist. Tiana is a complex and relatable character who embodies many of the qualities that make a great heroine: intelligence, determination, and a willingness to take risks. Her journey is both inspiring and empowering, making her one of the most beloved Disney princesses of all time.

The film's themes of perseverance, friendship, and following your dreams are timeless and universal, making it a must-see for audiences of all ages. The Princess and the Frog is a beautifully crafted tale that will leave you smiling, singing along to the music, and rooting for Tiana and Naveen as they navigate their magical adventure together.

Overall, The Princess and the Frog is a delightful film that showcases the best of Disney's storytelling and animation. With its stunning visuals, catchy music, and strong female protagonist, it's a movie that will leave you enchanted and eager to return to the world of New Orleans magic.

documents.title: The Tale of Despereaux
documents.tagline: Small Mouse. Big Dreams
documents.overview: Once upon a time... in the far away kingdom of Dor... lived a brave and virtuous mouse with comically oversized ears who dreamt of becoming a knight. Banished from his home for having such lofty ambitions, Despereaux sets off on an amazing adventure with his good-hearted rat friend Roscuro, who leads him, at long last, on a very noble quest to rescue an endangered princess and save an entire kingdom from darkness.
documents.plot:
The Tale of Despereaux is a 2008 animated fantasy adventure comedy film loosely based on Kate DiCamillo's 2003 Newbery Medal-winning novel. Directed by Sam Fell and Robert Stevenhagen and written by Gary Ross from a story by Will McRobb and Chris Viscardi, it features the voices of Matthew Broderick as the title character, with Emma Watson, Dustin Hoffman, Tracey Ullman, Kevin Kline and Robbie Coltrane, and Sigourney Weaver as narrator. Universal Pictures released it on December 19, 2008.

The rat Roscuro and his sailor companion arrive in the kingdom of Dor, famous for its soups, on the annual Royal Soup Day. Roscuro accidentally falls into the queen's soup, and the shock kills her. The grieving king bans soup and outlaws rats, and Dor falls into a gray gloom; the royal chef, Andre, loses his magical companion, Boldo, a spirit made of vegetables, and Princess Pea mourns her mother. Abandoned by his sailor, Roscuro takes refuge in the dungeon below, ruled by the cruel rat leader Botticelli.

In a mouse community hidden in the castle, Despereaux Tilling is born with oversized ears and an unusual lack of fear. Rather than chewing books, he reads them. When he befriends Princess Pea, breaking mouse law by speaking to a human, his family turns him over to the mouse council, which banishes him to the dungeon. There he is thrown into the rats' arena with a cat, until Roscuro saves him by claiming him as food. The two become friends, as Despereaux tells him stories of the princess. When Roscuro tries to apologize to Pea for her mother's death and is rejected, he vows revenge and persuades Mig, a simple-minded servant girl who dreams of being a princess, to help him kidnap Pea, then betrays Mig and takes the princess to the rats.

Despereaux seeks help, but the king is too depressed to listen and the mice fear him as a ghost. Andre, inspired by the sound of the castle bell, defies the ban and begins making soup again, bringing back Boldo, who sacrifices himself to help Despereaux reach the arena. As the rats prepare to devour Pea, Roscuro realizes Pea is sorry for her harshness and regrets his betrayal. Sunlight breaking through the clouds blinds the rats, and Roscuro helps defeat Botticelli, who is cornered by the cat. The king lifts his bans, and Despereaux sets out to see the world.

The film received mixed reviews, with critics praising its striking visuals but finding its story familiar; Rotten Tomatoes reported 57% approval and Metacritic a score of 53.

documents.title: The Day the Earth Stood Still
documents.original_title: The Day the Earth Stood Still
documents.tagline: 12.12.08 is the Day the Earth Stood Still
documents.overview: A representative of an alien race that went through drastic evolution to survive its own climate change, Klaatu comes to Earth to assess whether humanity can prevent the environmental damage they have inflicted on their own planet. When barred from speaking to the United Nations, he decides humankind shall be exterminated so the planet can survive.
documents.plot:
The Day the Earth Stood Still is a 2008 American science fiction film directed by Scott Derrickson from a screenplay by David Scarpa, remaking the 1951 film of the same name, which was based on the 1940 short story "Farewell to the Master". This version replaces the original's Cold War fear of nuclear war with concern about humanity's damage to the environment. Keanu Reeves, who agreed because he saw the script as a reimagining, stars as the alien Klaatu and insisted that the line "Klaatu barada nikto" be included.

In 1928 a mountaineer in the Karakoram meets a glowing sphere and wakes with a scar on his hand. In the present day, an object speeding toward Earth turns out to be a giant spherical ship that lands in Central Park. Astrobiologist Helen Benson, recruited by NASA official Michael Granier, watches as the emerging alien is shot and a towering robot disables the troops until the wounded being commands it to stop. In the laboratory, the alien sheds its placenta-like suit and becomes Klaatu, resembling the 1928 climber. He tells Secretary of Defense Regina Jackson that an alliance of planetary civilizations has sent him to save Earth from humanity, then escapes interrogation and turns to Helen and her stepson, Jacob.

As smaller spheres collect animal species around the world, Klaatu meets Mr. Wu, an alien living on Earth who considers humans destructive but has come to love them. Helen takes Klaatu to Nobel laureate Professor Barnhardt, who argues that humanity, like Klaatu's own people, can change when faced with extinction. Meanwhile the captured robot, nicknamed GORT, dissolves into a swarm of self-replicating insect-like machines that devour every man-made object in their path. At the grave of Jacob's father, Klaatu witnesses the boy's grief and the love between him and Helen and decides to stop the swarm. He walks through it to touch the sphere, sacrificing himself, and the swarm halts, though all electronics on Earth shut down as the sphere departs.

Jennifer Connelly plays Helen, Jaden Smith plays Jacob, Kathy Bates plays Jackson, John Cleese plays Barnhardt and Jon Hamm plays Granier. Critics were largely negative, with 21% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but the film opened at number one in North America and grossed $233.1 million worldwide on an $80 million budget. Smith won a Saturn Award for his performance.

documents.title: Yes Man
documents.tagline: One Word Can Change Everything.
documents.overview: Carl Allen has stumbled across a way to shake free of post-divorce blues and a dead-end job: embrace life and say yes to everything.
documents.plot:
Yes Man is a 2008 American comedy film directed by Nicholas Stoller and starring Jim Carrey, Zooey Deschanel, and Bradley Cooper.

The movie begins with Carl Allen (Jim Carrey), a recently divorced man who feels lost and uncertain about his life. He has been stuck in a rut, feeling unfulfilled and disconnected from the world around him. On his 39th birthday, he is given an unusual gift by his brother: a "yes" card that forces him to say "yes" to every opportunity that comes his way.

At first, Carl is hesitant and struggles with the idea of committing to everything that's presented to him. However, as time passes, he starts to realize the benefits of saying "yes" to new experiences and people. He begins to reconnect with old friends, try new hobbies, and even start dating again.

One of the people Carl meets through his newfound enthusiasm is Allison (Zooey Deschanel), a quirky and charming woman who becomes his love interest. As they spend more time together, Carl finds himself falling for her, but he's also faced with challenges from his brother, who wants him to say "no" to everything.

As the story unfolds, Carl faces various obstacles and learns valuable lessons about taking risks, being open-minded, and embracing uncertainty. He says "yes" to a job offer that turns out to be a disaster, joins a group of eccentric friends who become like a surrogate family to him, and even takes up skydiving.

Throughout the movie, Jim Carrey's performance is both hilarious and heartwarming as he brings Carl's transformation from a hesitant to an enthusiastic "yes" man. The supporting cast, including Bradley Cooper and Rhys Ifans, add to the humor and charm of the film.

As the story reaches its climax, Carl must confront his brother and figure out what it truly means to say "yes" to life. In the end, he learns that embracing uncertainty and taking risks can lead to personal growth, new relationships, and a sense of fulfillment.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Carl having found a new sense of purpose and happiness. He's still got his "yes" card, but now he knows how to use it wisely. The film is a lighthearted and entertaining exploration of the importance of taking chances and living life to the fullest.

Overall, Yes Man is a delightful comedy that will leave you smiling and feeling inspired to take a few risks in your own life.

documents.title: Bedtime Stories
documents.tagline: Whatever they dream up... he has to survive.
documents.overview: Skeeter Bronson is a down-on-his-luck guy who's always telling bedtime stories to his niece and nephew. But his life is turned upside down when the fantastical stories he makes up for entertainment inexplicably turn into reality. Can a bewildered Skeeter manage his own unruly fantasies now that the outrageous characters and situations from his mind have morphed into actual people and events?
documents.plot:
Bedtime Stories is a 2008 American fantasy comedy film directed by Adam Shankman and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie stars Adam Sandler, Keri Russell, and Guy Pearce.

The story begins with Skeeter Bronson (Adam Sandler), a struggling hotel handyman who dreams of becoming an author. He lives in a small apartment with his wife, Maggie (Keri Russell), and their two children, Max (Taylor Lautner) and Sugar (Bailee Madison). Despite his creative ambitions, Skeeter's life is mundane and unfulfilling.

One night, while working at the hotel, Skeeter stumbles upon an old book of bedtime stories that belonged to a former guest. As he reads through the book, he discovers that the stories come to life when no one is looking. The characters from the stories begin to invade his reality, causing chaos and confusion in his daily life.

Skeeter's world becomes increasingly surreal as the characters from the stories start to interact with him and his family. He must navigate this new reality while trying to keep his sanity intact. Meanwhile, Maggie starts to notice strange occurrences around the house, which puts a strain on their relationship.

As Skeeter tries to find a way to stop the characters from invading his life, he also begins to write his own bedtime stories. However, his writing skills are not as magical as those of the book's author, and his stories start to take on a life of their own.

The plot thickens when Skeeter discovers that the book is actually a magical portal created by a former guest who was a writer himself. The guest had used the book to bring his characters to life, but he had also left behind a curse that would destroy the world if the stories were not completed.

Skeeter realizes that he must finish writing the stories and complete the curse in order to save the world. With the help of his family and some unexpected allies, Skeeter embarks on a journey to write the final story and restore balance to his reality.

In the end, Skeeter completes the story, and the characters from the book return to their own world. The movie ends with Skeeter's family returning to normal life, but not before Skeeter realizes that he has found his true calling as an author.

Throughout the movie, Adam Sandler delivers a comedic performance as Skeeter Bronson, bringing humor and heart to the story. The film's blend of fantasy and comedy makes it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Around the World in 80 Days
documents.tagline: Let your imagination soar.
documents.overview: A bet pits a British inventor, a Chinese thief and a French artist on a worldwide adventure that they can circle the globe in 80 days.
documents.plot:
Around the World in 80 Days is a 2004 action adventure comedy directed by Frank Coraci from a script by David Titcher, David Benullo and David Goldstein. Loosely based on Jules Verne's 1873 novel, it deliberately departs from the book for comic effect and includes many anachronisms. It stars Jackie Chan as Passepartout, Steve Coogan as Phileas Fogg, Cécile de France as Monique La Roche and Jim Broadbent as Lord Kelvin, with Ewen Bremner, Ian McNeice and cameo appearances by Arnold Schwarzenegger, Owen Wilson, Luke Wilson and others.

In Victorian London, a Chinese thief named Lau Xing steals a jade Buddha from the Bank of England. The statue had been given to Lord Kelvin, head of the Royal Academy of Science, by the Black Scorpions, a violent criminal group, in exchange for his support. Hiding from the police, Lau Xing takes refuge in the home of the eccentric inventor Phileas Fogg and, calling himself Passepartout, becomes his valet and helps test his inventions. When Fogg claims that it is possible to travel around the world in eighty days, the arrogant Kelvin, who despises innovation, wagers that if Fogg succeeds he will give up his position, but if he fails Fogg must abandon science forever.

Passepartout sees the journey as a way to return the Buddha to his village in China. Pursued by agents sent by Kelvin, Fogg and Passepartout travel to Paris, where they are joined by Monique, an aspiring impressionist painter. Their adventures take them by balloon, train and ship through Turkey, where a vain prince wants Monique for his harem, India and China, where Fogg learns Passepartout's true identity and helps defend his village. Crossing the Pacific to America, they meet the Wright brothers before racing back to London. Despite Kelvin's attempts to sabotage the journey, the travelers fight to arrive in time to win the bet and expose the corrupt lord.

The film emphasizes Chan's martial arts comedy over Verne's original story, transforming Passepartout into the central character.

Around the World in 80 Days premiered at the El Capitan Theatre on 13 June 2004 and opened in the United States three days later. It was a box-office bomb, earning about 72.6 million dollars worldwide against a 110 million dollar budget. Reviews were mixed to negative, with 32 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49.

documents.title: Son of the Mask
documents.tagline: Who's next?
documents.overview: Tim Avery, an aspiring cartoonist, finds himself in a predicament when his dog stumbles upon the mask of Loki. Then after conceiving an infant son "born of the mask", he discovers just how looney child raising can be.
documents.plot:
Son of the Mask is a 2005 American fantasy comedy film directed by Jay Roach and starring Jamie Kennedy, Ben Affleck, and Christina Applegate. The movie is a sequel to the 1994 film The Mask.

The story begins with Stanley Ipkiss (Jamie Kennedy), a shy and awkward bank clerk who has been living with the spirit of Loki, the Norse god of mischief, in a magical mask. After a series of events, including a confrontation with his boss and a failed attempt to win back his girlfriend, Tina Carlyle (Christina Applegate), Stanley is forced to return the mask to its rightful owner.

However, things take a turn when Stanley discovers that he has a son, Timmy (Jamie Kennedy's younger brother), who possesses the same magical abilities as his father. The two of them soon find themselves on a wild adventure, with Loki's spirit trying to manipulate Timmy into using the mask for evil purposes.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Timmy is not just a ordinary child, but rather a vessel for Loki's spirit. The two of them form an unlikely bond, with Loki trying to teach Timmy how to use his powers for good and Timmy struggling to control his newfound abilities.

Meanwhile, Stanley is trying to navigate his new role as a single father and figure out how to help his son deal with the consequences of having a magical mask. Along the way, he must confront his own insecurities and learn to trust himself and his son.

As the plot thickens, Timmy becomes increasingly entangled in Loki's plans, leading to a series of hilarious and action-packed misadventures. In the end, Stanley and Timmy must work together to defeat Loki and save the city from chaos.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, including Jamie Kennedy's signature awkwardness and Ben Affleck's over-the-top performance as a villainous character. The film also features a number of clever references to Norse mythology and pop culture.

Overall, Son of the Mask is a lighthearted and entertaining film that explores themes of family, identity, and self-discovery. While it may not be as groundbreaking as its predecessor, it offers plenty of laughs and excitement for fans of the original movie.

documents.title: High Tension
documents.tagline: Hearts will bleed.
documents.overview: Best friends Marie and Alexia decide to spend a quiet weekend at Alexia's parents' secluded farmhouse. But on the night of their arrival, the girls' idyllic getaway turns into an endless night of horror.
documents.plot:
High Tension is a 2003 French thriller film directed by Alexandre Aja. The movie follows two young women, Marie (Maïwenn) and Alex (Cécile de France), who are on their way to meet up with their friends at a remote cabin in the woods for a weekend getaway.

The main themes of High Tension include:

1. **Friendship and Betrayal**: The film explores the complexities of female friendships, particularly between Marie and Alex. As they spend more time together, their relationship is put to the test by secrets, lies, and misunderstandings.
2. **Isolation and Vulnerability**: The remote cabin setting serves as a metaphor for the characters' emotional isolation. As they become trapped in the woods, they are forced to confront their deepest fears and vulnerabilities.
3. **Violence and Trauma**: High Tension is known for its graphic and intense violence, which serves as a catalyst for the characters' emotional breakdowns. The film explores the long-term effects of trauma on individuals and relationships.
4. **Female Empowerment and Agency**: Through Marie's character, the film critiques traditional feminine roles and expectations. As she takes charge and asserts her independence, she begins to break free from societal constraints.

The plot development is marked by a series of escalating events, including a car accident, a mysterious stranger, and a violent confrontation that ultimately leads to a shocking twist ending.

Overall, High Tension is a tense (pun intended) and thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of female relationships, vulnerability, and empowerment.

documents.title: A Walk to Remember
documents.tagline: It all comes down to who's by your side.
documents.overview: When the popular, restless Landon Carter is forced to participate in the school drama production he falls in love with Jamie Sullivan, the daughter of the town's minister. Jamie has a "to-do" list for her life and also a very big secret she must keep from Landon.
documents.plot:
A Walk to Remember is a 2002 American romantic drama film directed by Adam Shankman, based on the novel of the same name by Nicholas Sparks.

The movie begins with Landon Carter (played by Shane West), a popular high school student who has just been sentenced to community service for hazing his classmate. During his service, he meets Jamie Sullivan (played by Mandy Moore), a shy and devout Christian girl who is diagnosed with leukemia. Despite their initial differences, the two begin to form a bond as they spend more time together.

As Landon gets to know Jamie, he learns about her strong faith and values, which challenge his own worldview. He also begins to see Jamie in a different light, beyond her illness, and develops feelings for her. However, their social differences and the fact that Jamie is terminally ill make their relationship complicated.

Throughout the film, Landon and Jamie's friendship blossoms into romance, but they face numerous obstacles, including Jamie's declining health and the disapproval of some of Landon's friends. As Jamie's condition worsens, Landon becomes her primary caregiver, and he learns to appreciate the beauty of life and the importance of living in the present.

As the story unfolds, Landon and Jamie's relationship deepens, and they face the reality of their mortality. The film takes a poignant turn when Jamie reveals that she has been praying for Landon to find faith, and that she wants him to be happy even if she is not around anymore.

The movie's climax is both heart-wrenching and uplifting as Landon comes to terms with his own spirituality and the meaning of life. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Landon finding solace in his newfound faith and the memories he shared with Jamie.

Throughout the film, the chemistry between Shane West and Mandy Moore is undeniable, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. The supporting cast, including Peter Coyote as Landon's father and Daryl Hannah as Jamie's mother, adds to the emotional resonance of the story.

Overall, A Walk to Remember is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of love, faith, and mortality with sensitivity and authenticity. The movie's poignant portrayal of a young couple's relationship has resonated with audiences worldwide, making it a timeless classic in the world of romantic dramas.

documents.title: Cries and Whispers
documents.tagline: Four women dressed in white in a mansion painted red... haunted by whispers and cries.
documents.overview: As Agnes slowly dies of cancer, her sisters are so deeply immersed in their own psychic pains that they can't offer her the support she needs. Maria is wracked with guilt at her husband's attempted suicide, caused by his discovery of her extramarital affair. The self-loathing, suicidal Karin seems to regard her sister with revulsion. Only Anna, the deeply religious maid who lost her young child, seems able to offer Agnes solace and empathy.
documents.plot:
Cries and Whispers is a poignant and powerful drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, grief, and the devastating effects of unrequited love. The film delves into the lives of four sisters, each struggling with their own unique demons, as they navigate the dark and troubled world of 19th-century Sweden.

At its core, Cries and Whispers is a deeply emotional and introspective exploration of the human experience, one that probes the depths of sorrow, longing, and the fragility of the human spirit. The film's narrative is characterized by a sense of claustrophobia and isolation, as each sister becomes increasingly entangled in her own personal hell.

Through the characters' struggles, the film sheds light on the oppressive nature of patriarchal society, where women are expected to conform to societal norms and suppress their desires and emotions. The sisters' experiences serve as a powerful critique of the restrictive roles imposed upon them, highlighting the devastating consequences of being trapped in a world that does not acknowledge or validate their feelings.

The film's use of stark, monochromatic cinematography adds to its sense of foreboding and despair, creating a haunting atmosphere that perfectly captures the mood of the characters. The result is a cinematic experience that is both deeply unsettling and profoundly moving, one that lingers long after the credits roll.

Ultimately, Cries and Whispers is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that confronts the darkest aspects of existence with unflinching honesty and emotional depth.

documents.title: Dragon Wars: D-War
documents.tagline: They've made our world their battleground.
documents.overview: Based on the Korean legend, unknown creatures will return and devastate the planet. Reporter Ethan Kendrick is called in to investigate the matter.
documents.plot:
D-War, released in North America as Dragon Wars: D-War, is a 2007 fantasy monster film written and directed by the South Korean filmmaker Shim Hyung-rae. Inspired by Korean legends of the Imugi, giant serpents that may become dragons, it stars Jason Behr, Amanda Brooks, Robert Forster, Craig Robinson, Aimee Garcia and Elizabeth Peña. A South Korean and American co-production made by a largely Korean crew in the United States, it was at the time the most expensive South Korean film ever made.

As a boy in Los Angeles, Ethan Kendrick is told by a mysterious antiques dealer, Jack, that he is the reincarnation of Haram, a young warrior who five hundred years ago was charged with protecting the Yuh Yi Joo, a girl born with the power to transform a chosen Imugi into a celestial dragon. In that earlier life, Haram and the girl chose to die together rather than let her be taken by Buraki, an evil Imugi seeking the power for itself. Jack gives Ethan Haram's medallion and tells him that the reborn Yuh Yi Joo, Sarah Daniels, will appear in Los Angeles.

Fifteen years later, Ethan is a television journalist when a series of strange events signals Buraki's return. He tracks down Sarah, now a young woman troubled by a mysterious mark on her shoulder, and saves her from an attack, explaining her destiny. As the two flee, they gradually recover memories of their past lives. Buraki, a gigantic serpent, rampages through the city, while its Atrox Army of armoured warriors, raptor-like beasts, winged dragons called Bulcos and huge rocket-bearing reptiles battles the police and the US Army, overwhelming the human forces.

Ethan and Sarah are captured by the Bulcos and carried to a fortress in a dark desert landscape. As Buraki moves to devour Sarah, Ethan's medallion unleashes a force that destroys the Atrox Army. The good Imugi, destined to receive Sarah's power, emerges to fight Buraki and appears to be beaten, but Sarah offers herself to it instead, and it transforms into a celestial dragon that destroys Buraki in flames. Sarah's spirit promises Ethan that they will meet again before the dragon carries her into the heavens, and Jack reappears to tell Ethan they have witnessed a great honour.

A major hit in South Korea, the film grossed over 44 million dollars there, though critics were harsh, giving it 28% approval on Rotten Tomatoes while acknowledging its special effects.

documents.title: The Madagascar Penguins in a Christmas Caper
documents.original_title: The Madagascar Penguins in a Christmas Caper
documents.overview: During the holiday season, when the animals of the Central Park Zoo are preparing for Christmas, Private, the youngest of the penguins notices that the Polar Bear is all alone. Assured that nobody should have to spend Christmas alone, Private goes into the city for some last-minute Christmas shopping. Along the way, he gets stuffed into a stocking
documents.plot:
The Madagascar Penguins in a Christmas Caper is a 2005 American animated Christmas comedy short produced by DreamWorks Animation and Pacific Data Images. Directed by Gary Trousdale and written by Michael Lachance, the 12-minute short features the voices of Tom McGrath as Skipper, Chris Miller as Kowalski, Christopher Knights as Private, John DiMaggio, Elisa Gabrielli and Bill Fagerbakke. Set before the events of the first Madagascar film, it is a spin-off centered on the four commando penguins who live in New York's Central Park Zoo and behave like a covert military unit. It was originally shown in cinemas with the feature Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit.

On Christmas Eve at the Central Park Zoo, Private, the youngest and most innocent member of the penguin team, surveys the zoo through a periscope disguised as a snowman. While most of the animals are enjoying the holiday, he notices that Ted, a polar bear, is spending Christmas alone. Private decides to find Ted a present to cheer him up, although his teammates Skipper, Kowalski and Rico show little interest in the idea.

Private sneaks out of the zoo and wanders the streets of Manhattan in search of a gift, but he is snatched by Nana, a cantankerous old woman, who mistakes him for a squeaky chew toy and takes him home for her vicious dog, Mr. Chew. When the other penguins realize Private is missing, they launch a rescue mission into Nana's apartment building, using their characteristic military tactics and gadgets. A chaotic battle with Mr. Chew follows, all unnoticed by Nana, who is absorbed in a televised football game. After rescuing Private, the team returns to the zoo, where their good deed for Ted takes an unexpected turn, and the penguins learn something about the holiday spirit.

The short was popular with audiences and helped establish the penguins as breakout characters from Madagascar. Nana and the penguins later reappeared in other parts of the franchise, and the characters went on to star in the television series The Penguins of Madagascar (2008–2015) and the feature film Penguins of Madagascar (2014). The short was later included on home video releases of the Madagascar films.

documents.title: Return to Paradise
documents.tagline: Give up three years of their lives or give up the life of their friend. They have eight days to decide.
documents.overview: Lewis, Sheriff and Tony are three friends vacationing in Malaysia. Sheriff and Tony eventually leave to pursue careers in New York, but Lewis stays behind to work with orangutans. Two years later, Sheriff and Tony learn that, because of their past actions, Lewis has been arrested for drug possession. With Lewis facing a death sentence, the friends are left with a difficult decision: return to Malaysia and split Lewis' sentence, or let him die.
documents.plot:
Return to Paradise is a 1998 American drama film directed by Joseph Ruben and starring Val Kilmer, Gena Rowlands, and Michelle Forbes.

The movie revolves around the story of an American doctor who travels to India in search of his missing sister. As he delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers dark secrets about his family's past and the true nature of his sister's disappearance.

One of the main themes of Return to Paradise is the exploration of identity and belonging. The protagonist's journey is a metaphor for finding one's place in the world and understanding where one comes from. His experiences in India force him to confront his own sense of self and question the values and traditions that have shaped his life.

Another significant theme in the movie is the struggle with morality and the complexities of human nature. The protagonist's investigation into his sister's disappearance leads him to encounter characters who embody different aspects of human morality, from the ruthless and cunning to the compassionate and selfless. This exploration raises questions about the nature of right and wrong and whether individuals can be redeemed or if they are forever trapped by their past actions.

The film also touches on the theme of colonialism and its legacy. The protagonist's experiences in India serve as a commentary on the historical and cultural impact of Western influence on non-Western societies, highlighting both the benefits and drawbacks of globalization.

Ultimately, Return to Paradise is a thought-provoking drama that explores complex themes and moral ambiguities, leaving audiences to ponder the complexities of human nature and the consequences of our choices.

documents.title: Urban Legends: Bloody Mary
documents.tagline: Turn Off The Light And See What Happens.
documents.overview: On a prom-night dare, a trio of high school friends chant an incantation, unleashing an evil spirit from the past with deadly consequences.
documents.plot:
Urban Legends: Bloody Mary is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology and the power of suggestion. The movie revolves around a group of teenagers who, while exploring an abandoned house, inadvertently awaken the vengeful spirit of Bloody Mary.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true terror lies not in the supernatural entity itself, but in the fear and vulnerability that it exploits. The film expertly weaves together themes of teenage angst, peer pressure, and the devastating consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control.

The movie also touches on the idea of the "power of suggestion," highlighting how a simple phrase or ritual can be twisted into a malevolent force that preys on the deepest fears of those who dare to confront it. This theme is skillfully intertwined with the notion of identity and self-discovery, as the characters are forced to confront their own dark pasts and the true nature of their relationships with one another.

Ultimately, Urban Legends: Bloody Mary presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of meddling with forces that are beyond human understanding, and the devastating consequences that can result when fear and curiosity are allowed to get the better of us.

documents.title: Starship Troopers 2: Hero of the Federation
documents.original_title: Starship Troopers 2: Hero of the Federation
documents.tagline: They're Coming Back to Wipe Us Out!
documents.overview: In the sequel to Paul Verhoeven's loved/reviled sci-fi film, a group of troopers taking refuge in an abandoned outpost after fighting alien bugs, failing to realize that more danger lays in wait.
documents.plot:
Starship Troopers 2: Hero of the Federation is a science fiction film directed by Phil Tippett, and it serves as a sequel to the 1997 film Starship Troopers. The movie takes place after the events of the first film and follows Johnny Rico (played by Casper Van Dien) as he becomes the commander of the Mobile Infantry's elite unit.

The main themes of Starship Troopers 2: Hero of the Federation include:

1. Leadership and Responsibility: As Johnny Rico assumes command, he must navigate the complexities of leadership and make difficult decisions that impact the lives of his soldiers.
2. Loyalty and Sacrifice: The film explores the bonds of loyalty between Rico and his fellow soldiers, as well as the sacrifices they must make to protect humanity from the Bug threat.
3. War and its Consequences: Starship Troopers 2 delves into the psychological effects of war on individuals and society, highlighting the moral dilemmas that come with fighting an alien invasion.
4. Power Struggles and Corruption: The movie introduces a new villain, General Hanly (played by Neil Patrick Harris), who seeks to overthrow the Federation's government and take control for himself.

The plot development revolves around Rico's efforts to stop Hanly's coup and save humanity from destruction. Along the way, he must confront his own demons and make tough choices that will determine the fate of the Federation.

As for the ending, it sets the stage for a potential third installment in the series, leaving room for further exploration of the Starship Troopers universe.

documents.title: The Men Who Stare at Goats
documents.original_title: The Men Who Stare at Goats
documents.tagline: No goats. No glory.
documents.overview: A reporter in Iraq might just have the story of a lifetime when he meets Lyn Cassady, a guy who claims to be a former member of the U.S. Army's New Earth Army, a unit that employs paranormal powers in their missions.
documents.plot:
The Men Who Stare at Goats is a 2009 film that delves into the world of military psychology and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. At its core, the movie explores the theme of the human psyche's capacity for both good and evil. The story follows Lyn Cassady, a charismatic con artist who becomes embroiled in a government experiment to develop psychic warfare capabilities.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the film is not just about the military's attempts to harness supernatural abilities but also about the darker aspects of human nature. The movie delves into the concept of the "warrior archetype," where individuals are driven by a primal urge for violence and control. This theme is expertly woven throughout the story, as characters like Lyn Cassady and Bob Wilton grapple with their own demons and the moral implications of their actions.

The film also touches on the idea of the power of storytelling and the manipulation of reality. The military's use of propaganda and disinformation serves as a metaphor for the ways in which individuals can shape their perceptions of the world to suit their own purposes. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Lyn Cassady, who uses his charisma and cunning to navigate the complexities of the government experiment.

Ultimately, The Men Who Stare at Goats is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of our nature and the ways in which we can be manipulated by those in power.

documents.title: Fantastic Mr. Fox
documents.tagline: Dig the life fantastic!
documents.overview: The Fantastic Mr. Fox bored with his current life, plans a heist against the three local farmers. The farmers, tired of sharing their chickens with the sly fox, seek revenge against him and his family.
documents.plot:
Fantastic Mr. Fox is a 2009 stop-motion animated adventure comedy directed by Wes Anderson, who wrote the screenplay with Noah Baumbach from Roald Dahl's 1970 novel. George Clooney voices Mr. Fox, with Meryl Streep, Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray, Willem Dafoe and Owen Wilson in the cast.

Caught in a trap while raiding a squab farm, Mr. Fox learns from his wife, Felicity, that she is pregnant and promises to find a safer line of work. Twelve fox-years later the couple and their son, Ash, live in a hole. Ignoring the warnings of his lawyer, Clive Badger, Mr. Fox moves the family into a tree near the operations of three notorious farmers, Walt Boggis, Nate Bunce and Frank Bean. Felicity's nephew Kristofferson comes to stay while his father is treated for double pneumonia. Missing his old life, Mr. Fox and his opossum friend Kylie steal poultry and cider from the three farms. The enraged farmers shoot off his tail and destroy his home, driving the Foxes underground, where they meet Badger and other animals made homeless by the farmers.

As the hungry animals start blaming the Foxes, Mr. Fox leads them in digging tunnels to all three farms and stealing the farmers' goods. In response the farmers and the fire chief flood the tunnels with Bean's cider, washing the animals into the sewers. Ash and Kristofferson sneak back to recover the tail, and Kristofferson is captured by Bean's wife. Bean's violent security guard, Rat, attacks Ash and Felicity, and after a fight with Mr. Fox he is electrocuted, revealing before he dies that Kristofferson is held in the attic of Bean Annex. Mr. Fox offers to surrender if the farmers free his nephew, and when they prepare an ambush, the animals counterattack, allowing Mr. Fox, Ash and Kylie to slip into the annex. Ash frees Kristofferson and impresses everyone by releasing a rabid beagle under fire. The animals settle into new homes in the sewers and soon raid a supermarket owned by the farmers, where Felicity announces another pregnancy.

Developed from 2004 at Revolution Studios with Henry Selick, the project moved to 20th Century Fox, and production began in 2007 at 3 Mills Studios in London. It opened the 53rd BFI London Film Festival in October 2009. Critics acclaimed its humor, animation and direction, with 93% on Rotten Tomatoes and 83 on Metacritic, but it earned only about $46.2 million against a $40 million budget. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score.

documents.title: The Ides of March
documents.tagline: Ambition seduces. Power corrupts.
documents.overview: Dirty tricks stand to soil an ambitious young press spokesman's idealism in a cutthroat presidential campaign where 'victory' is relative.
documents.plot:
The Ides of March is a 2011 American political drama directed by George Clooney from a screenplay by Clooney, Grant Heslov and Beau Willimon, adapted from Willimon's 2008 play Farragut North. It stars Ryan Gosling as press secretary Stephen Meyers and Clooney as Governor Mike Morris, with Philip Seymour Hoffman as campaign manager Paul Zara, Paul Giamatti as rival campaign manager Tom Duffy, Marisa Tomei as New York Times reporter Ida Horowicz, Jeffrey Wright as Senator Franklin Thompson and Evan Rachel Wood as the intern Molly Stearns.

Stephen Meyers is a gifted young political operative serving as junior campaign manager for Mike Morris, the charismatic Democratic governor of Pennsylvania, who is competing in the presidential primaries. Unlike his cynical boss Paul Zara, Stephen genuinely believes in Morris and his ideals. Days before the crucial Ohio primary, the campaign is pursuing the endorsement of North Carolina senator Franklin Thompson, whose delegates could secure the nomination.

Stephen agrees to a secret meeting with Tom Duffy, the campaign manager of Morris's rival Ted Pullman, who tries to recruit him and reveals that Pullman has won over Thompson by promising him a cabinet post. Stephen urges Morris to make a similar deal, but the governor refuses on principle. Meanwhile, Stephen begins an affair with Molly Stearns, a campaign intern and the daughter of the chairman of the Democratic National Committee, and stumbles upon a secret that could destroy Morris's candidacy. When news of his meeting with Duffy leaks, Stephen finds himself betrayed by people he trusted, and he must decide how far he is willing to go, and how much of his idealism he is willing to sacrifice, to save his career.

The film examines the compromises and moral corruption at the heart of electoral politics, tracing the transformation of an idealist into a ruthless player.

The Ides of March opened the 68th Venice International Film Festival and was released in theaters on October 7, 2011, grossing about 76 million dollars worldwide. It received positive reviews, with 84 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised it as supremely well-acted drama, and a Metacritic score of 67. Clooney, Heslov and Willimon were nominated for the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay.

documents.title: Our Brand Is Crisis
documents.tagline: May the best campaign win.
documents.overview: Based on the documentary "Our Brand Is Crisis", this feature focuses on the use of American political campaign strategies in South America.
documents.plot:
Our Brand Is Crisis is a 2015 American comedy-drama directed by David Gordon Green, written by Peter Straughan and produced by George Clooney and Grant Heslov. Inspired by Rachel Boynton's 2005 documentary of the same name, it offers a fictionalised account of the role played by the American consultancy Greenberg Carville Shrum in Bolivia's 2002 presidential election. Sandra Bullock leads a cast that includes Billy Bob Thornton, Anthony Mackie, Zoe Kazan and Scoot McNairy.

The former president Pedro Castillo, seeking to regain office, hires a team of American political consultants, who bring in "Calamity" Jane Bodine, a burned-out veteran of American campaigns, to run his struggling operation. Her rival on the opposing side is her old nemesis Pat Candy, another American strategist. Bolivia is tense, with the indigenous majority, largely excluded from real political power, protesting for constitutional reform.

Knowing little of the country, the Americans are persuaded by Bodine to make up for their candidate's weaknesses with negative campaigning. Castillo at first refuses to allow it, until Bodine secretly circulates a flyer accusing him of an old affair and blames it on his opponents. From then on the campaign's message is that Bolivia faces a crisis, frightening voters into choosing the cold but familiar Castillo over younger rivals. They even publish photographs of a rival with the Nazi war criminal Klaus Barbie in the background.

When protesters halt Castillo's bus to oppose the International Monetary Fund, he promises not to bring in the IMF without a referendum, deeply impressing Eduardo, a young volunteer who has idolised him since childhood, although Eduardo's brothers remain sceptical. In the final stretch, Bodine tricks Candy into feeding his candidate a quotation that turns out to come from Joseph Goebbels.

Castillo wins narrowly and immediately invites the IMF in, breaking his word. Eduardo confronts Bodine, who insists she is not responsible for what Castillo does, and he joins his brothers at a protest that turns into a riot. On the way to the airport, as her colleagues discuss new jobs abroad, Bodine realises she has helped put a liar in office, stops the car and goes to join the protesters.

Premiering at the 2015 Toronto International Film Festival, the film was a box-office disappointment, grossing $8.6 million against a $28 million budget, and earned 36% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though Bullock's performance was widely praised.

documents.title: The Ring Two
documents.tagline: The dead don't sleep.
documents.overview: Rachel Keller must prevent evil Samara from taking possession of her son's soul.
documents.plot:
The Ring Two is a 2005 supernatural horror film directed by Hideo Nakata and written by Michael Robert Johnson. It is the sequel to the 2002 remake of the Japanese horror film Ringu, starring Naomi Watts.

The story begins with Samara Morgan (Naomi Watts), the vengeful spirit from the first film, who has been trapped in a well for over 50 years. However, she manages to escape and begins to wreak havoc on the world once again.

The main protagonist of the film is Rachel Keller (Brynn Thayer), a young journalist who discovers that Samara's curse can be broken by finding her mother's diary. Rachel sets out to find the diary, which leads her to a mysterious woman named Anna Morgan (Amber Valletta), who claims to be Samara's mother.

As Rachel delves deeper into the mystery of Samara's past, she discovers that Anna was a former actress who became pregnant with Samara after being seduced by a wealthy and powerful man. The baby, Samara, was born with a rare genetic disorder that made her extremely intelligent and vengeful.

Anna, realizing that she had created a monster, tries to kill Samara as an infant, but the child survives and grows up to become the vengeful spirit that haunts Rachel in the present day. Anna's plan is to use Rachel to find the diary and break the curse, which would allow her to finally be at peace.

As the story unfolds, Rachel becomes increasingly entangled in a web of deceit and danger, as she tries to uncover the truth about Samara's past and the mysterious Anna Morgan. Along the way, she must confront her own dark past and the evil forces that are driving Samara's vengeful spirit.

The film builds towards a climactic showdown between Rachel and Anna, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Rachel manages to outsmart Anna and find the diary, which breaks the curse and allows Samara to finally rest in peace.

However, the film ends on a somewhat ambiguous note, leaving the audience wondering whether Samara's spirit has truly been laid to rest or if there is still more evil lurking in the shadows. Overall, The Ring Two is a thrilling and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of motherhood, guilt, and redemption.

documents.title: Legally Blonde 2: Red, White & Blonde
documents.tagline: Bigger. Bolder. Blonder.
documents.overview: Now a rising young lawyer, Elle Woods is about to make partner at her firm, but when she finds out her dog's relatives are being used as cosmetic test subjects, she heads to Washington D.C. to fight for animal rights.
documents.plot:
Legally Blonde 2: Red, White & Blonde is a comedy film that explores several themes, including:

1. **Feminism and Empowerment**: The movie follows Elle Woods' journey as she navigates the male-dominated world of politics and law. Through her experiences, the film highlights the importance of female empowerment and challenges societal norms that restrict women's opportunities.

2. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Elle delves deeper into the world of politics, she discovers a new sense of purpose and identity beyond her initial persona as a fashion merchandising major. This theme is reflected in her character development throughout the film.

3. **Social Commentary on Politics and Policy**: The movie tackles issues like animal rights, environmental policies, and women's rights, providing a satirical commentary on the politics of the time. Elle's character serves as a proxy for the audience, allowing viewers to engage with these complex topics in an entertaining way.

4. **Friendship and Loyalty**: The film showcases the strong bond between Elle and her friends, particularly Paulette (Jennifer Coolidge) and Emmett (Luke Wilson). Their relationships serve as a source of support and motivation for Elle throughout her journey.

5. **Personal Growth and Transformation**: Throughout the movie, Elle undergoes significant personal growth, transforming from an airheaded sorority girl to a confident, intelligent, and determined individual. This transformation is both humorous and inspiring, making the film an enjoyable watch.

Overall, Legally Blonde 2: Red, White & Blonde offers a lighthearted yet thought-provoking exploration of themes that continue to resonate with audiences today.

documents.title: Freaky Friday
documents.tagline: Mondays are manic. Wednesdays are wild. And Fridays are about to get a little freaky.
documents.overview: Mother and daughter bicker over everything -- what Anna wears, whom she likes and what she wants to do when she's older. In turn, Anna detests Tess's fiancé. When a magical fortune cookie switches their personalities, they each get a peek at how the other person feels, thinks and lives.
documents.plot:
Freaky Friday is a 2003 American fantasy comedy film directed by Mark S. Waters and produced by Robert L. Levy, with Walt Disney Pictures as the distributor.

The story revolves around Tess Coleman (played by Jamie Lee Curtis) and her daughter Anna (played by Lindsay Lohan), who are extremely close but also have their differences. The movie begins with Tess, a busy and stressed-out mother, trying to balance her career and family life. She is constantly at odds with her daughter, who is struggling to find her place in the world.

On the day of their annual Thanksgiving dinner, Tess and Anna get into an argument over a variety of issues, including school, boys, and personal space. As they are arguing, they suddenly switch bodies, waking up the next morning as each other's physical forms.

Initially, both Tess and Anna struggle to adjust to their new lives in each other's bodies. Tess, now in Anna's body, is shocked by her daughter's carefree and popular lifestyle, while Anna, now in Tess's body, is overwhelmed by her mother's responsibilities and stress.

As the day progresses, they begin to understand each other's perspectives and struggles. Tess learns about the challenges of being a teenager, including peer pressure, social media, and self-acceptance. Meanwhile, Anna gains insight into her mother's life as a working professional, dealing with office politics, work-life balance, and personal relationships.

Throughout the day, they make amends for their past arguments and learn to appreciate each other's strengths and weaknesses. They also develop a deeper understanding of themselves and their relationship.

As the day comes to an end, Tess and Anna wake up in their own bodies, but with a newfound appreciation for each other. The movie ends on a positive note, with the two women having a heart-to-heart conversation about their experiences and the lessons they learned from switching bodies.

The film features a strong performance from Jamie Lee Curtis and Lindsay Lohan, who bring depth and nuance to their characters. The movie's themes of mother-daughter relationships, self-discovery, and acceptance are timely and relatable, making it a beloved classic among both children and adults.

Overall, Freaky Friday is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores the complexities of family relationships and personal growth through the magical lens of body-swapping.

documents.title: Zack and Miri Make a Porno
documents.original_title: Zack and Miri Make a Porno
documents.tagline: What would you do to get out of debt?
documents.overview: Lifelong platonic friends Zack and Miri look to solve their respective cash-flow problems by making an adult film together. As the cameras roll, however, the duo begin to sense that they may have more feelings for each other than they previously thought.
documents.plot:
Zack and Miri Make a Porno is a 2008 American sex comedy film directed by Kevin Smith and starring Seth Rogen, James Franco, Katy Perry, and Elizabeth Banks. The movie follows the story of two friends, Zack (Seth Rogen) and Miri (Katy Perry), who are struggling to make ends meet in Pittsburgh.

Zack is a slacker who works as a delivery boy for a local pizza place, while Miri is a nude model who poses for art classes. Despite their financial struggles, they have a strong friendship and often hang out together, sharing their deepest secrets and desires.

One day, Zack comes up with an idea to make money by creating a pornographic film featuring himself and his friends. He convinces Miri to be the star of the film, and she agrees on one condition: that the movie will not feature any explicit sex scenes. However, things take a turn when they realize that they need to raise $5,000 to complete the film.

To achieve this goal, Zack and Miri come up with a series of outrageous and often humiliating stunts to get attention from women and raise money for their project. Along the way, they encounter a number of eccentric characters, including a seductive stripper named Delilah (Elizabeth Banks) who becomes a key player in their scheme.

As the story progresses, Zack and Miri's friendship is put to the test as they navigate their feelings for each other and confront their own insecurities. Meanwhile, their friends, including Dale (Jay Baruchel), Kevin (Craig Robinson), and Pedro (Danny McBride), provide comedic relief and support throughout the film.

Throughout the movie, Kevin Smith explores themes of friendship, love, and identity, often using humor to tackle deeper issues. The film's title, "Zack and Miri Make a Porno," is a play on the idea that even in the most unlikely of circumstances, two people can come together and create something beautiful.

Ultimately, Zack and Miri's plan succeeds, but not without its fair share of ups and downs. In the end, they learn to appreciate each other's strengths and weaknesses, and their friendship is stronger than ever. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Zack and Miri embracing their newfound love for each other and looking forward to a bright future together.

Overall, Zack and Miri Make a Porno is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the power of friendship. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and irreverent humor, it's no wonder this movie has become a cult classic among fans of Kevin Smith and adult comedy.

documents.title: Ginger Snaps 2: Unleashed
documents.tagline: It only dies if you do.
documents.overview: Brigitte has escaped the confines of Bailey Downs but she's not alone. Another werewolf is tailing her closely and her sister's specter haunts her. An overdose of Monkshood - the poison that is keeping her transformation at bay - leads to her being incarcerated in a rehabilitation clinic for drug addicts where her only friend is an eccentric young girl by the name of Ghost.
documents.plot:
Ginger Snaps 2: Unleashed is a horror-comedy film that explores the theme of female empowerment and self-discovery, particularly in the context of adolescence. The movie delves into the complexities of sisterly relationships, as Ginger's transformation into a werewolf forces her to confront her own identity and assert her independence from her family.

The film also touches on the idea of societal expectations and conformity, as Ginger struggles to balance her desire for individuality with the pressures of living up to traditional feminine norms. Through Ginger's journey, the movie critiques the notion that women must conform to certain standards of beauty and behavior, instead embracing a more authentic and empowered expression of femininity.

Furthermore, Unleashed explores themes of family dynamics and the challenges of sibling relationships, particularly in the context of Ginger's transformation into a werewolf. The film highlights the complexities of sisterly love and loyalty, as well as the difficulties of navigating complex family relationships during adolescence.

Overall, Ginger Snaps 2: Unleashed is a movie that celebrates female empowerment, self-discovery, and individuality, while also exploring the complexities of adolescent life and the challenges of growing up.

documents.title: Two Lovers
documents.tagline: Sometimes we leave everything to find ourselves.
documents.overview: A depressed man moves back in with his parents following a recent heartbreak and finds himself with two women.
documents.plot:
Two Lovers is a poignant and introspective drama that explores the complexities of love, loss, and longing. The film delves into the emotional turmoil of its protagonist, Leo, as he navigates his all-consuming passion for his childhood sweetheart, Tina.

At its core, Two Lovers is a movie about the fragility of human connection and the devastating consequences of unchecked emotions. Leo's obsessive love for Tina becomes an all-encompassing force that drives him to make choices that ultimately lead to his downfall. The film masterfully captures the intensity and desperation of first love, as well as its capacity to both uplift and destroy.

Through Leo's character, the movie sheds light on the destructive nature of unrequited love and the devastating consequences of allowing emotions to consume us. The film also explores themes of nostalgia, longing, and the bittersweet nature of memories that refuse to fade with time.

The cinematography and direction by Jim Mickle skillfully evoke a sense of melancholy and wistfulness, perfectly capturing the mood of Leo's emotional journey. Overall, Two Lovers is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that lingers long after the credits roll, leaving the viewer to ponder the complexities of love, loss, and the fragility of the human heart.

documents.title: D-Tox
documents.tagline: Survival is a Killer.
documents.overview: A disgraced FBI agent with a drinking problem joins nine other troubled law enforcement officers at an isolated detox clinic in the wilds of Wyoming. But the therapeutic sanctuary becomes a nightmarish hellhole when a major snowstorm cuts off the clinic from the outside world and enables a killer on the inside to get busy.
documents.plot:
D-Tox, also released as Eye See You, is a 2002 American action thriller film directed by Jim Gillespie and starring Sylvester Stallone, with a supporting cast that includes Tom Berenger, Charles S. Dutton, Polly Walker, Robert Patrick, Stephen Lang, Jeffrey Wright, Courtney B. Vance and Kris Kristofferson. Set largely in an isolated rehabilitation clinic for police officers, it follows an FBI agent who discovers that a serial killer of cops has followed him there.

In Seattle, FBI agent Jake Malloy is hunting a killer who targets police officers. After murdering Malloy's former partner, the killer telephones him from Malloy's own home, explaining that he is taking revenge for an earlier pursuit, and kills Malloy's girlfriend, Mary. The trail ends with what looks like the killer's suicide. Three months later Malloy has sunk into alcoholism, and after he attempts suicide, his friend and supervisor Chuck Hendricks enrolls him in a remote Wyoming clinic for troubled officers run by Doc Mitchell, a former cop and recovering alcoholic. Among the patients are a paranoid ex-SWAT officer, a cynical British policeman named Frank Slater, a religious homicide detective and an elderly Mountie, and Malloy grows close to the psychiatrist and nurse Jenny Munroe.

When a blizzard cuts the clinic off, patients begin dying in apparent suicides that Malloy suspects are murders. Doc is killed with an axe, a missing orderly falls under suspicion, and a group attempting to drive out for help crashes after hitting the orderly's body. The killer cuts the power and heating, and Malloy concludes that a murderer is posing as a cop and is likely Mary's killer. Briefly locked up by a staff member who suspects him, Malloy finds a matchbook from a Seattle restaurant frequented by police in Slater's cell, along with the stolen badges, identifying Slater as the killer. In the tunnels and snowfields around the clinic, Slater picks off more victims and pursues Jenny before Malloy kills him in a final fight, then leaves his engagement ring for Mary on a tree branch.

Announced at Universal in 1998, the film was shot in Washington, D.C. and Vancouver and completed in 1999, but poor test screenings led to reshoots, a new ending and a largely replaced John Powell score. After further delays, DEJ Productions gave it a limited U.S. release in 2002 as Eye See You. Critics were dismissive; Rotten Tomatoes reported 17% approval.

documents.title: Lost Souls
documents.tagline: They've had their 2000 years... now it's our turn.
documents.overview: A young woman who becomes aware of a conspiracy to enable the Devil to walk the earth in human form. To defeat the prophesy, she must convince a respected New York crime journalist, who is devoid of faith, that he is in fact the target of the conspiracy.
documents.plot:
Lost Souls is a supernatural drama film that delves into the complexities of human nature and the struggle between good and evil. The story revolves around a young woman named Aimee (played by Winona Ryder) who becomes embroiled in a world of vampires, exploring themes of desire, temptation, and the blurred lines between love and obsession.

As Aimee navigates this dark and seductive world, she must confront her own desires and the darkness within herself. The film raises questions about the nature of evil and whether it is inherent or learned, as well as the consequences of succumbing to one's baser instincts.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to confront their own moral ambiguities, leading to a exploration of the human condition and the struggle between light and darkness. The film ultimately presents a nuanced portrayal of the complexities of human nature, suggesting that even the most well-intentioned individuals can be tempted by the shadows within themselves.

The main themes of Lost Souls are deeply rooted in the psychological and philosophical aspects of human existence, inviting viewers to ponder the intricacies of desire, morality, and the human condition.

documents.title: Supernova
documents.tagline: In the farthest reaches of space, something has gone terribly wrong.
documents.overview: Set in the 22nd century, when a battered salvage ship sends out a distress signal, the seasoned crew of the rescue hospital ship Nova-17 responds. What they find is a black hole--that threatens to destroy both ships--and a mysterious survivor whose body quickly mutates into a monstrous and deadly form.
documents.plot:
Supernova is a 2000 American science fiction thriller directed by Walter Hill, who was credited under the pseudonym "Thomas Lee", from a screenplay by David C. Wilson based on a story by William Malone and Daniel Chuba. James Spader, Angela Bassett, Robert Forster, Lou Diamond Phillips, Peter Facinelli, Robin Tunney and Wilson Cruz star. Malone had first developed the project in the late 1980s as Dead Star, pitched as a cross between Hellraiser and Dead Calm in space, before Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer acquired and retitled it. The production was notoriously troubled: after Hill left, other directors were brought in for uncredited reshoots and Francis Ford Coppola was involved in re-editing the film.

In the early twenty-second century, the medical rescue ship Nightingale 229 patrols deep space with a six-member crew: captain and pilot A. J. Marley, co-pilot Nick Vanzant, medical officer Kaela Evers, medical technician Yerzy Penalosa, paramedic Danika Lund and computer technician Benjamin Sotomejor. They receive a distress call from an ice-mining operation on a distant moon, Titan 37, more than 3,000 light-years away. The crew makes a dimension jump to respond, but a malfunction during the jump fatally injures Captain Marley, and the ship arrives in the path of a debris cloud that destroys most of its manoeuvring fuel.

Worse still, the moon orbits a blue giant star whose gravity is dragging the damaged ship toward destruction within seventeen hours, almost exactly the time needed to recharge the jump drive, leaving only a narrow window to escape. Under Vanzant's command, the survivors take aboard Karl Larson, a disturbing young man who claims to be the only survivor of the mining operation, and who has brought with him a mysterious alien artefact. The object has strange effects on whoever touches it, and as Larson's true intentions emerge, the crew find themselves fighting for their lives against a threat that could destroy not only them but Earth itself.

The film combines elements of space survival drama and horror with sexual tension among the crew, set aboard a sleek, technology-filled vessel.

Supernova was a critical and commercial failure. It opened with about 6.7 million dollars over the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday weekend in January 2000, and on Rotten Tomatoes only about 12 percent of critics' reviews are positive.

documents.title: Bless the Child
documents.tagline: Mankind's last hope just turned six.
documents.overview: When Maggie's sister Jenna saddles her with an autistic newborn named Cody she touches Maggie's heart and becomes the daughter she has always longed for. But six years later Jenna suddenly re-enters her life and, with her mysterious new husband, Eric Stark, abducts Cody. Despite the fact that Maggie has no legal rights to Cody, FBI agent John Travis takes up her cause when he realizes that Cody shares the same birth date as several other recently murdered children.
documents.plot:
Bless the Child is a supernatural thriller film that revolves around the story of a young girl who is accused of being involved in a series of mysterious events and murders. The movie explores the theme of demonic possession, which serves as the central plot device.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the main character, Angela Vidal, is not what she seems to be. She is actually possessed by a malevolent entity that is manipulating her actions. This possession serves as a metaphor for the darker aspects of human nature and the struggle between good and evil.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its effects on individuals, particularly children. Angela's past experiences have left her with emotional scars, which are exploited by the demonic entity to further its own agenda. The movie suggests that unresolved trauma can create vulnerabilities that can be exploited by malevolent forces.

Furthermore, Bless the Child explores the idea of faith and spirituality as a means of coping with adversity. The main character's Catholic upbringing and her priest's attempts to help her serve as a source of comfort and strength in the face of supernatural terror.

Overall, the movie presents a gripping narrative that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, trauma, and the struggle between good and evil.
production_companies: Munich Film Partners & Company (MFP) BTC Productions

documents.title: The Death and Life of Bobby Z
documents.original_title: The Death and Life of Bobby Z
documents.tagline: To live a life of his own, he has to die first.
documents.overview: A DEA agent provides former Marine Tim Kearney with a way out of his prison sentence: impersonate Bobby Z, a recently deceased drug dealer, in a hostage switch with a crime lord. When the negotiations go awry, Kearney flees, with Z's son in tow.
documents.plot:
The Death and Life of Bobby Z is a crime drama film that delves into the complexities of loyalty, identity, and redemption. The movie follows Bobby Z, a former hitman who tries to leave his past life behind but finds himself drawn back in for one final job.

At its core, the film explores the theme of identity and how it's shaped by our experiences and choices. Bobby Z is a character torn between two personas: the person he was before his life of crime and the person he wants to become after trying to leave that life behind. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for his journey, as he struggles to reconcile his past and present selves.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty, particularly in the context of Bobby Z's relationships with those around him. His connections to his family, friends, and associates are put to the test as he navigates the moral gray areas of his profession. The film raises questions about the nature of loyalty and whether it can be genuine or if it's always tainted by self-interest.

Furthermore, The Death and Life of Bobby Z explores the theme of redemption, albeit in a nuanced and complex manner. Bobby Z's desire to leave his past life behind is rooted in a desire for redemption, but the film suggests that this may not be as straightforward as he hopes. Through Bobby Z's character, the movie raises questions about whether it's possible to truly change one's ways or if our past actions will always define us.

Overall, The Death and Life of Bobby Z is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human nature through its protagonist's journey.

documents.title: Friday After Next
documents.tagline: The party's back in the 'hood!
documents.overview: Craig and his cousin Day Day have finally moved out of their parents' houses and into their own crib, working nights at a local mall as security guards. When their house is robbed on Christmas Eve they set out to track down the culprit.
documents.plot:
Friday After Next is a 2002 American stoner comedy film directed by Fred Durst and written by Fred Durst, David Zuckerman, and Chris "Ludacris" Bridges. The movie stars Ice Cube, Mike Epps, and Faizon Love.

The main themes of Friday After Next revolve around the struggles of growing up, friendship, and finding one's identity. The film takes place during a snowstorm on Christmas Eve in Atlanta, Georgia, where three friends - Big Worm (Mike Epps), B-Dawg (Faizon Love), and Big Worm's cousin, Big Worm Jr. (Ice Cube) - try to survive the harsh winter conditions while dealing with their personal issues.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges, including family problems, relationships, and finding a sense of purpose. The film also explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and the importance of supporting one another through thick and thin.

The movie's plot is driven by Big Worm Jr.'s attempts to save his family's Christmas celebration from being ruined by a snowstorm, which serves as a metaphor for the challenges that come with growing up and finding one's place in the world. Ultimately, the film concludes on a heartwarming note, highlighting the power of friendship and the importance of holding onto what truly matters.

Overall, Friday After Next is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the struggles of growing up, all set against the backdrop of a hilarious snowstorm.

documents.title: Takedown
documents.tagline: The world has a right to know.
documents.overview: Kevin Mitnick is quite possibly the best hacker in the world. Hunting for more and more information, seeking more and more cyber-trophies every day, he constantly looks for bigger challenges.
