When he breaks into the computer of a security expert and an ex-hacker, he finds one - and much more than that...
documents.plot:
Takedown, released in the United States as Track Down, is a 2000 American crime thriller directed by Joe Chappelle and loosely based on Takedown, the nonfiction book by the computer security expert Tsutomu Shimomura and the New York Times journalist John Markoff about the pursuit of the hacker Kevin Mitnick. The screenplay is by David and Leslie Newman, John Danza and Howard A. Rodman. Skeet Ulrich plays Mitnick and Russell Wong plays Shimomura, with Tom Berenger and Christopher McDonald as federal agents, and Angela Featherstone, Donal Logue, Master P, Jeremy Sisto and Amanda Peet in supporting roles.

For years Mitnick has eluded the FBI while breaking into corporate and government computers, seeing himself as a crusader for freedom of information against "Big Brother". A gifted social engineer and smooth-talking con man, he is also socially awkward and obsessive, and his only real confidant is his friend Alex Lowe (Logue). Feeling slighted by Shimomura, a renowned security researcher, Mitnick breaks into his computers simply to prove that he can. In doing so he obtains the encrypted code of a powerful computer virus Shimomura had created for security research. Since it is only a matter of time before Mitnick cracks the encryption, Shimomura and his team become even more eager than the federal agents to catch him, and the case turns into a high-tech duel of wits and a personal grudge match that leads across the country to Seattle.

The film was produced by Dimension Films and Millennium Films, with Shimomura as co-executive producer and a cameo as a hacker. It opened in French cinemas in March 2000 as Cybertraque and was later released on DVD in Europe as Takedown, but its American release was delayed for years by controversy: Mitnick called the book and film extremely inaccurate, and the author Jonathan Littman sued Disney and Miramax, alleging that parts of the script were taken from his own, more sympathetic book, The Fugitive Game. Among the invented elements were face-to-face confrontations between the two men and hacks into NORAD and the NSA that never happened. It was finally released direct to video in the US in September 2004. Critics found it tense but hollow; Variety likened it to a stylish television episode and praised Ulrich while calling the supporting roles underwritten.

documents.title: War
documents.tagline: Vengeance is the ultimate weapon.
documents.overview: FBI agent Jack Crawford is out for revenge when his partner is killed and all clues point to the mysterious assassin Rogue. But when Rogue turns up years later to take care of some unfinished business, he triggers a violent clash of rival gangs. Will the truth come out before it's too late? And when the dust settles, who will remain standing?
documents.plot:
War, released in many countries as Rogue Assassin, is a 2007 American action thriller directed by Philip G. Atwell in his feature debut, with fight choreography by Corey Yuen. Jason Statham plays FBI agent John Crawford and Jet Li the mysterious assassin Rogue, in the actors' second pairing after The One (2001), with John Lone, Devon Aoki and Luis Guzmán in supporting roles. Its working title, Rogue, was changed to avoid confusion with another film.

During a shootout with the yakuza at a San Francisco dock warehouse, Crawford and his partner, Tom Lone, encounter Rogue, a former CIA assassin working for the Japanese gangsters. Rogue is about to execute Crawford when Lone shoots him in the face and he falls into the water, presumed dead. Soon afterward, Lone, his wife and his daughter are murdered and their house burned. Three years later Rogue resurfaces as an enforcer for Triad boss Li Chang, secretly igniting a war between the Triads and the yakuza of Shiro Yanagawa while recovering a pair of antique gold horses, heirlooms of Chang's family. Crawford, now head of the FBI's Asian organized crime unit, pursues him obsessively, at the cost of his own family, but Rogue always stays a step ahead and wins the trust of both bosses. He kills Chang but spares his wife and child, then turns on the yakuza.

When Rogue delivers the horses to Yanagawa and kills his men, a sword duel reveals that he is not Rogue at all but Tom Lone, who survived and surgically altered his appearance to take the dead assassin's identity and avenge his family. Yanagawa tells him that Crawford was on his payroll and leaked Lone's address, and Lone kills him, sending Chang's widow a gold horse and Yanagawa's daughter her father's head, each with the message "Make a new life". Lone then summons Crawford to the dock warehouse, where, backed by FBI sniper Goi, Crawford fights him and learns his identity. Crawford confesses that he was blackmailed into giving up the address, believing Lone would only be roughed up, and begs forgiveness. Lone refuses; when Crawford steps into Goi's line of fire to protect him, Lone shoots him dead and drives off to start a new life.

Released in the United States on August 24, 2007, the film opened with $9.8 million and grossed $40.7 million worldwide. Critics panned it, giving it 14% on Rotten Tomatoes and 36 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Queen Margot
documents.tagline: She was the wife of a king… and the lover of a soldier.
documents.overview: Paris, Kingdom of France, August 18, 1572. To avoid the outbreak of a religious war, the Catholic princess Marguerite de Valois, sister of the feeble King Charles IX, marries the Huguenot King Henry III of Navarre.
documents.plot:
La Reine Margot, released in North America as Queen Margot, is a 1994 French historical romantic drama directed by Patrice Chéreau from a screenplay he wrote with Danièle Thompson, based on the 1845 novel by Alexandre Dumas. It stars Isabelle Adjani as Marguerite de Valois, known as Margot, Daniel Auteuil as Henri of Navarre, Jean-Hugues Anglade as King Charles IX, Vincent Perez as La Môle and Virna Lisi as Catherine de' Medici.

In 1572, France is torn by the bitter conflict between Catholics and Protestant Huguenots. The kingdom is nominally ruled by the unstable and sickly Charles IX, but real power lies with his mother, the scheming Catherine de' Medici. In a gesture meant to reconcile the factions, Catherine arranges for her Catholic daughter Margot to marry Henri de Bourbon, the Protestant King of Navarre. Only days after the wedding, however, Catherine's maneuvering helps unleash the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre, in which thousands of Protestants who had gathered in Paris for the celebrations are slaughtered in the streets.

Margot, who does not love her husband, begins a passionate affair with La Môle, a Protestant nobleman caught up in the violence. At the same time she forms a pragmatic alliance with Henri, who must survive in a court that wants him dead. Poisonings, betrayals and conspiracies multiply as Catherine plots to secure the throne for her favorite son, the Duke of Anjou. A book whose pages have been coated with arsenic, meant for Henri, instead falls into the hands of King Charles, leading to tragic consequences for the lovers and for the crown.

Chéreau's version is noted for its brutal violence, sensuality and visceral depiction of religious hatred, contrasting with earlier, more decorous costume dramas.

The film premiered in competition at the 1994 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Jury Prize and the Best Actress award for Lisi. It received twelve nominations at the César Awards and won five, including Best Actress for Adjani and supporting awards for Anglade and Lisi. It drew about two million admissions in France, and an abridged version was released internationally.

documents.title: DragonHeart: A New Beginning
documents.overview: When Geoff, an orphaned stable boy (Chris Masterson), discovers Drake (voice of Robby Benson), the world's last living dragon, he realizes that his dream of becoming a knight in shining armor can now come true. Together, they soon face challenges that turn them into heroes. But caught up in the excitement of their new lives, Geoff and Drake fail to see the hidden dangers that surround them.
documents.plot:
Dragonheart: A New Beginning is a 2000 fantasy action-adventure film directed by Doug Lefler and released direct to video as a sequel to the 1996 film Dragonheart. Christopher Masterson stars as the stable boy Geoff, with Robby Benson voicing the young dragon Drake, and Harry Van Gorkum, Rona Figueroa and Henry O in supporting roles.

A year before his death, the knight Bowen finds an egg in the cave of his late dragon friend Draco and entrusts it to the monastery of Brother Gilbert. Mindful of a prophecy that a dragon's heart could doom mankind when a two-tailed comet crosses the sky, the friars hide the hatchling for twenty years. Geoff, an orphan who does menial chores at the monastery and dreams of becoming a knight like Bowen, stumbles on the hidden dragon, Drake, and the two lonely outsiders quickly become friends. Meanwhile, the king has appointed a man named Osric as his chief adviser; Osric claims to uphold the knightly Old Code but secretly corrupts it, poisoning the king's mind and imposing coloured tunics that mark each subject's station.

Two travellers from China, Master Kwan and his apprentice, arrive having read in the stars that a new dragon was born and that the comet is days away. The apprentice turns out to be Lian, a disguised member of the Chinese royal line. When knights threaten Geoff for not wearing his tunic, Drake takes his first flight to rescue him, revealing himself to the kingdom. Osric names boy and dragon protectors of the realm against invading Teregoths, while Kwan trains Drake in his powers, including the rare gift of ice breath. Lian explains that a renegade dragon, Griffin, once betrayed the dragons' code until his heart was taken and sealed in an amulet, and that fear of such dragons led a Chinese emperor to have all Eastern dragons killed, leaving Drake the last of his kind.

On the day of the comet Osric fakes a mortal wound to trick Drake into sharing his heart, but Geoff sees through it. Osric kills Kwan and reveals that he is Griffin, condemned to live as a human; reclaiming his heart, he regains his dragon form and invites Drake to join him in conquering humanity. Drake refuses and, mastering his ice breath, freezes Griffin, whose body shatters. When a shard kills Geoff, Drake revives him with part of his heart, and the two become brothers. Rotten Tomatoes lists a 40% score from only five reviews.

documents.title: Driven
documents.tagline: Get ready for the race of your life.
documents.overview: Talented rookie race-car driver Jimmy Bly has started losing his focus and begins to slip in the race rankings. It's no wonder, with the immense pressure being shoveled on him by his overly ambitious promoter brother as well as Bly's romance with his arch rival's girlfriend Sophia. With much riding on Bly, car owner Carl Henry brings former racing star Joe Tanto on board to help Bly. To drive Bly back to the top of the rankings, Tanto must first deal with the emotional scars left over from a tragic racing accident which nearly took his life.
documents.plot:
Driven is a 2001 American sports action film directed by Renny Harlin and written and produced by Sylvester Stallone, who also stars. Set in the CART FedEx Championship Series, it follows a young driver's attempt to win the title. Kip Pardue plays the rookie Jimmy Bly and Stallone the veteran Joe Tanto, with Burt Reynolds as the team owner Carl Henry, Til Schweiger as Beau Brandenburg, Estella Warren as Sophia Simone, Gina Gershon as Cathy, Cristián de la Fuente as Memo Moreno and Robert Sean Leonard as Jimmy's brother Demille.

Halfway through the season, the rookie Jimmy has already won five races, angering the reigning champion Beau, who blames his own slump on his fiancée Sophia and breaks off their engagement, after which his form returns. Carl, Jimmy's wheelchair-using team owner, notices his driver making more mistakes and talks his former champion Joe out of retirement to mentor him, replacing Memo, who is now married to Joe's ex-wife Cathy. Jimmy and Sophia grow close. In Canada, Carl holds Joe in the pits so that he can rejoin just in time to block Beau and hand Jimmy the win, while Demille resents Joe's influence. Distracted by Sophia, Jimmy crashes in Japan, and when she reconciles with Beau at a party in Chicago, Jimmy steals one of the new prototype cars and tears through the city streets until Joe chases him down and calms him.

Carl reinstates Memo and moves Joe to the pit lane. In a rain-soaked race in Germany, Memo, urged on by Cathy, goes for the win instead of protecting Jimmy and crashes, ending up in a lake; Jimmy and Beau dive in and pull him out just before the car explodes. Furious that Jimmy has sacrificed his title hopes, Carl arranges to replace him with Beau through Demille, but Beau tears up the contract and Sophia punches Demille. Jimmy, cleared to race despite an injured foot, goes into the Detroit finale with Joe back as his teammate. Joe damages his suspension avoiding a crash, and on the last lap Jimmy edges past Beau by inches to win the championship, celebrating with Joe and Beau as Demille watches proudly.

Driven was a commercial failure, grossing $32 million against a $72 million budget, though it was Stallone's first number-one opening since Cop Land. Critics panned it, with 14% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it received seven Golden Raspberry nominations; Warren won Worst Supporting Actress for this film and Planet of the Apes.

documents.title: Rules of Engagement
documents.tagline: A hero should never have to stand alone.
documents.overview: A Marine Colonel is brought to court-martial after ordering his men to fire on demonstrators surrounding the American embassy in Yemen.
documents.plot:
Rules of Engagement is a 2000 American romantic comedy film directed by Robert Luketic. The movie follows the story of two friends, Paul (Samuel L. Jackson) and Charlie (Tom Cruise), who are both recently divorced and struggling to navigate their lives.

At its core, Rules of Engagement explores themes of friendship, love, and self-discovery. The film delves into the complexities of male relationships, particularly those between friends who have been through similar experiences, such as divorce and heartbreak. Through Paul and Charlie's interactions, the movie highlights the importance of having a strong support system in times of need.

The film also touches on the theme of vulnerability, as both characters learn to open up and trust each other again after their respective divorces. This vulnerability allows them to form a deeper connection with each other, which ultimately leads to a romantic relationship.

Furthermore, Rules of Engagement pokes fun at societal expectations surrounding masculinity and relationships. The movie's portrayal of two men navigating the dating world is both humorous and relatable, highlighting the challenges that come with trying to balance emotional intimacy with traditional masculine norms.

Overall, Rules of Engagement is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, love, and self-discovery in a way that is both authentic and engaging.
production_companies: Munich Film Partners & Company (MFP) ROE Production

documents.title: 102 Dalmatians
documents.tagline: Meet Two Unlikely Heroes With A Bone To Pick.
documents.overview: Get ready for a howling good time as an all new assortment of irresistible animal heroes are unleashed in this great family tail! In an unlikely alliance, the outrageous Waddlesworth - a parrot who thinks he's a Rottweiler - teams up with Oddball - an un-marked Dalmatian puppy eager to earn her spots! Together they embark on a laugh-packed quest to outwit the ever-scheming Cruella De Vil.
documents.plot:
102 Dalmatians is a 2000 American family adventure comedy directed by Kevin Lima and written by Kristen Buckley, Brian Regan, Bob Tzudiker and Noni White. A sequel to the live-action 101 Dalmatians (1996), itself drawn from the 1961 animated film and Dodie Smith's novel, it brings back Glenn Close as Cruella de Vil, with Gérard Depardieu as the furrier Jean-Pierre LePelt, Ioan Gruffudd as Kevin Shepherd, Alice Evans as Chloe Simon and Tim McInnerny as Alonzo.

After three years in prison, Cruella appears to have been cured of her passion for fur by the behavioural therapy of Dr. Pavlov. She is paroled on condition that any violation will send her back to prison and force her to hand her remaining fortune of eight million pounds to the dog shelters of Westminster. Reformed, she makes peace with her long-suffering valet Alonzo and rescues Kevin Shepherd's struggling Second Chance dog shelter from bankruptcy. Her probation officer, Chloe, remains suspicious; she owns Dipstick, one of the Dalmatians Cruella once stole, whose mate Dottie has just had three puppies, among them the spotless Oddball, who grows up self-conscious about her plain coat.

Pavlov has discovered, and kept quiet, that the chimes of Big Ben undo his treatment, and when Cruella hears them she reverts to her old self. She enlists LePelt to design a coat made from Dalmatian puppies, with a hood from Dipstick's litter. Knowing that her fortune would go to Kevin's shelter, the only one in Westminster, she frames him for the theft of dozens of puppies, exploiting an old conviction, and lures Chloe to a dinner party while LePelt steals Dottie and the puppies; Dipstick is captured too.

Kevin breaks out of jail with the help of his talking macaw Waddlesworth and explains that his earlier offence was freeing animals from a laboratory. He and Chloe chase Cruella onto the Orient Express but miss the train, while Waddlesworth and Oddball follow the villains to LePelt's Paris factory. Cruella locks the couple in a cellar, but they help the puppies escape. Alonzo finally turns on his employer, defeats LePelt and frees Kevin and Chloe, and the puppies trap Cruella inside a giant cake in a bakery. Cruella and LePelt are arrested, her fortune goes to Kevin and Chloe, and Oddball at last grows a few spots.

The film grossed $183.6 million worldwide, less than its predecessor, and earned only 30% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though it was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Costume Design.

documents.title: Death Race
documents.tagline: Get ready for a killer race.
documents.overview: Terminal Island, New York: 2020. Overcrowding in the US penal system has reached a breaking point. Prisons have been turned over to a monolithic Weyland Corporation, which sees jails full of thugs as an opportunity for televised sport. Adrenalized inmates, a global audience hungry for violence and a spectacular, enclosed arena come together to form the 'Death Race', the biggest, most brutal event.
documents.plot:
Death Race is a 2008 science fiction action film directed by Paul W.S. Anderson, starring Jason Statham, Joan Allen, and Ian McShane.

In the year 2012, the United States has been transformed into a dystopian society where corporations have replaced governments. The tyrannical President John Spilner rules with an iron fist, and the poor are forced to live in poverty-stricken areas called "The Slums." To maintain control, Spilner creates a deadly game show called "Death Race," where prisoners are forced to compete in a high-stakes, televised event.

The main character, Jensen Ames (played by Jason Statham), is an ex-con who is sentenced to Death Race after being framed for a crime he didn't commit. In prison, Ames befriends the current champion of Death Race, Frankenstein (played by Joan Allen's character's husband, played by Ian McShane). However, when Ames is released from prison, he discovers that his wife has been killed in a brutal attack.

Ames' desire for revenge leads him to participate in Death Race, where he becomes the new favorite to win. With the help of his mechanic friend, Doc (played by John Leguizamo), Ames builds a customized car called the "Tyrant," which gives him an edge over the other competitors.

As the game progresses, Ames forms alliances with other prisoners and begins to uncover the dark secrets behind Death Race. He also discovers that President Spilner is using the show as a means to distract the population from his corrupt regime.

Throughout the film, Ames faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and ruthless opponents. However, he remains determined to win and take down President Spilner.

In the climactic final showdown, Ames faces off against Frankenstein in a high-speed battle on the Death Race track. With his Tyrant car, Ames outmaneuvers Frankenstein and emerges victorious, killing her in the process.

With his victory, Ames is hailed as a hero by the people, and he becomes a symbol of resistance against President Spilner's regime. However, Ames' newfound fame comes with a price, as he realizes that he has become a pawn in a larger game.

The film ends with Ames driving away from the Death Race track, ready to take on his next challenge and continue his fight for justice.

documents.title: My Father the Hero
documents.tagline: Fathers have just one problem with raising their daughters. They grow up!
documents.overview: A teenage girl on vacation in the Bahamas with her divorced father tries to impress a potential boyfriend by saying that her father is actually her lover. Remake of the 1991 French film Mon père, ce héros.
documents.plot:
My Father the Hero is a 1994 American teen comedy film directed by Raja Gosnell. The movie revolves around Jack Walton (played by Gerard Depardieu), a French aristocrat who poses as his daughter's boyfriend to impress her classmates, while hiding his true identity as her father.

The main theme of My Father the Hero explores the complexities of family relationships and the challenges of navigating social hierarchies. As Jack navigates his new role as a high school student, he must confront his own insecurities and biases about class differences, cultural expectations, and the difficulties of adapting to a new environment.

Through Jack's character, the film highlights the importance of acceptance, understanding, and empathy in bridging gaps between different social classes. As Jack forms connections with his daughter's friends and classmates, he learns to let go of his aristocratic pretensions and find common ground with those around him.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, as Jack struggles to reconcile his old life as a wealthy aristocrat with his new role as a high school student. This internal conflict serves as a metaphor for the challenges many people face in adapting to change and finding their place within a new community.

Ultimately, My Father the Hero is a heartwarming story about the power of love, acceptance, and self-discovery, as Jack learns to find his true identity and form meaningful connections with those around him.

documents.title: Nim's Island
documents.tagline: Be the hero of your own story.
documents.overview: A young girl inhabits an isolated island with her scientist father and communicates with a reclusive author of the novel she's reading.
documents.plot:
Nim's Island is an adventure drama film that revolves around the story of a young girl named Nim, who lives on a remote island with her scientist father. The movie explores several themes that are woven throughout the narrative.

One of the primary themes of Nim's Island is the importance of family and the bond between parents and children. The relationship between Nim and her father is at the heart of the story, as they work together to survive on the island and overcome various challenges. The film highlights the sacrifices that parents make for their children and the love that they have for them.

Another significant theme in Nim's Island is environmentalism and conservation. The movie showcases the beauty and fragility of nature, emphasizing the need to protect our planet and its resources. The island where Nim lives is a self-sustaining ecosystem, and the film encourages viewers to adopt eco-friendly practices and respect the natural world.

The movie also explores themes of independence, self-reliance, and empowerment. As Nim navigates her way through various challenges on the island, she learns valuable lessons about taking care of herself and relying on her own resources. The film promotes a sense of confidence and self-assurance in young girls, encouraging them to be brave, resourceful, and determined.

Lastly, Nim's Island touches on the theme of loss and grief. The father's absence from the island is a significant plot point, and the movie explores the emotional impact of his departure on Nim. The film handles this sensitive topic with care, highlighting the importance of coping mechanisms and finding ways to heal and move forward.

Overall, Nim's Island is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the beauty of nature, the power of family bonds, and the resilience of the human spirit.

documents.title: Enigma
documents.tagline: Unlock the secret.
documents.overview: The story of the WWII project to crack the code behind the Enigma machine, used by the Germans to encrypt messages sent to their submarines.
documents.plot:
Enigma is a 2001 spy thriller film directed by Michael Apted, based on the novel of the same name by Robert Harris.

The main themes of Enigma include:

1. **Code-breaking and cryptography**: The movie revolves around the story of a cryptanalyst, Thomas Creasy (played by Dougray Scott), who is tasked with cracking an unbreakable German Enigma code during World War II.
2. **Moral dilemmas and sacrifice**: As Creasy delves deeper into the code, he faces moral dilemmas and must make difficult choices that put him at odds with his superiors and colleagues. The film explores the consequences of these decisions on individuals and society.
3. **Loyalty and duty**: The movie highlights the tension between personal loyalty and professional duty, as Creasy struggles to balance his commitment to his country with his growing sense of unease about the code's implications.
4. **The human cost of war**: Enigma portrays the devastating effects of war on individuals and communities, emphasizing the importance of understanding the human side of conflict.
5. **Intelligence and power**: The film explores the complexities of intelligence gathering and the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to sensitive information.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a gripping narrative that keeps viewers engaged until the very end.

Would you like me to elaborate on any specific aspect of the story or characters?

documents.title: Perfect Blue
documents.tagline: The color of illusion is Perfect Blue.
documents.overview: A retired pop singer turned actress' sense of reality is shaken when she is stalked by an obsessed fan and seemingly a ghost of her past.
documents.plot:
Perfect Blue is a psychological thriller anime film written and directed by Satoshi Kon, released in 2002 (not 1997) but it was originally produced as an OVA (original video animation) series in 1997. The story follows the life of Mima Kirigoe, a former member of the popular idol group CHAM! or CHAM!, who decides to leave the entertainment industry and pursue a career in acting.

The film begins with Mima's departure from CHAM!, where she is struggling to cope with the pressures of fame. She then starts taking acting classes and lands a role in a television drama, "On Air". As Mima becomes more immersed in her new role, she begins to experience strange and unsettling events that blur the lines between reality and fantasy.

Mima's mental state deteriorates as she becomes increasingly paranoid and detached from reality. Her relationships with those around her begin to fray, including her friends and colleagues. The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between Mima's past and present, making it difficult for the viewer to discern what is real and what is not.

As the story progresses, Mima's grip on reality begins to slip further. She becomes convinced that her alter ego, a character she plays in "On Air", has taken over her life. The film's climax features a surreal and disturbing sequence where Mima's identity is torn apart, leaving the viewer questioning what is left of her.

Throughout the film, Kon explores themes of identity, celebrity culture, and the blurring of reality and fantasy. Perfect Blue is a thought-provoking and unsettling work that challenges the viewer to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

It's worth noting that while the film was released in 2002, it was originally produced as an OVA series in 1997 by Madhouse. The story has undergone some changes since its initial release, but the core themes and narrative remain intact.

documents.title: The Road to El Dorado
documents.tagline: They came for the gold. They stayed for the adventure.
documents.overview: After a failed swindle, two con-men end up with a map to El Dorado, the fabled "city of gold," and an unintended trip to the New World.  Much to their surprise, the map does lead the pair to the mythical city, where the startled inhabitants promptly begin to worship them as gods.  The only question is, do they take the worshipful natives for all they're worth, or is there a bit more to El Dorado than riches?
documents.plot:
The Road to El Dorado is a 2000 American animated adventure comedy film produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of two con artists, Tulio and Miguel, who stumble upon a treasure map that leads them on an epic journey to the mythical city of gold, El Dorado.

The film begins with Tulio (voiced by Kevin Kline) and Miguel (voiced by Kenneth Branagh), two charming but unscrupulous con artists from 16th-century Spain. They pose as nobles and swindle their way through various towns, always staying one step ahead of the law. One day, they stumble upon a mysterious map that supposedly leads to the fabled city of gold, El Dorado.

Believing the map will make them rich beyond their wildest dreams, Tulio and Miguel set sail for South America, accompanied by a loyal but dim-witted servant named Chel (voiced by Armand Assante). As they navigate through treacherous jungle terrain, they encounter various obstacles, including fierce warriors, deadly traps, and treacherous rivals.

Upon arriving at the gates of El Dorado, Tulio and Miguel are met with a mixture of awe and suspicion. The city is inhabited by the ancient civilization of the Incas, who possess advanced knowledge and technology that surpasses anything the Europeans have ever seen. The two con artists soon discover that they are not alone in their quest for wealth; a ruthless Spanish conquistador named Cortés (voiced by Ross Malinger) is also on the hunt.

As Tulio and Miguel try to navigate the complexities of Inca culture, they begin to develop an unlikely friendship with the Incas' leader, Tia (voiced by Rosie Perez). She teaches them about the city's history, customs, and values, which slowly changes their perspective on life. However, Cortés and his men are determined to claim El Dorado for themselves, leading to a series of comedic misadventures and action-packed battles.

Throughout their journey, Tulio and Miguel learn valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and the true meaning of wealth. They also discover that the map they found was not just a treasure map but a key to unlocking the secrets of El Dorado. In the end, the two con artists must decide whether to return to their old ways or forge a new path with their newfound friends.

The Road to El Dorado features stunning animation, witty humor, and memorable characters. The film's blend of adventure, comedy, and heartwarming moments makes it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages. With its richly detailed world-building and engaging storyline, this animated classic has become a beloved favorite among fans of DreamWorks Pictures.

documents.title: Bride Wars
documents.tagline: May the best bride win.
documents.overview: Two best friends become rivals when their respective weddings are accidentally booked for the same day.
documents.plot:
Bride Wars is a 2009 American romantic comedy film directed by Gary Winick and written by Greg DePaul and Karen McCullah Lutz. The movie stars Kate Hudson, Anne Hathaway, Candice Bergen, and Bryan Greenberg.

The story revolves around two best friends, Emma Allan (Kate Hudson) and Olivia "Liv" Hanson (Anne Hathaway), who have been inseparable since childhood. They share a New York City apartment and are known for their identical style, from their clothes to their hairstyles. The movie begins with the announcement that both women will be getting married on the same day, which sparks an argument over the venue.

The two friends decide to settle the dispute by flipping a coin, but they end up choosing the same venue, a luxurious mansion in Manhattan. As the wedding dates approach, Emma and Liv become increasingly stressed about finding a new venue that can accommodate both weddings simultaneously. The situation escalates when the venue owner refuses to rent out the space on the same day.

As the tension between the two friends grows, they start to drift apart. Emma becomes engaged to her fiancé, Nathan (Bryan Greenberg), while Liv starts dating a charming but unreliable man named James (Chris Pratt). Meanwhile, their mothers, Mrs. Allan (Candice Bergen) and Mrs. Hanson (Mary Steenburgen), become involved in the dispute, adding to the chaos.

The situation reaches its boiling point when Emma and Liv discover that they have been booked at the same venue on the same day, despite their earlier agreement. The two friends engage in a series of escalating pranks and sabotage, trying to outdo each other and claim the wedding as their own.

In the end, Emma and Liv realize that their friendship is more important than their individual desires. They come up with a plan to have both weddings on the same day at the same venue, but with separate entrances and exits. The movie ends with a heartwarming moment of reconciliation between the two friends, as they share a laugh and a toast to their enduring friendship.

Throughout the movie, the chemistry between Kate Hudson and Anne Hathaway is undeniable, making their characters' complicated relationship both relatable and entertaining. The supporting cast adds to the humor and drama, particularly Candice Bergen's scene-stealing performance as Emma's mother. Overall, Bride Wars is a lighthearted and engaging romantic comedy that explores the complexities of female friendship and the challenges of growing up.

documents.title: Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa
documents.tagline: Still together. Still lost!
documents.overview: Alex, Marty, and other zoo animals find a way to escape from Madagascar when the penguins reassemble a wrecked airplane. The precariously repaired craft stays airborne just long enough to make it to the African continent. There the New Yorkers encounter members of their own species for the first time. Africa proves to be a wild place, but Alex and company wonder if it is better than their Central Park home.
documents.plot:
Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa is a computer-animated comedy-adventure film released in 2008 by DreamWorks Animation. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Madagascar film and follows the further adventures of Alex the lion, Marty the zebra, Gloria the hippopotamus, Melman the giraffe, and their friends.

The story begins with Alex (voiced by Ben Stiller), who has become an international celebrity after his appearance on "Wild Kingdom" with the famous animal trainer, Ken. However, Alex starts to feel suffocated by the constant attention and longs for the freedom of the wild. He decides to escape from the zoo and embark on a journey back to Africa, where he hopes to find his ancestors' homeland.

Along the way, Alex is joined by Marty (voiced by Chris Rock), Gloria (voiced by Jada Pinkett Smith), Melman (voiced by David Schwimmer), and their friend, King Julian (voiced by Sacha Baron Cohen). The group faces numerous challenges as they navigate through the jungle, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and rival zoos.

As they journey deeper into Africa, the group discovers that Alex's ancestors were not just ordinary lions but were actually royalty. They also meet a new character, Maurice (voiced by Cedric the Entertainer), who claims to be Alex's long-lost uncle. However, it is revealed that Maurice has ulterior motives and is trying to take over the throne.

The group eventually reaches the kingdom of Madagascar, where they are welcomed as heroes. However, their joy is short-lived as they soon discover that the island is in danger due to a severe drought. The animals must work together to find a solution to save their home.

In the end, Alex and his friends successfully defeat Maurice and restore balance to the kingdom. Along the way, Alex comes to terms with his royal heritage and finds a new sense of purpose as the rightful king of Madagascar. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Alex and his friends enjoying a newfound appreciation for their home and each other's company.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities shine through in their interactions and relationships with one another. Marty's sarcastic humor and Gloria's sassy attitude provide comedic relief, while Melman's anxiety and King Julian's eccentricity add to the movie's lighthearted tone.

Overall, Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, community, and belonging. With its colorful animation, engaging characters, and exciting plot twists, it is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Sherlock Holmes
documents.tagline: Nothing escapes him.
documents.overview: Eccentric consulting detective Sherlock Holmes and Doctor John Watson battle to bring down a new nemesis and unravel a deadly plot that could destroy England.
documents.plot:
Sherlock Holmes is a 2009 action mystery film directed by Guy Ritchie, starring Robert Downey Jr. as the iconic detective Sherlock Holmes and Jude Law as his trusted sidekick Dr. John Watson.

The film begins with a prologue set in 1891, where we see a young Sherlock Holmes (Eddie Marsan) being bullied at school due to his exceptional intelligence. He is eventually befriended by Mycroft Holmes (Jude Law), who recognizes his exceptional abilities and encourages him to use them for the greater good.

The story then jumps forward to 1895, where we meet Dr. John Watson (Jude Law), a veteran of the British Army who has just returned from Afghanistan. He is struggling to find purpose in his life until he meets Sherlock Holmes (Robert Downey Jr.), who is now a consulting detective in London.

The two men form an unlikely partnership, with Watson serving as both Holmes' biographer and partner in crime-solving. Their first case together involves a mysterious murder at Reichenbach Falls, where they encounter the villainous Lord Blackwood (Mark Strong).

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Holmes and Watson uncover a sinister plot by Blackwood to use a deadly gas to kill thousands of people in London. Along the way, they must navigate a complex web of clues, red herrings, and double-crosses.

Throughout the film, Ritchie's signature fast-paced dialogue and witty banter are on full display, as Holmes and Watson engage in clever repartee and intellectual sparring matches. Downey Jr.'s portrayal of Holmes is particularly notable, capturing the character's eccentricities and intensity with remarkable accuracy.

As the story unfolds, Holmes and Watson must use all their skills and resources to stay one step ahead of Blackwood and his accomplices. The film's action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, with a memorable showdown between Holmes and Blackwood at Reichenbach Falls.

In the end, Holmes and Watson succeed in stopping Blackwood's plot, but not before he reveals that he has been working for a larger organization known as the "Shadow." The film concludes with Holmes and Watson reflecting on their adventure, while also hinting at future cases to come.

Overall, Sherlock Holmes is a fun and engaging adaptation of the classic characters, with Ritchie's unique style and Downey Jr.'s energetic performance bringing new life to the iconic detective.

documents.title: Outlander
documents.tagline: It destroyed his world. He won't let it destroy ours.
documents.overview: During the reign of the Vikings, a man from another world crash-lands on Earth, bringing with him an alien predator. The man must fuse his advanced technology with the weaponry of the vikings to fight the monster.
documents.plot:
Outlander is a science fiction action film of 2008 written and directed by Howard McCain, loosely based on the Old English epic Beowulf but reimagined around a spaceship that crashes in Iron Age Norway. Jim Caviezel stars as Kainan, a humanoid alien warrior, with Sophia Myles as Freya, Jack Huston as Wulfric, John Hurt as King Hrothgar, Ron Perlman as the rival chieftain Gunnar, Cliff Saunders as the smith Boromir and Bailey Maughan as the orphan Erik.

In 709 AD a spacecraft crashes into a lake in Scandinavia. Its lone survivor, Kainan, learns from his ship's computer that he has landed on Earth, a seed colony abandoned by his people, and has the local Norse language and customs downloaded into his brain. Finding a village destroyed, he is captured by Wulfric, the heir of King Hrothgar, and taken to Hrothgar's fortified settlement, where the king fears that Gunnar will blame the massacre on them. Calling himself a man from the north hunting a dragon, Kainan reveals, after an unseen beast kills several warriors that night, that the attacker is a Moorwen, a predator that stowed away on his ship and caused the crash. He wins the villagers' respect by killing a giant bear during a hunt.

After a clash with Gunnar's men, who return fleeing the Moorwen, Kainan devises a trap: a pit of whale oil inside the gate, crossed by floating shields. He confides to Freya, who is drawn to him, that his people slaughtered the Moorwens to colonise their planet, and that this last survivor massacred his colony, including his wife and child. Freya gives him an ancestral sword. The burning pit only wounds the beast, which kills Gunnar and escapes, while its offspring slips in through the well and kills Hrothgar. Kainan retrieves metal from his sunken ship to forge stronger blades, but the young Moorwen seizes Freya. Descending the well, the hunters lose many men, including Boromir, before Freya kills the offspring. At a waterfall the adult Moorwen mortally wounds Wulfric, who passes the crown to Kainan before Kainan and Freya send the creature over the cliff. Bidding farewell to his wife's coffin, Kainan destroys his distress beacon, lets the rescue ship leave without him, and stays to rule, marrying Freya and adopting Erik.

Based on a story McCain first wrote in 1992, the film received only a limited American release in January 2009. It earned around $6 million worldwide on a reported budget of $47 million, and critics were unimpressed, giving it 37% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Doors
documents.tagline: The Ultimate Story of Sex, Drugs & Rock 'N' Roll
documents.overview: The story of the famous and influential 1960s rock band and its lead singer and composer, Jim Morrison.
documents.plot:
The Doors is a 1991 American biographical musical drama directed by Oliver Stone, who co-wrote it with J. Randall Jahnson, about the Los Angeles rock band the Doors and their singer Jim Morrison. Val Kilmer stars as Morrison, with Meg Ryan as his partner Pamela Courson, Kyle MacLachlan as Ray Manzarek, Frank Whaley as Robby Krieger, Kevin Dillon as John Densmore, Kathleen Quinlan as the journalist Patricia Kennealy and Billy Idol. The film presents Morrison as a mythic figure of 1960s rock and the counterculture, dwelling on his excesses and fascination with death.

In 1949 the young Morrison and his family drive past a road accident in the New Mexico desert, where he sees a Native American man dying, an image that haunts him for life. In 1965 Jim, now a film student at UCLA living the Venice Beach life, falls in love with Pamela Courson and meets Ray Manzarek, and with Robby Krieger and John Densmore they form the Doors. After a trip to Death Valley to take psychedelics, they win a devoted following at the Whisky a Go Go, until an obscene rendition of "The End" gets them thrown out. The producer Paul Rothchild and Jac Holzman of Elektra Records sign them on the spot.

Success comes quickly. Booked on The Ed Sullivan Show, the band is told to change a drug reference in "Light My Fire", but Jim sings the original line live and they are never invited back. Increasingly absorbed by his persona as the Lizard King, Jim sinks into alcohol and drug abuse. He begins an affair with Patricia Kennealy, a rock journalist involved in witchcraft, and takes part in a pagan handfasting ceremony with her, while the spirit of the dying man appears to watch over him.

His bandmates grow tired of his missed sessions and late arrivals. At a chaotic 1969 concert in Miami he arrives drunk, taunts the crowd and threatens to expose himself, bringing criminal charges, cancelled shows and deep resentment within the group. Convicted of indecent exposure in 1970, he remains free pending appeal. After urging Patricia to end her pregnancy, he says farewell to the band at Ray's birthday party, giving them copies of his poetry. In 1971 Jim and Pam move to Paris, where she finds him dead in the bath; he is buried at Père Lachaise cemetery, and Pam dies three years later.

Kilmer's uncanny performance was widely praised, though critics were divided on Stone's portrait, giving it a 58% Rotten Tomatoes approval and a Metacritic score of 62.

documents.title: Shark Tale
documents.tagline: Behind every little fish is a great white lie.
documents.overview: Oscar is a small fish whose big aspirations often get him into trouble. Meanwhile, Lenny is a great white shark with a surprising secret that no sea creature would guess: He's a vegetarian. When a lie turns Oscar into an improbable hero and Lenny becomes an outcast, the two form an unlikely friendship.
documents.plot:
Shark Tale is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2004 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie takes place in the underwater city of New York, where fish live and thrive.

The story begins with Oscar, a small fish who lives on the outskirts of the city. Oscar dreams of becoming a great hero like his idol, Lenny, a famous fish who saved the city from a shark attack years ago. However, Oscar's life is mundane and uneventful, working as a "fish food" taste-tester for a local restaurant.

One day, while swimming near the surface, Oscar meets Don Lino, a great white shark who rules the ocean with an iron fin. Don Lino is feared by all fish in the city, and his reputation is built on his brutal attacks on other sea creatures. However, Oscar soon discovers that Don Lino's life is not as glamorous as it seems.

As Oscar navigates his new friendship with Don Lino, he also meets Lenny, who has become a legend among the fish for saving the city from sharks. Oscar becomes obsessed with meeting Lenny and earning his respect, but things take a turn when Oscar accidentally kills Don Lino's son, Lenny Jr., in self-defense.

Panicked, Oscar flees the scene and hides behind a coral reef, where he meets Lenny himself. However, to Oscar's surprise, Lenny is not the hero he expected. Instead, Lenny is a cowardly fish who has been hiding from Don Lino for years.

Together, Oscar and Lenny concoct a plan to convince Don Lino that his son was killed by another shark, thereby avoiding a war between sharks and fish. Along the way, they meet a motley crew of fish, including Angie, a sassy fish who becomes Oscar's love interest, and Sykes, a wise-cracking fish who serves as their guide.

As the story unfolds, Oscar learns valuable lessons about bravery, loyalty, and being true to oneself. In the end, Don Lino is convinced that his son was killed by another shark, and he vows to protect the city from other sharks. However, in a surprising twist, it is revealed that Lenny Jr. was actually alive all along, and he has been hiding with Oscar.

The movie ends with Oscar being hailed as a hero for saving Don Lino's life, and he finally earns the respect of his idol, Lenny. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, with Oscar and Angie sharing a romantic moment, and the city of New York thriving in peace.

Overall, Shark Tale is a fun and entertaining animated film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has become a beloved classic among children and families.

documents.title: Frequency
documents.tagline: The future is listening.
documents.overview: When a rare phenomenon gives police officer John Sullivan the chance to speak to his father, 30 years in the past, he takes the opportunity to prevent his dad's tragic death.  After his actions inadvertently give rise to a series of brutal murders he and his father must find a way to fix the consequences of altering time.
documents.plot:
Frequency is a 2000 American science fiction thriller film directed by Craig Mazin, starring Dennis Quaid, Jim Caviezel, and Shawn Doyle.

The main themes of Frequency include:

1. **Time Travel and its Consequences**: The movie explores the concept of time travel through a police scanner radio connection between two men across different timelines. This theme delves into the consequences of altering the past and the potential impact on one's present and future.
2. **Family and Legacy**: The story revolves around the relationship between Martin (Dennis Quaid) and his son Jake (Jim Caviezel), who are connected through a mysterious police scanner radio. As they navigate their different timelines, they must also confront their own personal struggles and learn to connect with each other across time.
3. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Throughout the film, both Martin and Jake face challenges that force them to re-evaluate their lives and make amends for past mistakes. This theme highlights the importance of redemption, forgiveness, and personal growth in overcoming adversity.
4. **The Butterfly Effect**: The movie illustrates the concept of the butterfly effect, where small changes in one's actions can have significant effects on the course of events in another timeline.

Overall, Frequency is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its unique blend of science fiction and family drama elements.

documents.title: Where the Heart Is
documents.tagline: Laughter is harder... Friendship is stronger... Trust is deeper... When it comes from the heart.
documents.overview: Novalee Nation is a 17-year-old Tennessee transient who has to grow up in a hurry when she's left pregnant and abandoned by her boyfriend on a roadside, and takes refuge in the friendly aisles of Wal-Mart. Eventually, some eccentric but kindly strangers 'adopt' Novalee and her infant daughter, helping them buck the odds and build a new life.
documents.plot:
Where the Heart Is is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the search for belonging. The movie delves into the life of Novalee Nation, a pregnant teenager who finds herself abandoned at a Walmart store in Oklahoma after her boyfriend leaves her.

As Novalee navigates this challenging situation, she must confront her own vulnerabilities and insecurities, as well as the harsh realities of poverty, loneliness, and social isolation. The film masterfully weaves together themes of resilience, hope, and redemption, showcasing Novalee's capacity to adapt and grow in the face of adversity.

Throughout the movie, the director, Matt Williams, skillfully explores the tensions between individual desire for autonomy and the need for human connection and community. Novalee's journey is marked by a series of encounters with various characters, each of whom offers her a unique perspective on life, love, and belonging.

Ultimately, Where the Heart Is is a powerful exploration of what it means to be human, to find one's place in the world, and to discover the depths of the heart. The film's narrative is both deeply personal and universally relatable, inviting audiences to reflect on their own experiences with identity, community, and the complexities of human relationships.

documents.title: Dinosaur
documents.tagline: You have never seen anything like this.
documents.overview: An orphaned dinosaur raised by lemurs joins an arduous trek to a sancturary after a meteorite shower destroys his family home.
documents.plot:
Dinosaur is a computer-animated adventure film produced by Walt Disney Pictures, released in 2000. The movie takes place during the Late Cretaceous period, around 65 million years ago.

The story begins with an elderly Iguanodon named Aladar, who lives on an island called Sodor with his adopted family, including his son Zip, daughter Saera, and nephew Bucky. Aladar is a kind and gentle soul, loved by all the animals on the island. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a severe storm hits the island, causing widespread destruction and separating Aladar from his family.

Aladar sets out on an epic journey to find his adopted family, facing numerous challenges and dangers along the way. He meets a group of young dinosaurs, including Yar, a brave and adventurous triceratops; Cera, a stubborn but lovable iguanodon; and Spike, a small but fierce stegosaurus. Together, they form an unlikely family unit, with Aladar as their leader.

As they travel across the treacherous terrain of the Late Cretaceous period, the group encounters various obstacles, including ferocious predators like the Tyrannosaurus Rex and the Gorgonops. However, through teamwork and determination, they overcome these challenges and continue on their quest to find Aladar's family.

Along the way, the group discovers a hidden oasis, where they meet a wise old Troodon named Ray. Ray becomes a mentor to the group, teaching them about the importance of working together and trusting one another. He also shares his knowledge of the ancient world, revealing secrets about the dinosaurs' habitats and behaviors.

As the journey progresses, the group faces its greatest challenge yet: a treacherous mountain pass filled with steep cliffs and raging rivers. However, through their combined strength and ingenuity, they successfully navigate this perilous terrain and finally reach Aladar's family.

The movie culminates in an emotional reunion between Aladar and his adopted family, as well as the young dinosaurs who have become like a second family to him. The group celebrates their reunion with a joyful dance party, marking the beginning of a new era of friendship and adventure for all.

Throughout the film, the characters undergo significant development, learning valuable lessons about loyalty, trust, and the importance of family. The movie's stunning animation and engaging storyline make it an unforgettable experience for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Dinosaur is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that explores the themes of family, friendship, and perseverance in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Small Time Crooks
documents.tagline: They took a bite out of crime
documents.overview: A loser of a crook and his wife strike it rich when a botched bank job's cover business becomes a spectacular success.
documents.plot:
Small Time Crooks is a 2000 American comedy film directed by Joel Coen and written by Joel Coen and Ethan Coen. The movie revolves around the story of a group of small-time crooks who plan to rob a bank in New York City.

The main theme of Small Time Crooks is the illusion of power and control that comes with crime, as well as the consequences of getting caught up in a life of dishonesty. The film explores how the characters' perceptions of themselves and their place in the world are shaped by their involvement in the underworld, and how this ultimately leads to their downfall.

The movie also touches on the idea of loyalty and friendship, highlighting the strong bonds between the main characters as they navigate the complexities of their illicit activities. However, these relationships are tested when one of the group members is forced to make a difficult choice that puts everyone at risk.

Furthermore, Small Time Crooks critiques the notion of the "American Dream," suggesting that it is an unattainable illusion that can lead individuals down a path of destruction and disappointment. The film's portrayal of the characters' failed attempts to achieve success through crime serves as a commentary on the emptiness and disillusionment that can result from chasing after material wealth and status.

Overall, Small Time Crooks presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, delving into themes of identity, morality, and the consequences of one's actions.

documents.title: Boys and Girls
documents.tagline: Warning: Sex Changes Everything
documents.overview: Ryan and Jennifer are opposites who definitely do not attract. At least that's what they always believed. When they met as twelve-year-olds, they disliked one another. When they met again as teenagers, they loathed each other. But when they meet in college, the uptight Ryan and the free-spirited Jennifer find that their differences bind them together and a rare friendship develops.
documents.plot:
Boys and Girls is a 2000 American romantic comedy film directed by Robert Iscove. Freddie Prinze Jr. and Claire Forlani star as two people whose lives keep intersecting over the years, with Jason Biggs, Amanda Detmer and Alyson Hannigan in supporting roles. It was released in the United States on June 16, 2000. Anna Friel was originally cast but withdrew before filming.

Ryan Walker and Jennifer Burrows first meet as twelve-year-olds seated next to each other on an airplane, and immediately clash. Four years later, they cross paths again at a high school football game in Los Angeles, where Ryan, his school's mascot, loses his costume head during a halftime chase, only for it to be crushed by the car carrying Jennifer, the rival school's homecoming queen. She tries to console him, but they part, convinced that they have nothing in common.

A year later, both are students at the University of California, Berkeley. Ryan is still with his high school sweetheart, Betty, while the free-spirited Jennifer lives with a musician boyfriend. Both relationships soon end. Ryan's roommate, Steve, who calls himself Hunter, fancies himself a ladies' man. Jennifer moves in with her best friend, Amy, who briefly dates Ryan and sends Jennifer to break up with him on her behalf. Instead, Ryan and Jennifer strike up a friendship, sharing long walks and consoling each other through failed romances until they become best friends. Jennifer even encourages Ryan to start dating again.

One night, when Jennifer is feeling cynical about love, Ryan comforts her and they end up sleeping together. Ryan is ready for a relationship, but Jennifer, frightened of commitment, insists that the night was a mistake. Hurt, Ryan withdraws from her and buries himself in his studies. Months later, as Jennifer prepares to leave for Italy after graduation, they meet at their favorite hilltop overlooking the Golden Gate Bridge, and Ryan confesses that he loves her. She claims not to feel the same, and they say goodbye. On the way to the airport, however, Jennifer realizes she loves him too, and learns from Steve, now involved with Amy, that Ryan is flying home to Los Angeles. She finds him aboard the plane and declares her love, reuniting them where they first met.

Boys and Girls received mainly negative reviews, with critics viewing it as a stale imitation of When Harry Met Sally...; Rotten Tomatoes reported 11% approval and Metacritic a score of 29.

documents.title: Dracula 2000
documents.tagline: The Most Seductive Evil of All Time Has Now Been Unleashed in Ours.
documents.overview: Abraham Van Helsing, who has tangled with Count Dracula in the past, works as an English antiques dealer. Simon is a vampire hunter in training under his apprenticeship.
documents.plot:
Dracula 2000 is a 2000 American horror film directed by Patrick Lussier and produced by New Line Cinema. The movie serves as a sequel to Bram Stoker's novel "Dracula" and offers a modern retelling of the classic tale.

The main themes of Dracula 2000 include:

1. **The struggle between good and evil**: The film explores the eternal conflict between good and evil, as embodied by the protagonist, Jack Crow (played by Gerard Butler), a vampire hunter, and the titular character, Count Dracula (played by Christopher Plummer). The movie highlights the moral implications of their actions and the consequences of their choices.

2. **The corrupting influence of power**: Dracula's character is driven by his insatiable desire for power and control. His ability to manipulate and dominate others serves as a metaphor for the dangers of unchecked ambition and the corrupting influence of power.

3. **Love and sacrifice**: The film also explores the theme of love and sacrifice, particularly in the relationship between Jack Crow and his love interest, Emily (played by Justine Waddell). Their bond is tested as they navigate the supernatural world and confront the evil forces head-on.

4. **The struggle for identity**: As a modern retelling of the classic tale, Dracula 2000 also delves into themes of identity and self-discovery. Jack Crow's character, in particular, grapples with his own identity and purpose as a vampire hunter, highlighting the tension between his human and supernatural selves.

5. **The consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control**: The movie serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human understanding. Dracula's actions have far-reaching consequences that threaten not only humanity but also the very fabric of society.

Overall, Dracula 2000 offers a fresh take on the classic vampire mythology, exploring themes that are both timeless and timely.

documents.title: Dracula II: Ascension
documents.tagline: The terrifying sequel to Dracula 2000.
documents.overview: Father Uffizi hunts vampires. He travels the world to behead them with his bullwhip, but his ultimate goal is to find the first vampire, Dracula. Medical students, Liz Blaine and Luke are charged with autopsying the body. When they open the abdominal cavity, they find that the liver and other organs are white, suggesting to Luke that the person did not produce his own blood but got it elsewhere, i.e., a vampire.
documents.plot:
Dracula II: Ascension is a 2003 American-Romanian direct-to-video horror film directed by Patrick Lussier, who wrote it with Joel Soisson, and the sequel to Dracula 2000. It stars Jason Scott Lee as Father Uffizi, a vampire-hunting priest, Diane Neal as the medical student Elizabeth Blaine, Craig Sheffer as her husband Lowell, Jason London as Luke, John Light as Eric and Stephen Billington as Dracula, with Roy Scheider as Cardinal Siqueros. It was filmed entirely in Romania at Castel Film Studios and released on 7 June 2003.

Uffizi kills two vampire twins but is bitten and infected, and holds the infection at bay by exposing himself to the sun. In New Orleans, Dracula's corpse arrives at the morgue where Elizabeth and her friend Luke work, and Elizabeth pricks her finger on one of its fangs. Her husband Lowell, a professor at her college with a fatal degenerative illness, tells them to take the body to his secluded family home, while a supposed wealthy investor offers to fund research into its secret of immortality. With fellow students Kenny and Tanya, they submerge the corpse in a bath of blood, and Dracula suddenly rises, kills Tanya and is held back by the investor, Eric, with a modified light gun. Tanya returns as a vampire, kills a police officer and is destroyed in sunlight by Uffizi, who has learned that Dracula is Judas Iscariot and seeks to grant him absolution. The group chains Dracula in an abandoned pool under ultraviolet light and Luke surrounds him with wards, while Elizabeth is increasingly drawn to him. The greedy Kenny injects himself with Dracula's blood, becomes a vampire and is beheaded by Uffizi. Elizabeth injects Lowell with the blood after Dracula lures him into the pool, and Lowell regains the ability to walk, only to reveal that there was no investor and that he and Eric had used the others to cure himself and to profit from an immortality serum. Uffizi kills Lowell, now a vampire, and Dracula breaks free, mauls Eric, who returns as a vampire and is destroyed by Luke, and slips through the wards. Elizabeth, already turned, refuses to step into sunlight. Uffizi overpowers the weakened Dracula and begins the rite of absolution, but Dracula torments him with visions of Christ's betrayal and crucifixion, and Elizabeth wounds the priest and leaves with Dracula, who spares Uffizi knowing he will keep hunting him.

It was shot alongside Dracula III: Legacy (2005). Critics were largely negative; it holds a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Dracula III: Legacy
documents.tagline: You can't fight it. You can't kill it.
documents.overview: In the near future, Uffizi and Luke travel to the remote reaches of war torn Romania to rescue Elizabeth and finish the vampire once and for all. Along the way, they encounter TV news journalist and a corps of rebels trying to fight the vampire uprising which plagues their country.
documents.plot:
Dracula III: Legacy is a 2005 horror film directed by Patrick Lussier and the third installment in the series that began with Dracula 2000 and continued with Dracula II: Ascension. It stars Jason Scott Lee as the vampire-hunting priest Uffizi, Jason London as his companion Luke, Diane Neal as Elizabeth Blaine, Alexandra Wescourt as the reporter Julia Hughes and Roy Scheider as Cardinal Siqueros. Rutger Hauer plays Dracula, succeeding Gerard Butler and Stephen Billington in the role and continuing the series' idea that the vampire's appearance changes as he regenerates.

Five years after the previous film, Uffizi and Luke learn that Dracula has returned to his castle in the Carpathian Mountains, taking Elizabeth with him. Cardinal Siqueros, fearing that Uffizi has been tainted by Dracula, refuses to bless the mission, so Uffizi leaves the priesthood and sets out with Luke for Bucharest. Romania has been torn apart by civil war, and NATO peacekeepers patrol the streets. In an abandoned village the two men find a crashed helicopter carrying Julia, a television news reporter, and her cameraman, Tommy. Tommy is turned by vampires who are terrorizing the village, but Uffizi and Luke destroy them all.

Leaving Julia behind, the hunters walk into a trap set by rebels, only to find Julia already with them; she refuses to return to England with nothing but a story about vampires. When the undead attack the rebel camp during the night, Uffizi, Luke and Julia survive and continue to Dracula's castle. There they find Elizabeth almost completely given over to Dracula's way of life. Dracula mortally wounds Julia and tells Uffizi that he can only truly die through God's forgiveness. Uffizi fights the ancient vampire, bites him and drains his blood, then beheads him, declaring that he may consider himself forgiven. At Elizabeth's own request, Luke beheads her. Luke then leaves the castle, while Uffizi takes his seat on Dracula's throne beside a revived Julia, now a vampire, suggesting that he has become the new vampire king with Julia as his queen.

The film was released directly to DVD and VHS on July 12, 2005. Critical reaction was mixed, though warmer than for Dracula II. John Puccio of DVD Town said it was hardly scary but had mood, tone and atmosphere to spare, along with decent acting, qualities he felt the first two films lacked. Kevin Carr of 7M Pictures ranked it below Hellraiser but above the Crow sequels and noted there is always a market for vampire films.

documents.title: Child's Play
documents.overview: A single mother gives her son a beloved doll for his birthday, only to discover that it is possessed by the soul of a serial killer.
documents.plot:
Child's Play is a 1988 American supernatural horror film directed by Tom Holland and written by Don Mancini. The movie was produced by Universal Pictures, not United Artists.

The story begins with the introduction of Charles Lee Ray (Brad Dourif), a serial killer who uses voodoo magic to transfer his soul into a doll, Chucky, in order to avoid being caught by the police. The ritual is performed on a doll named Good Guy, which becomes possessed by Ray's spirit.

Meanwhile, Karen Spencer (Catherine Hicks) and her son Andy (Alex Vincent) move into a new home, where they discover that it was previously owned by a serial killer who had used the same voodoo ritual to transfer his soul into a doll. Unbeknownst to them, Chucky is now living in their house.

As the story unfolds, Karen begins to experience strange and terrifying events, which she initially attributes to the house's history. However, it soon becomes clear that Chucky is responsible for the haunting. The doll begins to manipulate Karen, using his charm and innocence to lure her into a trap.

Andy, who has been struggling with his mother's recent death, forms a bond with Chucky, unaware of the doll's true nature. As the days pass, Andy starts to notice that something is off about Chucky, but he cannot quite put his finger on it.

As the body count rises, Karen and Detective Mike Norris (Chris Sarandon) begin to investigate the strange occurrences in the house. They soon discover that Chucky was once a serial killer who had been killed by a police officer, but his spirit had managed to transfer into the doll.

In the climactic final act, Karen and Andy are trapped in the house with Chucky, who has become increasingly aggressive and violent. In a desperate bid to stop him, Karen uses the voodoo ritual that Ray used to transfer his soul into the doll, hoping to trap Chucky's spirit once again.

However, Chucky proves to be too powerful, and he manages to escape the ritual. In a final confrontation, Andy is forced to kill Chucky with a shotgun, but not before the doll reveals his true nature and taunts him with his own mortality.

The movie ends with Karen, who has been traumatized by her experiences, being taken away by social services, leaving Andy alone in the house. As the credits roll, it is revealed that Chucky's spirit may still be alive, setting the stage for a sequel.

Overall, Child's Play is a classic horror film that combines elements of supernatural terror and dark humor to create a unique viewing experience. The movie's success spawned a franchise with multiple sequels, remakes, and spin-offs, cementing its place as a beloved horror icon.

documents.title: The Cat in the Hat
documents.tagline: Don't mess with the hat.
documents.overview: During a rainy day, and while their mother is out, Conrad and Sally, and their pet fish, are visited by the mischievous Cat in the Hat. Fun soon turns to mayhem, and the siblings must figure out how to rid themselves of the maniacal Cat.
documents.plot:
The Cat in the Hat is a 2003 live-action/CGI comedy film directed by Bo Welch, based on the children's book of the same name by Dr. Seuss. The movie stars Mike Myers as the iconic character of the Cat in the Hat.

The story begins with two mischievous children, Sally (Dakota Fanning) and her brother Conrad (Spencer Breslin), who are left alone at home on a rainy day while their mother is away. The kids are bored and looking for something to do when they hear a knock at the door. To their surprise, it's the Cat in the Hat (Mike Myers), a mischievous and eccentric feline with a penchant for trouble.

The Cat in the Hat promises to entertain the children and keep them out of trouble, but his antics quickly spiral out of control. He brings along two of his friends, Thing 1 and Thing 2 (also played by Mike Myers), who are just as mischievous as he is. The trio wreaks havoc on the house, causing chaos and destruction wherever they go.

As the day progresses, the Cat in the Hat's antics become more and more outrageous, with the children getting into all sorts of trouble. However, despite the chaos, the kids begin to enjoy themselves and have a blast with their new feline friend.

Meanwhile, the mother (Kelly Preston) is frantically trying to find a way to get home from her trip, but she's stuck in traffic due to the rain. The Cat in the Hat tries to help her by creating a diversion, but things only get worse.

As the day comes to an end, the Cat in the Hat realizes that he has gone too far and that it's time for him to leave. He cleans up the mess he made and says goodbye to the children, who are both relieved and disappointed that their fun-filled adventure is over.

In the end, the mother returns home, none the wiser about the chaos that occurred while she was away. The Cat in the Hat disappears into thin air, leaving behind a note for the children that reads: "I'm off to find something else to do... but don't worry, I'll be back soon!"

Overall, The Cat in the Hat is a fun and entertaining film that brings Dr. Seuss's beloved character to life on the big screen. While it may not be perfect, it's a delightful and lighthearted movie that's sure to bring smiles to the faces of both kids and adults alike.

documents.title: After the Sunset
documents.tagline: Who will walk away?
documents.overview: An FBI agent is suspicious of two master thieves, quietly enjoying their retirement near what may - or may not - be the biggest score of their careers.
documents.plot:
After the Sunset is a 2004 action comedy film directed by Brett Ratner and starring Pierce Brosnan, Salma Hayek, and Sean Bean.

The main themes of After the Sunset revolve around:

1. Redemption: The protagonist, Charlie Cavendish (Pierce Brosnan), is a retired thief who tries to leave his past life behind. However, he's pulled back into the game when an old flame, Sandra (Salma Hayek), asks for his help in pulling off one last heist.

2. Loyalty and Betrayal: As Charlie navigates the complex web of loyalty and betrayal within his team, he must confront his own morals and values. The film explores the blurred lines between right and wrong, highlighting the consequences of choosing between personal gain and doing what's right.

3. Identity and Self-Discovery: Throughout the film, Charlie struggles to reconcile his past and present selves. As he navigates the world of high-stakes thievery, he begins to question who he truly is and what he wants from life.

4. Love and Sacrifice: The relationship between Charlie and Sandra serves as a catalyst for the plot, highlighting the complexities of love, loyalty, and sacrifice. The film shows how these themes can both drive us forward and hold us back.

5. Deception and Appearance vs Reality: After the Sunset is full of twists and turns, keeping viewers guessing about who to trust. This theme speaks to the idea that appearances can be deceiving, and that nothing is as it seems.

Overall, After the Sunset is a thrilling ride filled with action, humor, and heart, exploring complex themes that keep audiences engaged until the very end.

documents.title: We Were Soldiers
documents.tagline: 400 U.S paratroopers. 4,000 Vietnamese soldiers. 12,000 miles away from home. 1 man led them into battle.
documents.overview: The story of the first major battle of the American phase of the Vietnam War and the soldiers on both sides that fought it.
documents.plot:
We Were Soldiers is a 2002 American war drama film directed by Randall Wallace, based on the book "We Were Soldiers Once... And Young" by Harold G. Schrier and George E. Wahlen. The film stars Mel Gibson as Lieutenant Colonel Hal Moore, a U.S. Army officer who led a company of soldiers during the Battle of Ia Drang in 1965.

The film begins with Lieutenant Colonel Hal Moore (Mel Gibson) arriving in Vietnam with his company, A Company, 1st Battalion, 7th Cavalry Regiment. The unit is tasked with conducting reconnaissance and gathering intelligence on the enemy. As they settle into their new surroundings, tensions rise between the American soldiers and the local Vietnamese villagers.

The story takes a dramatic turn when the North Vietnamese Army (NVA) launches a surprise attack on A Company's position in the Ia Drang Valley. The battle is intense and chaotic, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. Despite being outnumbered, Lieutenant Colonel Moore's leadership and tactical skills help to hold off the NVA, but not before several of his soldiers are killed or wounded.

As the battle rages on, it becomes clear that the NVA is using guerrilla tactics, employing hit-and-run attacks and booby traps to devastating effect. The American soldiers are forced to adapt quickly in order to survive, but they soon realize that they are facing a formidable enemy.

The film's climax features an intense and emotional confrontation between Lieutenant Colonel Moore and his men as they fight for their lives against overwhelming odds. Despite being vastly outnumbered, the Americans manage to hold off the NVA long enough for reinforcements to arrive, but not before several of their comrades have fallen in battle.

In the aftermath of the battle, Lieutenant Colonel Moore is hailed as a hero by his superiors, but he is also deeply shaken by the experience. The film ends with him reflecting on the cost of war and the sacrifices made by those who fight it.

Throughout the film, Mel Gibson delivers a powerful performance as Lieutenant Colonel Hal Moore, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Greg Kinnear, Adam Beach, and Sam Elliott, also deliver strong performances that add to the overall impact of the film.

Overall, We Were Soldiers is a gripping and intense war drama that explores the complexities and challenges of modern warfare. The film's attention to historical detail and its commitment to telling a true story make it a compelling watch for anyone interested in military history or drama.
production_companies: Motion Picture Production GmbH & Co. Erste KG

documents.title: Replicant
documents.tagline: A ruthless killer... to destroy him, they had to create him.
documents.overview: Scientists create a genetic clone of a serial killer in order to help catch the killer, teaming up with two cops.
documents.plot:
Replicant is a 2001 American science fiction action film directed by Ringo Lam, starring Jean-Claude Van Damme in a dual role opposite Michael Rooker. It was the second collaboration between Van Damme and the Hong Kong director and the third time Van Damme played two characters in one film, after Double Impact and Maximum Risk. Shot in Bulgaria and Vancouver, it received a limited theatrical release in many European countries and went straight to DVD in the United States on September 18, 2001.

In Seattle, Detective Jake Riley has spent three years hunting Edward "the Torch" Garrotte, a serial killer who murders mothers and sets their bodies on fire.
