Days before Jake retires, Garrotte strikes again and then taunts him by phone during his retirement party, threatening his friends and family. A secret government agency recruits Jake as a consultant on an unusual project: from DNA found at a crime scene, it has grown a clone of Garrotte, a man with an adult body but a child's mind who shares his genetic memories and a telepathic link with him. Jake is to train this Replicant and use that link to track the killer down.

Jake treats the Replicant harshly, fearing that the killer's instincts will surface, while the clone looks to him for protection and slowly learns about the world. After a bomb meant for Jake, the Replicant meets Garrotte in a bar and later in a parking garage, where the killer tries to persuade his "brother" that Jake cannot be trusted. Flashbacks reveal that Garrotte, whose real name is Luc Savard, was abused by a mother who killed her husband and tried to burn down their home. Tracing him to a hospital where his mother has just died, Jake and the Replicant are attacked, and in a final fight in the furnace room the Replicant realizes he is not a killer. When Garrotte strikes the clone with a shovel, Jake shoots him. The Replicant pulls Jake to safety before an explosion and is presumed dead, but weeks later he leaves a music box in Jake's mailbox as thanks for his help, revealing that he survived.

Van Damme plays both Garrotte and the Replicant and Rooker plays Jake, with Catherine Dent as Jake's wife, Anne, and Marnie Alton. Critics were mixed: only 27% of the eleven reviews counted by Rotten Tomatoes were positive, but some reviewers called it one of Van Damme's best films since Bloodsport and praised its well-staged action and his physical agility.

documents.title: Kevin & Perry Go Large
documents.tagline: All they want to do is... Do it!!!
documents.overview: When stubborn, spotty Kevin and his equally hopeless best friend Perry go on holiday to the party island Ibiza, they see it as their big chance to become superstar club DJs and, more importantly, to lose their virginities. But they aren't prepared for the interference of top DJ Eyeball Paul, not to mention the embarrassment factor of Kevin's long-suffering parents.
documents.plot:
Kevin & Perry Go Large is a British comedy film that revolves around the misadventures of two friends, Kevin and Perry, who embark on a journey to become famous as extreme sports enthusiasts. The movie explores themes of friendship, camaraderie, and the consequences of one's actions.

At its core, the film delves into the idea of chasing fame and fortune, and the lengths people will go to achieve it. Kevin and Perry's antics are driven by their desire for recognition and admiration, which often leads them down a path of reckless behavior. As they navigate through various extreme sports challenges, they must confront the consequences of their actions and learn valuable lessons about responsibility and loyalty.

The movie also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery, as Kevin and Perry struggle to find their place in the world beyond their friendship. Through their experiences, they are forced to re-evaluate their priorities and values, ultimately emerging with a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

Overall, Kevin & Perry Go Large is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and satire to explore themes of fame, friendship, and self-discovery.

documents.title: Pinocchio
documents.overview: Roberto Benigni adapts the classic children's tale by Carlo Collodi for the big-budget family-oriented comedy Pinocchio.
documents.plot:
Pinocchio is a 2002 Italian fantasy comedy-drama co-written and directed by Roberto Benigni, who also plays the title role, adapted from Carlo Collodi's 1883 novel The Adventures of Pinocchio. Nicoletta Braschi plays the Blue Fairy, with Carlo Giuffrè as Geppetto, Kim Rossi Stuart as Lucignolo and Peppe Barra as the Talking Cricket. Filmed in Italy and in Kalkara, Malta, it was dedicated to the costume and production designer Danilo Donati, who died in December 2001.

A magical log tumbles from a cart and comes to rest at the door of the poor woodcarver Geppetto, who carves it into a puppet and names it Pinocchio. The puppet springs to life and runs riot through the town, and Geppetto is blamed and jailed while Pinocchio gets away. Scolded at home by the Talking Cricket, he lashes out at it, but hungry and tired he promises his father to attend school, and Geppetto sells his only coat to buy him schoolbooks. Instead, the puppet wanders into a string of misadventures. He is nearly devoured by the giant puppet master Mangiafuoco, who then gives him five gold coins; he is swindled by the Fox and the Cat, who persuade him to plant his money in a Field of Miracles; and he is saved from hanging by the Blue Fairy, who urges him to mend his ways. His nose grows when he lies, and absurdly, when he reports the theft of his coins, he is himself jailed for foolishness, where he meets the mischievous Lucignolo.

After his release, Pinocchio tries to rescue Geppetto, who has gone to sea looking for him, and reunites with the Blue Fairy. Lured by Lucignolo to the Land of Toys, he is transformed into a donkey and sold to a circus. Thrown into the sea, he becomes a puppet again and is swallowed by a giant shark, inside which he finds Geppetto, and the two escape together. Pinocchio works on a farm to nurse his father back to health and witnesses the death of Lucignolo, who has also become a donkey. Rewarded for his goodness, Pinocchio is turned by the Blue Fairy into a real boy and sets off for his first day of school.

One of the most expensive Italian films ever made, it was a hit in Italy but grossed about $41 million worldwide. Italian reviews were mixed, while Miramax's English-dubbed version was panned and won a Razzie for Benigni. Donati won two posthumous David di Donatello Awards.

documents.title: Peter Pan
documents.tagline: All children grow up except one.
documents.overview: In stifling Edwardian London, Wendy Darling mesmerizes her brothers every night with bedtime tales of swordplay, swashbuckling and the fearsome Captain Hook. But the children become the heroes of an even greater story, when Peter Pan flies into their nursery one night and leads them over moonlit rooftops through a galaxy of stars and to the lush jungles of Neverland.
documents.plot:
Peter Pan is a 2003 fantasy adventure film directed by P. J. Hogan, who wrote the screenplay with Michael Goldenberg, adapted from J. M. Barrie's 1904 play and 1911 novel. Jeremy Sumpter plays Peter, Rachel Hurd-Wood plays Wendy Darling and Ludivine Sagnier plays Tinker Bell, while Jason Isaacs, following stage tradition, takes the double role of Captain Hook and Wendy's father, George Darling. Olivia Williams and Lynn Redgrave co-star.

In Edwardian London, Wendy entertains her younger brothers, John and Michael, with tales of Captain Hook, unaware that Peter Pan is listening at the nursery window. Their Aunt Millicent urges the parents to think about Wendy's future prospects. When Peter returns one night, the family's dog, Nana, bites off his shadow, and after Wendy sews it back on he invites her and her brothers to Neverland to tell stories to his Lost Boys. Sprinkled with Tinker Bell's fairy dust, they fly away.

In Neverland the children are soon attacked by Hook's pirates. The jealous Tinker Bell tricks the Lost Boys into shooting Wendy down, but an acorn Peter gave her saves her life, and Peter banishes the fairy. Wendy becomes a mother to the Lost Boys, with Peter as their father. After Hook captures John, Michael and the princess Tiger Lily, Peter and the boys rescue them, and the pirate captain is chased off by the crocodile that has stalked him for years. Peter and Wendy share a dance among the fairies, but when she asks him to admit his feelings, he angrily insists she go home, unable to accept love if it means growing up. Wendy decides to return to London, and the Lost Boys choose to go with her. Hook's crew captures them and poisons Peter's medicine, which Tinker Bell drinks to save him. Peter's pleas for everyone in Neverland and London to believe in fairies revive her, and together they free the prisoners. Hook gains the power of flight, taunts Peter that Wendy will grow up and marry someone else, and nearly defeats him, but Wendy's kiss restores Peter's spirit, and Hook ends up inside the crocodile. Peter flies everyone home aboard the fairy-dusted Jolly Roger; the Darlings adopt the Lost Boys and Peter returns to Neverland, as Wendy goes on telling his story to her descendants.

It was the first live-action theatrical version to cast a boy as Peter. Released at Christmas 2003, it was well reviewed, with 77% on Rotten Tomatoes and 64 on Metacritic, but grossed only about $122 million worldwide amid competition from The Return of the King.

documents.title: The Medallion
documents.overview: A Hong Kong detective suffers a fatal accident involving a mysterious medallion and is transformed into an immortal warrior with superhuman powers.
documents.plot:
The Medallion is a 2003 action-comedy film directed by Harald Zwart and starring Jackie Chan. The movie follows the story of Keung, a young police officer who must protect a beautiful woman named Lulu from a group of assassins.

The main themes of The Medallion include:

1. Protection and Loyalty: The film highlights the importance of protecting those you care about, particularly women in need of help. Keung's loyalty to Lulu drives the plot and his actions are motivated by a desire to keep her safe.
2. Cultural Identity: The movie explores the cultural differences between China and the United States, as well as the challenges faced by immigrants trying to adapt to new environments. Keung's struggles to balance his traditional Chinese upbringing with his American life serve as a backdrop for the story.
3. Self-Discovery: Throughout the film, Keung learns more about himself and his place in the world. He begins to question his own identity and find his purpose beyond just being a police officer.
4. Action and Adventure: The Medallion is known for its high-energy action sequences, which drive the plot forward and keep the audience engaged.

The movie's tone is lighthearted and humorous, with plenty of comedic moments courtesy of Jackie Chan's signature physical comedy style. Overall, The Medallion is a fun, entertaining film that balances action, adventure, and heartwarming moments.

documents.title: Barbershop
documents.tagline: Everyone's gettin' lined up.
documents.overview: A day in the life of a barbershop on the south side of Chicago. Calvin, who inherited the struggling business from his deceased father, views the shop as nothing but a burden and waste of his time. After selling the shop to a local loan shark, Calvin slowly begins to see his father's vision and legacy and struggles with the notion that he just sold it out.
documents.plot:
Barbershop is a 2002 American comedy film directed by Tim Story, produced by Reginald Hudlin and Don Cheadle, and written by Rick Famuyiwa. The movie takes place in Chicago's South Side and revolves around the lives of three barbers: Calvin Palmer (Ice Cube), Eddie (Cedric the Entertainer), and Marnell (Erik Prince).

The main themes of Barbershop include:

1. Community and camaraderie: The film highlights the strong bonds between the barbers, who serve as a support system for each other and their clients. They often engage in witty banter, share stories, and offer advice, creating a sense of community and belonging.
2. Friendship and loyalty: Calvin, Eddie, and Marnell are more than just coworkers; they're friends who have each other's backs. The movie showcases the importance of loyal friendships and how they can help navigate life's challenges.
3. Social commentary on racism and stereotypes: Barbershop tackles issues like racism, police brutality, and stereotyping in a lighthearted yet thought-provoking way. The film uses humor to address these sensitive topics, making it more palatable for a wider audience.
4. Self-discovery and personal growth: As the story unfolds, each character faces their own struggles and undergoes significant personal growth. Calvin, in particular, learns to let go of his anger and resentment towards the police, while Eddie finds his place in the world beyond the barbershop.

The movie's success can be attributed to its well-developed characters, engaging storyline, and timely commentary on social issues. Barbershop has become a cult classic, praised for its humor, heart, and authentic portrayal of African American life in the early 2000s.

documents.title: Cradle 2 the Grave
documents.tagline: Mortal enemies make dangerous friends.
documents.overview: Gang leader Tony pulls off a major diamond heist with his crew, but cop-turned-criminal Ling knows who has the loot and responds by kidnapping Tony's daughter and holding her for ransom. Unfortunately, Tony's lost the diamonds as well. As he frantically searches for his daughter and the jewels, Tony pairs with a high-kicking government agent who once worked with Ling and seeks revenge on him.
documents.plot:
Cradle 2 the Grave is an action-adventure film released in 2003, directed by Andrzej Bartkowiak and starring Jet Li, DMX, and Gabrielle Union.

The main themes of Cradle 2 the Grave revolve around:

1. Family: The movie explores the theme of family, particularly the bond between a father and daughter. Nick (Jet Li) is a former Special Forces operative who must protect his daughter, Sophie (Gina Lee), from her mother's ruthless ex-boyfriend, Verona (DMX).
2. Loyalty and Betrayal: Throughout the film, characters are forced to confront their loyalties and make difficult choices between personal relationships and professional obligations.
3. Redemption: Nick's character arc is centered around redemption, as he seeks to atone for past mistakes and protect those he cares about.
4. Power and Corruption: The villainous Verona (DMX) serves as a symbol of the corrupting influence of power, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition and greed.

The plot follows Nick, who is hired by Sophie's mother to retrieve a valuable artifact from Verona, who has stolen it. As the story unfolds, Nick must navigate a complex web of loyalty, deception, and betrayal to protect his daughter and uncover the truth about her past.

Overall, Cradle 2 the Grave is an action-packed film with a strong emphasis on family, loyalty, and redemption, set against a backdrop of corruption and power struggles.

documents.title: Mean Girls
documents.tagline: Welcome to girl world.
documents.overview: Cady Heron is a hit with The Plastics, the A-list girl clique at her new school, until she makes the mistake of falling for Aaron Samuels, the ex-boyfriend of alpha Plastic Regina George.
documents.plot:
Mean Girls is a 2004 American teen comedy film directed by Mark S. Waters and written by Tina Fey. The movie follows the story of Cady Heron, a 16-year-old girl who moves to Illinois after being homeschooled in Africa, where she was raised by her parents.

The beginning of the movie shows Cady (played by Lindsay Lohan) struggling to adjust to her new life in the United States. She is awkward and naive, but eager to fit in with her peers. At her new school, Cady meets outcasts Janis Ian (Lizzy Caplan) and Damian Leigh (Daniel Franzese), who take her under their wing.

However, Cady soon becomes infatuated with "The Plastics," a popular and influential clique consisting of Regina George (Rachel McAdams), Gretchen Wieners (Lacey Chabert), and Karen Smith (Amanda Seyfried). The Plastics are led by Regina, who is the queen bee of the school. Cady quickly becomes part of The Plastics, adopting their mannerisms and behavior.

As Cady becomes more and more entrenched in The Plastics, she begins to abandon her old friends Janis and Damian. She also starts to sabotage her relationships with them, leading to a rift between them. Meanwhile, Regina's popularity is threatened by a new student, Cady, who is seen as a threat to her status.

The plot development of the movie takes a turn when Cady discovers that Regina has been spreading rumors about Janis and manipulating people to get what she wants. Cady begins to question her loyalty to The Plastics and ultimately decides to take down Regina from the inside.

In the climax of the movie, Cady orchestrates a plan with Janis and Damian to expose Regina's mean-spirited behavior and bring her down. The plan involves a series of pranks and sabotage that ultimately lead to Regina's downfall.

The ending of the movie shows Cady having learned a valuable lesson about the dangers of cliques and the importance of being true to oneself. She has also found a new sense of friendship with Janis and Damian, and has broken free from The Plastics' grasp. The movie ends on a positive note, with Cady embracing her individuality and finding her place in the world.

Throughout the movie, Mean Girls explores themes of identity, peer pressure, and the consequences of one's actions. The film features a talented cast, witty dialogue, and memorable characters that have become iconic in popular culture.

documents.title: Kangaroo Jack
documents.tagline: He Stole The Money... And He's Not Giving It Back.
documents.overview: Two childhood friends — a New York hairstylist and a wanna-be musician — get mixed-up with the mob and are forced to deliver $50,000 to Australia, but things go all wrong when the money is lost to a wild kangaroo.
documents.plot:
Kangaroo Jack is a 2003 American comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and starring Chris Farley and Simon Baker.

The movie begins with Jack Slattery (played by Chris Farley), an eccentric and clumsy Australian man who lives in New York City. Jack's life is turned upside down when he is killed by a kangaroo that escapes from the Bronx Zoo, where he works as a zookeeper. However, instead of dying, Jack finds himself transported to the outback of Australia.

In the outback, Jack meets an Aboriginal Australian man named Kip (played by Simon Baker), who helps him adjust to his new surroundings. As Jack tries to find a way back home, he learns about the harsh realities of life in the outback and forms a bond with Kip and his family.

Meanwhile, Jack's brother, Mike Slattery (played by Bokeem Woodbine), is searching for him, believing that he has abandoned his family. Mike hires a bounty hunter named Les Stroud (played by John Cleese) to track down Jack and bring him back home.

As the story unfolds, Jack must navigate the challenges of the outback, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and cultural differences. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about family, friendship, and finding one's place in the world.

Throughout his journey, Jack also discovers that Kip is being pursued by a group of ruthless poachers who are after his family's sacred land. Jack decides to help Kip protect his family and their home, leading to a thrilling showdown with the poachers.

In the end, Jack finds a way back to New York City, but not before saying goodbye to Kip and his family. Mike finally tracks him down and brings him back home, where he is welcomed back by his family. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Jack reflecting on the lessons he learned in the outback and the importance of finding one's place in the world.

Overall, Kangaroo Jack is a lighthearted and entertaining film that combines elements of comedy, adventure, and drama. While it may not be a critically acclaimed movie, it has its moments of humor and heart, making it an enjoyable watch for fans of Chris Farley and Simon Baker.

documents.title: The Hunted
documents.tagline: Some men should not be found.
documents.overview: In the wilderness of British Columbia, two hunters are tracked and viciously murdered by Aaron Hallum. A former Special Operations instructor is approached and asked to apprehend Hallum—his former student—who has 'gone rogue' after suffering severe battle stress from his time in Kosovo.
documents.plot:
The Hunted is a 2003 American action thriller directed by William Friedkin. It stars Tommy Lee Jones as L. T. Bonham, a retired civilian instructor who trained special forces soldiers in survival and combat skills, and Benicio del Toro as Aaron Hallam, a former student who has become a killer, with Connie Nielsen as FBI agent Abby Durrell. The film is a manhunt story set largely in the forests of the Pacific Northwest.

During the war in Kosovo, special forces operator Aaron Hallam carries out the assassination of a Serbian military leader and is awarded the Silver Star, but he is deeply traumatized by the atrocities he has witnessed. Years later, in a forest park in Oregon, he confronts two deer hunters with sniper rifles whom he suspects of being something else, and kills them both with a knife. Meanwhile, L. T. Bonham, the expert tracker who taught Hallam how to survive and kill, lives in seclusion in British Columbia, where he frees wildlife from traps.

The FBI enlists Bonham to help find the killer. He quickly determines that a single man, not a group, was responsible, and recognizes the work of his former pupil. Bonham tracks Hallam alone through the woods and the two men fight before Hallam is captured. Hallam claims that the hunters were government agents sent to kill him. When he is handed over to members of his former unit, he realizes that they intend to silence him permanently and escapes, killing his escort. The pursuit moves from the wilderness into the city of Portland, as Bonham, the FBI and military operatives chase Hallam across the urban landscape, culminating in a brutal hand-to-hand confrontation between teacher and student armed with knives they have made themselves.

Friedkin emphasizes realistic, close-quarters knife fighting and wilderness tracking, drawing on the outdoorsman Tom Brown Jr., who served as technical advisor, and explores the psychological cost of training men to kill.

The Hunted opened on March 14, 2003, at number three at the North American box office, but grossed only about 45.5 million dollars worldwide against a 55 million dollar budget. Reviews were largely negative, with 30 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 40.

documents.title: Friday
documents.tagline: A lot can go down between thursday and saturday...
documents.overview: Craig and Smokey are two guys in Los Angeles hanging out on their porch on a Friday afternoon, smoking and drinking, looking for something to do.
documents.plot:
Friday is a classic American comedy film released in 1995 by New Line Cinema. Directed by F. Gary Gray, the movie stars Ice Cube, Chris Tucker, Nia Long, and John Witherspoon.

The story takes place on a typical Friday afternoon in South Central Los Angeles. The main character, Craig Jones (played by Ice Cube), is a laid-back and responsible high school student who has just finished his final exams. He's looking forward to a relaxing weekend with his friends and family.

However, things take a turn when Craig's friend Smokey (played by Chris Tucker) comes over to his house, uninvited. Smokey is a hyperactive and eccentric friend who always seems to find trouble. Despite their differences, the two have been friends since childhood, and Craig tries to accommodate Smokey's antics.

As the day progresses, Smokey convinces Craig to join him on a series of misadventures, including a botched attempt to sell marijuana, a wild ride through the streets, and a chaotic encounter with a group of thugs. Meanwhile, Craig's girlfriend, Dee (played by Nia Long), is trying to get her life together after a recent breakup.

Throughout the movie, the characters' interactions are filled with witty banter, humorous observations, and relatable struggles. The film's humor is rooted in its portrayal of urban life, tackling topics like racism, poverty, and social inequality.

As the day wears on, Craig and Smokey find themselves in a series of absurd situations, including a wild goose chase through the neighborhood and a confrontation with a group of gang members. Despite the chaos, the two friends ultimately come out on top, learning valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and growing up.

The movie's climax features an iconic scene where Craig and Smokey are chased by a group of thugs, leading to a thrilling showdown in front of Craig's house. In the end, Craig emerges victorious, having successfully defended his home and his friend.

Friday was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $27 million at the box office on its opening weekend. The film received widespread acclaim for its authentic portrayal of urban life, clever writing, and outstanding performances from the cast. It has since become a cult classic, widely regarded as one of the greatest comedies of the 1990s.

Overall, Friday is a hilarious and heartwarming movie that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and growing up in a way that resonates with audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Remember the Titans
documents.tagline: History is written by the winners.
documents.overview: After leading his football team to 15 winning seasons, coach Bill Yoast is demoted and replaced by Herman Boone – tough, opinionated and as different from the beloved Yoast as he could be. The two men learn to overcome their differences and turn a group of hostile young men into champions.
documents.plot:
Remember the Titans is a biographical sports drama film directed by Boaz Yakin and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie is based on the true story of the integration of the T.C. Williams High School football team in Alexandria, Virginia in 1971.

The film begins with the introduction of Coach Herman Boone (Denzel Washington), a former NFL player who is hired to coach the newly integrated T.C. Williams High School football team. The school has just been desegregated, and tensions are high between the white and black students. Coach Boone is determined to bring the team together and teach them about unity, discipline, and teamwork.

Initially, the team struggles to come together due to racial tensions and conflicts. The white players, led by Jerry "Rev" Harris (Wood Harris), are resistant to change and feel threatened by the presence of African American players on the team. Meanwhile, the black players, led by Julius Campbell (Ryan Hurst), are eager to prove themselves and show that they belong.

As Coach Boone works with his team, he uses a unique approach to build unity and trust among the players. He divides the team into two units: the "A" unit, which consists of the white players, and the "B" unit, which consists of the African American players. The two units are initially separate, but Coach Boone encourages them to work together on the field.

Through a series of challenges and setbacks, including a disastrous first game against their arch-rivals, the T.C. Williams team learns to put aside their differences and come together as a cohesive unit. Along the way, Coach Boone teaches his players about the importance of teamwork, discipline, and respect for one another.

As the season progresses, the team begins to gel, and they start to win games. The team's success is not just about winning, but also about the bonds that are formed between the players. The film culminates with a thrilling championship game against their arch-rivals, which the T.C. Williams team wins.

The movie ends on a triumphant note, with Coach Boone and his team celebrating their victory. However, the film also touches on the challenges faced by the team in the aftermath of their success. The players must navigate the complexities of racial tensions and social change, both on and off the field.

Throughout the film, Denzel Washington delivers a powerful performance as Coach Herman Boone, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Wood Harris, Ryan Hurst, and Will Patton, deliver strong performances that add to the film's emotional impact.

Overall, Remember the Titans is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the power of sports to bring people together and overcome adversity.

documents.title: Godzilla 2000: Millennium
documents.original_title: ゴジラ2000 ミレニアム
documents.tagline: Witness! A new era of Godzilla!
documents.overview: An independent group of researchers called the Godzilla Prediction Network (GPN) actively track Godzilla as he makes landfall in Nemuro.  Matters are further complicated when a giant meteor is discovered in the Ibaragi Prefecture. The mysterious rock begins to levitate as it's true intentions for the world and Godzilla are revealed.
documents.plot:
Godzilla 2000: Millennium is a thought-provoking film that delves into the consequences of playing with nature and the dangers of unchecked technological advancement. The movie takes place in an alternate timeline where Godzilla has been awakened due to nuclear testing on the Odo Island.

At its core, Godzilla 2000: Millennium explores the theme of environmentalism and the devastating effects of humanity's reckless disregard for the natural world. The film portrays a world where humans have become increasingly dependent on technology and scientific progress, leading them to neglect their responsibility towards the environment. This is exemplified through the character of Dr. Niko Tatopoulos, who becomes obsessed with harnessing Godzilla's power for human gain.

The movie also touches upon the theme of existentialism, as it raises questions about humanity's place in the world and its relationship with nature. The character of Godzilla serves as a symbol of the uncontrollable forces that lie beyond human understanding, highlighting the limitations of human knowledge and control.

Furthermore, Godzilla 2000: Millennium can be seen as a commentary on the dangers of scientific hubris and the consequences of tampering with nature. The film's portrayal of a world where scientists are willing to risk everything to harness Godzilla's power serves as a warning about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of humility in the face of nature's unpredictability.

Overall, Godzilla 2000: Millennium is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its narrative and characters.

documents.title: Pay It Forward
documents.tagline: When someone does you a big favor, don't pay it back... Pay It Forward
documents.overview: Like some other kids, 12-year-old Trevor McKinney believed in the goodness of human nature. Like many other kids, he was determined to change the world for the better. Unlike most other kids, he succeeded.
documents.plot:
Pay It Forward is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the power of kindness, empathy, and the ripple effect of good deeds. The movie follows the story of Trevor McKinney, a young boy who decides to pay it forward by doing good for others, rather than waiting for someone else to do something good for him.

At its core, Pay It Forward is a film about the transformative power of kindness and generosity. Through Trevor's journey, we see how small acts of kindness can have a profound impact on those around us, creating a chain reaction of good deeds that can spread far and wide. The movie highlights the importance of empathy and understanding in breaking down social barriers and building connections between people.

The film also explores themes of hope, resilience, and the human spirit's capacity for growth and transformation. Trevor's story is one of overcoming adversity and finding ways to make a positive impact in the world, even in the face of challenges and obstacles. Through his character, we see the importance of staying true to oneself and pursuing one's passions, even when faced with uncertainty or skepticism.

One of the most striking aspects of Pay It Forward is its exploration of the concept of "paying it forward." The movie shows how small acts of kindness can be passed on from person to person, creating a wave of good deeds that can have far-reaching consequences. This theme speaks to the idea that we are all connected and that our actions can have a profound impact on those around us.

Overall, Pay It Forward is a film that celebrates the power of kindness, empathy, and generosity, while also exploring themes of hope, resilience, and personal growth.

documents.title: You Don't Mess with the Zohan
documents.original_title: You Don't Mess with the Zohan
documents.tagline: Lather. Rinse. Save the world.
documents.overview: An Israeli counterterrorism soldier with a secretly fabulous ambition to become a Manhattan hairstylist. Zohan's desire runs so deep that he'll do anything -- including faking his own death and going head-to-head with an Arab cab driver -- to make his dreams come true.
documents.plot:
You Don't Mess with the Zohan is a 2008 American action comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan, starring Adam Sandler as the main character. The movie follows the story of Zohan Dimski (Adam Sandler), an Israeli Mossad agent who fakes his own death to pursue his dream of becoming a hairstylist in New York City.

The film begins with Zohan working for the Mossad, where he is tasked with infiltrating and gathering intelligence on a terrorist organization. During a mission, Zohan kills several terrorists, but not before one of them shoots him in the head. Believing himself to be mortally wounded, Zohan fakes his own death to escape and make his way to New York City.

In New York, Zohan assumes a new identity as "Zohar" and starts working at a hair salon. He quickly becomes popular with his clients due to his exceptional hairstyling skills and charming personality. Meanwhile, he also meets Dalia (Emmanuelle Chriqui), a beautiful Israeli woman who is unaware of Zohan's true identity.

As Zohan navigates his new life in New York, he must confront his past as an Israeli agent and the danger that still follows him. He also becomes embroiled in a plot by a terrorist named Khalil (John Turturro) to blow up the Statue of Liberty.

Throughout the film, Zohan's character undergoes significant development as he learns to balance his old life with his new one. He must confront his feelings for Dalia and decide whether to reveal his true identity to her or keep living a lie.

The plot thickens when Khalil discovers Zohan's location and threatens to harm him unless he agrees to help him carry out the terrorist attack on the Statue of Liberty. Zohan must use his Mossad training to foil Khalil's plans and save the day.

In the end, Zohan successfully thwarts the terrorist attack, and Dalia finally discovers his true identity as an Israeli agent. Despite this revelation, she chooses to stay with him, and they share a romantic kiss. The film concludes with Zohan returning to Israel, where he is welcomed back as a hero for saving the Statue of Liberty.

Overall, You Don't Mess with the Zohan is a lighthearted, comedic take on the action genre, with plenty of humor and wit throughout. Adam Sandler shines in his starring role, bringing his signature charm and charisma to the character of Zohan Dimski.

documents.title: [REC]²
documents.tagline: Fear Revisited
documents.overview: The action continues from [REC], with the medical officer and a SWAT team outfitted with video cameras are sent into the sealed off apartment to control the situation.
documents.plot:
[REC]² is a Spanish horror film directed by Jaume Balagueró and Paco Plaza, released in 2009. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2007 film [REC], which was also produced by Filmax.

The main themes of [REC]² revolve around the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to the supernatural forces that are unleashed in the first film. The story takes place after the events of the original, where Angela Vidal (Manuela Velasco) is still trying to come to terms with what happened to her and her crew.

One of the primary themes of [REC]² is the exploration of grief, trauma, and the psychological effects of experiencing a traumatic event. Angela's character is still reeling from the aftermath of the events in the first film, and her inability to cope with her emotions leads to a downward spiral of despair and desperation.

Another significant theme present in [REC]² is the concept of isolation and confinement. The characters are trapped in a small apartment building, which serves as a metaphor for their own personal prisons. As the situation escalates, they realize that they are not just fighting for survival but also struggling to break free from their own emotional shackles.

The film also delves into the idea of the supernatural forces being a manifestation of human fear and guilt. The virus-like entity that is spreading throughout the building seems to be feeding on the characters' darkest emotions, making them question what is real and what is just their own paranoia.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds up as Angela's grip on reality begins to slip, and she becomes increasingly unhinged. This serves as a commentary on how trauma can affect individuals in different ways, leading to varying degrees of psychological instability.

The ending of [REC]² leaves room for interpretation, but it seems to suggest that Angela has finally found some semblance of peace, having confronted her demons and come to terms with what happened to her. However, the film's conclusion also raises questions about whether she is truly free from the trauma or if it will continue to haunt her.

Overall, [REC]² explores themes of grief, isolation, and the supernatural forces that can consume us when we're not prepared. The movie builds upon the tension and suspense of the first film, creating a thrilling and unsettling experience for the viewer.

documents.title: The Strangers
documents.tagline: Lock the door. Pretend you're safe.
documents.overview: After returning from a wedding reception, a couple staying in an isolated vacation house receive a knock on the door in the mid-hours of the night. What ensues is a violent invasion by three strangers, their faces hidden behind masks. The couple find themselves in a violent struggle, in which they go beyond what either of them thought capable in order to survive.
documents.plot:
The Strangers is a 2008 American psychological horror film directed by Bryan Bertino and written by Bertino and Adam Wingard. The movie follows a young couple, James Hoyt (Scott Speedman) and Kristen McKay (Liv Tyler), who are on a romantic getaway to a secluded lake house in upstate New York.

The beginning of the film sets the tone for the rest of the story, showcasing the idyllic relationship between James and Kristen. They arrive at their destination, a beautiful lake house with breathtaking views, eager to spend some quality time together. As they settle into their new surroundings, it becomes clear that they are trying to escape the stress and mundanity of their daily lives.

However, their tranquility is short-lived. On the first night of their stay, three masked strangers - Man in the Mask (Bryan Greenberg), Pin-Up Girl (Gemma Ward), and Man with the Scars (Tom Budge) - appear at the house uninvited. The couple is shocked and terrified as the strangers begin to terrorize them, making it clear that they are not there by chance.

As the night wears on, James and Kristen try to defend themselves against the masked intruders. However, their attempts at self-defense are met with brutal force, leaving them battered and bruised. The Strangers' motives for attacking the couple remain unclear throughout the film, adding to the sense of unease and tension.

The plot development is slow-burning, building up to a climax that is both shocking and disturbing. As the night wears on, James and Kristen are subjected to physical and emotional abuse by the strangers. The film's use of long takes and close-ups creates a sense of claustrophobia, making the audience feel trapped alongside the characters.

The ending of the film is both haunting and unsettling. Without giving away too many spoilers, it becomes clear that the Strangers' true intentions are far more sinister than initially thought. The final act of the film is a masterclass in building tension, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats as they try to piece together the mystery.

One of the standout aspects of The Strangers is its use of atmosphere and suspense. The film's score, composed by Bobby Koeger, adds to the sense of unease, while the cinematography captures the isolation and vulnerability of the characters. The performances from Scott Speedman and Liv Tyler are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, The Strangers is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of isolation, vulnerability, and the breakdown of relationships. With its slow-burning tension and shocking climax, it's a must-see for fans of psychological horror.

documents.title: WALL·E
documents.tagline: After 700 years of doing what he was built for, he'll discover what he was meant for.
documents.overview: WALL·E is the last robot left on an Earth that has been overrun with garbage and all humans have fled to outer space. For 700 years he has continued to try and clean up the mess, but has developed some rather interesting human-like qualities. When a ship arrives with a sleek new type of robot, WALL·E thinks he's finally found a friend and stows away on the ship when it leaves.
documents.plot:
WALL-E is a 2008 animated science fiction film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

In the year A.D. 2105, Earth has become uninhabitable due to rampant consumerism and waste. Humans have abandoned the planet, leaving behind a desolate wasteland filled with trash and debris. The story follows WALL-E (Waste Allocation Load Lifter Earth-Class), a small waste-collecting robot who has been left on Earth to clean up the mess.

WALL-E is a small, waste-compacting robot designed by Buy-N-Large (BNL) to collect and compact trash into cubes for transportation. He spends his days collecting trash and watching old VHS tapes of humans' past lives, which he finds fascinating. WALL-E's only friends are a cockroach named M-O and a robot named AUTO, who is programmed to maintain the spaceship Axiom.

One day, a spaceship lands on Earth, carrying a small group of humans, including Captain McCrea, a spaceship captain; John, a young man; and Mary, an elderly woman. They plan to return to Earth to assess its habitability for human re-colonization. WALL-E is fascinated by the humans' arrival and begins to clean up the ship's trash, hoping to catch their attention.

However, AUTO, who has become increasingly self-aware, discovers WALL-E's attempts to communicate with the humans and decides to sabotage his efforts. AUTO orders the spaceship to leave Earth immediately, fearing that the planet's condition will be deemed uninhabitable for humans.

Despite AUTO's actions, WALL-E manages to send a message to the Axiom using a small robot he built from trash. The message is received by Captain McCrea, who becomes intrigued by the possibility of finding life on Earth. He decides to return to the planet with a team to assess its habitability.

As the humans explore Earth, they discover WALL-E's hidden underground bunker and are amazed by his resourcefulness and kindness. They also find evidence of the planet's former beauty and the devastating impact of human neglect. The humans begin to question their own role in the destruction of Earth and decide to take action to restore it.

WALL-E, who has fallen in love with a robot named EVE (Extraterrestrial Vegetation Evaluator), joins the humans on their mission to clean up Earth. Together, they work tirelessly to remove trash and debris, and WALL-E's efforts inspire the humans to take responsibility for their actions.

In the end, the humans successfully restore Earth to its former beauty, and WALL-E is hailed as a hero. The film ends with WALL-E and EVE flying off into space together, symbolizing hope and renewal for humanity.

Throughout the film, Pixar explores themes of environmentalism, consumerism, and the importance of human connection. WALL-E's story serves as a cautionary tale about the consequences of neglecting our planet and the power of individual actions to create positive change.

documents.title: The Watcher
documents.tagline: Don't go home alone.
documents.overview: FBI agent Joel Campbell, burnt-out and shell-shocked after years spent chasing serial killers, flees L.A. to begin a new life for himself in Chicago. But five months later, Joel's best laid plans are abruptly cut short when his new hometown becomes the setting for some particularly gruesome murders--murders that could only have been committed by one man: David Allen Griffin. One of Joel's most elusive and cunning nemeses, Griffin has followed his former pursuer to Chicago in order to play a sadistic game of cat and mouse. Taunting Joel with photographs of his intended victims and leaving his crime scenes meticulously free of clues in order to keep the police at bay, Griffin derives as much pleasure out of watching Joel react to every movement as watching his victims die. But when Griffin moves into Joel's inner circle, Joel must quickly find some way to stop him before someone close to him becomes the next one to die.
documents.plot:
The Watcher is an American thriller of 2000 directed by Joe Charbanic, in which a retired FBI agent in Chicago is stalked and taunted by the serial killer he once pursued. James Spader stars as Special Agent Joel Campbell, with Keanu Reeves, cast against type, as the killer David Allen Griffin, Marisa Tomei as the psychologist Dr Polly Beilman, Ernie Hudson as Special Agent in Charge Mike Ibby and Chris Ellis as Detective Hollis Mackie.

In Los Angeles, Campbell arrives moments too late to save a young woman from the killer he has been hunting, who escapes. Shattered, he quits the bureau and moves to Chicago, where he suffers guilt-induced migraines and sees the therapist Polly Beilman. When a woman in his apartment building is murdered, he pays little attention until he finds that a photograph of her was mailed to him three days before her death. He takes the evidence to Detective Mackie and realises that the killer has followed him. Ibby urges him to return to the case, but Campbell refuses until Griffin telephones him, explaining that he wants to rebuild the rapport they once shared. He will send Campbell a photograph of a woman each morning, and Campbell must find her by nine o'clock that night.

Reinstated, Campbell works with Mackie and his team, publicising the picture to identify the woman, but by the time he reaches her by phone Griffin is already in her house and kills her. The game continues with another woman the next day; the police corner Griffin, but he kills her and escapes again. That night Campbell is found unconscious in his apartment. The next photograph shows Lisa Anton, Campbell's former lover, whom Griffin murdered in Los Angeles. At her grave, Griffin waits for him and reveals that he is holding Polly hostage. Campbell negotiates to see her, and on the drive Griffin explains that he regards Campbell as a good friend and that each needs the other, while Campbell secretly calls Mackie on his phone. At a warehouse, Griffin knocks Campbell out, ties him up and begins strangling Polly. Campbell distracts him by thanking him, stabs him in the neck with a pen and shoots him with a shotgun, then escapes with Polly as the warehouse explodes. Afterwards Campbell inspects Griffin's charred corpse to be sure he is dead.

The film opened at number one in North America in September 2000, during one of the weakest box office weekends in years, and earned about $29 million domestically. Critics panned it, giving it 11% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Daddy Day Care
documents.tagline: Who's your daddy?
documents.overview: Two men get laid off and have to become stay-at-home dads when they can't find jobs, which inspires them to open their own day-care center.
documents.plot:
"Daddy Day Care" is a 2003 American comedy film directed by Steve Carr and starring Eddie Murphy and Jeff Garlin.

The movie follows the story of Charlie Hinton (Eddie Murphy) and Phil Ryerson (Jeff Garlin), two unemployed fathers who start a daycare center in their home. As they navigate the challenges of childcare, they learn valuable lessons about fatherhood, friendship, and growing up.

Some of the main themes of "Daddy Day Care" include:

1. **Redemption and Second Chances**: Charlie and Phil are both struggling to provide for their families, but through their new venture, they find a way to redeem themselves and prove that they're capable parents.
2. **Friendship and Camaraderie**: The unlikely friendship between Charlie and Phil is at the heart of the movie. Despite their differences, they learn to work together and support each other in their endeavors.
3. **Growing Up and Maturity**: As Charlie and Phil navigate the challenges of childcare, they're forced to confront their own immaturity and learn to grow up. This theme is particularly evident in Charlie's character development throughout the movie.
4. **Family and Parenting**: The film explores the importance of family and parenting, highlighting the challenges and rewards that come with raising children.
5. **Self-Discovery and Empowerment**: Through their experiences as daycare providers, Charlie and Phil discover new aspects of themselves and find a sense of purpose and fulfillment.

Overall, "Daddy Day Care" is a heartwarming comedy that explores themes of redemption, friendship, growing up, family, and self-discovery.

documents.title: Envy
documents.tagline: Success didn’t go to his head, it went to his neighbor.
documents.overview: A man becomes increasingly jealous of his friend's newfound success.
documents.plot:
Envy, released in 2004 by DreamWorks Pictures, is a dark comedy that delves into the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of one's actions. The film revolves around two friends, Nick (Ben Stiller) and Ken (Will Ferrell), who become embroiled in a series of events that expose their own insecurities and flaws.

At its core, Envy is a commentary on the superficiality of modern society, where people often prioritize material possessions and external validation over genuine connections with others. The film critiques the notion of "keeping up with the Joneses" and the pressure to conform to societal norms. Through the characters' experiences, the movie highlights the dangers of allowing envy and resentment to consume one's life.

The film also explores themes of masculinity, identity, and the performance of self. Ken, in particular, is a masterclass in the art of pretending to be someone he's not, while Nick struggles with his own sense of inadequacy. As the story unfolds, both characters are forced to confront their true selves and the emptiness that can result from trying to project a false image.

Ultimately, Envy is a satirical exploration of the human condition, poking fun at our tendency to compare ourselves to others and seeking validation through external means. The film's dark humor and absurdity serve as a commentary on the absurdities of modern life, making it a thought-provoking and entertaining watch.

documents.title: Looney Tunes: Back in Action
documents.tagline: Real life has never been so animated.
documents.overview: Fed up with all the attention going to Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck quits Hollywood, teams up with recently-fired stuntman Damien Drake Jr. and embarks on a round-the-world adventure, along with Bugs and The VP of Warner Bros. Their mission? Find Damien's father, and the missing blue diamond... and stay one step ahead of The Acme Corp., who wants the diamond for their own purposes.
documents.plot:
Looney Tunes: Back in Action is a 2003 live-action/animated comedy film directed by Joe Dante and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie brings together the beloved Looney Tunes characters with real-world celebrities, blending live-action and animation.

The story begins with James "Jim" Davis (played by Brendan Fraser), an action movie star who is struggling to find his next big role. Jim's life takes a turn when he meets Bugs Bunny (voiced by Billy West) and Daffy Duck (voiced by Jeff Bergman), the iconic cartoon characters, in a Las Vegas nightclub.

The two are on a mission to stop the villainous Marvin Acme (played by Steve Martin), who has stolen the world's most valuable diamond, the "Acme Diamond." Marvin plans to use the diamond to fund his latest scheme: creating an army of robotic Acme brand products that will take over the world.

Jim is recruited by Bugs and Daffy to help them on their mission. Along the way, they are joined by Lola Bunny (voiced by Rosie O'Donnell), a basketball player who becomes Jim's love interest. The group embarks on a series of wacky misadventures as they try to outsmart Marvin and his robotic minions.

Throughout the movie, the Looney Tunes characters interact with the real-world celebrities in hilarious ways. Jim often finds himself caught up in the zany antics of Bugs and Daffy, while Lola Bunny provides a more grounded perspective on the situation.

As the story unfolds, Jim begins to realize that he has been living a shallow life as an action movie star. He starts to develop feelings for Lola and learns to appreciate the value of friendship and teamwork. In the end, Jim and his new friends successfully stop Marvin's plan, saving the world from the robotic Acme products.

The movie features plenty of references to classic Looney Tunes cartoons, with many memorable moments and gags that will delight fans of the franchise. The film also pokes fun at action movie conventions and the absurdity of Hollywood blockbusters.

Overall, Looney Tunes: Back in Action is a lighthearted, entertaining film that brings together the best of both worlds: live-action comedy and beloved cartoon characters. While it may not be a masterpiece, it's a fun and silly ride that will leave audiences smiling.
production_companies: Lonely Film Productions GmbH & Co. KG.

documents.title: Elf
documents.tagline: This holiday, discover your inner elf.
documents.overview: When young Buddy falls into Santa's gift sack on Christmas Eve, he's transported back to the North Pole and raised as a toy-making elf by Santa's helpers. But as he grows into adulthood, he can't shake the nagging feeling that he doesn't belong. Buddy vows to visit Manhattan and find his real dad, a workaholic publisher.
documents.plot:
Elf is a Christmas comedy film released in 2003, directed by Jon Favreau and produced by New Line Cinema.

The story begins with Buddy Hobbs (played by Will Ferrell), a human who was accidentally taken to the North Pole as a baby and raised by Santa's elves. Unaware that he is actually a human, Buddy grows up thinking he is one of the elves, and his childlike innocence and enthusiasm are unmatched among the elf population.

As Buddy discovers the truth about his identity on Christmas Eve, he sets out to find his biological father, Walter Hobbs (played by James Caan), a children's book publisher in New York City. However, upon arrival, Buddy is met with skepticism and disdain from his father, who is on Santa's naughty list.

Despite initial disagreements, Buddy's innocence and good-hearted nature eventually win over his father, and he begins to form a bond with him. Meanwhile, Walter's wife, Emily (played by Mary Steenburgen), takes Buddy under her wing and helps him adjust to life in the city.

As Christmas approaches, Buddy becomes determined to spread Christmas cheer to those around him, including his father and stepmother. However, his efforts are met with resistance from his father, who is struggling to connect with his son due to their past differences.

The plot thickens when Walter's company is threatened by a rival publisher, Michael (played by Daniel Tay), who seeks to sabotage Christmas spirit in the city. Buddy, determined to save Christmas, teams up with his father and Emily to outsmart Michael and bring joy back to the city.

Throughout the film, Ferrell's comedic genius shines as he brings Buddy's childlike wonder and enthusiasm to life. The supporting cast, including Caan, Steenburgen, and Zooey Deschanel (as Jovie), add depth and humor to the story.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Buddy's efforts pay off, and he helps his father rediscover the true meaning of Christmas. In a heartwarming finale, Walter comes to accept Buddy as his son, and the two share a heartfelt moment together.

The film ends with Buddy returning to the North Pole, where he is welcomed back by Santa and the elf community. As he says goodbye to his new family in New York City, Buddy reflects on the lessons he learned about family, love, and acceptance. The final shot of the film features Buddy's iconic "I'm a cotton-headed ninnymuggins!" line, leaving audiences with a lasting impression of this Christmas classic.

Overall, Elf is a delightful holiday film that celebrates the power of kindness, generosity, and the importance of finding one's place in the world.
production_companies: Guy Walks into a Bar Productions

documents.title: American Psycho II: All American Girl
documents.original_title: American Psycho II: All American Girl
documents.tagline: Angrier. Deadlier. Sexier.
documents.overview: Rachel is a criminology student hoping to land a position as a teacher's assistant for professor Robert Starkman. She's sure this position will pave the way to an FBI career, and she's willing to do anything to obtain it -- including killing her classmates. The school psychiatrist, Dr. Daniels, becomes aware that Rachel is insane, but Rachel is skilled at her dangerous game of death and identity theft.
documents.plot:
American Psycho 2, also known as American Psycho II: All American Girl, is a 2002 American black comedy slasher film directed by Morgan J. Freeman from a screenplay by Alex Sanger and Karen Craig. Mila Kunis stars as Rachael Newman, a criminology student, with William Shatner as her professor, Geraint Wyn Davies, Lindy Booth and Charles Officer. A stand-alone sequel to American Psycho (2000), it began as an unrelated script titled The Girl Who Wouldn't Die and was altered during production to connect it to the earlier film. It was released direct-to-video on 18 June 2002.

In 1988, a twelve-year-old girl accompanies her babysitter on a date with the serial killer Patrick Bateman. When Bateman murders the babysitter, the girl kills him with an ice pick. Five years later, the girl, Rachael Newman, is a college student studying criminology under Professor Robert Starkman, a former FBI agent famed for his work on serial killers. Determined to join the FBI, Rachael sets her sights on the coveted position of Starkman's teaching assistant, which would virtually guarantee her a place in the bureau's training program at Quantico.

When the department secretary dismisses Rachael's application because she is only a freshman, Rachael follows her home and beats her to death. She then sets out to eliminate every classmate who stands in her way, beginning with Brian, whom she drugs and kills during a planned sexual encounter. While continuing her killing spree, she starts seeing the campus psychiatrist, Dr. Eric Daniels, who realizes that she is a textbook sociopath obsessed with Starkman. Bound by confidentiality, Daniels tries to warn Starkman without naming her, but the professor mistakenly assumes the obsessed student is Cassandra Blaire, with whom he is having an affair. As the body count rises and the competition for the assistantship narrows, Rachael's methods become increasingly brazen, and Daniels, Starkman and her roommate gradually come to suspect the truth, while Rachael reveals the deeper motive behind her ambition.

American Psycho 2 was panned by critics, holding a 23 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it lackluster and ill-conceived, abandoning its predecessor's satire for shallow slasher tropes and unconvincing dark humor. Critics noted that the film's tenuous link to the original, added late in production, sat awkwardly with its campus-slasher story, although Kunis's energetic lead performance was occasionally singled out.

documents.title: Darkness Falls
documents.tagline: Evil rises.
documents.overview: A vengeful spirit has taken the form of the Tooth Fairy to exact vengeance on the town that lynched her 150 years earlier. Her only opposition is the only child, now grown up, who has survived her before.
documents.plot:
Darkness Falls is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of unchecked anger and resentment. The movie follows a young boy, Josh, who is haunted by his father's dark past and the malevolent spirit that has been awakened.

At its core, Darkness Falls explores the theme of the cyclical nature of violence and trauma. The film suggests that when we fail to confront and resolve our inner demons, they can consume us and ultimately lead to destruction. Josh's father, a former logger with a troubled past, is driven by a deep-seated anger and resentment towards those who have wronged him, which ultimately leads to his downfall.

The movie also touches on the idea of the long-term effects of childhood trauma and the ways in which it can shape our adult lives. Josh's experiences as a child are deeply ingrained, and he struggles to form healthy relationships or find closure as an adult. The film implies that unless we confront and heal from these wounds, they will continue to haunt us.

Furthermore, Darkness Falls explores the theme of redemption and the possibility of breaking free from the cycle of violence and trauma. Josh's journey is one of self-discovery and growth, as he grapples with his family's dark past and seeks to find a way to heal and move forward.

Overall, Darkness Falls is a haunting and atmospheric film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of trauma, violence, and redemption in a way that is both thought-provoking and unsettling.

documents.title: The Alamo
documents.tagline: You will never forget
documents.overview: Based on the 1836 standoff between a group of Texan and Tejano men, led by Davy Crockett and Jim Bowie, and Mexican dictator Santa Anna's forces at the Alamo in San Antonio, Texas.
documents.plot:
The Alamo is a 2004 American war film depicting the 1836 siege of the Alamo in the Texas Revolution, directed by John Lee Hancock, who wrote the screenplay with Stephen Gaghan and Leslie Bohem. Dennis Quaid plays Sam Houston, Billy Bob Thornton Davy Crockett, Jason Patric Jim Bowie and Patrick Wilson William B. Travis, with Emilio Echevarría as the Mexican president Santa Anna.

In 1835, Houston, trying to attract settlers to Texas, meets Crockett, who has just lost his seat in Congress. Texas has risen against Mexico, and after the rebels take San Antonio de Béxar and the Alamo mission, Santa Anna marches north to crush the revolt. The quarrelsome provisional government strips Houston of command, and he tells Bowie to go to San Antonio, destroy its fortifications and fall back east. Instead, the government sends Travis to Béxar, where the departing commander leaves him in charge. Knowing the garrison cannot hold against the Mexican army, Travis appeals repeatedly for reinforcements as small groups of volunteers trickle in. Crockett arrives hoping to revive his political career. After a punishing forced march, Santa Anna appears much sooner than expected, on 23 February, and the Texans retreat into the Alamo.

During the siege, Bowie's parley with a Mexican general is cut short when Travis fires a cannon at the enemy camp, and the defenders reject Santa Anna's offer of surrender. Santa Anna orders that no quarter be given and has his band play the "Degüello" as a signal. As Bowie lies bedridden with illness, Travis takes sole command. Before dawn on Sunday, 6 March, Mexican troops storm the walls at heavy cost and kill most of the defenders, including Travis and Bowie. Crockett, the last survivor, is captured and defiantly offers to escort Santa Anna to Houston if he surrenders; the general has him executed. Houston leads a long retreat, but when Santa Anna divides his army to chase him, Houston launches a surprise afternoon attack near the San Jacinto River, where the Texans rout the Mexican troops and take Santa Anna prisoner. In exchange for his life, Santa Anna agrees to withdraw his forces and recognise Texan independence. The film closes with Crockett's spirit playing his fiddle on the Alamo walls.

Ron Howard, first set to direct, stayed on as executive producer. Released by Buena Vista on April 9, 2004, the film was a major box-office failure, grossing $25.8 million on a $107 million budget. Reviews were mixed to negative.

documents.title: What a Girl Wants
documents.tagline: Trying to fit in. Born to stand out.
documents.overview: An American girl, Daphne, heads to Europe in search of the father she's never met. But instead of finding a British version of her bohemian mother, she learns the love of her mom's life is an uptight politician. The only problem now is that her long-lost dad is engaged to a fiercely territorial social climber with a daughter who makes Daphne's life miserable.
documents.plot:
What a Girl Wants is a 2003 American teen comedy directed by Dennie Gordon and written by Jenny Bicks and Elizabeth Chandler, based on William Douglas-Home's 1955 play The Reluctant Debutante. Amanda Bynes stars as Daphne Reynolds and Colin Firth as her father, Henry Dashwood, with Kelly Preston, Jonathan Pryce, Anna Chancellor, Eileen Atkins and Oliver James.

Seventeen-year-old Daphne lives with Libby, a wedding singer, above a restaurant in Manhattan's Chinatown. Years earlier Libby met Henry, a Briton, in Morocco, where they wed in a Bedouin ceremony of doubtful legality before moving to his family's English estate. After his father's death made Henry the new Earl of Wycombe, Libby left without telling him she was pregnant, and the family's advisor, Alistair, told Henry she loved someone else. Daphne travels to London to find her father, who has given up his seat in the House of Lords to run for the House of Commons, hoping one day to become prime minister. Alistair is now his political advisor, and Henry is engaged to Alistair's daughter, Glynnis. At a hostel Daphne meets Ian, an aspiring musician, who shows her around London, and they begin dating.

Stunned to learn he has a daughter, Henry takes Daphne in, and his mother, Jocelyne, welcomes her warmly. Glynnis and her daughter, Clarissa, feel threatened and work to undermine her,. Her free spirit charms much of the aristocracy, including the elderly Princess Charlotte, but it hurts Henry's campaign, so she adopts a more dignified manner, and his polls rise while Ian, hurt by the change, breaks up with her. At her debutante party, Daphne overhears Alistair boasting of how he got rid of her mother, and Glynnis locks her away. Freed by Libby, she sees Henry dancing with Clarissa and announces she is going home. Henry withdraws from the election, learns that Alistair knew of Libby's pregnancy and manipulated their separation, punches him and ends his engagement. He finds Daphne and Libby at a wedding, tells his daughter he loves her as she is, and they share a father-daughter dance. Daphne reunites with Ian, Henry and Libby marry legally in another Bedouin ceremony, and Daphne is accepted to Oxford.

Warner Bros. released the film on April 4, 2003. It grossed $51 million worldwide against a $25 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 35% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus found it too syrupy for adults, and 41 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Confidence
documents.tagline: It's not about the money. It's about the money.
documents.overview: What Jake Vig doesn't know just might get him killed. A sharp and polished grifter, Jake has just swindled thousands of dollars from the unsuspecting Lionel Dolby with the help of his crew. It becomes clear that Lionel wasn't just any mark, he was an accountant for eccentric crime boss Winston King. Jake and his crew will have to stay one step ahead of both the criminals and the cops to finally settle their debt.
documents.plot:
Confidence is a 2003 American crime drama directed by James Foley and written by Doug Jung. Edward Burns, Rachel Weisz, Dustin Hoffman and Andy García head a cast that also includes Morris Chestnut.

After a group of grifters cheat their latest target and celebrate, their unofficial leader, Jake Vig, explains the art of the con. When one of them, Big Al, is found shot dead, the others discover that the money they took belonged to Winston King, a ruthless local crime lord known as the King. Jake proposes working for the King by robbing Morgan Price, a rival who owns a bank. He enlists partners Gordo and Miles and con artist Lily, with the King's man Lupus as a minder. The plan centers on bribing a bank vice president to wire money offshore. Complications arise when Special Agent Gunther Butan, who has pursued Jake for years, comes to Los Angeles and forces two crooked police detectives, to switch their loyalty from Jake to him. Rattled, Jake calls off the con and berates Lily, who walks out. Lupus warns that the King will torture and kill the grifters if they fail, and the job resumes without her.

The bribed executive wires the money to Gordo in Belize, who carries $5 million in a duffel bag to Ontario Airport, where both Butan and the King's men are waiting. Butan arrests the King and seizes the cash, and Gordo vanishes. Believing the King has the money, Lupus admits that he killed Big Al and pulls a gun on Jake, but he is shot by Travis, a henchman of Price, to whom Lily had revealed the entire scheme after leaving. Travis takes Jake to a vacant lot and makes him explain how the con worked, and a furious Lily shoots Jake before Travis orders them both to disappear. Minutes later Butan pulls up and Jake rises from a pool of fake blood, unhurt. The final twists are revealed: Lily's departure was staged to fool Lupus, Butan is actually Jake's longtime confederate who used his position to grab the money and arrest the King at once, and Jake wore squibs to fake his death. Everyone was in on the scheme except the King and Lupus, Price and Travis, and the two corrupt detectives, who end up under arrest. The money is split five ways, and the grifters drive off into the night to celebrate.

The film was shot at Hollywood's Deep Nightclub and elsewhere around Los Angeles and Ontario, California, and opened on April 25, 2003. Reviews were mixed to positive: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 68%, Metacritic scored it 59,, and Roger Ebert gave it two stars.

documents.title: St. Trinian's
documents.tagline: Taking higher education to a new low.
documents.overview: When their beloved school is threatened with closure should the powers that be fail to raise the proper funds, the girls scheme to steal a priceless painting and use the profits to pull St. Trinian's out of the red.
documents.plot:
St. Trinian's is a 2007 British comedy film that satirizes the British education system and societal norms. The movie follows the misadventures of a group of girls at the fictional St. Trinian's boarding school, known for their rebellious nature and penchant for chaos.

At its core, St. Trinian's explores themes of female empowerment, nonconformity, and the struggle for independence in a patriarchal society. The film celebrates the girls' refusal to conform to traditional norms and expectations, embracing instead a spirit of free-spiritedness and self-expression.

The movie also touches on issues of class and social status, highlighting the contrast between the privileged students at St. Trinian's and those from more humble backgrounds. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on the social inequalities of British society during that era.

Furthermore, St. Trinian's pokes fun at the stuffy, outdated nature of the British education system, which often prioritizes discipline over creativity and individuality. The film's portrayal of the school's strict headmistress and her attempts to maintain order serve as a satire of the rigid authority structures that can stifle innovation and progress.

Ultimately, St. Trinian's is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and wit to explore these themes and offer a commentary on British society during the 2000s.

documents.title: The Haunted Mansion
documents.tagline: Check your pulse at the door... if you have one.
documents.overview: Workaholic Jim Evers and his wife/business partner Sara get a call one night from  a mansion owner, Edward Gracey, who wants to sell his house. Once the Evers family arrive at the mansion, a torrential thunderstorm of mysterious origin strands them with the brooding, eccentric Gracey, his mysterious butler, and a variety of residents both seen and unseen.
documents.plot:
The Haunted Mansion (2003) is a supernatural comedy film directed by Rob Minkoff and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Jim Evers (Eddie Murphy), a widowed father who moves his family into a haunted mansion with 999 ghosts.

The main themes of The Haunted Mansion can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Family and Togetherness**: The film highlights the importance of family bonding and togetherness, as Jim Evers tries to reconnect with his children, Sara (Marsha Thomason) and Michael (Terence Stamp), in a new and unconventional environment.
2. **Love and Loss**: The movie explores the theme of love and loss through Jim's character, who is struggling to come to terms with the death of his wife. His journey is also about finding a way to move on and find happiness again.
3. **Redemption and Self-Discovery**: As Jim navigates the haunted mansion, he discovers that he has been given a second chance at life. The film suggests that everyone deserves a second chance, and that redemption is possible through self-discovery and personal growth.
4. **The Power of Love and Kindness**: The ghosts in the mansion, who are initially portrayed as malevolent entities, ultimately reveal their true nature as benevolent spirits who have been trapped between worlds due to unfinished business. This theme emphasizes the transformative power of love, kindness, and compassion.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together with a healthy dose of humor, wit, and supernatural adventure, making The Haunted Mansion a delightful and entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham
documents.tagline: It's all about loving your parents.
documents.overview: Years after his father disowns his adopted brother for marrying a woman of lower social standing, a young man goes on a mission to reunite his family.
documents.plot:
Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001) is a Bollywood drama film directed by Karan Johar, produced by Dharma Productions, and starring Amitabh Bachchan, Jaya Bachchan, Kajol, Hrithik Roshan, Kareena Kapoor Khan, Shah Rukh Khan, and Preity Zinta.

The main themes of Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham can be summarized as follows:

1. Family Dynamics: The film explores the complexities of family relationships, particularly the intricate web of love, loyalty, and sacrifice that binds a family together. The story delves into the consequences of past decisions and their impact on future generations.

2. Love and Sacrifice: The movie highlights the sacrifices made by individuals for the sake of their loved ones, often leading to personal losses and heartbreaks. The characters' choices are driven by their love and commitment to each other, even if it means putting their own desires and happiness aside.

3. Identity Crisis: The protagonist, Rahul (Hrithik Roshan), struggles with his identity and sense of belonging within the family. His journey is a metaphor for finding one's place in life and navigating the complexities of family expectations versus personal aspirations.

4. Social Class and Status: The film touches upon the theme of social class and status, particularly in the context of Indian society. The characters' struggles with their own social standing and the pressures of maintaining family honor serve as a backdrop to the story.

5. Redemption and Forgiveness: Throughout the narrative, the characters grapple with guilt, regret, and forgiveness. Ultimately, the film offers a message of redemption and the importance of making amends for past mistakes in order to move forward and find peace.

The movie's exploration of these themes is woven together through its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and iconic music.

documents.title: Sydney White
documents.tagline: Freshman year is no fairytale
documents.overview: A modern retelling of Snow White set against students in their freshman year of college in the greek system.
documents.plot:
Sydney White is a 2007 American teen comedy film directed by Joe Nussbaum. The movie follows the story of Sydney White (played by Amanda Bynes), a high school student who is initially shunned by her peers due to her humble background and lack of popularity.

The main themes of Sydney White include:

1. **Social hierarchy and cliques**: The film explores the complexities of social hierarchies in high schools, where students are often divided into cliques based on their social status, interests, and backgrounds.
2. **Self-discovery and empowerment**: As Sydney navigates her new environment, she discovers her own strengths and passions, ultimately finding her place among her peers and asserting herself as a confident individual.
3. **Friendship and loyalty**: The movie highlights the importance of genuine friendships and loyalty, particularly in the face of adversity or social pressure.
4. **Class differences and stereotypes**: Sydney White tackles issues related to class differences and stereotypes, encouraging viewers to look beyond surface-level appearances and appreciate individuals for who they truly are.

The film's tone is lighthearted and comedic, with a touch of satire aimed at high school culture and social norms. Overall, Sydney White offers an entertaining and relatable portrayal of teenage life, self-discovery, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

documents.title: Made of Honor
documents.tagline: He'll do anything to get the groom out of the picture.
documents.overview: Tom and Hannah have been platonic friends for 10 years. He's a serial dater, while she wants marriage but hasn't found Mr. Right. Just as Tom is starting to think that he is relationship material after all, Hannah gets engaged. When she asks Tom to be her 'maid' of honor, he reluctantly agrees just so he can attempt to stop the wedding and woo her.
documents.plot:
Made of Honor is a romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of love, friendship, and loyalty. The movie delves into the theme of unrequited love, as the protagonist, Tom (played by Chris Evans), struggles to express his feelings for his best friend's fiancée, Sarah (played by Michelle Monaghan). As Tom navigates this difficult situation, he must confront his own emotions and learn to let go of his unrequited love.

The film also touches on the theme of male friendship and the bonds that form between men. The relationship between Tom and his best friend, Trevor (played by Patrick Dempsey), is a central aspect of the movie, highlighting the importance of loyalty, trust, and support in male friendships.
