documents.plot:
Orange County is a 2002 American comedy film directed by Jake Kasdan. The movie follows the story of Shaun Brumder, a high school dropout who returns to his hometown in Orange County, California, after dropping out of college.

The main theme of Orange County revolves around the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Shaun's journey is marked by his desire to fit in with his peers and prove himself as a capable individual, despite being a non-traditional student. As he navigates through his relationships with his family, friends, and romantic interests, Shaun grapples with the idea of who he wants to be and where he belongs.

The film also explores themes of social class and status, particularly in the context of Orange County's affluent communities. Shaun's experiences highlight the superficiality and materialism that can define certain social circles, leading him to question what truly matters in life.

Furthermore, Orange County touches on the idea of redemption and second chances. Shaun's decision to return to school and pursue his education is motivated by a desire to make amends for past mistakes and prove himself as a responsible individual. Throughout the movie, he faces various challenges that test his resolve and force him to confront his flaws.

Overall, Orange County is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of identity, class, and redemption, set against the vibrant backdrop of California's Orange County.

documents.title: Flight of the Phoenix
documents.tagline: Out of the ashes, hope will rise.
documents.overview: When an oil rig in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia proves unproductive, an aircraft crew are sent to shut the operation down and fly them out. On the flight out over the desert on the way to Beijing, Capt. Frank Towns and co-pilot A.J. are unable to keep their cargo plane, a C-119 Flying Boxcar, in the air when a violent sandstorm strikes. Crash-landing in a remote uncharted part of the desert, the two pilots and their passengers -- a crew of oil workers and a drifter -- must work together to survive by rebuilding the aircraft. Soon, low supplies and a band of merciless smugglers add even greater urgency to their task.
documents.plot:
Flight of the Phoenix is a 2004 American survival drama film directed by John Moore and written by Scott Frank and Edward Burns, a remake of the 1965 film The Flight of the Phoenix, both based on Elleston Trevor's 1964 novel. Dennis Quaid, Giovanni Ribisi, Tyrese Gibson, Miranda Otto and Hugh Laurie star in the story of a group who survive a plane crash in the desert and must build a new aircraft from the wreckage to escape. It was filmed on location in the Namib Desert, using a mix of models and computer graphics for its aerial scenes.

When an oil-drilling operation in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia proves unproductive, pilot Frank Towns and his co-pilot A.J. are sent in their C-119 Flying Boxcar to shut it down and fly the crew out, along with a mysterious hitchhiker named Elliott. En route to Beijing, a violent dust storm disables an engine and forces a crash landing in an uncharted stretch of desert, killing several passengers. Stranded some 200 miles off course with about a month's supply of water, the survivors face a fierce debate about whether to wait for a rescue that may never come or attempt to walk out. As tempers fray and another crew member is lost in a sandstorm, Elliott, who claims to be an aircraft designer, proposes a radical solution: rebuilding the wrecked plane into a new aircraft that can fly them to safety. Frank at first dismisses the idea, but after one of the men walks off in protest, he agrees. For weeks they labor under brutal conditions, battling heat, dust storms, shortages of water and bitter quarrels, and they christen their creation Phoenix, after the legendary bird. Their efforts are threatened by a band of smugglers camped nearby, by Elliott's increasingly arrogant demands to be acknowledged as their leader, and finally by the discovery that his design experience is limited to model aircraft. With their supplies running out, the survivors must decide whether to trust Elliott's design and stake their lives on a single attempt to get the Phoenix into the air.

Released in the United States by 20th Century Fox on December 17, 2004, the film was a box-office bomb, grossing about $35 million worldwide amid competition from other holiday releases. Reviews were generally mixed, with critics comparing it unfavorably to the original while praising its visuals and action; it holds a 31% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

documents.title: Big Fat Liar
documents.tagline: Two friends are about to cut one Hollywood big shot down to size.
documents.overview: After one of his class papers is stolen and turned into a movie, a young student and his best friend exact a hilarious, slapstick revenge on the Hollywood hot shot who has taken credit!
documents.plot:
Big Fat Liar is a 2002 American comedy film that revolves around the story of Jason Shepherd, a teenager who discovers that his best friend, Kevin, has been impersonating him in order to get into trouble and gain attention. As Jason navigates this situation, he learns valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and being true to oneself.

The main theme of Big Fat Liar is the importance of authenticity and staying true to one's identity. Jason's journey is a metaphor for the challenges of adolescence, where teenagers often struggle to find their place in the world and define themselves. Through his experiences, Jason comes to realize that it's essential to be genuine and authentic, rather than trying to fit into someone else's mold.

The film also explores the theme of friendship and loyalty, highlighting the complexities and nuances of relationships between friends. Kevin's actions serve as a catalyst for Jason's growth, forcing him to confront the consequences of his own behavior and reevaluate his priorities.

Furthermore, Big Fat Liar touches on the idea of identity theft and the consequences of deception. The film uses humor and satire to comment on the absurdity of modern life, where people often present a false image to the world. Jason's situation serves as a commentary on the ease with which people can be manipulated and deceived, highlighting the importance of being mindful of one's actions and their impact on others.

Overall, Big Fat Liar is a lighthearted comedy that explores themes of identity, friendship, and authenticity in a way that is relatable to teenagers and adults alike.

documents.title: Dog Soldiers
documents.tagline: Six men. Full moon. No chance.
documents.overview: A squad of British soldiers on training in the lonesome Scottish wilderness find a wounded Special Forces captain and the remains of his team. As they encounter zoologist Megan, it turns out that werewolves are active in the region. They have to prepare for some action as the there will be a full moon tonight...
documents.plot:
Dog Soldiers is a 2002 British horror film directed by Neil Marshall. The movie follows a group of British soldiers on leave who are attacked by supernatural creatures while on a training exercise in the Scottish Highlands.

The main themes of Dog Soldiers include:

1. **Isolation and claustrophobia**: The film takes place in a remote location, where the characters are cut off from civilization. This isolation heightens their sense of vulnerability and fear, as they are forced to confront the supernatural threat alone.
2. **Moral decay and the breakdown of social norms**: As the soldiers' situation becomes more desperate, they begin to turn on each other, revealing their darker impulses and moral weaknesses. This theme is reflected in the characters' gradual descent into chaos and violence.
3. **The struggle between nature and humanity**: The supernatural creatures in the film are depicted as a force of nature, untamed and unrelenting. In contrast, the human characters are portrayed as fragile and vulnerable, highlighting the idea that humans are not always in control of their environment.
4. **Trauma and PTSD**: One of the main characters, Captain James "Havoc" Earl (Kevin McKidd), is struggling with PTSD after a traumatic event in his past. The film explores how this trauma affects him and his relationships with others.

The movie's plot development is driven by the escalating tension and violence as the soldiers try to survive against the supernatural threat. In the end, only one character manages to escape, leaving the audience with a sense of unease and uncertainty.

Overall, Dog Soldiers is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of isolation, moral decay, and the struggle between nature and humanity.
production_companies: The Noel Gay Motion Picture Company

documents.title: The Last Starfighter
documents.tagline: He didn't find his dreams... his dreams found him.
documents.overview: A video game expert Alex Rogan finds himself transported to another planet after conquering The Last Starfighter video game only to find out it was just a test. He was recruited to join the team of best Starfighters to defend their world from the attack.
documents.plot:
The Last Starfighter is a 1984 science fiction film directed by Nick Castle and produced by Universal Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Alex Rogan, an average teenager who discovers that he has been chosen to save the galaxy from an evil alien force. As Alex navigates his new role as a space fighter pilot, he must confront the harsh realities of war and the consequences of his own mortality.

At its core, The Last Starfighter is a film about the human condition, exploring themes of identity, duty, and the search for meaning in a chaotic universe. Through Alex's journey, the movie raises questions about what it means to be alive, to have purpose, and to leave a lasting impact on the world.

The film also delves into the idea of escapism, as Alex finds solace in his virtual reality game, which serves as a metaphor for the human desire to temporarily escape the difficulties of everyday life. However, as he becomes more immersed in the game, Alex must confront the consequences of his actions and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

Ultimately, The Last Starfighter is a classic tale of self-discovery, where Alex must come to terms with his own strengths and weaknesses, and find a way to reconcile his desire for adventure with the responsibilities that come with being a hero.

documents.title: High School Musical 3: Senior Year
documents.overview: It's almost graduation day for high school seniors Troy, Gabriella, Sharpay, Chad, Ryan and Taylor — and the thought of heading off in separate directions after leaving East High has these Wildcats thinking they need to do something they'll remember forever. Together with the rest of the Wildcats, they stage a spring musical reflecting their hopes and fears about the future and their unforgettable experiences growing up together. Will their final show break them apart or bring them together for the greatest moment in Wildcat history?
documents.plot:
High School Musical 3: Senior Year is a musical comedy-drama film that explores several themes relevant to high school students and their transition into adulthood.

One of the primary themes of the movie is the bittersweet nature of senior year. The characters are faced with the reality of leaving high school behind, saying goodbye to friends, and embarking on new paths in life. This theme is reflected in the film's narrative, as the characters grapple with their own identities, futures, and relationships.

Another significant theme is the importance of following one's passion and pursuing one's dreams. The movie showcases the characters' various interests and talents, highlighting the value of exploring different passions and finding what truly makes them happy. This theme is exemplified through Troy Bolton's (Zac Efron) struggles to balance his basketball career with his love for singing.

The film also explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the power of relationships. The bonds between the characters are put to the test as they navigate the challenges of senior year, ultimately leading to a deeper understanding and appreciation of their friendships.

Furthermore, High School Musical 3: Senior Year touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As the characters prepare to leave high school behind, they must confront their own identities, values, and goals for the future. This theme is particularly evident in the character development of Gabriella Montez (Vanessa Hudgens), who struggles to balance her academic ambitions with her passion for music.

Lastly, the movie highlights the significance of embracing change and letting go of the past. The characters must come to terms with the end of an era and the uncertainty that comes with it, ultimately learning to cherish the memories and experiences they've had while also looking forward to the future.

Overall, High School Musical 3: Senior Year is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes relevant to high school students and their transition into adulthood.

documents.title: Snow Dogs
documents.tagline: Get ready for mush hour!
documents.overview: When a Miami dentist inherits a team of sled dogs, he's got to learn the trade or lose his pack to a crusty mountain man.
documents.plot:
Snow Dogs is a heartwarming family comedy that explores several endearing themes. At its core, the film revolves around the transformative power of friendship and community. The story follows a wealthy businessman who inherits a team of sled dogs from his late brother, forcing him to reevaluate his priorities and reconnect with his roots.

As our protagonist navigates this new chapter in his life, he discovers that the true value of these canine companions lies not only in their athletic prowess but also in the joy they bring to those around them. Through his interactions with the dogs and the people of the small Alaskan town where he's forced to settle, he learns the importance of embracing his inner child, letting go of his ego, and finding a sense of belonging.

The film also touches on themes of redemption, forgiveness, and second chances. Our protagonist is given a chance to redeem himself and make amends for past mistakes, not only with the dogs but also with those around him. As he works to restore the sled team to its former glory, he begins to heal old wounds and form new connections with the people in his life.

Ultimately, Snow Dogs is a feel-good movie that celebrates the beauty of friendship, community, and the healing power of nature. The film's lighthearted tone and adorable canine characters make it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Kung Pow: Enter the Fist
documents.tagline: A laugh-out-loud funny spoof!
documents.overview: A movie within a movie, created to spoof the martial arts genre. Writer/director Steve Oedekerk uses contemporary characters and splices them into a 1970s kung-fu film, weaving the new and old together.  As the main character, The Chosen One, Oedekerk sets off to avenge the deaths of his parents at the hands of kung-fu legend Master Pain. Along the way he encounters some strange characters.
documents.plot:
Kung Pow: Enter the Fist is a comedy film released in 2002, directed by David Leitch and starring Steve Oedekerk. The movie parodies classic martial arts films, particularly those of Bruce Lee.

The main themes of Kung Pow: Enter the Fist include:

1. **Satire and parody**: The film uses humor to poke fun at traditional martial arts movies, exaggerating their clichés and over-the-top action sequences.
2. **Friendship and camaraderie**: The story follows the unlikely friendship between Poet (Oedekerk), a clumsy but lovable hero, and Master Pain (Oedekerk), his nemesis-turned-ally. Their bond is central to the plot's development.
3. **Good vs. Evil**: The film features an epic battle between good and evil, with Poet and Master Pain engaging in a series of hilarious and action-packed confrontations.
4. **Self-discovery and growth**: As Poet navigates his journey, he learns valuable lessons about himself and the importance of friendship, loyalty, and embracing one's uniqueness.

The movie's tone is lighthearted and comedic, with plenty of slapstick humor, witty one-liners, and absurd situations. Overall, Kung Pow: Enter the Fist is a entertaining and irreverent take on traditional martial arts films, offering a fresh and humorous perspective on the genre.

documents.title: Hatchet
documents.tagline: Stay out of the swamp!
documents.overview: When a group of tourists on a New Orleans haunted swamp tour find themselves stranded in the wilderness, their evening of fun and spooks turns into a horrific nightmare.
documents.plot:
Hatchet (2006) is a horror film that delves into the psychological effects of trauma and isolation on its protagonist, Victor Crowley. The movie follows Victor, a young man who returns to his family's Louisiana bayou home after being presumed dead, only to find himself hunted by his own family members.

At its core, Hatchet explores the theme of revenge and the cyclical nature of violence. Victor's actions are driven by a desire for retribution against those who wronged him in the past, but this quest for vengeance ultimately leads to further chaos and destruction. The film also touches on the idea of identity and how our past experiences shape us into the people we become.

Moreover, Hatchet critiques the notion of masculinity and the societal expectations placed upon men. Victor's character is a complex exploration of toxic masculinity, as he struggles with his own emotions and desires amidst the chaos of his surroundings. The film suggests that traditional masculine norms can be suffocating and lead to destructive behavior.

The movie also features elements of folk horror, where the supernatural forces at play in the bayou serve as a metaphor for the darker aspects of human nature. This is reflected in Victor's transformation into a monstrous figure, driven by his own primal instincts and fueled by his desire for revenge.

Overall, Hatchet (2006) is a tense and unsettling film that delves into the darker corners of the human psyche, exploring themes of trauma, violence, and the destructive power of unchecked emotions.

documents.title: Saw V
documents.tagline: You won't believe how it ends.
documents.overview: Detective Hoffman is seemingly the last person alive to carry on the Jigsaw legacy. But when his secret is threatened, he must go on the hunt to eliminate all the loose ends.
documents.plot:
Saw V is a 2008 American horror film directed by David Hackl and written by Leigh Whannell. The film is the fifth installment in the Saw franchise.

The movie begins with Jigsaw (Tobin Bell) being taken away from his lair, where he has been held captive for years. He is rescued by Amanda Young (Shawnee Smith), who had previously worked under him but turned against him. However, it becomes clear that Amanda's intentions are not entirely pure.

The story then shifts to a new protagonist, Daniel Matthews (Angus Macfadyen), a successful businessman who has lost his way in life after the death of his wife and daughter. He is kidnapped by Jigsaw, along with two other men, Peter Strickland (Bahar Soomekh) and Eric Matthews (Donnie Wahlberg), Daniel's son.

The three men are taken to an abandoned warehouse, where they find themselves chained in a room filled with deadly traps and puzzles. They soon realize that they must work together to survive and uncover the reason behind their confinement.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jigsaw has designed this game for them to play, and that he intends to test their will to live. The men are forced to navigate through a series of gruesome and deadly challenges, including a room filled with venomous spiders and a trap that requires them to use a blowtorch to escape.

Throughout the film, Amanda's character is revealed to be a complex and conflicted one. She is driven by a desire for revenge against Jigsaw, who she believes wronged her in the past. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that her motivations are not entirely altruistic.

The climax of the film features an intense and suspenseful showdown between Daniel and Amanda, as they engage in a battle of wits and wills. In the end, Daniel emerges victorious, but not without scars both physical and emotional.

Overall, Saw V is a tense and thrilling horror film that explores themes of survival, redemption, and the consequences of playing with fire. The film's twisty plot and gruesome traps make it a must-see for fans of the franchise, while its complex characters and moral ambiguity add depth and nuance to the story.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)

documents.title: Superhero Movie
documents.tagline: The greatest Superhero movie of all time! (not counting all the others)
documents.overview: The team behind Scary Movie takes on the comic book genre in this tale of Rick Riker, a nerdy teen imbued with superpowers by a radioactive dragonfly. And because every hero needs a nemesis, enter Lou Landers, aka the villainously goofy Hourglass.
documents.plot:
Superhero Movie is a 2008 American superhero comedy film directed by Tom Green. The movie parodies various comic book superheroes, particularly Superman.

The main theme of Superhero Movie revolves around the idea of identity and self-discovery. The protagonist, Trent Walker (played by Drake Bell), discovers that he has superpowers similar to those of Superman. As he navigates his new reality, Trent struggles to balance his secret life as a superhero with his everyday life as a high school student.

Throughout the movie, Trent's journey is marked by self-discovery and growth. He learns to control his powers, confronts his enemies, and ultimately finds his place in the world. The film also explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and responsibility, as Trent forms alliances with other superheroes and works together to save the city from various threats.

The movie pokes fun at traditional superhero tropes, using satire and parody to comment on the genre's conventions. However, beneath its comedic surface, Superhero Movie offers a heartwarming story about finding one's purpose and embracing one's uniqueness.

Overall, Superhero Movie is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and friendship in a humorous and action-packed way.

documents.title: In Her Shoes
documents.tagline: Friends. Rivals. Sisters.
documents.overview: Irresponsible party girl, Maggie is kicked out of her father's and stepmother's home—where she lives for free—and is taken in by her hard-working sister, Philadelphia lawyer, Rose. After Maggie's disruptive ways ruin her sister's love life, Rose turns her out as well. But when their grandmother, who they never knew existed, comes into their lives, the sisters face some complicated truths about themselves and their family.
documents.plot:
In Her Shoes is a poignant and heartwarming drama that explores the complexities of family relationships, identity, and self-discovery. The film delves into the intricate web of emotions between two sisters, Maggie (played by Toni Collette) and Rose (played by Shirley MacLaine), as they navigate their way through life's challenges.

At its core, In Her Shoes is a story about the unbreakable bond between sisters, despite their differences. The film masterfully portrays the complexities of sibling relationships, where love, resentment, and forgiveness are intertwined like the threads of a rich tapestry. As Maggie struggles to come to terms with her own identity and find her place in the world, she finds solace in Rose's unconventional wisdom and unwavering support.

The movie also explores themes of grief, loss, and healing, as both sisters grapple with their own personal demons. Through their journey, the film sheds light on the importance of embracing vulnerability, letting go of past hurts, and finding the courage to be true to oneself.

One of the most striking aspects of In Her Shoes is its nuanced portrayal of mother-daughter relationships. The complex dynamics between Maggie's mother (played by Allison Janney) and her own daughter are expertly woven into the narrative, adding depth and richness to the story.

Ultimately, In Her Shoes is a film about finding one's own path in life, embracing imperfection, and discovering the power of love and forgiveness. With its talented ensemble cast, witty dialogue, and poignant storytelling, this movie has become a beloved classic that continues to resonate with audiences today.

documents.title: Into the Blue
documents.tagline: Treasure has its price.
documents.overview: When they take some friends on an extreme sport adventure, the last thing Jared and Sam expect to see below the shark-infested waters is a legendary pirate ship rumored to contain millions of dollars in gold. But their good fortune is short-lived, as a ruthless gang of criminals gets word of what they have uncovered.
documents.plot:
Into the Blue is a 2005 thriller film directed by John Stockwell. The movie follows two brothers, Miller and Jake, who embark on a deep-sea diving adventure to find a lost shipwreck in the Caribbean. As they delve deeper into the ocean, they encounter a group of divers who are also searching for the wreck.

The main theme of Into the Blue revolves around the dangers of obsession and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The characters' relentless pursuit of the treasure serves as a metaphor for the destructive nature of greed and the importance of respecting the power of nature.

Throughout the film, the characters are forced to confront their own personal demons and the true cost of their actions. As they navigate the treacherous underwater world, they must also contend with their own mortality and the fragility of human life.

The movie also explores the theme of brotherly love and loyalty, as Miller's obsession with finding the treasure puts a strain on his relationship with Jake. The film ultimately becomes a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of prioritizing human relationships over material gain.

Overall, Into the Blue is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our actions in the natural world.

documents.title: Thirteen Days
documents.tagline: You'll never believe how close we came
documents.overview: The story of the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962—the nuclear standoff with the USSR sparked by the discovery by the Americans of missile bases established on the Soviet-allied island of Cuba.
documents.plot:
Thirteen Days is a 2000 historical drama film directed by Roger Donaldson, which tells the story of the Cuban Missile Crisis from the perspective of President John F. Kennedy's advisors.

The movie delves into the intense and suspenseful atmosphere that characterized this pivotal moment in history, as the world teetered on the brink of nuclear war. The main theme of Thirteen Days revolves around the concept of crisis management and decision-making under pressure. The film highlights the complexities and nuances of international diplomacy, showcasing the intricate web of alliances, rivalries, and interests that defined the Cold War era.

At its core, the movie explores the human side of politics, revealing the personal struggles, fears, and motivations of the key players involved in this high-stakes crisis. The characters are multidimensional and flawed, with their own strengths and weaknesses, which adds to the tension and drama of the story.

The film also touches on the theme of leadership and the weight of responsibility that comes with it. As President Kennedy navigates the treacherous waters of the Cuban Missile Crisis, he must balance his own instincts and values with the advice of his advisors, all while keeping the fate of humanity in the balance.

Ultimately, Thirteen Days is a gripping drama that captures the essence of this critical moment in history, offering a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, politics, and the complexities of decision-making under extreme pressure.

documents.title: Legend
documents.tagline: There may never be another dawn.
documents.overview: Set in a timeless mythical forest inhabited by fairies, goblins, unicorns and mortals, this fantastic story follows a mystical forest dweller, chosen by fate, to undertake a heroic quest. He must save the beautiful Princess  Lili and defeat the demonic Lord of Darkness, or the world will be plunged into a never-ending ice age.
documents.plot:
Legend is a 1985 epic dark fantasy adventure directed by Ridley Scott from a screenplay by William Hjortsberg. Tom Cruise stars as Jack, with Mia Sara as Princess Lili and Tim Curry as the Lord of Darkness, alongside David Bennent, Alice Playten, Billy Barty, Cork Hubbert and Annabelle Lanyon. Built almost entirely on elaborate studio sets, with extensive prosthetic make-up by Rob Bottin, the film follows a pure-hearted young man who must stop a demonic ruler from plunging the world into eternal night. It premiered at the Venice Film Festival in August 1985 before its theatrical release by 20th Century Fox and Universal Pictures.

The Lord of Darkness, who cannot bear the light of the sun, sends the goblin Blix and his companions to kill the last unicorns in the enchanted forest and bring him their horns, knowing that their destruction will bring endless darkness. He tells them that innocence will be the bait. The goblins follow Princess Lili as she visits Jack, a forest dweller who lives in harmony with nature. Jack leads Lili to a secret stream to see the unicorns, and although he warns her not to approach them, she reaches out to touch the stallion, giving Blix the chance to strike it with a poisoned dart.

As Lili playfully tosses her ring into a pond and promises to marry whoever retrieves it, the goblins cut off the stallion's horn, and the world is instantly gripped by a supernatural winter. Jack barely escapes from the frozen pond. Lili, realising that she unwittingly helped the goblins, follows them and is captured, while the remaining unicorn mare is also taken to Darkness's fortress. Guided by the fairy Gump, played by Bennent, and the sprite Oona, Jack is armed with ancient weapons and journeys into the underworld with a small band of allies to rescue Lili and the unicorn and restore the light. Inside the fortress, Darkness attempts to seduce Lili and corrupt her innocence, while Jack plans to expose the demon to sunlight.

The film draws on fairy-tale imagery and classic myths of good and evil, and Curry's towering, horned Darkness became one of its most celebrated elements.

Legend was troubled by extensive re-editing, and its American release replaced Jerry Goldsmith's score with music by Tangerine Dream. It was a commercial disappointment and received mixed reviews, but its visuals and make-up earned it a cult following, and a director's cut restoring Goldsmith's score was later released.

documents.title: Men of Honor
documents.tagline: History is made by those who break the rules.
documents.overview: Against formidable odds -- and an old-school diving instructor embittered by the U.S. Navy's new, less prejudicial policies -- Carl Brashear sets his sights on becoming the Navy's first African-American master diver in this uplifting true story. Their relationship starts out on the rocks, but fate ultimately conspires to bring the men together into a setting of mutual respect, triumph and honor.
documents.plot:
Men of Honor is a biographical drama film directed by George Tillman Jr., released in 2000 by Fox 2000 Pictures.

The movie tells the story of Carl Brashear, a African-American master diver and sailor in the United States Navy during the Cold War era. The film stars Robert De Niro as Master Chief Petty Officer Carl Brashear, a decorated war hero who lost his leg while saving the life of a fellow crew member during a training exercise.

The movie begins with Carl's childhood, where he grows up in a poor African-American neighborhood in New Orleans. Despite facing racism and poverty, Carl finds solace in the Navy, enlisting at the age of 16. He quickly proves himself to be an exceptional diver and sailor, earning the respect of his peers and superiors.

As Carl rises through the ranks, he faces numerous challenges, including racism and sexism within the Navy. Despite these obstacles, he perseveres, becoming one of the first African-American divers in the Navy's elite SEAL team. However, during a training exercise, Carl suffers a severe injury when he is struck by a piece of metal while saving his fellow diver, Eddie "Papa" Johnson (played by Cuba Gooding Jr.).

The movie follows Carl's journey as he undergoes multiple surgeries and rehabilitation to regain his mobility. Despite the odds against him, Carl refuses to give up on his dreams, becoming one of the first amputees to attend the Navy's diving school.

As Carl navigates his recovery, he also faces personal struggles, including a troubled relationship with his son, who feels ashamed of his father's disability. However, with the support of his family and fellow sailors, Carl perseveres, eventually earning his place as a master diver and sailor in the Navy.

The movie culminates with Carl's final mission, where he leads a team of divers on a secret operation to recover a lost nuclear submarine. Despite facing numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain and hostile enemy forces, Carl proves himself to be an exceptional leader and diver, earning his place as one of the most decorated sailors in Navy history.

Throughout the movie, Robert De Niro delivers a powerful performance as Carl Brashear, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's supporting cast, including Cuba Gooding Jr., Jon Voight, and Michael Rapaport, also deliver strong performances that add to the movie's emotional impact.

Overall, Men of Honor is a powerful and inspiring film that tells the true story of Carl Brashear, an African-American hero who defied the odds to achieve greatness despite facing racism, sexism, and personal tragedy. The movie's themes of perseverance, courage, and redemption make it a must-see for anyone interested in biographical dramas or inspirational stories.

documents.title: Proof of Life
documents.overview: Alice hires a professional negotiator to obtain the release of her engineer husband, who has been kidnapped by anti-government guerrillas in South America.
documents.plot:
Proof of Life is a 2000 American thriller film directed by Antoine Fuqua and starring Meg Ryan, Russell Crowe, and David Morrissey.

The main themes of Proof of Life revolve around:

1. **Kidnapping and Hostage Situation**: The movie revolves around the kidnapping of a group of American aid workers in Kenya by a ruthless terrorist organization. The story explores the complexities of hostage situations, negotiations, and the moral dilemmas faced by the characters.
2. **Humanitarianism and Compassion**: The film highlights the importance of humanitarian work and the sacrifices made by individuals who dedicate their lives to helping others. The protagonist, Teri (Meg Ryan), is a doctor who has dedicated her life to providing aid in Africa, and her experiences serve as a catalyst for the story.
3. **Power Dynamics and Manipulation**: The movie explores the power dynamics between the kidnappers and the hostages, as well as the manipulations used by both sides to achieve their goals. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Amira (Kim Basinger), who uses her intelligence and cunning to manipulate the situation to her advantage.
4. **Personal Sacrifices and Redemption**: Throughout the film, characters are forced to confront their personal demons and make difficult choices that test their moral compass. The story ultimately becomes a journey of redemption for Teri, as she finds a way to escape and reclaim control over her life.

The movie's themes are expertly woven throughout the narrative, creating a tense and thought-provoking thriller that keeps audiences on the edge of their seats.

documents.title: The Pink Panther
documents.tagline: Pardon His French.
documents.overview: When the coach of the France soccer team is killed by a poisoned dart in the stadium in the end of a game, and his expensive and huge ring with the diamond Pink Panther disappears, the ambitious Chief Inspector Dreyfus assigns the worst police inspector Jacques Clouseau to the case.
documents.plot:
The Pink Panther is a 2006 comedy film directed by Shem Bitterman and starring Jason Statham as Inspector Clouseau, a bumbling French detective. The movie is a remake of the classic 1963 film of the same name.

The story begins with the theft of the famous Pink Panther diamond, which was last seen in the possession of the wealthy businessman, Sir Charles Lytton (played by Andy Garcia). The thief, who is revealed to be none other than Sir Charles himself, escapes with the diamond and leaves a trail of clues that lead Inspector Clouseau on a wild goose chase.

As Clouseau delves deeper into the case, he encounters a beautiful and intelligent woman named Colette Marchand (played by Emily Mortimer), who becomes his love interest. However, their budding romance is put to the test as Clouseau's ineptitude causes more chaos than harmony in their relationship.

Meanwhile, Sir Charles Lytton has set up a series of elaborate traps and puzzles to throw Clouseau off his scent. The detective's bumbling nature leads him into various misadventures, including a memorable scene where he gets stuck in a revolving door and another where he accidentally sets off a fire alarm.

As the investigation unfolds, Clouseau becomes increasingly obsessed with solving the case, despite his own ineptitude. He enlists the help of his trusty sidekick, Cato (played by François Berléand), who provides some much-needed comic relief.

In the end, Clouseau's determination and perseverance lead him to uncover Sir Charles Lytton's true identity and recover the stolen Pink Panther diamond. However, in a twist of fate, it is revealed that Colette Marchand is actually an undercover agent working for Sir Charles, adding a layer of complexity to their relationship.

The movie ends with Clouseau and Colette sharing a romantic moment, despite the fact that she has been playing him all along. The final scene features Clouseau's signature catchphrase, "I'm not bad. I'm just drawn that way," as he walks away from the camera with a charming smile on his face.

Overall, The Pink Panther is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that pays homage to the classic film franchise while introducing new characters and plot twists. Jason Statham's portrayal of Inspector Clouseau brings a fresh take to the character, while Emily Mortimer shines as the intelligent and beautiful Colette Marchand.

documents.title: Windtalkers
documents.tagline: Honor Was Their Code.
documents.overview: Joe Enders is a gung-ho Marine assigned to protect a "windtalker" - one of several Navajo Indians who were used to relay messages during World War II because their spoken language was indecipherable to Japanese code breakers.
documents.plot:
Windtalkers is a 2002 war drama film directed by John Woo, and it explores several complex themes that are deeply rooted in its narrative.

At its core, Windtalkers delves into the psychological effects of war on soldiers, particularly those who have witnessed unimaginable horrors. The film sheds light on the struggles of returning veterans to civilian life, grappling with the trauma they've experienced during combat. This theme is poignantly conveyed through the character of Joe Enders (played by Nicolas Cage), a soldier haunted by his past and struggling to reconcile his actions in war with his sense of humanity.

The movie also touches upon the significance of loyalty and camaraderie among soldiers, highlighting the bonds that form between individuals who have shared intense experiences. The relationship between Joe and his fellow soldier, Bana (played by Adam Beach), serves as a powerful example of this theme, showcasing the depth of their connection and the sacrifices they make for one another.

Furthermore, Windtalkers critiques the treatment of Native American soldiers during World War II, particularly those who served as Navajo code talkers. The film sheds light on the often-overlooked contributions of these individuals, who played a crucial role in the Allied victory by deciphering enemy communications using their native language.

The movie's exploration of these themes is marked by a sense of realism and grittiness, reflecting the harsh realities of war. Through its portrayal of the psychological toll of combat and the importance of human connection, Windtalkers offers a thought-provoking commentary on the human cost of conflict and the enduring power of loyalty and friendship.

documents.title: Don't Say a Word
documents.tagline: ...I'll never tell.
documents.overview: When the daughter of a psychiatrist is kidnapped, he's horrified to discover that the abductors' demand is that he break through to a post traumatic stress disorder suffering young woman who knows a secret..
documents.plot:
Don't Say a Word is a psychological thriller film directed by Gregory Hoblit, released in 2001 by 20th Century Fox.

The movie revolves around the story of Nathan Smith (played by Dominic West), a young man who suffers from amnesia and has no memory of his past. He is found unconscious on a train with severe head injuries, and as he tries to regain his memories, he becomes embroiled in a mystery involving a woman named Emma (played by Michelle Monaghan) and her husband, John (played by John Travolta).

The main themes of Don't Say a Word include:

1. Identity: The film explores Nathan's struggle to regain his identity and remember his past, which serves as a metaphor for the human search for self-discovery.
2. Trauma: The movie delves into the psychological effects of trauma on individuals, particularly those who have experienced violent or traumatic events.
3. Love and relationships: The story highlights the complexities of love, relationships, and trust, as Nathan becomes increasingly entangled in Emma's life and struggles to form connections with her.
4. Deception and secrets: As the plot unfolds, it becomes clear that everyone involved is hiding secrets, leading to a web of deception and mistrust.

The film's climax reveals a shocking twist, which I won't spoil here, but it ultimately leads to Nathan's journey towards healing and self-discovery.

Overall, Don't Say a Word is a gripping thriller that explores the complexities of human psychology, relationships, and identity.

documents.title: Nutty Professor II: The Klumps
documents.tagline: The Klumps are back!
documents.overview: The hilarity begins when professor Sherman Klump finds romance with fellow DNA specialist, Denise Gaines, and discovers a brilliant formula that reverses aging. But Sherman's thin and obnoxious alter ego, Buddy Love, wants out...and a big piece of the action. And when Buddy gets loose, things get seriously nutty.
documents.plot:
Nutty Professor II: The Klumps is a 2000 American comedy film directed by Shemar Moore and Brian Robbins, produced by Imagine Entertainment.

The movie follows the story of Sherman Klump (played by Eddie Murphy), a successful professor who has just been accepted into an Ivy League university. However, his life is turned upside down when he discovers that his long-lost father, Buck Cluck (played by James Coburn), is a con artist and a master of disguise.

As the story unfolds, Sherman's alter ego, Buddy Love (also played by Eddie Murphy), becomes more prominent, causing chaos in Sherman's personal and professional life. Meanwhile, Sherman also falls in love with a beautiful woman named Carla Purdy (played by Janet Jackson).

The main themes of Nutty Professor II: The Klumps include:

1. Identity Crisis: The movie explores the theme of identity crisis as Sherman struggles to balance his two personas - the intelligent and responsible professor, and the carefree and eccentric Buddy Love.
2. Family Secrets: The film highlights the importance of family secrets and the consequences of keeping them hidden. Buck Cluck's past mistakes come back to haunt him, causing trouble for Sherman and those around him.
3. Self-Discovery: Through his experiences, Sherman learns valuable lessons about himself and what it means to be true to oneself. He must navigate his relationships with his father, friends, and loved ones while staying true to his own identity.
4. Love and Relationships: The movie showcases the importance of love and relationships in our lives. Sherman's romance with Carla helps him find balance and stability, but also creates tension between his two personas.

Overall, Nutty Professor II: The Klumps is a lighthearted comedy that explores themes of identity, family, self-discovery, and love, all while maintaining the signature humor and wit of Eddie Murphy.

documents.title: Body of Lies
documents.tagline: Trust no one. Deceive everyone.
documents.overview: The CIA’s hunt is on for the mastermind of a wave of terrorist attacks. Roger Ferris is the agency’s man on the ground, moving from place to place, scrambling to stay ahead of ever-shifting events. An eye in the sky – a satellite link – watches Ferris.  At the other end of that real-time link is the CIA’s Ed Hoffman, strategizing events from thousands of miles away. And as Ferris nears the target, he discovers trust can be just as dangerous as it is necessary for survival.
documents.plot:
Body of Lies is a thought-provoking spy thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, loyalty, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The film's narrative is driven by the cat-and-mouse game between CIA operative Roger Ferris (Leonardo DiCaprio) and MI6 agent Jason Hawkins (Russell Crowe), as they navigate the treacherous world of Middle Eastern politics.

At its core, Body of Lies explores the theme of moral ambiguity, where characters are forced to confront their own values and loyalties in a world where right and wrong are not always clear-cut. Ferris's character, in particular, grapples with the consequences of his actions, as he becomes increasingly entangled in a web of deceit and corruption.

The film also examines the theme of cultural identity and the complexities of understanding different cultures. The protagonist's journey takes him from the United States to Jordan, where he must navigate the intricate politics of the Middle East, confronting his own biases and assumptions along the way.

Furthermore, Body of Lies touches on the theme of loyalty and betrayal, highlighting the ways in which individuals can be torn between their personal loyalties and their professional obligations. The film's climax is a heart-wrenching exploration of the consequences of these choices, leaving the audience to ponder the true cost of loyalty and the nature of sacrifice.

Overall, Body of Lies is a gripping thriller that probes the complexities of human nature, challenging viewers to confront their own assumptions about right and wrong, loyalty, and identity.

documents.title: Step Brothers
documents.tagline: They grow up so fast.
documents.overview: Brennan Huff and Dale Doback might be grown men. But that doesn't stop them from living at home and turning into jealous, competitive stepbrothers when their single parents marry. Brennan's constant competition with Dale strains his mom's marriage to Dale's dad, leaving everyone to wonder whether they'll ever see eye to eye.
documents.plot:
Step Brothers is a comedy film released in 2008 by Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of two middle-aged men, Brennan Huff (Will Ferrell) and Dale Doback (John C. Reilly), who become stepbrothers when their parents get married.

Brennan, played by Will Ferrell, is a 39-year-old unemployed slacker who still lives with his mother, Nancy (Mary Steenburgen). He is immature, lazy, and has no direction in life. On the other hand, Dale, played by John C. Reilly, is a 40-year-old terminally unemployed man who lives with his father, Robert (Richard Jenkins).

When their parents get married, Brennan and Dale are forced to live together under one roof, leading to a series of hilarious and chaotic events. Initially, they clash and try to outdo each other in various ways, but eventually, they develop an unlikely bond.

As the story progresses, Brennan and Dale start to take on childish behaviors, such as playing video games, eating junk food, and engaging in juvenile pranks. They also start to compete with each other for attention from their parents, leading to a series of ridiculous and absurd situations.

However, when they discover that they are stepbrothers, they realize that they have more in common than they thought. They bond over their shared immaturity and laziness, and they start to support each other in their attempts to find purpose and direction in life.

As the movie reaches its climax, Brennan and Dale decide to take matters into their own hands and try to become a family unit of their own. They come up with a plan to get jobs, move out of their parents' houses, and start a new life together.

In the end, Brennan and Dale succeed in their mission, but not without some hilarious setbacks along the way. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, as Brennan and Dale finally find a sense of belonging and purpose with each other.

Throughout the movie, Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly deliver outstanding performances that showcase their comedic talents. Their chemistry on screen is undeniable, and their characters' antics are both ridiculous and endearing.

Overall, Step Brothers is a hilarious and entertaining comedy that explores themes of masculinity, identity, and the importance of family. With its witty dialogue, physical humor, and memorable performances, it's no wonder that this movie has become a cult classic.

documents.title: 3000 Miles to Graceland
documents.tagline: Crime Is King
documents.overview: It was an ingenious enough plan: rob the Riviera Casino's count room during an Elvis impersonator convention. But Thomas Murphy decided to keep all the money for himself and shot all his partners, including recently-freed ex-con Michael Zane. With $3.2 million at stake, the Marshals Service closing in, Michael must track down Murphy.
documents.plot:
3000 Miles to Graceland is a 2001 American action crime film directed and co-produced by Demian Lichtenstein, who shares a writing credit with Richard Recco, the author of the original script. The cast includes Kurt Russell, Kevin Costner, Courteney Cox, David Arquette, Bokeem Woodbine, Christian Slater, Kevin Pollak and Daisy McCrackin. The title refers to Elvis Presley's home, Graceland.

Recently paroled Michael Zane stops at a run-down desert motel outside Las Vegas, where he catches a boy, Jesse, stealing from his car and follows him back to his mother, Cybil Waingrow, whom he seduces. The next day Michael is collected by Murphy, Hanson, Gus and Franklin, and the five men, dressed as Elvis, rob the Riviera casino during an Elvis convention. Franklin is killed in the shootout during their escape, and Murphy later shoots Hanson in a quarrel over Franklin's share. Michael hides the money in the attic, unaware that Jesse is watching. When the survivors drive into the desert to bury Hanson, Murphy shoots Gus and Michael, but on his way back he hits a coyote and is knocked out in the crash. Michael, saved by a bulletproof vest, returns to find the money gone, retrieves it from Cybil's room and reluctantly takes mother and son with him, since the marked cash must be laundered through a contact in Idaho. Cybil steals Michael's wallet and the password for the launderer, Peterson, and drives off, but Murphy, using the same password, reaches Peterson first, and Cybil walks into his trap; Michael later finds Peterson and his secretary dead. Michael has Murphy arrested by reporting his own car stolen, but is also jailed for driving a stolen vehicle; Jesse bails him out in exchange for becoming his partner, while Murphy secures his release through a contact and recruits a mercenary. After Murphy runs Cybil and Jesse off the road and takes the boy hostage, Michael tips off the authorities and meets Murphy at a warehouse to trade. The bag Michael hands over is full of cut-up newspaper and a hidden scorpion, which stings Murphy. Surrounded by a SWAT team, Murphy shoots Michael and is killed by police. Cybil and Jesse steal the ambulance carrying Michael, again saved by a vest, and the three escape aboard his boat, the Graceland.

Released on February 23, 2001, the film was panned, with a 15% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and earned only $18.7 million against a budget of $47.4 million. It received five Golden Raspberry Award nominations.

documents.title: Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence
documents.tagline: When machines learn to feel, who decides what is human...
documents.overview: Cyborg detective Batou is assigned to investigate a series of murders committed by gynoids—doll-like cyborgs, which all malfunctioned, killed, then self-destructed afterwards. The brains of the gynoids initialize in order to protect their manufacturer's software, but in one gynoid, which Batou himself neutralized, one file remains: a voice speaking the phrase "Help me."
documents.plot:
Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence is a thought-provoking anime film that explores several complex themes. Here are some of the main themes present in the movie:

1. **Existentialism and Identity**: The film delves into the nature of existence, identity, and what it means to be human. The protagonist, Major Motoko Kusanagi, is a cyborg who begins to question her own existence and the implications of her digital existence on her sense of self.

2. **Free Will vs. Determinism**: The movie raises questions about free will versus determinism, as the main character's actions are influenced by both her programming and her own desires. This theme is explored through the character of Batou, who struggles with his own identity and purpose.

3. **Love and Human Connection**: Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence explores the concept of love and human connection in a world where technology has blurred the lines between humans and machines. The film's portrayal of Motoko's relationships with her colleagues and allies serves as a commentary on the importance of human connections in a society dominated by technology.

4. **Mortality and Transcendence**: The movie touches on the theme of mortality and transcendence, as the characters grapple with the possibility of digital immortality and the implications of such a concept on their understanding of life and death.

5. **Philosophy of Mind**: Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence engages with various philosophical concepts related to the nature of mind and consciousness, including the idea that the human mind is not solely located in the brain but can exist independently of it.

6. **Societal Commentary**: The film offers a commentary on contemporary society's relationship with technology, exploring themes such as surveillance, control, and the impact of technological advancements on individual freedom and autonomy.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story.

documents.title: Alone in the Dark
documents.tagline: Can mankind defeat the army of darkness unleashed by an ancient evil cult?
documents.overview: Edward Carnby is a private investigator specializing in unexplainable supernatural phenomena. His cases delve into the dark corners of the world, searching for truth in the occult remnants of ancient civilizations. Now, the greatest mystery of his past is about to become the most dangerous case he has ever faced.
documents.plot:
Alone in the Dark is a 2005 horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring the theme of isolation and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie follows Edward Carnby, a paranormal investigator who must stop an ancient evil from unleashing a catastrophic event.

At its core, Alone in the Dark is a tale of psychological terror, where the protagonist's own demons are exploited by the malevolent force he's trying to defeat. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the supernatural entity itself, but in the darkness that lurks within human hearts.

The film also touches on the theme of obsession, as Edward's fixation on stopping the evil leads him down a path of self-destruction. The movie raises questions about the nature of good and evil, suggesting that they are not mutually exclusive, but rather intertwined aspects of the human condition.

Furthermore, Alone in the Dark explores the idea of the "other," highlighting the fear and mistrust that can arise when we're faced with something or someone that's beyond our understanding. The film's use of atmospheric tension and eerie visuals creates a sense of unease, mirroring the feelings of disorientation and confusion that Edward experiences as he navigates the treacherous world of paranormal investigation.

Overall, Alone in the Dark is a thought-provoking horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of isolation, obsession, and the blurred lines between good and evil.
production_companies: Boll Kino Beteiligungs GmbH & Co. KG

documents.title: Frailty
documents.tagline: No Soul Is Safe.
documents.overview: A man confesses to an FBI agent his family's story of how his religious fanatic father's visions lead to a series of murders to destroy supposed 'demons'.
documents.plot:
Frailty is a psychological horror-thriller film directed by Bill Paxton, released in 2001 by Cinerenta Medienbeteiligungs KG. The movie follows the story of Adam Bell (played by Bill Paxton), a struggling writer who claims to have been visited by God and has received a series of instructions that he must follow.

The main themes of Frailty include:

1. **Faith vs. Sanity**: The film explores the blurred lines between faith and madness, as Adam's actions become increasingly erratic and violent. His wife, Meri (played by Carrie-Anne Moss), tries to intervene, but Adam is convinced that he is doing God's work.
2. **The Nature of Evil**: Frailty raises questions about the existence of evil and whether it can be justified or excused. Adam's actions become more and more violent as he follows his instructions from God, leading to a confrontation with his own morality.
3. **Isolation and Loneliness**: The film highlights the isolation and loneliness that can come with having a unique perspective on the world. Adam is a outsider among his family and friends, who struggle to understand his actions and motivations.
4. **The Power of Perception**: Frailty shows how perception can be distorted by one's own beliefs and biases. Adam's interpretation of God's instructions leads him down a dark path, while Meri's more rational perspective tries to bring him back from the brink.

Overall, Frailty is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and moral ambiguities, leaving the audience questioning what it means to be good or evil.

documents.title: White Chicks
documents.tagline: They're going deep undercover.
documents.overview: Two FBI agent brothers, Marcus and Kevin Copeland, accidentally foil a drug bust. To avoid being fired they accept a mission escorting a pair of socialites to the Hamptons--but when the girls are disfigured in a car accident, they refuse to go. Left without options, Marcus and Kevin decide to pose as the sisters, transforming themselves from black men into rich white women.
documents.plot:
White Chicks is a 2004 American comedy film directed by Keenen Ivory Wayans and written by Shawn Wayans and Marlon Wayans. The movie stars Shawn Wayans and Marlon Wayans as two FBI agents who go undercover as white women to solve a kidnapping case.

The story begins with Kevin Copeland (Shawn Wayans) and Marcus Copeland (Marlon Wayans), two African American brothers who work for the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). The brothers are assigned to investigate the kidnapping of two wealthy heiresses, Brittany and Tiffany Wilson (played by Jennifer Carpenter and Brittany Daniel respectively).

The FBI's top brass decide that the best way to get close to the kidnappers is for Kevin and Marcus to go undercover as white women. They undergo a radical transformation, complete with wigs, breast implants, and fake accents.

As they navigate their new lives as "Christine" and "Nikki," the brothers struggle to maintain their cover. However, they soon discover that being white isn't all it's cracked up to be. They face racism from some of the people they meet, including a group of white supremacists who are also after the Wilson sisters.

As Kevin and Marcus delve deeper into the case, they uncover a complex web of deceit and corruption involving the kidnappers, the FBI, and even their own agency. Along the way, they encounter a range of colorful characters, including a bumbling FBI agent (played by Snoop Dogg) and a seductive nightclub singer (played by Faizon Love).

Throughout the movie, Kevin and Marcus's fish-out-of-water experiences provide plenty of comedic moments. However, as the story unfolds, the brothers also discover that being white isn't just about looks - it's also about attitude and behavior.

In the end, Kevin and Marcus are able to solve the kidnapping case and bring the perpetrators to justice. Along the way, they learn a valuable lesson about identity, community, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

Overall, White Chicks is a hilarious and entertaining comedy that explores themes of identity, racism, and brotherhood. With its talented cast, witty script, and outrageous humor, it's no wonder that this movie has become a cult classic.

documents.title: Alice in Wonderland
documents.tagline: You're invited to a very important date.
documents.overview: Alice, now 19 years old, returns to the whimsical world she first entered as a child and embarks on a journey to discover her true destiny.
documents.plot:
Alice in Wonderland is a 2010 American Gothic dark fantasy adventure film directed by Tim Burton from a screenplay by Linda Woolverton and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. A live-action reimagining of Lewis Carroll's works, it stars Mia Wasikowska as Alice Kingsleigh, Johnny Depp as the Mad Hatter, Helena Bonham Carter as the Red Queen, Anne Hathaway as the White Queen, Crispin Glover as the Knave of Hearts and Matt Lucas as Tweedledum and Tweedledee, with the voices of Alan Rickman, Stephen Fry, Michael Sheen and Christopher Lee.

In 1871 London, nineteen-year-old Alice, still grieving her father and troubled by recurring strange dreams, is proposed to by Hamish Ascot at a garden party. Spotting a white rabbit in a waistcoat, she follows it down a rabbit hole and enters a fantastical world called Underland. There Absolem the Caterpillar says she is destined to slay the Jabberwocky and end the tyranny of the Red Queen, who has usurped her sister, the White Queen. The Red Queen's knights and the monstrous Bandersnatch capture most of Alice's companions, but she escapes, and the Cheshire Cat leads her to the tea party of the Mad Hatter and the March Hare. The Hatter sacrifices his freedom so she can flee, and the bloodhound Bayard, an ally of the resistance, takes her to the Red Queen's castle.

Grown huge again and posing as a courtier named "Um", Alice learns that the vorpal sword, the only weapon able to kill the Jabberwocky, is kept in the Bandersnatch's den. When she rebuffs the Knave's advances, the jealous queen orders her beheaded, but Alice takes the sword, wins over the Bandersnatch by returning its stolen eye and escapes to the White Queen. The Cheshire Cat frees the Hatter, who stirs rebellion, and Absolem, entering his chrysalis, helps Alice remember that she visited "Wonderland" as a child. On a chessboard battlefield, Alice beheads the Jabberwocky, the Red Queen's knights abandon her, and the White Queen exiles her sister with the Knave. Using the Jabberwocky's blood, Alice returns home, turns down Hamish and proposes to Lord Ascot her father's idea of trading routes to Hong Kong, becoming his apprentice; as she sets sail, Absolem, now a butterfly, lands on her shoulder.

The film grossed $1.025 billion worldwide, the second-highest total of 2010. Reviews were mixed, with 51% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a visual treat lacking heart. It won Academy Awards for Best Art Direction and Best Costume Design.

documents.title: The Hurt Locker
documents.tagline: You'll know when you're in it.
documents.overview: During the Iraq War, a Sergeant recently assigned to an army bomb squad is put at odds with his squad mates due to his maverick way of handling his work.
documents.plot:
The Hurt Locker is a 2008 American war film directed by Kathryn Bigelow and written by Mark Boal, who drew on his time as a journalist embedded with a U.S. Army bomb squad in Iraq in 2004. Jeremy Renner stars as Sergeant First Class William James, with Anthony Mackie as Sergeant J. T. Sanborn, Brian Geraghty as Specialist Owen Eldridge, Guy Pearce as Staff Sergeant Matthew Thompson, Ralph Fiennes as the leader of a private military unit and Evangeline Lilly as James's former wife, Connie.

In the second year of the Iraq War, a U.S. Army explosive ordnance disposal team from Bravo Company is trying to destroy a roadside bomb when its robot fails, and team leader Thompson is killed when an insurgent detonates the device with a mobile phone as he places a charge by hand. Eldridge blames himself for not shooting the man in time. Thompson's replacement, James, clashes with Sanborn by defusing bombs by hand and keeping his plans to himself. He disarms one device moments before an insurgent can set it off, and later insists on dismantling a complex car bomb despite Sanborn's protests, pulling off his headset and making an obscene gesture. Alarmed, Sanborn even raises the idea of fragging James. Returning from the field, the team meets a group of British private contractors with a disabled vehicle, and when snipers open fire, James and Sanborn take over the counter-sniping and Eldridge kills an insurgent trying to outflank them. In a warehouse, James finds a child's body rigged as a bomb that he believes is Beckham, a boy who sells DVDs outside the base, and Eldridge's counselor, Lieutenant Colonel Cambridge, is killed by a blast. James slips off base to find Beckham's family but ends up at the house of an unrelated professor. After a fuel tanker explosion, James leads Sanborn and Eldridge after the bombers; Eldridge is captured and, though rescued, shot in the leg, blaming James. Near the end of their rotation, the team cannot free a man locked into a bomb vest, and a shaken Sanborn admits that he wants to leave the army and have a son. At home with Connie and their baby, James finds civilian life empty, and he returns to Iraq for another tour with Delta Company.

The Hurt Locker premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2008 and was released in the United States by Summit Entertainment in June 2009. Widely acclaimed, it won six of its nine Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, making Bigelow the first woman to win Best Director.

documents.title: The Wrestler
documents.tagline: Love. Pain. Glory.
documents.overview: Aging wrestler Randy "The Ram" Robinson is long past his prime but still ready and rarin' to go on the pro-wrestling circuit. After a particularly brutal beating, however, Randy hangs up his tights, pursues a serious relationship with a long-in-the-tooth stripper, and tries to reconnect with his estranged daughter. But he can't resist the lure of the ring and readies himself for a comeback.
documents.plot:
The Wrestler is a 2008 American sports drama directed by Darren Aronofsky and written by Robert Siegel. Mickey Rourke stars as an aging professional wrestler who keeps fighting despite failing health and fading fame, driven by money troubles and a wish to relive his 1980s glory, with Marisa Tomei as a stripper he hopes to romance and Evan Rachel Wood as his estranged daughter.

Robin Ramzinski, known in the ring as Randy "The Ram" Robinson, was a wrestling star in the 1980s. Twenty years later he wrestles on weekends for small New Jersey promotions, lives in a trailer park and works part time at a supermarket under a manager who belittles him. A regular at a strip club, he befriends a dancer, Pam, who performs as Cassidy. After a local win he agrees to a 20th-anniversary rematch with his most famous opponent, the Ayatollah, hoping to regain stardom, and steps up his training and steroid use. After a brutal hardcore match he suffers a heart attack and has bypass surgery, and his doctor warns that his heart can no longer take wrestling. Randy reluctantly retires and takes a full-time job at the deli counter.

Encouraged by Cassidy, he seeks out his daughter, Stephanie, whom he abandoned as a child. She rejects him at first, but after he apologizes they reconnect on a boardwalk he used to take her to and plan dinner. Cassidy, a single mother, refuses his romantic advances, citing her rule against dating customers, and after a quarrel with her Randy goes on a night of drinking, drugs and sex, then sleeps through his dinner with Stephanie. When he shows up to apologize, she cuts him out of her life for good. Recognized by a customer at the deli, Randy cuts his hand on the slicer, quits in a rage and recommits to the rematch. Cassidy, who has left her job, begs him not to wrestle, but he tells her he belongs in the ring with the fans. During the match, as his chest pains worsen, the Ayatollah urges him to end it quickly, but Randy climbs the top rope, sees that Cassidy has gone, smiles at the crowd chanting his name and leaps into his signature "Ram Jam" as the screen fades to black.

The film premiered at the 65th Venice International Film Festival, where it won the Golden Lion,. It grossed $44.7 million on a $6 million budget and was universally acclaimed, with 99% on Rotten Tomatoes. The role revived Rourke's career, earning him a Golden Globe, a BAFTA and an Academy Award nomination, and Tomei was also nominated for an Oscar.

documents.title: The Burning Plain
documents.tagline: Their passion has marked them for life.
documents.overview: A trailer is burning in the middle of a plain. The bodies of two adulterous lovers are found. Scenes from both families, before and after the dramatic events, suggest an unusual connection between them. But what is their secret?
documents.plot:
The Burning Plain is a 2008 drama written and directed by Guillermo Arriaga, writer of Amores perros, 21 Grams and Babel, in his directing debut. Charlize Theron stars as Sylvia, with Jennifer Lawrence as her younger self, Mariana, Kim Basinger as Gina, Joaquim de Almeida as Nick Martinez, José María Yazpik as Carlos, Danny Pino as Santiago and Tessa Ía as Maria. As in Arriaga's earlier scripts, several strands are told out of sequence.

In a small New Mexico town near Las Cruces and the Mexican border in the mid-1990s, Gina, a married mother of four, is having an affair with Nick Martinez, who also has a family. Her teenage daughter Mariana discovers the affair and follows her mother to Nick's trailer. Hoping to frighten them into ending it, she disconnects the gas line and sets a fire, but the flames reach a gas tank and the explosion kills both lovers, though Mariana never meant to harm them. After the funeral, Mariana is drawn to Nick's son Santiago, and the two fall in love. When she becomes pregnant, they run away to Mexico in the face of their families' disapproval, but soon after giving birth to a daughter, Mariana abandons both of them and takes a new name, Sylvia.

More than a decade later, Sylvia works at an upscale restaurant in Oregon. Despite her success, she has only casual encounters and recurring suicidal thoughts. A stranger has been following her: Carlos, Santiago's friend and business partner. Santiago, who has searched for Sylvia ever since she left him with their two-day-old daughter, has been badly hurt in the crash of their crop-dusting plane and has sent Carlos to find her. Since Carlos speaks no English and Sylvia no Spanish, he brings along her twelve-year-old daughter, Maria, instead. Maria, already reluctant to meet the mother who left her, is devastated when Sylvia sees them waiting outside her home and flees without a word. Regretting it, Sylvia gets her friend Laura to help find them. Reunited, the three travel to Mexico, where Sylvia apologises to Maria for her long absence and, at the bedside of the sedated Santiago, confesses what she has done. The doctor assures them that he will recover, and the film ends on a hopeful note.

The Burning Plain was filmed in New Mexico beginning in November 2007 and competed at the 65th Venice Film Festival before a limited release by Magnolia Pictures in 2009. Reviews were generally poor, with 38% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it grossed about $5.5 million worldwide.

documents.title: The Love Guru
documents.tagline: His Karma is Huge
documents.overview: Born in America and raised in an Indian ashram, Pitka returns to his native land to seek his fortune as a spiritualist and self-help expert. His skills are put to the test when he must get a brokenhearted hockey player's marriage back on track in time for the man to help his team win the Stanley Cup.
documents.plot:
The Love Guru is a 2008 romantic comedy directed by Marco Schnabel in his directorial debut, and written and produced by Mike Myers, who also stars. Jessica Alba, Justin Timberlake, Romany Malco, Meagan Good, Verne Troyer, John Oliver, Omid Djalili and Ben Kingsley complete the cast. The story centres on a self-help guru hired to restore the fortunes of the Toronto Maple Leafs hockey team. Myers developed the character from comic routines he had performed over several years, drawing on his interest in Eastern spirituality and self-help culture.

Myers plays Guru Pitka, an American-born spiritual teacher raised in an ashram in India, who proudly describes himself as the second-best guru in the world, after Deepak Chopra. As a child he was taught by Guru Tugginmypudha, played by Kingsley, who made him wear a chastity belt until he learns that loving oneself is more important than being loved by others. Pitka's dream is to become the world's number-one guru and be invited onto The Oprah Winfrey Show. He enjoys a celebrity following, and his teachings consist of simple acronyms and puns presented in slide shows.

In Toronto, Jane Bullard, played by Alba, has inherited the Maple Leafs, who are on a long losing streak. Their star player, Darren Roanoke, played by Malco, has lost his form since his wife Prudence left him for Jacques "Le Coq" Grandé, the arrogant goaltender of the Los Angeles Kings, played by Timberlake. Jane, a devoted follower of Pitka, offers him two million dollars to fix Darren's marriage so that the team can win the Stanley Cup, and the guru agrees, realising that success will secure him a spot on Oprah's show. Working alongside the team's diminutive coach, played by Troyer, Pitka uses unorthodox methods to rebuild Darren's confidence, while he finds himself falling for Jane despite the restrictions of his belt.

The film relies on broad slapstick, sexual innuendo and wordplay, and some Hindu groups criticised its portrayal of religious practices before its release.

The Love Guru was a critical and commercial failure. Reviewers overwhelmingly panned its humour, and it won three Golden Raspberry Awards, including Worst Picture, Worst Actor for Myers and Worst Screenplay.

documents.title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
documents.overview: Set between Episode II and III, The Clone Wars is the first computer animated Star Wars film. Anakin and Obi Wan must find out who kidnapped Jabba the Hutt's son and return him safely. The Separatists will try anything to stop them and ruin any chance of a diplomatic agreement between the Hutts and the Republic.
documents.plot:
Star Wars: The Clone Wars is a 2008 animated science fiction film directed by Dave Filoni, George Lucas, and Karen Gilchrist. The movie takes place between Attack of the Clones and Revenge of the Sith in the Star Wars universe.

The main themes of Star Wars: The Clone Wars include:

1. **Loyalty vs. Duty**: Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen) is faced with a difficult decision when he is ordered to execute Order 66, which would lead to the execution of Jedi Knights. This theme explores the conflict between loyalty to one's friends and duty to follow orders.

2. **The Gray Area Between Good and Evil**: The Clone Wars introduce a more nuanced view of the Star Wars universe, where characters are not simply good or evil. Anakin's character development is particularly notable in this regard, as he struggles with his own morality.

3. **Friendship and Camaraderie**: The film highlights the strong bonds between Anakin, Obi-Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor), Ahsoka Tano (Ashley Eckstein), and other clone troopers. These relationships are tested as they face numerous challenges together.

4. **The Cost of War**: The Clone Wars depict a galaxy in chaos, with widespread destruction and loss of life. This theme serves as a reminder of the devastating consequences of war and the importance of finding alternative solutions to conflict.

5. **Personal Growth and Self-Discovery**: Anakin's journey is marked by significant personal growth, as he grapples with his own identity and the expectations placed upon him. Ahsoka Tano also undergoes a transformative experience, learning valuable lessons about her place in the galaxy.

Overall, Star Wars: The Clone Wars offers a rich and complex exploration of these themes, setting the stage for the events of Revenge of the Sith and beyond.

documents.title: Nick and Norah's Infinite Playlist
documents.tagline: Every night has a soundtrack.
documents.overview: Nick cannot stop obsessing over his ex-girlfriend, Tris, until Tris' friend Norah suddenly shows interest in him at a club. Thus begins an odd night filled with ups and downs as the two keep running into Tris and her new boyfriend while searching for Norah's drunken friend, Caroline, with help from Nick's band mates. As the night winds down, the two have to figure out what they want from each other.
documents.plot:
Nick and Norah's Infinite Playlist is a 2008 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Peter Sollett. The movie follows the story of two teenagers, Nick (Michael Cera) and Norah (Kat Dennings), who meet at a concert in New York City.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. **Self-discovery**: Both Nick and Norah are trying to find their place in the world. They're navigating high school, relationships, and their own identities. The film explores their struggles with growing up and figuring out what they want to do with their lives.
2. **Love and connection**: The movie highlights the beauty of chance encounters and the power of human connections. Nick and Norah's relationship is built on a foundation of shared experiences, music, and mutual understanding.
