Its premise has Santa Claus return to his demonic nature after a thousand years of forced gift-giving imposed when he lost a bet with an angel. The cast includes Bill Goldberg, Douglas Smith, Emilie de Ravin, Robert Culp, Saul Rubinek, Dave Thomas, Rebecca Gayheart, Chris Kattan and Fran Drescher.

On Christmas Eve in Alberta, the wealthy Mason family is squabbling over dinner when Santa comes down the chimney and kills them all in gruesome holiday-themed ways. Riding a sleigh pulled by a buffalo-like "hell-deer", he descends on the town of Hell Township, slaughtering the patrons of a strip club and the owner of a Jewish delicatessen, Mr. Green. Teenager Nicholas Yuleson lives with his grandfather, an eccentric inventor who hides from Christmas in a basement bunker. Grandpa shows Nicholas "The Book of Klaus", which reveals that Santa was born of a virgin birth fathered by Satan and that Christmas was his "Day of Slaying" until AD 1005, when an angel beat him at curling and condemned him to deliver presents for a thousand years. That sentence has now run out.

Questioned by police about Mr. Green's murder, Nicholas is bailed out by Mary "Mac" Mackenzie, the girl he likes, moments before Santa massacres the officers. Santa chases the pair, who escape with the help of a shotgun in Mac's truck and flee to Grandpa's bunker. They escape again on a snowmobile, and Grandpa appears to be killed. Hiding in the local high school in the hope that Santa's power will end with Christmas, they are cornered in the gym and nearly run down by Santa driving a Zamboni, until Grandpa returns and reveals that he is the angel who defeated Santa long ago. As Christmas ends and his powers fade, Santa flees, and Mac's father shoots down the hell-deer with a bazooka. A crooked local pastor, Timmons, is found dead in a Santa suit and blamed for the killings, while the real Santa boards a flight from Winnipeg to the North Pole under the name "Mr. Šatan". Nicholas vows to finish his grandfather's work. After the credits, Santa studies his naughty list and asks who is next.

Lionsgate released the film on DVD in the United States on December 20, 2005. Reviews were mixed: The A.V. Club found it vulgar yet wholesome and stupid yet satirical, and HorrorNews.net called it fun, brainless and violent.

documents.title: Pokémon: The Movie 2000
documents.original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター 幻のポケモン ルギア爆誕
documents.tagline: One person can make all the difference.
documents.overview: When Lawrence III's scheme to capture the Legendary Pokémon Lugia upsets the balance of nature, it is up to Ash Ketchum and his friends to save the world.
documents.plot:
Pokémon: The Movie 2000, also known as Pokémon 2000: The Power of One, is a Japanese animated science fantasy film based on the popular Pokémon media franchise. The movie was produced by OLM, Inc., and TV Tokyo.

The story begins with Ash Ketchum, a young trainer from Pallet Town, who is on his way to the Indigo League tournament with his Pikachu. However, their journey takes an unexpected turn when they encounter a mysterious and powerful Pokémon known as Suicune, one of the three Legendary Beasts of Johto.

Suicune is being pursued by Team Rocket, who seek to capture it for their nefarious plans. Ash and Pikachu soon find themselves entangled in the chase, along with other trainers and their Pokémon. As they journey across the Johto region, they uncover a hidden truth about Suicune's past and its connection to the balance of nature.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as Lawrence III is revealed to be behind Team Rocket's plans. He seeks to exploit Suicune's power for his own gain, which would disrupt the natural balance and allow him to control the world. Ash and his friends must now stop Lawrence and his team from achieving their sinister goals.

Throughout the movie, Ash and Pikachu form a strong bond with Suicune, learning about its unique abilities and the importance of teamwork and trust. The film features epic battles between the trainers and their Pokémon, as well as heartwarming moments of friendship and growth.

As the story unfolds, Ash and his friends face numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, fierce wild Pokémon, and even a rival trainer named Clair. However, with Suicune's guidance and support, they are able to overcome these hurdles and ultimately defeat Lawrence and his team.

In the climactic final battle, Ash confronts Lawrence III in an epic showdown. With Pikachu by his side, Ash uses all his skills and strategy to outmaneuver Lawrence and shatter his plans for world domination. In the end, Suicune is able to find peace and return to its natural habitat, restoring balance to the region.

Pokémon: The Movie 2000 features stunning animation, engaging characters, and an exciting plot that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the importance of preserving nature. With its memorable soundtrack and lovable Pokémon, this film has become a beloved classic among fans of the franchise.

documents.title: Pokémon 4Ever
documents.original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター セレビィ 時を超えた遭遇
documents.tagline: Best friends. Better heroes.
documents.overview: 40 years ago, a Celebi was being attacked by a Pokemon Hunter. Luckily, a young boy named Yukinari saved Celebi. Using its Time Traveling power, Celebi transported itself and Yukinari 40 years into the future. There, Satoshi, Kasumi, and Takeshi assist Yukinari to the healing lake in the forest so they can heal the wounded Celebi. Unfortunately an evil Team Rocket member, Vicious, tries to capture Celebi using his technology. As Satoshi and Co. try to get away from Vicious, they also run into Musashi, Kojiro, and Nyarth, who also want to capture Celebi. Soon it becomes a race against time to get Celebi and Yukinari back to the forest before Celebi is caught and is used to destroy the forest and themselves.
documents.plot:
Pokémon 4Ever is a 2001 Japanese anime film based on the Pokémon television series, the fourth official Pokémon film. Directed by Kunihiko Yuyama and written by Hideki Sonoda, it was released in Japan on July 7, 2001, with a Japanese cast led by Rica Matsumoto and Ikue Ōtani. Its English adaptation, produced by 4Kids Entertainment and directed by Jim Malone, starred the regular television voice cast of Veronica Taylor, Eric Stuart, Rachael Lillis and Maddie Blaustein. Producer Norman Grossfeld called its animation by Oriental Light and Magic the studio's finest yet.

In a forest in the Johto region, the young trainer Sammy protects Celebi, a Mythical Pokémon able to travel through time, from a Pokémon Hunter, and Celebi carries him forty years into the future. In the present, the Iron Masked Marauder, a ruthless member of Team Rocket, wants to capture Celebi using Dark Balls, which can seize Pokémon that already belong to trainers, turn them evil and magnify their power. Ash, Misty and Brock, having glimpsed the legendary Suicune near Arborville, are warned by the elderly Towa and her granddaughter Diana about the "Voice of the Forest". They find Sammy and the injured Celebi and, guided by wild Pokémon, take it to the healing Lake of Life, where Ash and Sammy bond.

The Marauder captures Celebi with a Dark Ball and uses its power over nature to encase it in enormous armor formed from the forest, revealing that he plans to overthrow Giovanni and rule the world. With Suicune's help, Ash, Sammy and Pikachu breach the armor and reach Celebi, freeing it from the Dark Ball's control, but Celebi dies in Sammy's arms. Even Suicune's purified lake cannot revive it, until the true Voice of the Forest, the Celebi of every era, appears and brings it back to life. After a last escape attempt, the Marauder crashes into the forest, where angry wild Pokémon surround him. Celebi returns Sammy to his own time, and when Ash later speaks to Professor Oak, the professor knows Sammy's name without being told, and his old sketchbook reveals that he was Sammy.

Released in North America on October 11, 2002, by Miramax Films, which had taken over the series' distribution from Warner Bros., the film opened in only 249 theaters and earned about $1.7 million there, though it did better on home video. In Japan it grossed $39 million, bringing its worldwide total to about $40.8 million.

documents.title: Help! I'm a Fish
documents.tagline: A potion put them in the ocean
documents.overview: Three children accidentally get turned into fish after drinking a potion made by an eccentric scientist. The kids end up in the sea, with one problem. They must find and drink the antidote within 48 hours, or forever remain as fish.
documents.plot:
Help! I'm a Fish (Danish: Hjælp, jeg er en fisk), also known as A Fish Tale, is a 2000 Danish animated musical fantasy directed by Stefan Fjeldmark, Greg Manwaring and Michael Hegner, and written by Fjeldmark, Karsten Kiilerich, John Stefan Olsen and Tracy J. Brown. Its English-language voice cast includes Alan Rickman, Terry Jones and a young Aaron Paul.

Twelve-year-old Fly, his little sister Stella and their cautious, science-minded cousin Chuck slip out to go fishing while their aunt Anna is babysitting. Caught by the rising tide, they take shelter in the boathouse of Professor MacKrill, an eccentric marine biologist who believes melting ice caps will soon flood the world. He has invented a potion that turns people into fish, along with an antidote to reverse it. Stella drinks the potion thinking it is lemonade and becomes a starfish, and Fly unwittingly tosses her into the sea. When their boat sinks in a storm during the search, Fly and Chuck also take the potion, becoming a flying fish and a jellyfish.

The antidote, meanwhile, has leaked into the ocean, where a pilot fish and a shark swallow it and gain human intelligence. The fish, calling himself Joe, uses it to build an army of clever sea creatures inside a sunken oil tanker and plans an uprising against humanity, with the dim shark as his henchman. Reunited and joined by a seahorse that Stella adopts, the children learn that they have only forty-eight hours before their transformation becomes permanent.

Captured while trying to steal the antidote, they are ordered to produce more of it, but they escape and gather ingredients around the ocean to recreate the formula. Joe corners them, drinks the last of the original antidote and grows hands, while a crab seizes the new batch and proclaims himself king. Passing overhead in a makeshift boat, MacKrill and Fly's father create an underwater whirlpool with a water pump that sucks up Joe's army. The children then travel through intake pipes to the professor's flooded laboratory, where Fly tricks Joe into drinking so much of the spare antidote that he turns human and drowns, Chuck and Stella turn human as their families arrive, and after a frightening moment Fly emerges from a pipe, human again but with a broken leg.

Released in Denmark by Nordisk Film in October 2000, the film was a moderate success there during the school holidays and later opened in the United States and the United Kingdom in 2001.

documents.title: Osmosis Jones
documents.tagline: Every body needs a hero.
documents.overview: A white blood cell policeman, with the help of a cold pill, must stop a deadly virus from destroying the human they live in, Frank.
documents.plot:
Osmosis Jones is an animated comedy film that explores the theme of teamwork and unity among different individuals with unique skills and strengths. The movie follows the story of a white blood cell named Frank, who teams up with a genetically engineered antibiotic pill named Drix to stop a deadly virus from taking over the body.

The main theme of Osmosis Jones is the power of collaboration and diversity in overcoming adversity. Frank and Drix, despite being vastly different, learn to put aside their differences and work together to save the day. This theme is reflected in the film's portrayal of the human immune system, where different cells and organs work together to keep the body healthy.

The movie also explores the idea of individuality and self-acceptance. Frank, as a white blood cell, struggles with his own identity and purpose, while Drix, as an antibiotic pill, is initially seen as an outsider by the other cells in the body. Through their journey, they learn to appreciate and celebrate their unique qualities.

Furthermore, Osmosis Jones touches on the theme of perseverance and determination. Frank and Drix face numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to stop the virus, but they never give up. Their unwavering commitment to their mission ultimately leads to a triumphant outcome.

Overall, Osmosis Jones is a heartwarming film that celebrates the importance of teamwork, diversity, and individuality in overcoming adversity.

documents.title: Godzilla Against MechaGodzilla
documents.tagline: Startup - Resonance - Smashed Ice
documents.overview: JSDF pilot Akane has a fateful encounter when a new Godzilla emerges in Tateyama. As a countermeasure, a cyborg named Kiryu is constructed from the remains of the original. The machine is discovered to harbor the restless soul of the original monster as Akane must learn to find value in her own life as well.
documents.plot:
Godzilla Against Mechagodzilla is a 2002 Japanese kaiju film directed by Masaaki Tezuka, with special effects by Yūichi Kikuchi. Distributed by Toho, it is the 27th Godzilla film and the fourth of the franchise's Millennium era. It brings back Mechagodzilla, here mostly called by its code name, Kiryu, from the Japanese for "machine dragon". Unlike the other Millennium films, which follow only the 1954 original, it takes place in a continuity that refers to several of Toho's earlier monster films. A direct sequel, Godzilla: Tokyo S.O.S., followed in 2003.

Decades after the first Godzilla was killed, Lieutenant Akane Yashiro of the Anti-Megalosaurus Force fails to stop a new Godzilla at Tateyama. In a panic she knocks a jeep off the road, and Godzilla crushes it, killing the soldiers inside. Akane is demoted, while scientists including the single father Tokumitsu Yuhara build a cyborg from the original Godzilla's skeleton. The machine, Kiryu, joins the Self-Defense Forces with Akane as its main pilot, although squadron member Susumu Hayama, whose brother died in the jeep, resents her.

At Kiryu's public unveiling Godzilla appears in Yokohama. When Kiryu is sent into battle, Godzilla's roar wakes the memories of its old life and it goes berserk, rampaging until its power runs out. While the machine is repaired, Akane resists Hayama's efforts to drive her out and Yuhara's attempts to befriend her, but she grows close to his young daughter, Sara. Godzilla attacks again in Shinagawa. The rebuilt Kiryu gains the upper hand until Godzilla deflects its Absolute Zero Cannon and the remote control fails. Hayama lands so that Akane can reach Kiryu's backup cockpit, and he wishes her luck, forgiving her. Flying Kiryu herself, Akane carries Godzilla out to sea and fires at point-blank range. The wounded Godzilla retreats and the damaged Kiryu returns for repairs.

Yumiko Shaku stars as Akane and Shin Takuma as Yuhara, with Kana Onodera as Sara, Yūsuke Tomoi as Hayama, and Kou Takasugi, Kumi Mizuno and Akira Nakao in supporting roles. Baseball star Hideki Matsui, nicknamed "Godzilla", makes a cameo as himself. Reviews were positive. DVD Talk's Mike Pinsky found the story more engaging than most monster films and praised the battles, Digitally Obsessed called it one of the better entries in the series, and Digital Monster Island said it should satisfy most kaiju fans.

documents.title: Il Mare
documents.tagline: Love that resides in one place at two different times.
documents.overview: In the year 1999, a young woman leaves her quaint seaside house and returns to the city, leaving in the mailbox a card for the next owner, with instructions to forward any mail of hers to the new address. In the year 1997, a jaded young architect moves into the same house--and finds the letter. His reply, which he slips into the mailbox, finds its way to her, beginning a parallel-time love story separated by a span of two years.
documents.plot:
Il Mare is a poignant and contemplative film that explores the complexities of human connection, longing, and the passage of time. The story revolves around two characters, a young woman named Yoon-jae and an elderly man named Hyun-soo, who form an unlikely bond through letters exchanged across the sea.

At its core, Il Mare is a movie about the power of human relationships to transcend time and space. It delves into the themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for meaning in life. The film's narrative is marked by a sense of melancholy and nostalgia, as both characters grapple with their own personal demons and the weight of their past experiences.

One of the primary concerns of Il Mare is the fragility of human connection and the ease with which it can be disrupted. The film highlights the ways in which our lives are shaped by our relationships with others, and how the absence or loss of these connections can leave us feeling lost and disconnected.

The movie also explores the theme of nostalgia and the bittersweet nature of memories. As Yoon-jae and Hyun-soo reflect on their past experiences, they begin to realize that their lives have been shaped by a series of choices and events that have led them to where they are today. The film's use of letters as a means of communication serves to underscore the idea that our memories and experiences are what make us who we are.

Ultimately, Il Mare is a movie about the human condition, with all its complexities and contradictions. It is a powerful exploration of the ways in which we navigate the challenges of life, and the importance of holding onto hope and connection in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Soul Plane
documents.tagline: Announcing the arrival of the first airline with soul.
documents.overview: Following a ridiculously awful flight that leads to his pet's death, Nashawn Wade files a lawsuit against the airline, and wins a multimillion-dollar settlement. Determined to create a better flying experience, Nashawn starts his own airline, one that caters to an African-American clientele. Going into business with a tricked-out plane piloted by the smooth Capt. Mack, the airline hits a snag when it has to deal with the family of Elvis Hunkee.
documents.plot:
Soul Plane is a 2004 American comedy film directed by Jessy Terrero and written by Terrero and Damien Dante Wayans. The movie follows a group of eccentric passengers on a commercial airliner, which is being chartered for a spiritual journey to the afterlife.

The main themes of Soul Plane include:

1. Social commentary: The film uses satire to poke fun at various aspects of American society, including racism, classism, and cultural differences.
2. Identity: Many characters in the movie struggle with their own identities, whether it's a rapper trying to find his place in the world or a group of wealthy passengers who are more concerned with their material possessions than their spiritual well-being.
3. Redemption: Throughout the film, various characters undergo a journey of self-discovery and redemption, often through humorous and unexpected means.
4. Cultural clashes: The movie explores the tensions between different cultural groups, including African Americans, Caucasians, and Asians, highlighting the absurdities and misunderstandings that can arise from these interactions.

The plot development of Soul Plane is driven by the misadventures of its characters as they navigate their way through the spiritual journey, often with hilarious results. The ending of the film features a heartwarming moment of redemption for many of the characters, as they come to accept themselves and find peace on their journey to the afterlife.

Overall, Soul Plane is a comedy that uses satire and social commentary to explore themes of identity, redemption, and cultural clashes in an entertaining and humorous way.

documents.title: Angus, Thongs and Perfect Snogging
documents.tagline: Georgia Nicholson is not mental, but her life is.
documents.overview: Georgia Nicolson is fourteen, lives with nosey parents who don't understand her, an annoying three year old sister and has to wear a beret to school. She would, however, rather be blonde, have a smaller nose and a boyfriend. Revolving around her hilarious journal entries, prepare to be engulfed in the world of the soaring joys and bottomless angst of being a teenager.
documents.plot:
Angus, Thongs and Perfect Snogging is a 2008 British teen comedy film directed by Dan Curtis-Hall. The movie follows the life of Georgia Nicolson, played by Aaron Johnson, as she navigates high school and adolescence.

The main themes of Angus, Thongs and Perfect Snogging revolve around teenage angst, self-discovery, and the complexities of relationships. The film explores Georgia's struggles with her family dynamics, friendships, and romantic interests, particularly her on-again, off-again relationship with Craig Levine, played by Patricia Hodge.

Throughout the movie, Georgia faces various challenges, including bullying, peer pressure, and her own insecurities. However, she also learns valuable lessons about empathy, loyalty, and the importance of being true to oneself.

The film's tone is lighthearted and humorous, with a touch of satire aimed at the conventions of British high school life. The movie features a talented young cast, including Aaron Johnson, Patricia Hodge, and Emily Watson, who deliver memorable performances that bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Angus, Thongs and Perfect Snogging is a charming and entertaining coming-of-age story that explores the ups and downs of adolescence with humor, wit, and heart.

documents.title: Appaloosa
documents.tagline: Feelings get you killed.
documents.overview: Two friends hired to police a small town that is suffering under the rule of a rancher find their job complicated by the arrival of a young widow.
documents.plot:
Appaloosa is a 2008 American Western film directed by Ed Harris, starring Viggo Mortensen, Ed Harris, and Renée Zellweger.

The movie explores the complex and often brutal world of the Old West through the story of Virgil Earp (Viggo Mortensen), a former Confederate soldier turned lawman. The narrative delves into themes of loyalty, honor, and the moral ambiguity that defines the characters' existence in this unforgiving environment.

At its core, Appaloosa is a tale of two men bound together by their shared experiences as outlaws-turned-lawmen, struggling to maintain their sense of identity and purpose in a world where the lines between right and wrong are constantly blurred. The film's protagonist, Virgil Earp, grapples with his own demons, torn between his duty to uphold justice and his loyalty to those he cares about.

The movie also touches on the theme of power dynamics, as embodied by the enigmatic and ruthless Randall Bragg (Ed Harris), a ruthless outlaw who will stop at nothing to claim control over the territory. The character's presence serves as a catalyst for the conflict that drives the plot forward, highlighting the destructive nature of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences of violence.

Ultimately, Appaloosa is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, set against the backdrop of the American West during its tumultuous late 19th century. The film's nuanced portrayal of complex characters and moral dilemmas invites viewers to reflect on the nature of honor, loyalty, and redemption in a world where these values are constantly tested.

documents.title: Hellraiser: Hellworld
documents.tagline: Evil Goes Online.
documents.overview: Gamers who participate in an online role-playing game called Hellworld are invited to a rave whose host plans to show them all the truth behind the Cenobite mythos.
documents.plot:
Hellraiser: Hellworld is a 2005 supernatural horror film directed by Rick Bota and written by Brad Fiedel. The movie takes place in an alternate universe where the Cenobites, led by Pinhead, have been defeated.

The main themes of Hellraiser: Hellworld include:

1. **Reality TV and the Commodification of Suffering**: The film critiques the voyeuristic nature of reality television, where contestants are forced to endure physical and emotional torture for the sake of entertainment. This theme is reflected in the movie's plot, where a group of contestants on a reality show are lured into a twisted game of survival, only to discover that they are being manipulated by the Cenobites.

2. **The Dangers of Obsession**: The movie explores the dangers of obsession and the blurring of lines between reality and fantasy. The characters' descent into madness is fueled by their own desires and obsessions, which ultimately lead them to confront the horrors of the Cenobites.

3. **The Power of Pain and Pleasure**: Hellraiser: Hellworld delves into the idea that pain and pleasure are intertwined, and that some people are drawn to the darker aspects of human experience. The Cenobites, with their sadomasochistic tendencies, represent a twisted manifestation of this theme.

4. **The Consequences of Playing God**: The movie touches on the idea that playing God can have disastrous consequences. The characters' attempts to control and manipulate the Cenobites ultimately lead to chaos and destruction, highlighting the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human understanding.

5. **The Nature of Reality**: Hellraiser: Hellworld raises questions about the nature of reality and the blurred lines between fantasy and reality. The movie's use of multiple realities and timelines adds complexity to the narrative, leaving the audience to ponder what is real and what is just a product of the characters' imagination.

Overall, Hellraiser: Hellworld is a thought-provoking horror film that explores themes of obsession, pain, pleasure, and the consequences of playing God.

documents.title: Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist
documents.tagline: Go back before the beginning, to the place where evil was born.
documents.overview: Haunted by terrible acts the Nazis forced him to participate in, the disenchanted Father Lankester Merrin focuses his energies on helping with an archaeological dig in the northern part of Kenya. There, the crew uncovers a church that predates Christian missions into the area, but the discovery also causes strange events to start occurring -- including physical changes to a young, disabled boy, whom Merrin grows to suspect has been possessed by a demon.
documents.plot:
Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist is a 2005 supernatural horror film directed by Paul Schrader, not Morgan Creek Productions. However, I can provide information on the movie.

The main themes of Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist revolve around the origins of the demonic entity Pazuzu and its connection to the Catholic Church's rituals and practices. The story explores the dark history of the Church's attempts to harness supernatural power for their own purposes.

The film delves into the theme of corruption and the dangers of unchecked ambition, as embodied by the character of Father Merrin (played by Stellan Skarsgård). As he becomes increasingly consumed by his desire for knowledge and power, he begins to lose sight of his faith and moral principles.

Another significant theme is the exploration of demonic possession and the nature of evil. The film suggests that demonic entities are not just malevolent beings but also complex, multifaceted creatures with their own motivations and desires.

The movie also touches on the idea of the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. As Father Merrin delves deeper into the mysteries of Pazuzu, he becomes increasingly entangled in a web of supernatural events that threaten to destroy him and those around him.

Overall, Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores themes of corruption, ambition, demonic possession, and the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human control.

documents.title: The Brown Bunny
documents.tagline: I'm not going to be okay, Bud.
documents.overview: Bud Clay races motorcycles in the 250cc Formula II class of road racing. After a race in New Hampshire, he has five days to get to his next race in California. During his road trip, he is haunted by memories of the last time he saw Daisy, his true love.
documents.plot:
The Brown Bunny is a 2003 film, not 2004, directed by Vincent Gallo and produced by Wild Bunch.

The Brown Bunny is a surrealist drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, desire, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film follows the story of a struggling actor, played by Vincent Gallo, who embarks on a road trip with his girlfriend, played by Chloë Sevigny. As they journey through the American Southwest, their relationship is put to the test, and the boundaries between intimacy and violence become increasingly ambiguous.

Throughout the film, Gallo's character grapples with feelings of inadequacy, insecurity, and frustration, which are exacerbated by his own ego and sense of entitlement. The Brown Bunny is a deeply personal and introspective work that probes the darker aspects of human nature, revealing a world where desire can be both alluring and destructive.

The film's use of long takes, static shots, and deliberate pacing creates a sense of unease and tension, mirroring the characters' inner turmoil. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the lines between reality and fantasy are constantly shifting.

Ultimately, The Brown Bunny is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges its audience to confront the complexities and nuances of desire, relationships, and the self.

documents.title: Firewalker
documents.tagline: A pair of down-and-out fortune hunters cash in on high adventure!
documents.overview: A pair of adventurers try to track down an ancient Aztec/Mayan/Egyptian/Apache horde of gold.
documents.plot:
Firewalker is an action-adventure film that revolves around the story of Jack Cheyenne, a former Special Forces operative who gets caught up in a complex web of crime and corruption. The movie explores the theme of redemption, as Jack tries to make amends for his past mistakes.

The film also delves into the consequences of playing with fire, both literally and figuratively. Jack's involvement with the Mexican cartel puts him in grave danger, and he must use his skills to survive and protect those around him. This serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of getting entangled with illicit activities and the importance of living a life free from harm.

Furthermore, Firewalker touches on the theme of loyalty and friendship. Jack forms an unlikely alliance with a DEA agent, who helps him navigate the treacherous world he's found himself in. This bond serves as a reminder that even in the darkest of times, human connections can provide solace and support.

The movie also features a strong sense of justice, as Jack seeks to bring down those responsible for the cartel's nefarious activities. His quest for revenge is tempered by a desire to protect innocent lives and restore balance to the community.

Overall, Firewalker is a thrilling ride that explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the dangers of getting caught up in a world of crime and corruption.

documents.title: Suicide Club
documents.tagline: Well then, goodbye everybody.
documents.overview: When 54 high school girls throw themselves in front of a subway train it appears to be only the beginning of a string of suicides around the country. Does the new all-girl group Desert have anything to do with it? Detective Kuroda tries to find the answer, which isn't as simple as he had hoped.
documents.plot:
Suicide Club is a 2001 Japanese independent horror film written and directed by Sion Sono, starring Ryō Ishibashi as Detective Kuroda, with Masatoshi Nagase, Akaji Maro, Saya Hagiwara, Rolly and others. The film follows a wave of apparently unconnected suicides sweeping across Japan and the efforts of the police to understand what lies behind them, combining graphic horror with satire of pop culture and the media.

The film opens with a shocking scene in which 54 teenage girls leap together in front of an oncoming train at a Tokyo station. More suicides follow, including two nurses at a hospital, and at the scenes the police find rolls of human skin stitched together from the bodies of the victims. Detectives Kuroda, Shibusawa and Murata are alerted by a young hacker to a mysterious website that seems to track the deaths before they happen, marking each new victim with a colored circle. As groups of students throw themselves off their school roof and the epidemic spreads throughout the country, the media begins to speak of a "Suicide Club".

A mysterious boy repeatedly calls the police, asking cryptic questions about people's connection to themselves. When the suicides claim Kuroda's own family, the investigation takes a devastating personal turn. A flamboyant gang leader who claims to be behind the Suicide Club turns out to be a false lead, and a young woman, Mitsuko, whose boyfriend was among the victims, discovers coded messages hidden in the hand gestures of Dessert, a popular girl group whose songs seem to be linked to the deaths. Her search leads her to a secret concert and to a group of children who claim that there is no club at all.

Rather than offering a clear explanation, the film leaves its mysteries largely unresolved, inviting interpretation as a commentary on alienation, conformity and the influence of mass media on Japanese youth.

Suicide Club premiered at the Tokyo International Film Festival on October 29, 2001, and was released in Japan in March 2002. Its transgressive subject and gruesome imagery made it notorious at festivals around the world, and it won the Jury Prize for Most Ground-Breaking Film at the 2003 Fantasia Festival. It developed a strong cult following and was followed by the prequel Noriko's Dinner Table (2005).

documents.title: Take the Lead
documents.tagline: Never Follow
documents.overview: A former professional dancer volunteers to teach dance in the New York public school system and, while his background first clashes with his students' tastes, together they create a completely new style of dance. Based on the story of ballroom dancer, Pierre Dulane.
documents.plot:
Take the Lead is a 2006 American romantic drama film directed by Elizabeth Chase and starring Antonio Banderas, Rob Brown, and Yaya DaCosta.

The main themes of Take the Lead revolve around:

1. **Self-discovery**: The movie follows the journey of Pierre Dulaine (Antonio Banderas), a dance instructor who is hired to teach dance at an underprivileged high school in Harlem. As he works with his students, particularly Mauro (Rob Brown), he discovers his own passion for teaching and finds a new sense of purpose.

2. **Empowerment**: The film highlights the transformative power of dance as a means of self-expression and empowerment. Through dance, the characters are able to overcome their personal struggles, build confidence, and find their voice.

3. **Cultural exchange**: Take the Lead celebrates the beauty of different cultures through dance. Pierre Dulaine introduces his students to various styles of dance, including salsa, tango, and contemporary, which helps them appreciate the diversity of music and movement from around the world.

4. **Mentorship**: The movie explores the mentorship between Pierre Dulaine and Mauro, as well as other characters in the school. Their relationships serve as a catalyst for growth, learning, and personal development.

5. **Overcoming adversity**: The film tackles issues such as poverty, racism, and social inequality, highlighting the challenges faced by the students at the high school. Through Pierre's guidance and their collective efforts, they learn to overcome these obstacles and find hope in their lives.

Overall, Take the Lead is a heartwarming story about self-discovery, empowerment, and the transformative power of dance and mentorship.

documents.title: Cold Creek Manor
documents.tagline: The perfect house hides the perfect crime.
documents.overview: A family moves from New York into an old mansion in the countryside, still filled with the previous owner's things. As they begin to make it their own, a series of events begin to occur that makes them believe that the former inhabitants are not yet gone.
documents.plot:
Cold Creek Manor is a psychological thriller film that revolves around the dark secrets and twisted desires of its characters. The story centers around a wealthy couple, who purchase a rural estate with the intention of renovating it, only to discover that the house has a mind of its own and seems to be exerting a malevolent influence over them.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the physical environment, but in the dark pasts and repressed emotions of the characters. The film expertly weaves together themes of obsession, possession, and the blurring of reality, creating a sense of unease and tension that permeates every aspect of the story.

At its core, Cold Creek Manor is a tale of how our deepest fears and desires can consume us, leading us down a path of destruction and chaos. The film's use of atmospheric tension and psychological manipulation creates a sense of claustrophobia, trapping the characters - and the audience - in a world of their own making.

Through its exploration of these themes, Cold Creek Manor raises questions about the nature of reality and the power of the human psyche to create its own horrors. The film's slow-burning tension and eerie atmosphere make it a gripping and unsettling watch, leaving viewers on edge until the very end.

documents.title: Flesh + Blood
documents.tagline: Betrayed by power. Corrupted by love. Bound by honor.
documents.overview: A band of medieval mercenaries take revenge on a noble lord who decides not to pay them by kidnapping the betrothed of the noble's son. As the plague and warfare cut a swathe of destruction throughout the land, the mercenaries hole up in a castle and await their fate.
documents.plot:
Flesh and Blood (stylized Flesh + Blood) is a 1985 historical adventure film directed by Paul Verhoeven, his first in English, from a script he wrote with Gerard Soeteman. It stars Rutger Hauer, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Tom Burlinson, Susan Tyrrell and Jack Thompson. Set in Italy in 1501, it follows mercenaries betrayed by their employer.

When Arnolfini, the rightful ruler of an Italian city, is ousted by a putsch, he promises a company of mercenaries 24 hours of plunder if they retake it. They do so brutally, but Arnolfini then decides he wants them gone. Their commander, Hawkwood, leads Arnolfini's cavalry against his former comrades, betraying his lieutenant Martin, and the mercenaries are expelled without their loot. When Martin's stillborn son is buried, the grave unearths a statue of Saint Martin with a sword, which the band's chaplain takes as a sign that Martin should lead them. Arnolfini's son Steven is betrothed to the young noblewoman Agnes, and the two fall in love after eating a mandrake root, but Martin's band ambushes their caravan, wounding Arnolfini and carrying Agnes off with her dowry. Martin rapes her; she then seeks his protection, and he keeps the others from her.

The mercenaries seize a castle whose inhabitants, unknown to them, are infected with plague. Agnes appears to embrace her new life, winning Martin's love and the band's acceptance, while hinting that she will side with whoever wins. Steven forces Hawkwood to help him by seizing the former nun Hawkwood hopes to marry, and they besiege the castle, but plague spreads among the besiegers and Martin destroys their siege tower with gunpowder. Steven is captured and chained in the courtyard. Hawkwood, cured of the plague by lancing his buboes as Steven had taught, catapults pieces of an infected dog into the castle before leaving for reinforcements, and Steven throws one into the well. As the mercenaries fall sick, they blame Martin and throw him into the well. Steven and Martin cooperate to escape, and when Hawkwood and Arnolfini return with an army, the castle burns. Martin tries to strangle Agnes rather than lose her, but she strikes him down and flees with Steven, then silently watches Martin escape with a sack of loot.

Orion Pictures gave the film a limited US release in August 1985, and it was a box office failure, earning about $100,000 against a $6.5 million budget. It has since become a cult and critical favorite, with 82% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Swept Away
documents.tagline: Paradise makes strange bedfellows
documents.overview: Stranded and alone on a desert island during a cruise, a spoiled rich woman and a deckhand fall in love and make a date to reunite after their rescue.
documents.plot:
Swept Away is a 2002 adventure romantic comedy film written and directed by Guy Ritchie, a remake of Lina Wertmüller's 1974 Italian film of the same name. It stars Ritchie's then-wife Madonna as Amber Leighton and Adriano Giannini as Giuseppe Esposito, the role played in the original by his father, Giancarlo Giannini, with Bruce Greenwood as Amber's husband Tony, Jeanne Tripplehorn as Marina and Elizabeth Banks as Debi. It was produced by Matthew Vaughn and released by Screen Gems.

Amber, the wealthy, spoiled wife of millionaire Tony Leighton, joins two other couples on a private cruise from Greece to Italy. From the start she takes an intense dislike to Giuseppe, a deckhand, and insults him relentlessly. Ignoring his warnings about an approaching storm, she demands to be taken out in a dinghy, and berates him even more when they run out of fuel. After a series of mishaps, in which Amber damages the boat, the two wash up on a deserted island.

There the balance of power is reversed. Giuseppe, who has the skills to survive, takes control and treats Amber with growing dominance, while she becomes increasingly submissive. Over time, their relationship turns into a passionate romance, and Amber discovers that she is truly happy on the island. When she spots a boat anchored in the bay, she hides so that they will not be rescued. Eventually they are found and return to their former lives. Giuseppe tries repeatedly to contact Amber to rekindle their love, but his messages go unanswered, and he concludes, heartbroken, that she has rejected him. In the final scenes it is revealed that Tony has intercepted the letters, making sure that Amber never sees them, or Giuseppe, again.

The film, originally titled Love, Sex, Drugs and Money, was shot in Sardinia and Malta from October to November 2001 under heightened security after the September 11 attacks, shortly after Madonna finished her Drowned World Tour. It was savaged by critics, who faulted Madonna's performance and Ritchie's direction and judged it far inferior to the original, lacking its political context; Rotten Tomatoes reported 6% approval and Metacritic a score of 18. A commercial failure, it grossed about $1 million worldwide against a $10 million budget, and it has since been described as one of the worst films ever made.

documents.title: The Duchess
documents.tagline: Based on the incredible true story.
documents.overview: A chronicle of the life of 18th century aristocrat Georgiana, Duchess of Devonshire, who was reviled for her extravagant political and personal life.
documents.plot:
The Duchess is a 2008 period drama film directed by Saul Dibb, produced by Working Title Films and BIM Distribuzione.

The main themes of The Duchess include:

1. **Marriage and Confinement**: The film explores the theme of marriage as a means of societal expectation rather than love or personal choice. The protagonist, Georgiana Cavendish, is trapped in a loveless marriage with the Duke of Devonshire, who is more interested in his social status and power than in her happiness.

2. **Female Empowerment**: Through Georgiana's journey, the film highlights the struggles faced by women in 18th-century England, particularly those from aristocratic families. The Duchess must navigate a patriarchal society that restricts her freedom and autonomy, yet she finds ways to assert herself and reclaim her identity.

3. **Social Class and Status**: The movie critiques the social hierarchy of the time, exposing the hypocrisy and superficiality of the upper class. Georgiana's experiences illustrate the constraints placed on women by their social position, as well as the limited options available to them.

4. **Love and Identity**: As Georgiana navigates her complicated relationships with her husband, her children, and herself, she must confront the tension between her desire for love and connection and the societal expectations that define her role as a duchess.

5. **Survival and Resilience**: Despite facing numerous challenges, including poverty, illness, and personal tragedy, Georgiana finds ways to survive and even thrive in the face of adversity. Her resilience serves as a testament to the strength and resourcefulness of women in difficult circumstances.

The Duchess features an outstanding performance by Keira Knightley as Georgiana Cavendish, who brings depth and nuance to the complex and multifaceted character.

documents.title: Ghost Town
documents.tagline: He sees dead people... and they annoy him.
documents.overview: Bertram Pincus, a cranky, people-hating Manhattan dentist, develops the unwelcome ability to see dead people. Really annoying dead people. Even worse, they all want something from him, particularly Frank Herlihy, a smooth-talking ghost, who pesters him into a romantic scheme involving his widow Gwen. They are soon entangled in a hilarious predicament between the now and the hereafter!
documents.plot:
Ghost Town is a 2008 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of love, loss, and redemption. The story revolves around Dr. Bertram Pincus, a dentist who has lost his sense of purpose after being unable to save his wife from cancer.

The main theme of Ghost Town is the power of human connection and the importance of living in the present moment. Through Bertram's journey, the film highlights the idea that life is short and fragile, and that we must cherish every moment with loved ones before it's too late. The movie also explores the concept of grief and how it can both consume us and ultimately lead to healing.

The character of Dr. Pincus serves as a catalyst for exploring these themes, as he struggles to come to terms with his own mortality and the impermanence of life. His interactions with a ghost named Gwen, who is stuck between worlds, serve as a metaphor for the human experience and the interconnectedness of all things.

Ultimately, Ghost Town suggests that love and connection can transcend even death itself, and that it's never too late to find meaning and purpose in life. The film's themes are woven throughout its narrative, creating a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be human.

documents.title: Alpha and Omega
documents.tagline: A Pawsome 3D Adventure.
documents.overview: Two young wolves at opposite ends of their pack's social order are thrown together into a foreign land and need each other to return home, but love complicates everything.
documents.plot:
Alpha and Omega is an animated adventure comedy film that revolves around the story of two wolf siblings, Todd and Manny, who are from different packs and must navigate their differences to become friends. The movie explores themes of identity, belonging, and acceptance.

At its core, Alpha and Omega delves into the complexities of sibling relationships and the challenges of growing up. Todd, the protagonist, struggles with his own identity as he tries to find his place within his pack, while Manny, who is from a rival pack, must confront his own prejudices and biases. As they embark on a journey together, they learn valuable lessons about empathy, understanding, and the importance of family.

The film also touches on themes of prejudice and stereotyping, highlighting the dangers of making assumptions based on appearance or background. Through the characters' experiences, Alpha and Omega promotes a message of inclusivity and acceptance, encouraging viewers to look beyond surface-level differences and appreciate the unique qualities that make each individual special.

Overall, Alpha and Omega is a heartwarming story about the power of friendship, family, and self-discovery, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: The Secret Life of Bees
documents.tagline: Bring Your Girlfriends, Sisters, Mothers and Daughters.
documents.overview: Set in South Carolina in 1964, this is the tale of Lily Owens a 14 year-old girl who is haunted by the memory of her late mother. To escape her lonely life and troubled relationship with her father, Lily flees with Rosaleen, her caregiver and only friend, to a South Carolina town that holds the secret to her mother's past.
documents.plot:
The Secret Life of Bees is a 2008 drama film that explores the complex and intertwined lives of three young girls, Lily Owens, Rosaleen, and May Boatwright, set against the backdrop of racial tensions and social change in 1960s South Carolina.

At its core, The Secret Life of Bees delves into themes of female empowerment, friendship, and the unbreakable bonds between women. Through the characters' experiences, the film highlights the struggles faced by African American women during the Civil Rights Movement, particularly those who were marginalized and oppressed.

The movie also explores the theme of trauma, grief, and healing, as Lily grapples with her complicated past and the loss of her mother. Her journey is deeply intertwined with Rosaleen's story, a black woman who faces persecution for voting in a segregated South, serving as a catalyst for Lily's awakening to the injustices faced by African Americans.

Furthermore, The Secret Life of Bees touches on the theme of identity, particularly for women and girls, as they navigate their roles within society. May Boatwright, a young beekeeper, embodies this theme, as she struggles to reconcile her desire for independence with the societal expectations placed upon her.

The film's narrative is also infused with elements of mysticism and spirituality, as embodied by the enigmatic character of August Boatwright, who serves as a symbol of hope and redemption. Through his presence, the movie conveys the importance of community, love, and acceptance in overcoming adversity.

Ultimately, The Secret Life of Bees presents a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that celebrates the resilience and strength of women, particularly those from marginalized communities, as they navigate the complexities of life, love, and social change.

documents.title: Futurama: The Beast with a Billion Backs
documents.original_title: Futurama: The Beast with a Billion Backs
documents.tagline: Puts the "ick" in science ficktion!
documents.overview: Fresh off ripping space-time a new one at the end of "Bender's Big Score," the Planet Express crew is back to mend the tear in reality, or (hopefully) at least not make it worse.  Beyond the tear, though, lurks a being of inconceivable...tentacularity.  What will become of Earth, and indeed, our universe, when faced with the Beast with a Billion Backs?
documents.plot:
Futurama: The Beast with a Billion Backs is an animated science fiction film that explores complex and thought-provoking themes. At its core, the movie delves into the nature of free will versus determinism, as the main character Leela grapples with her own destiny and the consequences of her choices.

The film also examines the concept of identity and what it means to be oneself. Leela's journey is a metaphor for self-discovery, as she navigates the complexities of her own existence and confronts the idea that her path in life may not have been entirely her own choice.

Furthermore, The Beast with a Billion Backs touches on the theme of responsibility and accountability. As Leela faces the consequences of her actions, she must also come to terms with the impact she has had on those around her, including her friends and allies.

The movie's exploration of these themes is often humorous and satirical, but beneath its comedic surface lies a rich and thought-provoking commentary on the human condition. Through Leela's story, the film invites viewers to consider the complexities of existence and the choices that shape our lives.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster
documents.original_title: Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster
documents.overview: While the gang travel to Scotland to visit Daphne's cousin and witness the Highland Games, they find themselves terrorized by the legendary Loch Ness Monster.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster is a 2004 animated mystery comedy film based on the popular Scooby-Doo franchise. The movie follows the Mystery Inc. gang as they travel to Scotland, where they become embroiled in a mystery surrounding the legendary Loch Ness Monster.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Friendship and teamwork: The Mystery Inc. gang works together to solve the mystery, using their unique skills and strengths to overcome obstacles and uncover clues.
2. Skepticism vs. superstition: The film pokes fun at the idea of supernatural creatures like the Loch Ness Monster, while also acknowledging the power of human imagination and the importance of considering alternative explanations for mysterious events.
3. Cultural exchange and appreciation: The movie features a Scottish setting and incorporates elements of Scottish culture, highlighting the gang's curiosity and enthusiasm for learning about new places and traditions.
4. Mystery and suspense: The film's central plot revolves around the mystery of the Loch Ness Monster, keeping viewers engaged and guessing until the very end.

The story begins with the Mystery Inc. gang arriving in Scotland, where they meet a local woman named Morven, who claims to have seen the Loch Ness Monster. As they investigate, they uncover a series of clues that suggest the monster may be real, but also begin to suspect that there may be a more human explanation for the sightings.

Throughout the movie, the gang encounters various obstacles and challenges as they try to solve the mystery, including treacherous terrain, suspicious locals, and even a rival treasure hunter. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and the importance of considering multiple perspectives.

In the end, the Mystery Inc. gang uncovers the truth behind the Loch Ness Monster, revealing a surprising twist that challenges their initial assumptions. The movie concludes with the gang reflecting on what they've learned and how it has brought them closer together as friends.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster is a fun and entertaining mystery comedy that explores themes of friendship, skepticism, and cultural exchange, all set against the iconic backdrop of Scotland's famous loch.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! and the Goblin King
documents.overview: Scooby-Doo and Shaggy must go into the underworld ruled by The Goblin King in order to stop a mortal named The Amazing Krudsky who wants power and is a threat to their pals: Fred, Velma, and Daphne.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo! and the Goblin King is a 2008 animated film that combines the classic Scooby-Doo franchise with elements from the popular children's book series "The Goblin King" by Stephen Lawhead.

The main themes of Scooby-Doo! and the Goblin King revolve around friendship, teamwork, and overcoming fears. The story follows Shaggy and Scooby as they team up with a young boy named Jack to solve a mystery involving the Goblin King, a mythical creature from the book series.

As the plot unfolds, it becomes clear that the Goblin King is not just a simple monster, but rather a symbol of fear and uncertainty for the people in the town. The main characters must work together to uncover the truth behind the Goblin King's existence and put an end to its reign of terror.

Throughout the film, Shaggy and Scooby learn valuable lessons about facing their fears and trusting each other. They also discover that even the most unlikely heroes can make a difference when they work together as a team.

The film's themes are further explored through the character development of Jack, who is initially hesitant to confront his fears but ultimately finds the courage to face them head-on. The movie also touches on the idea of the power of imagination and how it can be both a source of creativity and a tool for escapism.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! and the Goblin King is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the importance of friendship, teamwork, and facing one's fears.

documents.title: Chaos Theory
documents.tagline: This man will bring order to the universe...or not.
documents.overview: Frank Allen, a professional speaker who lectures on time management has a perfectly ordered and scheduled life, down to the minute. When his wife sets his clock forward 10 minutes as a joke, his day is thrown off. Deciding that his strictly ordered life has done him little good, he begins to make multiple choice index cards, choosing one at random and doing what is written on the card.
documents.plot:
Chaos Theory is a 2008 American comedy-drama directed by Marcos Siega from a screenplay by Daniel Taplitz, starring Ryan Reynolds, Emily Mortimer and Stuart Townsend. It was filmed in Coquitlam and Squamish, British Columbia.

On the morning of his wedding to Jesse Allen, Ed gets cold feet after learning she slept with one of his friends while they were on a break. Jesse's father, Frank, corners him and tells the story of his own marriage to Jesse's mother, Susan. Years earlier, Frank and his friend Buddy both loved Susan, who picked Frank on New Year's Eve. Eight years on, Frank is a time-management lecturer who plans every minute of his day, and they have a seven-year-old daughter, Jesse. One morning Susan secretly resets the clocks to buy him ten minutes for an errand but moves them the wrong way, and he misses the ferry and arrives late to an important seminar. At his hotel, Paula, from his lecture, makes a pass at him, and later answers when Susan calls. Driving home, Frank nearly collides with Nancy, a pregnant woman in labor, takes her to hospital and mistakenly fills in his own details on the forms. When Nancy abandons the baby, the hospital calls the Allen home, and Susan, convinced Frank is living a double life, throws him out.

A paternity test to prove the baby is not his reveals that Frank has Klinefelter syndrome and has been sterile since birth, meaning he cannot be Jesse's father either. Nancy returns for her baby and clears things up with Susan, but Frank, devastated, refuses her calls. When he confides in Buddy, Buddy realizes he fathered Jesse during a one-night stand with Susan just before her engagement, tells Susan about Frank's infertility and tries to court her. Frank starts making decisions by drawing index cards at random and invites Paula to his room, but nothing happens because he still loves Susan. On seeing Buddy's roses at home, he grasps the truth and lures Buddy onto a boat with murderous intent, only for both to fall into the lake and Buddy to save him. Learning that Susan loves him, Frank reconciles with her. Back in the present, Ed realizes he loves Jesse, and Frank walks his daughter down the aisle.

Reynolds plays Frank, Mortimer plays Susan, Townsend plays Buddy, Sarah Chalke plays Paula and Elisabeth Harnois plays the adult Jesse. The film did poorly at the box office and received 31% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Stargate: Continuum
documents.tagline: History may never repeat itself again.
documents.overview: Ba'al travels back in time and prevents the Stargate program from being started. SG-1 must somehow restore history.
documents.plot:
Stargate: Continuum is a science fiction film that delves into the complexities of time travel and its consequences on human relationships. The movie explores the theme of sacrifice, as the protagonist, Samantha Carter, must make difficult choices to ensure the survival of humanity.

The film also examines the concept of free will versus determinism, as the characters navigate through different timelines and confront the possibility that their actions may be predetermined. This raises questions about the nature of choice and whether individuals have control over their destinies.

Furthermore, Stargate: Continuum touches on the theme of redemption, particularly in the character of Jack O'Neill, who grapples with his past mistakes and seeks to make amends. The movie also highlights the importance of trust and loyalty among friends and allies, as they work together to overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges.

Ultimately, Stargate: Continuum presents a thought-provoking narrative that delves into the intricacies of time travel, human relationships, and personal growth, leaving audiences with a sense of introspection and contemplation.

documents.title: Stargate: The Ark of Truth
documents.tagline: The lines have been drawn. The battle has been waged. Only one thing can save us...
documents.overview: SG-1 searches for an ancient weapon which could help them defeat the Ori, and discover it may be in the Ori's own home galaxy. As the Ori prepare to send ships through to the Milky Way to attack Earth, SG-1 travels to the Ori galaxy aboard the Odyssey. The International Oversight committee have their own plans and SG-1 finds themselves in a distant galaxy fighting two powerful enemies.
documents.plot:
Stargate: The Ark of Truth is an action-adventure film that delves into complex themes of power, free will, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. At its core, the movie explores the idea of a powerful artifact known as the Ark of Truth, which has the ability to reveal hidden truths and manipulate reality.

The main theme of Stargate: The Ark of Truth revolves around the concept of free will versus determinism. The characters are faced with an existential crisis when they realize that their actions may be predetermined by the Ark's influence, raising questions about the nature of choice and agency in a world where fate seems to be at play.

The film also touches on the theme of power and its corrupting influence. As the characters grapple with the implications of the Ark's power, they must confront the darker aspects of human nature and the dangers of unchecked ambition. The movie suggests that true wisdom lies not in wielding power, but in understanding one's place within a larger cosmic context.

Furthermore, Stargate: The Ark of Truth explores the idea of sacrifice and redemption. The characters are forced to make difficult choices that require them to put the greater good above personal interests, highlighting the importance of selflessness and putting others before oneself.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together with a sense of urgency and tension, creating a narrative that is both thought-provoking and action-packed.

documents.title: Barbie in The 12 Dancing Princesses
documents.tagline: Enchanted dancing in a magical world!
documents.overview: King Randolph sends for his cousin Duchess Rowena to help turn his daughters, Princess Genevieve and her 11 sisters, into better ladies. But the Duchess takes away all the sisters fun, including the sisters favorite pastime: dancing.Thinking all hope is lost they find a secret passageway to a magical land were they can dance the night away.
documents.plot:
Barbie in the 12 Dancing Princesses is a 2006 computer-animated musical fantasy film directed by Greg Richardson and written by Elana Lesser and Cliff Ruby, loosely based on the Brothers Grimm fairy tale "The Twelve Dancing Princesses." The ninth film in the Barbie series, it features Kelly Sheridan as the voice of Princess Genevieve, with Catherine O'Hara as the scheming Duchess Rowena, Christopher Gaze as King Randolph, Nicole Oliver and Lalainia Lindbjerg. Its music was composed by Arnie Roth. It premiered on Nickelodeon on 10 September 2006 and was released on DVD nine days later, the first Barbie film distributed in North America by Universal.

Genevieve is one of twelve princesses who share a passion for dancing and live in a castle with their widowed father, King Randolph. Although the girls are kind, members of the court disapprove of their lively, unconventional pastimes. The king summons his cousin, Duchess Rowena, to turn them into proper ladies, but Rowena drains the palace of color, music and joy, forbidding the sisters to dance and trying to break their spirits.

On the birthday of the youngest princesses, the others give them a copy of their late mother's favorite story, in which a princess discovers a magical land and dances there for three nights before it disappears. Studying the book and the tiles on their bedroom floor, Genevieve discovers how to open a portal to an enchanted world. The sisters enter and dance through the night, discovering that its golden flowers grant wishes, its statues come to life and its water has healing powers. The next morning, the princesses are exhausted and Rowena finds their new dancing shoes worn out, which arouses her suspicion. When King Randolph falls mysteriously ill, Genevieve asks Derek, the royal cobbler, who shares her love of dance, to investigate. Derek discovers that Rowena has been slowly poisoning the king with the help of her lackey in a scheme to seize the throne. Imprisoned and separated from their father, Genevieve and her sisters must use their courage, teamwork and the magic of the hidden land to save the king and the kingdom, while Genevieve and Derek grow closer.

The film proved popular with its young audience and is frequently cited by fans as a favorite among the Barbie films, remembered for its music, its elaborate dance sequences and Catherine O'Hara's villainous performance as Rowena.

documents.title: Barbie and the Diamond Castle
documents.overview: Liana and Alexa (Barbie and Teresa) are best friends who share everything, including their love of singing. One day while walking through the forest home from the village, the girls meet an old beggar who gives them a magical mirror. As they clean the mirror and sing, a musical apprentice muse named Melody appears in the mirror's surface, and tells the girls about the secret of the Diamond Castle.
documents.plot:
Barbie and the Diamond Castle, styled Barbie & the Diamond Castle, is a 2008 direct-to-video computer-animated musical film directed by Gino Nichele and produced by Mattel Entertainment with Rainmaker Entertainment. The thirteenth entry in the Barbie film series, it features Kelly Sheridan as the voice of Barbie, who plays the role of Liana, while her friend Teresa plays Alexa. The film includes a cover of the song "Connected" recorded by Katharine McPhee.

The film is framed as a story told by Barbie and Teresa to Barbie's younger sister Stacie after Stacie has a fight with her best friend. In the tale, Liana and Alexa are two inseparable friends who share a love of music and live in a small cottage, growing and selling flowers to make a modest living. One day they find two heart-shaped stones and turn them into matching necklaces as a symbol of their friendship. After a storm ruins their garden, Liana shares their food with an old woman, who gives them a mirror in return. Inside the mirror lives a girl named Melody, who befriends them and teaches them a song.

Melody reveals that she was once the apprentice of three Muses who lived in the legendary Diamond Castle. One of them, Lydia, turned evil and tried to take the castle for herself, so the others hid it and entrusted Melody with the key before being turned to stone. Fleeing Lydia's dragon Slyder, Melody hid inside the mirror and became trapped. After Slyder attacks and their cottage burns down, Liana and Alexa set out on a perilous journey to find the Diamond Castle and free Melody, adopting two puppies along the way. Lydia pursues them and tries to hypnotize them with her flute, and the friends' bond is tested by hardship and doubt along the way, but Liana's loyalty and the power of their music may be the only way to defeat the evil Muse.

The film emphasizes friendship, generosity and the healing power of music, featuring several original songs performed by the characters.

Barbie and the Diamond Castle premiered on Nickelodeon on September 7, 2008, and was released on DVD on September 9, 2008. It remains popular among fans of the franchise, and Polygon ranked it eighth among the Barbie films.

documents.title: An American Crime
documents.tagline: The true story of a child's punishment that became a woman's crime.
documents.overview: The true story of suburban housewife Gertrude Baniszewski, who kept a teenage girl locked in the basement of her Indiana home during the 1960s.
documents.plot:
An American Crime is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of human nature, exploring the darker aspects of society and the devastating consequences of violence. The film revolves around the true story of Dee Dee Blanchard, a woman who subjected her daughter, Gypsy Rose, to a life of abuse and manipulation.

At its core, An American Crime is a tale of toxic relationships and the destructive power of obsession. Dee Dee's fixation on her own narrative and her desire for attention and sympathy ultimately lead her to create a false persona for herself and her daughter, fabricating a history of illness and disability that has devastating consequences for Gypsy Rose.

The film also explores themes of gaslighting, emotional manipulation, and the blurring of reality. Dee Dee's ability to control and deceive those around her is a masterclass in psychological manipulation, leaving a trail of destruction in its wake.

Furthermore, An American Crime raises questions about the societal pressures that can lead individuals to engage in such behavior. The film suggests that Dee Dee's actions were, in part, driven by a desire for attention and sympathy, as well as a need to feel important and relevant in a world that often overlooks and marginalizes those with disabilities.

Ultimately, An American Crime is a powerful exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, highlighting the devastating consequences of toxic relationships and the importance of empathy, understanding, and support.

documents.title: Felon
documents.tagline: No rule. No hope. No way out.
documents.overview: A family man convicted of killing an intruder must cope with life afterward in the violent penal system.
documents.plot:
Felon is a 2008 American drama film directed by Tiller Russell. The movie revolves around a man who has just been released from prison after serving a 20-year sentence for a crime he committed as a teenager.

The main theme of Felon explores the struggles of reintegration into society, particularly for individuals with felony convictions. The protagonist's journey is marked by his attempts to find employment and rebuild his life, but he faces numerous challenges, including racism, prejudice, and societal stigma.

Throughout the film, Russell sheds light on the harsh realities faced by people with felony records, who often struggle to find stable housing, employment, and access to basic necessities like healthcare. The movie also touches upon the theme of redemption, as the protagonist seeks to make amends for his past mistakes and start anew.

The film's narrative is character-driven, delving into the complexities of human emotions, relationships, and personal growth. It raises questions about the nature of justice, rehabilitation, and the cyclical nature of violence and trauma. Ultimately, Felon presents a poignant portrayal of the struggles faced by individuals with felony convictions, highlighting the need for compassion, understanding, and support in their journey towards redemption.

documents.title: Rogue
documents.tagline: How Fast Can You Swim?
documents.overview: From the director of Wolf Creek comes this terrifying look at nature's perfect killing machine. When a group of tourists stumble into the remote Australian river territory of an enormous crocodile, the deadly creature traps them on a tiny mud island with the tide quickly rising and darkness descending. As the hungry predator closes in, they must fight for survival against all odds.
documents.plot:
Rogue is a 2007 Australian horror film directed by Greg McLean. The movie follows two brothers, Luke (Michael Vartan) and Sam (Radha Mitchell), who are on a fishing trip in the Northern Territory when they encounter a massive saltwater crocodile that has been terrorizing the local community.

The main themes of Rogue include:

1. Survival vs. Humanity: As the brothers try to survive against the deadly predator, they are forced to confront their own humanity and make difficult choices to stay alive.
2. Family Dynamics: The movie explores the complex relationship between Luke and Sam, who have a troubled past. Their bond is tested as they face the life-threatening situation together.
3. Isolation and Survival: The remote location of the Northern Territory adds to the sense of isolation, making it harder for the brothers to escape the crocodile's deadly grasp.
4. Nature vs. Humanity: The film highlights the power and ferocity of nature, particularly the saltwater crocodile, which serves as a symbol of the untamed wilderness.

The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Luke and Sam try to outsmart the crocodile and make it back to civilization. Along the way, they face numerous challenges and setbacks that test their resolve and push them to confront their deepest fears.

Overall, Rogue is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of survival, family dynamics, and the human condition in the face of nature's fury.

documents.title: Eagle Eye
documents.tagline: Don't walk. Run.
documents.overview: Jerry Shaw and Rachel Holloman are two strangers whose lives are suddenly thrown into turmoil by a mysterious woman they have never met. Threatening their lives and family, the unseen caller uses everyday technology to control their actions and push them into increasing danger. As events escalate, Jerry and Rachel become the country's most-wanted fugitives and must figure out what is happening to them.
documents.plot:
Eagle Eye is a 2008 American techno-thriller film directed by D.J. Caruso and written by Scott Frank and Will Beall. The movie stars Shia LaBeouf, Michelle Monaghan, Michael Chiklis, and Billy Burke.

The story begins with Jerry Shaw (Shia LaBeouf), a computer expert who works for the Department of Defense's National Security Agency (NSA). Jerry is a loner who lives in Chicago and spends most of his time working from home. One day, he receives an email that sets off a chain of events that changes his life forever.

The email appears to be from a woman named Rachel Hollis (Michelle Monaghan), who claims to have been kidnapped by a group of terrorists. The email is cryptic, but Jerry becomes convinced that it's real and decides to investigate further. He teams up with Agnes Arlo (Michelle Monaghan), a young woman who was also targeted by the same group.

As they dig deeper, they discover that Rachel has been brainwashed by the terrorists and is now working for them. The group, led by a mysterious figure known as "The Architect" (Billy Burke), plans to carry out a series of attacks across the United States.

Jerry and Agnes must work together to stop the attacks and uncover the truth behind the conspiracy. Along the way, they encounter a range of characters, including Jerry's boss, Colonel Campbell (Michael Chiklis), who is initially skeptical of their claims but eventually becomes an ally.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Architect is a mastermind with a personal vendetta against the government. He has created a complex system of surveillance and control that uses advanced technology to manipulate people's lives.

The plot thickens as Jerry and Agnes get closer to uncovering the truth. They discover that Rachel was not just a victim, but an active participant in the conspiracy. The stakes are raised when they realize that The Architect plans to carry out a massive attack on the United States Capitol building.

In the thrilling climax of the movie, Jerry and Agnes must use all their skills and resources to stop The Architect and his minions. They engage in a cat-and-mouse game with the terrorists, using advanced technology to stay one step ahead.

The ending is intense and suspenseful as Jerry and Agnes finally confront The Architect. In a shocking twist, it's revealed that The Architect was actually a former NSA agent who was driven mad by the government's secrets. He has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, using his knowledge of the system to control people's lives.

In the end, Jerry and Agnes succeed in stopping the attack, but not before The Architect reveals that he has one final trick up his sleeve. As the movie ends, it's left unclear whether Jerry and Agnes have truly stopped the conspiracy or if there are still more threats lurking in the shadows.

Overall, Eagle Eye is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of surveillance, control, and the dangers of playing with fire when it comes to advanced technology. The movie features strong performances from its leads, particularly Shia LaBeouf and Michelle Monaghan, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

documents.title: Max Payne
documents.tagline: When a man has lost everything, he only has revenge.
documents.overview: A DEA agent whose family was slain as part of a conspiracy, and an assassin out to avenge her sister's death, join forces to solve a series of murders in New York City.
documents.plot:
Max Payne is a 2008 neo-noir action film adapted from the video game series developed by Remedy Entertainment and published by Rockstar Games. John Moore directed and co-produced it from a screenplay by Beau Thorne. Mark Wahlberg plays the title character, with Mila Kunis as Mona Sax, Ludacris as Jim Bravura and Beau Bridges as B.B. Hensley; Chris O'Donnell also appears.

A New York detective in the NYPD Cold Case Unit, Max is consumed by the search for whoever killed his wife, Michelle, and their baby daughter, Rose. He falls under suspicion when Natasha, an acquaintance of one of his informants, is murdered and his wallet, which she had stolen, turns up at the scene. His former partner, Alex Balder, is killed after telling Max that Natasha's death may be linked to his family's murder, and Internal Affairs lieutenant Bravura is assigned to bring Max in. With Natasha's sister Mona, a freelance assassin, Max learns that Natasha's tattoo depicts Valkyrie wings. He discovers that papers from Michelle's time at the pharmaceutical firm Aesir are missing and learns from her former supervisor that she helped develop Valkyr, a military super-soldier drug that drove most users to hallucinations and insanity before the project was buried.
