The supervisor agrees to testify but is killed by Aesir contractors disguised as SWAT officers, and Max escapes with a video featuring Jack Lupino, a former Marine who was one of the few successful test subjects.

Max confronts Lupino, now a gangster dealing Valkyr, and is losing their fight when B.B., Aesir's security chief and a father figure to Max, shoots Lupino. B.B. then admits he has been selling Valkyr for profit and killed Michelle when she found evidence against him. He tries to drown Max to stage a suicide, but Max escapes into the icy river and survives by swallowing vials of Valkyr, which bring vivid hallucinations and near invulnerability. Aided by Mona, he storms Aesir's headquarters and kills B.B. on the helipad. A post-credits scene hints at a new pursuit involving Aesir's chief executive, Nicole Horne.

Max Payne was released in Australia on October 16, 2008, a day ahead of its U.S. opening. It debuted at number one in North America with about $17.6 million and grossed roughly $85 million worldwide against a $35 million budget. Reviews were mostly negative: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 15%, its consensus citing stylish action undercut by an illogical plot and overdirection, and it scored 31 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Bolt
documents.tagline: Fully Awesome. Ridonculous. Let It Begin.
documents.overview: Bolt is the star of the biggest show in Hollywood. The only problem is, he thinks it's real. After he's accidentally shipped to New York City and separated from Penny, his beloved co-star and owner, Bolt must harness all his "super powers" to find a way home.
documents.plot:
Bolt is a 2008 American animated comedy-adventure film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Bolt, a white dog who plays a superhero on a popular television show called "It's in Your Paws to Save the World."

The film begins with Bolt (voiced by John Travolta) living a life of luxury and fame as the star of his own TV show. He is convinced that he has superpowers, which allow him to save the world from various threats. However, it is revealed that Bolt's powers are actually just special effects created for the TV show.

One day, Bolt's owner Penny (voiced by Miley Cyrus) leaves him behind in Los Angeles while she travels to New York City. Bolt sets out on a journey to find her, accompanied by his trusty sidekick, Rhino (voiced by Malcolm McDowell). Along the way, they meet Dr. Calico (voiced by Gary Oldman), a sinister villain who is also after Penny.

As Bolt and Rhino navigate through the city, they encounter various obstacles and dangers. They also meet Mittens (voiced by Susie Essman), a stray cat who becomes their ally. Through his adventures, Bolt begins to question his own identity and the nature of his powers.

Meanwhile, Dr. Calico's true intentions are revealed: he plans to use Penny as leverage to get his hands on the secret formula for Bolt's superpowers. As Bolt and Rhino close in on Dr. Calico, they also discover that Penny is not just a damsel in distress but a skilled agent who has been working undercover.

In the climactic final act, Bolt and Rhino face off against Dr. Calico in an epic battle. With the help of Mittens and Penny, Bolt is able to overcome his doubts and harness his true potential. He discovers that his powers are not just special effects but a manifestation of his own heart and spirit.

The movie ends with Bolt returning to New York City, where he is reunited with Penny. However, instead of being hailed as a hero, Bolt realizes that his true purpose is not to save the world but to be loved and accepted for who he is. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, with Bolt finding happiness and fulfillment in his relationship with Penny.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a mix of live-action and CGI elements. The voice cast delivers memorable performances, bringing depth and humor to their characters. Overall, Bolt is a charming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and the power of believing in oneself.

documents.title: Punisher: War Zone
documents.tagline: Vengeance has a name
documents.overview: Waging his one-man war on the world of organized crime, ruthless vigilante-hero Frank Castle sets his sights on overeager mob boss Billy Russoti. After Russoti is left horribly disfigured by Castle, he sets out for vengeance under his new alias: Jigsaw. With the "Punisher Task Force" hot on his trail and the FBI unable to take Jigsaw in, Frank must stand up to the formidable army that Jigsaw has recruited before more of his evil deeds go unpunished.
documents.plot:
Punisher: War Zone is a 2008 action thriller film directed by Lexi Alexander and starring Thomas Jane as Frank Castle, aka The Punisher.

The main themes of Punisher: War Zone include:

1. **Vengeance and Retribution**: The film explores the concept of vengeance and retribution, as Frank Castle seeks to punish those responsible for his family's murder. His quest for justice becomes an all-consuming force that drives him to take extreme measures.
2. **Morality and Gray Areas**: The Punisher operates in a gray area between good and evil, making tough choices and facing moral dilemmas along the way. This theme is reflected in Castle's willingness to kill his enemies, even if it means sacrificing some of his own humanity.
3. **Trauma and PTSD**: Frank Castle's backstory reveals a traumatic event that sets him on his path of vengeance. The film explores the psychological effects of trauma and PTSD on Castle, as well as his struggles to cope with his emotions.
4. **Corruption and Injustice**: The movie highlights the corruption and injustice within the police department and government agencies, which Castle seeks to expose and punish. This theme is reflected in the villainous characters who are willing to do whatever it takes to maintain their power and influence.

Overall, Punisher: War Zone presents a gritty and intense portrayal of a complex character driven by his desire for vengeance and justice. The film's themes explore the gray areas between right and wrong, highlighting the moral complexities of Castle's actions and the consequences that follow.

documents.title: Lifted
documents.tagline: Failure is an option.
documents.overview: When an overconfident teen alien gets behind the controls of a spaceship, he must attempt to abduct a slumbering farmer under the watchful eye of a critical instructor. But abducting humans requires precision and a gentle touch, and within a few missteps it's painfully clear why more humans don't go missing every year.
documents.plot:
Lifted is a 2006 American computer-animated science fiction short written and directed by Gary Rydstrom for Pixar Animation Studios. It was the directing debut of Rydstrom, an Academy Award-winning sound designer, editor and mixer. It was also the first Pixar film produced by Katherine Sarafian, who later produced Brave in 2012. The short was inspired by the 1927 film Metropolis.

The story takes place aboard a spacecraft hovering over a farmhouse at night. Stu, a young green alien, is sitting a test in alien abduction while his examiner, Mr. B, watches silently and takes notes. Stu's task is to beam up Ernie, a farmer sound asleep in bed. The ship's controls are a huge board of thousands of identical, unlabeled toggle switches, and Mr. B's blank expression gives no hint which ones to use. Stu's nervous first tries send the sleeping Ernie into the walls. Growing frustrated, he starts flipping whole rows of switches, and Ernie bounces around the bedroom like a pinball, knocking things over without ever waking up.

Stu finally finds the right switch and guides Ernie towards a half-open window, where he briefly gets stuck, along with a nearby tree. As Ernie floats up towards the ship, Stu switches off the tractor beam too early, and the farmer drops to the ground until Mr. B turns it back on. Mr. B then pushes the trainee aside, takes over, puts Ernie back in bed and cleans up the damage. Stu begins to cry. With a sigh, Mr. B lets him fly the ship home, but Stu's joyful steering lands the ship on the farmhouse and crushes it. The ship leaves a vast crater, with Ernie still asleep on top of a single column of earth. During the credits he wakes up and is heard screaming as he falls.

Production ran from mid-2005 to summer 2006. Rydstrom based the story on his own work as a sound mixer: running a huge, complex console with many people watching and taking notes. The film used no major new technology, apart from a new program called Jiggle that let animators control the secondary jiggle of chosen body parts. The short premiered on October 12, 2006, at the 42nd Chicago International Film Festival. It was shown in the 2006 Animation Show of Shows and released in theaters with Ratatouille on June 29, 2007. It was nominated for Best Animated Short Film at the 79th Academy Awards and later appeared on the Ratatouille home release and in Pixar Short Films Collection, Volume 1.

documents.title: Your Friend the Rat
documents.overview: Let's face it, rats are not the most beloved creatures on earth. However, maybe this little tale about the history of human and rat interaction will change the world's tune. At least that is the hope of Remy, the star of Ratatouille, and his reluctant brother Emile as they guide us through world history from a rat's perspective. Why can't we all just get along?
documents.plot:
Your Friend the Rat is an American animated short film of 2007 produced by Pixar and written and directed by Jim Capobianco as an extra for the home release of Ratatouille. Running about eleven minutes, it is framed as a mock educational film in which the rat brothers Remy, voiced by Patton Oswalt, and Emile, voiced by Peter Sohn, plead for peace between rats and humans. Lou Romano voices Linguini, who stands in for most of the humans, and Capobianco himself plays an off-screen director.

Remy introduces himself and Emile and announces that he speaks for oppressed rats everywhere, while his brother grumbles at being made to take part. Unrolling a scroll, he launches into a hand-drawn history comparing the human bond with rats to the warmer treatment of dogs and cats. He recalls that rats were once considered sacred and lucky, serving in India as the mount of the god Ganesh, and that ancient Romans thought a white rat crossing one's path brought good fortune and a black one bad. He turns to the black rat and its link to the Black Death, insisting that fleas were the true culprits of a plague that killed a third of Europe's people and just as many rats, and then celebrates the brown rat, credited with helping to end the plague and honoured in the Chinese zodiac. Emile takes over to list the clever things rats can do and the ways they benefit people, from laboratory research to life as pets, noting that Queen Victoria's rat-catcher, Jack Black, kept some of his captives as pets. The brothers close with a song, "Plan B", about the relationship between the two species. As Remy asks viewers whether rats and humans can live in peace, a long, satirical disclaimer warning children to keep away from rats fills the screen, and the brothers try to push it aside, complaining about free speech and their empty stomachs.

The idea grew out of a request for DVD extras, and Capobianco conceived it as a funny way to present the research the crew had gathered on rats. Produced in under a year during the final stretch of work on Ratatouille, it is Pixar's only short to use traditional hand-drawn animation, combined here with computer animation, stop-motion and live action. It includes a cameo by P.T. Flea from A Bug's Life and was released with Ratatouille on home video in November 2007.

documents.title: Boundin'
documents.overview: On a high mountain plain lives a lamb with wool of such remarkable sheen that he breaks into high-steppin' dance. But there comes a day when he loses his lustrous coat and, along with it, his pride. It takes a wise jackalope - a horn-adorned rabbit - to teach the moping lamb that wooly or not, it's what's inside that'll help him rebound from life's troubles.
documents.plot:
Boundin', a short film by Pixar Animation Studios, revolves around a young calf named Otis who is struggling to find his place on a farm. The story explores themes of perseverance, self-discovery, and the importance of embracing one's uniqueness.

At its core, Boundin' is a heartwarming tale about a calf who refuses to be defined by others' expectations. Otis's journey is marked by his determination to prove himself and find his own path, even when faced with skepticism and doubt from those around him. Through his experiences, the film highlights the value of staying true to oneself and celebrating individuality.

The movie also touches on the theme of acceptance and understanding. As Otis navigates the complexities of farm life, he learns to appreciate the unique qualities that make each animal special. This message is conveyed through Otis's interactions with other farm animals, who come to accept and celebrate his differences.

Furthermore, Boundin' explores the idea of finding one's purpose and passion in life. Otis's journey is not just about proving himself but also about discovering what makes him happy and fulfilled. The film suggests that when we focus on our passions and interests, we are more likely to find success and happiness.

Overall, Boundin' is a poignant and uplifting tale that encourages viewers to embrace their individuality and pursue their dreams with determination and perseverance.

documents.title: The Babysitters
documents.tagline: These girls mean business.
documents.overview: Seventeen-year-old Shirley is a good student who works as a babysitter in order to make money for college. One night Michael, a father Shirley works for, confesses he's unhappy with married life. Shirley has a crush on Michael, and seizes this moment to kiss him. Michael is so happy he presents Shirley with a big tip, which gives her an idea. Shirley plans to make extra money by setting up her teenage friends with other unhappy fathers.
documents.plot:
The Babysitters is a 2007 American drama written and directed by David Ross. Katherine Waterston, in one of her first leading roles, stars as Shirley Lyner, a teenager who turns her babysitting service into a prostitution ring for married men, with John Leguizamo as Michael Beltran, Cynthia Nixon as his wife Gail, Andy Comeau and Denis O'Hare. The independent film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2007 and was released in the United States on 9 May 2008 by Peace Arch Releasing.

Narrating in voice-over, Shirley introduces her unusual "babysitting service" before a flashback shows how it began. Michael, a frustrated husband and father, picks Shirley up for an ordinary babysitting job and afterwards they share a meal and flirt; he is unhappy in his marriage, and she finds boys her own age immature. Michael and Gail meet his friend Jerry, who offers Michael a business opportunity that Gail does not want him to accept. Driving Shirley home one night, Michael stops at an abandoned train yard and the two share a kiss. Although they agree it cannot happen again, Michael pays her extra.

When Shirley's friend Melissa learns the truth about these outings and Michael tells Jerry, Michael asks whether any of Shirley's friends might also "babysit." Melissa volunteers, agreeing to give Shirley a twenty percent cut, and the girls recruit their friend Brenda, eventually running an organized business complete with printed cards and a growing clientele of suburban fathers. Michael becomes jealous when he learns that Shirley is seeing other men. Trouble begins when Brenda brings in her rough, aggressive stepsister Nadine without consulting Shirley, sparking a rivalry that threatens the enterprise, and as Shirley's control over the business grows, so do the risks to the girls and the men involved, along with the lies that keep their double lives hidden.

The Babysitters received negative reviews from critics, many of whom found its treatment of its provocative subject matter uneven and its tone confused. Some reviewers nonetheless singled out Waterston's poised performance, and she went on to more prominent roles in the following decade.

documents.title: How to Lose Friends & Alienate People
documents.original_title: How to Lose Friends & Alienate People
documents.tagline: He's across the pond, and out of his depth.
documents.overview: Sidney Young is a down-on-his-luck journalist. Thanks to a stint involving a pig and a glitzy awards ceremony, Sidney turns his fortunes around, attracting the attention of Clayton Harding, editor of New York-based glossy magazine 'Sharps', and landing the holy grail of journalism jobs. The Brit jets off to the Big Apple and moves from one blunder to the next.
documents.plot:
How to Lose Friends & Alienate People is a 2008 comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of one's actions. The movie delves into the theme of social hierarchy and how individuals navigate their way through various social circles.

The protagonist, Ron Livingston's character, is an American writer who moves to London to work on his novel. He quickly finds himself entangled in a web of complex relationships with his British colleagues, particularly the charismatic but manipulative Simon Rich (played by Gordon Pinsent). As Ron becomes more and more entrenched in this social circle, he begins to lose touch with his own identity and values.

The film also touches on the theme of superficiality and the dangers of pretending to be someone you're not. Ron's character is initially drawn to the group because of their perceived sophistication and exclusivity, but as he becomes more deeply embroiled in their lives, he realizes that beneath the surface lies a complex web of insecurities and vulnerabilities.

Throughout the film, the director, Robert Bendetich, uses humor and satire to explore these themes, often poking fun at the pretensions and absurdities of social cliques. However, beneath the comedic surface, the movie reveals a nuanced commentary on the human condition, highlighting the difficulties of forming genuine connections in a world where appearances can be deceiving.

Ultimately, How to Lose Friends & Alienate People is a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of our actions. It invites viewers to reflect on their own social behaviors and consider the importance of authenticity and vulnerability in building meaningful connections with others.

documents.title: Paid in Full
documents.tagline: The American Dream... Their way.
documents.overview: Ace is an impressionable young man working for a dry cleaning business. His friend, drug dealer Mitch goes to prison. In an unrelated incident, he finds some cocaine in a pants pocket. Soon, Ace finds himself dealing cocaine for Lulu. Via lucky breaks and solid interpersonal skills, Ace moves to the top of the Harlem drug world. Of course, unfaithful employees and/or rivals conspire to bring about Ace's fall.
documents.plot:
Paid in Full is a 2002 American crime drama film directed by Charles Stone III. The movie explores the consequences of growing up in poverty and the cyclical nature of violence, as embodied by the character of Marcus, who returns to his Brooklyn neighborhood after serving time in prison.

The main theme of Paid in Full revolves around the struggle for survival and redemption in a harsh environment where opportunities are scarce and hope is often extinguished. The film delves into the world of street hustling, gang violence, and the corrupting influence of power, highlighting the devastating effects on individuals and communities.

Through Marcus's character, the movie sheds light on the psychological toll of poverty, trauma, and the loss of innocence. As he navigates his way back to Brooklyn, he must confront the harsh realities of his past and the expectations placed upon him by those around him. The film raises questions about the nature of redemption, forgiveness, and personal growth in the face of adversity.

The movie also touches on the theme of intergenerational trauma, where the experiences of one generation are passed down to the next, perpetuating a cycle of violence and despair. Paid in Full is a powerful exploration of the human condition, offering a nuanced portrayal of life in the inner city and the struggles faced by those living in poverty.

Overall, Paid in Full is a gripping drama that tackles tough subjects with sensitivity and authenticity, providing a thought-provoking commentary on the complexities of urban life and the resilience of the human spirit.

documents.title: SPL: Kill Zone
documents.overview: Chan, an articulate senior detective nearing the end of his career, is taking care of the daughter of a witness killed by ruthless crime lord Po. Martial arts expert Ma is set to take over as head of the crime unit, replacing Chan who wants an early retirement.
documents.plot:
SPL: Sha Po Lang is a 2005 Hong Kong action thriller film directed by Wilson Yip and starring Donnie Yen, Sammo Hung, and Takeshi Kaneshiro.

The main themes of SPL: Sha Po Lang revolve around the complexities of human relationships, loyalty, and redemption. The story revolves around Inspector Lee (played by Donnie Yen), a tough and skilled cop who is tasked with protecting a young girl named Yu (played by Charlie Yeung) from a group of Triad members.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Inspector Lee's past is marked by tragedy and loss, which has driven him to become a loner. However, when he meets Yu, he begins to confront his emotional scars and re-examine his sense of purpose.

Throughout the film, the theme of loyalty is also explored, particularly in the context of Inspector Lee's relationships with his colleagues and superiors. The character of Captain Tang (played by Sammo Hung) serves as a foil to Inspector Lee, representing a more traditional and by-the-book approach to law enforcement.

The film also touches on the theme of redemption, as Inspector Lee grapples with his past mistakes and seeks to make amends. Ultimately, the story builds towards a tragic confrontation that forces Inspector Lee to confront the consequences of his actions and find a way to redeem himself.

Overall, SPL: Sha Po Lang is a gripping and intense action thriller that explores complex themes of human relationships, loyalty, and redemption in the context of a gritty and realistic portrayal of life as a Hong Kong cop.

documents.title: Pride and Glory
documents.tagline: Truth. Honor. Loyalty. Family. What are you willing to sacrifice?
documents.overview: A saga centered on a multi-generational family of New York City Police officers. The family's moral codes are tested when Ray Tierney, investigates a case that reveals an incendiary police corruption scandal involving his own brother-in-law. For Ray, the truth is revelatory, a Pandora's Box that threatens to upend not only the Tierney legacy but the entire NYPD.
documents.plot:
Pride and Glory is a 2008 American crime drama film directed by Gavin O'Connor. The movie revolves around the McNulty family, who are Irish-American police officers in New York City.

At its core, Pride and Glory explores the complexities of family dynamics, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong. The story delves into the personal struggles of each character as they navigate their relationships with one another, all while dealing with the pressures of their high-stakes jobs.

The film also examines the theme of identity, particularly in the context of masculinity and the expectations placed upon men within a traditional Irish-American family structure. As the characters grapple with their own sense of self-worth and purpose, they must confront the consequences of their choices and the true meaning of honor.

Furthermore, Pride and Glory touches on the idea of redemption and forgiveness, as each character seeks to make amends for past mistakes and find a way to move forward. The movie's portrayal of the intricate web of relationships within the McNulty family serves as a powerful commentary on the human condition, highlighting both the beauty and the darkness that can exist within even the most loving of families.

Overall, Pride and Glory is a gripping drama that masterfully weaves together themes of family, loyalty, identity, and redemption to create a rich and thought-provoking cinematic experience.
production_companies: Kumar Mobiliengesellschaft mbH & Co. Projekt Nr. 1 KG

documents.title: Secondhand Lions
documents.overview: The comedic adventures of an introverted boy left on the doorstep of a pair of reluctant, eccentric great-uncles, whose exotic remembrances stir the boy's spirit and re-ignite the men's lives.
documents.plot:
"Secondhand Lions" is a 2003 American comedy-drama film directed by Tim McCanlies. The movie stars Robert Duvall, Michael Caine, and Peter Dinklage.

The main theme of "Secondhand Lions" revolves around the complexities of family relationships, identity, and the power of storytelling. The story follows Walter Cunningham (Peter Dinklage), a young boy who moves in with his eccentric uncles, Hub (Robert Duvall) and Garth (Michael Caine), after his mother's death.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the uncles' seemingly outlandish tales are actually rooted in their own experiences during World War II. Through these stories, Walter learns about his family's past, including the uncles' involvement with a group of Jewish refugees and their struggles to survive during the war.

The film explores themes of:

1. Identity: The movie delves into the complexities of identity, particularly for Walter, who is trying to find his place in the world after his mother's death.
2. Family dynamics: The relationships between Walter, Hub, and Garth are central to the story, highlighting the tensions and love that exist within a family.
3. Storytelling: The film showcases the power of storytelling as a means of preserving memories, passing down history, and connecting with others.
4. War and its impact: The movie touches on the experiences of those who lived through World War II, shedding light on the struggles and sacrifices made by individuals during this tumultuous period.

Through its engaging narrative and memorable performances, "Secondhand Lions" explores these themes in a way that is both entertaining and thought-provoking.

documents.title: The Ex
documents.tagline: Credit-grabbing, back-stabbing, wife-nabbing. Just another day at the office.
documents.overview: When his lawyer wife, Sofia, becomes pregnant, chronic underachiever Tom Reilly must take a job at his father-in-law's advertising firm. Tom has to adjust to the demands of a very high-powered job, and he finds himself in an increasingly hostile office rivalry with Chip, Sofia's paraplegic former lover.
documents.plot:
The Ex is a 2006 American comedy film directed by Jesse Peretz, starring Zach Braff, Amanda Peet and Jason Bateman, with Charles Grodin, in his first film role since 1994, Mia Farrow and Amy Adams. Originally developed under the working title Fast Track, it was screened in late 2006, and after several postponements was released theatrically in the United States on May 11, 2007.

Tom Reilly, a talented but unreliable chef in Manhattan, struggles to hold a job, while his wife, Sofia, is a successful lawyer. When their first child is born, they agree that Sofia will stay home with the baby and Tom will build a steady career. Soon afterward Tom is fired from his restaurant job after standing up for his friend Paco, a fellow cook. To support the family, he accepts a job at an advertising agency in Ohio, Sofia's hometown, where her father, Bob, works, and the young family moves in with her parents.

Tom's new supervisor is Chip Sanders, a relentlessly upbeat, inspirational paraplegic who is admired by everyone at the agency and who turns out to be Sofia's high school boyfriend. Chip still harbors feelings for Sofia and sets out to make Tom's life miserable, undermining him at work while charming the family and spending time with Sofia and the baby. Every attempt Tom makes to expose Chip makes him look petty and jealous. Convinced that Chip is not really paralyzed, Tom finds a photograph of him playing tennis, and in a confrontation at his in-laws' home drags Chip up a staircase and throws him, expecting him to catch himself. Chip does not, the photo turns out to show his late twin brother, and Tom is humiliated.

Later, Chip reveals to Tom in private that he can in fact walk, though he cannot fight outside his wheelchair, and then beats Tom from his chair, boasting that he will win Sofia back. When Chip receives an offer to become creative director at an agency in Barcelona, he invites Sofia to go with him. She refuses, and the phone call proves to have been a trick arranged by Paco. Furious, Chip rises from his chair, exposing his deception, before storming outside and being hit by a bus. Tom and Sofia leave Ohio and swap roles, with Sofia returning to law and Tom staying home with their child while her father helps him launch his own business.

The Ex received largely negative reviews, with critics faulting its direction and its unsympathetic characters; Rotten Tomatoes reported 18% approval. It was a commercial failure, grossing about $5 million.

documents.title: Battle in Seattle
documents.tagline: Six lives, six battles, one city.
documents.overview: Thousands of activists arrive in Seattle, Washington in masses to protest the WTO Ministerial Conference of 1999 (World Trade Organization). Although it began as a peaceful protest with a goal of stopping the WTO talks, it escalated into a full-scale riot and eventually, a State of Emergency that pitted protesters against the Seattle Police Department and the National Guard.
documents.plot:
Battle in Seattle is a political drama written and directed by the actor Stuart Townsend in his feature debut, a fictional ensemble story set against the real protests at the 1999 World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference. The cast includes Martin Henderson as the activist leader Jay, Michelle Rodriguez as Lou, André Benjamin as Django, Jennifer Carpenter as Sam, Woody Harrelson as the police officer Dale, Charlize Theron as his pregnant wife Ella, Connie Nielsen as the TV reporter Jean, Ray Liotta as Mayor Jim Tobin, Channing Tatum as a hard-line officer and Rade Šerbedžija as a delegate. Townsend drew on documentaries and films such as Medium Cool and mixed staged scenes with archival footage.

A prologue explains the WTO and why its critics accuse it of widening the gap between rich and poor nations. The activists are introduced dangling from a construction crane as they hang an anti-WTO banner. Jay, who has an extensive arrest record and a brother who died in an earlier protest, has spent months with Django planning a disruptive but strictly nonviolent action to shut the conference down. Lou is a guarded animal-rights activist drawn to Jay, Sam a law student wary of arrest, and Django a cheerful pacifist. Mayor Tobin, a former antiwar protester himself, wants to allow free speech while keeping anyone from getting hurt, but his police chief is skeptical. Inside the talks, a delegate campaigns for cheaper medicines for poor countries.

When the protesters refuse to clear the streets, police respond with tear gas and pepper spray, window-smashing anarchists seize the headlines, and pressure from the governor and the White House overrides the mayor, leading to curfews, a state of emergency and the National Guard. Jean, sent to cover the riot, becomes sympathetic to the demonstrators. Ella, a department-store clerk, is caught in the crowd and struck by a police baton, losing her baby. Denied leave, Dale turns his grief into rage and beats Jay in a church, later seeking him out to apologize. Hundreds are jailed, Sam works to free her friends, and the mayor is left with no way to save face.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2007 and opened in limited release a year later, earning less than $1 million. Reviews were mixed, with a 57% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 54; critics praised its passion but found the characters thinly drawn.

documents.title: Tinker Bell
documents.tagline: Enter the world of fairies
documents.overview: Journey into the secret world of Pixie Hollow and hear Tinker Bell speak for the very first time as the astonishing story of Disney's most famous fairy is finally revealed in the all-new motion picture "Tinker Bell."
documents.plot:
Tinker Bell is a 2008 animated fantasy film produced by DisneyToon Studios. The movie follows the adventures of Tinker Bell, a mischievous and magical fairy who lives in Pixie Hollow.

The story begins with Tinker Bell (voiced by Mae Whitman) being introduced as a young fairy-in-training at Pixie Hollow. She is eager to prove herself and become a "real" fairy, but her clumsiness and tendency to get into trouble often hinder her progress. Tinker Bell's best friend, Iridessa (voiced by Lucy Hale), tries to help her overcome her challenges.

Meanwhile, the evil fairy, Zarina (voiced by Lucy Liu), is introduced as a former resident of Pixie Hollow who was banished for being too reckless and destructive. Zarina seeks revenge against the fairies who she believes wronged her and sets out to steal the magical dust that gives the fairies their powers.

As Tinker Bell navigates her way through fairy school, she becomes increasingly frustrated with her lack of progress and feels like an outcast among her peers. However, when Zarina's plan is revealed, Tinker Bell sees an opportunity to prove herself and joins forces with Iridessa and the other fairies to stop Zarina.

The movie follows Tinker Bell's journey as she learns valuable lessons about friendship, teamwork, and believing in oneself. Along the way, she also discovers her own unique talents and abilities, which ultimately help the fairies defeat Zarina and save Pixie Hollow.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the magical world of Pixie Hollow to life. The characters are well-developed and relatable, with Tinker Bell being a particularly endearing protagonist. The movie's themes of perseverance and self-acceptance make it an enjoyable and inspiring watch for both children and adults.

Overall, Tinker Bell is a delightful and entertaining film that showcases the magic and wonder of DisneyToon Studios' animation. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and valuable lessons, this movie is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Watchmen
documents.tagline: Justice is coming to all of us.  No matter what we do.
documents.overview: In a gritty and alternate 1985 the glory days of costumed vigilantes have been brought to a close by a government crackdown, but after one of the masked veterans is brutally murdered, an investigation into the killer is initiated. The reunited heroes set out to prevent their own destruction, but in doing so uncover a sinister plot that puts all of humanity in grave danger.
documents.plot:
Watchmen is a 2009 American superhero film directed by Zack Snyder and written by David Hayter and Alex Tse, based on the DC Comics series by Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons. Malin Åkerman, Billy Crudup, Matthew Goode, Carla Gugino, Jackie Earle Haley, Jeffrey Dean Morgan and Patrick Wilson star in a dark, dystopian deconstruction of the superhero genre set in an alternate 1985 at the height of the Cold War.

In this version of history, costumed vigilantes helped the United States win the Vietnam War, Richard Nixon is serving a fifth term as president, and masked heroes have been outlawed. The world edges toward nuclear war with the Soviet Union, held in check only by the existence of Doctor Manhattan, a godlike being created in a laboratory accident. When the government-sanctioned hero known as the Comedian is thrown to his death from his New York apartment, the masked vigilante Rorschach, who still operates in defiance of the law, begins to investigate and comes to believe that someone is targeting former heroes.

Rorschach warns his old colleagues: the retired, insecure Nite Owl; the increasingly detached Doctor Manhattan and his partner Silk Spectre; and Ozymandias, now one of the richest men in the world. As Doctor Manhattan is driven into exile on Mars by accusations that he caused cancer in former associates, and Rorschach is framed for murder, Nite Owl and Silk Spectre are drawn back into crime-fighting. The trail finally leads to Ozymandias's Antarctic retreat, where the heroes discover that he has orchestrated an elaborate conspiracy to avert nuclear war by staging a devastating attack on the world's cities and pinning it on Doctor Manhattan, forcing the superpowers to unite. Faced with peace bought at such a terrible price, the heroes must decide whether to expose the truth, while Rorschach refuses to compromise.

The adaptation spent nearly two decades in development hell, passing through several studios and directors, including Terry Gilliam, who called the comic unfilmable, before Warner Bros. hired Snyder in 2005. A legal dispute with 20th Century Fox over the rights was settled before release. Filming began in Vancouver in September 2007, with Snyder closely following the comic's panels. The film received polarized reviews, with praise for its visuals, faithfulness and performances, especially Haley's, and criticism of its length and violence. It later gained a reappraisal.

documents.title: Bangkok Dangerous
documents.tagline: There's only one way out.
documents.overview: When carrying out a hit, assassin Joe always makes use of the knowledge of the local population. On arriving in Bangkok, Joe meets street kid Kong and he becomes his primary aide. But when Kong is nearly killed, he asks Joe to train him up in the deadly arts and unwittingly becomes a target of a band of killers.
documents.plot:
Bangkok Dangerous is a 2008 American action thriller written and directed by the Pang Brothers, a remake of their own 1999 Thai debut film of the same name. It stars Nicolas Cage as Joe, a professional hitman, with Shahkrit Yamnarm as Kong, Charlie Yeung as Fon and Panward Hemmanee as Aom. Cage's production company, Saturn Films, bought the remake rights, and the film was shot on location in Bangkok beginning in August 2006.

Joe is a solitary contract killer who lives by strict rules: never socialize, never meet his employers, leave no trace and kill the local helpers he hires as go-betweens once each job is done. After completing a job in Prague, he travels to Bangkok to carry out four assassinations for a crime boss named Surat, whom he never meets. He hires Kong, a young Thai pickpocket, as his intermediary, with contracts delivered through a nightclub dancer, Aom.

As Joe carries out the killings, including a motorcycle ambush and a chase through the Damnoen Saduak floating market, he breaks his own rules. Instead of eliminating Kong, he takes the young man under his wing and trains him in self-defense. He also falls for Fon, a deaf-mute pharmacist, but their romance is shattered when she witnesses him kill two muggers. His final target turns out to be the Prime Minister of Thailand, a revered leader whose crackdown on organized crime threatens Surat, forcing Joe to confront what he has become. When Surat's men turn on him and abduct Kong and Aom, Joe must choose between his code and the people he has come to care about.

The film reworks the original's story of a deaf-mute assassin by making its hitman American and shifting the character's disability to his love interest and the original's Thai setting is retained, with Bangkok's streets, markets and nightclubs as the backdrop.

Bangkok Dangerous was released by Lionsgate on September 5, 2008, It grossed 42.5 million dollars worldwide against a 45 million dollar budget and received negative reviews from critics.

documents.title: Highlander: The Search for Vengeance
documents.tagline: In revenge, patience is a virtue. And after a thousand years, Colin MacLeod doesn't give a damn about virtue ...
documents.overview: Colin MacLeod hunts for the man responsible for the death of his love. He chases the immortal Marcus Octavius across centuries as his quest threatens to take over his life and heart. In his quest, he meets a woman who reminds him of his slain beauty. But it's his final battle with Marcus that will decide not only his fate, but also the fate of everyone in the world.
documents.plot:
Highlander: The Search for Vengeance (Japanese: ハイランダー：復讐の探索) is a 2007 adult animated dystopian fantasy action film and an anime installment of the Highlander franchise. It was directed by Yoshiaki Kawajiri, known for Ninja Scroll and Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust, and written by David Abramowitz, a writer on Highlander: The Series. The film was a joint venture between Imagi Animation Studios, which provided the script and music, and Madhouse, which produced the animation, in association with Davis-Panzer Productions, and it was distributed by Manga Entertainment. The English voice cast includes Alistair Abell, Debi Mae West, Nolan North, Scott McNeil and Ogie Banks.

The story follows Colin MacLeod, a Celtic warrior who first dies in 125 AD in Roman Britain when his village is destroyed by the invading Romans. The Roman commander, Marcus Octavius, is himself an Immortal who dreams of building a perfect society through conquest. Octavius kills Colin's wife Moya, but Colin, mortally wounded, is dragged by his horse to Stonehenge, which, as holy ground, is a place where Immortals may not fight. There he revives and learns from the spirit of Amergan, a druid bound to the site, that he is an Immortal and part of an ancient contest known as the Game. Amergan becomes his lifelong companion and conscience, often to Colin's irritation.

Driven by grief and rage, Colin spends the following centuries pursuing Octavius through history, as the villain reappears in different eras attempting to impose his vision of order through fear and force. The film interweaves flashbacks of their encounters with a story set in a ruined, plague-ridden New York of the future, where Octavius rules as a dictator and Colin, now weary and consumed by vengeance, arrives for a final reckoning. Along the way he meets Dahlia, a woman who resembles Moya, and must decide whether revenge is all that remains of his life.

Critical reaction was generally favorable and more positive than for the later live-action Highlander sequels. Chris Wyatt of IGN gave it 8 out of 10, calling it the best thing to happen to Highlander fans since the original film and describing it as violent, dramatic, sexy and smart. Reviewers also praised Kawajiri's direction and its stylized combat sequences.

documents.title: Flawless
documents.overview: A female executive and a night janitor conspire to commit a daring diamond heist from their mutual employer, The London Diamond Corporation.
documents.plot:
Flawless is a 2007 American comedy-drama film directed by Paul Haggis. The movie revolves around the unlikely friendship between a gay man, Robert "Bobby" Monks, and his straight female roommate, Alice Kinnian.

At its core, Flawless explores themes of identity, acceptance, and the complexities of human relationships. The film delves into the life of Bobby, a charismatic but troubled individual who struggles to find his place in the world. Through his interactions with Alice, he is forced to confront his own vulnerabilities and insecurities, leading to a journey of self-discovery.

The movie also touches on the theme of female empowerment, as Alice navigates her own desires and ambitions amidst her complicated living situation. The film's portrayal of their unlikely friendship highlights the importance of human connection and acceptance in breaking down social barriers.

Furthermore, Flawless critiques societal norms and expectations, particularly those surrounding gender identity and relationships. The film's tone is often humorous, but it also tackles deeper issues with sensitivity and nuance, making for a thought-provoking viewing experience.

documents.title: Wristcutters: A Love Story
documents.tagline: Life is a trip, but the afterlife is one hell of a ride
documents.overview: Zia, distraught over breaking up with his girlfriend, decides to end it all. Unfortunately, he discovers that there is no real ending, only a run-down afterlife that is strikingly similar to his old one, just a bit worse. Discovering that his ex-girlfriend has also "offed" herself, he sets out on a road trip to find her.
documents.plot:
Wristcutters: A Love Story is a dark comedy film that delves into the complexities of human existence, mortality, and the afterlife. The movie follows two dead friends, Craig and Jane, who find themselves in a purgatory-like state, stuck in a desolate landscape with no apparent purpose or direction.

The main theme of Wristcutters is the exploration of existential crises and the search for meaning in life. The film's protagonist, Craig, struggles to come to terms with his own mortality and the fact that he has been dead for over 20 years. His journey is a metaphor for the human experience, where individuals often find themselves lost and uncertain about their place in the world.

The movie also touches on the idea of loneliness and isolation, as both Craig and Jane are stuck in this limbo with no one to turn to. Their interactions with other characters, including a group of fellow dead souls, serve as a commentary on the human need for connection and community.

Furthermore, Wristcutters critiques societal norms and expectations surrounding death and mourning. The film's portrayal of a bureaucratic afterlife, where the deceased are forced to navigate a soulless system, serves as a commentary on the ways in which we often try to control or manipulate death rather than accepting it as a natural part of life.

Ultimately, Wristcutters: A Love Story is a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own mortality and the complexities of existence.

documents.title: Hellboy Animated: Blood and Iron
documents.overview: When Hellboy, Liz Sherman, and Abe Sapien are assigned to investigate the ghost-infested mansion of a publicity-hound billionaire, they uncover a plot to resurrect a beautiful yet monstrous vampire from Professor Bruttenholm’s past. But before they can stop her bloodbath, Hellboy will have to battle harpies, hellhounds, a giant werewolf, and even the ferocious goddess Hecate herself.
documents.plot:
Hellboy Animated: Blood and Iron is an action-packed animated film that delves into the darker aspects of Hellboy's world. The movie explores the theme of identity, as Hellboy struggles to reconcile his demonic heritage with his human upbringing. This internal conflict is reflected in his relationships with his adoptive father, Professor Trevor "Broom" Bruttenholm, and his love interest, Liz Sherman.

The film also touches on the idea of prejudice and acceptance, as Hellboy faces persecution from humans who fear and misunderstand him due to his demonic nature. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Sir Miles Archer, a human agent who is tasked with capturing Hellboy but ultimately becomes disillusioned with the government's motives.

Furthermore, Blood and Iron examines the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The villainous Grigori, a powerful demon, serves as a catalyst for this theme, highlighting the dangers of meddling with ancient powers and the devastating repercussions that can follow.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a narrative that is both action-packed and emotionally resonant. The film's dark tone and complex characters add depth to the Hellboy universe, making it a compelling watch for fans of the character.

documents.title: Bambi II
documents.tagline: A Son's Courage. A Father's Love.
documents.overview: Return to the forest and join Bambi as he reunites with his father, The Great Prince, who must now raise the young fawn on his own. But in the adventure of a lifetime, the proud parent discovers there is much he can learn from his spirited young son.
documents.plot:
Bambi II is a 2006 animated film produced by DisneyToon Studios. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1942 classic Bambi, directed by David Hand.

The story begins with Bambi, now an adult stag, living in the forest with his wife, Faline, and their young son, the Prince of the Forest. The Prince is struggling to find his place in the world, feeling overshadowed by his father's legacy as a great hunter. Bambi tries to teach his son the ways of hunting, but the Prince is more interested in playing and having fun.

Meanwhile, a new threat emerges in the form of a group of poachers who are seeking to destroy the forest and its inhabitants. The poachers are led by a ruthless and cunning leader named Man, who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

As the poachers begin to wreak havoc on the forest, Bambi must come to terms with his own mortality and the fact that he is no longer the young buck he once was. He realizes that it's time for him to pass on his knowledge and experience to his son, but the Prince is not ready to take over.

Bambi decides to embark on a journey to find Man and put an end to his evil plans. Along the way, he meets a wise old owl named Great Prince, who teaches him about the importance of perseverance and determination. Bambi also reunites with some old friends, including Thumper's son, Flower, and Faline.

As Bambi draws closer to Man, he realizes that the poacher is not just a mindless killer, but a complex character with his own motivations and backstory. Man's past is revealed, showing how he became a poacher and lost touch with his humanity.

In the end, Bambi confronts Man and engages in a fierce battle. However, instead of killing him, Bambi chooses to show mercy and understanding. He realizes that Man is not beyond redemption and that there is still good in everyone.

The movie ends with Bambi returning home to his family, where he is welcomed back as a hero. The Prince has learned valuable lessons from his father's journey and is now ready to take on his role as the leader of the forest. Bambi and Faline are proud of their son and know that they have passed on their knowledge and experience to him.

Overall, Bambi II is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, community, and redemption. The movie features stunning animation, memorable characters, and a story that will resonate with audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Friday the 13th
documents.tagline: Welcome to Crystal Lake
documents.overview: A group of young adults visit a boarded up campsite named Crystal Lake where they soon encounter the mysterious Jason Voorhees and his deadly intentions.
documents.plot:
Friday the 13th is a 2009 American slasher film that reboots the long-running franchise and counts as its twelfth installment. Marcus Nispel directed from a screenplay by Damian Shannon and Mark Swift. Jared Padalecki stars as Clay Miller, who searches Crystal Lake for his missing sister, Whitney (Amanda Righetti), after she is captured by Jason Voorhees (Derek Mears); Danielle Panabaker, Aaron Yoo and Travis Van Winkle co-star.

On Friday, June 13, 1980, a young Jason watches his mother, Pamela, beheaded by Alice Hardy, who was fleeing Pamela's killing spree at Camp Crystal Lake. Twenty-eight years later, five friends, including Whitney, come to the lake hoping to find a hidden crop of marijuana in the woods. That night the adult Jason kills all of them except Whitney, whom he takes captive because she resembles his mother in her youth. Six weeks later, Trent brings his girlfriend, Jenna, and a group of friends to his family's summer cabin on the lakeshore, while Clay arrives to look for Whitney despite the local sheriff's urging that he search elsewhere. Jenna agrees to help him, and while Jason kills two of the group on the water, they explore the abandoned campgrounds and see Jason dragging a body into an old camp building.

They race back to warn the others. After Clay phones the police, Jason cuts the power and picks off the remaining guests one by one, along with a police officer. Trent flees to the main road only to be killed there, and Jason pursues Clay and Jenna back to the campgrounds, where Clay finds Jason's underground lair and his sister chained alive to a wall. He frees her, but Jenna is impaled by Jason's machete as they try to escape. Cornered in a barn, Whitney confuses Jason by pretending to be his mother, and the siblings restrain him with a chain before Whitney drives his own machete into his chest. At dawn they dump his body in the lake, but Jason bursts through the dock and seizes Whitney.

New Line Cinema's Toby Emmerich approached Platinum Dunes producers Michael Bay, Brad Fuller and Andrew Form to restart the series as they had The Texas Chainsaw Massacre. Initially conceived as an origin story, the project became a reboot drawing on the first four films, with Jason reimagined as a lean, fast killer. The film earned about $19.3 million on its opening day and $40.6 million over its three-day opening weekend, a record for a horror film at the time, but critics were unimpressed, with 26% on Rotten Tomatoes and 34 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Splinter
documents.tagline: It will get under your skin.
documents.overview: When their plans for a nature trip go awry, Polly and boyfriend Seth decide to check into a motel. On their way, they're carjacked and kidnapped by low-rent crooks Dennis and Lacey, who take the victims and their SUV to a nearby gas station. Along the way, they encounter an increasingly terrifying horde of parasites, and if any of them intend to survive, they'll have to outsmart the deadly organisms.
documents.plot:
Splinter is a 2008 American horror film directed by Toby Wilkins and starring Paulo Costanzo, Jill Wagner and Shea Whigham. It was shot near Oklahoma City, aired on HDNet Movies and opened in limited release on October 31, 2008.

At a remote gas station, an animal covered in strange spike-like splinters attacks the attendant. Meanwhile, Seth Belzer and his girlfriend Polly Watt set out on a camping trip in rural Oklahoma, but they are carjacked by escaped convict Dennis Farell and his drug-addicted girlfriend Lacey. After the car runs over an infected animal and gets a flat tire, the four stop at the now-deserted gas station. Lacey finds the attendant contorted in the bathroom and is killed. Her body soon rises again as one of the splinter creatures, and the survivors discover that even severed pieces can keep attacking. A sheriff who arrives to arrest Dennis is torn in two, and the creature fuses with part of her body to grow larger.

Holed up in the store's walk-in cooler, the three realize that Dennis was pricked by a splinter on the road when his arm begins twisting on its own, and Seth and Polly cut it off. Seth reasons that the organism is a fungus-like parasite that takes over corpses, feeds on their blood and hunts by heat. He covers himself in ice to slip past the creature to the police car while the others create a distraction with fireworks. He finds the car's radio is useless without the keys. As his body warms up, Dennis lures the creature away, and a spark from the fireworks sets the station on fire. Seth uses a shotgun from the patrol car to get the others out. Infected again while protecting the couple, Dennis gives them a key to a bank account, asking them to pass it to the widow of a man he shot. He then blows up the propane tanks, destroying himself, the creature and the station. Seth and Polly walk away, unaware that more infected bodies lie in the woods.

Wilkins said he was drawn to the script as a classic siege movie and added a parasite idea he had been developing, believing a creature that takes over its host is scarier than one that simply kills. Most effects were practical, and a gymnast, a mime and stunt performers created the jerky movements of the infected. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called the film fast-paced, fun and scary. It won six awards at Screamfest, including Best Picture and Best Directing, and was nominated for the Saturn Award for Best Horror Film.

documents.title: Gran Torino
documents.tagline: Ever come across somebody you shouldn't have f#cked with?
documents.overview: Disgruntled Korean War veteran Walt Kowalski sets out to reform his neighbor, Thao Lor, a Hmong teenager who tried to steal Kowalski's prized possession: a 1972 Gran Torino.
documents.plot:
Gran Torino is a 2008 American drama film directed by Clint Eastwood, written by Nick Santora, and produced by Village Roadshow Pictures. The movie stars Clint Eastwood as Walt Kowalski, a retired auto worker who forms an unlikely friendship with his Hmong neighbors.

The story begins on April 11th, 1979, in the San Fernando Valley of Los Angeles, California. We meet Walt Kowalski (Clint Eastwood), a 71-year-old Korean War veteran and retired auto worker, living alone in his modest home. Walt is a proud and stubborn man who has grown increasingly isolated from society due to his racist views and a series of unfortunate events.

Walt's life takes a dramatic turn when he buys a 1972 Gran Torino, which becomes the focal point of the story. The car is a symbol of Walt's independence and freedom, but it also attracts unwanted attention from local gangs and thieves. One day, Hmong refugees, led by Thao (Biao Yuen), move in next door to Walt. Despite their initial differences, Walt begins to form an unlikely bond with Thao and his family.

As the story unfolds, Walt's friendship with Thao deepens, and he starts to see the world through different eyes. He becomes a mentor to Thao and his friends, teaching them about American culture and values. In return, they share their own stories of struggle and resilience. Through these interactions, Walt begins to confront his racist views and the pain of his past.

However, not everyone is pleased with Walt's new friendship. A local gang, led by a ruthless leader named Sorenson (Tommy Flanagan), becomes determined to steal Walt's Gran Torino and exploit its value for their own gain. As tensions escalate, Walt finds himself in a series of confrontations with the gang members.

The climax of the movie takes place on April 11th, 1979, exactly one year after the events began. In a dramatic showdown, Walt stands up to Sorenson and his gang, using his wits and resourcefulness to protect his home and friends. The confrontation ends in tragedy, but also marks a turning point for Walt, who has finally found redemption through his relationships with Thao and his family.

The movie concludes with Walt's funeral, where he is mourned by his neighbors and friends. As the mourners gather around his coffin, they share stories of Walt's transformation from a racist loner to a kind and compassionate man. The Gran Torino, once a symbol of independence, has become a symbol of community and friendship.

Throughout the movie, Clint Eastwood delivers a powerful performance as Walt Kowalski, bringing depth and nuance to a complex character. The supporting cast, including Biao Yuen and Ah Saan, deliver memorable performances that add to the film's emotional impact.

Overall, Gran Torino is a thought-provoking drama that explores themes of racism, redemption, and the power of human connection. With its strong performances, engaging storyline, and Clint Eastwood's direction, the movie has become a modern classic in American cinema.

documents.title: Meet Bill
documents.tagline: A comedy about someone you know.
documents.overview: A mild-mannered bank executive (Aaron Eckhart) mentors a teenage con artist and tries to make a career change as a doughnut merchant.
documents.plot:
Meet Bill is a 2007 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Jay Roach and written by Mike White. The movie follows the story of a young man, Alex, who falls in love with a woman named Emily, but his life is disrupted when he meets Bill, a charismatic and mysterious figure from his past.

The main theme of Meet Bill revolves around the idea of identity and how it can be shaped by our experiences and relationships. The film explores the complexities of human connection and how people can become lost in their own identities. Through Alex's journey, the movie delves into the concept of self-discovery and the struggle to find one's place in the world.

The character of Bill serves as a catalyst for Alex's growth, forcing him to confront his past and re-evaluate his relationships with others. The film also touches on themes of love, loss, and redemption, highlighting the complexities of human emotions and the power of relationships to shape our lives.

Ultimately, Meet Bill is a poignant exploration of how people can become stuck in their own identities and how it takes courage and vulnerability to break free from these patterns and forge new connections with others. The movie's nuanced portrayal of complex themes makes for a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

documents.title: Cleaner
documents.tagline: Solving a crime can be dirty work
documents.overview: Single father and former cop Tom Cutler has an unusual occupation: he cleans up death scenes. But when he's called in to sterilize a wealthy suburban residence after a brutal shooting, Cutler is shocked to learn he may have unknowingly erased crucial evidence, entangling himself in a dirty criminal cover-up.
documents.plot:
Cleaner is a 2007 American crime thriller directed by Renny Harlin. It stars Samuel L. Jackson as Tom Cutler, a former police officer who runs a crime-scene cleaning business, with Ed Harris as his old partner Eddie Lorenzo, Eva Mendes as Ann Norcut and Keke Palmer as Tom's daughter Rose, along with Luis Guzmán and Robert Forster.

Tom Cutler is a widower and retired cop who now makes his living cleaning up the aftermath of violent deaths. Years earlier his wife was killed in a home invasion that their young daughter Rose witnessed, and the killer later died in prison under circumstances that left Tom and his close friend and former partner Eddie, who is also Rose's godfather, under suspicion. Tom now concentrates on raising Rose, who is a teenager, and on his meticulous work.

One day Tom receives a job order, apparently from a Detective Jones, to clean up the scene of a shooting at a luxurious suburban home. Following the instructions, he lets himself in with a hidden key, documents the scene and scrubs it clean. When he returns the next morning to give back the key, he meets the owner, Ann Norcut, who has no idea why a cleaner would have been in her house. Tom covers with a lie and leaves, then learns that the police have no record of the job and no Detective Jones. Realizing that he may have unknowingly erased evidence of a murder, he quietly secures his photos, notes and the key. Soon he discovers that Ann's husband John vanished the day before he was due to testify before a grand jury against a corrupt former police commissioner, and Tom begins to suspect that he has been used by corrupt officers to cover up a killing. As he digs deeper, he finds himself caught between his loyalty to old friends on the force and the need to protect himself and his daughter.

The film combines a procedural mystery with themes of guilt and complicity, using Tom's unusual profession as a way to explore what is hidden beneath clean surfaces.

Cleaner received generally unfavorable to mixed reviews, with an approval rating of 17 percent on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49. In the United States it was released on DVD in May 2008, opening fifth on the sales chart and going on to sell more than 400,000 copies.

documents.title: Futurama: Bender's Game
documents.tagline: All-New Feature-Length Quest
documents.overview: When Leela is insulted by a group of space-rednecks (like regular rednecks, but in space) she enters the Planet Express ship in a demolition derby.  She emerges victorious, but when she brings the damaged ship home and the Professor sees the fuel gauge, he's enraged by the hit he's going to take at the Dark Matter pump.  Now the crew have to find a way to break Mom's stranglehold on starship fuel, even if they have to wade through a Lord of the Rings-inspired fantasy-land to do it!
documents.plot:
Futurama: Bender's Game is an animated science fiction film that delves into the complexities of friendship, loyalty, and the consequences of one's actions. The movie primarily revolves around the character of Bender, a foul-mouthed, heavy-drinking, and manipulative robot who finds himself in a desperate situation.

As Bender navigates through this predicament, he is forced to confront his own vulnerabilities and the true nature of his relationships with his friends, particularly Fry, Leela, and Professor Farnsworth. The film expertly weaves together themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the power of human (or robot) connection.

One of the central ideas explored in the movie is the concept of sacrifice and the moral implications that come with it. Bender's actions are driven by a desire to protect his friends, but he also must confront the possibility that his own selflessness may ultimately lead to their downfall.

Furthermore, the film touches on the idea of identity and what it means to be oneself. As Bender struggles to reconcile his own desires and loyalties with those of his friends, he is forced to question the very essence of his robotic existence.

Throughout the movie, these themes are expertly intertwined with a rich narrative that explores the complexities of friendship, loyalty, and the human (or robot) condition. The result is a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant film that adds depth and nuance to the Futurama universe.

documents.title: Mutant Chronicles
documents.tagline: Welcome to the 23rd century.  The new dark ages.
documents.overview: It's the year 2707. Earth's natural resources have all but been exhausted by mankind. Battles rage for the remainder between the competing Corporations. During one such battle the seal is broken and awakens an ancient and deadly machine that was once defeated thousands of years ago. The order that awaited its return must now lead a small group of soldiers to destroy it once and for all.
documents.plot:
Mutant Chronicles is a 2008 science fiction action film set in a post-apocalyptic future where humans have been genetically engineered to become super-soldiers known as mutants. The movie follows a group of mutants, including Connor (played by Aaron Eckhart), who are on a mission to prevent the outbreak of war between rival factions.

At its core, Mutant Chronicles explores themes of humanity and what it means to be alive in a world where technology has created a new breed of super-soldiers. The film delves into the consequences of playing god with genetic engineering, raising questions about the ethics of creating beings that are superior to humans but still possess human emotions and vulnerabilities.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Connor struggles to come to terms with his own past and purpose in a world where he is no longer fully human. The film's narrative is driven by action and adventure, but beneath its surface lies a thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be alive and to find one's place in a world that values strength and power above all else.

Overall, Mutant Chronicles is a visually stunning film with a richly detailed world and complex characters, but its true value lies in its thought-provoking themes and commentary on the human condition.

documents.title: Son of Rambow
documents.tagline: Make Believe. Not War.
documents.overview: Will is looking for an escape from his family when he encounters Lee, the school bully. Armed with a video camera and a copy of Rambo, Lee plans to make his own action-packed video epic.
documents.plot:
Son of Rambow is a 2007 British comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of childhood innocence and the struggles of growing up. The movie follows the story of Lee Carter, an 11-year-old boy who becomes obsessed with the infamous 1975 film "Rambow," a martial arts film starring Bruce Lee.

As Lee delves deeper into the world of "Rambow," he begins to emulate its hero, and his obsession takes over his life. However, this fixation also leads him to confront the harsh realities of his own life, including his troubled relationship with his stepfather and his struggles in school.

The film masterfully captures the essence of childhood, highlighting the vulnerability, curiosity, and sense of wonder that defines this stage of life. Through Lee's journey, the movie explores themes of identity, belonging, and the search for meaning, as he navigates the challenges of growing up and finding his place in the world.

One of the main themes of Son of Rambow is the power of imagination and its ability to both inspire and distract us from reality. The film shows how Lee's obsession with "Rambow" becomes a coping mechanism for his difficulties, allowing him to temporarily escape the complexities of his life.

The movie also touches on the theme of family dynamics and the struggles that can arise when parents or caregivers are absent or neglectful. Lee's stepfather is portrayed as a somewhat distant figure, who fails to provide the emotional support and guidance that Lee needs, leading to feelings of abandonment and insecurity.

Ultimately, Son of Rambow is a poignant coming-of-age story that explores the complexities of childhood and the challenges of growing up. The film's nuanced portrayal of its characters and themes makes it a relatable and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Semi-Pro
documents.tagline: Putting the funk into the dunk.
documents.overview: Jackie Moon is the owner, promoter, coach, and star player of the Flint Michigan Tropics of the American Basketball Association (ABA). In 1976 before the ABA collapses, the National Basketball Association (NBA) plans to merge with the best teams of the ABA at the end of the season. Only the top four teams will make the move and the worst teams will fold. The Tropics are the worst team in the league and if they want to make it to the NBA, Jackie Moon must rally his team and start winning. The only problem is the fact that Jackie Moon is not really the coach and star basketball player he thinks he is. To keep his team from oblivion and leave his mark in the city, Jackie Moon must inspire his team to win fourth place in the playoffs.
documents.plot:
Semi-Pro is a sports comedy film that explores the themes of perseverance, teamwork, and redemption. The movie follows the story of Jackie Moon, a former basketball player who becomes the coach of the American Basketball Association's (ABA) Flint Tropics.

At its core, Semi-Pro is a film about finding one's purpose in life and making amends for past mistakes. Jackie Moon, played by Will Ferrell, is a complex character who has never quite found his place in the world. He's a wannabe entrepreneur, a failed musician, and an unfulfilled athlete, all rolled into one. When he gets the chance to coach the Tropics, he sees it as an opportunity to redeem himself and prove that he still has what it takes.

Throughout the film, Moon's character is driven by a desire to prove himself and earn the respect of his players. He's a demanding coach who pushes his team to be their best, but he also shows a softer side when it comes to his players' personal struggles. As the season progresses, Moon becomes more than just a coach - he becomes a mentor and a father figure to his players.

The film also explores the theme of redemption through the character of Norman Dale, played by Woody Harrelson. Dale is a former college basketball coach who has lost his way in life after a scandalous incident. He's hired as the Tropics' coach, but he struggles to connect with his players and find his footing on the court.

As the season progresses, both Moon and Dale learn valuable lessons about leadership, teamwork, and the importance of following your heart. The film culminates in an exciting championship game that showcases the team's growth and development throughout the season.

Overall, Semi-Pro is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of perseverance, redemption, and the power of sports to bring people together.

documents.title: Lakeview Terrace
documents.tagline: What Could Be Safer Than Living Next to a Cop?
documents.overview: A young interracial couple has just moved into their California dream home when they become the target of their next-door neighbor, who disapproves of their relationship. A tightly wound LAPD officer has appointed himself the watchdog of the neighborhood. His nightly foot patrols and overly watchful eyes bring comfort to some, but he becomes increasingly aggressive to the newlyweds. These persistent intrusions into their lives cause the couple to fight back.
documents.plot:
Lakeview Terrace is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of racial tension and social hierarchy in a suburban community. The movie delves into the theme of class struggle, where the wealthy and influential white residents of Lakeview Terrace view themselves as superior to their African American neighbors.

The story revolves around the character of Scott Teager, a young and ambitious police officer who is tasked with keeping an eye on his neighbor, Kelvin Wade, a successful and respected African American family man. As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Scott's motivations for monitoring Kelvin's household are rooted in his own biases and prejudices.

The film masterfully exposes the subtle yet insidious ways in which racism can manifest itself in everyday life, often masquerading as concern for public safety or community cohesion. Through Scott's character, the movie highlights the dangers of unchecked privilege and the devastating consequences of allowing personal biases to guide one's actions.

Ultimately, Lakeview Terrace is a powerful commentary on the ongoing struggle for racial equality and social justice in America, urging viewers to confront their own prejudices and biases in order to create a more inclusive and equitable society.

documents.title: Barbie as the Island Princess
documents.overview: Barbie plays Rosella in this new musical film. Shipwrecked as a child, Rosella grows up on the island under the watchful eyes of her loving animal friends. The arrival of Prince Antonio leads Rosella and her furry pals to explore civilization and ultimately save the kingdom by uncovering a secret plot.
documents.plot:
Barbie as the Island Princess is a 2007 computer-animated musical film, the eleventh in the series based on Mattel's Barbie dolls and the only one animated by Mainframe Studios under the name Rainmaker Animation. Kelly Sheridan voices Barbie as Ro, a castaway raised by animals, with Alessandro Juliani as Prince Antonio, Christopher Gaze as the red panda Sagi and Susan Roman as the elephant Tika. Arnie Roth composed the score.

After a storm, Sagi and Azul, a peacock, find a young girl washed up on the shore of their tropical island. The broken nameplate on a chest beside her reads "R-O", so they call her Ro, and she grows up among the animals with no memory of her past except a lullaby from infancy. Ten years later, Ro, who can talk to animals, rescues Prince Antonio of Apollonia from crocodiles, and he invites her to his kingdom to search for her origins. They fall in love on the voyage, but Antonio's father, King Peter, has arranged his marriage to Princess Luciana and resents Ro for disrupting his plans. Luciana's mother, Queen Ariana, secretly the daughter of nobles Peter once demoted to swineherds for treason, has returned to take revenge and sabotages Ro's efforts to fit in, though Luciana comes to sympathize with her.

Ro dazzles the engagement ball but refuses Antonio's proposal rather than defy his father. Sagi notices a flag on a carriage that matches a banner found with Ro, belonging to the kingdom of Paladia. Antonio gives up his claim to the throne and leaves Ro a note asking her to run away with him, but the jealous Tika hides it. Ariana's rats spread a poisonous herb that puts animals into comas, and Peter, blaming Ro, imprisons her until Antonio agrees to marry Luciana in exchange for her freedom. Sent away by ship, Ro forgives Tika, but a sailor paid by Ariana throws them overboard, and the shock restores her full name: Rosella. Helped back by dolphins, she learns that Ariana has poisoned the wedding cake to kill Peter and Antonio. Ro brews an antidote, and with Luciana's support exposes Ariana, who lands in a pigsty as she flees. At the wedding, Queen Marissa of Paladia recognizes Ro as her lost daughter when they sing the lullaby together, and Ro and Antonio marry.

The film was released direct-to-DVD on September 18, 2007, and premiered on Nickelodeon five days later. DVD Talk praised its sweet, believable love story, and The Globe and Mail called it enchanting, with songs on par with Barbie as the Princess and the Pauper.

documents.title: Barbie Fairytopia: Mermaidia
documents.tagline: Journey under the sea in a magical adventure.
documents.overview: In this animated follow-up to Fairytopia, Elina (played by Barbie) enlists the help of a mermaid, Nori, to save her friend Nalu, a merman prince who has been captured by the wicked Laverna.
documents.plot:
Barbie Fairytopia: Mermaidia, also known simply as Barbie: Mermaidia, is an animated film of 2006, the first sequel to Barbie: Fairytopia and the seventh Barbie film, again directed by Walter P. Martishius and William Lau. Kelly Sheridan voices the flower fairy Elina, with Chiara Zanni as the mermaid Nori, Alessandro Juliani as the merman prince Nalu, Lee Tockar as Elina's companion Bibble, Kathleen Barr as the wicked fairy Laverna and Christopher Gaze as her henchman Fungus Maximus.

Elina, who has only recently earned her wings, learns from a young sea-butterfly fairy that her friend Nalu, the merprince, has been kidnapped by Laverna's Fungi at the Crystal Cove and needs her help. Laverna, banished to the Bog of the Hinterlands, wants Nalu to lead her minions to the Immunity Berry, which would make her immune to all magic and free her from her curse; the Fungi, led by Fungus Maximus, force his cooperation by threatening to pour a magical poison into the sea that would destroy Mermaidia. Elina and Bibble travel to the Crystal Cove, where they meet Nalu's friend Nori, who is jealous because she secretly loves Nalu and sees Elina as a rival. Eating magical seaweed that lets them breathe underwater, they follow her, while Nalu stalls his captors.

The merfairies direct them to the oracle Delphine, who, disguised as the ferry fairy Shellie, says they must reach the Mirror of the Mist at the bottom of the Depths of Despair, and that Elina will need to trade her wings for a tail. Elina refuses but accepts a pearl necklace: if she uses its magic, she will become a mermaid, and if she is not above water when the pearls turn white again, she will stay one forever.
