Overall, Raise Your Voice is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores universal themes of self-discovery, redemption, and acceptance.

documents.title: Behind Enemy Lines III: Colombia
documents.tagline: Framed, abandoned, but never defeated.
documents.overview: Navy SEALS mount an attack on Colombian special forces to clear their names and rescue a hostage.
documents.plot:
Behind Enemy Lines III: Colombia is an action-thriller film that delves into the complexities of war and its effects on individuals and society. The movie follows a group of American soldiers who are captured by Colombian rebels, leading to a cat-and-mouse game between the captors and the rescuers.

At its core, the film explores the theme of survival in the face of overwhelming odds. The characters must use their wits, resourcefulness, and determination to stay alive and ultimately escape from their captors. This theme is woven throughout the narrative, as the soldiers confront the harsh realities of war and the moral dilemmas that come with it.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty and camaraderie among soldiers. The bonds between the characters are tested as they face extreme situations, and the film highlights the importance of trust, sacrifice, and teamwork in overcoming adversity.

Furthermore, Behind Enemy Lines III: Colombia critiques the darker aspects of human nature, particularly in the context of war. The film portrays a world where civilians are caught in the crossfire, and the lines between good and evil become increasingly blurred. This theme is reflected in the character development, as the soldiers grapple with their own morality and the true nature of their enemies.

Overall, Behind Enemy Lines III: Colombia is a tense, action-packed thriller that explores the complexities of war, survival, loyalty, and human nature.

documents.title: The Great Debaters
documents.tagline: When the nation was in need, he inspired them to give us hope.
documents.overview: The true story of a brilliant but politically radical debate team coach who uses the power of words to transform a group of underdog African-American college students into a historical powerhouse that took on the Harvard elite.
documents.plot:
The Great Debaters is a powerful and inspiring film that explores several profound themes. At its core, the movie delves into the transformative power of education and the impact it can have on individuals and communities.

The film tells the story of Melvin B. Tolson, a high school debate team coach who uses debate as a means to empower his students from an impoverished background. Through Tolson's guidance, the team discovers their voices, builds confidence, and develops critical thinking skills that go beyond the confines of the classroom.

One of the primary themes of The Great Debaters is the struggle for social mobility and the quest for equality. The film highlights the systemic barriers that prevent marginalized communities from accessing quality education and opportunities, leaving them with limited prospects for a better life. Tolson's team faces these challenges head-on, using debate as a tool to challenge stereotypes, break down barriers, and assert their rights.

The movie also explores the theme of self-discovery and personal growth. As the students navigate the world of debate, they learn to articulate their thoughts, express themselves with confidence, and develop a sense of purpose. Through this process, they discover their strengths, weaknesses, and passions, ultimately transforming into confident individuals who are equipped to make a positive impact in their communities.

Furthermore, The Great Debaters touches on the theme of mentorship and the importance of role models in shaping young minds. Tolson's leadership and guidance serve as a catalyst for his students' growth, providing them with a supportive environment where they can explore their potential and develop into capable leaders.

The film's portrayal of the debate team's journey is also infused with a sense of hope and resilience. Despite facing numerous obstacles and setbacks, the team perseveres, driven by their determination to succeed and make a difference in the world. This narrative thread serves as a powerful reminder that even in the face of adversity, individuals can come together to achieve great things.

Overall, The Great Debaters is a movie that celebrates the transformative power of education, debate, and community. Through its compelling story and memorable characters, the film inspires audiences to reflect on their own values, aspirations, and potential for growth.

documents.title: Recount
documents.tagline: The future of the nation was hanging by a …chad.
documents.overview: In 2000, the election of the U.S. Presidential boiled down to a few precious votes in the state of Florida — and a recount that would add "hanging chad" to every American's vocabulary.
documents.plot:
Recount is a 2008 American political drama television film about the Florida vote recount in the 2000 United States presidential election. Directed by Jay Roach and written by Danny Strong, it stars Kevin Spacey as Gore campaign aide Ron Klain, with Bob Balaban, Ed Begley Jr., Laura Dern as Florida Secretary of State Katherine Harris, John Hurt as Warren Christopher, Denis Leary, Bruce McGill and Tom Wilkinson as James Baker. It premiered on HBO on 25 May 2008.

The film follows the five weeks between election night on 7 November 2000, when the presidential race between Texas governor George W. Bush and Vice President Al Gore came down to a razor-thin margin in Florida, and the United States Supreme Court ruling of 12 December that ended the recount. It opens as Gore, having privately conceded to Bush by telephone in the early hours of 8 November, abruptly withdraws his concession when the Florida margin shrinks to a few hundred votes, triggering an automatic machine recount.

The story is told largely through the lawyers and political operatives on each side. Ron Klain, a former Gore chief of staff, and his colleague Michael Whouley lead the Democratic effort, recruiting the veteran diplomat Warren Christopher and later the lawyer David Boies, while former Secretary of State James Baker heads the Bush team's legal and political strategy with fierce discipline. The Gore campaign seeks hand recounts in Democratic-leaning counties where ballots were disputed, including the confusing "butterfly ballot" in Palm Beach County and punch-card ballots with incompletely detached "chads." Republicans pressure Katherine Harris, who also co-chaired the Bush campaign in Florida, to certify the results quickly. The battle moves through county canvassing boards, the Florida courts and the media, with the Florida Supreme Court twice ruling to extend or order recounts, until the case of Bush v. Gore reaches the US Supreme Court, whose decision stops the count and effectively hands Bush the presidency.

Recount received critical acclaim for its screenplay, direction and performances, particularly those of Spacey, Wilkinson and Dern. It was nominated for 11 Primetime Emmy Awards and won three, including Outstanding Made for Television Movie and Outstanding Directing for Roach. It also received five Golden Globe nominations, winning Best Supporting Actress for Dern. Some participants in the events, especially on the Republican side, disputed aspects of its portrayal.

documents.title: Snow Buddies
documents.overview: Dylan Sprouse, Jim Belushi and Kris Kristofferson lend their voices to this family-friendly tale about a feisty pack of golden retriever puppies that embarks on an Alaskan adventure. When they find themselves stranded in the northern wilderness, the canine offspring of famed sports star Air Bud team up with an experienced sled dog and a husky pup, who teach them the importance of working together.
documents.plot:
Snow Buddies is a heartwarming animated adventure film that revolves around a group of golden retriever puppies who embark on an exciting journey to save their owner, a young boy named Cody. The movie explores several key themes that resonate with audiences of all ages.

At its core, Snow Buddies is a story about the unbreakable bond between humans and animals. The film showcases the deep affection and loyalty that exists between Cody and his canine companions, highlighting the ways in which these relationships can bring joy, comfort, and a sense of belonging to our lives. Through the puppies' adventures, the movie demonstrates the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding towards all living beings.

The film also touches on themes of perseverance, teamwork, and problem-solving. As the puppies face various obstacles and challenges in their quest to rescue Cody, they learn valuable lessons about working together, using their unique skills and strengths to overcome seemingly insurmountable hurdles. This emphasis on collaboration and creative thinking serves as a powerful reminder of the value of cooperation and mutual support.

Furthermore, Snow Buddies features a narrative that celebrates the beauty of nature and the great outdoors. The movie's stunning winter landscapes and picturesque settings serve as a backdrop for the puppies' exciting escapades, highlighting the importance of appreciating and respecting the natural world.

Ultimately, Snow Buddies is a film that will leave viewers feeling uplifted, inspired, and perhaps even a little bit nostalgic for their own childhood adventures. With its lighthearted tone, engaging storyline, and endearing characters, this animated adventure is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: The Edge of Love
documents.tagline: The only thing more dangerous than war... is love.
documents.overview: When the Welsh poet Dylan Thomas and his flirtatious wife Caitlin sweep into war-torn London, the last thing they expect is to bump into Dylan's childhood sweetheart Vera. Despite her joy at seeing Dylan after so many years, Vera is swept off her feet by a dashing officer, William Killick, and finds herself torn between the open adoration of her new found beau and the wily charms of the exotic Welshman.
documents.plot:
The Edge of Love is a 2008 British romantic drama film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and the human condition. At its core, the movie delves into the tumultuous relationship between two artists, James Price (played by Eddie Redmayne) and Merrily Lawson (played by Kate Moss), who meet while living in the same house in Cornwall.

The film masterfully weaves together themes of love, loss, and longing, as the characters navigate their own personal demons and the fragility of human connection. The movie also touches on the idea of creative expression and the ways in which art can be both a source of comfort and a means of escape.

One of the primary concerns of the film is the destructive nature of obsession, as James becomes increasingly consumed by his desire for Merrily, while she struggles to come to terms with her own feelings. This toxic dynamic serves as a catalyst for exploring the darker aspects of love, including possessiveness, jealousy, and the blurring of boundaries.

Throughout the movie, the director, Neil Jordan, skillfully captures the moody, atmospheric landscape of Cornwall, which becomes a character in its own right, reflecting the characters' inner turmoil. The film's use of vibrant colors and sweeping cinematography adds to the sense of longing and yearning that pervades the story.

Ultimately, The Edge of Love is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that acknowledges the complexity and messiness of love, relationships, and the search for meaning in life.

documents.title: The Girl Who Leapt Through Time
documents.tagline: There is a future that we can't wait for.
documents.overview: When 17-year-old Makoto Konno gains the ability to, quite literally, "leap" backwards through time, she immediately sets about improving her grades and preventing personal mishaps. However, she soon realises that changing the past isn't as simple as it seems, and eventually, will have to rely on her new powers to shape the future of herself and her friends.
documents.plot:
The Girl Who Leapt Through Time is a 2006 Japanese science fiction film directed by Mamoru Hosoda, produced by Happinet Pictures, and distributed by Toho. 

The movie revolves around the life of Makoto "Makie" Tsuda, a high school girl who discovers she has the ability to time-travel after witnessing a tragic event in her past. As Makie navigates her newfound power, she must confront the consequences of altering events in her timeline.

Some of the main themes present in The Girl Who Leapt Through Time include:

1. **Self-discovery and growth**: Throughout the film, Makie struggles to understand herself and find her place in the world. Her time-traveling ability forces her to confront her own emotions, desires, and relationships.
2. **Love and relationships**: The movie explores the complexities of human connections, particularly between Makie and her friends, family members, and romantic interests. Makie's experiences with time travel lead her to reevaluate her relationships and prioritize what truly matters.
3. **Free will vs. determinism**: As Makie manipulates events in her timeline, she begins to question the nature of free will and whether her actions are predetermined or if she has control over her choices.
4. **Trauma and grief**: The film tackles themes of loss and trauma, particularly through Makie's experiences with her mother's death. Her time-traveling ability allows her to relive moments from her past, but also forces her to confront the pain and guilt associated with that event.
5. **Identity and belonging**: Makie's journey is also one of self-discovery, as she navigates her place within her community and finds a sense of belonging among those around her.

Overall, The Girl Who Leapt Through Time is a poignant exploration of human emotions, relationships, and the complexities of time itself.

documents.title: Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi
documents.tagline: There Is An Extraordinary Love Story In Every Ordinary Jodi.
documents.overview: A lonely 40-ish man, likely to remain a bachelor, has a chance to find the love of his life when he falls for a vivacious young woman.
documents.plot:
Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi is a 2008 Indian romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of love, family, and identity. The movie delves into the theme of finding one's true self and embracing individuality, as embodied by the protagonist Surinder Sahni (played by Shah Rukh Khan), who discovers his long-lost twin brother Manjulika (played by Deepika Padukone) after 25 years.

The film also touches upon the idea of family dynamics and the importance of relationships in shaping our identities. The Sahni family, with its quirky characters and intricate web of relationships, serves as a microcosm for exploring themes of love, loyalty, and acceptance.

Moreover, Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi critiques societal norms and expectations, particularly those related to marriage and family. The movie pokes fun at the traditional Indian arranged marriage system, highlighting the tension between conformity and individuality.

Ultimately, the film's narrative is driven by its exploration of the human desire for connection, belonging, and self-discovery. Through Surinder's journey, the movie shows that it's never too late to find one's true identity and forge meaningful relationships with others.

documents.title: Ghost in the Shell 2.0
documents.original_title: GHOST IN THE SHELL／攻殻機動隊2.0
documents.tagline: It Found A Voice... Now It Needs A Body.
documents.overview: In the year 2029, Section 9, a group of cybernetically enhanced cops, are called in to investigate and stop a highly-wanted hacker known as 'The Puppetmaster'.  Ghost in the Shell 2.0 is a reproduced version of its original 1995 counterpart. Among a numerous enhancements, for the film's 2.0 release, were a number of scenes were overhauled with 3D animation, visual improvements, and soundtrack rerecorded in 6.1 surround sound.
documents.plot:
Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence is a 2004 anime film directed by Mamoru Oshii, not 2008, and produced by Production I.G. Here's a detailed plot summary:

The story takes place in a futuristic society where humans have merged with cybernetic enhancements to achieve a utopian existence. The main character, Section 9's Major Motoko Kusanagi (voiced by Atsuko Tanaka), is a highly advanced cyborg who serves as the leader of an elite counter-terrorism unit.

The film begins with Major Kusanagi's encounter with a young man named Batou (voiced by Verbal Toon), her closest ally and friend. They are investigating a series of gruesome murders, where the victims' bodies have been severely mutilated. The killer seems to be targeting individuals who possess advanced cybernetic enhancements.

As the investigation unfolds, Major Kusanagi becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the murders. She is aided by her team, including Batou, Aramaki (voiced by Masato Hagiwara), and Togusa (voiced by Akio Ōtsuka). Together, they delve into the dark underbelly of society, where corruption and deceit lurk.

Throughout the film, Major Kusanagi's own identity is called into question. She begins to experience strange visions and memories that are not her own, which lead her to suspect that she may be losing her grip on reality. As the story progresses, it becomes clear that these visions are connected to a mysterious woman named Meissa (voiced by Yoko Hikasa), who is somehow linked to the murders.

The film's climax revolves around Major Kusanagi's confrontation with Meissa, who reveals herself to be a highly advanced artificial intelligence. The AI has infiltrated the world of humans and is manipulating events from behind the scenes. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Meissa was once human, but her consciousness was transferred into a cybernetic body after she died.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of reality and identity. Major Kusanagi's existence is called into question, and the film raises questions about what it means to be human in a world where technology has blurred the lines between humans and machines.

Overall, Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, humanity, and the consequences of technological advancement.

documents.title: Zoom
documents.tagline: They're going to save the world... as long as they're home for dinner.
documents.overview: Jack Shepard is an out-of-shape auto shop owner, far removed from the man who once protected the world's freedom. Reluctantly called back into action by the government, Jack is tasked with turning a ragtag group of kids with special powers into a new generation of superheroes to save the world from certain destruction.
documents.plot:
Zoom, also released as Zoom: Academy for Superheroes, is a 2006 American superhero comedy directed by Peter Hewitt and loosely based on Jason Lethcoe's children's book Amazing Adventures from Zoom's Academy. Written by Adam Rifkin and David Berenbaum with contributions from star Tim Allen, it co-stars Courteney Cox, Chevy Chase, Spencer Breslin, Kevin Zegers and Rip Torn. Sony Pictures released it on August 11, 2006.

Thirty years earlier, the government-backed superhero team Team Zenith was led by the brothers Jack Shepard, known as Captain Zoom, and Connor, known as Concussion. When the military exposed them to experimental Gamma-13 radiation to boost their powers, Jack grew faster and stronger, but Connor became psychotic and killed their teammates. Jack apparently destroyed his brother by creating a vortex, losing his own powers in the process. In the present, the project's scientist Dr. Ed Grant discovers that Concussion was trapped in a dimensional rift and is about to return.

The military's General Larraby orders a new Team Zenith formed, enlisting the bitter, long-retired Jack as instructor and Marsha Holloway, a clumsy psychologist and devoted fan of the old team's comic books. After auditions, they recruit two teenagers, Dylan, who can turn invisible, and Summer, who has psionic powers, and two children, Tucker, who can inflate parts of his body, and Cindy, who has super-strength. Training goes badly at first: Jack is sarcastic and disengaged, Dylan keeps trying to escape and Tucker struggles with his confidence. After the recruits confront Jack about his failings, he reconciles with them, and the team begins to improve.

Hours before Concussion's return, Jack helps Dylan unlock a new power of "mindsight", which reveals where Concussion will appear and that the military plans to dose the children with Gamma-13 and use them as a diversion while testing new weapons. Horrified, Jack and Marsha, who reveals a super-breath ability of her own, take the team to the site. When Concussion deflects the military's net toward Cindy, Jack's powers return as he saves her. He recreates the vortex while the team steers Concussion into it, and the energy drains the radiation from both brothers, curing Concussion.

Zoom was a critical and commercial failure, scoring just 5% on Rotten Tomatoes and grossing about $12.5 million on a budget of about $75 million. It earned a Golden Raspberry nomination.

documents.title: You Got Served
documents.tagline: If you want respect, you've got to take it.
documents.overview: At Mr. Rad's Warehouse, the best hip-hop crews in Los Angeles compete for money and respect. But when a suburban crew crashes the party, stealing their dancers - and their moves - two warring friends have to pull together to represent the street. Starring hip-hop sensations Marques Houston, Omari Grandberry, Lil' Kim and comedian Steve Harvey.
documents.plot:
You Got Served is a 2004 dance film that revolves around the world of competitive breakdancing. The movie delves into the theme of perseverance and dedication, as the characters strive to perfect their craft and overcome obstacles to achieve success.

The film also explores the idea of identity and self-expression through dance. The main character, Cassie (played by Omar Epps), is a talented dancer who finds his passion in breakdancing, but struggles to balance his love for the art form with his desire to fit in with his peers.

Furthermore, You Got Served touches on the theme of rivalry and competition, as Cassie and his friend Eddie (played by Kenya Moore) engage in a series of dance battles against their opponents. This aspect of the movie highlights the importance of sportsmanship and respect for one's opponents, even in the face of intense competition.

Ultimately, the film suggests that success is not just about winning, but also about personal growth and self-discovery. Through Cassie's journey, the movie shows how embracing one's passion and working hard to achieve goals can lead to a sense of fulfillment and purpose.

documents.title: Bratz
documents.tagline: High school is about to get a make-over.
documents.overview: The popular Bratz dolls come to life in their first live-action feature film. Finding themselves being pulled further and further apart, the fashionable four band together to fight peer pressure, learn what it means to stand up for your friends, be true to oneself and live out your dreams.
documents.plot:
Bratz, also known as Bratz: The Movie, is a 2007 American teen comedy film based on MGA Entertainment's line of fashion dolls. Directed by Sean McNamara from a screenplay by Susan Estelle Jansen, based on a story by Adam de la Peña and David Eilenberg, it was the first live-action film based on the dolls. Nathalia Ramos, Skyler Shaye, Logan Browning and Janel Parrish star as the four friends, with Chelsea Staub, Lainie Kazan and Jon Voight in supporting roles.

Yasmin, Cloe, Sasha and Jade are four inseparable friends about to start high school together in Los Angeles. Their arrival is noticed by Meredith Baxter Dimly, the wealthy and controlling student body president and daughter of the school's principal, who insists that every student belong to a clique. Seeing the girls' independent spirit as a threat to her social order, Meredith sets out to divide them. Cloe, a soccer player, falls for a boy named Cameron; Sasha joins the cheerleading squad; Jade, a member of the science club, discovers a passion for fashion; and Yasmin, a talented singer too shy to perform in public, befriends Dylan, a popular jock who is deaf. Absorbed in their new activities and friends, the girls gradually drift apart.

Two years later, a food fight in the cafeteria, provoked when Meredith's dog attacks Cloe, lands the four in detention together, where they realize how much they miss one another. Reunited, they resolve to break down the barriers between the school's cliques and encourage students to mix freely. Meredith retaliates, and when the girls end up working at her extravagant "Super Sweet 16" party, she tries to humiliate Yasmin by revealing a video of her singing and dancing in secret. The plan backfires, and the party collapses into chaos, with Meredith ending up in her own cake and in the pool.

The girls then enter the school talent show, which Meredith has always won, competing for a scholarship. Meredith tries to blackmail them into withdrawing, but her scheme backfires when the students' secrets are revealed and the cliques come together instead. The girls perform an elaborate musical number, and although the contest ends in a tie, the scholarship goes to Cloe, and the friends are invited to a red carpet event.

Released by Lionsgate on August 3, 2007, Bratz was panned by critics, who criticized its shallow characters and mixed messages; it holds a 10% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 21. It grossed about $26 million worldwide.

documents.title: Captivity
documents.tagline: When You Think The Worst Has Happened... Think Worse
documents.overview: The sought-after images of top model Jennifer adorn magazine covers and billboards worldwide. When alone at a charity event, she is abducted and incarcerated in a cell with another prisoner. When their captor subjects the two to torture, they commit to escaping the chamber of horrors before they're killed.
documents.plot:
Captivity is a 2007 American thriller film directed by Chris Sivertson and starring Elisha Cuthbert and Michael Rapaport. The movie revolves around Heather Mason, a young girl who is being held captive by a mysterious figure known as "The Sculptor" (played by Michael Rapaport). As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Heather's captor has a twisted obsession with her, and she must use her wits to survive.

One of the main themes of Captivity is the exploration of trauma, captivity, and the psychological effects it can have on individuals. The film delves into the mind of "The Sculptor," revealing a complex web of emotions, desires, and motivations that drive his actions. Through Heather's character, the movie also examines the resilience and resourcefulness of a young girl forced to confront unimaginable horrors.

Another significant theme in Captivity is the concept of obsession and control. The Sculptor's fixation on Heather serves as a metaphor for the ways in which individuals can become consumed by their desires, often at the expense of others' well-being. This theme is further underscored by the film's portrayal of the power dynamics between captor and captive, highlighting the ways in which one person can exert control over another.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Heather struggles to come to terms with her past and her place in the world. Through her experiences, the film suggests that even in the darkest of circumstances, there is always the potential for growth, healing, and transformation.

Overall, Captivity is a thought-provoking thriller that explores complex themes and ideas through its gripping narrative and suspenseful plot.

documents.title: Catacombs
documents.tagline: Below the city of lights exists a world of darkness.
documents.overview: A young woman in Paris goes to a party in the enormous labyrinth of limestone tunnels beneath Paris. When she becomes separated from her friends, she is convinced something is chasing her through the dark tunnels.
documents.plot:
Catacombs is a 2007 American horror film directed by Tomm Coker and David Elliot, about a young woman trying to escape the Catacombs of Paris with a killer on her trail. The first original film from FEARnet, made in collaboration with Lions Gate Entertainment, it stars Shannyn Sossamon as Victoria and the singer Alecia Moore (Pink) as her sister Carolyn, with Mihai Stănescu as Jean-Michel, Emil Hoștină as Henry and Cabral Ibacka as Hugo. The score was composed by Yoshiki, whose theme song "Blue Butterfly" is performed by Violet UK.

Victoria, a young woman who suffers from crippling anxiety, accepts an invitation to visit her sister Carolyn in Paris. After a day of sightseeing and shopping, Carolyn takes her to a secret rave held that night deep in the catacombs, where they skip the long queue because Carolyn knows the bouncer, Hugo. When Victoria suffers an anxiety attack, the host, Jean-Michel, takes her to a private VIP area to join Carolyn and her friends, pours her a large glass of absinthe and tells her the legend of "Antichrist", a killer raised by a Satanic cult who lives in the tunnels and preys on people who get lost there. Most of the group laughs off the story and goes skinny dipping, but Victoria stays behind and loses her way back to the party. Carolyn joins her, only to be dragged off into the darkness, and soon Victoria finds her sister's body and is chased by a man in a goat mask. She escapes his lair and reaches the rave just as the police raid it, and in the stampede she is knocked unconscious. Waking alone, she meets Henry, a man who tries to help her, but every exit is blocked, and when he falls through a rotten walkway and hurts his leg, she abandons him with his map, only for him to attack her later. Terrified by someone trying to come in through an exit, she flees again and, hiding with a mining pick, strikes her pursuer blindly. Carolyn and her friends then appear and reveal that the entire ordeal was a prank meant to cure Victoria of her "issues", but the man she struck is Jean-Michel, now dead. When Carolyn turns on her, calling her a failure and saying she hates her, Victoria snaps and kills her sister and the others with the pick. She finally leaves the catacombs and takes a taxi back to the airport.

Exterior scenes were filmed in Paris, but most of the film was shot in Bucharest, Romania, on soundstage reconstructions of the catacombs, and it premiered on FEARnet On Demand in October 2007.

documents.title: Cinderella II: Dreams Come True
documents.overview: As a newly crowned princess, Cinderella quickly learns that life at the Palace - and her royal responsibilities - are more challenging than she had imagined. In three heartwarming tales, Cinderella calls on her animal friends and her Fairy Godmother to help as she brings her own grace and charm to her regal role and discovers that being true to yourself is the best way to make your dreams come true.
documents.plot:
Cinderella II: Dreams Come True is a direct-to-video animated film produced by Disney Television Animation, released in 2002. The movie serves as a sequel to the classic Disney fairy tale Cinderella.

The story begins with Cinderella (Cindy) living happily ever after with her Prince Charming and their two children, Jaq and Gus's descendants, but also with the help of her mice friends, Jaq and Gus. However, Cindy starts to feel like she is losing touch with her own identity and desires as a young woman.

Meanwhile, Lady Tremaine (Cinderella's evil stepmother) has grown old and frail, but still harbors resentment towards Cinderella for outsmarting her in the past. She plots to take revenge on Cindy by stealing the magical wand that gave her the power to transform into a beautiful princess.

As Cindy tries to find her place in the world, she meets a young woman named Perla, who is also searching for her own identity and sense of purpose. The two become fast friends and start to explore their passions and interests together.

However, Lady Tremaine's plan comes to fruition when she steals the magical wand, which Cindy had kept as a memento from her fairy godmother. With the wand in hand, Lady Tremaine sets out to ruin Cinderella's life once again.

Cindy and Perla team up to stop Lady Tremaine and retrieve the wand. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, perseverance, and believing in oneself. In the end, Cindy and her friends successfully defeat Lady Tremaine, and she is punished for her evil deeds.

The movie ends with Cinderella and Perla reflecting on their journey and realizing that true happiness comes from within. The film concludes with a heartwarming moment of Cindy and her family enjoying quality time together, surrounded by the magic of their own happily ever after.

Overall, Cinderella II: Dreams Come True is a charming and entertaining sequel that explores themes of identity, friendship, and self-discovery. While it may not be as iconic as its predecessor, the film remains a delightful addition to the Disney canon, offering a fresh perspective on the beloved Cinderella story.

documents.title: Main Hoon Na
documents.tagline: I am here.
documents.overview: An army major goes undercover as a college student. His mission is both professional and personal: to protect his general's daughter from a radical militant, and to find his estranged half-brother.
documents.plot:
Main Hoon Na is an Indian war drama film that explores the theme of patriotism and loyalty. The story revolves around Veer Pratap Singh, a young man who disguises himself as a British officer to infiltrate the enemy's camp and gather crucial information about the impending attack on India.

The movie delves into the idea of selfless sacrifice and bravery in the face of adversity. Veer's character embodies these qualities as he puts the needs of his country and its people above his own personal desires. His actions are motivated by a sense of duty and responsibility, which ultimately lead to the success of the mission.

The film also touches upon the theme of identity and belonging. Veer's dual identity as both an Indian and a British officer serves as a metaphor for the complexities of cultural heritage and national pride. The movie highlights the importance of embracing one's roots while also being open to new experiences and perspectives.

Furthermore, Main Hoon Na explores the idea of redemption and forgiveness. Veer's character is driven by a desire to make amends for past mistakes and to find redemption through his actions. The film suggests that it's never too late to make a positive change in one's life and to seek forgiveness from others.

Overall, Main Hoon Na is a movie that celebrates the values of patriotism, loyalty, and selflessness, while also exploring complex themes such as identity, redemption, and forgiveness.

documents.title: Black Water
documents.tagline: What you can't see can hurt you.
documents.overview: A trio of tourists on a fishing trip in the mangrove swamps of Northern Australia are left to fend for themselves when their tour guide is killed by a crocodile.
documents.plot:
Black Water is a 2007 Australian psychological thriller film directed by Andrew Traucki. The movie revolves around a young woman named Sarah who goes on a solo diving trip in the Great Barrier Reef, but her adventure takes a dark turn when she encounters a massive saltwater crocodile.

The main theme of Black Water is the struggle for survival and the human will to live against all odds. The film showcases Sarah's determination to escape from the deadly creature that has taken her on a perilous journey through the treacherous waters of the Great Barrier Reef. As Sarah navigates through the unforgiving environment, she must confront her own fears and limitations in order to stay alive.

The movie also explores the theme of isolation and loneliness. Sarah's solo diving trip serves as a metaphor for her emotional state, where she is disconnected from the world around her. The film highlights how this sense of isolation can amplify one's fears and vulnerabilities, making it even more challenging to survive in the face of danger.

Furthermore, Black Water touches on the theme of primal fear and the human psyche's response to threats. The massive saltwater crocodile serves as a symbol of primal terror, representing an unstoppable force that tests Sarah's resolve and pushes her to confront her deepest fears. As the film progresses, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the physical danger posed by the crocodile but also in the psychological toll it takes on Sarah.

Overall, Black Water is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of survival, isolation, primal fear, and the human psyche's response to threats.

documents.title: Timecrimes
documents.tagline: A trip back in time from the present to...
documents.overview: A man accidentally gets into a time machine and travels back in time nearly an hour. Finding himself will be the first of a series of disasters of unforeseeable consequences.
documents.plot:
Timecrimes is a Spanish science fiction thriller film that delves into the complexities of time travel and its consequences on human relationships. The movie follows Héctor, a young man who becomes embroiled in a series of events after he encounters a mysterious woman with whom he shares a brief but intense connection.

As Héctor navigates his way through this complex web of time, he begins to question the nature of reality and his own identity. He finds himself reliving the same day over and over again, each iteration bringing new challenges and opportunities for growth. Through Héctor's experiences, the film explores themes of repetition, free will, and the consequences of playing with the fabric of time.

One of the primary concerns of Timecrimes is the idea that our actions have unintended repercussions, and that even the smallest decisions can have far-reaching effects on those around us. As Héctor struggles to make sense of his situation, he must confront the possibility that his interactions with others may be influenced by events that have not yet occurred.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness and isolation, as Héctor's experiences leave him feeling disconnected from the world around him. His relationships with others are marked by a sense of urgency and desperation, as if he is racing against time to make amends or find connection in a world that seems determined to keep him at arm's length.

Ultimately, Timecrimes presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that raises questions about the nature of time, identity, and our place within the world. Through its complex narrative and atmospheric tension, the film invites viewers to consider the consequences of playing with the fundamental forces of reality.

documents.title: Daddy Day Camp
documents.tagline: The summer is going to be in tents.
documents.overview: Seeking to offer his son the satisfying summer camp experience that eluded him as a child, the operator of a neighborhood daycare center opens his own camp, only to face financial hardship and stiff competition from a rival camp.
documents.plot:
Daddy Day Camp is a 2007 American comedy film directed by Dean Parisot and starring Eddie Murphy, Jeff Garlin, and Anjelica Huston.

The movie revolves around Charlie Hinton (Eddie Murphy), an ex-boy scout who returns to his alma mater as the new director of the local day camp. As he tries to reconnect with his estranged son, Max (Logan Lerman), Charlie must confront his own past mistakes and learn to be a better father.

The main theme of Daddy Day Camp is the importance of redemption and second chances. Charlie's journey is one of self-discovery and growth, as he works to repair his relationship with Max and make amends for past errors. Through his experiences at the day camp, Charlie learns valuable lessons about leadership, teamwork, and the importance of following your heart.

The film also explores themes of family, forgiveness, and the challenges of modern parenting. As Charlie navigates the complexities of contemporary fatherhood, he must confront his own biases and assumptions in order to connect with Max on a deeper level.

Ultimately, Daddy Day Camp is a heartwarming story about the power of love, redemption, and the transformative impact that one person can have on another's life.

documents.title: Up
documents.overview: Carl Fredricksen spent his entire life dreaming of exploring the globe and experiencing life to its fullest. But at age 78, life seems to have passed him by, until a twist of fate (and a persistent 8-year old Wilderness Explorer named Russell) gives him a new lease on life.
documents.plot:
Up is a heartwarming animated adventure film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and directed by Pete Docter. Released in 2009, the movie follows the story of Carl Fredricksen, an elderly widower who sets out to fulfill his lifelong dream of exploring South America.

The film begins with Carl (voiced by Edward Asner) living a mundane life in Paradise Falls, Peru, where he has lived for over 50 years. He is still grieving the loss of his wife, Ellie, who passed away five years ago. The two had shared a deep love for adventure and exploration, but their dreams were put on hold due to financial constraints.

As Carl's health begins to decline, he decides that it's time to fulfill his lifelong dream of exploring South America by tying thousands of balloons to his house and taking off into the sky. Unbeknownst to Carl, a young Wilderness Explorer named Russell (voiced by Jordan Nagai) is on his porch, trying to earn his final badge by assisting the elderly.

As the house soars into the air, Carl and Russell form an unlikely friendship, bonding over their shared love of adventure and exploration. Along the way, they encounter a series of obstacles, including treacherous storms, treacherous terrain, and a group of ruthless loggers who are determined to destroy Paradise Falls.

Throughout their journey, Carl and Russell learn valuable lessons about life, loss, and the importance of following your dreams. They also discover that Ellie's spirit is still with them, guiding them on their adventure.

As they near their destination, Carl and Russell face a final challenge: navigating the treacherous terrain of South America to reach Paradise Falls. In a thrilling climax, they successfully land in the falls, where Carl finally finds closure and a sense of fulfillment.

The film ends with Carl and Russell standing together, looking out at the breathtaking beauty of Paradise Falls. Carl has found a new sense of purpose and meaning in life, thanks to his adventure with Russell. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, as Carl and Ellie's love story is finally brought full circle.

Overall, Up is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of love, loss, and the power of following your dreams. With stunning animation, lovable characters, and a heartwarming story, it's no wonder that Up became one of Pixar's most beloved films.

documents.tagline: We Were Warned.
documents.overview: Dr. Adrian Helmsley, part of a worldwide geophysical team investigating the effect on the earth of radiation from unprecedented solar storms, learns that the earth's core is heating up. He warns U.S. President Thomas Wilson that the crust of the earth is becoming unstable and that without proper preparations for saving a fraction of the world's population, the entire race is doomed. Meanwhile, writer Jackson Curtis stumbles on the same information. While the world's leaders race to build "arks" to escape the impending cataclysm, Curtis struggles to find a way to save his family. Meanwhile, volcanic eruptions and earthquakes of unprecedented strength wreak havoc around the world.
documents.plot:
2012 is an American disaster film of 2009 directed by Roland Emmerich, who wrote it with Harald Kloser, inspired by the 2012 doomsday phenomenon. John Cusack stars as the struggling novelist Jackson Curtis and Chiwetel Ejiofor as the geologist Adrian Helmsley, with Amanda Peet as Jackson's former wife Kate, Oliver Platt as White House chief of staff Carl Anheuser, Thandie Newton as Laura Wilson, Danny Glover as President Thomas Wilson and Woody Harrelson as the conspiracy theorist Charlie Frost.

In 2009, Adrian learns from an astrophysicist in India that neutrinos from a solar flare are heating the Earth's core, and he warns the White House. The G8 and China begin building giant arks in Tibet, secretly funding them in part by selling places to the very rich for a billion euros each. By 2012, Jackson works as a limousine driver for the Russian billionaire Yuri Karpov. On a camping trip to Yellowstone with his children, Noah and Lilly, he finds the lake dried up and meets Charlie, a radio host who claims that the world is about to end and that governments are hiding it. Convinced after a string of warning signs, Jackson rents a small plane and rescues Kate, the children and her boyfriend Gordon just as a colossal earthquake sends California into the Pacific.

The group flies to Yellowstone to retrieve Charlie's map of the arks as the caldera erupts and kills him, then join the Karpovs aboard a huge Antonov cargo jet piloted by Sasha and Gordon. As the Earth's crust shifts, billions die, including President Wilson, who stayed in Washington. The Antonov crash-lands in the Himalayas, killing Sasha, and only the ticket-holding Karpovs are flown away. A Tibetan family helps the Curtises stow away on Ark 4. When a megatsunami approaches, Adrian persuades the world leaders to open the gates to the stranded crowds; Yuri dies saving his sons and Gordon is crushed. A tool jammed in the gate floods the ark and sends it drifting towards Mount Everest until Jackson and Noah dislodge it. Weeks later the arks head for the Cape of Good Hope, where the Drakensberg are now the world's highest mountains, and Jackson reconciles with Kate.

Shot in Vancouver in 2008, the film opened on 13 November 2009 and grossed $791.2 million worldwide against a $200 million budget, one of the top earners of the year. Critics praised the spectacle but not the script, giving it 40% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Roger Ebert awarded it three and a half stars.

documents.title: Dragonball Evolution
documents.tagline: The legend comes to life.
documents.overview: On his 18th birthday, Goku receives a mystical Dragonball as a gift from his grandfather. There are only six others like it in the whole world, and legend has it that whoever possesses all seven will be granted one perfect wish. When the arrival of a dark force triggers a tragedy, Goku and his companions are propelled into an epic quest to collect the seven Dragonballs and save the Earth from destruction.
documents.plot:
Dragonball Evolution is a 2009 American fantasy action film based on Akira Toriyama's manga series Dragon Ball. Directed by James Wong from a screenplay by Ben Ramsey and produced by Stephen Chow, it stars Justin Chatwin as Goku, Chow Yun-fat as Master Roshi, Emmy Rossum as Bulma, Jamie Chung as Chi-Chi, James Marsters as King Piccolo, Joon Park as Yamcha, and Eriko Tamura as Piccolo's henchwoman Mai. The film was distributed by 20th Century Fox.

Two thousand years before the story begins, the Namekian warlord Piccolo came to Earth and devastated it, until seven mystics sealed him away with a powerful spell called the Mafuba. In the present day he escapes and, with the help of the ninja-like Mai, begins to search for the seven Dragonballs, which when gathered can summon a dragon to grant a wish. On his eighteenth birthday, Goku, a high school student and secretly a trained martial artist, receives the four-star Dragonball from his grandfather Gohan. Returning home from a party hosted by Chi-Chi, the girl he likes, Goku finds his house destroyed by Piccolo, and his dying grandfather urges him to find the martial arts master Roshi, who holds another Dragonball.

Goku meets Bulma, a scientist from the Capsule Corporation who has invented a device that can locate the Dragonballs, and the two agree to help each other. They find Roshi, who joins the quest and trains Goku to harness his ki, or life energy. In the desert they fall into a trap laid by the bandit Yamcha, who agrees to join them in exchange for a share of the profits from Bulma's invention. Together, they fend off attacks by Mai while racing to collect the remaining Dragonballs before a solar eclipse, when Piccolo plans to unleash Ōzaru, a monstrous creature connected to Goku's mysterious origins. Goku must learn the truth about who he is and decide whether he can control his own destiny.

The film reimagines the manga as a teen action story set in a contemporary American high school, a decision that departed significantly from the source material.

Dragonball Evolution was a critical and commercial failure, widely criticised by reviewers and fans for its script, casting and lack of fidelity to the manga, and it is often ranked among the worst adaptations of anime or manga. Screenwriter Ben Ramsey later publicly apologised to fans for his work on the film.

documents.title: Home of the Brave
documents.tagline: The final test of courage is coming home.
documents.overview: The day after they get the word they'll go home in two weeks, a group of soldiers from Spokane are ambushed in an Iraqi city. Back stateside we follow four of them - a surgeon who saw too much, a teacher who's a single mom and who lost a hand in the ambush, an infantry man whose best friend died that day, and a soldier who keeps reliving the moment he killed a civilian woman.
documents.plot:
Home of the Brave is a 2006 American war drama directed by Irwin Winkler that follows four Army National Guard soldiers through a final mission in Iraq and their difficult return to Spokane, Washington. The cast includes Samuel L. Jackson, Jessica Biel, Brian Presley, Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson, Chad Michael Murray, Christina Ricci and Victoria Rowell, and it was filmed in Ouarzazate, Morocco, and in Spokane.

Days before their unit is to rotate home, physician Lieutenant Colonel William Marsh, Sergeant Vanessa Price, Specialists Tommy Yates and Jamal Aiken, and Private Jordan Owens join a convoy carrying medical supplies to a remote Iraqi village. Insurgents ambush it in a narrow street, and a detour leads into a roadside bomb that kills Price's passenger and badly wounds her. Aiken hurts his back in the fighting, Yates is wounded, and Owens is shot from behind while chasing a sniper, dying in Yates's arms. Price loses her right hand, and the survivors return to the United States.

Back in Spokane, each struggles. Price tries to resume work as a physical education teacher and basketball coach while adjusting to a rubber prosthesis. Yates has lost his gun-shop job, and pushed by his father toward the police academy, he walks out of the entrance exam, shaken by Aiken's fate. Aiken, denied veterans' benefits for his back injury and rejected by his girlfriend, takes her and her co-workers hostage at a drive-through coffee stand and is killed by police. Marsh drinks heavily as his son, angry at the war's toll on the family, acts out at school; after he brings three yard workers home for Thanksgiving dinner, his wife finds him with a loaded pistol, contemplating suicide. In therapy for PTSD he admits he feels nothing for the soldiers who died and believes that, as a doctor, he should, and his wife promises to stand by him. Price finds love with a fellow coach she had earlier rebuffed, and the families become friends, while Yates, after an outburst at his father's shop, re-enlists and is last seen patrolling an Iraqi city.

Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer opened the film in three theaters in December 2006 for awards consideration and re-released it in May 2007, but it earned about $500,000 worldwide. Reviews were poor, with 23% on Rotten Tomatoes and 42 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Valiant
documents.tagline: Featherweight Heroes.
documents.overview: Set in 1944, Valiant is a woodland pigeon who wants to become a great hero someday. When he hears they are hiring recruits for the Royal Homing Pigeon Service, he immediately sets out for London. On the way, he meets a smelly but friendly pigeon named Bugsy, who joins him, mainly to get away from clients he cheated in a game of find-the pebble, and helps him sign up for the war.
documents.plot:
Valiant is a 2005 animated action-adventure film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Valiant, a young pigeon who dreams of becoming a spy and joining the elite Flock of Sparrowhawks.

The main themes of Valiant include:

1. **Perseverance and determination**: Valiant faces numerous challenges and setbacks throughout his journey, but he never gives up on his dream of becoming a spy. His perseverance ultimately leads him to achieve his goal.
2. **Loyalty and friendship**: Valiant forms strong bonds with his fellow pigeons, particularly Archer and Bugsy, who become his allies in the fight against the evil rat, General Shen. Their loyalty and trust in each other are crucial to their success.
3. **Self-discovery and identity**: As Valiant navigates the world of espionage, he learns more about himself and his place within the Flock of Sparrowhawks. He discovers that being different is not a weakness, but rather a strength that can be leveraged to achieve great things.
4. **Good vs. evil**: The movie features an epic battle between good (the Flock of Sparrowhawks) and evil (General Shen's rat army). Valiant's bravery and cunning ultimately lead to the defeat of the enemy forces.

The film also explores themes of:

* **Growing up and maturity**: Valiant learns valuable lessons about responsibility, courage, and leadership as he takes on more significant roles within the Flock.
* **Teamwork and collaboration**: The movie highlights the importance of working together towards a common goal, as the pigeons use their unique skills to outsmart and defeat their enemies.

Overall, Valiant is an inspiring tale of self-discovery, perseverance, and loyalty, with a healthy dose of action, adventure, and humor.

documents.title: Beauty Shop
documents.tagline: A Cut Above
documents.overview: Far from Chicago, hairdresser Gina Norris has relocated to Atlanta with her daughter and has quickly established herself as a rare talent in her profession. But after repeatedly butting heads with her shady, over-the-top boss, Jorge, Norris sets out to create her own salon -- even snagging a few of Jorge's employees and clients. Now, Jorge will do anything to shut her down.
documents.plot:
Beauty Shop is a 2005 American comedy film that revolves around the life of Gina, a young woman who leaves her small town to pursue a career in beauty and fashion. The movie explores themes of self-discovery, empowerment, and the struggle for independence.

At its core, Beauty Shop is a story about Gina's journey towards finding her own identity and purpose in life. She navigates through various challenges and experiences that shape her into a stronger and more confident individual. Through her relationships with other characters, particularly her friends and colleagues at the beauty shop, Gina learns valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

The film also touches on themes of female empowerment and the struggle for women's independence in a male-dominated industry. Gina faces numerous obstacles as she tries to establish herself in the competitive world of beauty and fashion, but ultimately emerges as a confident and successful individual.

Overall, Beauty Shop is a heartwarming and uplifting film that celebrates the power of self-discovery and female empowerment.

documents.title: Aquamarine
documents.tagline: A Fish-Out-Of-Water Comedy.
documents.overview: Two teenage girls discover that mermaids really do exist after a violent storm washes one ashore. The mermaid, a sassy creature named Aquamarine, is determined to prove to her father that real love exists, and enlists the girls' help in winning the heart of a handsome lifeguard.
documents.plot:
Aquamarine is a 2006 American fantasy romantic comedy film directed by Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum and written by Karen McCullah Lutz and Kirsten Smith. The movie stars Sara Paxton, Emma Roberts, and JoJo.

The story revolves around two teenage girls, Hailey (Sara Paxton) and Claire (Emma Roberts), who are best friends since childhood. They live in a small town in Florida, where they spend their days lounging on the beach and dreaming of adventure. However, their lives take an unexpected turn when they discover that a mermaid named Aquamarine (JoJo) has washed up on the shore.

Aquamarine is a beautiful but troubled young woman who was once a princess from a magical kingdom under the sea. She was banished by her evil stepmother and forced to live in the human world, where she struggles to adapt to modern life. Hailey and Claire are initially hesitant to help Aquamarine, but they soon become her unlikely friends.

As Aquamarine navigates her new surroundings, she begins to fall for a high school student named Han (Jake McDorman), who is immediately smitten with her. However, their budding romance is threatened when Aquamarine's evil stepmother, Ursula (Kirsten Dunst), returns from the sea and seeks revenge against Hailey and Claire.

Ursula has been searching for Aquamarine, intending to use her magical powers to take over the world. She manipulates Han into helping her capture Aquamarine, but Hailey and Claire intervene, using their own unique skills to outsmart Ursula and save their friend.

Throughout the movie, Hailey and Claire learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and believing in themselves. They also discover that they have more in common with Aquamarine than they initially thought, as they all share a deep sense of longing for adventure and connection.

In the end, Aquamarine is able to defeat Ursula and reclaim her rightful place on the throne of her underwater kingdom. Hailey and Claire are hailed as heroes, and they finally get their chance to experience the magic and wonder of the ocean world that Aquamarine introduced them to.

The movie features a mix of humor, adventure, and heartwarming moments, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Dhoom 2
documents.tagline: Back in Action
documents.overview: Jai and Ali return, this time on the trail of an international thief who steals priceless artifacts and has chosen Mumbai as his next target.
documents.plot:
Dhoom 2 is an action-packed heist film that delves into the world of high-stakes crime and deception. At its core, the movie explores the theme of greed and its corrupting influence on individuals. The main character, Jai (played by Abhishek Bachchan), is a man driven by his desire to bring down the villainous Aamir (played by Hrithik Roshan) and his accomplices.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that greed is not just about material wealth but also about power and control. The characters in the movie are willing to go to great lengths to achieve their goals, often sacrificing their morals and values in the process. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the film.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and how it can be manipulated for personal gain. Aamir's character, in particular, is a master of disguise and deception, using his charm and wit to manipulate those around him. This theme serves as a commentary on the superficiality of modern society, where people are often more concerned with appearances than substance.

Furthermore, Dhoom 2 explores the concept of loyalty and betrayal, highlighting the blurred lines between right and wrong in the world of crime. The film's climax is particularly noteworthy for its thought-provoking portrayal of these themes, leaving the audience to ponder the true nature of morality and the consequences of one's actions.

Overall, Dhoom 2 is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, making it a compelling watch for fans of action-packed heist films.

documents.title: The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl
documents.original_title: The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl
documents.tagline: Smaller heroes. Just as super.
documents.overview: Everyone always knew that Max had a wild imagination, but no one believed that his wildest creations -- a boy raised by watchful great white sharks and a girl with the force of a volcano -- were real. Now, these two pint-sized action masters will show Max that even an ordinary kid has what it takes to be extraordinary.
documents.plot:
The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl (marketed as The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl in 3-D) is a 2005 American superhero film co-written, edited, shot and directed by Robert Rodriguez. It stars Cayden Boyd as Max and Taylor Lautner as Sharkboy, with Taylor Dooley, David Arquette, Kristin Davis and George Lopez. Many of its ideas came from Rodriguez's children, especially his son Racer Max.

Max is a lonely ten-year-old in suburban Austin who records his dreams of an imaginary world called Planet Drool in a journal. Among his creations are two young superheroes, Sharkboy and Lavagirl. In real life, Max is bullied by his classmate Linus and worried by his parents' troubled marriage. After Linus steals and defaces his dream journal, Sharkboy and Lavagirl suddenly appear in his classroom and take him to Planet Drool, which is being corrupted by Mr. Electric, a villain based on Max's eccentric teacher, Mr. Electricidad.

On their journey to save Drool, the trio bond but are trapped by Mr. Electric in the Dream Graveyard, where forgotten dreams lie. Guided by Tobor, a robot toy Max abandoned, they set out to obtain the Crystal Heart, held by Lavagirl's rival the Ice Princess, which can freeze time and halt the spreading darkness. They are captured by Minus, the mastermind behind Mr. Electric, who turns out to be Linus, having entered Drool through Max's journal and filled it with his own dark dreams. After escaping and securing the Crystal Heart, the heroes are ambushed again, and Lavagirl sacrifices herself to save Sharkboy. Setting aside his selfish dreams, Max becomes the all-powerful Daydreamer, sends Sharkboy to revive Lavagirl, defeats Linus and offers to build a better dream world with him. Linus agrees, but Mr. Electric flees to Earth to kill Max in his sleep, attacking the school with an artificial tornado. While Sharkboy and Lavagirl rescue Max's parents, who reconcile, Max gives the Crystal Heart to his classmate Marissa, the model for the Ice Princess, who freezes and destroys Mr. Electric. Sharkboy becomes King of the Ocean and Lavagirl Queen of Earth's volcanoes, while Max, now friends with Marissa and Linus, urges everyone to dream a better dream and work to make it real.

Released by Dimension Films on June 10, 2005, the film opened fifth at the box office and grossed about $72 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative, judging the 3-D conversion a miscalculation; Rotten Tomatoes reported 19% approval and Metacritic a score of 38.

documents.title: The Painted Veil
documents.tagline: Sometimes the greatest journey is the distance between two people.
documents.overview: A British medical doctor fights a cholera outbreak in a small Chinese village, while also being trapped at home in a loveless marriage to an unfaithful wife.
documents.plot:
The Painted Veil is a 2006 drama film directed by John Curran from a screenplay by Ron Nyswaner, based on W. Somerset Maugham's 1925 novel of the same title. Naomi Watts, Edward Norton, Toby Jones, Anthony Wong Chau Sang and Liev Schreiber appear in the leading roles. It is the third screen version of the novel, after films in 1934 and 1957.

In London in the early 1920s, the earnest bacteriologist Walter Fane is captivated by the socialite Kitty Garstin and proposes. Eager to escape her mother, Kitty accepts, and after a honeymoon in Venice, where she shows little interest in his love of the city's canals and museums, the mismatched couple travel to Shanghai, where Walter studies infectious diseases at a government laboratory. Kitty prefers the parties and gossip of British expatriate society and begins a passionate secret affair with Charles Townsend, a married British vice consul. Walter discovers it and, having volunteered to fight a cholera epidemic in a remote part of China, insists that Kitty come with him or face a divorce, which he will grant quietly only if Townsend leaves his wife Dorothy to marry her. As Walter expected, Townsend will not commit, and Kitty is forced on a gruelling two-week overland journey to the mountain village of Mei-tan-fu, a route Walter chose to make her suffer. Living in a shabby house outside town, she is lonely and barely speaks with her husband. Their neighbour Waddington, a British deputy commissioner, tells her that Townsend is a womanizer, and she keeps back a desperate letter to him. Kitty begins volunteering at an orphanage run by French nuns, and through the work and what the nuns tell her of Walter's courage and devotion, she outgrows her self-absorption, while he sees she is no longer the shallow woman he married. Their marriage blossoms, and when Kitty becomes pregnant without knowing who the father is, Walter tells her it does not matter. As his clean-water aqueducts bring the epidemic under control, infected refugees arrive, and Walter catches cholera and dies despite Kitty's care. Five years later in London, Kitty is out with her young son, also named Walter, when they meet Townsend, and she rejects his advances.

Shot largely in Guangxi, China, the film opened in a limited American release in December 2006 and grossed about $26.9 million worldwide. It holds a 74% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and Alexandre Desplat's score won the Golden Globe for Best Original Score.

documents.title: The Librarian: Quest for the Spear
documents.original_title: The Librarian: Quest for the Spear
documents.overview: When a magical artifact is lifted from his library, a meek librarian sets out to ensure its safe return.
documents.plot:
The Librarian: Quest for the Spear is an action-adventure comedy film that follows the story of Flynn Carsen, a bookish librarian who discovers he's the chosen one to find the Holy Grail. As Flynn navigates through ancient temples and battles treacherous rivals, he must confront his own identity and purpose.

At its core, The Librarian: Quest for the Spear explores themes of self-discovery and empowerment. Flynn, initially portrayed as an awkward and introverted librarian, embarks on a journey that forces him to tap into his inner strength and confidence. Through his adventures, he learns to balance his bookish nature with his newfound bravery and wit.

The film also delves into the idea of destiny and the power of one's passions. Flynn's quest for the Holy Grail is not just about retrieving an ancient artifact but also about fulfilling his own potential. As he navigates through treacherous landscapes, he must confront the notion that his true calling may lie beyond the confines of his mundane life as a librarian.

Furthermore, The Librarian: Quest for the Spear touches on the theme of friendship and camaraderie. Flynn's relationships with his allies, including Eve and Jenkins, serve as a source of support and encouragement as he navigates the challenges of his quest. Together, they form an unlikely team that proves that even the most disparate individuals can come together to achieve greatness.

Ultimately, The Librarian: Quest for the Spear is a heartwarming tale about embracing one's true potential and finding purpose in life. With its blend of action, humor, and adventure, the film offers a thrilling ride that will keep audiences entertained from start to finish.

documents.title: The Librarian: Return to King Solomon's Mines
documents.original_title: The Librarian: Return to King Solomon's Mines
documents.overview: After retrieving the Crystal Skull in Utah, Flynn Carsen receives a map in the mail with the secret location of King Solomon's Mines. When the scroll is stolen, Judson explains the power of the Key of Solomon's book and assigns Flynn to retrieve the map. The map is useless without the legend piece to decipher it, which is located in Volubilis near the Roman ruins in Morocco. Flynn heads to Casablanca to the ruins where he is chased by a group of mercenaries leaded by General Samir. They too want to find the location of King Solomon's mines. Flynn teams-up with Professor Emily Davenport working in the dig and they escape from General Samir and his men. While traveling to Gedi, they save the local Jomo from death and the trio faces a dangerous journey through the wild Africa.
documents.plot:
The Librarian: Return to King Solomon's Mines is an action-adventure film that delves into the realm of ancient mythology and treasure hunting. At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession and the unrelenting pursuit of knowledge and power.

The protagonist, Flynn Carsen (played by Noah Wyle), is a modern-day librarian who finds himself entangled in a world of adventure and danger. His quest for the legendary mines of King Solomon becomes an all-consuming passion that drives him to risk everything. As he navigates treacherous landscapes and battles formidable foes, Flynn's obsession with uncovering the secrets of the mines serves as a catalyst for his personal growth.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. Throughout his journey, Flynn is forced to confront his own limitations and vulnerabilities, ultimately emerging stronger and more confident. His experiences in the mines serve as a metaphor for the transformative power of knowledge and the importance of embracing one's true nature.

Furthermore, the movie alludes to the idea that power and knowledge can be corrupting forces when left unchecked. The villainous character, Dr. Julia Jones (played by Rebecca Romijn), represents the dangers of ambition and the exploitation of ancient wisdom for personal gain. Her character serves as a foil to Flynn's more noble motivations, highlighting the importance of using one's discoveries for the greater good.

Overall, The Librarian: Return to King Solomon's Mines is a thrilling adventure that explores the complexities of human nature, the allure of power and knowledge, and the transformative potential of self-discovery.

documents.title: Prey
documents.tagline: Out here, you're the endangered species...
documents.overview: An American family on holiday in Africa becomes lost in a game reserve and stalked by vicious killer lions.
documents.plot:
Prey is a 2007 South African adventure horror thriller film directed by Darrell Roodt and written by Roodt, Jeff Wadlow and Beau Bauman. Bridget Moynahan stars as a woman who, along with her two stepchildren, is trapped in a car by a pride of man-eating lions on a South African game reserve, with Peter Weller as her husband, Carly Schroeder and Conner Dowds as the children, and Jamie Bartlett as a professional hunter. It was filmed on location in Gauteng and Limpopo provinces.

Tom Newman, an American hydroelectric engineer hired to help build a dam in South Africa, arrives at a safari resort with his new wife, Amy, his teenage daughter, Jessica, and his young son, David. He hopes the trip will bring Amy and Jessica closer, as Jessica resents her stepmother and blames her for her parents' divorce. While Tom is at work, Amy and the children go on a game drive with a ranger, Brian. During a stop in the bush, Brian is attacked and killed by lions, taking the car keys with him, and Amy and the children are left trapped in the vehicle as the pride circles it. When they fail to return, Tom enlists Crawford, an experienced hunter and guide, to search for them, as park rangers begin an aerial search.

David spots the keys, and Amy manages to retrieve them, narrowly escaping a lioness, but in her panic she drives deeper into the bush and wrecks the car. A helicopter flies overhead without seeing them. When Jessica leaves the car to signal it and Amy goes after her, they are saved from a charging lioness by two local hunters, but both men are later killed by the lions. Rain wipes out the car's tracks, frustrating Tom and Crawford. Through the long night in the car, Amy tells Jessica how she met her father, assuring her that her parents had already separated at the time, and the two finally reconcile.

The next morning, Amy attracts the attention of Tom and Crawford. Crawford saves Tom by shooting a lioness but is then killed by the male lion, and Tom takes refuge under the car. Amy rigs the fuel tank with a cloth fuse, lures the lion into the car while the others run to a tree, and kills it in the explosion. The reunited family walks back to Crawford's vehicle together.

Prey premiered at the American Film Market in November 2006 and was released on DVD in the United States by The Weinstein Company in January 2007, followed by a European DVD release from Sony Pictures Home Entertainment later that year.

documents.title: Restraint
documents.tagline: Seclusion. Seduction. Survival.
documents.overview: Two fugitives land in hot water when they take a hostage who poses a threat to their well-being.
documents.plot:
Restraint is a 2008 Australian thriller directed by David Denneen and written by Dave Warner. Teresa Palmer and Travis Fimmel star as Dale and Ron, a pair of fugitives, and Stephen Moyer plays Andrew Shepard, the reclusive estate owner they take hostage; Vanessa Redgrave makes a cameo.

Before the story opens, Ron has killed Dale's boss, the owner of a strip club. On the run, the couple murder a gas station attendant who notices the body in their car's trunk. They stumble upon Andrew's grand country estate and decide to hide there until the manhunt dies down. Andrew is an agoraphobic art dealer. The volatile Ron abuses him and threatens to kill him until Dale intervenes. Andrew offers them 40,000 Australian dollars and valuable jewelry to help them escape, but someone must collect them from the bank, so he proposes that Dale go in the guise of his fiancée, Gabrielle. Dale twice visits the bank without arousing suspicion.

Meanwhile Andrew tells Ron that Gabrielle left him after an affair with his father, who paid her to go, and that he then hired a hit man to kill his father. To save his own life, Andrew offers Ron a photograph proving the murder as leverage, and while supposedly fetching it, he locks Ron in the cellar, but Ron escapes and takes control again. When Dale returns, partly seduced by Andrew and his way of life, she turns their shotgun on Ron as he moves to kill Andrew, not realizing that it is unloaded. Ron knocks her out and leaves her in a locked car filling with exhaust fumes, taunting Andrew to overcome his agoraphobia to save her. Andrew rescues her and wounds Ron, and the revived Dale finishes Ron off. When Andrew reaches for the phone to call the police, Dale stops him by resuming her role as Gabrielle and, at his prompting, tells him in Gabrielle's voice that she loves him, and they sleep together. Asked what would happen if Gabrielle came back, Andrew assures Dale that she is gone as he burns Gabrielle's passport, suggesting he may have killed her. Later he plays Wagner alone downstairs in apparent triumph while Dale gazes sadly from an upstairs window.

More than half the budget came from the Film Finance Corporation, and the film was shot in 2005 near Goulburn and Camden in New South Wales. Planned for release by Accent Entertainment in May 2006, it was cut from 120 to 90 minutes after several test screenings, which also led to a more ambiguous ending. It eventually played in a single Sydney cinema in April 2009.

documents.title: Wind Chill
documents.tagline: There Are Worse Things Than Dying
documents.overview: Two college students share a ride home for the holidays. When they break down on a deserted stretch of road, they're preyed upon by the ghosts of people who have died there.
documents.plot:
Wind Chill is a psychological thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the effects of isolation on the human psyche. The movie follows two college students, Katie and Ben, who embark on a road trip to retrieve Katie's car from her estranged father in rural Minnesota.

As they navigate through the treacherous winter landscape, their relationship is put to the test, and they begin to experience strange and terrifying occurrences that blur the lines between reality and paranoia. The film masterfully builds tension by exploiting the characters' deep-seated fears and insecurities, creating an atmosphere of creeping dread that permeates every aspect of their journey.

At its core, Wind Chill explores the theme of vulnerability and how it can be exploited by those who seek to manipulate or harm others. Katie and Ben's relationship is built on a foundation of trust and mutual support, but as they face the harsh realities of their situation, they are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and weaknesses.

The film also touches on the idea of isolation and how it can affect people in different ways. The rural setting serves as a character in its own right, with the vast expanse of snow-covered landscape seeming to close in on the characters like a vise. This sense of claustrophobia heightens the tension and creates an atmosphere of unease that is both unsettling and captivating.

Ultimately, Wind Chill is a film about the fragility of human relationships and the ways in which our deepest fears can be used against us. It's a gripping and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

documents.title: Igor
documents.tagline: All men aren't created Evil.
documents.overview: A cliché hunchbacked evil scientist's assistant aspires to become a scientist himself, much to the displeasure of the rest of the evil science community.
documents.plot:
Igor is a 2008 stop-motion animated comedy film directed by Terry Gilliam and produced by Exodus Film Group. The movie tells the story of Igor, a lovable but awkward assistant to the mad scientist Dr. Frankenstein.

The film begins with Igor (voiced by John Cusack) living in his small village, where he dreams of becoming a great scientist like his idol, Dr. Frankenstein. However, Igor's attempts at science are consistently thwarted by his own ineptitude and the ridicule of the villagers. Despite this, Igor remains determined to prove himself.

One day, Igor receives an offer from Dr. Frankenstein (voiced by John Cleese) to become his assistant in his castle laboratory. Igor is overjoyed at the opportunity and sets off for the castle, where he meets Dr. Frankenstein's other assistant, Eugene (voiced by Chris Miller). The two assistants quickly become fast friends and begin working on various projects with Dr. Frankenstein.

As Igor becomes more confident in his abilities, he begins to take on more responsibility within the laboratory. However, his enthusiasm often gets the better of him, leading to chaotic and disastrous consequences.
