Despite this, Dr. Frankenstein remains patient and supportive, encouraging Igor to pursue his dreams.

Meanwhile, a rival scientist, Dr. Vortex (voiced by Will Arnett), is also working on creating life. However, his methods are far more sinister than Dr. Frankenstein's, and he will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

As the story unfolds, Igor becomes increasingly obsessed with creating life, much to the dismay of Dr. Frankenstein. The two scientists engage in a series of escalating pranks and competitions, with Igor determined to outdo his mentor.

In the end, Igor's creation comes to life, but it is not what he had intended. Instead of a beautiful and intelligent being, Igor has created a grotesque and terrifying monster. Dr. Frankenstein is horrified by the creature, and Igor is left feeling guilty and ashamed.

Despite the chaos that ensues, Igor ultimately learns a valuable lesson about responsibility and humility. He realizes that his enthusiasm and ambition must be balanced with caution and consideration for others. The film ends with Igor returning to his village, where he is welcomed back as a hero. However, it is clear that Igor has grown and matured as a result of his experiences in the laboratory.

Overall, Igor is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of ambition, responsibility, and friendship. With its talented voice cast and clever stop-motion animation, the movie is a delight to watch.

documents.title: The Uninvited
documents.tagline: Can you believe what you see?
documents.overview: Anna returns home after spending time in a psychiatric facility following her mother's tragic death and discovers that her mother's former nurse, Rachel, has moved into their house and become engaged to her father. Soon after she learns this shocking news, Anna is visited by her mother's ghost, who warns her that Rachel has evil intentions.
documents.plot:
The Uninvited is a 2009 supernatural horror film directed by Charles Guard and Thomas Guard. The movie follows two sisters, Abigail (Elizabeth Reaser) and Sam (Sara Paxton), who return to their family's ancestral home in Maine after their father's death.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. **Trauma and grief**: The film explores the emotional trauma that the sisters experience after their mother's death and their father's subsequent remarriage, which leads to a rift between them.
2. **Isolation and loneliness**: The isolated setting of the family's old mansion serves as a backdrop for the sisters' emotional isolation from each other and the outside world.
3. **Family dynamics and secrets**: As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the family's past is shrouded in secrets, which are slowly revealed through the supernatural events that occur.
4. **Female empowerment and sisterhood**: The movie highlights the strong bond between Abigail and Sam, who must work together to survive the supernatural forces that threaten them.

The Uninvited received mixed reviews from critics but has since become a cult classic among horror fans. While it may not be as well-known as some other horror films, it offers a unique blend of atmospheric tension, creepy setting, and strong female characters.

documents.title: Delusions of Grandeur
documents.overview: Don Sallust is minister of the King of Spain. It is a being disingenuous, hypocritical and greedy that collects the taxes himself, he turns in part to his advantage. He is hated by the people he oppresse.Accusé by Queen, a beautiful princess Bavarian, of having an illegitimate child to one of her maids of honor, he was stripped of his duties and ordered to retire to a monastery. Decided to revenge, it comes in contact with his nephew seducing Caesar ...
documents.plot:
Delusions of Grandeur (French: La Folie des grandeurs) is a 1971 historical comedy directed by Gérard Oury, starring Louis de Funès as the scheming minister Don Salluste and Yves Montand as his valet Blaze, with Alice Sapritch, Karin Schubert and Alberto de Mendoza. A very loose comic adaptation of Victor Hugo's play Ruy Blas, it was a co-production between France, Italy, Spain and West Germany. It premiered in Paris on December 8, 1971.

In 17th-century Spain, Don Salluste de Bazan is the greedy, hypocritical finance minister of King Charles II, who personally collects taxes from the downtrodden peasants and pockets most of them. When the queen, a beautiful Bavarian princess, accuses him of fathering a child with one of her ladies-in-waiting, he is stripped of his office and ordered to retire to a monastery. Bent on revenge, he plans to compromise the queen so that the king will repudiate her. When his nephew Caesar, now a bandit, refuses to take part, Salluste has him sold into slavery in the Barbary states. He turns instead to Blaze, the valet he has just dismissed, having discovered that Blaze is secretly in love with the queen, and passes him off at court as Caesar.

At his presentation, Blaze foils an attempt on the king's life and wins the favour of the royal couple, especially the queen, who returns his feelings, and he quickly becomes a minister. Unlike his former master, Blaze is generous: he hands Salluste's fortune to the poor and taxes the rich instead, enraging the nobility, who plot to kill him. In a garden game, he declares his love to the person behind a hedge, not realising that the queen has been replaced by her severe duenna, Doña Juana, who falls passionately for him. When Salluste rescues Blaze from a poisoning plot at his birthday celebration, Blaze takes it as a favour, unaware that he is now his master's prisoner and a pawn in a larger scheme.

Salluste lures the queen to an inn, drugs her and places her in a room with the bound Blaze, intending for the king to find them together. The plan collapses when the real Caesar, escaped from slavery, frees Blaze, and Doña Juana arrives and performs a striptease for him. When the king arrives, Blaze convinces him that he is Doña Juana's suitor while Caesar spirits the queen away. The king sends both Salluste and Blaze to the Barbary slave market, where the deranged Salluste hatches yet another scheme, and Doña Juana arrives in the desert proclaiming her love as Blaze flees.
cast: Don Jaime de Mora y Aragón

documents.title: Miracle
documents.tagline: If you believe in yourself, anything can happen.
documents.overview: When college coach Herb Brooks is hired to helm the 1980 U.S. men's Olympic hockey team, he brings a unique and brash style to the ice. After assembling a team of hot-headed college all-stars, who are humiliated in an early match, Brooks unites his squad against a common foe: the heavily-favored Soviet team.
documents.plot:
Miracle is a 2004 American sports drama film directed by Gavin O'Connor and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie tells the story of the 1980 US Olympic ice hockey team, led by coach Herb Brooks, as they prepare to compete in the Winter Olympics.

The main theme of Miracle revolves around the idea of perseverance and teamwork. The film showcases how a group of underdog American hockey players, many of whom were not experienced or skilled enough to play at that level, came together to form a cohesive unit and achieve greatness through their collective efforts. Despite facing significant odds and setbacks, including a lack of resources and equipment, the team persevered and ultimately achieved a historic victory over the heavily favored Soviet Union.

The movie also explores themes of redemption and personal growth. Many of the characters on the team are struggling with their own personal demons, including feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt. Through their experiences on the ice, they learn to overcome these obstacles and find a sense of purpose and belonging.

Furthermore, Miracle highlights the importance of leadership and vision. Coach Herb Brooks is portrayed as a complex and nuanced character who embodies both the qualities of a great leader and those of a flawed individual. His unorthodox coaching methods and emphasis on teamwork and discipline ultimately lead to the team's success, but also create tension and conflict within the group.

Overall, Miracle is a film about the power of human spirit and the importance of working together towards a common goal. It is an inspiring and uplifting story that celebrates the triumphs of the underdog and the enduring bonds of friendship and camaraderie.

documents.title: You Can Count on Me
documents.tagline: Family first. Love always.
documents.overview: A single mother's life is thrown into turmoil after her struggling, rarely-seen younger brother returns to town.
documents.plot:
You Can Count on Me is a poignant and introspective drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the struggles of everyday life. The film delves into the emotional landscape of its protagonist, Sam, a single mother struggling to cope with her own demons and find stability in her life.

At its core, the movie is a nuanced portrayal of the fragility of human connection and the ways in which our relationships can both heal and harm us. Through Sam's story, the film sheds light on the intricate web of emotions that bind us together, revealing the beauty and pain that can arise from these connections.

The movie also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for meaning in a chaotic world. Sam's struggles to balance her own needs with those of her son, Toby, serve as a powerful metaphor for the universal human quest for connection and belonging.

Through its thoughtful pacing and nuanced character development, You Can Count on Me offers a deeply moving exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.

documents.title: Marley & Me
documents.tagline: Heel the love.
documents.overview: A newly married couple who, in the process of starting a family, learn many of life's important lessons from their trouble-loving retriever, Marley. Packed with plenty of laughs to lighten the load, the film explores the highs and lows of marriage, maturity and confronting one's own mortality, as seen through the lens of family life with a dog.
documents.plot:
Marley & Me is a 2008 American comedy-drama film directed by David Frankel from a screenplay by Scott Frank and Don Roos, based on John Grogan's 2005 memoir of the same name. Owen Wilson and Jennifer Aniston star as John and Jenny Grogan, journalists whose family life is shaped over many years by their unruly yellow Labrador retriever, Marley, and the cast also includes Eric Dane, Kathleen Turner and Alan Arkin.

After moving from Michigan to South Florida, the newlyweds take reporting jobs at rival newspapers: Jenny quickly lands front-page stories at The Palm Beach Post, while John is stuck writing obituaries and short news items at the South Florida Sun-Sentinel. Sensing Jenny is thinking about motherhood, John's colleague Sebastian Tunney suggests a dog to test their readiness, and they adopt a puppy John names after Bob Marley. Marley grows to around 100 pounds and proves impossible to control, getting thrown out of obedience school. When editor Arnie Klein offers John a twice-weekly column on any subject he likes, John writes about Marley's misadventures, and the column becomes so popular that it helps double the paper's circulation. Jenny suffers a miscarriage early in her first pregnancy, and the couple return from a belated honeymoon in Ireland to find that Marley has wrecked the house under an overwhelmed sitter. Jenny later gives birth to two sons, Patrick and Conor, and decides to stay at home while John takes on a daily column. The family moves to a larger house in Boca Raton, but the exhausted Jenny grows short-tempered with both Marley and John and demands that the dog be rehomed, before quickly realizing he is an essential member of the family. After their daughter Colleen is born and John turns 40, envy of Sebastian's new job at The New York Times leads him to take a reporting post at The Philadelphia Inquirer, and the family moves to a farm in rural Pennsylvania, though John soon realizes he is a better columnist than reporter. Their contentment is shaken when the aging Marley suffers a near-fatal intestinal illness; he recovers, but after a second attack, too old for surgery, he is put down with John at his side and buried beneath a tree in the yard.

Released by 20th Century Fox on December 25, 2008, the film set a Christmas Day box office record of $14.75 million and grossed $247.8 million against a $60 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with a 64% Rotten Tomatoes rating. A prequel, Marley & Me: The Puppy Years, followed in 2011.

documents.title: The Wild Thornberrys Movie
documents.tagline: You don't need extraordinary powers to do extraordinary things.
documents.overview: Eliza and Debbie are two sisters who don't always get along. But their relationship is put to the test when Debbie's life is in danger, and Eliza might have to give up her power to talk to animals....
documents.plot:
The Wild Thornberrys Movie is a 2002 animated film produced by Nickelodeon Movies and Paramount Pictures.

The movie follows the adventures of Eliza Thornberry, a young girl who has the ability to communicate with animals. The story begins with the Thornberry family, including parents Marianne and Donnie, and their children Eliza, Debbie, and Darwin, embarking on a journey to Africa for a documentary film project.

As they travel through the African wilderness, the family faces various challenges and dangers, including poachers and treacherous terrain. However, Eliza's unique gift allows her to help the animals in need and ultimately save the day.

The main themes of The Wild Thornberrys Movie include:

1. Environmentalism: The film highlights the importance of conservation and protecting wildlife habitats.
2. Family values: The movie showcases the love and support within the Thornberry family, as they work together to overcome challenges and learn valuable lessons.
3. Empowerment: Eliza's ability to communicate with animals gives her a sense of purpose and confidence, allowing her to make a positive impact on the world around her.
4. Friendship: The film features various animal characters who become Eliza's friends and allies, teaching her about teamwork and cooperation.

The movie also explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and growing up, as Eliza navigates her unique gift and learns to balance her individuality with her family responsibilities.

Overall, The Wild Thornberrys Movie is a heartwarming and entertaining film that promotes positive values and messages for both children and adults.

documents.title: Nights in Rodanthe
documents.tagline: It's never too late for a second chance
documents.overview: Adrienne is trying to decide whether to stay in her unhappy marriage or not, and her life changes when Paul, a doctor who is travelling to reconcile with his estranged son, checks into an inn where she is staying.
documents.plot:
Nights in Rodanthe is a 2008 romantic drama film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and personal growth. The movie delves into the emotional journeys of its two main characters, Adria Collins (played by Diane Lane) and Paul Flanner (played by Richard Gere), as they navigate their way through heartbreak, loss, and self-discovery.

At its core, Nights in Rodanthe is a poignant tale about the power of human connection and the resilience of the human spirit. The film masterfully weaves together themes of love, forgiveness, and redemption, creating a narrative that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.

Through Adria's character, the movie explores the pain of losing a loved one and the struggle to move on from grief. Her journey serves as a catalyst for Paul's own emotional awakening, forcing him to confront his past mistakes and re-evaluate his priorities in life.

The film also touches on the theme of second chances, highlighting the possibility of finding love again after experiencing heartbreak. As Adria and Paul navigate their blossoming relationship, they must confront their own fears and doubts, ultimately learning to trust themselves and each other.

One of the most striking aspects of Nights in Rodanthe is its thoughtful portrayal of the complexities of human relationships. The movie shows how people can be both flawed and lovable, and how love can be a messy, imperfect thing that requires effort and commitment to sustain.

Overall, Nights in Rodanthe is a moving and thought-provoking film that explores the intricacies of the human heart with sensitivity and nuance.

documents.title: Primer
documents.tagline: What happens if it actually works?
documents.overview: Friends and fledgling entrepreneurs invent a device in their garage which reduces the apparent mass of any object placed inside it, but they discover that it has some highly unexpected capabilities - ones that could enable them to do and to have seemingly anything they want. Taking advantage of this unique opportunity is the first challenge they face. Dealing with the consequences is the next.
documents.plot:
Primer is a 2004 science fiction film written, directed, edited, and scored by Shane Carruth. The movie follows two engineers, Aaron (Shane Carruth) and Abe (David Sullivan), who work for a company that specializes in developing technology related to time travel.

The story begins with Aaron and Abe working on a project to develop a device that can send information through time. They successfully test the device, but their excitement is short-lived as they soon realize the consequences of their actions. The device creates a closed timelike curve, allowing them to send messages to their past selves, which in turn causes a series of paradoxes and disruptions to their timeline.

As the story unfolds, Aaron and Abe try to navigate the complexities of time travel, but their attempts only lead to more problems. They start to experience strange occurrences, such as finding themselves in different locations at the same time, and encountering alternate versions of themselves. The two men become increasingly paranoid and isolated, struggling to maintain a sense of reality.

One of the most striking aspects of Primer is its exploration of the consequences of playing with time. Carruth raises questions about the nature of free will and the potential risks of tampering with the timeline. As Aaron and Abe try to fix their mistakes, they begin to realize that every decision they make has a ripple effect on the world around them.

Throughout the film, Carruth employs a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth between different points in time. This creates a sense of disorientation and confusion, mirroring the characters' experiences as they try to navigate the complexities of their own timeline.

As the story reaches its climax, Aaron and Abe are forced to confront the consequences of their actions. They realize that their attempts to fix their mistakes have created a new reality, one in which they are no longer sure what is real and what is not. The film ends with a sense of ambiguity, leaving the audience wondering what will happen next.

Overall, Primer is a thought-provoking and intellectually stimulating film that challenges viewers to think critically about the nature of time and its consequences. With its complex narrative structure and exploration of philosophical themes, Primer has become a cult classic among fans of science fiction and independent cinema.

documents.title: Doubt
documents.tagline: There is no evidence. There are no witnesses. But for one, there is no doubt.
documents.overview: In 1964, a Catholic school nun questions a priest's ambiguous relationship with a troubled young student, suspecting him of abuse. He denies the charges.
documents.plot:
Doubt is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of faith, morality, and the human condition. The movie revolves around Father Brendan Flynn, a Catholic priest who is accused of abusing a young boy at his school. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the lines between truth and deception are blurred.

At its core, Doubt explores the theme of doubt itself, both literal and metaphorical. The title of the film is a clever play on words, as it not only refers to the uncertainty surrounding Father Flynn's actions but also serves as a reflection of the characters' inner turmoil. As the story progresses, it becomes apparent that each character has their own doubts and fears, which are expertly woven into the narrative.

One of the primary concerns of the film is the nature of faith and its relationship with morality. The characters in Doubt struggle with questions of right and wrong, often finding themselves at odds with one another. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for the plot, driving the characters to confront their own biases and assumptions.

The movie also touches on the theme of power dynamics, particularly in the context of the Catholic Church. Father Flynn's position of authority is both a blessing and a curse, allowing him to wield significant influence over the lives of those around him while also creating an environment where accusations can be easily leveled against him.

Furthermore, Doubt raises important questions about the reliability of human perception and the dangers of making assumptions based on incomplete information. As the characters navigate their complex web of relationships and motivations, it becomes clear that nothing is ever as simple or straightforward as it initially seems.

Ultimately, Doubt presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own doubts and biases. Through its thought-provoking narrative and outstanding performances, the film invites us to consider the complexities of faith, morality, and the nature of truth itself.

documents.title: Killing Me Softly
documents.tagline: How do you escape… what you can't resist?
documents.overview: A woman grows suspicious of her controlling husband after she discovers secrets about the women in his past.
documents.plot:
Killing Me Softly is a 2002 erotic thriller directed by Chen Kaige, starring Heather Graham and Joseph Fiennes, with Natascha McElhone, Ulrich Thomsen and Ian Hart in supporting roles. Adapted from the 1999 novel of the same name by Nicci French, the film makes several significant changes to the book and places heavy emphasis on the intense sexual relationship between its two leads. It remains Chen's only English-language feature.

Alice is a young American living in London, settled in a secure job and a steady relationship. After a chance encounter on the street with a striking stranger, she seeks him out, goes home with him and begins a passionate affair. She learns that he is Adam, a celebrated mountaineer hailed as a hero for rescuing six people during a disastrous expedition that killed several others, including the woman he loved. Alice leaves her boyfriend for him, and after Adam violently beats a man who mugs her, he proposes and she accepts. They honeymoon at a remote cabin and then settle into married life.

Alice soon begins receiving anonymous letters and phone calls hinting at a darker side to her husband. A journalist forwards her a letter from a woman accusing Adam of rape, and Alice, posing as a reporter, interviews her. Searching the flat, she finds old letters from a former lover, Adele, and discovers that Adele has been missing for eight months, as well as a photograph of Adele at the very cabin where Alice and Adam spent their honeymoon. Fearing for her safety, Alice goes to the police, but without evidence they can hold Adam for only a few hours.

Alice turns to Adam's sister Deborah for help. Deborah confesses that she sent the warnings, and at the cabin Alice uncovers a buried body wearing the same necklace Deborah had given her. Deborah reveals her incestuous obsession with her brother, which drove her to eliminate the women in his life, and tries to kill Alice. Adam arrives in time to save her, and Alice stops Deborah with a flare pistol. Two years later, Alice and Adam pass each other on an escalator without a word.

The film was savaged by critics. Rotten Tomatoes reported a 0% approval rating, with the consensus calling it a spectacularly misguided erotic thriller marked by ludicrous twists and cringe-worthy dialogue.

documents.title: Leviathan
documents.tagline: The true meaning of fear
documents.overview: Underwater deep-sea miners encounter a Soviet wreck and bring back a dangerous cargo to their base on the ocean floor with horrifying results. The crew of the mining base must fight to survive against a genetic mutation that hunts them down one by one.
documents.plot:
Leviathan is a 1989 American drama film directed by George C. Scott, who also stars in the movie alongside Richard Farnsworth.

The main theme of Leviathan revolves around the struggle for power and control within a small fishing village. The story centers around Jonas, a grizzled fisherman played by George C. Scott, who is determined to protect his community from the corrupt and oppressive local politician, Moses Prayle. As the conflict escalates, it becomes clear that Prayle's intentions are far more sinister than initially thought.

The film explores themes of corruption, greed, and the dangers of unchecked power. It also touches on the idea of a small group of individuals standing up against an oppressive system, highlighting the importance of community and collective action in the face of adversity.

Through Jonas' character, the film showcases a strong sense of moral integrity and a commitment to doing what is right, even in the face of overwhelming odds. The movie ultimately becomes a powerful commentary on the human condition, revealing the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of allowing power to corrupt individuals and institutions.

documents.title: Death Wish II
documents.tagline: When murder and rape invade your home, and the cops can't stop it... This man will. His way.
documents.overview: Paul Kersey is again a vigilante trying to find five punks who murdered his housekeeper and daughter in Los Angeles.
documents.plot:
Death Wish II is a 1982 American vigilante action thriller directed and co-edited by Michael Winner. It is the sequel to the 1974 film Death Wish and the second instalment in the Death Wish series. Charles Bronson returns as Paul Kersey, with Jill Ireland as his girlfriend Geri Nichols, Vincent Gardenia reprising his role as Detective Frank Ochoa, and J. D. Cannon and Anthony Franciosa in supporting roles. The film was produced by Menahem Golan and Yoram Globus for Cannon Films, and its score was composed by Jimmy Page of Led Zeppelin.

Several years after the events of the first film, Paul Kersey has rebuilt his life in Los Angeles, where he works as an architect and is in a relationship with Geri, a radio journalist. His daughter Carol, still traumatised by the attack that ended the first film, has been living in a psychiatric hospital but is beginning to make progress. During an outing at a fairground, Paul's wallet is stolen by a street gang. He chases down one of its members but lets him go when he cannot find the wallet.

Using the address in the wallet, the gang breaks into Paul's house, brutally assaults and murders his housekeeper Rosario, knocks Paul unconscious and abducts Carol, who dies while trying to escape after being assaulted. Convinced that the police will not deliver justice, and wanting to keep Geri out of it, Paul rents a cheap room in a rough neighbourhood under a false identity and begins hunting the gang members one by one at night. Detective Ochoa, who knows Kersey's history from New York, travels to Los Angeles, realising that the vigilante is active again. The hunt culminates in a final confrontation with the gang's leader inside a psychiatric hospital.

The film is considerably more violent and exploitative than its predecessor, particularly in its depiction of sexual assault, and it established the formula of escalating revenge sequences that later sequels in the series would follow.

Death Wish II was heavily criticised on release for its brutality and gratuitous violence, and it required cuts before it could be released in several countries. Nevertheless, it was a commercial success and led to three further sequels starring Bronson.

documents.title: The Warlords
documents.overview: A heroic tale of three blood brothers and their struggle in the midst of war and political upheaval. It is based on "The Assassination of Ma," a Qing Dynasty (1644-1911) story about the killing of general Ma Xinyi.
documents.plot:
The Warlords, originally titled The Blood Brothers, is a 2007 epic historical action film directed and co-produced by Peter Chan, starring Jet Li, Andy Lau, Takeshi Kaneshiro and Xu Jinglei. A Hong Kong-Chinese co-production set during the Taiping Rebellion in the 1860s, it centers on the sworn brotherhood of three men. Chan said it was influenced by, though not a remake of, Chang Cheh's 1973 film The Blood Brothers, and that he had long wanted to make a film about male bonds after seeing John Woo's A Better Tomorrow. Filming began in December 2006 in Beijing and also took place in Shanghai and at Hengdian World Studios.

Pang Qingyun, commander of an imperial battalion, is the sole survivor of a battle with rebel forces. He befriends Zhao Erhu and Jiang Wuyang, leaders of a bandit gang in a poor, starving village, and secretly begins an affair with Liansheng, Zhao's wife. When imperial troops seize the food the bandits have stolen, Pang persuades them to become a militia in the emperor's service, and the three swear a blood oath of brotherhood on pain of death. The militia wins a series of victories, but jealous superiors starve Pang of supplies, and his attack on rebel-held Suzhou becomes a long siege.

Zhao slips into Suzhou and makes a deal with the rebel commander, who lets Zhao kill him in exchange for a promise that the surrendering rebels will be spared. Lacking food for prisoners, Pang breaks the promise, chains Zhao and has Jiang oversee the massacre, then convinces Zhao that the killing was needed to end the war. After the fall of Nanjing, Pang is made a viceroy, but he and Zhao drift apart, and fearing that Zhao is beyond his control, Pang reluctantly plots his death. Jiang tries to stop him, discovers the affair and kills Liansheng, while Zhao is lured into a trap and murdered without knowing who betrayed him. Learning the truth, Jiang attacks Pang, who is shot by a sniper sent by his political rivals and allows Jiang to deliver the final blow. Jiang is later made a scapegoat and executed.

Li plays Pang, Lau plays Zhao, Kaneshiro plays Jiang and Xu plays Liansheng. Released across most of Asia on 13 December 2007, it won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Film and the Golden Horse Award for Best Feature Film, and Li won Best Actor at the Hong Kong Film Awards. Li's fee made him the highest-paid actor in a Chinese-language film, and the film holds 65% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.
production_companies: Beijing Jinyinma Movie & TV Culture Co.

documents.title: The Heir Apparent: Largo Winch
documents.overview: After a powerful billionaire is murdered, his secret adoptive son must race to prove his legitimacy, find his father's killers and stop them from taking over his financial empire.
documents.plot:
The Heir Apparent: Largo Winch is a 2008 adventure film that revolves around the story of Largo Winch, a young and wealthy playboy who inherits a vast fortune from his father. As he navigates his new life, Largo discovers that his inheritance comes with a price - a powerful organization known as the Syndicate, which will stop at nothing to claim the Winch fortune for themselves.

The film explores themes of power, greed, and corruption, highlighting how the pursuit of wealth and control can lead individuals down a dark path. Through Largo's journey, the movie delves into the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to power and the corrupting influence it can have on even the most well-intentioned individuals.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Largo struggles to find his place in the world beyond his privileged upbringing. As he becomes embroiled in a web of intrigue and deception, Largo must confront his own demons and learn to rely on himself rather than relying solely on his wealth and connections.

Ultimately, The Heir Apparent: Largo Winch is a thrilling adventure that explores the darker side of human nature, revealing how even the most seemingly carefree individuals can be driven by a desire for power and control.

documents.title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua
documents.tagline: 50% Warrior. 50% Lover. 100% Chihuahua.
documents.overview: A pampered Beverly Hills chihuahua named Chloe who, while on vacation in Mexico with her owner Viv's niece, Rachel, gets lost and must rely on her friends to help her get back home before she is caught by a dognapper who wants to ransom her.
documents.plot:
Beverly Hills Chihuahua is a 2008 American live-action/CGI comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Chloe, a pampered and spoiled Chihuahua living with her wealthy owner, Vivian.

The film begins with Chloe's life in Beverly Hills, where she spends her days lounging on designer furniture and getting pampered by her loyal staff. However, when Vivian is kidnapped by a Mexican cartel, Chloe finds herself separated from her beloved owner and forced to embark on an adventure of a lifetime.

Along the way, Chloe meets a group of stray dogs who become her unlikely friends and allies. There's Delgado, a street-smart dog with a heart of gold; Lola, a sassy and confident Chihuahua who becomes Chloe's rival; and Tino, a lovable but dim-witted dog who often gets them into trouble.

As Chloe navigates the dangers of Mexico City, she learns valuable lessons about courage, loyalty, and friendship. With the help of her new friends, Chloe sets out to find Vivian and bring her home safely.

Throughout their journey, Chloe and her companions face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, fierce predators, and even a rival dog named Lola's owner, who seeks to capture Delgado for his own gain. Despite these obstacles, the group remains determined and resourceful, using their unique skills and personalities to overcome each hurdle.

As they near their destination, Chloe and her friends discover that Vivian is being held captive by a ruthless cartel leader. In a thrilling showdown, Chloe and her companions use all their wits and cunning to outsmart the cartel and rescue Vivian.

In the end, Chloe and Vivian are reunited, and the group returns home to Beverly Hills as heroes. Along the way, Chloe has undergone a significant transformation from a pampered pet to a confident and capable companion who has discovered her own strength and resilience.

The film features stunning animation, lovable characters, and plenty of humor, making it a delightful treat for both children and adults. With its uplifting message about friendship and perseverance, Beverly Hills Chihuahua is a heartwarming adventure that will leave viewers smiling long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Notorious
documents.tagline: No dream is too B.I.G.
documents.overview: "Notorious" is the story of Christopher Wallace. Through raw talent and sheer determination, Wallace transforms himself from Brooklyn street hustler (once selling crack to pregnant women) to one of the greatest rappers of all time: The Notorious B.I.G. Follow his meteoric rise to fame and his refusal to succumb to expectations - redefining our notion of "The American Dream."
documents.plot:
Notorious is a 2009 biographical drama film that tells the story of Belinda "Belita" Moreno, a Jamaican singer and actress who became embroiled in the life of Toots Hibbert, the lead singer of the reggae band Toots and the Maytals. The movie explores themes of love, loyalty, and the complexities of relationships.

At its core, Notorious is a story about the all-consuming power of love and how it can both uplift and destroy us. Belita's relationship with Toots is portrayed as intense and passionate, but also fraught with possessiveness and jealousy. As their romance deepens, Belita becomes increasingly entangled in Toots' life, including his struggles with addiction and personal demons.

The film also delves into the theme of identity and how it can be shaped by our relationships with others. Belita's journey is one of self-discovery, as she navigates her own desires, ambitions, and sense of purpose outside of her relationship with Toots. Through her experiences, the movie raises questions about the nature of love, loyalty, and sacrifice.

Furthermore, Notorious touches on the theme of cultural heritage and the impact of colonialism on Jamaican identity. The film highlights the complexities of Belita's mixed heritage and how it shapes her experiences as a black woman in Jamaica.

Overall, Notorious is a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of love, relationships, identity, and culture, set against the vibrant backdrop of 1960s Jamaica.

documents.title: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas
documents.original_title: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas
documents.overview: The sailor of legend is framed by the goddess Eris for the theft of the Book of Peace, and must travel to her realm at the end of the world to retrieve it and save the life of his childhood friend Prince Proteus.
documents.plot:
Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas is a 2003 animated adventure comedy film produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of Sinbad, a sailor who gets caught up in a quest to retrieve the magical Golden Chalice.

The film begins with Sinbad (voiced by Brad Pitt), a charismatic and cunning sailor who has lost his way after being shipwrecked on a deserted island. He is rescued by a group of pirates led by Captain Cutler (voiced by John Cleese) and his daughter, Marina (voiced by Michelle Pfeiffer). Sinbad soon discovers that the Golden Chalice, which can grant any wish, has been stolen from the sea goddess, Eris (voiced by Catherine Zeta-Jones).

Eris tasks Sinbad with retrieving the chalice, but he is not the only one on the quest. The villainous Captain Cutler and his crew are also after the chalice, intending to use its power to gain control over the seas. Along the way, Sinbad meets a talking parrot named Pola (voiced by Leila Arcieri) who becomes his unlikely ally.

As Sinbad navigates through treacherous waters, he faces various obstacles and challenges, including fierce sea creatures and treacherous storms. He also discovers that Marina is not just a beautiful woman, but also a skilled warrior with her own motivations for retrieving the chalice.

Throughout the journey, Sinbad's character undergoes significant development as he learns to put aside his selfish desires and work towards a greater good. He forms an unlikely bond with Marina, who becomes a valuable partner in his quest.

The film features stunning animation, witty humor, and memorable characters. The voice cast delivers impressive performances, bringing depth and nuance to their respective roles. The movie's climax features an epic battle between Sinbad and Captain Cutler, with the fate of the seas hanging in the balance.

In the end, Sinbad successfully retrieves the Golden Chalice, but not before learning a valuable lesson about the importance of friendship and sacrifice. He returns to Eris' kingdom, where he is hailed as a hero and rewarded for his bravery. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with Sinbad and Marina sharing a romantic moment, hinting at a possible future together.

Overall, Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas is a thrilling adventure that combines humor, action, and romance. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's no wonder this film has become a beloved classic among animated movie fans.

documents.title: Herod's Law
documents.tagline: Why don't they want you to see it?
documents.overview: Mexico, 1949. The fable of a janitor turned Mayor on a little town lost in the Mexican desert, who gradually realizes how far his new acquainted power and corruption can get him.
documents.plot:
Herod's Law (Spanish: La ley de Herodes) is a 1999 Mexican satirical black comedy directed by Luis Estrada and produced by Bandidos Films. Damián Alcázar stars, with Pedro Armendáriz Jr., Delia Casanova, Juan Carlos Colombo, Leticia Huijara and the British director Alex Cox in supporting roles. A caricature of corruption under the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which governed Mexico for most of the twentieth century, it was the first Mexican film to criticize the PRI explicitly by name, and government attempts to interfere with its release caused a public controversy.

The story is set in the run-up to the 1952 general elections. After the mayor of the remote town of San Pedro de los Saguaros is killed by an angry mob while trying to escape with stolen money, the state governor orders his secretary López to find a replacement quickly and quietly. The job falls to Juan Vargas, the naïve manager of a garbage dump and a loyal PRI member, who sees it as the start of a political career. He and his wife Gloria are dismayed when they arrive in San Pedro, a desperately poor village whose largely Indigenous inhabitants barely speak Spanish. With the help of his secretary Pek, Vargas meets the town's notables: Doña Lupe, the brothel madam; a grasping priest; and Doctor Morales, an educated man who belongs to the opposition party.

When Vargas asks the state capital for funds to improve the town, López gives him only a copy of the Mexican Constitution and a revolver. Vargas soon discovers that both are useful tools. He combs the Constitution for pretexts to levy fines and taxes on the villagers, uses the pistol to impose his will and gradually turns from a well-meaning outsider into a ruthless, greedy local tyrant, abusing his position for money and power. His rise and moral collapse serve as a broad allegory of how the system rewarded and reproduced corruption, culminating in a darkly ironic ending.

The film is considered one of the most important Mexican films of its era for its biting humor and direct political criticism, and it won several Ariel Awards. It was released shortly before the 2000 presidential election, in which the PRI lost the presidency for the first time since its founding in 1929. It also launched a series of satirical films by Estrada starring Alcázar, including Hell (2010) and The Perfect Dictatorship (2014).

production_companies: Fondo para la Producción Cinematográfica de Calidad

documents.title: My Bloody Valentine
documents.tagline: He's gonna break your heart.
documents.overview: Ten years ago, a tragedy changed the town of Harmony forever. Tom Hanniger, an inexperienced coal miner, caused an accident in the tunnels that trapped and killed five men and sent the only survivor, Harry Warden, into a permanent coma. But Harry Warden wanted revenge. Exactly one year later, on Valentine’s Day, he woke up…and brutally murdered twenty-two people with a pickaxe before being killed.
documents.plot:
My Bloody Valentine is a 2009 Canadian horror film directed by Patrick Lussier, not Lionsgate. 

The movie is loosely based on the 1981 Canadian slasher film of the same name and serves as a remake. The story takes place in the small town of Harmony, where a group of miners are stalked and killed by a vengeful figure known as Tom Hanniger.

The main themes of My Bloody Valentine (2009) include:

1. Revenge: Tom's backstory reveals that he was brutally disfigured by his coworkers after they discovered his secret: he had been infected with a rare fungal infection, which caused him to grow long hair and become severely disfigured.
2. Isolation and claustrophobia: The miners are trapped in the mine, making them vulnerable to Tom's attacks. This isolation also serves as a metaphor for the characters' emotional confinement and inability to escape their past traumas.
3. Small-town secrets and lies: Harmony is portrayed as a tight-knit community with dark secrets hidden beneath its idyllic surface. The film explores how these secrets can lead to violence and tragedy when they are uncovered.
4. Trauma and PTSD: Tom's character serves as a symbol of the long-lasting effects of trauma on individuals. His disfigurement and subsequent isolation have driven him to seek revenge against those who wronged him.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics, with some praising its atmospheric tension and others criticizing its predictable plot and lack of originality.

documents.title: Fireproof
documents.tagline: Never leave your partner behind.
documents.overview: Caleb Holt, a heroic fire captain who values dedication and service to others above all else. But the most important partnership in his life, his marriage, is about to go up in smoke. This gripping story follows one man's desire to transform his life and marriage through the healing power of faith and fully embrace the fireman's code: "Never leave your partner behind."
documents.plot:
Fireproof is a 2008 American Christian drama film directed by Alex Kendrick and written by Alex and Stephen Kendrick. The movie stars Kirk Cameron as Captain David Thompson, a firefighter who must confront his own faith and relationship with his wife, played by Erin Cottrell.

The story begins with Captain David Thompson, a respected firefighter in the community, who is struggling to balance his career and family life. He is married to his high school sweetheart, Katherine (Erin Cottrell), and they have two young children together. However, their relationship has become stale, and they are no longer intimate.

One day, Captain David's friend, played by Ted McGinley, challenges him to read the Bible and apply its teachings to his life. The challenge is a test of faith, and Captain David accepts it. As he begins to study the Bible, he starts to see his marriage and relationships in a new light.

Meanwhile, Katherine has been feeling unappreciated and unheard in their relationship. She feels like she's carrying the load of parenting and household responsibilities while Captain David is always busy with work. The tension between them builds, and they start to drift apart.

As Captain David delves deeper into his faith, he begins to see the importance of communication, forgiveness, and intimacy in marriage. He starts to make changes in his behavior, such as being more present and attentive to Katherine, and apologizing for his mistakes.

However, Katherine is resistant to change, and she feels like Captain David is trying to "fix" their problems without really listening to her concerns. The situation escalates, and they have a series of confrontations that leave them both feeling hurt and angry.

In the climax of the movie, Captain David has an epiphany and realizes that he needs to make a choice between his faith and his marriage. He decides to take a stand and fight for their relationship, using the principles of the Bible to guide him.

The ending is redemptive, as Captain David and Katherine work through their issues and come out stronger on the other side. They learn to communicate effectively, forgive each other, and rekindle their romance. The movie ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as they look forward to rebuilding their relationship and growing together.

Throughout the movie, Alex Kendrick brings his signature Christian values to the story, emphasizing the importance of faith, forgiveness, and redemption. While some critics have accused the movie of being overly simplistic or heavy-handed, many viewers have found it to be a powerful and inspiring exploration of marriage and relationships.

Overall, Fireproof is a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant film that challenges viewers to think about their own relationships and priorities. With its strong performances, engaging storyline, and uplifting message, it's no wonder why this movie has become a beloved favorite among Christian audiences.

documents.title: Ella Enchanted
documents.tagline: Get enchanted
documents.overview: Ella lives in a magical world in which each child, at the moment of their birth, is given a virtuous "gift" from a fairy godmother. Ella's so-called gift, however, is obedience. This birthright proves itself to be quite the curse once Ella finds herself in the hands of several unscrupulous characters whom she quite literally cannot disobey. Determined to gain control of her life and decisions, Ella sets off on a journey to find her fairy godmother who she hopes will lift the curse. The path, however, isn't easy -- Ella must outwit a slew of unpleasant obstacles including ogres, giants, wicked stepsisters, elves and Prince Charmont's evil uncle, who wants to take over the crown and rule the kingdom.
documents.plot:
Ella Enchanted is a 2004 jukebox musical fantasy comedy film directed by Tommy O'Haver and written by Karen McCullah Lutz and Kirsten Smith, loosely based on Gail Carson Levine's 1997 novel. A satire of the fairy tale genre, it stars Anne Hathaway as Ella of Frell and Hugh Dancy as Prince "Char" Charmont, with Cary Elwes as his scheming uncle Sir Edgar, Vivica A. Fox as the fairy Lucinda, Joanna Lumley as Ella's stepmother Dame Olga and Jimi Mistry as Benny. An international co-production between the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom, it was filmed in Ireland at Ardmore Studios and on location in County Wicklow in 2002.

At her birth, Ella receives a misguided "gift" from the fairy Lucinda: she must instantly and literally obey any command she is given. Before dying, Ella's mother warns her to keep it secret and tells her that something in her is stronger than any spell. Years later, Ella's father marries the cruel socialite Dame Olga, whose daughter Hattie discovers the secret and uses it to humiliate her. Having caught the eye of Prince Char, a reluctant teen heartthrob who invites her to his coronation ball, Ella sets out to find Lucinda and have the spell lifted, taking along Benny, the boyfriend of the household fairy Mandy, who has accidentally turned him into a talking book. On her journey she rescues Slannen, an elf who dreams of becoming a lawyer, and when ogres capture them, Char comes to the rescue. As they travel together, Ella opens Char's eyes to the unjust laws against elves and giants passed by Sir Edgar, the King Regent, and the two fall in love. Learning of Ella's curse, Edgar, who secretly murdered Char's father, orders her to kill the prince at midnight and keep it secret, so that he can take the throne. Ella has herself chained to a distant tree to wait out the command, but Lucinda frees her, insisting that Ella must break the spell herself, leaving her to find the inner strength her mother spoke of before the coronation.

Released by Miramax Films on April 9, 2004, Ella Enchanted received mixed reviews and holds a 51% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed about $27.4 million worldwide and was considered a box-office bomb.

documents.title: The Manchurian Candidate
documents.tagline: Everything is under control.
documents.overview: Years after his squad was ambushed during the Gulf War, Major Ben Marco finds himself having terrible nightmares. He begins to doubt that his fellow squad-mate Sergeant Raymond Shaw, now a vice-presidential candidate, is the hero he remembers him being. As Marco's doubts deepen, Shaw's political power grows, and, when Marco finds a mysterious implant embedded in his back, the memory of what really happened begins to return.
documents.plot:
The Manchurian Candidate is a 2004 American psychological political thriller film directed and produced by Jonathan Demme. A remake of the 1962 film, itself adapted from Richard Condon's 1959 novel, it stars Denzel Washington as Bennett Marco, Liev Schreiber as Raymond Shaw, Jon Voight as Senator Tom Jordan and Meryl Streep as Eleanor Prentiss Shaw, Raymond's ruthless mother, with Kimberly Elise. While it keeps the title of the novel, the film changes the meaning of "Manchurian", which no longer refers to brainwashing in Manchuria during the Korean War but to a sinister multinational company. Paramount Pictures released it on July 30, 2004.

During the Persian Gulf War in 1991, Major Bennett Marco commanded a U.S. Army unit whose reconnaissance patrol was ambushed in Kuwait. Sergeant Raymond Shaw was awarded the Medal of Honor for leading the survivors on a three-day escape through the desert. Years later, Shaw is a congressman from New York, and his mother, the domineering Senator Eleanor Prentiss Shaw, uses her influence to secure him the vice-presidential nomination over the favorite, Senator Tom Jordan, whose daughter Jocelyn was Raymond's childhood sweetheart. When Al Melvin, one of Marco's former soldiers, tells him about disturbing dreams in which the patrol was captured, tortured and brainwashed, Marco feels compelled to investigate. In New York he meets Rosie, a friendly supermarket clerk who offers him a place to stay, and he discovers a small metal implant buried in his back. Convinced that Shaw has one too, Marco confronts him and bites one out of his back, and with the help of a scientist friend he links the devices to Manchurian Global, a powerful private equity firm with deep political connections, including to Senator Shaw. As he recovers clearer memories of what happened in the desert and learns of a South African geneticist accused of experimenting on political prisoners, Marco realizes that he and Shaw were programmed during their missing days, and that a plot to place a controlled agent a heartbeat away from the presidency is nearing completion, putting him in a desperate race to stop it.

The film received positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 79% of 208 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus that although it is not the classic its predecessor is, the update is well acted and has a chilling resonance, and Metacritic gave it a score of 76 out of 100. It grossed $96.1 million worldwide against an $80 million budget.

documents.title: New in Town
documents.tagline: She's an executive on the move. But her career is taking her a little farther than she expected.
documents.overview: Lucy Hill is an ambitious up-and-coming executive living in Miami. She loves her shoes, she loves her cars and she loves climbing the corporate ladder. When she is offered a temporary assignment — in the middle of nowhere — to restructure a manufacturing plant, she jumps at the opportunity, knowing that a big promotion is close at hand. What begins as a straightforward assignment becomes a life-changing experience as Lucy discovers greater meaning in her life and, most unexpectedly, the man of her dreams.
documents.plot:
New in Town is a 2009 romantic comedy-drama directed by Jonas Elmer. It was shot in Winnipeg and Selkirk, Manitoba, as well as in Los Angeles and in South Beach, Miami.

Lucy Hill, an ambitious consultant who loves her upscale Miami life, is sent to New Ulm, Minnesota, to restructure a food plant where new automation will cut at least half of the staff. The frozen weather, slippery roads and small-town customs come as a shock. At a home-cooked dinner arranged by the plant's secretary Blanche, Lucy insults the guest of honor, Ted Mitchell, only to discover the next day that he leads the workers' union. She also offends Flo, a waitress at the local diner who turns out to be the former wife of Stu, the foreman she is expected to fire.

Lucy and the townspeople slowly warm to each other. Ted rescues her when she swerves to avoid a cow and gets stuck in the snow, and Lucy uses her sense of style to help Ted's 13-year-old daughter prepare for her first dance. Lucy and Ted admit their attraction and share a kiss. At a corporate meeting in Florida, however, Lucy is told to shut the plant down entirely, which would leave the whole town out of work. After Blanche finds a list of workers to be laid off and confronts her, Lucy admits the truth and begins rethinking her priorities.

Inspired by Blanche's homemade tapioca pudding, Lucy convinces the company to produce and sell it, reviving an old yogurt line and keeping the existing staff. The pudding is such a hit that the company again plans to close the plant, which is too small for national demand. Lucy instead brings together investors to buy the plant, with ownership gradually passing to the workers, and she becomes chief executive. When she announces the deal, Ted pledges the union's support and the two kiss as the employees cheer.

Renée Zellweger plays Lucy and Harry Connick Jr. plays Ted, with Siobhan Fallon Hogan as Blanche, J. K. Simmons as Stu and Frances Conroy as Trudy. Released on January 30, 2009, the film spent one week in the domestic top ten, at eighth place. It grossed $16.7 million in North America and $29 million worldwide against an $8 million budget. Critics were mostly negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported 28% approval and called the film clichéd and charmless, while Metacritic gave it a score of 29. The Daily Express found it predictable and uninspired, and Peter Bradshaw of The Guardian mocked Zellweger's simpering performance in a film slavishly following the feel-good romcom formula.

documents.title: Three Kingdoms: Resurrection of the Dragon
documents.overview: The aging Zhao embarks on his final and greatest campaign, a road to adventure that will crown his name in glory for all time.
documents.plot:
Three Kingdoms: Resurrection of the Dragon is a 2008 action war film directed by Daniel Lee, who co-wrote it with Lau Ho-leung. Loosely based on parts of the 14th-century Chinese classical novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms, it follows the life of the celebrated general Zhao Zilong (Zhao Yun). Andy Lau stars as Zhao, with Sammo Hung, Maggie Q, Vanness Wu, Andy On and Ti Lung. A co-production between Hong Kong, mainland China and South Korea with a reported budget of US$25 million, it opened in Hong Kong cinemas on 3 April 2008. Its publicity said the script was inspired by chapter 92 of the novel.

The story begins in the late Eastern Han dynasty, as China fragments into rival states. Zhao Zilong, a young man from Changshan, joins the army of the warlord Liu Bei as a foot soldier and befriends Luo Ping'an, an older soldier from the same region who becomes his lifelong companion and narrates much of the story. Zhao proves his worth in a night raid and later wins fame at the Battle of Changban, where Liu Bei's forces are routed by the army of his rival Cao Cao. After defending Luo against Liu Bei's sworn brothers Zhang Fei and Guan Yu, Zhao is entrusted with rescuing Liu Bei's family, and he fights his way alone through enemy lines with Liu Bei's infant son strapped to his body, seizing a sword from Cao Cao along the way. Cao Cao's granddaughter, Cao Ying, witnesses his feat.

The film then follows Zhao's rise to become one of the Five Tiger Generals of the Shu Han kingdom and the long decades of war that follow. As his old comrades die and the kingdom weakens, an elderly Zhao leads one final northern expedition against the Wei kingdom. He faces Cao Ying, now a formidable commander bent on avenging her grandfather's humiliation, and becomes trapped at Phoenix Heights, where he must confront betrayal, the cost of a lifetime of warfare and the question of what his legend means.

Derek Elley of Variety praised the tightly cut film, its clearly defined cast, its fresh-looking costumes and armor and its music, which he said gave it true heroic stature. Some critics argued that Zhao's armor resembled that of a samurai, to which Lee replied that Japanese military costume had itself derived from Chinese designs, and others questioned the casting of Maggie Q in a Chinese period piece.
production_companies: Xian Longrui Film and TV Culture Media Co.

documents.title: The Matrix Revisited
documents.overview: The film goes behind the scenes of the 1999 sci-fi movie The Matrix.
documents.plot:
The Matrix Revisited is a 2001 American documentary directed by Josh Oreck about the making of the 1999 science fiction film The Matrix. Released by Warner Home Video on DVD and VHS on 20 November 2001, it runs 123 minutes and features interviews with the cast, including Keanu Reeves, Carrie-Anne Moss, Laurence Fishburne and Hugo Weaving, and with the filmmakers, among them the writer-directors the Wachowskis, who rarely gave interviews, producer Joel Silver, cinematographer Bill Pope, visual effects supervisors John Gaeta and Janek Sirrs, production designer Owen Paterson and action choreographer Yuen Woo-ping.

The documentary traces the history of The Matrix from its development and pre-production through filming and post-production to its release. It explains how some of the film's most complicated scenes were achieved, including its groundbreaking visual effects, and covers set construction and stunt work. Among the anecdotes it offers are that Reeves had to undergo neck surgery while making the film and that the Wachowskis had their star read philosophy before shooting. The program also offered audiences an early look at the two sequels then in production, The Matrix Reloaded and The Matrix Revolutions, both released in 2003. Alongside the main documentary, the disc included featurettes on the sequels, the comic books inspired by the film, the official website and the fan community, on the building of particular sets and sequences, on the special effects, and Yuen Woo-ping's test footage for the kung fu scenes. An Easter egg in the language menu, reached by highlighting a telephone booth, gave access to a jukebox of 41 techno tracks used in the documentary.

Initially issued as a stand-alone title, the documentary was later included in a two-disc collector's edition of The Matrix and became part of The Ultimate Matrix Collection box set. Reviewers were generally appreciative. The DVD Journal welcomed Warner's decision to release the supplements separately, so that owners of the popular original disc, criticized for its weak extras, did not have to replace it. It judged the documentary better than standard electronic press kits and pleasantly light on film clips, though not as engaging as the best behind-the-scenes accounts such as Hearts of Darkness, and noted the absence of some cast members, including Joe Pantoliano. Other reviewers found it thorough, though some considered it largely promotional.

documents.title: Paul Blart: Mall Cop
documents.tagline: Safety Never Takes A Holiday.
documents.overview: Mild-mannered Paul Blart has always had huge dreams of becoming a State Trooper. Until then, he patrols the local mall as a security guard. With his closely cropped moustache, personal transporter and gung-ho attitude, only Blart seems to take his job seriously. All that changes when a team of thugs raids the mall and takes hostages. Untrained, unarmed and a super-size target, Blart has to become a real cop to save the day.
documents.plot:
Paul Blart: Mall Cop is a 2009 American action comedy film directed by Kevin Heffernan and produced by Adam Sandler, Robert Smigel, and Jack Giarraputo. The movie stars Kevin James as the titular character, Paul Blart.

The story begins with Paul Blart (Kevin James), a well-meaning but awkward security guard at the West Orange Pavilion Mall in New Jersey. Despite his lack of popularity among the mall's patrons, Paul is dedicated to his job and takes pride in keeping the mall safe. He lives with his mother, Rita (Keir O'Donnell), who is also a mall employee.

The movie starts on Christmas Eve, where Paul is tasked with patrolling the mall during the holiday rush. However, things take a turn when a group of thieves, led by the cunning and ruthless Saperstein (Jayma Mays), plan to steal millions of dollars' worth of merchandise from the mall's stores. The thieves use advanced technology to evade security cameras and alarms, leaving Paul and the mall's security team baffled.

As the night progresses, Paul becomes determined to catch the thieves and prove himself as a capable security guard. He teams up with his fellow security guards, including his friend and rival, Kevin (Jayma Mays), and together they embark on a series of hilarious misadventures to outsmart the thieves.

Throughout the movie, Paul's character undergoes significant development as he faces various challenges and setbacks. Despite his initial awkwardness, Paul proves himself to be resourceful and determined, using his wits and instincts to stay one step ahead of the thieves.

As the night reaches its climax, Paul confronts Saperstein and her team in an epic showdown. With the help of his friends and a bit of luck, Paul manages to outsmart the thieves and recover the stolen merchandise.

The movie ends with Paul being hailed as a hero by the mall's patrons and employees, and he finally receives the recognition he deserves for his hard work and dedication. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, with Paul returning home to his mother, who is proud of her son's accomplishments.

Overall, Paul Blart: Mall Cop is a lighthearted, comedic take on the action genre, with plenty of laughs and exciting moments. Kevin James shines as the titular character, bringing humor and charm to the role. The movie's themes of perseverance and self-discovery make it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Ultimate Avengers: The Movie
documents.tagline: Saving the world, one enemy at a time.
documents.overview: When a nuclear missile was fired at Washington in 1945, Captain America managed to detonate it in the upper atmosphere. But then he fell miles into the icy depths of the North Atlantic, where he remained lost for over sixty years. But now, with the world facing the very same evil, Captain America must rise again as our last hope for survival.
documents.plot:
Ultimate Avengers: The Movie is a 2006 animated superhero film produced by Marvel Animation. The movie brings together some of Marvel's most iconic heroes, including Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow, and Hawkeye.

The main themes of Ultimate Avengers: The Movie revolve around the concept of unity, sacrifice, and the responsibility that comes with great power. Here are some key takeaways:

1. **Unity in the face of adversity**: The movie highlights the importance of teamwork and cooperation among superheroes when faced with a common threat. Despite their differences, the heroes put aside their personal agendas to work together and save the world from the villainous Loki.
2. **Sacrifice for the greater good**: Many characters in the movie are forced to make sacrifices for the sake of others, demonstrating that true heroism involves putting the needs of others before one's own interests. This theme is particularly evident in Captain America's selfless actions and Iron Man's willingness to put himself in harm's way to protect his teammates.
3. **The responsibility that comes with power**: The movie explores the consequences of wielding great power and the importance of accountability. Characters like Thor, who struggles with his newfound abilities, and Hulk, who grapples with his rage-filled nature, serve as cautionary tales about the dangers of unchecked power.
4. **Redemption and forgiveness**: Throughout the movie, characters are given opportunities to make amends for past mistakes or wrongdoing. This theme is particularly relevant in Captain America's storyline, where he seeks redemption for his past actions during the Cold War.

Overall, Ultimate Avengers: The Movie offers a compelling exploration of these themes, showcasing the complexities and nuances of Marvel's iconic heroes as they navigate their relationships with each other and confront the challenges of being superheroes.

documents.title: Ultimate Avengers 2: Rise of the Panther
documents.original_title: Ultimate Avengers 2: Rise of the Panther
documents.tagline: To save humanity, the Earth's mightiest heroes must reunite for a rematch of heroic proportions.
documents.overview: Mysterious Wakanda lies in the darkest heart of Africa, unknown to most of the world. An isolated land hidden behind closed borders, fiercely protected by its young king: Black Panther. But when brutal alien invaders attack, the threat leaves Black Panther with no option but to go against the sacred decrees of his people and ask for help from outsiders.
documents.plot:
Ultimate Avengers 2: Rise of the Panther is a 2006 American animated superhero film released direct to video by Lionsgate on 8 August 2006. The second entry in the Marvel Animated Features line produced by MLG Productions 2 with Marvel Enterprises, it is the sequel to Ultimate Avengers released earlier that year and is loosely based on Mark Millar and Bryan Hitch's comic series The Ultimates. Credited directors include Will Meugniot, Dick Sebast and Bob Richardson, with a screenplay credited to Greg Johnson and Craig Kyle, music by Guy Michelmore and animation by the South Korean studio Dong Woo Animation.

Some time after the defeat of the Chitauri, Captain America continues to fly missions for S.H.I.E.L.D. but is haunted by memories of Kleiser, the shape-shifting alien commander he fought in the Second World War, and takes increasingly reckless risks. In the isolated African kingdom of Wakanda, Kleiser resurfaces and the Chitauri attack, killing the king, T'Chaka. The invaders are after vibranium, a metal found only in Wakanda that they use to build their ships and weapons. Prince T'Challa assumes his father's mantle as the Black Panther and, defying his nation's sacred tradition of isolation from outsiders, seeks out Captain America for help.

Nick Fury reassembles the team, though Thor is initially unavailable and Bruce Banner remains under guard. A misunderstanding with Wakandan soldiers leaves the Wasp injured and Captain America's shield stolen, but the heroes, now joined by Thor, unite with the Black Panther against the Chitauri. From his confinement, Banner works out that gamma radiation weakens vibranium and sends Betty Ross to Wakanda with a gamma-ray projector. The weapon cripples the invaders, and Iron Man and Giant-Man destroy the power core of the Chitauri mothership, though Giant-Man is fatally wounded. After the Black Panther thanks his allies, the team returns home to learn that Banner has transformed into the Hulk and escaped.

The voice cast includes Justin Gross as Captain America, Marc Worden as Iron Man, Olivia d'Abo as Black Widow, Michael Massee as Bruce Banner with Fred Tatasciore as the Hulk, David Boat as Thor, Andre Ware as Nick Fury and Jeffrey D. Sams as the Black Panther, alongside Grey DeLisle and Nolan North. The film was later broadcast on Cartoon Network's Toonami block and received a mixed critical response.

documents.title: Next Avengers: Heroes of Tomorrow
documents.tagline: The children of heroes past are our only hope for the future!
documents.overview: The children of the Avengers hone their powers and go head to head with the very enemy responsible for their parents' demise.
documents.plot:
Next Avengers: Heroes of Tomorrow is a 2008 animated superhero film produced by Marvel Animation. The movie follows the story of a group of young superheroes, including Kate Bishop, Wiccan, Speed, and Patriot, as they team up to stop an alien invasion.

The main themes of Next Avengers: Heroes of Tomorrow include:

1. Coming-of-age: The movie explores the challenges and struggles faced by these young heroes as they navigate their newfound powers and responsibilities.
2. Teamwork and camaraderie: The film highlights the importance of teamwork, friendship, and trust among the young heroes as they work together to save the world from an alien threat.
3. Identity and self-discovery: Each character in the movie grapples with their own identity and sense of purpose, particularly Kate Bishop, who struggles to live up to her father's legacy.
4. Responsibility and duty: The film emphasizes the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and fulfilling one's duties as a hero.

The movie also explores some deeper themes, such as:

1. The weight of legacy: Kate Bishop's struggle to live up to her father's reputation serves as a metaphor for the pressure that can come with having a famous or influential family member.
2. Balancing personal life and superhero responsibilities: Many of the characters in the movie face challenges in balancing their personal lives with their duties as superheroes.

Overall, Next Avengers: Heroes of Tomorrow is a fun and action-packed film that explores themes relevant to young adults and fans of the Marvel universe.

documents.title: The Butterfly Effect 2
documents.tagline: Can you change your past without destroying your future?
documents.overview: After his girlfriend, Julie, and two best friends are killed in a tragic auto accident, Nick struggles to cope with his loss and grief. Suffering from migraine-like seizures, Nick soon discovers that he has the power to change the past via his memories. However, his time-traveling attempts to alter the past and save his one true love have unexpected and dire consequences.
documents.plot:
The Butterfly Effect 2 is a 2006 American science fiction psychological thriller film directed by John R. Leonetti and written by Mike Werb. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2004 film The Butterfly Effect.

The main themes of The Butterfly Effect 2 revolve around the consequences of altering one's past, the fragility of reality, and the devastating effects of playing with time. The story follows Evan Treborn (played by Ashton Kutcher), who is still struggling to cope with his traumatic childhood experiences.

As the movie progresses, it becomes clear that Evan's actions in the first film have created a ripple effect, causing chaos and destruction throughout his life. The film explores the idea of how even small changes can have significant and far-reaching consequences, leading to a downward spiral of events that are difficult to control or predict.

The Butterfly Effect 2 also delves into the theme of guilt and responsibility, as Evan grapples with the repercussions of his actions and tries to make amends for the harm he has caused. The film raises questions about the nature of free will and whether our choices truly determine our destiny.

Throughout the movie, the narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, mirroring the time-travel elements of the story. This structure adds to the sense of disorientation and confusion, reflecting Evan's own struggles to navigate the complexities of his altered reality.

Ultimately, The Butterfly Effect 2 presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of meddling with the timeline and the importance of accepting one's past experiences as a part of who they are.

documents.title: The Ultimate Gift
documents.tagline: Life is how you live it... not how you spend it.
documents.overview: When his wealthy grandfather finally dies, Jason Stevens fully expects to benefit when it comes to the reading of the will. But instead of a sizable inheritance, Jason receives a test, a series of tasks he must complete before he can get any money.
documents.plot:
The Ultimate Gift is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of family relationships, love, and the true meaning of wealth. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of letting go and embracing the present moment.

The story follows Jason Stevens, a young man who has lost touch with his roots and is struggling to find direction in life. As he navigates through various challenges, he comes to realize that the ultimate gift he can give himself is the ability to appreciate the beauty of simplicity and the love of those around him.

Through Jason's journey, the film highlights the importance of family bonds and the value of cherishing memories with loved ones. The movie also touches on the theme of material wealth versus spiritual wealth, suggesting that true happiness and fulfillment come from within.

One of the most striking aspects of The Ultimate Gift is its exploration of the concept of legacy. The character of Buck Stevens, Jason's grandfather, serves as a symbol of wisdom, love, and selflessness. Through his story, the film shows how our actions and decisions can have a lasting impact on those around us, leaving behind a legacy that transcends time.

Ultimately, The Ultimate Gift is a movie about finding one's way back to what truly matters in life – love, family, and the present moment. It is a poignant reminder to appreciate the beauty of simplicity and to cherish the relationships that bring joy and meaning to our lives.

documents.title: Beau Travail
documents.tagline: Maybe freedom begins with remorse
documents.overview: Foreign Legion officer Galoup recalls his once glorious life, training troops in the Gulf of Djibouti. His existence there was happy, strict and regimented, until the arrival of a promising young recruit, Sentain, plants the seeds of jealousy in Galoup's mind.
documents.plot:
Beau Travail is a 1999 film directed by Claire Denis, not La Sept-Arte. The movie is set in French Polynesia and explores the complexities of colonialism, power dynamics, and the human condition.

The main theme of Beau Travail revolves around the tension between discipline and freedom, as embodied by the character of Captain Galoup (played by Denzel Washington). On the surface, he appears to be a strict and authoritative figure, but beneath this façade lies a complex web of emotions and desires. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Galoup's rigid exterior is a coping mechanism for his own vulnerabilities and sense of disconnection.

The film also delves into the theme of identity, particularly in the context of colonialism and cultural exchange. The characters are caught between their French identities and their Polynesian surroundings, leading to a blurring of boundaries and a search for meaning. This is reflected in the character of Gilbert (played by Denzel Washington's on-screen doppelganger), who struggles to reconcile his own identity with the expectations placed upon him.

Furthermore, Beau Travail touches on the theme of masculinity and its performance. The film critiques traditional notions of masculinity, highlighting the performative nature of male identity and the ways in which it can be both a source of strength and weakness.

Overall, Beau Travail is a nuanced exploration of human relationships, power dynamics, and the search for meaning in a complex and often fraught world.

documents.title: The Rookie
documents.tagline: Sometimes dreams come back to life.
documents.overview: Jim Morris never made it out of the minor leagues before a shoulder injury ended his pitching career twelve years ago. Now a married-with-children high-school chemistry teacher and baseball coach in Texas, Jim's team makes a deal with him: if they win the district championship, Jim will try out with a major-league organization. The bet proves incentive enough for the team, and they go from worst to first, making it to state for the first time in the history of the school. Jim, forced to live up to his end of the deal, is nearly laughed off the try-out field--until he gets onto the mound, where he confounds the scouts (and himself) by clocking successive 98 mph fastballs, good enough for a minor-league contract with the Tampa Bay Devil Rays.
