The film also explores the complexities of female friendships and the importance of supporting one another through life's ups and downs. Ivan's character serves as a catalyst for Kate's growth, forcing her to confront her own vulnerabilities and insecurities in order to move forward.

Overall, I Could Never Be Your Woman is a heartwarming and engaging romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and self-discovery with humor, wit, and sensitivity.

documents.title: Against the Dark
documents.tagline: He lives by the sword. They will die by it.
documents.overview: When most of the population of Earth is infected by a virus and transformed into flesh eaters and blood drinking creatures, a group of hunters lead by Tao and his sword chase the vampire zombies to eliminate them. Six non-infected survivors try to find the exit of an abandoned hospital crowded of the infected creatures. Meanwhile, the military is ready to bomb the whole area.
documents.plot:
Against the Dark is a 2009 American action thriller film directed by John Hlattin. The movie follows a former Special Forces operative who must rescue his kidnapped daughter from a group of mercenaries in Eastern Europe.

The main theme of Against the Dark revolves around the struggle for survival and redemption. The protagonist, a rugged and skilled ex-Special Forces operative, is driven by his desire to protect his family and make amends for past mistakes. As he navigates the treacherous landscape of Eastern Europe, he must confront his own demons and face off against ruthless adversaries.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as the protagonist's determination to rescue his daughter puts him at odds with the mercenaries who are holding her captive. The movie takes a dark and gritty tone, exploring themes of violence, loyalty, and sacrifice.

One of the most striking aspects of Against the Dark is its portrayal of the human cost of war and violence. The film does not shy away from depicting the brutal realities of conflict, highlighting the devastating impact on civilians caught in the crossfire. This theme is particularly evident in the protagonist's relationship with his daughter, whose innocence and vulnerability serve as a stark contrast to the harsh world he finds himself in.

Ultimately, Against the Dark is a tense and gripping thriller that explores the complexities of human nature and the lengths people will go to protect those they love.

documents.title: Futurama: Into the Wild Green Yonder
documents.original_title: Futurama: Into the Wild Green Yonder
documents.tagline: All the other galaxies will be green with envy!
documents.overview: Leela becomes an outlaw when she and a group of ecologically-minded feminists attempt to save an asteroid of primitive life forms and the Violet Dwarf star from being destroyed, while Fry joins a secret society and attempts to stop a mysterious species known as the "Dark Ones" from destroying all life in the universe.
documents.plot:
Futurama: Into the Wild Green Yonder is an animated science fiction film that explores various themes, primarily focusing on environmentalism and the consequences of humanity's actions. The movie delves into a world where Earth has been ravaged by pollution and destruction, leading to a catastrophic collapse of ecosystems.

The story follows Bender, Fry, Leela, Professor Farnsworth, and Hermes as they embark on a journey through a post-apocalyptic wasteland in search of a mythical "Green Planet." Along the way, they encounter various characters who embody different aspects of human nature, from the selfish and destructive to the selfless and redemptive.

Throughout their adventure, the characters grapple with existential questions about the meaning of life, the importance of preserving the natural world, and the consequences of unchecked technological advancement. The film critiques modern society's relationship with technology, consumerism, and environmental degradation, often using satire and humor to make pointed commentary on these issues.

Ultimately, Futurama: Into the Wild Green Yonder presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of neglecting our planet's well-being and the importance of taking responsibility for our actions. The movie encourages viewers to reflect on their own relationship with the environment and consider the long-term consequences of their choices.

documents.title: The Good, the Bad, the Weird
documents.original_title: 좋은 놈, 나쁜 놈, 이상한 놈
documents.tagline: One map. Three villains. Winner takes all.
documents.overview: The story of three Korean outlaws in 1930s Manchuria and their dealings with the Japanese army and Chinese and Russian bandits. The Good (a bounty hunter), the Bad (a hitman), and the Weird (a thief) battle the army and the bandits in a race to use a treasure map to uncover the riches of legend.
documents.plot:
The Good, the Bad, the Weird is a 2008 South Korean Western film directed by Kim Jee-woon, produced by CJ Entertainment and CJ E&M. 

The movie follows three main characters: Kang-ho (played by Song Kang-ho), a former soldier; Cheon-bong (played by Byung-hun Lee), a young gunslinger; and Ban-gi (played by Ma Dong-seok), a mysterious outlaw. The story revolves around their quest for a buried treasure in the American West during the 1890s.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Friendship: Throughout the film, the three characters form an unlikely bond despite their differences. They learn to trust and rely on each other as they face various challenges.
2. Loyalty: The characters' loyalty to one another is tested when they are forced to make difficult choices that put their relationships at risk.
3. Redemption: Kang-ho's character, in particular, seeks redemption for past mistakes and finds a new sense of purpose through his journey with Cheon-bong and Ban-gi.
4. Morality: The film explores the gray areas between good and evil, as the characters are forced to confront their own moralities in the face of violence and betrayal.

The movie's unique blend of action, drama, and dark humor creates a captivating narrative that keeps viewers engaged until the very end.

documents.title: Only Yesterday
documents.tagline: I’m going on a trip with Me.
documents.overview: It’s 1982, and Taeko is 27 years old, unmarried, and has lived her whole life in Tokyo. She decides to visit her family in the countryside, where she begins to reconnect to forgotten longings. In lyrical switches between the present and the past, Taeko contemplates the arc of her life, and wonders if she has been true to the dreams of her childhood self.
documents.plot:
Only Yesterday is a 1991 Japanese animated drama film written and directed by Isao Takahata, produced by Studio Ghibli. The movie follows the story of Taeko Okajima, a young office worker who embarks on a journey to rediscover her childhood memories and find her place in the world.

The film begins with Taeko (voiced by Yuriko Kishitani) as an adult, working in Tokyo and feeling unfulfilled. She reminisces about her childhood, particularly her summer vacation spent at her grandparents' farm in the countryside. As she reflects on these memories, Taeko is transported back to her youth.

In the past, we see Taeko as a young girl, spending her summers with her grandparents in the rural town of Kusakabe. She spends her days exploring the surrounding countryside, playing with her friends, and helping out at her grandparents' farm. The film beautifully captures the carefree nature of childhood, showcasing Taeko's innocence and curiosity.

As the story progresses, we see Taeko develop feelings for a young man named Toshio, who is visiting from Tokyo. Their romance blossoms during Taeko's summer vacation, but it ultimately ends when Toshio returns to the city. The loss of this first love leaves a lasting impact on Taeko, shaping her perspective on life and relationships.

The film's narrative jumps back and forth between Taeko's childhood memories and her present-day struggles as an adult. As she navigates her career and personal life in Tokyo, Taeko begins to realize that she has lost touch with the simple joys of childhood. She starts to feel disconnected from her own desires and aspirations.

In a poignant moment, Taeko visits her grandparents' farm again, this time accompanied by Toshio's son, who is now a young boy. As they explore the countryside together, Taeko begins to see the world through the eyes of a child once more. She starts to appreciate the beauty of nature and the importance of human connections.

The film concludes with Taeko returning to her life in Tokyo, but with a newfound sense of purpose and appreciation for the simple things. She has come to realize that childhood is not just a nostalgic memory, but a state of mind that can be recaptured at any age. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that it's never too late to rediscover one's sense of wonder and connection with the world.

Throughout the film, Takahata's direction masterfully weaves together themes of nostalgia, identity, and the human experience. The animation is beautiful, capturing the vibrant colors and textures of rural Japan in the 1950s. The voice acting is also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to Taeko's character.

Overall, Only Yesterday is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

documents.title: Crank: High Voltage
documents.tagline: Stay Charged, Stay Alive!
documents.overview: Chelios faces a Chinese mobster who has stolen his nearly indestructible heart and replaced it with a battery-powered ticker that requires regular jolts of electricity to keep working.
documents.plot:
Crank: High Voltage, also known as Crank 2: High Voltage, is a 2009 American action film written and directed by Mark Neveldine and Brian Taylor, known as Neveldine/Taylor, and the sequel to their 2006 film Crank. Jason Statham returns as Chev Chelios, with Amy Smart as his girlfriend Eve, Dwight Yoakam as Doc Miles, Efren Ramirez, Clifton Collins Jr., Bai Ling and David Carradine, and the film includes numerous cameo appearances by personalities from music, sports and adult entertainment.

The film picks up moments after the end of the first film, as Chev Chelios lands in the middle of a Los Angeles street after falling from a helicopter. Before ambulances can reach him, he is scooped up by Chinese gangsters. Three months later he regains consciousness in a makeshift operating room, just as doctors working for the Triad boss Johnny Vang are removing his heart, which is destined for a Triad leader named Poon Dong who needs a transplant. In its place they have fitted an artificial heart powered by an external battery pack.

Chev escapes and learns from Doc Miles, a surgeon who works for the mob, that once the external battery is gone, the internal battery will last only a short time. When the battery pack is destroyed in a crash, Chev must keep himself constantly charged by any means available, from jumper cables to static electricity generated by friction, while he tears through Los Angeles in pursuit of the men who stole his real heart. Along the way he reunites with Eve, now working as a stripper, gains an ally in Venus, the brother of his late informant, and finds himself targeted by a Mexican gang leader known as El Hurón as well as by the Triads. As his body repeatedly runs out of power, he faces ever more absurd and violent situations in a race to get his heart back.

The directors shot much of the film with lightweight prosumer high-definition camcorders, adding to its frenetic, video-game-like style and its deliberately outrageous, over-the-top humor.

Crank: High Voltage opened in April 2009 at number six at the North American box office and grossed about 34.6 million dollars worldwide. It was not screened for critics in advance but received mixed reviews, with 64 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 41.

documents.title: Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone
documents.original_title: ヱヴァンゲリヲン新劇場版：序
documents.overview: After the Second Impact, Tokyo-3 is being attacked by giant monsters called Angels that seek to eradicate humankind. The child Shinji's objective is to fight the Angels by piloting one of the mysterious Evangelion mecha units. A remake of the first six episodes of GAINAX's famous 1996 anime series. The film was retitled "Evangelion: 1.01" for its home video version and "Evangelion: 1.11" for a release with additional scenes.
documents.plot:
Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone is a 2007 Japanese animated science fiction film directed by Hideaki Anno and produced by Khara, a studio founded by Anno. The film is the first installment of the Neon Genesis Evangelion franchise's re-imagining, also known as "Rebuild of Evangelion."

The story takes place in 2015, three years after the events of the original Neon Genesis Evangelion series. Shinji Ikari, now a teenager, lives with his mother Yui and stepfather Gendo Ikari in Tokyo-3. Shinji's life is marked by loneliness and self-doubt, as he struggles to cope with the trauma of his past.

Shinji's existence changes when he receives a message from NERV, an organization that develops giant humanoid robots called Evangelions, to pilot the Evangelion Unit-01. Gendo Ikari, Shinji's stepfather, is the director of NERV and has been searching for Shinji, who possesses a unique connection to the Evangelion project.

Upon arrival at NERV headquarters, Shinji meets Rei Ayanami, a mysterious and stoic young woman who pilots the Evangelion Unit-00. As Shinji begins his training as an Evangelion pilot, he is forced to confront his emotional baggage and the harsh realities of his new role.

The story takes a dark turn when Shinji's mother, Yui, appears in a vision, revealing that she had been working on the Evangelion project before her death and that Shinji has a crucial role to play in its success. This revelation sets off a chain of events that leads to a catastrophic confrontation with the Angel, Sachiel.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of existentialism, psychological trauma, and the human condition. Shinji's struggles to come to terms with his past and find his place in the world are mirrored by the Evangelion Unit-01's own struggle to cope with its programming and purpose.

The climax of the film features a dramatic showdown between Shinji and Sachiel, which ultimately leads to the destruction of Tokyo-3. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience questioning the fate of the characters and the future of humanity.

Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone sets the stage for the Rebuild of Evangelion series, which continues to explore the complexities of Shinji's character and the world of Evangelion. The film's dark and introspective tone has become a hallmark of Anno's style, and its influence can be seen in many other anime productions.

Overall, Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that delves into the depths of human psychology and existential crisis. Its exploration of complex themes and characters has made it a cult classic among anime fans worldwide.

documents.title: Sixteen Candles
documents.tagline: When you're just sixteen anything can happen!
documents.overview: A teenage girl deals with her parents forgetting her birthday and a crush on her high school's heartthrob.
documents.plot:
Sixteen Candles is a classic American coming-of-age comedy film released in 1984, directed by John Hughes and produced by Universal Pictures.

The story revolves around Samantha "Sam" Baker (played by Molly Ringwald), a high school sophomore who is struggling to navigate her 16th birthday. Sam's life is marked by embarrassment and humiliation as she tries to fit in with her peers. Her parents are divorced, and her mother has remarried, making Sam feel like an outsider.

On the day of her birthday, Sam wakes up to find that her family has forgotten her special day. She feels unloved and unwanted, especially when her mother gives her a pair of white Keds as a gift instead of something more exciting. As she walks through school, Sam is subjected to ridicule and teasing from her classmates, who seem to be enjoying her misfortune.

However, things take a turn for the better when Sam meets Jake Ryan (played by Michael Schoeffling), a popular and charming student who becomes her crush. Despite their initial awkward encounter, Sam and Jake start to develop feelings for each other, but their social differences make it difficult for them to connect.

Meanwhile, Sam's life is further complicated by her ex-boyfriend Ted (played by Anthony Michael Hall), who still has feelings for her. As the day progresses, Sam must navigate a series of embarrassing and humiliating situations, including a disastrous dance with Ted and a awkward encounter with her mother's new husband.

Despite the ups and downs, Sam ultimately finds herself at the school dance, where she gets to experience the magic of Jake Ryan's presence. The film culminates in a romantic moment between Sam and Jake, as they share a kiss under the mistletoe.

Throughout the movie, John Hughes' signature wit and insight into teenage life shine through, capturing the complexities and nuances of adolescence with humor and sensitivity. The film's portrayal of high school cliques, social hierarchies, and first loves resonated with audiences in the 1980s and continues to be relatable today.

Sixteen Candles is widely regarded as one of the greatest teen movies of all time, and its influence can still be seen in many modern coming-of-age films. The movie's success helped establish John Hughes as a major voice in American cinema, and it remains a beloved classic among fans of 80s cinema.

documents.title: Another Cinderella Story
documents.tagline: Once upon a time....can happen again.
documents.overview: A guy who danced with what could be the girl of his dreams at a costume ball only has one hint at her identity: the Zune she left behind as she rushed home in order to make her curfew. And with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity in front of him, he sets out to find his masked beauty.
documents.plot:
Another Cinderella Story is a 2008 American romantic comedy film directed by Mary Lambert and written by Elizabeth M. Nystrom. The movie is a modern retelling of the classic fairy tale Cinderella, set in a high school environment.

The story follows Sam Montgomery (played by Selena Gomez), a shy and awkward teenager who is constantly bullied by her stepmother, Fiona (played by Jane McNeill), and her two spoiled stepsisters, Brianna (played by Meaghan Martin) and Taylor (played by Sofia Carson). Despite being treated poorly at home, Sam is a talented singer-songwriter who dreams of attending the prestigious West Beverly High School.

One day, Sam's life changes when she meets Austin Ames (played by Drew Seeley), a popular and charming student who becomes her love interest. However, their social differences make it difficult for them to connect. Meanwhile, Fiona and Brianna are trying to sabotage Sam's chances of getting into the school's annual Spring Fling dance, which is being held at West Beverly High.

As the story unfolds, Sam discovers that Austin has a crush on her and asks her to be his date for the Spring Fling. However, things get complicated when Fiona and Brianna try to ruin their relationship by spreading rumors about Sam's past. Despite the obstacles, Sam and Austin grow closer, and they share a romantic dance at the Spring Fling.

However, just as things are starting to look up for Sam and Austin, Fiona reveals that she has been hiding a secret: she is actually a former pop star who was dumped by her record label. Feeling jealous and insecure, Fiona tries to sabotage Sam's relationship with Austin once again.

In the end, Sam and Austin confess their love for each other, and they share a romantic kiss at the Spring Fling. The movie ends on a happy note, with Sam and Austin looking forward to their future together.

Throughout the movie, the film pays homage to the classic Cinderella story, while also incorporating modern themes and characters. The movie features a mix of music, comedy, and romance, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Another Cinderella Story is a fun and lighthearted take on the classic fairy tale, with a strong female lead and a charming love interest. The movie's message about perseverance and believing in oneself is inspiring and relatable, making it a great choice for viewers looking for a feel-good romantic comedy.

documents.title: The Pink Panther 2
documents.tagline: Inspect the unexpected.
documents.overview: When legendary treasures from around the world are stolen, including the priceless Pink Panther Diamond, Chief Inspector Dreyfus is forced to assign Inspector Clouseau to a team of international detectives and experts charged with catching the thief and retrieving the stolen artifacts.
documents.plot:
The Pink Panther 2 is a 2009 American comedy mystery film directed by Harald Zwart, the eleventh installment in the Pink Panther series and the sequel to the 2006 film The Pink Panther. Steve Martin, Jean Reno and Emily Mortimer reprise their roles, joined by Alfred Molina, Andy García, Aishwarya Rai, Lily Tomlin and John Cleese, who replaces Kevin Kline as Chief Inspector Dreyfus.

When a master thief known as the Tornado, who has been inactive for a decade, resurfaces and begins stealing priceless treasures around the world, an international "Dream Team" of detectives is assembled to catch him. Inspector Jacques Clouseau, demoted to parking duty by Dreyfus, is reluctantly assigned to the team, and protests that leaving France will leave the Pink Panther diamond unguarded. As soon as he leaves the country, the diamond is stolen. Clouseau joins Inspector Pepperidge of Scotland Yard, the Italian detective Vincenzo Brancaleoni, the Japanese electronics expert Kenji Mazuto and the Indian criminologist Sonia Solandres, while Vincenzo flirts with Clouseau's beloved Nicole.

In Rome, the team questions the fence Alonso Avellaneda, but rules him out because he lacks the bullet wound the Tornado received years earlier. Clouseau and his partner Ponton bungle an attempt to bug a restaurant meeting, setting the place on fire for a second time, and when the Tornado steals the Pope's ring, public anger and Clouseau's blunders get him voted off the team. The Tornado, identified as Laurence Milliken, is then found dead, apparently by suicide, with a note claiming he destroyed the Pink Panther. DNA confirms his identity, and the team celebrates, but Clouseau is unconvinced.

At the celebration, Clouseau declares that Sonia, Milliken's former lover, is the real thief. Confronted, she shoots Clouseau, but the bullet ricochets off his medal, and after a chaotic chase she destroys the diamond in defiance before being arrested. Clouseau then reveals that she destroyed a fake: he had secretly replaced the museum's diamond with a replica before leaving France. Since the Tornado, an expert on gems, would have known the stone was fake, the suicide note must have been forged. Clouseau marries Nicole in a ceremony officiated by Dreyfus, which ends in typical chaos.

The film was poorly received by critics, who felt it wasted its talented cast on lame slapstick; Rotten Tomatoes reported 13% approval. It grossed about $76 million worldwide against a $70 million budget.

documents.title: Barbie as The Princess & the Pauper
documents.original_title: Barbie as The Princess & the Pauper
documents.overview: Princess Anneliese finds an unexpected friendship when she meets her humble look-alike, Erika.
documents.plot:
Barbie as the Princess and the Pauper is a 2004 computer-animated musical fantasy film directed by William Lau and produced by Mainframe Entertainment for Mattel. Released direct to video in September 2004 and premiered on Nickelodeon that November, it was the first musical entry in the Barbie film series, featuring a set of original songs. Kelly Sheridan voices both lead characters, Princess Anneliese and the commoner Erika, with Melissa Lyons, Julie Stevens, Mark Hildreth and Mark Luna among the supporting voice cast. The story is loosely inspired by Mark Twain's 1881 novel The Prince and the Pauper.

In a small kingdom, a blonde princess and a brunette girl from a poor family are born at the same moment and grow up looking almost identical. Years later, Anneliese learns that her mother, Queen Genevieve, has arranged for her to marry the wealthy King Dominick in order to save the realm from bankruptcy, even though Anneliese is secretly in love with her tutor, Julian. Erika, meanwhile, works as an indentured seamstress at Madame Carp's dress shop to pay off her parents' debts, while dreaming of a career as a singer and a chance to see the world.

The kingdom's financial troubles are no accident: the queen's scheming adviser Preminger has been secretly emptying the royal gold mines. Learning of the planned wedding, he plots to have Anneliese disappear so that he can pretend to rescue her and claim her hand, and with it the throne. After a chance meeting in the village, the princess and the pauper discover their striking resemblance, and when Anneliese is abducted by Preminger's henchmen, Nick and Nack, Erika is persuaded to pose as the princess at the palace to buy time. While Erika struggles with royal life and grows close to King Dominick, Anneliese, Julian and a pair of loyal animal companions work to expose Preminger and return home before the wedding.

Built around themes of duty, freedom and following one's dreams, the film contrasts Anneliese's sense of obligation with Erika's longing for independence, and it ends with each young woman choosing her own path. Its songs, including "Free" and "I'm a Girl Like You", became among the best-known in the Barbie series.

The film was a commercial success on home video and is often regarded by fans as one of the strongest entries in the Barbie franchise.

documents.title: Barbie in the Nutcracker
documents.overview: "Barbie" stars as Clara in this animated retelling of the classic Christmas ballet, complete with Tchaikovsky soundtrack and ballet choreography.
documents.plot:
Barbie in the Nutcracker is a 2001 Canadian-American computer-animated fantasy film co-produced by Mainframe Entertainment and Mattel Entertainment and distributed by Artisan Home Entertainment. Loosely based on E. T. A. Hoffmann's 1816 story "The Nutcracker and the Mouse King" and set to music from Tchaikovsky's ballet, it was Barbie's first film since two 1987 television specials and her first CGI film. Kelly Sheridan voices Barbie, with Kirby Morrow and Tim Curry also in the cast.

Barbie tells a story to her little sister, Kelly, who is struggling with a ballet solo. In 1890s Germany, Clara lives with her stern grandfather, Drosselmeyer, and her little brother, Tommy. On Christmas Eve their aunt Elizabeth gives Clara a nutcracker, which Tommy breaks in a tussle. Clara mends it and falls asleep by the tree, and at midnight she wakes to see the Nutcracker come to life and fight the army of the wicked Mouse King, who shrinks her with magic. The Nutcracker, also under the Mouse King's spell, takes Clara to find the Sugarplum Princess, the only one who can undo their enchantments, and an owl gives Clara a locket that will send her home when opened.

Helped by snow fairies, they reach the Nutcracker's homeland, Parthenia, where they learn that its heir, Prince Eric, has vanished. Major Mint and Captain Candy rescue them from the Mouse King's soldiers and explain that the old king had made the Mouse temporary ruler until the careless prince grew responsible. Clara realizes that the Nutcracker is Eric, transformed when the Mouse decided to keep the throne. On the journey they free trapped flower fairies and defeat a rock giant. The Princess's island proves a trap, and the Mouse King's bat henchman, Pimm, carries off the Nutcracker, Mint and Candy, but Clara frees them at the Mouse King's castle. In the duel, the Mouse King's spell rebounds and shrinks him. Clara kisses the wounded Nutcracker, restoring Eric, and is revealed to be the Sugarplum Princess herself. As Eric is crowned, the Mouse King steals and opens the locket, sending Clara home. Her grandfather dismisses her tale, but Aunt Elizabeth arrives with a young man named Eric, who asks Clara to dance. Inspired, Kelly masters her solo.

Released on VHS on October 2, 2001, and on DVD later that month, the film sold more than 3.5 million units and generated $150 million in total sales including merchandise. The New York Times called it a diverting, inoffensively sweet tale for very small children.

documents.title: Hotel for Dogs
documents.tagline: No stray gets turned away.
documents.overview: Placed in a foster home that doesn't allow pets, 16-year-old Andi and her younger brother, Bruce, turn an abandoned hotel into a home for their dog. Soon other strays arrive, and the hotel becomes a haven for every orphaned canine in town. But the kids have to do some quick thinking to keep the cops off their tails.
documents.plot:
Hotel for Dogs is an American family comedy of 2009 directed by Thor Freudenthal and written by Jeff Lowell, Bob Schooley and Mark McCorkle, based on Lois Duncan's 1971 novel. Emma Roberts and Jake T. Austin star as Andi and Bruce, orphaned siblings in foster care who secretly shelter stray dogs in an abandoned hotel, with Johnny Simmons and Kyla Pratt as the pet store workers Dave and Heather, Troy Gentile as their neighbor Mark, Lisa Kudrow and Kevin Dillon as the uncaring foster parents Lois and Carl Scudder, and Don Cheadle as the social worker Bernie Wilkins.

Andi and Bruce con a pawnbroker to buy food for their dog Friday and end up at the police station, from which Bernie collects them and returns them to the Scudders, who care little for the children or the dog. When Friday is caught by animal control, the siblings learn from Dave and Heather to check the pound, where they cannot claim him without a parent, so they bribe a guard to get him back. On the way home they find Friday sheltering in a derelict hotel along with two strays, a tiny Boston Terrier and an English Mastiff, whom they name Georgia and Lenny. When Andi tells Dave that her parents often rescue dogs, he asks her to take three more that no one wants.

With Mark's help, the friends fix up the hotel to meet the dogs' needs and rescue more strays to fill it. Dave invites Andi to a party, but it is ruined when an old acquaintance reveals that she and Bruce are orphans, while Bruce, caught stealing a hairdryer, is questioned by the Scudders. Escaping, he finds the hotel in chaos, and the Scudders follow him there. The dogs are sent to the pound to be put down, the children are taken by the police, and when the Scudders refuse to take them back, Bernie must place them in separate foster homes. Friday escapes and leads Dave, Heather and Mark to the siblings, while Bernie, exploring the hotel, finds a remaining dog and understands what the children have built. Andi and Bruce break into the pound and free the dogs, who head back to the hotel, followed by crowds, reporters and police. Bernie wins everyone over by describing the family of dogs and their stories, the children are allowed to keep them, and Bernie and his wife adopt Andi and Bruce. With the city's support, the hotel reopens as a place to adopt or board dogs.

Shot in Los Angeles and Universal City, California, from November 2007, the film was released on 16 January 2009 and grossed about $117 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed.

documents.title: Species: The Awakening
documents.tagline: Irresistible beauty. Unstoppable instincts.
documents.overview: A scientist, Dr Holander, takes his niece Miranda to Mexico in an attempt to reverse the effects of the alien DNA he used to create her. However the treatment goes horribly wrong, and sets Miranda on a killing spree as she sets out to find a mate.
documents.plot:
Species: The Awakening is a 2007 American science fiction action thriller made for television, the fourth and final installment of the Species franchise. Directed by Nick Lyon, it stars Ben Cross as Tom Hollander, Helena Mattsson as Miranda Hollander, Dominic Keating as Forbes McGuire and Marlene Favela as Azura. It is the only film in the series without Natasha Henstridge.

Miranda, a college professor, lives with her "uncle" Tom, a museum employee. She can read a book by touch, and believes her parents died in an accident when she was a baby. After her birthday she collapses and, in the hospital, transforms into an alien and kills several people. Tom injects her with human hormones, drives her to Mexico and admits the truth. Miranda was created in an experiment combining human and alien DNA, which he carried out with his college friend Forbes, and the hormone injections he has given her since childhood suppressed her alien nature. In Mexico they find Forbes, who lives with Azura, another hybrid who is his assistant and lover. Forbes finds that Miranda will die within days. The only cure is fresh human DNA, which requires a human sacrifice that Miranda refuses to accept.

Tom goes looking for a donor and is mugged, and Azura subdues the mugger. The procedure extends Miranda's life, but Forbes has bungled it, and her alien side grows dominant. She makes advances to Tom, then seduces and kills the innkeeper Calderon, another hybrid, after learning he is sterile, and hunts for a mate in a bar wearing a red dress stolen from a singer. Forbes gives Tom a near-lethal sedative, while Azura, resentful of Tom's arrival, attacks him in a church. Miranda lures Forbes to an abandoned warehouse, mates with him and then kills him in her alien form. Back at the house, an X-ray reveals a hybrid child growing rapidly inside her. Miranda says she does not want to become entirely alien. Azura attacks in alien form, and in the battle she fatally impales Miranda before Tom kills her with a shotgun. Miranda thanks Tom for giving her a life and dies in her human form. Tom opens the gas in Forbes's house and walks away as it explodes.

The film premiered on the Sci Fi Channel on September 29, 2007, and was released on DVD on October 2. Reviews were sparse, but Den of Geek wrote that it exceeded expectations for a direct-to-DVD release.

documents.title: Everyone's Hero
documents.tagline: No matter where life takes you, always keep swingin'
documents.overview: A boy begins a grand journey to return Babe Ruth's baseball bat before the deciding game of the 1932 World Series comes to a close.
documents.plot:
Everyone's Hero is an animated film that tells the story of a young boy named Metro Man Jr., who dreams of becoming a superhero like his idol, Metro Man. However, when Metro Man is killed in action, Metro Man Jr. discovers that he has inherited not only his father's powers but also his legacy.

The main theme of Everyone's Hero revolves around the idea of identity and self-discovery. Metro Man Jr. must navigate his new role as a superhero while also coming to terms with his own sense of purpose and belonging. As he struggles to live up to his father's expectations, he learns valuable lessons about responsibility, courage, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

The film also explores the theme of grief and loss, particularly in the context of Metro Man Jr.'s relationship with his deceased father. The movie shows how Metro Man Jr. grapples with the weight of his father's legacy and the pressure to fill his shoes, all while trying to find his own path in life.

Furthermore, Everyone's Hero touches on the idea of heroism and what it means to be a true hero. The film challenges traditional notions of heroism by presenting a more nuanced and relatable portrayal of a superhero, one who is flawed but ultimately driven by a desire to do good.

documents.title: This Christmas
documents.tagline: You can't exchange family.
documents.overview: This year Christmas with the Whitfields promises to be one they will never forget. All the siblings have come home for the first time in years and they've brought plenty of baggage with them. As the Christmas tree is trimmed and the lights are hung, secrets are revealed and family bonds are tested. As their lives converge, they join together and help each other discover the true meaning of family.
documents.plot:
This Christmas is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the complexities of family relationships and the power of love and forgiveness during the most wonderful time of the year.

At its core, the movie delves into the theme of second chances, as the main character, Quinn Cummings' character, Lisa, navigates her complicated past with her estranged father. The film masterfully weaves together a narrative that highlights the importance of confronting one's demons and making amends in order to heal old wounds.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Lisa struggles to find her place within her family and navigate her own sense of purpose. Through her journey, the film shows how embracing our flaws and imperfections can lead to a deeper understanding of ourselves and those around us.

Furthermore, This Christmas celebrates the beauty of forgiveness and the transformative power of love. The movie demonstrates that even in the most difficult relationships, there is always room for growth, understanding, and ultimately, reconciliation.

Overall, This Christmas is a poignant exploration of the human experience, reminding us that it's never too late to make amends, forgive ourselves and others, and find our way back to those we love.

documents.title: Undisputed II: Last Man Standing
documents.tagline: Wrongfully Accused. Unjustly Imprisoned. Now He's Fighting Back.
documents.overview: Heavyweight Champ George "Iceman" Chambers is sent to a Russian jail on trumped-up drug charges. In order to win his freedom he must fight against the jailhouse fighting champ Uri Boyka in a battle to the death. This time he is not fighting for a title, he is fighting for his life!
documents.plot:
Undisputed II: Last Man Standing is a 2006 American sports drama film directed by Eric Laneuville, starring Ving Rhames and Michael Rapaport. The movie serves as the sequel to the 2002 film Undisputed.

The story takes place in the fictional prison of Red Rock Penitentiary, where former heavyweight champion Chris Vaughn (Ving Rhames) is serving a life sentence for murder. Vaughn is considered one of the toughest inmates in the prison, and his reputation precedes him.

Upon arrival at Red Rock, Vaughn is met with hostility by the other inmates, who are intimidated by his presence. However, he soon befriends a young inmate named Jake Tyler (Michael Rapaport), who becomes his ally and confidant.

As tensions rise within the prison, a new inmate named Victor "The Bull" DeSoto (Tito Ortiz) arrives, seeking revenge against Vaughn for a past encounter that left him severely injured. DeSoto is a formidable fighter with a personal vendetta against Vaughn, and he sets his sights on taking down the former champion.

As the story unfolds, Vaughn must navigate the treacherous world of prison politics, where alliances are forged and broken at will. He must also confront his own demons and the consequences of his past actions, all while trying to protect himself and those around him from DeSoto's wrath.

Throughout the film, the tension between Vaughn and DeSoto builds towards a climactic showdown in the prison's boxing ring. The two fighters engage in an intense and brutal battle, with Vaughn ultimately emerging victorious but at great cost.

In the end, Vaughn is forced to confront the reality of his own mortality and the harsh realities of life behind bars. Despite his tough exterior, he begins to show signs of vulnerability and humanity, particularly in his relationship with Jake Tyler.

The film's conclusion sets the stage for a potential third installment, leaving audiences wondering what will become of Vaughn and DeSoto in the future. Overall, Undisputed II: Last Man Standing is a gripping and intense drama that explores the darker side of human nature and the consequences of violence.

documents.title: Hulk vs. Wolverine
documents.overview: Department H sends in Wolverine to track down a mysterious beast known by the US Military as the Hulk, who is rampaging across the Canadian wilderness. Surveying the extent of the damage to a destroyed town, Wolverine notices a toxic scent as well as the smell of gunpowder. He is then deployed to the wilderness to resume tracking the creature.
documents.plot:
Hulk vs. Wolverine is a 2009 American animated superhero short feature produced by Marvel Studios and released by Lionsgate on 27 January 2009 as one half of the direct-to-video double feature Hulk Vs., alongside Hulk vs. Thor. Running a little under forty minutes, it was directed by Frank Paur from a script by Craig Kyle and Christopher Yost, with animation by the Japanese studio Madhouse and music by Guy Michelmore. The story draws on The Incredible Hulk #181, the 1974 comic that gave Wolverine his first full appearance, and the film shares its continuity with the series Wolverine and the X-Men.

The Canadian agency Department H sends Wolverine to track down the Hulk, a creature blamed for destroying the town of Elkford in British Columbia. Surveying the ruins, Wolverine picks up a strange chemical scent and the smell of gunpowder before heading into the wilderness after his quarry. The two collide in a savage, prolonged brawl that ends only when both are knocked out by tranquiliser darts. They wake as prisoners of Weapon X, the secret programme that once bonded adamantium to Wolverine's skeleton and conditioned him as a living weapon, scenes revealed in flashbacks to his escape years earlier. Its leader, a scientist known as the Professor, explains that his own soldiers, not the Hulk, wrecked Elkford while hunting the creature, and that he intends to erase Bruce Banner's mind and reprogram the Hulk as the most powerful weapon on Earth.

Wolverine breaks free, frees Banner and fights his way through his former teammates of Team X: Sabretooth, Lady Deathstrike, Omega Red and the wisecracking mercenary Deadpool. When the drugged Banner cannot transform on his own, Wolverine provokes the change by force, and the unleashed Hulk smashes the assassins and the facility, which collapses in an explosion. Emerging from the flames, Hulk and Wolverine square off to resume their fight, and a scene after the credits shows a battered Deadpool surviving the wreckage.

The voice cast includes Steve Blum as Wolverine, Fred Tatasciore as the Hulk, Bryce Johnson as Banner, Nolan North as Deadpool, Tom Kane as the Professor, Mark Acheson, Janyse Jaud and Colin Murdock. First screened at San Diego Comic-Con in 2008, the film was praised for its intense action, unusually bloody violence for a Marvel cartoon and Deadpool's scene-stealing humour, though some reviewers found the Weapon X backstory a distraction from the title bout.

documents.title: Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li
documents.original_title: Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li
documents.tagline: Some fight for power. Some fight for us.
documents.overview: When a teenager, Chun-Li witnesses the kidnapping of her father by wealthy crime lord M. Bison. When she grows up, she goes on a quest for vengeance and becomes the famous crime-fighter of the Street Fighter universe.
documents.plot:
Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li is a 2009 American martial arts action film based on Capcom's Street Fighter video game series, directed by Andrzej Bartkowiak from a screenplay by Justin Marks. A non-canonical spin-off and tie-in to Street Fighter IV, and the second live-action adaptation after the 1994 film, it stars Kristin Kreuk as Chun-Li, Neal McDonough as M. Bison, Chris Klein as Interpol agent Charlie Nash, Michael Clarke Duncan as Balrog, Moon Bloodgood as detective Maya Sunee, Taboo as Vega and Robin Shou as Gen.

As a child, Chun-Li moves from San Francisco to Hong Kong with her family and trains in wushu under her father, Xiang. One night, the criminal organization Shadaloo abducts her father in front of her. Years later, Chun-Li has abandoned martial arts and become a celebrated concert pianist. After her mother dies of cancer, she receives a mysterious scroll written in ancient Chinese.

Meanwhile in Bangkok, the ruthless M. Bison seizes control of Shadaloo with the help of the masked assassin Vega, and police detective Maya Sunee teams up with Interpol agent Charlie Nash to investigate a massacre of crime families. Following the scroll's message, Chun-Li travels to Bangkok in search of a man named Gen. After days of fruitless searching, a fight with local gangsters leaves her unconscious, and she is rescued by Gen, a former associate of Bison, who offers to help her find her father on condition that she complete her martial arts training. Learning that Bison is forcing property owners to sign over their land so that Shadaloo can operate in the open, Chun-Li sets out to disrupt his plans, including a mysterious shipment known as the White Rose, and to confront the man who destroyed her family.

The film presents itself as an origin story for one of the series' most popular characters, focusing on revenge and self-discovery rather than the tournament format of the games.

Released on February 27, 2009, the film was not screened in advance for critics and opened in ninth place. It was a box office bomb, grossing 12.8 million dollars against a 50 million dollar budget, and was savaged by reviewers, holding just 3 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus blamed its shallow plot and miscast performers.

documents.title: Pom Poko
documents.tagline: A Fantastic Tale Of Survival
documents.overview: The Raccoons of the Tama Hills are being forced from their homes by the rapid development of houses and shopping malls. As it becomes harder to find food and shelter, they decide to band together and fight back. The Raccoons practice and perfect the ancient art of transformation until they are even able to appear as humans in hilarious circumstances.
documents.plot:
Pom Poko is a 1994 animated fantasy film written and directed by Isao Takahata, produced by Studio Ghibli. The movie is loosely based on a novel of the same name by Kenji Miyazawa.

The story takes place in post-World War II Japan, where a group of tanuki (Japanese raccoons) live in harmony with humans in a small village called Kusakabe. The main character, Koriki, is a young tanuki who lives with his family and friends in the forest. However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when a group of developers threatens to destroy their home to build a new highway.

The tanuki, led by Koriki's father, decide to take action against the humans and their plans. They use their magical powers to transform into various objects, such as cars, buildings, and trees, in order to sabotage the construction process. The tanuki also begin to develop human-like characteristics, such as wearing clothes and using tools.

As the battle between the tanuki and humans intensifies, Koriki becomes increasingly conflicted about his role in the conflict. He begins to question whether it is right for him to fight against the humans, who are simply trying to build a new life for themselves. Meanwhile, a young girl named Satsuki moves into the village with her family, and Koriki finds himself drawn to her kindness and compassion.

The plot thickens as the tanuki's actions become more aggressive, causing chaos in the village. The humans, led by a ruthless developer named Tanaka, retaliate against the tanuki, leading to a series of escalating confrontations. Koriki is forced to confront his own identity and the true nature of the conflict between humans and animals.

In the end, Koriki and Satsuki form an unlikely alliance, and together they find a way to resolve the conflict peacefully. The tanuki realize that their actions have caused harm to both themselves and the humans, and they must make amends. The movie ends with the tanuki and humans coming together in a spirit of mutual understanding and respect.

Throughout the film, Takahata explores themes of environmentalism, identity, and the complexities of human-animal relationships. The animation is stunning, with intricate details and textures that bring the world of the tanuki to life. Pom Poko is a powerful and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider their place in the natural world.

Overall, Pom Poko is a beautifully crafted film that showcases Studio Ghibli's unique blend of fantasy, adventure, and social commentary. With its richly detailed world-building and complex characters, it is a must-see for fans of animation and environmentalism.

documents.title: The Pixar Story
documents.tagline: Documentary about the history of Pixar animation
documents.overview: A look at the first years of Pixar Animation Studios - from the success of "Toy Story" and Pixar's promotion of talented people, to the building of its East Bay campus, the company's relationship with Disney, and its remarkable initial string of eight hits. The contributions of John Lasseter, Ed Catmull and Steve Jobs are profiled. The decline of two-dimensional animation is chronicled as three-dimensional animation rises. Hard work and creativity seem to share the screen in equal proportions.
documents.plot:
The Pixar Story is a 2007 American documentary directed by Leslie Iwerks about the history of Pixar Animation Studios. Narrated by Stacy Keach, it features interviews with key figures in the studio's history, including Ed Catmull, Steve Jobs and John Lasseter, as well as animators, directors, executives and voice actors. An early version premiered at the Sonoma Film Festival in 2007, followed by a limited theatrical run and broadcasts on the Starz network in the United States and BBC Two in the United Kingdom. It was later included as a bonus feature on home-video releases of WALL-E.

The film traces Pixar's origins to the computer graphics research of the 1970s, when Catmull and other pioneers worked to create images on computers at a time when few believed the technology could produce feature films. It follows Lasseter's early career as an animator at Disney, where his enthusiasm for computer animation was not shared by the studio, and his move to the computer division of Lucasfilm, where he joined Catmull's team. In 1986, Steve Jobs bought the division from George Lucas and founded Pixar as an independent company, initially selling computer hardware and creating short films and commercials to showcase its technology.

The documentary recounts the company's financial struggles in its early years and its breakthroughs with short films such as Luxo Jr. and Tin Toy, which won an Academy Award. It follows the long and difficult production of Toy Story (1995), the first feature-length computer-animated film, which became a phenomenal success, and then the studio's string of hits, including A Bug's Life, Toy Story 2, Monsters, Inc., Finding Nemo and The Incredibles. Along the way, it explores Pixar's creative culture, built on collaboration and storytelling, the near-disastrous production of Toy Story 2, and the strained relationship with Disney that culminated in Disney's acquisition of Pixar in 2006, with Catmull and Lasseter put in charge of Disney's own animation studios.

The Pixar Story received generally positive reviews, with an 86 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on seven reviews. Iwerks, a granddaughter of Disney animation pioneer Ub Iwerks, was praised for her access to the studio's archives and key personnel, and for presenting the studio's story through the voices of the people who built it.

documents.title: Ace Ventura Jr: Pet Detective
documents.overview: "I will try to be normal" 12-year-old Ace Ventura Jr. promises. Thats cool, except whats normal for him is finding missing mutts, kidnapped kitties or gone gators and creating hilarious chaos every step of the way.
documents.plot:
Ace Ventura Jr.: Pet Detective, also known as Ace Ventura 3, is a 2009 American made-for-television family comedy directed by David Mickey Evans and written by Jeff Sank, Jason Heimberg and Justin Heimberg. A stand-alone sequel to Ace Ventura: Pet Detective (1994) and Ace Ventura: When Nature Calls (1995), it was made without the involvement of star Jim Carrey or the earlier films' writers. Josh Flitter stars as Ace Ventura Jr., with Emma Lockhart, Art LaFleur as his grandfather Rex, Reed Alexander, William Haze and Ann Cusack as his mother Melissa. Filmed in Orlando, Florida, beginning in September 2007, it was released on DVD in March 2009.

Ace Ventura Jr. is the son of the eccentric pet detective Ace Ventura, who disappeared when the boy was a baby. Ace Jr. is determined to follow in his father's footsteps, to the dismay of his mother, Melissa, who repeatedly tries to discourage him. At school he is investigating a series of pet thefts, including the disappearance of a rare emerald koi belonging to Laura, a girl on whom he has a crush. He relies on his friend A-Plus, a science whiz with a laboratory in his locker, for forensic analysis, and like his father he is openly mocked by his classmates.

When Ting Tang, a baby panda newly arrived at the Miami Zoo, is stolen, Melissa, who was responsible for preparing the enclosure for the cub and its mother, is blamed and arrested. With her parents away on a cruise, Melissa reluctantly calls on Ace Jr.'s paternal grandfather, Rex Ventura, to look after him, and Rex begins training his grandson in the family trade so he can clear his mother's name. At the trial, Ace Jr. proves that the footprints found in the panda's pen could not have been made by Melissa, but the case against her is not dropped. Together with Laura, A-Plus and his grandfather, Ace Jr. follows clues across Miami, using his father's unorthodox methods, his talent for communicating with animals and plenty of slapstick, to track down the real culprits behind the panda's kidnapping and the school pet thefts, and to rescue Ting Tang before it is too late.

The film received largely negative reviews from critics and fans of the original films, who found it a pale imitation lacking Carrey's comic energy, though some considered it harmless entertainment for young children. Flitter's broad physical comedy was nonetheless noted as an attempt to channel the spirit of the original character.

documents.title: The Girl Next Door
documents.tagline: In this town, murder became the neighborhood game.
documents.overview: In a quiet suburban town in the summer of 1958, two recently orphaned sisters are placed in the care of their mentally unstable Aunt Ruth. But Ruth's depraved sense of discipline will soon lead to unspeakable acts of abuse and torture that involve her young sons, the neighborhood children, and one 12-year-old boy whose life will be changed forever.
documents.plot:
The Girl Next Door, also released as Jack Ketchum's Evil, is a 2007 American psychological horror film directed by Gregory M. Wilson from a screenplay by Daniel Farrands and Philip Nutman, based on Jack Ketchum's 1989 novel. The novel was inspired by the real-life torture and murder of Sylvia Likens, and the film is dedicated to her. It stars Blythe Auffarth as Meg Loughlin, Blanche Baker as Ruth Chandler and Daniel Manche as the young David Moran.

In the present day, David, now an adult, witnesses a man struck by a car in New York and tries to save him, an event that brings back memories of the summer of 1958. That summer, as a boy, he meets and falls for Meg, a teenager who, with her disabled younger sister Susan, has come to live with their aunt Ruth and her sons, Willie, Ralphie and Donny, after their parents died in a car crash.

Ruth is popular with the neighborhood children, letting them drink beer and smoke in her house, but she treats Meg with growing cruelty, starving her, berating her and punishing her sister in front of her. When Meg reports the abuse to a local police officer, nothing is done, and Ruth's punishment becomes even more brutal. Meg is tied up in the basement, where Ruth, her sons and the neighborhood children begin to torture her, treating the abuse as entertainment. David, torn between fear, complicity and his feelings for Meg, is unable to tell his parents what is happening. As the violence escalates, he must find the courage to help Meg and Susan escape before it is too late.

The film is an unflinching depiction of child abuse and the way group cruelty and silence enable it, focusing on the moral failure of the bystanders as much as on the abusers.

The film received mixed reviews, with a 67 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 29. The New York Times was harshly critical, while Stephen King praised it as the first authentically shocking American film he had seen since Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer, warning that viewers who are easily disturbed should not watch it.

documents.title: District 13: Ultimatum
documents.overview: Damien and Leito return to District 13 on a mission to bring peace to the troubled sector that is controlled by five different gang bosses, before the city’s secret services take drastic measures to solve the problem.
documents.plot:
District 13: Ultimatum is a French science fiction action film directed by Patrick Maisse, released in 2009. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2004 film District 13 and is based on the comic book series of the same name.

The story takes place five years after the events of the first film. In this time, the resistance movement led by Leito (played by Damiano Dattoli) has managed to drive the corrupt government out of District 13, a heavily fortified and impoverished neighborhood in Paris. However, a new threat emerges when a mysterious virus begins to spread across the city, turning people into violent, zombie-like creatures.

As the situation spirals out of control, Leito is forced to flee District 13 with his team, including his sister, Sartana (played by Karine Gounon), and his friend, Jérôme (played by David Belle). They embark on a perilous journey across Paris, fighting off hordes of infected civilians and government forces who seek to exploit the chaos for their own gain.

Meanwhile, a new character, Captain Duffaut (played by Nicolas Duval-Beaulieu), is introduced as the leader of an elite military unit tasked with containing the outbreak. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Duffaut's true intentions are far from altruistic, and he will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

Throughout the film, Leito and his team face numerous challenges as they navigate the treacherous landscape of Paris. Along the way, they encounter other survivors, including a young woman named Zole (played by Eva Green), who becomes a key player in their quest to find a cure for the virus.

As the stakes grow higher, Leito's group discovers that the source of the outbreak is a mysterious facility hidden beneath the city. There, they uncover evidence of a sinister government conspiracy involving the creation and release of the virus as a means of controlling the population.

In the climactic final act, Leito and his team launch a daring raid on the facility, fighting off Duffaut's forces in a desperate bid to stop the spread of the virus. In the end, they succeed in destroying the facility and finding a cure for the outbreak, but not before many lives have been lost.

The film concludes with Leito reflecting on the sacrifices made by his team and the lessons learned from their experiences. As he looks out over the ruins of Paris, he knows that there is still much work to be done to rebuild and restore hope to the city.

Overall, District 13: Ultimatum is a gripping and intense action film that explores themes of resistance, sacrifice, and redemption in the face of overwhelming adversity. With its breakneck pacing, stunning stunts, and memorable characters, it is a must-see for fans of science fiction and action movies.

documents.title: Wonder Woman
documents.tagline: Courageous princess. Fierce warrior. Legendary superhero.
documents.overview: On the mystical island of Themyscira, a proud and fierce warrior race of Amazons have raised a daughter of untold beauty, grace and strength: Princess Diana. When an Army fighter pilot, Steve Trevor, crash-lands on the island, the rebellious and headstrong Diana defies Amazonian law by accompanying Trevor back to civilization.
documents.plot:
Wonder Woman is a 2009 American animated superhero film based on the DC Comics character, the fourth entry in the DC Universe Animated Original Movies line. Directed by Lauren Montgomery from a screenplay by Gail Simone and Michael Jelenic, and produced by Bruce Timm, its story is loosely based on George Pérez's "Gods and Mortals" storyline, which relaunched the character in 1987. Keri Russell voices Princess Diana, with Nathan Fillion as Steve Trevor, Alfred Molina as Ares, Virginia Madsen as Hippolyta and Rosario Dawson as Artemis.

In ancient times, the Amazons, led by their queen, Hippolyta, rise up against Ares, the god of war. Hippolyta kills Ares's son, but before she can kill Ares himself, Zeus intervenes, and Ares is instead bound in magic bracelets that cut him off from the power he draws from violence. The Amazons are granted the hidden island of Themyscira, where they live in eternal youth, guarding Ares as their prisoner. Hippolyta is also given a daughter, Diana, whom she sculpts from sand and brings to life with her blood.

Centuries later, Diana longs to see the outside world. When the American fighter pilot Steve Trevor crash-lands on the island, the Amazons decide that he must be escorted home. Forbidden to compete for the task, Diana enters in disguise and wins. Meanwhile, the Amazon Persephone, seduced by Ares, kills Diana's friend Alexa and frees him. Diana and Steve fly to New York City in his invisible jet to track Ares down. They defeat one of Ares's demigod sons, Deimos, and follow his trail to a gateway to the underworld, where Ares escapes after persuading Hades to remove his bracelets.

Ares raises an army and attacks Washington, D.C. Diana and Steve are joined by the Amazons, and Ares summons the spirits of dead Amazons to fight their sisters, until the undead Alexa reveals a chant that breaks his hold over them. Hippolyta kills Persephone. Under Ares's influence, the President launches a nuclear missile at Themyscira, which Steve shoots down with the invisible jet. Diana finally defeats Ares, who is condemned to serve Hades in the underworld. Hippolyta allows Diana to return to the world of men as an ambassador, and she settles in New York with Steve as Wonder Woman.

Released directly to video on March 3, 2009, the film received mostly positive reviews, with IGN praising its humor, action and voice performances, particularly Fillion's.

documents.title: The Cat Returns
documents.tagline: It’s not so bad being a cat, now is it?
documents.overview: Young Haru rescues a cat from being run over, but soon learns it's no ordinary feline; it happens to be the Prince of the Cats.
documents.plot:
The Cat Returns is a 2002 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hiroyuki Morita, produced by Toho.

The story follows Haru, an 11-year-old girl who lives in a small town with her father. On the way to school one day, she meets a mysterious cat named Muta, who is actually a prince from the Cat Kingdom. The Cat Kingdom is a parallel world where cats are the dominant species, and humans are their subjects.

Muta tells Haru that he has been sent by his mother, the Queen of Cats, to invite her to the royal ball in honor of her upcoming birthday. However, Muta's visit coincides with a severe storm that causes him to lose his way back home. As a result, he is forced to take refuge in Haru's house.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Muta has fallen in love with Haru and wants to stay with her forever. However, their social differences make their relationship impossible, as cats are not allowed to interact with humans in the Cat Kingdom.

The Queen of Cats, who is also Muta's mother, disapproves of his relationship with Haru and orders him to return home immediately. But Muta refuses to leave Haru behind, leading to a confrontation between the two.

In the end, Haru decides to take Muta back to the Cat Kingdom to meet her parents and face the Queen's wrath. However, upon arrival, she discovers that the Queen is not as cruel as she seemed. Instead, she is a kind and loving ruler who wants her son to be happy.

The Queen reveals that she has been searching for Haru all along, as she is the only human who can see beyond the superficial differences between humans and cats. She decides to allow Muta to stay with Haru, but also warns him that their relationship will not be easy and may require sacrifices from both parties.

As the story concludes, Haru and Muta return home, where they are welcomed by Haru's father. However, it is clear that Haru has undergone a significant transformation, having gained a new perspective on life and her relationships with others.

Throughout the film, Morita explores themes of identity, culture, and acceptance, highlighting the importance of understanding and empathy in breaking down social barriers. The animation is beautiful and vibrant, bringing the fantastical world of the Cat Kingdom to life in a way that is both captivating and endearing.

Overall, The Cat Returns is a charming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the beauty of diversity and the power of love to overcome even the most daunting obstacles.

documents.title: Role Models
documents.tagline: They're about to get more than they plea-bargained for.
documents.overview: Two salesmen trash a company truck on an energy drink-fueled bender. Upon their arrest, the court gives them a choice: do hard time or spend 150 service hours with a mentorship program. After one day with the kids, however, jail doesn't look half bad.
documents.plot:
Role Models is a 2008 American comedy film directed by David Wain and written by Paul Sado and David Wain. The movie stars Seann William Scott, Christopher Mintz-Plasse, Jane Lynch, and Bobby Moynihan.

The main themes of Role Models (2008) include:

1. Friendship: The movie explores the unlikely friendship between two middle-aged men, Danny O'Neill (Seann William Scott) and Albert Bandino (Christopher Mintz-Plasse), who become role models for a group of misfit kids.
2. Redemption: Both Danny and Albert are struggling with their own personal demons, and through their journey as role models, they find a chance to redeem themselves and make amends for past mistakes.
3. Coming-of-age: The movie tackles themes of growing up, self-discovery, and finding one's place in the world, particularly for the young characters who look up to Danny and Albert as role models.
4. Social responsibility: The film highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and being a positive influence on others, especially children.

The movie follows Danny and Albert as they are forced by their company, Auto Parts Inc., to become role models for a group of troubled kids from a local youth center. As they navigate this new role, they learn valuable lessons about themselves, their relationships, and the importance of being good role models.

Throughout the film, Wain uses humor, satire, and heart to explore these themes, often poking fun at societal norms and expectations while also delivering a message about the power of positive influence and redemption.

documents.title: Red Cliff Part II
documents.tagline: Destiny Lies In The Wind
documents.overview: The battle of Red Cliff continues and the alliance between Xu and East Wu is fracturing.  With Cao Cao's massive forces on their doorstep, will the kingdoms of Xu and East Wu survive?
documents.plot:
Red Cliff Part II is a 2009 epic war film produced and directed by John Woo, the second half of his two-part adaptation of the Battle of Red Cliffs (208–209 AD), fought at the end of the Eastern Han dynasty on the eve of the Three Kingdoms period. An international co-production led by Lion Rock and China Film Group, it continues directly from the first part and stars Tony Leung Chiu-wai as the commander Zhou Yu and Zhang Fengyi as the warlord Cao Cao, with Takeshi Kaneshiro, Chang Chen, Zhao Wei, Hu Jun and Lin Chi-ling. Woo said the film was only about half based on history, favoring how audiences felt about the battle over strict accuracy.

As Cao Cao's vast army and fleet camp across the river from Red Cliff, Lady Sun Shangxiang, sister of the warlord Sun Quan, infiltrates the enemy camp and sends details to the strategist Zhuge Liang by carrier pigeon. When typhoid strikes his troops, Cao Cao sends the corpses on rafts to spread the plague to his enemies, and a disheartened Liu Bei withdraws, apparently breaking the alliance, while Zhuge Liang stays to help Sun Quan. Zhou Yu and Zhuge Liang wager their lives on rival tasks: eliminating Cao Cao's naval commanders Cai Mao and Zhang Yun, and obtaining 100,000 arrows. Zhuge Liang sends straw-covered boats to draw enemy fire and collects the arrows, while Zhou Yu deceives the envoy Jiang Gan, and together the ruses lead Cao Cao to execute his two admirals. Predicting that the winds will turn to blow from the southeast, the allies plan a fire attack on Cao Cao's interlocked fleet, as Zhou Yu's wife Xiaoqiao goes alone to Cao Cao's camp and stalls him with an elaborate tea ceremony. When the wind rises at night, burning boats ram the enemy ships while Liu Bei's forces, whose departure was a ruse, strike on land. By dawn the fleet is destroyed, and after a costly assault on Cao Cao's main camp, the allies gain the upper hand but spare his life.

Red Cliff Part II was released in China on 7 January 2009, and the 142-minute film completed a two-part version running nearly five hours, while Western audiences first saw a single abridged 148-minute cut in 2009. It was shot in Beijing and Hebei. The Hollywood Reporter praised Woo's ordering of the narrative and kinetic action, which propel the film to a thundering climax, and Variety, calling the second half heavier on action yet rich in human interest, judged the two-part version one of the great Chinese costume epics of all time.

documents.title: Mickey's Once Upon a Christmas
documents.overview: Mickey, Minnie, and their famous friends Goofy, Donald, Daisy and Pluto gather together to reminisce about the love, magic and surprises in three wonder-filled stories of Christmas past.
documents.plot:
Mickey's Once Upon a Christmas is a direct-to-video animated film produced by Disney Television Animation, released on November 2, 1999. The movie features three separate stories, each with its own unique characters and plotlines.

**Story 1: "Donald Duck: Stuck on Christmas"**

The first story revolves around Donald Duck, who is struggling to find the perfect Christmas gift for his nephews, Huey, Dewey, and Louie. However, every time he tries to buy a gift, it ends up being ruined or misplaced. As Christmas Eve approaches, Donald becomes increasingly stressed and anxious about not being able to get the perfect present.

In the end, Donald's nephews help him realize that the true spirit of Christmas is not about gifts, but about spending quality time with loved ones. The story features Donald's signature temper tantrums and comedic misadventures, making it a heartwarming and entertaining tale for both children and adults.

**Story 2: "Mickey & Minnie's Gift of the Magi"**

The second story is an adaptation of O. Henry's classic short story "The Gift of the Magi." In this version, Mickey Mouse and Minnie Mouse are struggling to make ends meet during the holiday season. Mickey wants to buy Minnie a special Christmas present, but he doesn't have enough money.

Mickey decides to sell his beloved watch to buy Minnie a beautiful necklace. Meanwhile, Minnie is trying to find the perfect gift for Mickey, but she can't afford it either. In a surprising twist, Mickey uses the money from selling his watch to buy Minnie a stunning necklace, and Minnie uses her long, curly hair to sell and buy Mickey a special present.

The story highlights the selfless love and sacrifice that defines the relationship between Mickey and Minnie, making it a beautiful and poignant tale for the holiday season.

**Story 3: "Goofy's Howl-O-Ween"**

The third and final story takes place on Halloween night, but with a Christmas twist. Goofy is excited to celebrate his favorite holiday, but he becomes worried that he won't be able to find any presents for his friends. As the night wears on, Goofy's anxiety grows, and he starts to feel like he's lost his way.

In the end, Goofy discovers that the true spirit of Christmas (or Halloween) is about being with the people you care about and having fun together. The story features Goofy's signature goofiness and comedic antics, making it a lighthearted and entertaining tale for all ages.

Overall, Mickey's Once Upon a Christmas is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the values of love, kindness, and generosity during the holiday season.

documents.title: Ben 10: Secret of the Omnitrix
documents.overview: After a battle in a power plant, Ben notices something strange is happening with the omnitrix, but doesn't tell anyone. Tetrax arrives, and tells them the omnitrix is broadcasting a self destruct signal. Tetrax and Ben go to find the creator of the omnitrix to fix the omnitrix before it destroys itself and the universe along with it. Gwen stows away to help her cousin.
documents.plot:
Ben 10: Secret of the Omnitrix is a 2007 animated science fiction comedy-adventure film directed by Alex Zamm and produced by Cartoon Network Studios. The movie follows the story of Ben Tennyson, a 10-year-old boy who discovers a powerful alien device called the Omnitrix.

The main themes of Ben 10: Secret of the Omnitrix include:

1. **Self-discovery**: Ben's journey is also one of self-discovery as he learns to control and understand the power of the Omnitrix, which allows him to transform into different alien creatures.
2. **Responsibility**: As Ben becomes more confident in his abilities, he must learn to take responsibility for using the Omnitrix for good, rather than letting it consume him.
3. **Friendship**: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and teamwork as Ben works with his grandfather Max and cousin Gwen to stop the villainous Vilgax from obtaining the Omnitrix.
4. **Power and corruption**: The film explores the dangers of power and corruption, as Vilgax's desire for control and domination drives him to seek out the Omnitrix at any cost.

The movie follows Ben's initial discovery of the Omnitrix, his subsequent battles against Vilgax, and his ultimate realization that he must learn to use the device responsibly in order to save the world.

documents.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
documents.tagline: Based on the Worldwide Best Seller
documents.overview: Swedish thriller based on Stieg Larsson's novel about a male journalist and a young female hacker. In the opening of the movie, Mikael Blomkvist, a middle-aged publisher for the magazine Millennium, loses a libel case brought by corrupt Swedish industrialist Hans-Erik Wennerström. Nevertheless, he is hired by Henrik Vanger in order to solve a cold case, the disappearance of Vanger's niece
documents.plot:
The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo (Swedish: Män som hatar kvinnor, literally "Men Who Hate Women") is a 2009 crime thriller directed by Niels Arden Oplev from a screenplay by Rasmus Heisterberg and Nikolaj Arcel, and produced by Søren Stærmose. It adapts the 2005 novel by Swedish writer Stieg Larsson, the first book in his Millennium series. Its sequels, The Girl Who Played with Fire and The Girl Who Kicked the Hornets' Nest, followed in September and November of the same year.

Journalist Mikael Blomkvist, co-owner of the magazine Millennium, loses a high-profile libel case brought by billionaire Hans-Erik Wennerström and faces a prison sentence. He is then hired by Henrik Vanger, the elderly patriarch of a wealthy family, to find out what happened to his niece Harriet, who vanished during a family gathering in 1966. Henrik suspects that one of his relatives, several of whom had Nazi ties, is responsible. Meanwhile, Lisbeth Salander, a brilliant but troubled hacker who had been hired to run a background check on Blomkvist, endures abuse and rape by her legal guardian, Nils Bjurman, before turning the tables and blackmailing him to secure her independence.

Living on the Vanger estate, Blomkvist finds a list of names and numbers in Harriet's diary. Salander, secretly monitoring his files, recognizes them as Bible references and joins the investigation, linking them to a series of unsolved murders with antisemitic overtones. Suspicion falls on Harriet's brother, Martin, who captures Blomkvist and reveals that he and his late father committed the killings. Salander rescues Blomkvist, and Martin dies in a car crash. The pair then discover that Harriet is alive in Australia, having escaped abuse, and that she had sent Henrik pressed flowers each year as a sign. With Salander's help, Blomkvist publishes an exposé that brings down Wennerström, while Salander quietly takes his money and starts a new life under another identity.

Michael Nyqvist plays Blomkvist and Noomi Rapace plays Salander, with Sven-Bertil Taube as Henrik Vanger, Lena Endre as Erika Berger, Peter Haber as Martin and Peter Andersson as Bjurman. Critics were enthusiastic, with 85% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and particular praise for Rapace; Roger Ebert gave it four stars. It grossed over $104 million worldwide, and in 2010 the trilogy was expanded into a six-part television miniseries.

documents.title: Disney Princess Enchanted Tales: Follow Your Dreams
documents.original_title: Disney Princess Enchanted Tales: Follow Your Dreams
documents.tagline: An Adventure Fit For A Princess!
documents.overview: Princess Aurora and Princess Jasmine learn valuable life lessons in two short stories.
documents.plot:
Disney Princess Enchanted Tales: Follow Your Dreams is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores the importance of believing in oneself, embracing one's unique talents, and following one's passions. The movie delves into the theme of self-discovery, encouraging viewers to look within themselves for their own inner strength and potential.

The story follows a young girl named Giselle, who is struggling to find her place in the world. As she navigates through various challenges and obstacles, she learns valuable lessons about perseverance, friendship, and the power of positive thinking. The film also touches on the theme of letting go of fear and embracing change, as Giselle discovers that sometimes, taking risks and stepping out of one's comfort zone can lead to incredible opportunities.

One of the main themes of the movie is the idea that everyone has a unique gift or talent that sets them apart from others. The film encourages viewers to recognize and nurture their own special talents, rather than trying to emulate someone else's path. This theme is beautifully illustrated through Giselle's journey as she discovers her own strengths and passions.
