Humans and Terrians make peace, the humans build an enormous oxygen-filled tent city on Terra, and a statue is raised in Jim's honour.

Conceived as a live-action feature, it became fully animated with backing from Snoot Entertainment. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2007, won the top feature prize at the 2008 Ottawa International Animation Festival and was released in the United States in May 2009. Reviews were mixed, with 50% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Easy Virtue
documents.tagline: Let's Misbehave!
documents.overview: A young Englishman marries a glamorous American. When he brings her home to meet the parents, she arrives like a blast from the future - blowing their entrenched British stuffiness out the window.
documents.plot:
Easy Virtue is a 2008 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships, social class, and personal identity. The movie follows the story of Lanier, a charming but aimless young man who becomes infatuated with his cousin's fiancée, Lady Victoria, despite her seemingly shallow and materialistic nature.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lady Victoria is hiding a more vulnerable side beneath her polished exterior. Through their interactions, the film reveals themes of societal pressure, the constraints of social class, and the struggle for individuality in the face of external expectations.

The movie also delves into the tension between appearance and reality, as characters navigate the complexities of relationships and personal growth. The film's portrayal of a seemingly perfect facade hiding underlying insecurities and flaws adds depth to its exploration of these themes.

Ultimately, Easy Virtue is a nuanced commentary on the human experience, highlighting the challenges of navigating complex social dynamics, the importance of self-discovery, and the power of genuine connection in transcending superficial boundaries.

documents.title: Naruto: Ninja Clash in the Land of Snow
documents.original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO 大活劇! 雪姫忍法帖だってばよ!!
documents.overview: Naruto is thrilled when he is sent on a mission to protect his favorite actress, Yukie Fujikaze, on the set of her new movie, The Adventures of Princess Gale. But when the crew ventures out to film in the icy, foreboding Land of Snow, Yukie mysteriously flees! Naruto and his squad set off to find her... unaware that three Snow Ninja lie in wait, with a sinister purpose that will force Yukie to face her hidden past!
documents.plot:
Naruto the Movie: Ninja Clash in the Land of Snow is a 2004 Japanese animated martial arts fantasy adventure film based on Masashi Kishimoto's manga and the Naruto anime series, set after the series' 101st episode. Most of the television voice cast returns, with Junko Takeuchi voicing the hero, Naruto Uzumaki, alongside Chie Nakamura, Noriaki Sugiyama and Kazuhiko Inoue.

Naruto, Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno watch a film starring Yukie Fujikaze, which their teacher Kakashi Hatake has assigned as preparation for their next mission: protecting Yukie, famous as the heroine Princess Gale, during production of her next film. Yukie is in fact Koyuki Kazahana, princess of an island called the Land of Snow, whose father, Sosetsu, was murdered in a coup by her uncle Doto Kazahana. During filming, Doto's henchmen, clad in chakra armor, attack, and Team 7 holds them off for a time.

Doto eventually captures Koyuki, killing her bodyguards, who had revealed themselves in an attempt to restore her to the throne. Naruto boards Doto's ship to rescue her but is caught and fitted with a device that drains his chakra. Doto takes a crystal necklace Koyuki received from her father as a child, believing it to be the key to a treasure Sosetsu hid. Sasuke, Sakura and Kakashi infiltrate the fortress as Naruto and Koyuki escape, but Doto seizes the necklace and flees with the princess. While Naruto pursues him, Kakashi defeats the henchman Nadare Roga, and Sasuke and Sakura defeat Fubuki Kakuyoku and Mizore Fuyukuma. Doto finds the hidden treasure, a heat generator that can transform the island into a Land of Spring. Overpowered at first, Naruto is helped by Sasuke's Chidori, which weakens Doto's armor, and then unleashes a new Seven Colored Chakra Rasengan that kills Doto and activates a mirror that transforms the land. Koyuki reclaims her throne and tells Team 7 that her acting career will continue. Later, Sasuke and Sakura give Naruto a signed photo of the princess kissing him in the hospital, and the team prepares for a new adventure.

The film opened in Japan on August 21, 2004, and was released on DVD in April 2005. In 2007 it had one-day theatrical screenings in the United States, Canada and Australia and aired on Cartoon Network. Reviews were positive; Helen McCarthy called it a good introduction to the series' themes of persistence and self-belief and praised its frozen landscapes.

documents.title: Naruto: Legend of the Stone of Gelel
documents.original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- 大激突!幻の地底遺跡だってばよ
documents.overview: Naruto, Shikamaru, and Sakura are executing their mission of delivering a lost pet to a certain village. However, right in the midst of things, troops led by the mysterious knight, Temujin, attack them. In the violent battle, the three become separated. Temujin challenges Naruto to a fight and at the end of the fierce battle, both fall together from a high cliff...
documents.plot:
Naruto the Movie: Legend of the Stone of Gelel is a 2005 Japanese animated martial arts fantasy adventure film based on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga and anime franchise. It was directed by Hirotsugu Kawasaki, who wrote it with Yuka Miyata, for Studio Pierrot. In the original Japanese version Junko Takeuchi voices Naruto Uzumaki, Chie Nakamura voices Sakura Haruno, Showtaro Morikubo voices Shikamaru Nara, Akira Ishida voices Gaara, Gamon Kaai voices the knight Temujin and Akio Nojima voices Haido.

On a deserted beach at night, Gaara and the ninja of the Sand village fight bulky, robot-like armored soldiers, whose retreat reveals a huge warship offshore. Elsewhere, Naruto, Shikamaru and Sakura are searching for a missing pet ferret when they too are attacked by the armored soldiers and by Temujin, a mysterious knight. In the fight, Naruto and Temujin are both blown off a cliff, and a vast machine like a moving cathedral crashes through the forest nearby. Naruto and Temujin regain consciousness inside a traveling caravan led by Kahiko and Emina. The ferret, Nerugui, has also survived and grows fond of Temujin, annoying Kahiko, the client behind the mission. In the cathedral, Shikamaru finds a chamber of pods holding people and sees Temujin's associates, Kamira and Ranke, using them to put souls into the armored soldiers. Temujin returns to his side with Naruto and introduces him to Haido, who explains the Gelel Stone, a powerful mineral lost by a destroyed clan that he claims to seek in order to bring peace to the world. At the beach Gaara defeats Ranke, and Shikamaru and Sakura rescue Kahiko from Fugai. Temujin begins to recall his past, and after being captured and questioned he leaves the caravan with Kahiko. At the Gelel mine, Naruto and his friends confront Haido over the lives he is willing to sacrifice, and while Shikamaru, Sakura and Kankuro defeat Kamira and Fugai, Haido reveals to Temujin that he killed his parents. When Haido turns the stone's power on the now repentant Temujin, the soldiers come to his aid, and Naruto destroys the stone with a Rasengan and defeats Haido. As the mine collapses, Temujin uses a space-time hole to destroy it and Naruto saves him. In a mid-credits scene, Temujin and the children sail away.

Released in Japanese cinemas on 6 August 2005, the film earned ¥1.18 billion. In the United States it skipped theaters, premiering on Cartoon Network on 26 July 2008 before its DVD release three days later.

documents.title: Into the Blue 2: The Reef
documents.tagline: It's not another day at the beach.
documents.overview: When they're hired to recover the lost treasure of Columbus, married scuba divers Sebastian and Dani think they've hit the jackpot. But as they get closer to the fortune, the couple begins to suspect their employers have their own agenda. Hitting upon the real plan, the two come to the chilling realization that they may be expendable and that there's much more than riches at stake.
documents.plot:
Into the Blue 2: The Reef is an action-adventure film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, particularly in the context of greed and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie follows a group of divers who embark on a perilous journey to find a lost treasure, only to discover that they are not alone in the depths of the ocean.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the characters' obsession with the treasure is driven by a desire for wealth and power, which ultimately leads them down a path of destruction and chaos. The film's portrayal of the destructive nature of greed serves as a cautionary tale, highlighting the devastating consequences of allowing ambition to consume one's values and principles.

Furthermore, the movie explores themes of redemption and personal growth, as some characters are forced to confront their past mistakes and make amends in order to survive. Through its narrative, Into the Blue 2: The Reef suggests that it is never too late to change one's ways and seek forgiveness, offering a message of hope and renewal.

The film also touches on the idea of the dangers of playing with nature, as the characters' actions have unintended consequences that put them and others at risk. This serves as a reminder of the importance of respecting the natural world and the delicate balance of ecosystems.

Overall, Into the Blue 2: The Reef is a thrilling adventure that explores complex themes and moral dilemmas, leaving viewers to ponder the consequences of human actions in the face of nature's power.

documents.title: Barbie Fairytopia: Magic of the Rainbow
documents.original_title: Barbie Fairytopia: Magic of the Rainbow
documents.overview: Elina goes to a fairy school to learn dancing and fairy magic. The spring of the fairy land is soon threatened by evil Laverna who intends to prevent fairies from performing the annual vital rainbow dance. Elina must stop quarreling with her fellow students and unite them to save the first bud of the spring.
documents.plot:
Barbie Fairytopia: Magic of the Rainbow, also known as Barbie: Magic of the Rainbow, is a 2007 computer-animated fantasy film directed by William Lau and written by Elise Allen. The tenth film in the Barbie series and the third and final installment of the Fairytopia trilogy, it features Kelly Sheridan as the voice of Elina, with Lee Tockar, Kathleen Barr, Christopher Gaze and Tabitha St. Germain. It was released direct-to-video in March 2007 and distributed internationally by Universal Pictures Video.

Elina, now celebrated for twice defeating the wicked Laverna, is invited to become an apprentice of the guardian fairy Azura at the Crystal Palace, where she will learn the Flight of Spring, the annual ritual that brings the season's first rainbow to life. She meets six fellow apprentices: Linden, a fairy who can talk to animals; Shimmer, a tiny and arrogant pixie; Lumina, a moon fairy who can glimpse the future; Sunburst, a sparkle fairy who resents Elina's fame; the vain Faben; and Glee, a cheerful wood nymph who becomes Elina's best friend. Glee's puffball, Dizzle, falls for Elina's companion Bibble.

Unknown to the apprentices, Laverna, the jealous sister of the Enchantress, is plotting to disrupt the Flight of Spring and plunge Fairytopia into a winter lasting ten years. Elina excels in her early lessons, which increases Sunburst's hostility, and a quarrel between the two gets them both reprimanded by Azura. Escaping her exile, Laverna disguises herself as an enchanted frog, tricking Elina and Linden into breaking the spell and freeing her. The guardians refuse to believe their warning, since Laverna has left a decoy in her place in the bogs, although Azura takes it seriously. Laverna then captures Sunburst and assumes her appearance to slip into the palace, where she poisons all the guardians and leaves them in a deep sleep. With the guardians helpless, the Enchantress calls on the young apprentices to perform the ritual themselves, and Elina and her companions must learn to trust each other and work together to create the rainbow and defeat Laverna.

The film won two Leo Awards in 2007, for best animation program or series and best overall sound in an animation program or series, and William Lau was nominated for best direction. It concluded the Fairytopia storyline begun with Barbie: Fairytopia (2005) and Barbie: Mermaidia (2006).

documents.title: Legally Blondes
documents.overview: Moving from England to California, the youngest cousins of Elle Woods must defend themselves when their schools reigning forces turn on the girls and try to frame them for a crime.
documents.plot:
Legally Blondes is an American teen comedy of 2009 directed by Savage Steve Holland, a spin-off and the third instalment of the Legally Blonde franchise, made for home video with Reese Witherspoon, the star of the earlier films, as a producer. The British twins Milly (Camilla) and Becky Rosso star as Annie and Izzy Woods, cousins of Elle Woods, with Brittany Curran as their rival Tiffany Donohugh, Bobby Campo as Chris Lopez, Chad Broskey as Justin Whitley and Lisa Banes as headmistress Elsa Higgins.

When their cousin Elle becomes a successful lobbyist and moves to Washington, D.C., the English twins Izzy and Annie move into her house in Southern California. To their dismay, they are enrolled at Pacific Preparatory, Elle's old school. There they meet Chris Lopez, a scholarship student who is instantly smitten with Annie, and Tiffany Donohugh, the spoiled daughter of one of the school's wealthy benefactors. Tiffany pretends to be their friend, then humiliates them by telling their classmates that they are at Pac Prep on partial scholarships. The twins befriend the other scholarship students and set about changing the snobbish culture of the school, while Izzy tries to help Chris win Annie over.

Before long Chris and Izzy are accused of cheating on a history test and set out to clear themselves. Discovering that Tiffany's boyfriend Justin has a master key to every door in the school and that Tiffany holds a passcode to all of its computers, which her father donated, the twins conclude that the pair stole the answers from the teacher's computer to frame them. During the student court hearing, Justin locks Izzy in a bathroom, so Annie must conquer her fear of public speaking and pose as her sister; even when Izzy returns, Annie keeps up the masquerade to finish the case. As she sums up the plot, the twins' supporters click their pens to goad Justin, who hates the sound, and he angrily admits that he framed Chris and Izzy for Tiffany. Tiffany confesses too, insisting that her family's status as founders and donors puts her beyond punishment, but Headmistress Higgins expels both of them. In the end Annie dances with Chris and Izzy with Brad, who helped them in court. The twins and their friends become popular, Tiffany and Justin are cut off by their families and sent to public school, and Tiffany's friend Ashley vows revenge.

Released on DVD by 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment in April 2009 and later shown on ABC Family, the film drew lukewarm reviews.

documents.title: State of Play
documents.tagline: Find the Truth
documents.overview: When a congressional aide is killed, a Washington, D.C. journalist starts investigating the case involving the Representative, his old college friend.
documents.plot:
State of Play is a 2009 American thriller film directed by Kevin Macdonald and written by Matthew Michael Carnahan. The movie stars Russell Crowe, Ben Affleck, and Robin Wright.

The story begins with Stephen Collins (Russell Crowe), a veteran journalist who works for the fictional Capitol News Network (CNN). Collins is investigating the death of a young woman named Darcy Spitz, who was found dead in her apartment. As Collins digs deeper into the case, he discovers that Spitz's death may be linked to a larger conspiracy involving corruption and murder.

Meanwhile, Tom Shayes (Ben Affleck), a young and ambitious journalist at Capitol News Network, is assigned to work with Collins on the story. Shayes is initially portrayed as a rival to Collins, but as they work together, their mutual respect for each other grows.

As Collins and Shayes dig deeper into the case, they uncover evidence of a massive conspiracy involving corrupt politicians, corporate interests, and murder. The investigation leads them to a mysterious woman named Janine (Robin Wright), who is somehow connected to Spitz's death.

Throughout the movie, Collins and Shayes face numerous obstacles and challenges as they try to expose the truth behind Spitz's death. They are pursued by powerful forces, including corrupt politicians and corporate interests, who will stop at nothing to silence them.

As the investigation unfolds, Collins becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth, while Shayes begins to question his own motivations and loyalties. The two men's relationship is put to the test as they work together to expose the conspiracy.

In the end, Collins and Shayes finally uncover the truth behind Spitz's death, which leads them to a shocking revelation about Janine's connection to the conspiracy. The movie ends with Collins and Shayes reflecting on the cost of their investigation and the sacrifices they made in pursuit of the truth.

Overall, State of Play is a gripping thriller that explores themes of corruption, power, and the importance of investigative journalism. The movie features strong performances from its leads, particularly Crowe and Affleck, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

documents.title: 17 Again
documents.tagline: Who says you're only young once?
documents.overview: On the brink of a midlife crisis, 30-something Mike O'Donnell wishes he could have a "do-over." And that's exactly what he gets when he wakes up one morning to find he's 17 years old again. With his adult mind stuck inside the body of a teenager, Mike actually has the chance to reverse some decisions he wishes he'd never made. But maybe they weren't so bad after all.
documents.plot:
"17 Again" is a 2009 American fantasy comedy film directed by Burr Steers and written by Jason Smathius and Thomas Lennon. The movie stars Zac Efron, Matthew Perry, and Leslie Mann.

The story begins with Mike O'Donnell (Matthew Perry), a successful high school basketball coach who has it all - a loving wife, Maggie (Leslie Mann), two beautiful children, and a thriving coaching career. However, Mike's life takes an unexpected turn when he is involved in a car accident on his way to a game.

As a result of the accident, Mike finds himself transported back in time to his 17-year-old self (Zac Efron). Initially confused and disoriented, Mike soon realizes that he has been given a second chance at high school. He decides to take advantage of this opportunity to relive his teenage years and make amends for past mistakes.

Mike's new life as a 17-year-old is filled with excitement and nostalgia. He rekindles an old friendship with his former best friend, Ned Gold (Thomas Lennon), and catches the eye of his high school crush, Scarlett (Amy Poehler). However, Mike soon realizes that being 17 again comes with its own set of challenges.

As Mike navigates his new life, he must confront the consequences of his past actions. He learns to appreciate the present moment and to make better choices. Meanwhile, Maggie is struggling to cope with her husband's absence from their family, and their relationship begins to fray.

Throughout the movie, Mike's dual identity creates comedic situations as he tries to balance his life as a 17-year-old with his responsibilities as a coach and a husband. The film also explores themes of friendship, love, and redemption.

As the story unfolds, Mike must make a choice between staying in the past or returning to his present self. In the end, Mike decides to return to his own time, but not before he has learned valuable lessons about life, love, and the importance of appreciating the present moment.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note as Mike returns to his family, and they are reunited. Mike's experience as a 17-year-old has changed him, and he is now more grateful for the time he has with his loved ones. The film concludes with a sense of closure and new beginnings for Mike and his family.

Overall, "17 Again" is a lighthearted and entertaining movie that explores themes of identity, friendship, and redemption. With its talented cast and witty script, the film is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Call Me Claus
documents.tagline: If She's Going To Save Christmas, She's Got Some Big Shoes To Fill.
documents.overview: When Lucy Cullins, a successful but cranky producer at a home shopping network hires an actor named Nick to play Santa Claus on the network, she gets more than she bargained for.
documents.plot:
Call Me Claus is a heartwarming Christmas comedy that explores the theme of redemption and second chances. The story revolves around Santa Claus, who has grown disillusioned with his role as a bringer of joy and gifts to children. Feeling overwhelmed and unappreciated, he decides to leave the North Pole and start a new life in New York City.

As he navigates this unfamiliar world, he meets a kind-hearted woman named Carol Newman, who helps him rediscover the true meaning of Christmas and his purpose as Santa Claus. Through their relationship, the film highlights the importance of kindness, generosity, and compassion.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Santa struggles to reconcile his old life with his new one. As he learns to let go of his past and find a new sense of purpose, he becomes a more authentic and genuine version of himself.

Ultimately, Call Me Claus is a feel-good Christmas film that celebrates the power of love, forgiveness, and second chances. It's a story about finding your true self and rediscovering the magic of the holiday season.

documents.title: Lake Placid 2
documents.overview: Man-eating crocodiles return to the lake as two males and one aggressive female crocodile, which is protecting her nest, wreak havoc on the locals.
documents.plot:
Lake Placid 2 is an action-comedy horror film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around the dangers of playing with nature and the consequences of human arrogance. The movie delves into the idea of a seemingly idyllic setting being turned upside down when a monstrous creature emerges from the depths of Lake Placid.

The film also touches on the theme of small-town secrets and the hidden dangers that can lurk beneath the surface of seemingly tranquil communities. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the town's residents are not as innocent as they initially appear, and that there are darker forces at play.

Furthermore, Lake Placid 2 critiques the notion of scientific hubris and the dangers of underestimating the power of nature. The movie's portrayal of a team of scientists who underestimate the creature's intelligence and ferocity serves as a cautionary tale about the risks of playing with forces beyond human control.

Ultimately, the film is a thrilling adventure that combines elements of horror, comedy, and action, all while exploring themes of nature, community, and the dangers of underestimating the power of the unknown.

documents.title: Agent Cody Banks 2: Destination London
documents.tagline: Adventure is an attitude.
documents.overview: With all-new gadgets, high-flying action, exciting chases and a wisecracking new handler, Derek (Anthony Anderson), Cody has to retrieve the device before the world's leaders fall under the evil control of a diabolical villain.
documents.plot:
Agent Cody Banks 2: Destination London is an action-comedy film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around identity, loyalty, and self-discovery. The movie follows Cody Banks as he navigates his dual life as a teenage spy and a high school student.

At its core, the film delves into the complexities of growing up and finding one's place in the world. Cody is torn between his responsibilities as a spy and his desire to live a normal life with his friends and family. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for his journey, as he learns to balance his dual identities and forge his own path.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty, both personal and professional. Cody's relationships with his mentor, Agent Finbar, and his friends are put to the test as he navigates the world of espionage. The film highlights the importance of trust, friendship, and sacrifice in maintaining strong bonds.

Furthermore, Destination London explores the idea of identity and how it evolves over time. As Cody grows older, he begins to question his role as a spy and the expectations placed upon him by those around him. This introspection leads to a deeper understanding of himself and his place in the world, ultimately allowing him to forge a new path that aligns with his true desires.

Overall, Agent Cody Banks 2: Destination London is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses its action-packed plot to explore themes of identity, loyalty, and self-discovery.

documents.title: Bleach the Movie: The DiamondDust Rebellion
documents.original_title: 劇場版 BLEACH The DiamondDust Rebellion もう一つの氷輪丸
documents.overview: When an artifact known as the "King's Seal" is stolen during transport from Soul Society, Hitsugaya Toushirou is assigned to retrieve it. Toushirou goes missing after a battle with the thieves, leading Seireitei to suspect him of treachery. They order his immediate capture and execution. Unwilling to believe him capable of such a crime, Ichigo, Rangiku, Rukia, and Renji set out to find Toushirou.
documents.plot:
Bleach the Movie: The DiamondDust Rebellion is a Japanese animated science fantasy film based on the popular manga and anime series Bleach, created by Tite Kubo. The movie was produced by Pierrot and directed by Noriyuki Abe.

The story begins with Ichigo Kurosaki, a high school student who has the ability to see ghosts. He lives in Karakura Town, where spirits from the afterlife are drawn into the human world. One day, Ichigo meets Rukia Kuchiki, a Soul Reaper (a being tasked with guiding souls to the afterlife) who is injured by a Hollow (a malevolent spirit). To save her life, Ichigo absorbs the power of the Hollow's Reiatsu, allowing him to become a temporary Substitute Shinigami.

However, this act of substitution causes Ichigo to lose his powers as a Soul Reaper and gain the ability to see Hollows. Rukia is forced to return to the afterlife, leaving Ichigo to deal with the consequences of her injury. Meanwhile, a mysterious entity known as the "Hollows' King" begins to wreak havoc on Karakura Town, using its immense power to destroy everything in its path.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the Hollows' King is actually Sosuke Aizen, a former captain of the Gotei 13 (the Soul Reapers' organization) who has been manipulating events from behind the scenes. Aizen's true intentions are revealed: he seeks to gain control over the spiritual energy known as Reiatsu and use it to become invincible.

Ichigo, along with his friends Orihime Inoue, Yasutora "Chad" Sadoya, and Uryuu Ishida, sets out on a perilous journey to stop Aizen and save Karakura Town. Along the way, they encounter various allies and enemies, including other Soul Reapers and Hollows.

As the battle between Ichigo's group and Aizen's forces intensifies, it becomes clear that the fate of Karakura Town hangs in the balance. In a climactic showdown, Ichigo faces off against Aizen, using his unique abilities to try and defeat him. However, Aizen proves to be a formidable opponent, and the two engage in an epic battle.

In the end, Ichigo emerges victorious, but not without great cost. The movie concludes with Ichigo reflecting on the lessons he has learned and the sacrifices he has made to protect his friends and town. The DiamondDust Rebellion serves as a pivotal moment in the Bleach series, setting the stage for future story arcs and character developments.

Overall, Bleach the Movie: The DiamondDust Rebellion is an action-packed and emotionally charged film that explores themes of friendship, sacrifice, and the struggle between good and evil.

documents.title: Shutter
documents.original_title: ชัตเตอร์ กดติดวิญญาณ
documents.tagline: The most terrifying images are the ones that are real.
documents.overview: A young photographer Thun and his girlfriend Jane discover mysterious shadows in their photographs after fleeing the scene of an accident. As they investigate the phenomenon, they find other photographs contain similar supernatural images, that Thun's best friends are being haunted as well, and Jane discovers that her boyfriend has not told her everything. It soon becomes clear that you can not escape your past.
documents.plot:
Shutter (Thai: ชัตเตอร์ กดติดวิญญาณ, roughly "Shutter: Press to Capture Ghosts") is a 2004 Thai supernatural horror film directed by Banjong Pisanthanakun and Parkpoom Wongpoom. It stars Ananda Everingham as the photographer Tun, Natthaweeranuch Thongmee as his girlfriend Jane, and Achita Sikamana, and follows a couple who begin to experience paranormal events after a hit-and-run accident.

Driving home after a party, Jane runs over a young woman on a dark road. Tun stops her from getting out, and they flee, leaving the victim behind. Soon Tun, a professional photographer, finds mysterious white shadows and faces in his pictures, and Jane suspects they are the ghost of the girl they hit. Tun has suffered severe neck pain since the accident, and a doctor finds that he weighs twice his normal weight. Although he dismisses talk of a haunting, his college friends are also being disturbed by a strange presence. Jane learns that the girl was Natre, a shy student from Tun's college, and Tun admits that he had a secret relationship with her and that she threatened to kill herself when he ended it.

Tun witnesses his friend Tonn commit suicide and learns that two other college friends have also killed themselves. Convinced Natre's ghost is behind the deaths, he and Jane visit Natre's mother and find the girl's decomposing body in her bedroom: Natre had killed herself, and her mother could not bear to cremate her. After a proper funeral, Natre's ghost still confronts Tun, who falls from a fire escape. Back in Bangkok, Jane develops photographs that lead her to a hidden set of negatives behind Tun's bookcase, showing his dead friends sexually assaulting Natre. Tun admits that he took the photos and did nothing to stop the attack because of peer pressure, and Jane leaves him. Alone, Tun photographs every room of his apartment in search of Natre. When his camera goes off by accident, the picture reveals her sitting on his shoulders, the cause of his pain and extra weight. She covers his eyes and he falls from a window. Later, Jane visits Tun in hospital, where he sits slumped and unresponsive, and a reflection shows Natre still perched on his shoulders.

Shutter was a box office success. It was remade in English in 2008 under the same title, unofficially remade three times in India, as Photo in Telugu, Sivi in Tamil and Click in Hindi, and officially remade in Indonesia in 2025. Rotten Tomatoes reported 63% approval from critics.

documents.title: Wild Things: Diamonds in the Rough
documents.original_title: Wild Things: Diamonds in the Rough
documents.tagline: Bad girls just want to have fun.
documents.overview: Two young women will stop at nothing for one to gain a $4 million inheritance of two priceless diamonds, while two detectives try to thwart their plans, but find complications abound.
documents.plot:
Wild Things: Diamonds in the Rough, also known as Wild Things 3, is a 2005 erotic thriller television film directed by Jay Lowi. The sequel to Wild Things 2 (2004) and the third installment in the Wild Things series, it stars Sandra McCoy as Elena Sandoval, Sarah Laine as Marie Clifton, Dina Meyer as probation officer Kristen Richards and Brad Johnson, with Linden Ashby reprising his role from the previous film. Like the earlier films, it centers on an elaborate scheme of seduction, false accusations and double-crosses in the wealthy seaside community of Blue Bay.

Marie Clifton is due to inherit two valuable diamonds, known as the "mother and daughter", left to her by her late mother, but her stepfather, Jay Clifton, contests the will, claiming she is not mature enough, while secretly wanting the diamonds for himself. At a swim meet at Marie's high school, Jay meets Elena Sandoval, a towel girl, and invites her to Marie's eighteenth birthday party, where Marie attacks her. Jay takes Elena to one of his construction sites to comfort her, and Elena later accuses him of rape.

Detective Michael Morrison and Kristen Richards, Elena's probation officer, who was herself the victim of an unidentified rapist years earlier, take up the case, while the physician Dr. Chad Johnson testifies that Elena was assaulted. Under pressure, Jay withdraws his claim on the diamonds, giving Marie control of them. But Marie, Elena and Chad are secretly lovers working together to steal the diamonds. As Richards and Morrison grow suspicious and discover that Elena based her testimony on details of Richards's own assault, the conspirators begin to turn on one another in a series of betrayals, murders and twists over who will end up with the real diamonds.

The film follows the formula of the original Wild Things, with its scheming young characters, sexual content and twist ending.

Wild Things: Diamonds in the Rough premiered on Encore Mystery on February 19, 2005, and was released on DVD on April 26. David Nusair of Reel Film Reviews called it trashy but entertaining, delivering exactly what it promises. It was followed by Wild Things: Foursome in 2010.

documents.title: 12 Rounds
documents.tagline: Can you survive 12 rounds for the one you love?
documents.overview: When New Orleans Police Detective Danny Fisher stops a brilliant thief from getting away with a multimillion-dollar heist, the thief's girlfriend is accidentally killed. After escaping from prison, the criminal mastermind enacts his revenge, taunting Danny with 12 rounds of near-impossible puzzles and tasks that he must somehow complete to save the life of the woman he loves.
documents.plot:
12 Rounds is a 2009 American action thriller directed by Renny Harlin and produced by WWE Studios. Professional wrestler John Cena stars as New Orleans police officer Danny Fisher, with Aidan Gillen as the villain Miles Jackson, Ashley Scott, Steve Harris, Gonzalo Menendez, Brian J. White and Taylor Cole. The film follows a detective forced to complete a series of twelve deadly challenges in exchange for his kidnapped girlfriend's life. It was released in theaters in the United States by 20th Century Fox on 27 March 2009.

Miles Jackson, an international arms dealer and terrorist, is hiding in New Orleans while being pursued by the FBI, led by agents George Aiken and Ray Santiago. Patrol officer Danny Fisher and his partner Hank Carver become caught up in the operation, and Fisher manages to track down Jackson and his girlfriend and accomplice, Erica. During the arrest, Erica is accidentally killed, and Jackson swears revenge.

A year later, Fisher has been promoted to detective. Jackson, having escaped from prison, calls him on his cellphone and reveals that he has kidnapped Fisher's girlfriend, Molly Porter, to avenge Erica's death. To save her, Fisher must complete twelve "rounds" of challenges across the city within strict time limits. The game begins with the destruction of Fisher's house and continues with increasingly dangerous tasks, including a runaway streetcar, a free-falling elevator and a bomb strapped to Molly's body. Working with Carver and with the FBI agents, who distrust him at first, Fisher races through New Orleans solving Jackson's clues, while gradually realizing that the elaborate game may be a cover for a much larger plan involving a massive theft.

The film received generally negative reviews, with critics finding its plot implausible and derivative of Die Hard with a Vengeance, while acknowledging the scale of its action set pieces filmed on location in New Orleans. It grossed about $17 million worldwide and later performed better on home video, leading WWE Studios to produce several direct-to-video sequels starring other wrestlers, beginning with 12 Rounds 2: Reloaded in 2013.

documents.title: Bleach the Movie: Fade to Black
documents.original_title: 劇場版 BLEACH Fade to Black 君の名を呼ぶ
documents.overview: A mysterious reiatsu (spiritual particle) explosion occurs in the center of Seireitei in Soul Society, causing it to be destroyed. At the exact same time, a major change overwhelms Kuchiki Rukia, which leaves her losing something important inside. Urahara Kisuke sends Kurosaki Ichigo to Soul Society to investigate the disturbance. Upon reaching Seireitei, Ichigo is attacked by his ally shinigamis.
documents.plot:
Bleach: Fade to Black, I Call Your Name is a 2008 Japanese animated supernatural adventure film and the third film based on Tite Kubo's manga and anime series Bleach. Directed by Noriyuki Abe, it features the voices of Masakazu Morita as Ichigo Kurosaki and Fumiko Orikasa as Rukia Kuchiki, with Kentaro Ito, Aya Hirano and Hiroshi Kamiya. It premiered in Japan on December 13, 2008, between episodes 198 and 199 of the television series.

In the Soul Society, the scientist Mayuri Kurotsuchi is attacked in his laboratory by a mysterious pair of siblings carrying a scythe that erases memories. In his panic he damages a machine, causing a vast explosion of spiritual energy. The siblings then attack Rukia Kuchiki, wiping her memories, along with everyone's memories of her, and carry her off to the poor outer district of Rukongai.

In the human world, Ichigo, a Substitute Soul Reaper, briefly forgets Rukia too, but Kon, a modified soul unaffected by the memory loss, reminds him. When even the shopkeeper Kisuke Urahara fails to remember her, Ichigo and Kon travel to the Soul Society, where the captains of the Gotei 13 no longer recognise Ichigo and treat him as an intruder.

Rukia, meanwhile, awakens in Rukongai with no memory of her life as a Soul Reaper. The nameless brother and sister tell her that they were once her close friends and that she had promised to give them names. Ichigo briefly finds Rukia, but the siblings flee with her. Rukia's childhood friend Renji Abarai sides with Ichigo, and Urahara explains to the captains that the siblings are under the influence of a memory-erasing parasitic Hollow.

The siblings, believing that the Soul Reapers took Rukia from them long ago, plan to destroy the Soul Society with another of Kurotsuchi's machines. When Ichigo and Renji arrive, Rukia's memories return, and in rage the sister fuses herself, her brother and Rukia into a single dark, hollowfied being, as the machine turns into a monster. While Renji and Rukia's adoptive brother Byakuya destroy the monster, Ichigo frees Rukia with his own spiritual energy and destroys the Hollow.

The siblings, mortally wounded, are revealed to have been Rukia's childhood friends who died in poverty and later absorbed the Hollow in order to return to her. Before they die, Rukia finally gives them names, Homura and Shizuku, and Ichigo reminds her that her memories of them will endure. The film opened in the top three at the Japanese box office.

documents.title: Why Did I Get Married?
documents.tagline: Because we complete each other's sentences.
documents.overview: The film is about the difficulty of maintaining a solid relationship in modern times. Eight married college friends plus one other non-friend (all of whom have achieved middle to upper class economic status) go to Colorado for their annual week-long reunion, but the mood shifts when one couple's infidelity comes to light. Secrets are revealed and each couple begins to question their own marriage
documents.plot:
Why Did I Get Married? is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of marriage and relationships. The movie masterfully weaves together several key themes, including the struggle for identity, the fragility of relationships, and the quest for personal growth.

At its core, Why Did I Get Married? explores the tension between individuality and conformity within marriages. The characters are forced to confront their own insecurities and desires, which often lead them to question whether they have made the right choices in their lives. This theme is skillfully intertwined with the idea of identity, as each character grapples with who they are outside of their relationships.

The film also sheds light on the fragility of relationships, highlighting how even the most seemingly strong bonds can be tested by the pressures of everyday life. The characters' interactions and conflicts serve as a catalyst for introspection, revealing the cracks that can form in even the most loving partnerships.

Ultimately, Why Did I Get Married? is a movie about personal growth and transformation. Through their experiences, the characters are forced to confront their own flaws and weaknesses, leading them on a journey of self-discovery and healing. The film's exploration of these themes serves as a powerful reminder that relationships require effort, communication, and a willingness to grow and evolve together.

Overall, Why Did I Get Married? is a nuanced and thought-provoking film that offers a candid look at the complexities of marriage and relationships.

belongs_to_collection.name: Why Did I Get Married Collection

documents.title: Jacquou the Rebel
documents.overview: In 1815, young Jacquou lives an idyllic peasant life with his parents in the Périgord region of France.  But one day, his childhood happiness is cruelly ended when his father is arrested, after a dispute with the arrogant Count de Nansac.  With both his parents dead, Jacquou is adopted by Bonal, a kind priest, under whose influence he grows into an assured, morally upright young man.  Now an adult, Jacquou has one desire.  To repay the Count de Nansac for the evil he once inflicted on his parents...
documents.plot:
Jacquou the Rebel is a 2007 French drama film directed by Michel Deville. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Jean Giono, published in 1904.

The main theme of Jacquou the Rebel revolves around the struggle between individual freedom and societal expectations. The protagonist, Jacquou, is a young shepherd who lives in rural France during the late 19th century. He is portrayed as an outcast, rejected by his community due to his unconventional behavior and refusal to conform to traditional norms.

Throughout the film, Jacquou's character embodies the spirit of rebellion against the oppressive forces that seek to control him. His actions are driven by a desire for autonomy, self-expression, and a sense of belonging. The movie explores the tension between Jacquou's inner world and the external constraints imposed upon him by society.

The film also touches on themes of isolation, loneliness, and the human need for connection. Jacquou's relationships with others are complex and often fraught, reflecting his struggles to find acceptance and understanding in a world that seems determined to reject him.

Ultimately, Jacquou the Rebel is a poignant exploration of the human condition, delving into the complexities of individuality, nonconformity, and the search for meaning in a seemingly indifferent world.

documents.title: Summer Days with Coo
documents.overview: A small, lone Kappa miraculously survives over 200 years into modern day Japan, when he is found by young Koichi. Coo, who is secretly adopted by Koichi's family, searches with his new human friend for unpopulated places in hopes of finding any remaining of his kind.
documents.plot:
Summer Days with Coo (Japanese: Kappa no Kū to Natsuyasumi, literally "Summer Holidays with Coo the Kappa") is a 2007 Japanese animated film written for the screen and directed by Keiichi Hara, based on two novels by Masao Kogure. It tells the story of a young kappa, a water creature from Japanese folklore, and the effect he has on an ordinary suburban family in modern Tokyo. Kazato Tomizawa, Takahiro Yokokawa, Naoki Tanaka and Tamaki Matsumoto are among the voice cast.

Two centuries ago, a young kappa's father is killed after an encounter with a samurai, and as the child weeps the ground opens up and swallows him. In present-day Tokyo, schoolboy Kōichi Uehara, who has been pressured by his friends into teasing a quiet classmate named Sayoko Kikuchi, finds a stone in a muddy ditch and brings it home, where it turns out to contain the kappa, still alive. The family names him Coo because he cannot remember his real name, and he quickly becomes part of the household, although Kōichi's little sister Hitomi takes longer to warm to him. Coo discovers that he can talk telepathically with the family dog, Ossan, who has a painful past of his own. Hoping to learn where Coo came from, Kōichi takes him on a summer trip to the countryside, where a house spirit tells Coo that he may be the last of his kind. When they return, news of a kappa sighting has spread across Japan, and journalists and photographers camp outside the family's house. Kōichi's father, Yasuo, agrees to let Coo appear on a television talk show, which brings an encounter with a cryptid expert who resembles the samurai of long ago and who displays a relic connected to Coo's father, a moment that leads to grief, chaos and a desperate chase through the city. Through his friendship with Coo, Kōichi slowly becomes kinder, especially toward Kikuchi, while Coo must decide where he truly belongs.

The film received several honors. It won the Best Animation Film award at the 2008 Mainichi Film Awards, the Grand Prize for Animation at the 11th Japan Media Arts Festival and the feature film category at the 2008 Tokyo Anime Award, and it was nominated for Best Animation Film at the Japan Academy Prize and for Best Animated Feature Film at the 2007 Asia Pacific Screen Awards.

documents.title: The Battle of Algiers
documents.tagline: The Revolt that Stirred the World!
documents.overview: Tracing the struggle of the Algerian Front de Liberation Nationale to gain freedom from French colonial rule as seen through the eyes of Ali from his start as a petty thief to his rise to prominence in the organisation and capture by the French in 1957. The film traces the rebels' struggle and the increasingly extreme measures taken by the French government to quell the revolt.
documents.plot:
The Battle of Algiers is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of colonialism, resistance, and the human cost of war. Set against the backdrop of Algeria's struggle for independence from France in the 1950s, the movie delves into the intricate web of relationships between the Algerian people, their French colonizers, and the local resistance fighters.

At its core, The Battle of Algiers is a nuanced portrayal of the brutal realities of colonialism, where the lines between good and evil are often blurred. The film masterfully captures the sense of desperation and frustration that drives individuals to take up arms against an oppressive regime. Through the eyes of the Algerian people, we witness the devastating consequences of war on civilians, including the loss of loved ones, displacement, and the erosion of cultural identity.

The movie also explores the complexities of resistance movements, highlighting the tensions between different factions and ideologies within the Algerian nationalist movement. The film's portrayal of the National Liberation Front (FLN) as a multifaceted organization, driven by both idealistic and pragmatic motivations, adds depth to the narrative.

One of the most striking aspects of The Battle of Algiers is its use of cinematic techniques to convey the chaos and disorder of war. The film's innovative editing style, combined with its stark black-and-white cinematography, creates a sense of urgency and immediacy that draws the viewer into the heart of the conflict.

Ultimately, The Battle of Algiers is a powerful anti-war statement that challenges viewers to confront the human cost of violence and the complexities of resistance movements. Through its thought-provoking narrative and masterful direction, the film continues to resonate with audiences today, offering a searing indictment of colonialism and a testament to the resilience of the human spirit in the face of oppression.

documents.title: The Soloist
documents.tagline: Life has a mind of its own
documents.overview: A Los Angeles journalist befriends a homeless Juilliard-trained musician, while looking for a new article for the paper.
documents.plot:
The Soloist is a 2009 biographical drama directed by Joe Wright, starring Jamie Foxx as Nathaniel Ayers and Robert Downey Jr. as the journalist Steve Lopez. It is based on the true story of Ayers, a gifted musician who developed schizophrenia and became homeless, and of Lopez, the Los Angeles Times columnist who wrote about him and befriended him.

In 2005, Steve Lopez is a columnist for the Los Angeles Times, divorced and working for his ex-wife Mary, an editor at the paper. One day he hears a homeless man playing a two-string violin beautifully on the streets of downtown Los Angeles. The man, Nathaniel Ayers, tells him that he once attended the Juilliard School. Intrigued, Lopez investigates and learns from Ayers's sister that he was a cello prodigy who began showing symptoms of schizophrenia while at Juilliard, dropped out and eventually ended up living on the streets.

Lopez writes a column about Ayers, and a moved reader sends him a cello. Lopez gives the instrument to Ayers and tries to improve his life, persuading him to keep it at a shelter for homeless people and arranging lessons with a professional cellist. He also tries to convince Ayers to accept an apartment and psychiatric help, but Ayers resists, and his growing attachment to Lopez strains their relationship. When Lopez pushes too hard, Ayers turns against him. Through their difficult friendship, Lopez comes to realize that Ayers has changed his life as much as he has changed Ayers's, and the two eventually reconcile.

The film depicts the realities of homelessness and mental illness in Los Angeles, and it ends by noting that Ayers remained a member of the LAMP Community, a nonprofit organization that helps people living with severe mental illness.

Originally scheduled for release in November 2008, The Soloist was released by Paramount Pictures on April 24, 2009. It grossed about 38 million dollars against a budget of 60 million dollars and received mixed reviews, with 57 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised the lead performances but faulted a lack of narrative focus, and a Metacritic score of 61.

documents.title: Obsessed
documents.tagline: Sharon and Derek have all they've ever wanted... but someone else wants it more.
documents.overview: Things couldn't be better for Derek Charles. He's just received a big promotion at work, and has a wonderful marriage with his beautiful wife, Sharon. However, into this idyllic world steps Lisa, a temporary worker at Derek's office. Lisa begins to stalk Derek, jeopardizing all he holds dear.
documents.plot:
Obsessed is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, particularly the theme of obsession and its destructive power. The movie follows Dr. Nathan Connelly (played by Aaron O'Connell), a successful architect who becomes the object of desire for his wife's former nanny, Sharon (played by Alice Braga), who is now obsessed with him.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Sharon's obsession is not just a product of her own desires but also a manifestation of her deep-seated emotional pain and sense of abandonment. Her fixation on Nathan is all-consuming, driving her to extreme measures in an attempt to claim him for herself.

The film expertly explores the blurred lines between love, desire, and possession, raising questions about the nature of obsession and its impact on individuals and relationships. Through Sharon's character, the movie sheds light on the devastating consequences of unchecked emotions, highlighting the ways in which obsession can consume and destroy those around it.

Furthermore, Obsessed touches on themes of class and social status, as Sharon's background and circumstances serve as a catalyst for her fixation on Nathan. The film also delves into the complexities of female desire and the societal expectations placed upon women, particularly in terms of their roles as caregivers and nurturers.

Ultimately, Obsessed is a gripping thriller that masterfully weaves together elements of psychological suspense, drama, and social commentary, creating a thought-provoking exploration of the darker aspects of human nature.

documents.title: Last Holiday
documents.tagline: She always thought she was somebody special... and she was.
documents.overview: The discovery that she has a terminal illness prompts introverted department store saleswoman Georgia Byrd to reflect on what she realizes has been an overly cautious life. With weeks to live, she withdraws her life savings, sells all her possessions and jets off to Europe where she lives it up at a posh hotel. Upbeat and passionate, Georgia charms everybody she meets, including renowned Chef Didier. The only one missing from her new life is her longtime crush Sean Matthews.
documents.plot:
Last Holiday is a 2006 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Wayne Wang and starring Queen Latifah, LL Cool J, and Timothy Hutton.

The movie follows the story of Georgia Byrd (played by Queen Latifah), a quiet and unassuming woman who lives in Baltimore with her husband, Mace (played by LL Cool J). On her 59th birthday, Georgia discovers that she has terminal cancer and decides to spend her last days traveling around the world. She buys a one-way ticket to Europe and embarks on a journey of self-discovery, meeting new people, trying new foods, and experiencing different cultures.

The main themes of Last Holiday include:

1. **Living in the moment**: Georgia's decision to travel and experience life to the fullest is a powerful metaphor for living in the present and making the most of every day.
2. **Self-discovery**: Through her travels, Georgia learns more about herself, her desires, and her dreams, which helps her come to terms with her mortality.
3. **Love and relationships**: The movie explores the complexities of love, friendship, and family relationships, highlighting the importance of human connections in our lives.
4. **Mortality and acceptance**: Last Holiday confronts the reality of death and encourages viewers to make the most of their time, cherish their loved ones, and live life on their own terms.

Overall, Last Holiday is a heartwarming and uplifting film that celebrates the beauty of life, love, and self-discovery, even in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Moon
documents.tagline: The last place you'd ever expect to find yourself.
documents.overview: With only three weeks left in his three year contract, Sam Bell is getting anxious to finally return to Earth. He is the only occupant of a Moon-based manufacturing facility along with his computer and assistant, GERTY. When he has an accident however, he wakens to find that he is not alone.
documents.plot:
Moon is a 2009 British science fiction film directed by Duncan Jones in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Nathan Parker based on Jones's story. Written as a vehicle for Sam Rockwell, it stars him as an astronaut nearing the end of a solitary three-year stint on the far side of the Moon, with Kevin Spacey voicing the station's robot.

In the future, after an energy crisis, the company Lunar Industries has made a fortune mining helium-3, a clean fuel, from the lunar surface. Its Sarang Station requires only one worker, Sam Bell, who maintains the automated harvesters and launches canisters of helium-3 to Earth, aided by the station's artificial intelligence, GERTY. With two weeks left on his contract, Sam longs to return to his wife, Tess, and their daughter. A broken satellite link prevents live calls, allowing only recorded messages. He begins seeing hallucinations and, distracted by one while out on the surface, crashes his rover.

Sam wakes in the infirmary with no memory of the accident. Suspicious after overhearing GERTY speaking live with the company, he tricks his way outside and finds at the crash site an injured man in the rover who is identical to himself. The two Sams at first quarrel until GERTY confirms that they are both clones of the original Sam Bell, carrying his implanted memories. Exploring, they discover that the company has been jamming communications with Earth, and logs reveal that earlier clones sickened as their terms ended and were incinerated rather than sent home. A hidden vault holds hundreds of sleeping clones. When the older Sam drives beyond the jamming and calls home, he reaches his daughter, now fifteen, who tells him that Tess died years ago.

With a company team on its way that will kill them if they are found together, the dying older Sam chooses to return to the wrecked rover so that his absence will not be noticed, while the younger Sam escapes to Earth aboard a helium-3 transport. At GERTY's suggestion, its memory is wiped, and the younger Sam destroys the jamming antenna before leaving. The rescue team finds a newly awakened clone and the body in the rover, and Sam's testimony on Earth sends Lunar Industries' stock crashing.

Moon premiered at the 2009 Sundance Film Festival and received critical acclaim, particularly for Rockwell's performance, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 90% approval. It was nominated for the BAFTA Award for Best British Film and won the Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation.

documents.title: Green Lantern: First Flight
documents.tagline: Superman was born a hero. Batman became a hero. But only Green Lantern was chosen.
documents.overview: Test pilot Hal Jordan finds himself recruited as the newest member of the intergalactic police force, The Green Lantern Corps.
documents.plot:
Green Lantern: First Flight is a direct-to-video animated superhero film based on the DC Comics character Hal Jordan, also known as Green Lantern. The movie takes place during the Silver Age of comic books and follows the origin story of Hal Jordan.

The film begins with Hal Jordan (voiced by Jason Lee), a test pilot who dreams of becoming an astronaut. However, his ambitions are crushed when he is rejected from the Air Force's astronaut program due to his reckless behavior. Feeling defeated, Hal decides to take matters into his own hands and becomes a private pilot, flying for various clients.

One day, Hal is hired by a mysterious woman named Carol Ferris (voiced by Kyra Sedgwick), who works for a company called Ferris Aircraft. Unbeknownst to Hal, Carol is actually the daughter of Thomas Wayne, a wealthy businessman with connections to the intergalactic police force known as the Green Lantern Corps.

Hal's life takes a dramatic turn when he is recruited by Abin Sur (voiced by Phil LaMarr), a Green Lantern who has been sent to Earth to find and train a new recruit. Hal is chosen for his bravery, intelligence, and sense of justice, making him an ideal candidate to become the next Green Lantern.

Abin Sur takes Hal to the planet Oa, where he meets other members of the Green Lantern Corps, including Kilowog (voiced by Michael Ironside), a tough but fair instructor who trains new recruits in the ways of the Corps. Hal is given a power ring that allows him to create energy constructs and project energy beams.

As Hal begins his training, he faces various challenges, including battling the villainous Sinestro (voiced by Kevin Kilner), a former Green Lantern turned dictator who seeks to overthrow Abin Sur and take control of the Corps for himself. Hal also meets Ch'p (voiced by Justin Long), a small, insectoid alien who becomes his sidekick.

Throughout the film, Hal struggles with the weight of responsibility that comes with being a Green Lantern. He must balance his desire for adventure and recognition with the need to protect the innocent and uphold justice. With the help of Abin Sur and Kilowog, Hal learns to harness his powers and become a true hero.

In the end, Hal faces off against Sinestro in an epic battle that tests his skills and courage. With the help of his friends and allies, Hal emerges victorious, having proven himself as a worthy Green Lantern. The film concludes with Hal returning to Earth, ready to face new challenges and defend the universe from threats both internal and external.

Overall, Green Lantern: First Flight is an exciting and action-packed origin story that introduces audiences to the iconic character of Hal Jordan and the world of the Green Lantern Corps.

documents.title: BloodRayne 2: Deliverance
documents.tagline: A heart-stopping adventure!
documents.overview: Rayne, a half-human half-vampire warrior, is in the America's 1880's Wild West to stop the vampired Billy the Kid and his posse of vampire cowboys.
documents.plot:
BloodRayne 2: Deliverance is a 2007 direct-to-DVD Western horror action film directed by Uwe Boll and a sequel to his 2005 film BloodRayne, which was based on the video game series. Natassia Malthe replaces Kristanna Loken in the title role of Rayne, with Zack Ward as Billy the Kid, Michael Paré as Pat Garrett and Chris Coppola as the reporter Newton Piles. The film moves the story of the half-vampire heroine from Eastern Europe to the American West of the 1880s.

Newton Piles, a reporter on assignment for the Chicago Chronicle, arrives in the small town of Deliverance, Montana, to collect colorful stories of the frontier. The quiet town is preparing for the arrival of the transcontinental railroad in a week's time, but along with the railroad comes a deadly visitor: Billy the Kid, who is in fact a centuries-old Transylvanian vampire. Billy intends to use the railway to spread his influence and build an army of vampire gunslingers with which to conquer the country and establish a vampire kingdom in the New World.

Billy and his followers terrorize Deliverance, killing many of the townspeople and kidnapping children. He spares Newton, promising him the greatest story ever written. His plans are complicated, however, by the arrival of Rayne, a dhampir born in Romania more than a century earlier from the union of a vampire and a human woman. Rayne possesses a vampire's strength and abilities without its weaknesses and has spent her long life hunting the undead. Determined to stop Billy, she must recruit allies among the few surviving townspeople and lawmen and face the vampire gang before the railroad can carry their plague across America.

Boll blends the conventions of the Western, including saloons, showdowns and gallows, with gothic vampire horror, filming on a modest budget for the home-video market.

BloodRayne 2: Deliverance was released in the United States on September 18, 2007, and in Germany on November 30 of that year. Like its predecessor it was received negatively, holding a zero percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews, which called it slow-paced, dry and anything but sexy. A third film, BloodRayne: The Third Reich, followed in 2011.
production_companies: Boll Kino Beteiligungs GmbH & Co. KG

documents.title: Shelter
documents.tagline: The power of being true to yourself.
documents.overview: Forced to give up his dreams of art school, Zach works dead-end jobs to support his sister and her son. Questioning his life, he paints, surfs and hangs out with his best friend, Gabe. When Gabe's older brother returns home for the summer, Zach suddenly finds himself drawn into a relationship he didn't expect.
documents.plot:
Shelter is a 2007 American romantic drama written and directed by Jonah Markowitz in his feature directorial debut and produced by JD Disalvatore. Trevor Wright, Brad Rowe and Tina Holmes star. The film became a favorite on the LGBT festival circuit and won Outstanding Film – Limited Release at the 2009 GLAAD Media Awards.

Zach is an aspiring artist living in the working-class port town of San Pedro, California. He has postponed his dream of going to art school to support his family: his disabled father, his older sister Jeanne and her five-year-old son Cody, whom Zach looks after much of the time while Jeanne goes out partying. He works as a short-order cook and spends his free time painting, surfing, seeing his on-and-off girlfriend Tori and hanging out with his best friend Gabe.

When Gabe's older brother Shaun, a published writer, returns home from Los Angeles for a few weeks, he and Zach bond over surfing. Shaun encourages Zach to take control of his life and apply to CalArts. One night after drinking, Shaun kisses Zach. Zach is unsure about his feelings and struggles with whether he might be gay, but after breaking up with Tori he goes to Shaun's house and the two spend the night together. When Jeanne leaves town with her boyfriend Alan for a job interview in Portland, Zach brings Cody along to see Shaun, and their relationship blossoms as Shaun forms a close bond with the boy.

When Gabe and Jeanne find out about the relationship, Gabe is supportive, but Jeanne expresses homophobic views and says she does not want Cody around Shaun. Overwhelmed, Zach ends things with Shaun, insisting that he is not like him, and Shaun calls him a coward for refusing to face his feelings. Shaun secretly submits Zach's portfolio to CalArts, and Zach is accepted, just as Jeanne announces that she intends to move to Oregon permanently with Alan without Cody. Torn between his responsibilities and his own future, Zach must finally decide whether to keep sacrificing his dreams for his family and whether he has the courage to choose the life and the love he truly wants.

Shelter won numerous festival honors, including Best New Director and Favorite Narrative Feature at the Seattle Lesbian & Gay Film Festival, the People's Choice Award at the Vancouver Queer Film Festival, Outfest's award for Outstanding First Dramatic Feature and the Best Actor prize for Wright in Tampa.

documents.title: S. Darko
documents.tagline: It's time to travel forward.
documents.overview: Seven years after her brother's death, Samantha Darko finds herself stranded in a small desert town after her car breaks down where she is plagued by bizarre visions telling of the universe's end. As a result, she must face her own demons, and in doing so, save the world and herself.
documents.plot:
S. Darko is a thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that delves into the complexities of time travel, free will, and the consequences of altering one's destiny.

At its core, the film explores the idea of a multiverse, where every possibility plays out in a separate reality. The main character, Sam, finds himself caught in a web of time travel, as he tries to prevent his future self from killing him. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that every decision Sam makes has a ripple effect on the timeline, leading to a series of events that are both thrilling and unsettling.

One of the primary themes of S. Darko is the concept of determinism versus free will. The film raises questions about whether our choices are truly our own, or if they're predetermined by forces beyond our control. As Sam navigates the complexities of time travel, he begins to realize that his actions may be part of a larger, predestined plan.

The movie also explores the idea of identity and how it's shaped by our experiences and relationships. Sam's journey is not just about preventing his own death, but also about understanding himself and finding his place in the world. Through his interactions with various characters, including his sister Daphne and his friend Kim, Sam grapples with the notion that his sense of self may be an illusion.

Furthermore, S. Darko touches on the theme of grief and loss. The film's central plot device is rooted in the idea of a traumatic event from Sam's past, which has left him feeling lost and disconnected from the world around him. As he tries to prevent his own death, Sam must also confront the pain and sadness that have defined his life.

Overall, S. Darko is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to think critically about the nature of time, free will, and identity. With its complex narrative and philosophical themes, it's a movie that lingers long after the credits roll.

documents.title: The Other Man
documents.tagline: What If everything you believed was a lie?
documents.overview: The story of a husband who suspects his wife of adultery, and sets out to track down the other man in her life.
documents.plot:
The Other Man is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of human relationships and the blurred lines between truth and deception.

At its core, the film explores the theme of identity and how it can be manipulated to serve one's own interests. The protagonist, Harry Petersen (played by William Fichtner), is a man who discovers that his wife has been having an affair with another man, but what he doesn't know is that this other man is actually his doppelganger, who has taken on the identity of his deceased brother.

This twist raises questions about the nature of self and how easily it can be altered. The film suggests that our sense of identity is fragile and can be easily manipulated by external forces. This theme is further underscored by the character of Alex (played by Antonio Banderas), who embodies the darker aspects of human nature, using his doppelganger persona to exact revenge on Harry's life.

The Other Man also explores the theme of grief and how it can consume us. Harry's brother has recently died, leaving him feeling lost and disconnected from the world around him. The arrival of Alex, who bears a striking resemblance to his deceased brother, serves as a catalyst for Harry's emotional journey, forcing him to confront his feelings of guilt, anger, and betrayal.

Throughout the film, the director, Nick Love, weaves together these themes with a sense of tension and unease, creating a narrative that is both suspenseful and thought-provoking. Ultimately, The Other Man is a movie about how our perceptions of ourselves and others can be distorted by deception and manipulation, leaving us to question what is real and what is not.

documents.title: Antichrist
documents.tagline: When nature turns evil, true terror awaits.
documents.overview: A grieving couple retreats to their cabin 'Eden' in the woods, hoping to repair their broken hearts and troubled marriage. But nature takes its course and things go from bad to worse.
documents.plot:
Antichrist is a 2009 psychological horror film written and directed by Lars von Trier. The film stars Willem Dafoe and Charlotte Gainsbourg as a couple, He and She, who are struggling to cope with the death of their six-year-old son.

The story begins with the family's home being set on fire, which is implied to be an accident, but also raises questions about the family's dynamics and the father's (He) inability to protect his child. The couple decides to leave Denmark and move to a remote cabin in the woods, where they hope to find solace and healing.

Initially, the film appears to be a slow-burning exploration of grief, love, and the human condition. He and She struggle to come to terms with their loss, and their relationship is put to the test as they try to navigate their new reality. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that something more sinister is at play.

She becomes increasingly unhinged, descending into a world of madness and despair. Her behavior becomes more erratic, and she starts to exhibit strange and disturbing behaviors, including self-mutilation and an obsession with death. He tries to care for her, but his own emotional state begins to deteriorate, and he becomes increasingly detached from reality.

As the film progresses, it becomes clear that She's descent into madness is not just a result of grief, but also a manifestation of her own dark desires and fantasies. The couple's relationship is revealed to be toxic and abusive, with He being emotionally distant and controlling. Their son's death serves as a catalyst for their deeper psychological issues.

The film's climax features a graphic and disturbing scene in which She gives birth to a stillborn child, which she then dismembers and eats. This act can be seen as a symbol of her own rebirth and her attempt to reclaim control over her life.

Throughout the film, von Trier explores themes of grief, trauma, and the human condition. He raises questions about the nature of love, relationships, and the complexities of the human psyche. The film's title, Antichrist, is a reference to the idea that She has become a symbol of Christ-like suffering and sacrifice.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for its unflinching portrayal of grief and trauma, as well as its bold and uncompromising style. However, it was also criticized for its graphic content and perceived misogyny. Despite this, Antichrist remains a thought-provoking and unsettling work that challenges viewers to confront the darkest aspects of human nature.

In conclusion, Antichrist is a complex and challenging film that explores themes of grief, trauma, and the human condition. The film's slow-burning tension and graphic content make it a difficult watch, but also a rewarding one for those who are willing to engage with its complexities.

documents.title: Year One
documents.tagline: Meet your ancestors
documents.overview: When a couple of lazy hunter-gatherers are banished from their primitive village, they set off on an epic journey through the ancient world.
documents.plot:
Year One is a 2009 American comedy film directed by Harold Ramis and written by Gene Stupnitsky and Lee Eisenberg. The movie stars Jack Black and Michael Cera as two of the first humans created by God.

The story begins with the creation of Adam (Jack Black) and Eve (Julianne Hough), the first humans, by God (David Koechner). However, they quickly become bored with their simple life in the Garden of Eden. They start to rebel against God's rules, and things take a turn for the worse.

After being kicked out of the Garden, Adam and Eve find themselves lost in the wilderness. They are forced to navigate through ancient civilizations, including Egypt, Babylon, and Assyria, all while trying to survive and figure out their place in the world.

Along the way, they encounter various historical figures, such as Abraham (Hannibal Buress), Moses (Jemaine Clement), and Noah (Christopher Mintz-Plasse). The duo's misadventures often land them in trouble, but they also learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and growing up.

One of the most significant challenges Adam and Eve face is their own relationship. They start to develop feelings for each other, which complicates their journey. As they navigate through different cultures, they must confront their own desires and learn to accept themselves as individuals.

Throughout their travels, Adam and Eve encounter various obstacles, including wars, plagues, and natural disasters. However, they also experience moments of joy, love, and connection with the people they meet along the way.

As the story unfolds, Adam and Eve begin to realize that they are not just ordinary humans but rather vessels for God's plan. They start to understand their purpose in life and the importance of following God's rules.

The movie culminates with Adam and Eve returning to the Garden of Eden, where they find a new understanding of themselves and their place in the world. However, this time around, they are not just innocent children but rather wise and experienced individuals who have learned from their journey.

Overall, Year One is a hilarious and entertaining comedy that explores themes of identity, community, and growth. The movie features outstanding performances from Jack Black and Michael Cera, who bring depth and humor to their characters. With its witty dialogue, engaging storyline, and impressive historical cameos, Year One is a must-see for fans of comedy and adventure movies.

documents.title: Lost and Delirious
documents.tagline: Friends. Roommates. Lovers.
documents.overview: After starting at an upmarket boarding school, a teenage girl forms close friendships with her two older roommates. However, when she discovers that her new friends are lovers she finds herself caught in a complicated situation.
documents.plot:
Lost and Delirious is a 2001 Canadian drama film directed by Léa Pool. The movie revolves around the lives of three teenage girls, Annie, Marcia, and Louise, who embark on a summer road trip to Quebec City with their friends' fathers. 

The main theme of Lost and Delirious explores the complexities of female adolescence, identity, and the struggles of growing up. It delves into the characters' desires for freedom, autonomy, and self-discovery as they navigate through the challenges of adolescence.

Throughout the film, Annie, Marcia, and Louise grapple with their own insecurities, fears, and dreams, often finding themselves at odds with each other. The movie also touches on themes of class differences, social status, and the constraints placed on women by societal expectations.

The title "Lost and Delirious" captures the essence of the characters' emotional states, as they become increasingly disoriented and disconnected from their surroundings. This sense of disorientation is mirrored in the film's use of vibrant colors, dreamlike sequences, and a non-linear narrative structure, which adds to the overall sense of confusion and uncertainty.

Ultimately, Lost and Delirious presents a poignant portrayal of female adolescence, one that is both raw and unflinching, yet ultimately hopeful and redemptive.

documents.title: District 9
documents.tagline: You are not welcome here.
documents.overview: Thirty years ago, aliens arrive on Earth. Not to conquer or give aid, but to find refuge from their dying planet. Separated from humans in a South African area called District 9, the aliens are managed by Multi-National United, which is unconcerned with the aliens' welfare but will do anything to master their advanced technology. When a company field agent contracts a mysterious virus that begins to alter his DNA, there is only one place he can hide: District 9.
documents.plot:
District 9 is a thought-provoking science fiction film directed by Neill Blomkamp, produced by Peter Jackson and Carolyn Markle, and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing. The movie was released on August 14, 2009.

In the year 2012, humanity has been forced to retreat to a distant planet called Monarch, where they are quarantined due to an alien virus that causes severe mutations in humans.
