The United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOSA) is responsible for managing the human population on Monarch, and it is here that we meet our protagonist, Wikus van der Merwe (played by Sharlto Copley), a bureaucrat who works for UNOSA.

Wikus's life takes a drastic turn when he is exposed to an alien substance while trying to evict a group of aliens from a slum-like area called District 9. The substance, known as "Prisoners' Compound," causes Wikus to undergo a terrifying transformation, turning him into a hybrid creature with the physical characteristics of both humans and aliens.

As Wikus struggles to cope with his new form, he befriends Christopher Johnson (played by Jason Cottle), a human who has been living in District 9 for years. Through their interactions, Wikus begins to understand the harsh realities of life on Monarch and the treatment of the alien population by humanity.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Wikus discovers that his new form grants him access to advanced technology that could potentially help the aliens. He also learns about the true nature of District 9 and the sinister plans of the UNOSA officials who are determined to exploit the aliens for their own gain.

As tensions rise, Wikus must navigate a complex web of politics, prejudice, and humanity's darker aspects. The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between humans and aliens, forcing Wikus to make an impossible choice that will determine the fate of both species.

District 9 is a powerful commentary on issues such as xenophobia, segregation, and the dangers of unchecked power. Through its thought-provoking narrative and visually stunning depiction of a dystopian future, the film challenges viewers to confront their own biases and prejudices. The movie's success can be attributed to its well-crafted storyline, memorable characters, and Blomkamp's direction, which masterfully balances action, drama, and social commentary.

Overall, District 9 is a gripping science fiction film that explores complex themes and features a compelling narrative with a strong protagonist at its center.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
The Department of Trade and Industry of South Africa
New Zealand Post Digital and Visual Effects Grant

documents.title: Hey Arnold! The Movie
documents.tagline: A Big Problem Calls For a Big Head.
documents.overview: Arnold and his friends must recover a stolen document in order to prevent the neighborhood from being bulldozed.
documents.plot:
Hey Arnold!: The Movie is a 2002 American animated adventure comedy film based on Craig Bartlett's Nickelodeon television series Hey Arnold!. Directed by Tuck Tucker and written by Bartlett and Steve Viksten, it features the voices of Spencer Klein as Arnold, Francesca Smith as Helga Pataki, Jamil Walker Smith as Gerald, Dan Castellaneta as Grandpa Phil and Nick Vermicelli, Tress MacNeille as Grandma Gertie and Mayor Dixie, Paul Sorvino as Alphonse Perrier du von Scheck and Jennifer Jason Leigh as Bridget.

Arnold and his best friend Gerald learn that Scheck, chief executive of the developer FutureTech Industries, plans to raze their neighborhood of Hillwood and replace it with a luxurious high-rise shopping mall. Helga's father, Big Bob, is working with the company. Arnold's protest block party, "Blockapalooza", collapses when Scheck's employees steal the permit and Grandma Gertie is arrested, and the disheartened neighbors start selling their homes. Then Grandpa Phil tells Arnold about the "Tomato Incident", a historic battle fought on the site of their boarding house, the Sunset Arms, and Arnold realizes that the area must have been declared a historic district. He and Gerald trace the document proving its landmark status to Scheck, who denies having it. A caller named "Deep Voice" tells Arnold that the paper is in Scheck's office safe, and the boys steal the safe key from Scheck's assistant Vermicelli, while Phil and the boarders rig the storm drains with dynamite to stop the bulldozers. With the help of the agent Bridget, Arnold and Gerald slip into FTI headquarters, where Scheck reveals that his ancestor, a British governor, was humiliated by colonists, including Arnold's forebears, over a tomato tax. He burns the document. "Deep Voice" then tells Arnold to get the security camera footage of the burning and is revealed to be Helga, who confesses that she did it out of love for him. Arnold and Bridget play the footage on a giant screen before Mayor Dixie, who reinstates the neighborhood's historic status. Scheck is arrested, and Helga later claims she spoke only in the heat of the moment, which Arnold pretends to believe.

Originally made for television as Arnold Saves the Neighborhood, the film was moved to cinemas by Paramount after strong test screenings. Released on 28 June 2002, it grossed over $15 million on a budget of $3 million to $4 million, but most critics were unimpressed, giving it a 29% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

documents.title: The Adventures of Rocky & Bullwinkle
documents.tagline: This summer it's not the same old bull.
documents.overview: Rocky and Bullwinkle have been living off the finances made from the reruns of their cartoon show. Boris and Natasha somehow manage to crossover into reality and team up with Fearless Leader, an evil criminal turned media mogul with some evil plans up his sleeve. Rocky and Bullwinkle must stop the three of them before they wreak havoc.
documents.plot:
The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle is a 2000 American adventure comedy that combines live action and animation, directed by Des McAnuff and written by Kenneth Lonergan, based on Jay Ward's animated series The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends. The animated heroes share the screen with live actors playing the villains: Robert De Niro, who also co-produced, as Fearless Leader, Jason Alexander as Boris Badenov and Rene Russo as Natasha Fatale. Randy Quaid and Piper Perabo co-star, June Foray returns as the voice of Rocky, and Keith Scott voices Bullwinkle and the narrator.

Since their show was canceled in 1964, Rocky the Flying Squirrel and Bullwinkle J. Moose have lived gloomily in a deforested Frostbite Falls; Rocky can no longer fly, and their narrator lives with his mother. Their old enemies, out of power since the Cold War ended, tunnel into a Hollywood studio and trick executive Minnie Mogul into green-lighting a film, which brings them into the real world in live-action form. Six months later they run RBTV, "Really Bad Television", a New York cable network designed to brainwash Americans into electing Fearless Leader president. FBI director Cappy von Trapment sends rookie agent Karen Sympathy to recruit Rocky and Bullwinkle, and she summons them into reality.

Boris and Natasha pursue the heroes with the CDI, or "Computer-Degenerating Imagery", a device that can trap cartoon characters inside the Internet. Karen is jailed but escapes with help from a lovestruck guard, Ole. At Bullwinkle's alma mater, Wossamotta U, the villains stage an honorary degree ceremony to kill him, but Rocky regains his power of flight and saves his friend. A starstruck judge later dismisses charges against them, and the trio escapes in a rickety biplane. Rocky carries Karen to New York, where they are captured, as Fearless Leader begins brainwashing the nation. Bullwinkle crash-lands at the White House, where his natural stupidity makes him immune to the broadcasts, and Cappy e-mails him to the studio to disrupt Fearless Leader's address. The villains are captured, and Bullwinkle accidentally triggers the CDI, turning them back into cartoons and banishing them to the Internet. Rocky and Bullwinkle get their own network, and they return to a replanted Frostbite Falls.

The film earned $35.1 million worldwide and was considered a box office failure. Critics found it faithful to the cartoon but unfunny, giving it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes and 36 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Powder Blue
documents.tagline: Every life has a breaking point
documents.overview: On the gritty streets of LA, the destinies of four people desperate for connection and redemption are about to collide.
documents.plot:
Powder Blue is a 2009 American independent drama written and directed by Timothy Linh Bui, built around several interconnected stories set in Los Angeles in the days before Christmas. The ensemble cast includes Jessica Biel as the stripper Rose-Johnny, Forest Whitaker as Charlie, Eddie Redmayne as the undertaker Qwerty Doolittle, Ray Liotta as Jack Doheny, Lisa Kudrow as Sally, Kris Kristofferson as Randall and Alejandro Romero as Lexus. It also features Patrick Swayze as the club owner Velvet Larry, his final film role before his death in September 2009.

The film opens with a vision of a man walking naked into the sea and drowning. Charlie, a suicidal priest still grieving the wife he lost on their wedding day, drives around the city with a gun and fifty thousand dollars, trying to pay someone to kill him because his faith forbids him to do it himself. He approaches Lexus, a transgender sex worker, who refuses. Elsewhere, Rose-Johnny, a stripper at Velvet Larry's club who dreams of seeing Paris, loses her dog when her landlord throws it out.

Qwerty, a lonely, nervous undertaker facing eviction, accidentally hits the dog with his hearse and nurses it back to health, growing attached to it. Jack Doheny, an aging gangster dying of cancer, has just been released after twenty-five years in prison and receives a suitcase of money along with a lead on how to find his estranged family, which leads him to Velvet Larry's club and to Rose-Johnny, whose young son lies in a coma in a hospital. As Charlie bonds with a kind waitress named Sally and offers Qwerty money to end his life, the lives of these lonely, damaged people converge in unexpected ways.

The film is a melodrama about loneliness, grief, redemption and the healing power of human connection, set against the backdrop of the holiday season.

Powder Blue received only a limited theatrical release in the United States and was released principally on DVD in May 2009. Critics were negative: Variety found its heartstring-pulling contrivances over the top, felt that Biel overacted and called Bui's message about love both loud and tone-deaf.

documents.title: Assault on Precinct 13
documents.tagline: L.A.'s deadliest street gang just declared war on the cops.
documents.overview: The lone inhabitants of an abandoned police station are under attack by the overwhelming numbers of a seemingly unstoppable street gang.
documents.plot:
Assault on Precinct 13 is a 1976 American action thriller film directed by John Carpenter. The movie takes place in a police station that has been quarantined due to a deadly virus outbreak in the city, and it follows a small group of survivors as they try to stay alive until help arrives.

The main theme of Assault on Precinct 13 is the struggle for survival in a desperate situation, where the characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the harsh realities of the world around them. The film explores the idea that even in the most dire circumstances, humanity can find ways to persevere and connect with each other.

The movie also touches on the theme of isolation and confinement, as the characters are trapped in the police station with no clear way out. This sense of claustrophobia creates a tense atmosphere, where every decision feels like a matter of life and death.

Furthermore, Assault on Precinct 13 can be seen as a commentary on the breakdown of social order and the collapse of institutions. The film depicts a city in chaos, where the rule of law has broken down, and the characters are forced to fend for themselves in a world that seems to have lost its way.

Overall, Assault on Precinct 13 is a gripping thriller that explores themes of survival, humanity, and the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Fired Up!
documents.tagline: 2 Guys. 300 Girls. You Do the Math.
documents.overview: Popular high schoolers and best friends Shawn and Nick decide to ditch football camp for cheerleader camp. For the girls and for the glory.
documents.plot:
Fired Up! is a coming-of-age comedy film that explores themes of male friendship, self-discovery, and the challenges of transitioning from adolescence to adulthood. The movie delves into the complexities of male relationships, particularly those between friends who are navigating the ups and downs of high school and early college life.

At its core, Fired Up! is a story about two inseparable friends, Luke and Noddy, who embark on a journey of self-discovery as they try to win over their crushes. Along the way, they face various obstacles, including rival suitors, family expectations, and their own personal growth. The film's narrative is driven by the characters' emotional journeys, as they learn to balance their desire for independence with the importance of loyalty and friendship.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, particularly in the context of masculinity. Luke and Noddy must navigate traditional masculine norms while forging their own paths and embracing their individuality. This struggle is reflected in their relationships with women, where they grapple with vulnerability, intimacy, and emotional expression.

Ultimately, Fired Up! presents a heartwarming and humorous portrayal of male friendship and the challenges of growing up. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic moments belie its thoughtful exploration of themes that are both universally relatable and uniquely adolescent.

documents.title: A Christmas Carol
documents.tagline: Season's Greedings
documents.overview: Miser Ebenezer Scrooge is awakened on Christmas Eve by spirits who reveal to him his own miserable existence, what opportunities he wasted in his youth, his current cruelties, and the dire fate that awaits him if he does not change his ways. Scrooge is faced with his own story of growing bitterness and meanness, and must decide what his own future will hold: death or redemption.
documents.plot:
A Christmas Carol (2009) is a musical fantasy film directed by Robert Zemeckis, based on Charles Dickens' classic novella of the same name. The story revolves around Ebenezer Scrooge (played by Jim Carrey), a miserly and bitter old man who has lost touch with his humanity.

The film begins on Christmas Eve, where Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his former business partner, Jacob Marley (played by Gary Oldman in a posthumous appearance). Marley's spirit warns Scrooge that he will be condemned to wander the earth wearing heavy chains if he does not change his ways. The ghost then disappears, and Scrooge is visited by the Ghost of Christmas Past (played by Colin Firth), who takes him on a journey through his childhood and early adulthood.

The Ghost of Christmas Past reveals to Scrooge how he became the person he is today, and how he has lost touch with his loved ones, including his sister Fan (played by Cary Elwes) and his former love, Belle (played by Laura Linney). The ghost also shows Scrooge how he mistreated his clerk, Bob Cratchit (played by Gary Oldman), and his family, particularly his son Tiny Tim (played by Jonas Ball).

The Ghost of Christmas Present (played by Daryl Hannah) then appears, showing Scrooge how others perceive him - as a cold and heartless man. However, the ghost also reveals to Scrooge that there are still good people in the world who care for him, including Bob Cratchit's family.

Finally, the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come (played by Christopher Plummer) appears, showing Scrooge a possible future where he has died and is mourned by no one. The ghost also reveals to Scrooge that Tiny Tim will die if he does not change his ways.

Scrooge is deeply moved by these visions and realizes the error of his ways. He wakes up on Christmas morning a changed man, determined to make amends with those he has wronged and to become a kinder and more generous person.

Throughout the film, Jim Carrey's performance as Scrooge is impressive, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's use of motion capture technology allows for a unique and expressive performance from Carrey, who also wrote and produced the film. Overall, A Christmas Carol (2009) is a visually stunning and emotionally powerful adaptation of Dickens' classic novella.

documents.title: The Secret of Moonacre
documents.tagline: A Magical Journey Begins.
documents.overview: When 13 year old Maria Merryweather's father dies, leaving her orphaned and homeless, she is forced to leave her luxurious London life to go and live with Sir Benjamin, an eccentric uncle she didn't know she had, at the mysterious Moonacre Manor.
documents.plot:
The Secret of Moonacre is a 2008 fantasy drama film directed by Gábor Csupó, produced by Australian Film Commission, and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing. 

The main themes of The Secret of Moonacre revolve around the struggles of adolescence, self-discovery, and the complexities of female relationships. The story follows 16-year-old Maria Merar, a young girl who moves to a mysterious mansion with her family after her father's death.

As Maria navigates her new surroundings, she discovers that the house holds secrets and magic, which slowly unravels as she uncovers the truth about her family's past and the mysterious Moonacre. The film explores themes of identity, belonging, and the power of female friendships in overcoming adversity.

Throughout the story, Maria faces challenges that force her to confront her own emotions, desires, and sense of self-worth. Her relationships with other characters, particularly her cousin Rose and the enigmatic Mrs. Fielding, play a significant role in shaping her journey towards self-discovery.

The film also touches on the idea of female empowerment and the importance of supporting one another in the face of adversity. As Maria navigates the complexities of her new life, she learns to rely on herself and those around her, ultimately emerging stronger and more confident.

Overall, The Secret of Moonacre is a poignant coming-of-age story that explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and female empowerment, set against a richly imaginative and atmospheric backdrop.

documents.title: Northanger Abbey
documents.overview: A young woman's penchant for sensational Gothic novels leads to misunderstandings in the matters of the heart.
documents.plot:
Northanger Abbey is a 2007 film adaptation of Jane Austen's novel of the same name, produced by WGBH Boston. The movie explores several timeless and thought-provoking themes that continue to resonate with audiences today.

At its core, Northanger Abbey is a commentary on the societal pressures and expectations placed on women during the late 18th century. The protagonist, Catherine Morland, embodies the ideal of a young woman navigating the complexities of high society, where appearances can be deceiving and social standing is everything. As Catherine navigates this treacherous landscape, she must confront her own desires, values, and sense of identity.

One of the primary themes of Northanger Abbey is the tension between reality and fantasy. Catherine's imagination often gets the better of her, leading her to misinterpret the world around her. This blurs the lines between what is real and what is imagined, highlighting the fragility of perception and the ease with which our understanding can be distorted.

The film also delves into the theme of social class and its impact on relationships. The contrast between Catherine's humble upbringing and the aristocratic world she enters serves as a backdrop for exploring issues of status, privilege, and the constraints placed on individuals by their social position.

Furthermore, Northanger Abbey touches upon the idea of female empowerment and independence. As Catherine navigates her way through various relationships and experiences, she begins to assert her own agency and develop a sense of self-worth that is not solely defined by her social standing.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that is both humorous and poignant. Through its thoughtful portrayal of complex themes, Northanger Abbey offers a rich and engaging commentary on the societal norms and expectations that shape our lives.

documents.title: Dragon Ball GT: A Hero's Legacy
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボールGT 悟空外伝! 勇気の証しは四星球(スーシンチュウ)
documents.overview: Son Goku Jr. is the great-great-great-great-grandson of the legendary martial artist Son Goku. However, unlike his predecessor he's not a brave fighter. He's constantly picked on by school bullies, his grandmother Pan sees this and she's worried, but even though Goku Jr. is not a strong and powerful Saiyan, he has a kind heart, and Pan loves him. When Pan gets sick Goku Jr. realizes he must do something if he doesn't want to lose Pan. Then he will remember about the legends of the Dragon Balls. It was told they granted a wish to the bearer, Goku Jr. needs a magical wish more than ever.
documents.plot:
Dragon Ball GT: A Hero's Legacy is a Japanese animated television special, the only one made for the Dragon Ball GT series. Directed by Osamu Kasai and credited to writers Akira Toriyama and Takao Koyama, it aired in Japan on March 26, 1997, between episodes 41 and 42, as a prelude to the very end of the series. The Japanese voice cast includes Masako Nozawa, Yuko Minaguchi and Shin Aomori.

A hundred years after Goku's defeat of Baby, all of his friends and family have died except his granddaughter Pan, now an old woman. Her great-great-grandson, Goku Jr., looks just like his famous ancestor but lacks his courage and fighting spirit. Pan takes the boy to visit Goku's grave and tries to train him, but he has no confidence and is bullied at school by his classmate Puck and his gang. While scolding Goku Jr. for not standing up for himself, Pan collapses and is hospitalized. Remembering stories of the wish-granting Dragon Balls, Goku Jr. resolves to find one on Mount Paozu to cure her. Mocked by Puck's gang, he loses his temper and knocks them out with a burst of hidden power, then sets off on foot. On the road he meets Puck again. Puck agrees to come along, at first hoping to see Goku Jr. eaten by a monster, and steals a cart of food for the trip; though he does not believe in the Dragon Balls, he decides to help because he admired Pan's strength.

After many obstacles, the pair reach a rickety rope bridge over a deep chasm. Puck crosses first, but Goku Jr. stumbles in the wind, and Puck falls when the bridge collapses while trying to save him. Continuing alone, Goku Jr. is attacked by a pig-like demon; a mother bear whose cub he had helped earlier comes to his defense, and in a rage Goku Jr. becomes a Super Saiyan, easily beats the demon and passes out with no memory of the change. At the summit he finds an old house holding the four-star Dragon Ball, but his wish fails, and he throws the ball away in tears. It rolls to the feet of the adult Goku, who explains that all seven balls are needed and tells his descendant that he is stronger and braver than he believes. A helicopter then lands carrying Pan and Puck, both safe. When Goku Jr. turns back, Goku has vanished, but his voice tells the boy that his own bravery saved them. Goku Jr. boards the helicopter with new confidence and the Dragon Ball.

 Funimation released an English dub on DVD in the United States on November 16, 2004, and a separate English version produced by AB Groupe aired on Toonami UK.

documents.title: Hannah Montana: The Movie
documents.tagline: She has the best of both worlds... Now, she has to choose just one.
documents.overview: When Miley Stewart (aka pop-star Hannah Montana) gets too caught up in the superstar celebrity lifestyle, her dad decides it's time for a total change of scenery. But sweet niblets! Miley must trade in all the glitz and glamour of Hollywood for some ol' blue jeans on the family farm in Tennessee, and question if she can be both Miley Stewart and Hannah Montana.
documents.plot:
Hannah Montana: The Movie is a 2009 American musical comedy film directed by D.J. Caruso and produced by Walt Disney Pictures.

The movie follows Miley Stewart (played by Miley Cyrus), a teenage girl who leads a secret double life as the pop star Hannah Montana. As Miley navigates her relationships with her family, friends, and fans, she must also confront the challenges of fame and identity.

Some of the main themes in the movie include:

1. Identity: The film explores the tension between Miley's two identities - her everyday life as a normal teenager and her public persona as Hannah Montana. As Miley struggles to balance these two roles, she learns valuable lessons about being true to oneself.
2. Family: The movie highlights the importance of family relationships and the challenges that come with having a famous parent (Ricky Stewart, played by Billy Ray Cyrus). Miley's desire for independence and her need for support from her loved ones drive much of the plot.
3. Fame and celebrity culture: The film satirizes the excesses of fame and the pressures of living in the public eye. Hannah Montana's rise to stardom is portrayed as both a blessing and a curse, highlighting the trade-offs between success and personal happiness.
4. Friendship: Miley's relationships with her friends, including Lilly Truscott (Emily Osment) and Oliver Oken (Mitchel Musso), are central to the movie. The film shows how these friendships can provide support, encouragement, and a sense of belonging.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together through Miley's journey as she navigates her dual identities and confronts the challenges of fame. Ultimately, the film suggests that true happiness and fulfillment come from staying true to oneself and nurturing meaningful relationships with others.

documents.title: Baby on Board
documents.overview: The story of Angela, an ambitious, image-conscious businesswoman working for over-demanding boss Mary. When Angela becomes unexpectedly pregnant at the peak of her career, her life with her divorce attorney husband, Curtis, is turned upside-down.
documents.plot:
Baby on Board is a 2009 American romantic comedy starring Heather Graham and Jerry O'Connell as a married couple facing an unexpected pregnancy, with John Corbett, Anthony Starke, Katie Finneran and Lara Flynn Boyle in supporting roles. It was released in the United States in April 2010.

Angela Marks is an ambitious executive at a cosmetics company, and her husband Curtis is a cutthroat divorce attorney. Their close friends Sylvia and Danny Chambers, Danny being Curtis's law partner, have two children and a strained marriage, and Angela watches Sylvia struggle with motherhood while Curtis observes Danny's wandering eye. Angela is hoping to lead a major advertising campaign for a new perfume aimed at expectant mothers, which could earn her a vice presidency, but her first pitch to her demanding boss Mary is derailed by a sudden bout of uncontrollable flatulence. She is nonetheless given a chance to develop the launch.

When Angela starts vomiting, her doctor confirms that she is pregnant, a shock because the couple had been using protection. Walking home in a daze, she passes a restaurant just as a flirtatious client throws herself onto Curtis's lap, and she does not see him trying to push the woman away. That evening Angela tells Curtis about the pregnancy but coldly hints that "he knows what he did," leaving him baffled. Danny convinces Curtis that, since they were using protection, Angela must be cheating on him and the baby may not be his. Each spouse now suspects the other of infidelity, and the misunderstandings multiply over the following months. Meanwhile, Angela hides her growing pregnancy at work for fear of losing the promotion, and the Chambers' marriage teeters after Sylvia throws Danny out of the house.

The confusion reaches a climax on the day of Angela's big presentation to investors, when she goes into labor in the middle of her pitch. The Chambers reconcile after Danny makes a heartfelt speech about commitment, and Curtis rushes to Angela's side. With her water breaking, all the misunderstandings are finally cleared up, and Angela and Curtis reunite as the proud parents of a baby boy.

The opening credits feature Natasha Bedingfield's song "I Wanna Have Your Babies." The film received overwhelmingly negative reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 20% approval rating from five critics. A credits error spelled Boyle's first name differently in the opening and closing titles.

documents.title: Unaccompanied Minors
documents.tagline: No plane, no parents, no problem!
documents.overview: Five disparate kids snowed in at the airport on Christmas Eve learn some lessons about friendship when they launch a bid to get back to their families and outsmart a disgruntled airport official who wants to keep them grounded.
documents.plot:
Unaccompanied Minors is a 2006 American comedy film directed by Paul Feig. The movie revolves around a group of unaccompanied minors who are left behind at an airport after their families' flights take off without them.

The main theme of Unaccompanied Minors is the struggle for identity and independence among these young characters, who are forced to navigate the complexities of adulthood in a foreign environment. As they try to survive on their own, they must confront their own vulnerabilities and limitations, as well as the harsh realities of being alone in an unfamiliar place.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with feelings of abandonment, loneliness, and disorientation, which serve as a catalyst for their personal growth and self-discovery. The movie also explores themes of resilience, resourcefulness, and the power of human connection in the face of adversity.

The film's tone is lighthearted and comedic, but it also touches on more serious issues such as the emotional toll of being left behind and the challenges of navigating a new environment without support or guidance. Overall, Unaccompanied Minors is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to be young, alone, and trying to find one's place in the world.

documents.title: All the Right Moves
documents.tagline: He has everything at stake. He can't afford to lose. He's got to make all the right moves.
documents.overview: Sensitive study of a headstrong high school football star who dreams of getting out of his small Western Pennsylvania steel town with a football scholarship. His equally ambitious coach aims at a college position, resulting in a clash which could crush the player's dreams.
documents.plot:
All the Right Moves is a coming-of-age sports drama film that explores the complexities of adolescence and the struggles of growing up. The movie delves into the theme of identity, as the protagonist, Steve Myers, navigates his way through high school and grapples with his own sense of self-worth.

The film also touches on the idea of social hierarchy and cliques, highlighting the difficulties of fitting in and finding one's place within a group. The character of Steve, who is an outsider among his peers, must confront the challenges of being different and learning to accept himself for who he is.

Furthermore, All the Right Moves examines the theme of masculinity and the pressure to conform to traditional masculine norms. Steve's relationships with other characters, particularly his friend and rival, Tony D'Amato, serve as a catalyst for exploring these themes.

The movie also explores the idea of perseverance and hard work, as Steve strives to become a better football player and find success on and off the field. Through Steve's journey, the film conveys the importance of staying true to oneself and pursuing one's passions, even in the face of adversity.

Overall, All the Right Moves is a poignant and relatable exploration of the challenges and triumphs of adolescence, making it a timeless classic that continues to resonate with audiences today.

documents.title: Barbie Mariposa
documents.overview: Elina, heroine of the Fairytopia films tells her friend Bibble the story of Flutterfield, a faraway kingdom populated by fairies with butterfly wings. Henna, the evil butterfly fairy has poisoned the queen of Flutterfield in an attempt to take over the kingdom.
documents.plot:
RV is a 2006 American comedy film directed by Barry Sonnenfeld and starring Robin Williams, Jeff Daniels, and Kristin Chenoweth.

The movie begins with Chris Cooper's character, Bob Munro, who is a divorced father of two daughters, Beth (Kristen Stewart) and Mollie (Abigail Breslin). The family is struggling to cope with the recent divorce, and their relationship is strained. To take his daughters on a vacation, Bob decides to buy an RV, which he names "RV" after himself.

As they set out on their journey, the family faces various challenges, including a run-in with a group of bikers, a wild animal attack, and a series of misadventures along the way. However, despite these setbacks, the family begins to bond and reconnect with each other.

One day, while stopped at a rest stop, Bob meets a woman named Rachel (Cameron Diaz), who is traveling in an RV with her two children. The two families strike up a conversation, and Bob finds himself drawn to Rachel's warmth and kindness. As they continue on their journey together, Bob begins to realize that he may have found love again.

As the trip progresses, Bob's daughters begin to open up about their feelings regarding their parents' divorce. Beth is struggling to cope with her mother's departure, while Mollie is trying to navigate her own emotions and sense of identity. Through a series of heart-to-hearts with Rachel, Bob helps his daughters to work through their issues and find closure.

Meanwhile, Bob and Rachel's relationship blossoms, and they begin to realize that they have found something special in each other. However, their happiness is short-lived, as they face a series of challenges, including a breakdown on the road and a confrontation with a group of hostile travelers.

In the end, Bob and Rachel's love prevails, and they are able to find happiness together. The movie concludes with the two families reunited, and Bob's daughters finally finding closure and healing from their emotional wounds.

Throughout the film, Robin Williams delivers a standout performance as Bob Munro, bringing his signature energy and wit to the role. The supporting cast, including Jeff Daniels and Kristin Chenoweth, add to the humor and heart of the movie.

Overall, RV is a heartwarming and hilarious comedy that explores themes of love, family, and redemption. With its talented cast and engaging storyline, it's no wonder that this film has become a beloved favorite among audiences.

documents.title: Boxing Helena
documents.tagline: Beyond love, beyond obsession, there hides something beyond reason.
documents.overview: A top surgeon is besotted with a beautiful woman who once rebuffed him. Unable to come to terms with life without her, he tries to convince her that they need each other. She has other ideas, but a horrific accident leaves her at his mercy.
documents.plot:
Boxing Helena is a 1993 American avant-garde thriller written and directed by Jennifer Lynch, from a story by Philippe Caland. Sherilyn Fenn stars as Helena, with Julian Sands as the surgeon who becomes obsessed with her, Bill Paxton as her lover, and Art Garfunkel and Betsy Clark in supporting roles. Before its release, the production became notorious for legal disputes with Madonna and Kim Basinger, both of whom withdrew from the title role; Basinger's departure led to a high-profile lawsuit and a large judgment against her, later overturned on appeal.

Sands plays Nick Cavanaugh, a lonely and emotionally stunted Atlanta surgeon who moves into the lavish home of his recently deceased mother with his girlfriend Anne. He remains fixated on his neighbour Helena, a beautiful and contemptuous woman with whom he once spent a single night and who now treats him with disdain. At a housewarming party, Helena leaves early with another man, and Anne, realising the depth of Nick's obsession, leaves him.

When Helena returns to retrieve an address book she forgot at the party, she storms out of the house on foot and is struck by a hit-and-run driver, suffering a severe leg injury. Instead of taking her to a hospital, Nick secretly treats her in his home and amputates both of her legs. After she tries to strangle him, he goes further and removes her arms as well, keeping her in a box-like existence under his total control. Despite her captivity, Helena remains defiant and verbally domineering, taunting Nick about his inadequacy, while he tries desperately to win her love. Their twisted relationship is ultimately reframed by a final twist that calls into question how much of the story has really happened.

Lynch, the daughter of David Lynch, made her feature debut with the film, which was intended as a dark fable about obsession, control and male possessiveness, though many viewers interpreted it as misogynistic.

The film debuted at the Sundance Film Festival in January 1993, where it was nominated for the Grand Jury Prize, but it was heavily panned on release. On Rotten Tomatoes only about 17 percent of critics' reviews are positive, and Lynch received the Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director.

documents.title: Lesbian Vampire Killers
documents.tagline: After Twilight, The Real Party Starts.
documents.overview: With their women having been enslaved by a pack of lesbian vampires, the remaining menfolk of a rural town send two hapless young lads out onto the moors as a sacrifice.
documents.plot:
Lesbian Vampire Killers is a 2009 British comedy horror film directed by Stewart Verchere and starring Casper Van Dien and Jody Horner. The movie follows two female vampire hunters, Fiona and Jane, as they travel across the country to kill vampires.

The main theme of Lesbian Vampire Killers revolves around the idea of female empowerment and friendship. The film showcases a strong bond between its two lead characters, Fiona and Jane, who are not only vampire hunters but also supportive and loving partners. Their relationship is portrayed as a positive and healthy one, which serves as a refreshing change from the typical heteronormative vampire lore.

The movie also explores themes of identity, community, and acceptance. The film's portrayal of a lesbian couple as the heroes of the story challenges traditional notions of masculinity and femininity, offering a more inclusive and diverse representation of love and relationships.

Furthermore, Lesbian Vampire Killers pokes fun at traditional vampire lore and horror tropes, using humor and satire to subvert expectations. This self-aware approach allows the film to comment on the conventions of the genre while still delivering an entertaining and engaging viewing experience.

Overall, Lesbian Vampire Killers is a lighthearted and humorous take on the vampire genre, focusing on themes of female friendship, empowerment, and acceptance, while also offering a playful critique of traditional horror tropes.

documents.title: The Proposal
documents.tagline: Here comes the bribe...
documents.overview: When she learns she's in danger of losing her visa status and being deported, overbearing book editor Margaret Tate forces her put-upon assistant, Andrew Paxton, to marry her.
documents.plot:
The Proposal is a romantic comedy film released in 2009, directed by Anne Fletcher and produced by Touchstone Pictures.

The movie begins with Margaret Tate (played by Sandra Bullock), a high-powered book editor from New York City, who is facing deportation back to her native Canada due to her expired visa. To stay in the United States, Margaret blackmails her assistant, Andrew Paxton (played by Ryan Reynolds), into pretending to be her fiancé.

Andrew, who has been pining for Margaret but never had a chance with her, reluctantly agrees to play along. They embark on a road trip from New York to Alaska, where they will pretend to get married in order to obtain a new visa for Margaret.

As they travel together, the tension between them gradually turns into romance. However, their initial reluctance to admit their feelings for each other is rooted in past heartbreaks and fears of vulnerability. Andrew's fear of commitment stems from his previous relationship with Margaret, which ended badly due to her lack of emotional maturity.

Throughout the journey, they face various challenges, including a series of hilarious misadventures, cultural clashes, and personal revelations. As they navigate their way through the rugged Alaskan wilderness, they begin to confront their own emotions and insecurities.

One of the most significant plot developments in the movie is when Andrew's estranged father, Joe Paxton (played by Craig T. Nelson), a former hockey player, invites them to his cabin for Thanksgiving dinner. This sets off a chain of events that forces Margaret to confront her past and reevaluate her priorities.

As they near their destination, Margaret begins to realize that she has developed genuine feelings for Andrew. However, just as things are starting to look up, Andrew's fear of commitment resurfaces, causing tension in their relationship.

In the end, Margaret must make a choice between her career ambitions and her growing love for Andrew. In a heartwarming climax, she decides to leave her high-powered job behind and start a new life with Andrew in Alaska.

The movie concludes on a hopeful note, as Margaret and Andrew finally confess their love for each other and begin their new life together. The Proposal is a delightful romantic comedy that explores themes of love, vulnerability, and personal growth, making it a charming watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Lady and the Tramp II: Scamp's Adventure
documents.original_title: Lady and the Tramp II: Scamp's Adventure
documents.tagline: Adventure has a new name.
documents.overview: Lady and Tramp's mischievous pup, Scamp, gets fed up with rules and restrictions imposed on him by life in a family, and longs for a wild and free lifestyle. He runs away from home and into the streets where he joins a pack of stray dogs known as the "Junkyard Dogs." Buster, the pack's leader, takes an instant disliking to the "house-dog" and considers him a rival. Angel, a junkyard pup Scamp's age, longs for the safety and comfort of life in a family and the two become instant companions. Will Scamp choose the wild and free life of a stray or the unconditional love of his family?
documents.plot:
Lady and the Tramp II: Scamp's Adventure is a direct-to-video animated film produced by Disney Television Animation, released in 2001. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Lady and the Tramp.

The story begins with Scamp, the son of Lady and Tramp, who has grown up watching his parents' romance and adventures. However, Scamp is more interested in exploring the city streets and getting into mischief than following in his parents' paw-steps. He befriends a stray dog named Darla, who becomes his partner in crime.

As Scamp navigates the urban jungle with Darla, he gets caught up in a plot by a villainous dog named Ratigan's nephew, Ratigan Jr., to take over the city's dog population. The plan involves using a mind-control device that can manipulate dogs into doing his bidding.

Meanwhile, Lady and Tramp are dealing with their own issues. They're struggling to balance their roles as parents and partners, and they begin to drift apart. Scamp, sensing his parents' tension, decides to take matters into his own paws and sets out to stop Ratigan Jr. and save the city's dogs.

As Scamp delves deeper into the mystery, he meets a street-smart dog named Angel, who becomes his ally in the fight against Ratigan Jr. Together, they gather a team of canine friends and embark on a series of daring adventures to outsmart the villain and destroy the mind-control device.

Throughout the movie, Scamp learns valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and following his heart. He also begins to understand the sacrifices his parents made for him and the importance of their relationship. In the end, Scamp and his friends successfully defeat Ratigan Jr., and he comes to appreciate the values and traditions that Lady and Tramp have taught him.

The movie features a mix of action, comedy, and heartwarming moments, with plenty of nods to the original Lady and the Tramp. The animation is colorful and vibrant, bringing the city streets and its canine characters to life in a way that's both nostalgic and fresh.

Overall, Lady and the Tramp II: Scamp's Adventure is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, family, and community. While it may not be as iconic as the original, it's a worthy sequel that offers plenty of excitement and adventure for fans of the franchise.

documents.title: The Young Victoria
documents.tagline: Love rules all.
documents.overview: As the only legitimate heir of England's King William, teenage Victoria gets caught up in the political machinations of her own family. Victoria's mother wants her to sign a regency order, while her Belgian uncle schemes to arrange a marriage between the future monarch and Prince Albert, the man who will become the love of her life.
documents.plot:
The Young Victoria (2009) is a historical drama film that explores the life of Queen Victoria, from her ascension to the throne at the tender age of 18 to her marriage and coronation. At its core, the movie delves into themes of identity, duty, and the constraints placed on women during the Victorian era.

The film portrays Queen Victoria's struggle to balance her personal desires with the weight of her royal responsibilities. As she navigates the complexities of statecraft and diplomacy, she must also contend with the societal expectations that dictate a woman's role in society. The movie highlights the limited options available to women during this period, including the prospect of marriage as a means of securing alliances and maintaining power.

One of the primary themes of The Young Victoria is the tension between personal freedom and royal duty. Queen Victoria must confront the reality of her circumstances and make difficult choices that will shape the course of her life and the future of the monarchy. This internal conflict is expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and nuance to the film's portrayal of the young queen.

The movie also explores the theme of love and relationships in a time when they were heavily restricted by societal norms. Queen Victoria's romance with Prince Albert serves as a catalyst for her growth and self-discovery, but it is also fraught with challenges and obstacles that threaten to upend her carefully constructed life.

Ultimately, The Young Victoria presents a powerful exploration of the complexities and constraints faced by women in positions of power during the Victorian era. Through its thoughtful portrayal of Queen Victoria's journey, the film sheds light on the intricate web of relationships, societal expectations, and personal desires that shape the lives of those who hold power.

documents.title: Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian
documents.original_title: Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian
documents.tagline: When the lights go off the battle is on.
documents.overview: Hapless museum night watchman Larry Daley must help his living, breathing exhibit friends out of a pickle now that they've been transferred to the archives at the Smithsonian Institution. Larry's (mis)adventures this time include close encounters with Amelia Earhart, Abe Lincoln and Ivan the Terrible.
documents.plot:
Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian is a 2009 American fantasy adventure comedy film directed by Shawn Levy and produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2006 film Night at the Museum.

The story begins with Larry Daley (played by Ben Stiller), now working as the head of security at the National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C. However, he soon discovers that the museum is facing financial difficulties and is threatened with closure. Meanwhile, a new exhibit featuring the Smithsonian Institution's collection has been installed, but it seems to be causing chaos.

As Larry tries to navigate this new situation, he learns that the Smithsonian's collection is coming to life at night due to magical artifacts created by the museum's founder, James Hudson (played by Mickey Rooney). The magical objects imbue the exhibits with human-like personalities and characteristics. 

Larry soon discovers that the villainous Kahmunrah (played by Patrick Gallagher), an ancient Egyptian pharaoh, has also been brought to life. He seeks revenge against Larry for inadvertently awakening him in the first film.

Kahmunrah's plan is to use the magical objects to take over the world by controlling the Smithsonian's collection and using its artifacts to conquer other museums around the globe. The museum's exhibits, including Teddy Roosevelt (played by Robin Williams), Sacagawea (played by Amy Adams), and Attila the Hun (played by Owen Wilson), join forces with Larry to stop Kahmunrah.

As the battle between good and evil intensifies, Larry must use his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart Kahmunrah's minions and prevent them from taking over the world. Along the way, he also learns more about the history of the Smithsonian Institution and its significance in American culture.

The film features a mix of action, adventure, humor, and heartwarming moments as Larry and his new friends work together to save the museum and the world from Kahmunrah's evil plans. In the end, Larry is able to defeat Kahmunrah and restore order to the Smithsonian's collection, saving the day once again.

Overall, Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian is a fun and entertaining film that combines humor, adventure, and historical significance, making it a great addition to the Night at the Museum franchise.

documents.title: Embrace of the Vampire
documents.tagline: Between innocence and evil lies the seduction.
documents.overview: An 18-year-old college freshman is seduced by a handsome vampire lover who introduces her to a dark world of carnal desires.
documents.plot:
Embrace of the Vampire is a 1995 American romantic horror film directed by John Murlowski and starring Tom Skerritt, Mary Stuart Masterson, and Chris Potter. The movie revolves around the story of a vampire hunter who falls in love with his prey.

The main theme of Embrace of the Vampire explores the idea of forbidden love and the struggle between good and evil. The protagonist, played by Tom Skerritt, is a vampire hunter tasked with killing a young woman, played by Mary Stuart Masterson, who is actually a vampire. As he gets to know her, he begins to question his mission and ultimately falls in love with her.

The film delves into the complexities of human nature, highlighting the blurred lines between good and evil. The protagonist's character grapples with his own morality as he navigates his feelings for the vampire, raising questions about the nature of right and wrong. The movie also touches on the theme of redemption, as the protagonist seeks to make amends for past mistakes.

The film's portrayal of a romantic relationship between a human and a vampire serves as a metaphor for the destructive power of desire and the consequences of succumbing to one's passions. Through the characters' interactions, the movie explores the tension between reason and emotion, highlighting the vulnerability that can arise when we allow ourselves to be consumed by our desires.

Overall, Embrace of the Vampire is a thought-provoking film that challenges traditional notions of good and evil, presenting a nuanced exploration of human nature and the complexities of love.

documents.title: The Last House on the Left
documents.original_title: The Last House on the Left
documents.tagline: If someone hurt someone you love, how far would you go to get revenge?
documents.overview: A group of teenage girls heading into the city hook up with a gang of drug-addled ne'er-do-wells and are brutally murdered. The killers find their way to the home of one of their victim's parents, where both father and mother exact a horrible revenge.
documents.plot:
The Last House on the Left is a 2009 American rape-and-revenge horror film directed by Dennis Iliadis and written by Adam Alleca and Carl Ellsworth, a remake of Wes Craven's 1972 film of the same name, with Craven serving as a producer. Tony Goldwyn and Monica Potter star as John and Emma Collingwood, with Sara Paxton as their daughter Mari, alongside Garret Dillahunt, Aaron Paul, Spencer Treat Clark, Riki Lindhome and Martha MacIsaac.

The killer Krug Stillo escapes custody when his brother Francis and girlfriend Sadie ram the police car transporting him and murder both officers. Meanwhile, Dr. John Collingwood, his wife Emma and their daughter Mari, a competitive swimmer, arrive at their remote lake house for a holiday. Mari borrows the car to visit her friend Paige in town, and the two girls meet Justin, a teenager passing through, who invites them to his motel room to smoke marijuana. When Krug, Francis and Sadie return, Krug, furious that Justin has brought strangers to their hideout, decides the girls cannot be released and the gang abducts them.

When Mari tries to escape, the car crashes. Paige breaks away but is recaptured, and in the woods the gang stab her to death in front of Mari before Krug rapes Mari. She manages to flee into the lake, but Krug shoots her in the back as she swims and leaves her for dead. Caught in a storm, the gang take shelter at the nearest house, which belongs to Mari's parents, who offer them their guest house for the night. Justin finds a photograph of Mari and discreetly leaves her necklace on the kitchen counter.

Mari, gravely wounded, drags herself home and collapses on the porch. Her parents see the necklace, realise that the strangers are responsible, and as they try to get her to hospital by boat they fight back, killing Francis with a hammer. In the guest house, Justin hands John a gun, and in the ensuing battle Emma shoots Sadie dead. Krug overpowers John and stabs Justin, but the couple manage to knock him unconscious and take Mari and Justin to hospital. John later returns to the house, where he has left Krug paralysed from the neck down, and exacts a gruesome final revenge with a rigged microwave oven.

The film opened in March 2009 to $14.1 million in its first weekend after cuts demanded by the MPAA to secure an R rating, chiefly to the rape scene. Rotten Tomatoes reported a 42% approval rating.

belongs_to_collection.name: The Last House on the Left Collection

documents.title: The Darwin Awards
documents.tagline: A comedy... to die for.
documents.overview: After botching the capture of a notorious serial killer, idiosyncratic detective Michael Burrows loses his job with the San Francisco Police. He becomes an investigator for an insurance company and joins forces with a cynical field agent to probe suspicious and unusual deaths.
documents.plot:
The Darwin Awards is a 2006 American adventure comedy written and directed by Finn Taylor and based on the website of the same name. Joseph Fiennes stars as Michael Burrows and Winona Ryder as Siri Taylor, with David Arquette, Juliette Lewis, Wilmer Valderrama, Chris Penn, Julianna Margulies, Robin Tunney, Ty Burrell Adam Savage, Jamie Hyneman and the band Metallica. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 25, 2006, the day after Penn's death; it was his final film.

The film opens with a car speeding along with a JATO rocket strapped to it, then turns to Michael, a criminal profiler with the San Francisco Police Department. It is presented in documentary style as the thesis project of a film-school graduate who follows Michael with a camera. Michael's fear of blood lets a serial killer escape, and he is fired from the force. After weeks of depression, he finds a way to combine his professional skill with his obsession with the Darwin Awards: he will help insurance companies identify the people most likely to kill themselves through sheer foolishness, so that they can be refused policies.

His profiling talent impresses an insurance executive, who pairs him with Siri, a specialist in bizarre claims. Together they travel the country investigating legendary cases of idiocy, including the rocket-powered car and a pair of ice fishermen who use a stick of dynamite to blast a hole in the ice, only for their dog to fetch the lit explosive and carry it back to their new SUV. Michael tries to find a common thread among the victims, but the only explanation on offer is Siri's rambling theory that insurers who deny claims drive people mad. Michael himself repeatedly comes close to earning a Darwin Award; stranded with Siri on a freezing night, he blows up his car trying to start a fire with gasoline.

By chance, Michael discovers where the killer who escaped him is now living and abseils down the side of the building to film him. The film student, glimpsed for the first time, is dangling on the other end of the same rope, and the heavy stone urn they are tied to starts creeping toward the edge of the roof. Inside, the killer slices the hand of the captive Siri to trigger Michael's fear of blood, but Michael overcomes it and defeats him.

The film was poorly received, with a 25% rating on Rotten Tomatoes; critics found it formulaic and unfunny.

documents.title: Castaway on the Moon
documents.tagline: Once in a life time, There comes a moment that you live in HOPE.
documents.overview: Mr. Kim is jobless, lost in debt and has been dumped by his girlfriend. He decides to end it all by jumping into the Han River - only to find himself washed up on a small, mid-river island. He soon abandons thoughts of suicide or rescue and begins a new life as a castaway. His antics catch the attention of a young woman whose apartment overlooks the river. Her discovery changes both their lives.
documents.plot:
Cast Away on the Moon is a 2009 South Korean romantic comedy film directed by Lee Jeong-ho. The movie tells the story of two people who fall in love despite being from different social classes.

The main theme of Cast Away on the Moon revolves around class differences and social inequality. The protagonist, Jang Geu-sik (played by Ryoo Seung-bum), is a poor but talented young man who dreams of becoming an astronaut. He falls in love with a wealthy woman, Yoon Soo-jin (played by Shin Min-a), from a higher social class.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various obstacles due to their different backgrounds, including disapproval from their families and societal expectations. However, they ultimately find a way to be together despite these challenges.

Another significant theme in Cast Away on the Moon is the power of love and relationships to overcome adversity. The film showcases how Jang Geu-sik and Yoon Soo-jin's love for each other helps them navigate their differences and find common ground.

The movie also explores the idea of social mobility and the importance of education and hard work in achieving one's goals. Jang Geu-sik's determination to pursue his dreams, despite facing numerous setbacks, serves as an inspiration to the audience.

Overall, Cast Away on the Moon is a heartwarming romantic comedy that celebrates the power of love and relationships to overcome social barriers and achieve happiness.

documents.title: Decoys
documents.tagline: They can seduce anyone... Prey it isn't you!
documents.overview: Luke and Roger are just another couple of college guys trying to lose their virginity. But when Luke sees something unusual, he begins to suspect that the girls on campus aren't exactly...human.
documents.plot:
Decoys is a 2004 American science fiction comedy film directed by David DeCoteau. The movie follows two male models, Sean and Derek, who are hired to pose as women for a high-end fashion show in New York City.

The main theme of Decoys revolves around the exploration of identity, self-discovery, and the societal expectations placed on individuals based on their appearance. The film delves into the idea that people often judge others based on superficial characteristics, such as physical appearance, rather than getting to know them as individuals.

Through the characters of Sean and Derek, the movie highlights the tension between conforming to societal norms and embracing one's true self. As they navigate their roles as women in a male-dominated world, they must confront their own identities and the expectations placed upon them.

The film also touches on themes of masculinity, femininity, and the blurring of boundaries between traditional gender roles. The movie's use of humor and satire allows it to poke fun at societal norms while still exploring deeper themes about identity and self-acceptance.

Overall, Decoys is a lighthearted and entertaining film that uses comedy to explore complex themes about identity, self-discovery, and societal expectations.

documents.title: Horsemen
documents.tagline: Four victims. Four painful secrets.
documents.overview: A recently widowed detective still grieving over his wife's death discovers a shocking connection between himself and the suspects in a serial killing spree linked to the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse.
documents.plot:
Horsemen is a 2009 American psychological thriller directed by Jonas Åkerlund, written by David Callaham and produced by Michael Bay. It stars Dennis Quaid as Aidan Breslin, a detective and forensic dentistry expert, and Zhang Ziyi as Kristen, the adopted daughter of one of the victims, with Lou Taylor Pucci, Clifton Collins Jr., Barry Shabaka Henley, Neal McDonough and Peter Stormare. The film was shot over eight weeks in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

Breslin is a widower who has become emotionally distant from his two sons, Alex and Sean, since his wife's death. Because of his expertise in dental forensics, he is called to a strange crime scene containing human teeth and the painted words "come and see". Soon after, a woman named Mrs. Spitz is found suspended from a hook contraption in her bedroom, the same message written on the walls, and the autopsy reveals that she was pregnant and that the fetus has been removed. Breslin concludes that four attackers were involved and that they filmed the murder.

As more victims are found in similarly staged scenes, a tattoo parlor owner who built four of the hook devices offers a lead, and a remark from his son Sean leads Breslin to the Bible. He realizes that the killings are modeled on the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse from the Book of Revelation, with each crime representing War, Famine, Pestilence or Death. Kristen unexpectedly confesses to the murder of her adoptive mother, revealing a disturbing history of abuse in the Spitz household. As the remaining killers carry out their ritual and Breslin struggles to uncover who is behind the group, the investigation leads him closer to his own home and family than he could have imagined.

The film combines a serial killer mystery with themes of parental neglect, abuse and alienated youth, presented with heavily stylized visuals and graphic violence.

Horsemen received a limited release in the United States on March 6, 2009, before arriving on home video in July. It was poorly received, with 17 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews; Variety's Jordan Mintzer found it predictable and full of clichés such as overstylized torture, whiplash editing and crude neon lighting.

documents.title: The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3
documents.tagline: I can't get it out of my head. I'm gonna die today.
documents.overview: Armed men hijack a New York City subway train, holding the passengers hostage in return for a ransom, and turning an ordinary day's work for dispatcher Walter Garber into a face-off with the mastermind behind the crime.
documents.plot:
The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3 (2009) is a gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly in the context of hostage situations and the moral dilemmas that arise from them. The film explores the theme of power dynamics, as seen through the character of Walter Garber, a transit authority employee who finds himself at the center of a high-stakes game of cat and mouse with the cunning and ruthless Ryder.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Ryder's motivations are not solely driven by a desire for financial gain, but also by a sense of control and a need to assert his dominance over others. This is reflected in his treatment of Garber and the other hostages, who are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and fears.

The film also touches on the theme of loyalty and duty, as Garber struggles with his obligations to both his employer and the hostages in his care. His ultimate decision to cooperate with Ryder raises questions about the nature of loyalty and whether it can ever truly be reconciled with doing what is right.

Furthermore, The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3 critiques the notion of heroism and the way in which individuals are perceived as heroes or villains. Garber's character, in particular, challenges traditional notions of heroism, as he navigates a complex web of moral gray areas and ultimately makes a choice that is both courageous and selfless.

Overall, The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3 is a thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of human nature and the moral dilemmas that arise in situations of crisis.

documents.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion
documents.original_title: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン劇場版 Air／まごころを、君に
documents.tagline: The fate of destruction is also the joy of rebirth
documents.overview: The second of two theatrically released follow-ups to the Neon Genesis Evangelion series. Comprising of two alternate episodes which were first intended to take the place of episodes 25 and 26, this finale answers many of the questions surrounding the series, while also opening up some new possibilities.
documents.plot:
Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion is a 96-minute anime film directed by Hideaki Anno, released in 1997. It serves as the final installment of the Neon Genesis Evangelion series and concludes the story of Shinji Ikari, a young boy who pilots the giant humanoid robot Evangelion Unit-01.

The film begins with Shinji, still reeling from the events of the previous episodes, struggling to cope with his emotional trauma. He is visited by Rei Ayanami, a mysterious and enigmatic being who has been a central figure in the series. Rei's presence serves as a catalyst for Shinji's introspection, and he begins to question his own identity and purpose.

As the story unfolds, Shinji becomes increasingly entangled with Asuka Langley Soryu, a rival pilot of Evangelion Unit-02. Their interactions are marked by tension and conflict, reflecting their deep-seated emotional scars. Meanwhile, the organization NERV, led by Gendo Ikari (Shinji's father), continues to pursue its goals of using the Evangelions to bring about human evolution.

The plot thickens as Shinji discovers a series of cryptic messages from his mother, Yui Ikari, who had been presumed dead. These messages reveal that she was involved in NERV's research and that her death was not what it seemed. This revelation sets off a chain reaction of events that lead to the climax of the film.

The final act of the movie is marked by an intense and surreal sequence of events. Shinji, Asuka, and Rei find themselves trapped in a series of nightmarish scenarios, each representing a different aspect of their psyches. These sequences are intercut with scenes of the Evangelions engaging in battle against monstrous creatures known as Angels.

As the story reaches its conclusion, Shinji is forced to confront his deepest fears and insecurities. He ultimately comes to terms with his own identity and finds a sense of acceptance and belonging. The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the meaning and significance of the events that have transpired.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of existentialism, psychological trauma, and the human condition. The movie's abstract and often surreal narrative style adds to its complexity and depth, making it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant conclusion to the Neon Genesis Evangelion series.

Ultimately, Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion is a powerful and haunting film that challenges viewers to confront their own emotions and insecurities. Its exploration of complex themes and abstract narrative style have made it a cult classic and a staple of anime fandom.

documents.title: Gamer
documents.tagline: In the near future, you don't live to play... you'll play to live.
documents.overview: Mind-control technology has taken society by a storm, a multiplayer on-line game called "Slayers" allows players to control human prisoners in mass-scale. Simon controls Kable, the online champion of the game. Kable's ultimate challenge becomes regaining his identity and independence by defeating the game's mastermind.
documents.plot:
Gamer is a 2009 science fiction action film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our actions in a virtual world. The movie explores the theme of escapism, where people can temporarily forget their troubles and immerse themselves in a fantasy world.

The main character, Ken Krepack (played by Gerard Butler), is an avid gamer who participates in a high-stakes gaming tournament, where he becomes trapped in his own game. As he navigates this virtual reality, he begins to question the nature of his existence and the true cost of his addiction.

Throughout the film, the theme of control vs. free will is also explored. The main antagonist, John "Black" Cremona (played by Gerard Butler), is a skilled gamer who uses his abilities to manipulate others and exert control over those around him. This raises questions about the extent to which we are willing to surrender our autonomy in pursuit of pleasure or power.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity, as Ken struggles to reconcile his virtual persona with his real-life self. As he becomes more entrenched in the game, he begins to lose touch with reality and his relationships with others suffer.

Ultimately, Gamer presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of becoming too immersed in our own fantasies and losing sight of what is truly important in life. The film serves as a commentary on our society's obsession with technology and entertainment, highlighting the need for balance and moderation in our pursuit of pleasure and excitement.

documents.title: Bronson
documents.tagline: The Man. The Myth. The Celebrity.
documents.overview: A young man who was sentenced to 7 years in prison for robbing a post office ends up spending 30 years in solitary confinement. During this time, his own personality is supplanted by his alter ego, Charles Bronson.
documents.plot:
Bronson is a 2008 British biographical prison film and black comedy directed by Nicolas Winding Refn, who co-wrote it with Brock Norman Brock. Tom Hardy stars as Michael Peterson, the man who took the name Charles Bronson in 1987 and came to be regarded as Britain's most violent prisoner, responsible for around a dozen hostage-takings behind bars. Matt King, James Lance, Kelly Adams and Amanda Burton co-star.

Peterson recounts his own life with mocking, self-deprecating humour, sometimes speaking straight to the camera in prison clothes and sometimes performing it as a stage act before a theatre audience. In 1974, aged 22, he robs a post office and receives seven years, but his violence inside keeps lengthening the sentence. Moved to a psychiatric hospital, he is sedated with drugs he says sap his strength, and in 1978 he tries to win a transfer back to prison by attempting to strangle a fellow inmate, a self-confessed paedophile, stopping short of murder. He points out that, for all his years in confinement, he has never killed anyone. He claims that a rooftop protest in 1982, which caused enormous damage, led the authorities to declare him sane and release him in 1987.

Free again, he visits his parents and his predatory Uncle Jack, who reunites him with a former inmate who arranges bare-knuckle fights and gives him the ring name Charles Bronson, after the American actor. On New Year's Day 1988 he steals a ring to propose to a woman who tells him he was only a fling, and after sixty-nine days of freedom he is back in jail. In 1993 he takes a prison librarian hostage, greases his naked body for the coming brawl with the guards, and is warned by the governor that he will die inside. In 1999 an art teacher sees promise in his drawings and Bronson briefly becomes a model prisoner, but when the art class is to close he seizes the teacher, paints himself black and arranges his captive as a living copy of René Magritte's The Son of Man before summoning the guards for another beating. Closing text notes that he has spent some thirty years in solitary confinement with no release date.

Hardy spoke with the real Bronson by phone before meeting him, and Bronson praised his portrayal. Filming took place in and around Nottingham. The film grossed about $2.3 million and drew positive reviews for Hardy's performance, holding 75% on Rotten Tomatoes and 71 on Metacritic, though some critics objected to its violence.

documents.title: The Ramen Girl
documents.tagline: Her romance is on pins and noodles.
documents.overview: An American woman is stranded in Tokyo after breaking up with her boyfriend. Searching for direction in life, she trains to be a râmen chef under a tyrannical Japanese master.
documents.plot:
The Ramen Girl is a 2008 romantic comedy-drama directed by Robert Allan Ackerman and starring Brittany Murphy, who also co-produced, as an American woman who learns to make ramen in Tokyo. Toshiyuki Nishida plays her demanding teacher and Kimiko Yo his wife, with Sohee Park, Tammy Blanchard, Gabriel Mann and Tsutomu Yamazaki, star of the noodle comedy Tampopo (1985). Much of the dialogue is in Japanese.

Abby has moved to Tokyo to be with her boyfriend Ethan, who soon dumps her and leaves for Osaka. Heartbroken, she wanders into a small ramen shop near her apartment, run by the gruff chef Maezumi and his wife Reiko, neither of whom speaks English. Maezumi serves her a bowl of noodles that leaves her strangely moved; she imagines the shop's beckoning cat waving at her, and the couple refuse her money. Returning, she helps out when Reiko is injured, and decides she wants to learn the art of ramen.

Maezumi reluctantly agrees to teach her but treats her harshly and gives her menial work in the hope that she will give up. Abby perseveres, wins over the customers as a waitress and meets Toshi Iwamoto, a young businessman with whom she bonds over the unexpected turns their lives have taken. When Maezumi's rival Udagawa boasts that a Grand Master will soon judge whether his son is worthy to carry on his ramen tradition, Maezumi drunkenly promises that Abby will be tested too. Abby learns from Reiko that Maezumi has not spoken in years to their son Shintaro, who left to become a chef in Paris.

Toshi is transferred to Shanghai and asks Abby to go with him, but she stays. Insisting that her ramen has no soul, Maezumi takes her to his mother, who tells her she must cook from the heart. Abby makes her broth in tears, and the customers who taste it are moved to tears themselves. The Grand Master enjoys her unconventional creation but withholds his blessing, saying she needs more restraint. Maezumi nonetheless names her his true successor before closing his shop after forty-five years, and gives her the lantern from its door.

A year later Abby runs her own ramen shop in New York, where Toshi, who has quit his job to make music, finds her. Reviews were mixed, with critics describing it as a gentle but slight mix of The Karate Kid and Tampopo.

documents.title: Eye of the Beholder
documents.tagline: Obsession is in the eye of the beholder.
documents.overview: A reclusive surveillance expert is hired to spy on a mysterious blackmailer, who just may be a serial killer.
documents.plot:
Eye of the Beholder is a 1999 mystery thriller with elements of magical realism, written and directed by Stephan Elliott. Based on Marc Behm's novel of the same name, which had previously been filmed by Claude Miller as the 1983 French thriller Deadly Circuit, it stars Ewan McGregor and Ashley Judd, with Patrick Bergin, k.d. lang and Geneviève Bujold. The film was an international co-production between Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia.

Stephen Wilson, known as "the Eye", is an intelligence agent who specialises in surveillance. He is still haunted by the loss of his young daughter, whom he has not seen since his former wife took her away, and her image constantly appears to him and talks to him. He is assigned to find out what trouble the socialite son of his superior has got into, and follows him to an encounter with a mysterious woman, Joanna Eris. Through his hidden camera, Stephen watches her murder the young man.

Instead of reporting her, Stephen becomes fascinated with Eris, whom he comes to see as a lost, vulnerable child, and he begins following her across the United States as she changes identities and kills again. Gradually he pieces together her past: she was abandoned by her father as a child, which seems to explain her deep hostility towards men. He keeps his discoveries to himself and protects her from a distance.

In one city, Eris meets Alexander, a wealthy blind man, and the two fall in love and plan to marry. Anxious to stop her from killing again, Stephen shoots out a tyre of their car on the way to the wedding, causing a crash that kills Alexander. A grieving Eris heads into the desert, where a drug addict named Gary picks her up when her car breaks down, then beats her and injects her with heroin in order to rape her. Stephen intervenes and beats Gary, but Eris loses the baby she was carrying.

She flees to Alaska and works as a waitress, and Stephen finally approaches her in person. They grow close over drinks, though Eris insists she has nothing to offer him. When the police and her psychiatrist come to arrest her, Stephen rescues her and takes her to his trailer, where she discovers that he has been watching her all along. Horrified, she shoots him, not knowing that his gun is loaded with blanks, and flees. He pursues her, and her car crashes through the ice of a lake. Stephen pulls her out, and she dies in his arms.

The film was a box-office failure and was panned by critics, with 10% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Lizzie McGuire Movie
documents.tagline: The only risk in taking an adventure is not taking it at all.
documents.overview: Lizzie McGuire has graduated from middle school and takes a trip to Rome, Italy with her class. And what was supposed to be only a normal trip, becomes a teenager's dream come true.
documents.plot:
The Lizzie McGuire Movie is a 2003 American teen comedy film directed by Jim Fall, based on the popular television series of the same name.

The movie follows Lizzie McGuire (Hilary Duff) as she travels to Rome with her family for a school trip.
