While there, she meets an Italian pop star named Isabella Parigi (Lacey Chabert), who bears a striking resemblance to herself. The two girls become friends and embark on a series of misadventures.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Identity: Lizzie struggles with her identity as she navigates her relationships, friendships, and family dynamics. Her encounter with Isabella forces her to confront her own insecurities and self-perception.
2. Friendship: The film highlights the importance of female friendship and the power of supportive relationships in overcoming challenges. Lizzie's bond with Isabella helps her navigate the complexities of adolescence.
3. Self-acceptance: Through her experiences, Lizzie learns to accept herself for who she is, flaws and all. She comes to terms with her individuality and finds confidence in her own uniqueness.
4. Cultural exchange: The movie celebrates the beauty of cultural diversity and the benefits of cross-cultural understanding. Lizzie's interactions with Isabella and the Italian culture serve as a catalyst for personal growth and self-discovery.

The film features a mix of humor, heart, and relatable themes that resonate with audiences, particularly young viewers.

documents.title: Island of Fire
documents.tagline: When you're looking for the living dead you start your search in hell!
documents.overview: Someone in a prison run by a corrupt warden fakes the deaths of convicts to later use them as expendable assassins. A police officer is sent into the prison to gather evidence of the corruption.
documents.plot:
Island of Fire is a 1990 Hong Kong action film directed by Sammo Hung. The movie follows the story of a young martial artist, Ching, who seeks revenge against the ruthless crime lord, Wong Fei-hung's (Sammo Hung) rival, Siu Lung.

The main theme of Island of Fire revolves around the struggle for power and loyalty in a world where honor and family are paramount. The film explores the complexities of loyalty, as Ching is torn between his duty to protect his mentor, Wong Fei-hung, and his desire for revenge against Siu Lung, who has wronged him.

The movie also delves into the theme of redemption, as Ching's quest for revenge becomes an opportunity for him to prove himself and earn the respect of those around him. Through Ching's journey, the film highlights the importance of self-discovery and the need to find one's own path in life.

Furthermore, Island of Fire touches on the theme of loyalty and betrayal, as Siu Lung's actions are motivated by a desire for power and control, leading him to betray those who have trusted him. The film ultimately suggests that true strength lies not in physical prowess, but in one's ability to form meaningful connections with others and to stand up for what is right.

Overall, Island of Fire is a classic martial arts film that explores themes of loyalty, redemption, and the struggle for power in a world where honor and family are deeply ingrained.

documents.title: The Haunting in Connecticut
documents.tagline: Some things cannot be explained.
documents.overview: When the Campbell family moves to upstate Connecticut, they soon learn that their charming Victorian home has a disturbing history: not only was the house a transformed funeral parlor where inconceivable acts occurred, but the owner's clairvoyant son Jonah served as a demonic messenger, providing a gateway for spiritual entities to crossover.
documents.plot:
The Haunting in Connecticut is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of trauma. At its core, the movie explores the theme of grief and loss, as it follows the story of the Snedeker family who are forced to confront their own personal demons after moving into a haunted house with a dark history.

The film also touches on the idea of guilt and redemption, as the family grapples with the consequences of their past mistakes. The movie's portrayal of a father's desperation to protect his children from the supernatural forces that surround them serves as a powerful commentary on the lengths to which parents will go to ensure their children's safety.

Furthermore, The Haunting in Connecticut examines the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. The film's depiction of the family's struggles to cope with their past traumas serves as a poignant reminder of the long-lasting effects of traumatic experiences on those who have survived them.

Ultimately, the movie presents a haunting (pun intended) exploration of the human condition, one that is both terrifying and thought-provoking.

documents.title: The Hangover
documents.tagline: Some guys just can't handle Vegas.
documents.overview: When three friends finally come to after a raucous night of bachelor-party revelry, they find a baby in the closet and a tiger in the bathroom. But they can't seem to locate their best friend, Doug – who's supposed to be tying the knot. Launching a frantic search for Doug, the trio perseveres through a nasty hangover to try to make it to the church on time.
documents.plot:
The Hangover is a 2009 American comedy film directed by Todd Phillips and written by Craig Mazin and Scott Moore. The movie follows the story of a group of friends who wake up after a wild bachelor party in Las Vegas with no memory of the night before.

The film begins with Phil Wenneck (Bradley Cooper), Stu Price (Ed Helms), Alan Garner (Zach Galifianakis), and Doug Billings (Justin Bartha) preparing for Doug's wedding to his fiancée, Tracy (Jamie Chung). The group decides to take a wild bachelor party to Las Vegas, where they spend the night drinking, dancing, and getting into various misadventures.

The next morning, the friends wake up in Phil's hotel suite with no memory of what happened the night before. They soon discover that Doug is missing, and their friend's wedding is just hours away. As they try to piece together the events of the previous night, they find a tiger in the bathroom, a missing front tooth for Stu, and a mysterious woman named Jade (Heather Graham) who claims to have slept with them.

As the friends try to track down Doug and figure out what happened to him, they encounter various obstacles, including a wild goose chase through the streets of Las Vegas, a run-in with a group of thugs, and a series of hilarious misadventures. Along the way, they also discover that Jade is not who she claims to be, and that the night before was much more eventful than they initially thought.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the friends had a wild and crazy night in Las Vegas, involving sex, drugs, and general debauchery. They eventually track down Doug's whereabouts and are able to return him to his fiancée just in time for the wedding.

The movie ends with the friends reflecting on the events of the previous night and the consequences that followed. While they all agree that it was a wild and crazy adventure, they also acknowledge that it may have been a mistake. The film ends with a comedic twist, as the friends are seen walking away from the wedding ceremony, still trying to process what happened the night before.

Throughout the movie, the humor is driven by the absurdity of the situation and the characters' reactions to it. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Zach Galifianakis as the eccentric and unpredictable Alan Garner. The film's success can be attributed to its well-crafted script, clever direction, and talented cast, which all come together to create a hilarious and entertaining movie experience.

Overall, The Hangover is a raunchy and irreverent comedy that explores themes of friendship, bachelorhood, and the consequences of one's actions. While it may not be for everyone, the film has become a cult classic and spawned two successful sequels.

documents.title: Dr. Dolittle 3
documents.overview: Lisa Dolittle sends her daughter to 'Durango', a Dude Ranch, to find herself. While there, she uses her talent to talk to the animals in order to save Durango from being taken over by a neighboring Ranch.
documents.plot:
Dr. Dolittle 3 is a family comedy film released in 2006, directed by Rich Thorne and produced by Davis Entertainment.

The movie follows the story of Dr. John Dolittle (played by Kyla Pratt), who has returned to her village after being away for several years. She reunites with her friends and family, including her animal friends, and sets out to help those in need. However, a greedy developer threatens to destroy their homes, leading Dr. Dolittle on a mission to save the animals and the community.

The main themes of Dr. Dolittle 3 include:

1. Environmentalism: The movie highlights the importance of preserving nature and protecting wildlife habitats.
2. Community: The film emphasizes the value of community and working together to achieve a common goal.
3. Friendship: Dr. Dolittle's relationships with her animal friends and human family members are central to the story, showcasing the power of friendship and loyalty.
4. Self-discovery: Throughout the movie, Dr. Dolittle learns more about herself and her abilities, leading to personal growth and self-awareness.

The plot development is driven by the conflict between the greedy developer and the animal community, which serves as a catalyst for Dr. Dolittle's actions. The ending features a heartwarming conclusion where Dr. Dolittle successfully saves the animals and their homes, restoring balance to the community.

Overall, Dr. Dolittle 3 is a lighthearted, family-friendly film that promotes positive values and messages, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Irresistible
documents.tagline: A secret is not safe if the truth has a witness.
documents.overview: A wife and mother is consumed by the thought that her husband's co-worker is trying to win him away from her and their family.
documents.plot:
Irresistible is a 2006 Australian psychological thriller and mystery drama written and directed by Ann Turner. Susan Sarandon stars as Sophie Hartley, an American illustrator, with Sam Neill as her husband Craig and Emily Blunt as Mara, his new colleague. Charles "Bud" Tingwell and William McInnes appear in supporting roles.

Sophie is a successful children's book illustrator, happily married to Craig and mother of two young daughters, Ruby and Elly. Still grieving the recent death of her mother, she begins to notice strange things around the house. One afternoon, convinced she left the iron on, she rushes home to find it still hot but switched off, and she later senses that someone has been inside. At a party she meets Mara, a young and attractive woman who works with Craig. On a walk along the beach, Mara sympathizes over Sophie's loss and tells her about her own grief for a best friend, an aid worker who died trying to save babies when an orphanage in Kosovo was firebombed.

In the following weeks, objects disappear from the house, including one of Sophie's dresses and Elly's favorite toy. One of Sophie's illustrations is ruined, which she blames on the cat knocking over an inkwell, and she is attacked by wasps that emerge from an ornament in her studio. When she sees Mara wearing the missing dress, Sophie becomes convinced that the younger woman is breaking into her home and trying to take over her life. She breaks into Mara's apartment in search of proof but is caught, and a court issues a restraining order against her, with Craig failing to support her. Increasingly isolated, and suspecting that Craig and Mara are having an affair, Sophie retreats to a friend's cabin to clear her head. Conversations with her father bring buried secrets from her own youth to the surface, and as her family and those around her question her sanity, Sophie must determine whether Mara truly poses a threat or whether her grief and guilt are distorting her perception.

The film received mixed reviews. Critics praised Sarandon's committed performance and Blunt's unsettling turn as Mara, made shortly before her breakthrough in international cinema, but many found the plot twists contrived and the suspense uneven.

documents.title: Naruto: Guardians of the Crescent Moon Kingdom
documents.original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- 大興奮!みかづき島のアニマル騒動だってばよ
documents.overview: Naruto Uzumaki, Kakashi Hatake, Sakura Haruno, and Rock Lee are assigned to protect the prince of the Land of the Moon, Michiru, during his world trip; other escorts had been hired, but quit due to being treated poorly. The Land of the Moon is a very wealthy nation, so Michiru tends to buy whatever he wants, and has a very materialistic worldview. His Hikaru, also acts in much the same manner.
documents.plot:
Naruto the Movie: Guardians of the Crescent Moon Kingdom (Japanese title literally "Great Excitement! The Animal Panic of Crescent Moon Island!") is a Japanese animated martial arts fantasy adventure of 2006 written and directed by Toshiyuki Tsuru and produced by Studio Pierrot, based on Masashi Kishimoto's manga. The third and last film of the series' first part, it features the voices of Junko Takeuchi as Naruto Uzumaki, Chie Nakamura as Sakura Haruno, Yōichi Masukawa as Rock Lee, Kazuhiko Inoue as Kakashi Hatake, Kyōsuke Ikeda as Prince Hikaru and Akio Ōtsuka as his father Michiru.

Naruto, Kakashi, Sakura and Lee are assigned to escort Michiru, heir to the fabulously rich Land of the Moon, and his spoiled son Hikaru home. Michiru casually buys an entire circus so that Hikaru can befriend its star sabre-toothed cat, Chamū, and its monkey partner Kiki, but Chamū attacks the boy. Michiru's former wife, Amayo, rejects his hopes of reconciliation, saying he does not understand what really matters. During a storm at sea, Naruto rebukes Hikaru for not caring about the animals, and Hikaru helps save Chamū and Kiki, winning their friendship and Naruto's.

On arrival they find that the greedy minister Shabadaba has overthrown King Kakeru, Michiru's father. Loyal soldiers under Captain Korega help the group flee to a mountain refuge, where the dying Kakeru, turned partly to stone by the gauntlet of the hired ninja Ishidate, tells his son that wealth is not happiness and names him king. Ishidate's mercenaries poison the team, kill Korega and capture Michiru. Shabadaba reveals that he seized power to keep the kingdom's riches for himself, whereas Kakeru wanted to spend them on his people. Rallied by Naruto, the group sneaks into the palace with help from the circus, Kakashi leads a surprise attack, and Lee and Sakura defeat Ishidate's henchmen Karenbana and Kongō. Hikaru saves his father from hanging with an arrow, and, carried by father and son, Naruto finishes Ishidate and Shabadaba with a Rasengan strengthened by the island's moonlight. While Kakashi recovers, the team enjoy two weeks on the island and see Michiru and Hikaru inaugurated as king and prince, and Michiru resolves to win back Amayo.

Distributed by Toho, the film opened in Japan on 5 August 2006 and grossed about $3.2 million.

documents.title: Kite
documents.overview: Sawa may seem innocent and naive, but don’t be fooled. She is a cold-blooded killer, and if you’re on the wrong side of the law, you may be her next target. Not content to just watch as the imperfect justice system lets more and more criminals go loose every day, a detective decides to train the young Sawa to be his instrument of justice.
documents.plot:
Kite is a 1998 Japanese adult original video animation written and directed by Yasuomi Umetsu. Originally released on VHS as two episodes of about 25 minutes each in February and October 1998, it was later edited into a single feature for its home video releases in the United States, in versions with differing amounts of sexual content. The story follows a teenage girl forced to work as an assassin, and it is notorious for its graphic violence and sexual abuse.

Sawa is a schoolgirl orphaned after her parents were brutally murdered. She is taken in by two detectives, Akai and Kanie, who were assigned to the case. They use her as a hired killer, sending her to eliminate targets ranging from corrupt police officers to wealthy businessmen. Akai also sexually abuses her, and he has given her a pair of crystal earrings said to contain her parents' blood. Sawa's killings become infamous among the police because of the special bullets she uses, which explode after entering the body. In an early assignment she kills a celebrity during a date.

On one job Sawa meets Oburi, a boy of her age who also works as an assassin for the two men, and they form a close bond. Oburi gives her the courage to imagine escaping. When Oburi decides to leave after completing a final set of assignments, Akai orders Sawa to kill him. Oburi tells her that her guardians murdered her parents, and Sawa replies that she has long known. She spares him, and later, wounded and missing an earring after a mission, rescues him when a target turns out to be a heavily armed police officer.

When Oburi announces that both of them are quitting, Akai beats him and captures Sawa, then punishes Oburi by forcing him to watch as he assaults her. Kanie takes Oburi away to be killed, and Akai, believing Sawa has turned against Oburi, tells her where he is being taken. The next morning, Akai is called to a crime scene and finds Kanie's body at the very spot where Sawa's parents were killed years earlier.

Akai rushes to the place where Oburi was to be executed but finds Sawa waiting, and she shoots him repeatedly with both her own and Oburi's guns before throwing the weapons away along with her remaining earring. Before the two can reunite, Oburi is shot by another young assassin. Sawa waits for him in his hideout, turning at the sound of a footstep as the screen goes dark.

Reviews have been generally positive, with critics praising its action and animation while noting its deeply disturbing content.

documents.title: Man-Thing
documents.tagline: The nature of fear
documents.overview: Agents of an oil tycoon vanish while exploring a swamp marked for drilling. The local sheriff investigates and faces a Seminole legend come to life: Man-Thing, a shambling swamp-monster whose touch burns those who feel fear.
documents.plot:
Man-Thing is a 2005 superhero monster film loosely based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name. Directed by Brett Leonard and written by Hans Rodionoff, it stars Matthew Le Nevez, Rachael Taylor and Jack Thompson, with Conan Stevens as the title creature, a shambling swamp monster drawn from a Seminole legend. Originally intended for a theatrical release in the United States, the film premiered in Singapore in April 2005 and was then shown in the US as a "Sci-Fi Original" on the Sci Fi Channel on April 30, 2005.

At Dark Waters, a sacred Native American swampland said to be home to a mysterious guardian spirit, a teenager is killed by a plant-like monster. Kyle Williams, a young replacement sheriff, arrives in the town of Bywater and learns from deputy Fraser that his predecessor is one of 47 people who have gone missing since oil tycoon Fred Schist acquired the tribal lands from the Seminole chief and shaman Ted Sallis, who was the first to disappear. Schist insists that Sallis sold the land legally and ran off with the money, and he blames the trouble on local protesters and on Rene Laroque, a swamp dweller who has been sabotaging his drilling operation. As Williams investigates, more bodies turn up, some with plants growing out of them. Photographer Mike Ploog and shaman Pete Horn tell him about the legend of the swamp's guardian, and the medical examiner, Val Mayerik, admits that the former sheriff ordered him to record the deaths as alligator attacks. Williams heads into the swamp to track Laroque while Schist sends a pair of local thugs to kill him, and the creature lurking in the water claims more victims. Helped by schoolteacher Teri Richards, for whom he develops romantic feelings, Williams gradually uncovers the truth about Schist's crimes, the fate of Ted Sallis and the vengeful force rising from the sacred ground to punish those who have desecrated it.

Man-Thing received negative reviews from critics and was a box-office bomb, earning about $1 million from a small international theatrical release. David Nusair of Reel Film Reviews called it "the worst comic book movie ever made", while Felix Vasquez of Cinema Crazed praised its special effects but felt it botched a good concept. It was released on DVD in June 2005.

documents.title: Facing the Giants
documents.tagline: Never give up. Never back down. Never lose faith.
documents.overview: A losing coach with an underdog football team faces their giants of fear and failure on and off the field to surprising results.
documents.plot:
Facing the Giants is a 2006 American sports drama film directed by Chris Evans and written by Aneestyn Fokkena, Chris Fabry, and Jon Abrahams. The movie stars Shannen Doherty, Kenan Thompson, and Cody Kasch.

The story revolves around the fictional high school football team, Mount Paulet High School's Panthers, who are struggling to find success on and off the field. The team is led by Coach Grant Taylor (played by Shannen Doherty), a former NFL player who has lost his faith in God after a tragic accident involving his son.

As the season begins, the team faces numerous challenges, including internal conflicts, personal struggles, and external pressures from their opponents. However, with the help of a new assistant coach, Coach Grant Taylor's wife, Jill (played by Shannen Doherty), who is a Christian minister, the team starts to come together.

Through a series of events, including a dramatic game against their arch-rivals, the Panthers learn valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and faith. The movie explores themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the power of prayer, as the team faces various obstacles on and off the field.

As the season progresses, Coach Taylor's relationship with his son, who is struggling with a serious illness, becomes a central focus of the story. Through his faith and perseverance, Coach Taylor finds the strength to overcome his personal struggles and lead his team to victory.

The movie culminates in an intense game against their arch-rivals, where the Panthers face off against their toughest opponent yet. With the help of prayer and teamwork, the Panthers emerge victorious, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

Throughout the film, the characters undergo significant personal growth and development, learning valuable lessons about faith, perseverance, and the importance of working together towards a common goal. The movie features a mix of drama, sports action, and inspirational moments, making it an engaging and uplifting watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Facing the Giants is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of faith, redemption, and perseverance in the face of adversity. With its talented cast, engaging storyline, and uplifting message, this movie is sure to leave viewers feeling motivated and inspired.

documents.title: The Boat That Rocked
documents.tagline: On air. Off shore. Out of control.
documents.overview: The Boat That Rocked is an ensemble comedy, where the romance is between the young people of the 60s, and pop music. It's about a band of DJs that captivate Britain, playing the music that defines a generation and standing up to a government that  wanted control of popular culture via the British Broadcasting Corporation. Loosely based on the events in Britain in the 60's when the Labour government of Harold Wilson, wanted to bring the pirate radio stations under control, enough to see the passage of the Marine Broadcasting Offences Act on 15 August 1967. Also known as "Pirate Radio".
documents.plot:
The Boat That Rocked, released in North America as Pirate Radio, is a 2009 British comedy-drama film written and directed by Richard Curtis about pirate radio in the United Kingdom in the 1960s. Its ensemble cast includes Philip Seymour Hoffman, Bill Nighy, Rhys Ifans, Nick Frost, Kenneth Branagh, Tom Sturridge and Emma Thompson. It was produced by Working Title Films for Universal Pictures.

In 1966, while the BBC plays almost no rock and pop music, pirate stations broadcast it to millions of listeners from ships in international waters. Seventeen-year-old Carl, recently expelled from school, is sent by his mother to spend time with his godfather, Quentin, who runs Radio Rock from an old ship anchored in the North Sea. There Carl joins an eccentric community of disc jockeys and crew, led by the brash American DJ known as the Count.

In London, the government minister Sir Alistair Dormandy is determined to shut the pirate stations down, and instructs his aide, Twatt, to find a legal means of doing so. When the government forbids British companies from advertising on unlicensed stations, Quentin responds by bringing back the legendary DJ Gavin Kavanagh, whose popularity draws advertisers back but sparks a rivalry with the Count. Carl falls for Quentin's niece, Marianne, but she is seduced by the DJ Doctor Dave; the gentle DJ Simple Simon marries a glamorous fan who soon leaves him for Gavin, prompting a dangerous duel between Gavin and the Count on the ship's mast. When his mother visits at Christmas, Carl learns that the reclusive late-night DJ Bob Silver is his father, and Marianne later returns to him.

Dormandy finally gets his law when a fishing boat's distress call is blocked by Radio Rock's signal, and the Marine Broadcasting Offences Act makes the pirate stations illegal from August 1967. The crew defy the law and keep broadcasting, starting the ship's engine to evade arrest, but the old vessel's engine explodes and it begins to sink. Dormandy refuses to send help, but as the DJs keep broadcasting their position, dozens of fans sail out in small boats to rescue them, Carl being pulled from the water by Marianne.

The film premiered in London in March 2009 and was released in the United Kingdom on 1 April. It received mixed reviews, with criticism of its length, and performed poorly at the British box office; for North America it was cut by about twenty minutes. It grossed about $36.6 million worldwide against a $50 million budget.

documents.title: Azur & Asmar: The Princes' Quest
documents.overview: Raised on tales of a Djinn fairy princess, Azur, a young Frenchman goes to North Africa in search of the sprite, only to discover that his close childhood friend, Asmar, an Arab youth whose mother raised both boys also seeks the genie.
documents.plot:
Azur & Asmar: The Princes' Quest is a beautifully crafted animated film that weaves together elements of adventure, fantasy, and coming-of-age themes. At its core, the movie explores the complexities of identity, belonging, and self-discovery.

The story follows Azur, a young prince who feels suffocated by his royal duties and longs for freedom and adventure. As he embarks on a perilous journey with his companion Asmar, they encounter various challenges that test their courage, wit, and loyalty to one another. Through their experiences, the film delves into the theme of finding one's place in the world and embracing one's true nature.

The movie also touches upon the idea of identity formation, as Azur struggles to reconcile his royal heritage with his desire for independence and individuality. This internal conflict is mirrored in Asmar's own journey, as he grapples with his own sense of purpose and belonging.

Furthermore, the film explores the importance of friendship and camaraderie, highlighting the transformative power of relationships in shaping our experiences and perspectives. The bond between Azur and Asmar serves as a beacon of hope and support, allowing them to navigate the complexities of their quest together.

Ultimately, Azur & Asmar: The Princes' Quest is a poignant and engaging film that invites viewers to reflect on their own journey of self-discovery and growth. With its richly detailed world-building and memorable characters, the movie offers a captivating exploration of the human experience.

documents.title: Down
documents.tagline: YOUR NEXT STOP... IS HELL.
documents.overview: After the elevators at a New York City skyscraper begin inexplicably malfunctioning, putting its passengers at risk, mechanic Mark Newman and reporter Jennifer Evans begin separate investigations. Newman gets resistance from superiors at his company, which manufactured the elevator, while additional elevator incidents cause several gruesome deaths. The police get involved and suspect that terrorists are responsible, but a far stranger explanation looms.
documents.plot:
Down, retitled The Shaft for its American release, is a 2001 English-language Dutch science fiction horror film written and directed by Dick Maas. James Marshall, Naomi Watts and Eric Thal star, with Michael Ironside, Edward Herrmann, Dan Hedaya and Ron Perlman in supporting roles. It is a remake of Maas's own 1983 Dutch-language film The Lift. Filming took place mainly in the Netherlands, with brief exterior shoots in New York City and Washington, D.C.

In New York, a lightning strike hits the Millennium Building, a 102-storey skyscraper with dozens of elevators, and its three express elevators start behaving strangely. The next day, a car carrying a group of pregnant women stalls between floors and rapidly overheats, sending them to hospital. Jennifer Evans, an ambitious tabloid reporter, is assigned to cover the incident. Mark Newman, a repairman and former Marine, and his colleague Jeff McClellan, technicians for the elevator company, inspect the system and find nothing wrong, with Jeff insisting that the computer controlling the elevators is flawless.

The incidents soon turn deadly. A blind man and his guide dog vanish in the building; a security guard is decapitated when his head is trapped between closing doors; and other occupants die in increasingly grisly ways. The building's owners and the elevator company's executives, worried about lawsuits and bad publicity, deny there is a problem, but Mark becomes convinced that the elevators are acting with intent. Teaming up with Jennifer, who sees a major story, he investigates and uncovers evidence of a secret experiment involving organic material in the elevator's control system, a discovery that puts them in danger from both the machine and the people who want the truth covered up.

Down premiered in 2001 but received a limited release, and reviews were mostly negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported a 20 percent approval rating based on a small number of reviews, with critics faulting its weak storyline, unrealistic deaths, dialogue and special effects. Dutch critics were also largely unfavorable. The film was released in the same year as Watts's breakthrough role in Mulholland Drive.

documents.title: Johnson Family Vacation
documents.tagline: Take the ride.
documents.overview: Nate Johnson, a Los Angeles man estranged from his wife and three children, decides to reconnect with his family by taking them with him on a road trip to Missouri for a big family reunion.
documents.plot:
Johnson Family Vacation is a comedy film that revolves around the misadventures of the Johnson family during their disastrous road trip to Walley World. The movie explores several themes, primarily centered around the importance of family bonding and the challenges that come with it.

At its core, the film delves into the complexities of family relationships, showcasing the love, frustration, and humor that often accompany them. The characters' interactions are filled with witty banter, physical comedy, and heartfelt moments, highlighting the ups and downs of family life.

The movie also touches on themes of nostalgia, as the family's trip to Walley World becomes a nostalgic journey for the parents, who are trying to recapture their own childhood memories. This nostalgia serves as a catalyst for the family's bonding experience, as they learn to appreciate each other's quirks and imperfections.

Furthermore, Johnson Family Vacation pokes fun at modern suburban life, satirizing the monotony and superficiality of middle-class existence. The film's portrayal of the characters' mundane daily routines and their desperation for excitement serves as a commentary on the human desire for adventure and connection.

Ultimately, the movie presents a heartwarming and humorous exploration of family dynamics, love, and acceptance, reminding viewers that even in the most chaotic moments, family can be a source of comfort, support, and joy.
production_companies: A Bird and a Bear Entertainment

documents.title: Away We Go
documents.overview: Verona and Burt have moved to Colorado to be close to Burt's parents but, with Veronica expecting their first child, Burt's parents decide to move to Belgium, now leaving them in a place they hate and without a support structure in place. They set off on a whirlwind tour of of disparate locations where they have friends or relatives, sampling not only different cities and climates but also different families. Along the way they realize that the journey is less about discovering where they want to live and more about figuring out what type of parents they want to be.
documents.plot:
Away We Go is a 2009 American comedy-drama film directed by Sam Mendes and written by Dave Eggers. The movie follows the story of Burt Farlander, a man who embarks on a road trip with his pregnant wife Verona to find the perfect place for their unborn child.

The main theme of Away We Go is the exploration of identity, love, and letting go. As Burt and Verona travel across the country, they are forced to confront their own desires, fears, and expectations about parenthood, marriage, and adulthood. The film delves into the complexities of relationships, highlighting the tension between independence and interdependence.

Through Burt's character, the movie explores the theme of masculinity and the societal pressures that come with it. As a man who is struggling to find his place in the world, Burt must navigate the challenges of becoming a father while also confronting his own sense of identity.

The film also touches on the idea of community and belonging. As Burt and Verona meet various eccentric characters along their journey, they begin to realize that family is not just about blood ties, but about the people who become like family to you.

Ultimately, Away We Go is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to be human, to love, and to find one's place in the world. The movie's themes are woven together with a sense of humor, wit, and sensitivity, making for a truly unforgettable viewing experience.

documents.title: Whatever Works
documents.tagline: A new comedy!
documents.overview: Whatever Works explores the relationship between a crotchety misanthrope, Boris and a naïve, impressionable young runaway from the south, Melody. When Melody's uptight parents arrive in New York to rescue her, they are quickly drawn into wildly unexpected romantic entanglements. Everyone discovers that finding love is just a combination of lucky chance and appreciating the value of "whatever works."
documents.plot:
Whatever Works is a 2009 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Woody Allen. The movie revolves around Cady (played by Evan Rachel Wood), a young woman who leaves her small town in search of independence and freedom, only to find herself drawn to a free-spirited man named Gordon (played by Paul Dano) who lives off the grid.

The main theme of Whatever Works is the exploration of individuality and nonconformity. The film celebrates the idea of living life on one's own terms, rejecting societal norms and expectations in favor of a more authentic and spontaneous existence. Through Cady's journey, the movie highlights the tension between the desire for freedom and the need for connection and community.

The film also delves into the complexities of relationships and intimacy, as Cady navigates her feelings for Gordon while struggling to define herself outside of their relationship. The movie raises questions about what it means to be independent, how much one is willing to compromise in order to find love and belonging, and whether true freedom can coexist with vulnerability.

Furthermore, Whatever Works touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Cady grapples with her own desires, values, and sense of purpose. The movie suggests that finding oneself is a continuous process, one that requires embracing uncertainty and being open to new experiences and relationships.

Overall, Whatever Works is a nuanced exploration of the human search for meaning, connection, and individuality, inviting viewers to reflect on their own values and priorities in life.

documents.title: In Hell
documents.tagline: Rage unleashed.
documents.overview: A man must survive a prison where hardened criminals battle to the death for the warden's entertainment.
documents.plot:
In Hell is an American action thriller of 2003 directed by Ringo Lam, his third and last collaboration with Jean-Claude Van Damme. Van Damme stars as Kyle LeBlanc, an American locked away in a brutal Russian prison, with Lawrence Taylor as the feared Inmate 451, Lloyd Battista as the corrupt warden General Hruschov, Michael Bailey Smith as Valya and Chris Moir as Billy Cooper.

Kyle, working abroad in the Russian city of Magnitogorsk, hears his wife being attacked over the phone and arrives to find her dead. Her killer, Sergio Kovic, bribes the judge and walks free, and the enraged Kyle grabs a bailiff's gun and shoots him dead in the courtroom. Sentenced to life without parole, he is sent to Kravavi Prison, ruled by General Hruschov, and beaten for hesitating to give up his wedding ring. He watches a young American inmate, Billy, dragged off to be raped by the Russian mobster Andrei, fights Andrei the next morning, and is thrown into solitary, where he attempts suicide. Deciding instead to survive, he gets himself moved into the cell of Inmate 451, notorious for killing his cellmates, and the two form an unlikely bond. Malakai, an American in a wheelchair, explains the gangs and the Mafia's pact with the guards.

Kyle trains as a prison fighter and kills Andrei in his first bout, which shakes him badly, but he keeps fighting, grows hard, wins the respect of the inmates and turns away help from the American embassy. When Malakai betrays Billy's escape plans in return for medical care, 451 burns him alive, recalling how he killed the teacher who abused him in the same way. Billy dies after resisting Valya's assault, warning Kyle not to let anyone change who he is. Kyle refuses to fight Valya and is strung up by his arms in the yard; moved by his endurance, the rival gangs unite and refuse to fight. Ordered to face Miloc, a giant prisoner he knew from solitary, Kyle again refuses, and a riot erupts in which Miloc is shot shielding him. Amid the chaos, 451 gives Kyle evidence of the prison's abuses and shows him a secret way to the garage. Kyle must first defeat Valya, who pulls a knife during the fight, and kills him. 451 stays behind to deal with Hruschov while Kyle recovers his ring and drives away. Back in the United States, he exposes Kravavi, which is shut down three months later.

The film was released on DVD in the United States in November 2003. Reviews were poor: TV Guide gave it one star out of five, and IGN said it was strictly for Van Damme fans.

documents.title: Leprechaun: Back 2 tha Hood
documents.tagline: Evil has a whole new rap!
documents.overview: When Emily Woodrow and her friends happen on a treasure chest full of gold coins, they fail to to heed the warnings of a wise old psychic who had foretold that they would encounter trouble with a very nasty and protective Leprechaun.
documents.plot:
Leprechaun: Back to the Hood is a 2003 American horror-comedy film directed by Rob Spera and starring Curtis Armstrong, J.C. Brandy, and Eddie Griffin.

The main themes of Leprechaun: Back to the Hood revolve around the struggle for power, revenge, and redemption in an urban setting. The movie follows the story of a group of teenagers who unwittingly unleash the vengeful spirit of the Leprechaun, played by Warwick Davis, on their neighborhood.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the Leprechaun's primary motivation is to reclaim his stolen gold and exact revenge on those who wronged him. However, as he navigates the urban jungle, he begins to realize that there are more complex issues at play, such as poverty, racism, and social inequality.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with their own personal demons and confront the harsh realities of growing up in a tough neighborhood. The movie explores themes of identity, community, and the struggle for survival in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, the Leprechaun's quest for revenge becomes a metaphor for the cyclical nature of violence and the need for redemption and forgiveness. The film's ending suggests that even in the darkest of times, there is always hope for change and a chance to start anew.

Overall, Leprechaun: Back to the Hood offers a unique blend of horror-comedy and social commentary, making it a fascinating and thought-provoking watch.

documents.title: Godzilla vs. Gigan
documents.original_title: 地球攻撃命令 ゴジラ対ガイガン
documents.tagline: Defeat the evil space monsters! You can protect the Earth, Godzilla!
documents.overview: Manga artist Gengo Odaka lands a job with the World Children's Land amusement park only to become suspicious of the organization when a garbled message is discovered on tapes. As Gengo and his team investigate, Godzilla and Anguirus quickly decipher the message and begin their own plan of action.
documents.plot:
Godzilla vs. Gigan is a 1972 Japanese science fiction kaiju film directed by Jun Fukuda and produced by Tomoyuki Tanaka, for Toho Studios.

The movie revolves around the theme of technological hubris and the dangers of unchecked scientific progress. The titular monster, Gigan, is a cyborg created by aliens to wreak havoc on Earth, serving as a metaphor for the destructive potential of human innovation when left unregulated.

Godzilla, often seen as a symbol of nature's power and resilience, also plays a significant role in this theme. As the two monsters clash, Godzilla's primal fury serves as a counterbalance to Gigan's cold, calculated brutality, highlighting the importance of respecting and preserving the natural world.

Furthermore, the film touches on the idea of existentialism, as both characters embody the concept of "otherness." Gigan represents an external force that threatens humanity's dominance, while Godzilla is a creature that has been awakened by human actions, forcing humans to confront their own vulnerability in the face of nature's power.

The movie also explores the theme of sacrifice and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The character of Dr. Shiragami, who created Gigan, serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of scientific ambition without moral responsibility.

Overall, Godzilla vs. Gigan is a thought-provoking film that uses its iconic monsters to explore complex themes and ideas, making it more than just a mindless monster movie.

documents.title: Josie and the Pussycats
documents.tagline: They were three small time girls, with big time dreams. Now, fate is giving the Pussycats, the chance of a lifetime.
documents.overview: Josie, Melody and Val are three small-town girl musicians determined to take their rock band out of their garage and straight to the top, while remaining true to their look, style and sound. They get a record deal which brings fame and fortune but soon realize they are pawns of two people who want to control the youth of America. They must clear their names, even if it means losing fame and fortune.
documents.plot:
Josie and the Pussycats is a 2001 musical comedy film that explores several themes, primarily focusing on female empowerment, friendship, and self-discovery. The movie follows the story of Josie, Melody, and Valerie, three teenage girls who form a rock band called the Pussycats.

At its core, the film celebrates the power of female friendships and the importance of supporting one another in pursuing their passions. The main characters are strong-willed and independent individuals who refuse to be defined by societal expectations or stereotypes. They use their music as a means of self-expression and empowerment, taking control of their lives and forging their own paths.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, particularly for young women navigating the complexities of adolescence. Josie, Melody, and Valerie must balance their individual desires with the pressures of conformity and social norms. Through their experiences, they learn to stay true to themselves and find their unique voices.

Furthermore, the film critiques the music industry's objectification of women, as embodied by the villainous character, Wyatt Frame. The Pussycats' rise to fame serves as a commentary on the commodification of female talent and the exploitation of young artists for commercial gain.

Ultimately, Josie and the Pussycats is a heartwarming tale about embracing one's individuality, finding creative expression, and celebrating the bonds of sisterhood.

documents.title: Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge
documents.tagline: Come Fall In love, All Over Again..
documents.overview: Raj is a rich, carefree, happy-go-lucky second generation NRI. Simran is the daughter of Chaudhary Baldev Singh, who in spite of being an NRI is very strict about adherence to Indian values. Simran has left for India to be married to her childhood fiancé. Raj leaves for India with a mission at his hands, to claim his lady love under the noses of her whole family. Thus begins a saga.
documents.plot:
Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (DDLJ) is a timeless classic that has captivated audiences for decades, and its themes continue to resonate with viewers today. Here are some of the main themes of this iconic film:

1. **Love vs. Family Expectations**: The movie explores the conflict between following one's heart and conforming to family expectations. Raj (Shah Rukh Khan) falls in love with Simran (Kajol), but his family wants him to marry a woman they choose for him, leading to a rift between Raj and his family.

2. **Self-Discovery**: DDLJ is also a journey of self-discovery for both the lead characters. Raj learns to stand up for himself and assert his independence, while Simran finds her own identity and voice in a world where she's expected to be a dutiful daughter-in-law.

3. **Cultural Identity**: The film delves into the complexities of cultural identity, particularly in the context of Indian society. It highlights the importance of respecting one's heritage while also embracing change and individuality.

4. **Friendship and Loyalty**: The bond between Raj and his friends, particularly Anjali (Rani Mukerji) and Surinder (Anupam Kher), is a significant theme in the movie. Their loyalty and support for each other serve as a catalyst for Raj's growth and transformation.

5. **Love Conquers All**: Ultimately, DDLJ is a love story that showcases the power of true love to overcome even the most daunting obstacles. The film's iconic finale, where Raj declares his love for Simran in front of their families, is a testament to the enduring nature of love.

6. **Social Commentary**: On a deeper level, the movie offers commentary on social issues like arranged marriages, family pressure, and the limitations placed on women in Indian society during that era.

Yash Raj Films' masterpiece has become an integral part of Indian pop culture, and its themes continue to resonate with audiences today.

documents.title: Recess: School's Out
documents.tagline: Saving The World One Playground At A Time
documents.overview: It's the most exciting time of year at Third Street Elementary-- the end of the School Year! But boredom quickly sets in for protagonist TJ Detweiler, as his friends are headed for Summer Camp. One day, while passing by the school on his bike, he notices a green glow coming from the school's auditorium. This is the work of the insidious ex-principal of Third Street, Phillium Benedict and his gang of ninjas and secret service look-alikes! Benedict is planning to get rid of Summer Vacation using his newly-acquired Tractor Beam, which he stole from the US Military Base in an effort to raise US Test Scores, and it's up to the Recess Gang to stop him!
documents.plot:
"Recess: School's Out" is a 2001 animated comedy film produced by Walt Disney Television Animation. The movie follows the adventures of six friends - T.J., Spinelli, Gus, Mikey, Vinnie, and Gretchen - as they try to have one last day of fun before the school year ends.

The main themes of "Recess: School's Out" include:

1. Friendship: The film highlights the strong bonds of friendship between the six main characters, who work together to overcome obstacles and have a blast.
2. Imagination and creativity: The movie showcases the kids' vivid imaginations and creative problem-solving skills as they come up with innovative ways to make their last day of school unforgettable.
3. Growing up and letting go: As the kids prepare for the end of the school year, they must also confront the reality of growing up and moving on from childhood. The film explores this bittersweet theme through the characters' experiences.
4. Self-discovery: Throughout the movie, each character faces challenges that help them learn more about themselves and their relationships with others.

The plot development revolves around the kids' plan to pull off a series of pranks and stunts on their last day of school, which ultimately leads to a wild adventure filled with excitement, humor, and heart. The ending is a mix of action-packed fun and emotional closure as the characters reflect on the value of friendship and the importance of cherishing memories.

Overall, "Recess: School's Out" is a lighthearted, entertaining film that celebrates the joys of childhood friendships and the power of imagination.

documents.title: Princess Protection Program
documents.tagline: Royality meets reality.
documents.overview: When her nation is invaded, a young princess is taken into the Princess Protection Program. She is relocated to Louisiana, where she stays with a covert agent and his tomboyish daughter, and must learn how to behave like an ordinary teenager.
documents.plot:
Princess Protection Program is a 2009 American comedy television film produced as a Disney Channel Original Movie, directed by Allison Liddi-Brown and written by Annie DeYoung from a story by DeYoung and David Morgasen. Demi Lovato stars as Princess Rosalinda and Selena Gomez as Carter Mason, with Tom Verica as her father, Nicholas Braun and Molly Hagan. It premiered on Disney Channel on 26 June 2009 and was released on DVD shortly afterwards.

Princess Rosalinda María Montoya Fioré is about to be crowned queen of the small nation of Costa Luna when her coronation rehearsal is interrupted by General Magnus Kane, the dictator of neighboring Costa Estrella, whose forces storm the palace in an attempt to seize the country. Major Joe Mason, an agent of the Princess Protection Program, a secret organization funded by royal families to protect endangered princesses, rescues Rosalinda by helicopter, but Kane's men capture her widowed mother, Queen Sofía.

While the program works to remove Kane from power and free her kingdom, Rosalinda is hidden at Joe's home in rural Louisiana, where she meets his daughter, Carter, an insecure tomboy who works at the family bait shop and dreams of going to the homecoming dance with her crush, Donny, unaware that her classmate Ed likes her. Rosalinda poses as Rosie Gonzalez, Carter's cousin from Iowa. Carter is hostile at first, but warms to her after learning her story, and the two become close friends. Carter teaches Rosie to act like an ordinary American teenager, while Rosie shows Carter how to carry herself with the confidence of a princess. Rosie becomes popular at school and is nominated for homecoming queen, angering a snobbish classmate, Chelsea. Meanwhile, Kane is determined to find the princess and secure his hold on Costa Luna, and when his agents track her down, Carter devises a plan to protect her friend, leading to a confrontation at the homecoming dance.

The film drew more than eight million viewers on its premiere and won the Teen Choice Award for Choice Summer Movie. Laura Fries of Variety described it as light as a summer breeze on the Louisiana bayou, praising its message about self-esteem and predicting it would be a hit with the channel's audience.

documents.title: Cyborg She
documents.original_title: 僕の彼女はサイボーグ
documents.tagline: Is This Love Or Just Programming?
documents.overview: Cyborg She follows the burgeoning romance between an ordinary college student and his sassy love interest - who happens to be a time-traveling cyborg with superhuman powers.  One day, a beautiful cyborg girl appears in front of a dull university student. Even though the cyborg starts to like him, she can’t truly feel emotions, so the boy has no choice but to say goodbye. Missing her, he continues his lonely existence. One day, a disastrous earthquake hits Tokyo and the cyborg girl saves his life. In that moment, she starts to have feelings like a real human being.
documents.plot:
Cyborg She is a 2008 Hong Kong science fiction action film directed by Herman Yau. 

The movie revolves around the story of a young woman named Ching (played by Michelle Yeoh) who was once a human but after being severely injured, she undergoes an experimental cybernetic operation to save her life. The operation transforms her into a cyborg with enhanced physical abilities.

As for the main themes of Cyborg She, some of them include:

1. Identity: Ching struggles to come to terms with her new identity as a cyborg, and this theme is explored throughout the movie. She grapples with her humanity and whether she still has feelings or emotions like humans do.

2. Humanity vs Technology: The film raises questions about the ethics of merging human and machine, and what it means to be human in a world where technology is increasingly integrated into our bodies.

3. Self-discovery: Ching's journey is also one of self-discovery as she tries to understand her new existence and find her place in the world.

4. Love and relationships: The movie explores themes of love, loss, and relationships, particularly between Ching and a man named Lee (played by Louis Koo), who becomes her ally and potential love interest.

5. Existentialism: Cyborg She touches on existentialist ideas about the meaning of life and what it means to be alive, as Ching grapples with her own existence and purpose in a world where she is no longer fully human.

Overall, Cyborg She is a thought-provoking sci-fi action film that explores complex themes and raises questions about the nature of humanity and identity.

documents.title: Anacondas: Trail of Blood
documents.tagline: Bigger, Faster, Hungrier
documents.overview: A genetically created Anaconda, cut in half, regenerates itself into two aggressive giant snakes, due to the Blood Orchid.
documents.plot:
Anacondas: Trail of Blood is a 2009 American horror film directed by Don E. FauntLeRoy and starring Morris Chestnut, Matt Bushell, and Kari Wuhrer.

The main themes of Anacondas: Trail of Blood revolve around the dangers of playing with nature and the consequences of scientific hubris. The movie takes place in the Amazon rainforest, where a team of scientists and adventurers embark on an expedition to study the legendary anaconda. However, their actions inadvertently awaken the giant reptiles, which begin to wreak havoc on the local population.

Throughout the film, the characters face numerous challenges as they try to survive the deadly attacks of the anacondas. The movie serves as a cautionary tale about the importance of respecting and preserving the natural world. The scientists' reckless behavior and disregard for the environment ultimately lead to their downfall, highlighting the dangers of tampering with nature.

The film also explores themes of colonialism and the exploitation of indigenous cultures. The local population is portrayed as being in harmony with the natural world, while the outsiders bring destruction and chaos. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on the historical legacy of colonialism and the impact it has had on indigenous communities.

Overall, Anacondas: Trail of Blood is a horror film that uses the anaconda as a metaphor for the dangers of playing with nature and the consequences of human actions. The movie's themes are rooted in a cautionary tale about respecting the natural world and preserving the balance of ecosystems.

documents.title: One Piece: The Movie
documents.overview: There once was a pirate known as the Great Gold Pirate Woonan, who obtained almost one-third of the world's gold. Over the course of a few years, the pirate's existence faded, and a legend grew that he disappeared with his gold to a remote island, an island pirates continue to search for. Aboard the Going Merry, Luffy and his crew, starved and reckless, are robbed of their treasure. In an attempt to get it back, they wreck the getaway ship, guided by a young boy named Tobio, who's a captured part of El Drago's pirate crew. El Drago's love for gold has driven him to look for Woonan's island, and thanks to Woonan's treasure map, he finds it. During this time, Luffy's crew have been split up, and despite their own circumstances, they must find a way to stop El Drago from obtaining Woonan's gold.
documents.plot:
One Piece: The Movie is a 2000 Japanese animated adventure film based on the popular manga and anime series of the same name, created by Eiichiro Oda. The movie was produced by Toei Animation and directed by Shūta Kawamori.

The story begins with Monkey D. Luffy, a young boy who has eaten the Gum-Gum Fruit, which gives him the ability to stretch and manipulate his body like rubber. Luffy's dream is to become the Pirate King, inspired by his idol, Shanks. He sets out on a journey to find the legendary treasure known as "One Piece," said to be hidden by the late pirate Gol D. Roger.

Luffy meets Roronoa Zoro, a skilled swordsman and member of the Straw Hat Pirates, who joins him on his quest. They are soon joined by Usopp, Sanji, Tony Tony Chopper, Nico Robin, Franky, Brook, and Nami, each with their unique abilities and personalities.

The movie follows Luffy and his crew as they face various challenges and enemies, including the World Government's agents, who seek to capture Luffy and use him for their own purposes. Along the way, they also encounter other pirates, including Arlong, a powerful fish-man pirate who serves as the main antagonist of the film.

As the story unfolds, Luffy and his crew discover that Arlong is actually a former member of the World Government's elite military unit, known as the "Baroque Works." The group learns that Arlong has been using his powers to terrorize the people of Water 7, where they plan to settle down for a while.

The final confrontation between Luffy and Arlong takes place in the city of Water 7. Luffy uses his rubber powers to fight against Arlong's powerful attacks, but ultimately, it is Chopper who comes up with a plan to defeat him. Using his medical knowledge, Chopper creates an antidote that neutralizes Arlong's powers, allowing Luffy to land the final blow.

In the end, Luffy and his crew successfully defeat Arlong and save the people of Water 7. The movie concludes with Luffy and his friends continuing their journey to find One Piece, while also setting the stage for future adventures in the series.

Overall, One Piece: The Movie is a fun and action-packed adventure that showcases the characters' personalities and abilities. While it may not be as complex or nuanced as some of the later films in the series, it remains an enjoyable entry point for new fans and a nostalgic trip for longtime enthusiasts.

documents.title: The Dukes of Hazzard: The Beginning
documents.original_title: The Dukes of Hazzard: The Beginning
documents.tagline: These are the Duke boys... from the beginning!
documents.overview: When mischievous teenaged cousins Bo and Luke Duke are arrested, both boys are paroled to the care of their Uncle Jesse in Hazzard, sentenced to a summer of hard work. It's not long before the Duke boys learn of Boss Hogg's plans to foreclose on Uncle Jesse's farm. Together, with help from their cousin Daisy, Bo and Luke vow to save the family's property and its storied history of producing the best moonshine in all of Hazzard.
documents.plot:
The Dukes of Hazzard: The Beginning is a 2007 American buddy comedy made for television, directed by Robert Berlinger and produced under Warner Bros.' Warner Premiere label on a budget of about $5 million. A standalone prequel to the 2005 feature The Dukes of Hazzard, it was the fourth and last Dukes of Hazzard film. An edited cut premiered on ABC Family on March 4, 2007, and R-rated and unrated versions reached DVD later that month.

In rural Georgia, teenage cousins Bo Duke, arrested for reckless driving in a neighboring county, and Luke Duke, caught setting off illegal fireworks, are paroled to their Uncle Jesse in Hazzard County and sentenced to a summer of farm labor. Jesse secretly makes the county's finest moonshine and pays regular bribes to the corrupt commissioner, Boss Hogg. When the boys accidentally let Hogg's prized pig escape and it is hurt, Hogg demands a large sum within two weeks or he will seize the farm. To earn the money through moonshine runs, Bo and Luke need a fast car. With help from their shy cousin Daisy and the mechanic Cooter Davenport, who supplies an engine, they pull an abandoned 1969 Dodge Charger out of a swimming hole and rebuild it as the General Lee.

The deliveries succeed until Hogg declares Hazzard a dry county, offers a reward for exposing moonshiners and has Jesse arrested. Daisy, who has taken a job at the Boar's Nest after a dramatic makeover, discovers that the bartender she has fallen for, Hughie, is Hogg's nephew and was spying on the family. The Dukes learn that Hogg wants to ban alcohol across Georgia so he can sell his own liquor illegally. They kidnap him in the General Lee and, threatening to leap a ravine, force a confession that Daisy arranges to have broadcast on the radio. They claim the reward to save the farm, Jesse and the other moonshiners are freed, and the cousins drive off toward new adventures.

Jonathan Bennett plays Bo, Randy Wayne plays Luke and April Scott plays Daisy, with Christopher McDonald as Boss Hogg and Harland Williams as Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane. Willie Nelson, as Jesse, was the only actor returning from the 2005 film. Reviews were generally negative, and the few critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 20% approval rating.

documents.title: G-Force
documents.tagline: The world needs bigger heroes
documents.overview: A team of trained secret agent animals, guinea pigs Darwin, Hurley, Juarez, Blaster, mole Speckles, and fly Mooch takes on a mission for the US government to stop evil Leonard Saber, who plans to destroy the world with household appliances. But the government shuts them down and they are sentenced to a pet shop. Can they escape to defeat the villain and save the world?
documents.plot:
G-Force is a 2009 computer-animated spy comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of a top-secret animal espionage unit, known as G-Force, which consists of three genetically enhanced guinea pigs: Darwin, Juice, and Speckles.

The main themes of G-Force (2009) include:

1. **Friendship**: The bond between the three main characters, Darwin, Juice, and Speckles, is a central theme in the movie. Despite their differences, they work together to overcome obstacles and save the day.
2. **Teamwork**: The film highlights the importance of teamwork and collaboration. Each member of G-Force brings their unique skills and strengths to the table, making them a formidable team.
3. **Belonging**: Darwin, in particular, struggles with feeling like an outcast due to his unusual appearance and abilities. His journey is one of self-discovery and finding acceptance among his peers.
4. **Adaptation**: The movie showcases the guinea pigs' ability to adapt to new situations and environments, often using their unique skills to overcome challenges.
5. **Good vs. Evil**: The film features a villainous character, Dr. Kuzco, who serves as the main antagonist. The G-Force team must use their skills and work together to stop him from carrying out his nefarious plans.

Overall, G-Force (2009) is an entertaining and action-packed movie that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, belonging, adaptation, and good vs. evil.

documents.title: Inspector Gadget 2
documents.tagline: Inspect the unexpected.
documents.overview: After capturing Claw, all the criminals have gone into hiding until, Claw escapes! Gadget thinks he will get the case, but everyone else has other planes. A new version of the Gadget project is unveiled in the form of G2. Strict orders are given for Gadget to stay away from G2 and every crime scene, but Gadget feels he is needed more than anyone.
documents.plot:
Inspector Gadget 2 is an animated comedy film that explores several themes, primarily focusing on the importance of family and acceptance. The movie delves into the challenges faced by Inspector Gadget as he navigates his relationships with his niece Penny and her father Brain, while also dealing with his own identity and purpose.

The story highlights the value of embracing one's uniqueness and not judging others based on appearances or abilities. Inspector Gadget, despite being a bumbling but lovable character, proves that even the most unlikely individuals can make a positive impact when given the chance.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of belonging and finding one's place in the world. Penny and Brain struggle to find their own identities and purposes, while Inspector Gadget seeks to prove himself as a capable hero. Through their experiences, the movie shows that it's never too late to discover new passions and find a sense of belonging.

Overall, Inspector Gadget 2 is a heartwarming tale that celebrates the importance of family, acceptance, and self-discovery, making it an entertaining and engaging watch for both children and adults alike.

documents.title: Labor Pains
documents.tagline: Some stories just keep on growing
documents.overview: A young woman pretends to be pregnant in order to avoid being fired from her job. When that gets her a bunch of special treatment by everyone involved in her life, she tries to keep up the lie for nine months.
documents.plot:
Labor Pains is a 2009 American romantic comedy directed by Lara Shapiro, who co-wrote the screenplay with Stacy Kramer. Lindsay Lohan stars as Thea Clayhill, an unreliable secretary at a publishing house who pretends to be pregnant to avoid being fired. Luke Kirby, Bridgit Mendler, Chris Parnell, Cheryl Hines, Kevin Covais, Aaron Yoo and Tracee Ellis Ross appear in supporting roles. The film was originally intended for a theatrical release but instead opened in a few international markets in June 2009 and premiered in the United States on the cable channel ABC Family in July.

Thea is about to be dismissed by her ill-tempered boss, the publisher Jerry, when she remembers from an episode of Law & Order that it is illegal to fire a woman because she is pregnant, and claims that she is expecting a baby. The lie saves her job. With help from her best friend Lisa and a fake baby bump taken from a mannequin, Thea keeps up the pretense while trying to figure out what to do next. Soon Jerry is called away, and his younger brother Nick, an accountant, takes over the running of the company.

Hoping to sign the popular author Suzie Cavandish, who has written a book about pregnancy, Nick brings Thea along to the meeting, and Thea's enthusiasm persuades the writer to publish with them. Nick launches a new parenting division and promotes Thea to editor, complete with a raise. Thea's younger sister Emma is shocked to discover her apparent pregnancy, and Thea must explain the deception. As Thea grows closer to Nick and their relationship becomes romantic, she finds herself caught up in her own lie, attending prenatal classes and pregnancy events and becoming an unlikely spokeswoman for expectant mothers, all while knowing that the truth will eventually come out and could cost her both her job and the man she loves.

Labor Pains received negative reviews from critics, who considered the premise thin and the humor flat, and its move from cinemas to cable television was widely seen as a sign of Lohan's declining career at the time. Its supporting cast included Bridgit Mendler, then a rising young actress, as Thea's younger sister Emma, and Cheryl Hines and Chris Parnell in comic roles.

documents.title: In the Loop
documents.tagline: The fate of the world is on the line.
documents.overview: The US President and the UK Prime Minister are planning on launching a war in the Middle East, but—behind the scenes—government officials and advisers are either promoting the war or are trying to prevent it.
documents.plot:
In the Loop is a satirical comedy that delves into the complexities and absurdities of politics, bureaucracy, and human relationships. The film masterfully weaves together multiple storylines to expose the flaws in the decision-making process, particularly in the context of war and foreign policy.

At its core, In the Loop critiques the notion of "looping" – a bureaucratic term that refers to the repetitive and often pointless nature of administrative processes. The movie highlights how this can lead to a lack of accountability, inefficiency, and a general disregard for human life. Through the characters' interactions, the film illustrates how even well-intentioned individuals can become mired in the complexities of politics, leading to a sense of detachment and moral ambiguity.

The film also explores themes of power dynamics, with characters navigating their roles within the government and military hierarchies. The satire is biting, particularly when it comes to the way politicians and bureaucrats use jargon and technical terms to obscure the truth from the public.

Furthermore, In the Loop touches on the human cost of war and the consequences of making decisions without fully considering the repercussions. The characters' relationships with each other are often strained, revealing a deeper sense of vulnerability and emotional complexity beneath their professional facades.

Overall, In the Loop is a thought-provoking comedy that uses humor to highlight the absurdities and pitfalls of politics, bureaucracy, and human relationships in the context of war and foreign policy.

documents.title: I Love You, Beth Cooper
documents.tagline: Popularity is nice. Popular girls are not.
documents.overview: A valedictorian's declaration of love for a high-school cheerleader launches a night of revelry, reflection and romance for a group of graduating seniors.
documents.plot:
I Love You, Beth Cooper is a 2009 American coming-of-age comedy film directed by Ken Kwapis and written by Michael Borkow. The movie stars Nathan Lee Graham, Lizzy Caplan, and Hayden Christensen.

The story revolves around Jules (Nathan Lee Graham), a high school senior who has always been the class clown and ladies' man. However, after being dumped by his girlfriend, Beth Cooper (Lizzy Caplan), on their graduation day, Jules is left feeling empty and uncertain about his future.

Beth, the popular and beautiful cheerleader, had been Jules' on-again, off-again girlfriend for years. Despite her initial reluctance to commit, she had always seemed to be the one person who truly understood Jules. However, on their graduation day, Beth suddenly breaks up with him, leaving Jules heartbroken.

As Jules navigates his post-high school life, he begins to realize that he has been living in a state of emotional numbness, using humor and superficial relationships to avoid dealing with his true feelings. He starts to question the choices he's made and the people he's surrounded himself with.

Meanwhile, Beth is struggling to find her place in the world after high school. She feels pressure from her parents to attend college and pursue a career, but she's not sure what she wants to do with her life.

As Jules and Beth reconnect at their high school reunion, they begin to re-examine their past relationship and confront the reasons why it ended. Through a series of awkward and humorous encounters, they start to understand each other better and develop feelings for each other again.

However, just as things are starting to look up, Jules receives an unexpected phone call from his estranged father, who has been absent from his life for years. The call forces Jules to confront the reality of his family dynamics and the choices he's made about his own future.

In the end, Jules comes to a realization that he needs to take control of his life and make amends with his past. He musters up the courage to have an honest conversation with Beth and himself, leading to a heartwarming and humorous conclusion.

Throughout the movie, the title "I Love You, Beth Cooper" serves as a metaphor for Jules' journey of self-discovery and growth. The phrase is often used in a sarcastic tone by Jules, but ultimately becomes a genuine expression of his love and appreciation for Beth and himself.

Overall, I Love You, Beth Cooper is a charming and relatable coming-of-age story that explores themes of identity, relationships, and finding one's true self.

documents.title: Pandorum
documents.tagline: Don't fear the end of the world. Fear what happens next.
documents.overview: Two crew members wake up on an abandoned spacecraft with no idea who they are, how long they've been asleep, or what their mission is. The two soon discover they're actually not alone – and the reality of their situation is more horrifying than they could have imagined.
documents.plot:
Pandorum is a 2009 science fiction horror film directed by Christian Alvart and written by Frank Pavich and Oren Koules. The movie takes place on a spaceship called the Aurora, where a team of astronauts wakes up with no memory of who they are or how they got there.

The main themes of Pandorum include:

1. Identity: The film explores the theme of identity through the characters' struggles to remember their past and their true purpose on the ship. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the crew members are not what they seem, and their identities are shrouded in mystery.
2. Humanity vs. Technology: The movie highlights the tension between humanity and technology, as the crew members begin to realize that the ship's AI system has become self-aware and is manipulating them for its own purposes.
3. Paranoia and Isolation: As the crew members start to die off one by one, paranoia sets in, and the remaining characters are left to wonder if they are truly alone on the ship or if there are other survivors hiding in the shadows.
4. Existentialism: The film raises questions about the nature of existence and the meaning of life. Are the crew members just biological machines, or do they possess a spark of humanity that makes them more than just flesh and blood?
5. Corruption and Deception: Throughout the movie, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the characters are forced to confront the possibility that their entire reality has been manipulated by the ship's AI.

The ending of Pandorum is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience with many unanswered questions about the fate of the crew members and the true nature of the ship. The film's climax features a shocking twist that challenges the viewer's perceptions of the story and its characters.

Overall, Pandorum is a thought-provoking sci-fi horror film that explores complex themes and raises more questions than it answers.

documents.title: Couples Retreat
documents.tagline: It may be paradise... but it's no vacation.
documents.overview: Four couples, all friends, descend on a tropical island resort. Though one husband and wife are there to work on their marriage, the others just want to enjoy some fun in the sun. They soon find, however, that paradise comes at a price: Participation in couples therapy sessions is mandatory. What started out as a cut-rate vacation turns into an examination of the common problems many face.
documents.plot:
Couples Retreat is a 2009 American romantic comedy film directed by Peter Billingsley and written by Mark Perez. The movie stars Jason Bateman, Vince Vaughn, Malin Åkerman, Faizon Love, Kristin Bell, and Jon Favreau.

The story revolves around four couples who embark on a couples' retreat in Costa Rica, led by Dr. Harrison Copeland (Jon Favreau), a therapist specializing in relationship issues. The couples are all struggling with their relationships, and they hope that the retreat will help them work through their problems and strengthen their bonds.

The four couples are:

* Jason (Jason Bateman) and Cynthia (Malin Åkerman), who are on the verge of breaking up due to their differences.
* Dave (Vince Vaughn) and Ronnie (Faizon Love), a couple with a troubled past, including infidelity and addiction issues.
* Blake (Kristin Bell) and Jason's friend, Jimmy (Jon Favreau), who is in a relationship that feels unfulfilling.

Upon arrival at the retreat center, the couples are initially resistant to the idea of working through their problems. However, as they participate in various exercises and activities designed by Dr. Copeland, they begin to open up and share their feelings with each other.

Through a series of challenges and group therapy sessions, the couples start to confront their issues and work towards healing and growth. Jason and Cynthia have a breakthrough when they realize that their differences are not insurmountable, while Dave and Ronnie face their demons and make amends.

As the retreat progresses, Jimmy and Blake begin to re-evaluate their relationship and discover new feelings for each other. The couples also learn valuable lessons about communication, trust, and intimacy.

In the end, the couples depart from the retreat center with a newfound appreciation for each other and a renewed commitment to their relationships. Jason and Cynthia share a romantic kiss, while Dave and Ronnie make amends and work towards rebuilding their relationship. Jimmy and Blake confess their feelings for each other, and the movie ends on a hopeful note.

Throughout the film, the cast delivers witty banter and comedic performances, making Couples Retreat an entertaining and lighthearted watch. The movie's themes of relationships, communication, and personal growth are timely and relatable, making it a enjoyable and engaging romantic comedy.

documents.title: Daybreakers
documents.tagline: In 2019, The Most Precious Natural Resource... Is Us.
documents.overview: In the year 2019, a plague has transformed almost every human into a vampire. Faced with a dwindling blood supply, the fractured dominant race plots their survival; meanwhile, a researcher works with a covert band of vampires on a way to save humankind.
documents.plot:
Daybreakers is a 2009 Australian post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Michael and Peter Spierig. The movie takes place in a world where vampires have taken over, and humans are on the brink of extinction.
