The main themes of Daybreakers include:

1. **Existentialism**: The film explores the idea that human existence is fragile and can be extinguished at any moment. The vampire apocalypse serves as a metaphor for the fragility of life and the inevitability of death.
2. **Addiction and Dependence**: The movie highlights the dangers of addiction and dependence on blood, which becomes an all-consuming force in the lives of the vampires. This theme is reflected in the character of Edward Dalton (Ewan McGregor), who struggles with his own addiction to blood.
3. **Humanity and Empathy**: As the world descends into chaos, the film raises questions about what it means to be human. The characters are forced to confront their own humanity and empathy in the face of unimaginable horror.
4. **Science vs. Nature**: Daybreakers explores the tension between scientific progress and the natural order of things. The vampires represent a force that is beyond human control, highlighting the limitations of science in understanding and combating nature.
5. **Redemption and Sacrifice**: Throughout the film, Edward Dalton grapples with his own morality and seeks redemption for past mistakes. His journey serves as a commentary on the importance of sacrifice and personal responsibility.

The movie's themes are woven throughout its narrative, which follows Edward Dalton (Ewan McGregor) as he navigates a world where vampires have taken over. The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Edward and the vampire leader, who represents the ultimate force of nature.

Overall, Daybreakers is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its unique blend of horror and science fiction elements.

documents.title: The Stepfather
documents.tagline: Daddy's home
documents.overview: Michael Harding returns home from military school to find his mother happily in love and living with her new boyfriend, David. As the two men get to know each other, Michael becomes more and more suspicious of the man who is always there with a helpful hand. Is he really the man of her dreams or could David be hiding a dark side?
documents.plot:
The Stepfather is a 2009 American psychological horror film directed by Nelson McCormick. It remakes the 1987 film of the same name, which was loosely inspired by the crimes of mass murderer John List, and is the fourth film in the series. Dylan Walsh plays the title character, with Sela Ward as Susan Harding, Penn Badgley as her son Michael, Amber Heard as Michael's girlfriend Kelly and Jon Tenney as Susan's ex-husband Jay.

In a Utah suburb, a man named Grady Edwards shaves his beard, dyes his hair and removes colored contact lenses before leaving behind the bodies of his wife and three children. Police link the murders to a similar massacre in New Jersey. In Oregon, recently divorced mother Susan Harding meets a charming widower who calls himself David Harris, and they rush into an engagement. Her eldest son, Michael, returns from military school and becomes suspicious, especially when David gets the name of his late daughter wrong and keeps the basement cabinets locked.

David kills anyone who threatens his new identity. A neighbor who saw a TV profile of a serial killer resembling him is pushed down her basement stairs and smothered. He quits his job with Susan's sister Jackie rather than show identification. When Jay questions his past, David kills him with a vase and a plastic bag and then uses Jay's phone to text Michael that everything checks out. When Jackie plans to hire an investigator, he drowns her in her pool. Ignoring Kelly's attempts to distract him with college plans, Michael breaks into the basement and finds his father's body in a freezer before David knocks Kelly out and locks him in. David's identity begins to crack in front of Susan, and he asks, "Who am I here?" She flees to the bathroom and stabs him in the neck with a shard of mirror. He gets up again and chases the family into the attic. He and Michael fall from the roof. Michael wakes from a month-long coma to learn that David escaped. In the final scene, under the new name Chris Ames, he meets a woman shopping with her two sons at a hardware store.

Terry O'Quinn, star of the original, reportedly declined a cameo. Filming ended in April 2008, and Sony Pictures released the film on October 16, 2009. It opened fifth with $11.6 million and grossed $31.2 million against a $20 million budget. Critics were largely negative, and Rotten Tomatoes called it a tepid remake that lacks the original's tension and satire, though the Los Angeles Times praised its craft and performances.

documents.title: The Goods: Live Hard, Sell Hard
documents.original_title: The Goods: Live Hard, Sell Hard
documents.overview: Don Ready is many things, but he is best-known as an extraordinary salesman. When a car dealership in Temecula teeters on the brink of bankruptcy, he and his ragtag team dive in to save the day. But what Ready doesn't count on is falling in love and finding his soul.
documents.plot:
The Goods: Live Hard, Sell Hard is a comedy film that explores the theme of redemption and personal growth through its protagonist, Mike Flaherty, played by Jeremy Piven. On the surface, the movie appears to be a satirical take on the world of telemarketing, but upon closer inspection, it reveals itself to be a nuanced commentary on the human condition.

At its core, The Goods is a story about finding one's purpose and making amends for past mistakes. Mike Flaherty, a former car salesman who has lost his way in life, is given a second chance when he lands a job at a telemarketing firm. As he navigates the cutthroat world of sales, he must confront his own demons and learn to connect with others on a deeper level.

The film also explores the theme of identity and how it can be shaped by our experiences and relationships. Mike's character is a complex one, full of contradictions and flaws, but as the story unfolds, we see him slowly transform into a more confident and empathetic person. This transformation is not just about personal growth, but also about finding a sense of belonging and purpose.

Furthermore, The Goods critiques the societal pressures that drive people to conform to certain expectations or roles. Mike's character is initially defined by his job as a car salesman, but as he navigates the telemarketing world, he begins to question the values and morals of this profession. This internal conflict serves as a commentary on the ways in which we are often forced to choose between our true selves and the expectations placed upon us by society.

Overall, The Goods: Live Hard, Sell Hard is a thought-provoking comedy that explores themes of redemption, personal growth, identity, and societal pressure.

documents.title: The Final Destination
documents.tagline: Rest In Pieces.
documents.overview: After a young man's premonition of a deadly race-car crash helps saves the lives of his peers, Death sets out to collect those who evaded their end.
documents.plot:
The Final Destination is a supernatural horror film directed by James Wong, released in 2009 by New Line Cinema.

The movie begins with four high school friends - Nick O'Bannon (Shawn Ashmore), Chase Sanford (Mykelti Williamson), Justin Conner (Jon Abrahams), and Peter Fountaine (Emile Hirsch) - who are all seated together on a plane that is taking off from New York to Los Angeles. As the plane reaches cruising altitude, Nick has a premonition of a catastrophic event occurring at the end of the flight.

Despite his friends' skepticism, Nick convinces them to disembark the plane and take a different flight, which they do. However, unbeknownst to them, their decision is actually a result of Nick's premonition, and the original flight has indeed crashed into a school bus carrying students on their way home from a field trip.

The group soon discovers that whenever someone dies in a specific sequence of events, death follows them. They start to experience a series of bizarre and gruesome deaths, which seem to be connected to their own premonitions. As the bodies pile up, they realize that Nick's initial warning was actually a warning from the future, trying to prevent them from dying.

The group tries to figure out who will die next and how to avoid it, but each time they think they've found a way to escape death, another member of their group meets an untimely demise. The deaths become increasingly gruesome and violent, with the victims being killed in creative and terrifying ways.

As the body count rises, Nick becomes more and more convinced that he is the only one who can prevent the deaths from occurring. He tries to find a way to change the course of events, but it seems like fate has other plans for him and his friends.

In the end, it's revealed that the group's deaths were all connected to their own premonitions, which were actually messages from the future trying to warn them of their impending doom. The movie ends with Nick being the only survivor, who is left to ponder the meaning of his premonition and whether he was able to change the course of events.

Throughout the movie, there are several twists and turns that keep the audience guessing, as well as some clever plot reveals that add to the tension and suspense. The Final Destination is a classic horror film that relies on its clever plot and gruesome deaths to create a thrilling and terrifying experience for viewers.

documents.title: (500) Days of Summer
documents.tagline: This is not a love story. This is a story about love.
documents.overview: Tom, greeting-card writer and hopeless romantic, is caught completely off-guard when his girlfriend, Summer, suddenly dumps him. He reflects on their 500 days together to try to figure out where their love affair went sour, and in doing so, Tom rediscovers his true passions in life.
documents.plot:
(500) Days of Summer is a 2009 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Marc Webb and written by Scott Neustadter and Michael H. Weber. The film stars Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Tom Hansen, a cartoonist who falls in love with Summer Finn (Zooey Deschanel), a free-spirited woman he meets at work.

The film begins on Valentine's Day, where we meet Tom, who is struggling to find meaning and connection in his life. He works at a greeting card company, designing cards for other people's relationships, but feels unfulfilled himself. One day, Summer walks into the office where Tom works, and he becomes immediately smitten with her quirky charm and beauty.

As Tom and Summer start dating, they embark on a whirlwind romance that takes them to various locations around Los Angeles. However, their relationship is marked by Summer's unpredictability and lack of commitment. She has a tendency to break up with Tom suddenly, only to get back together again, leaving him feeling confused and uncertain.

Despite the ups and downs, Tom finds himself falling deeper in love with Summer, and he becomes increasingly invested in their relationship. He writes her 500 letters, each one detailing his feelings and hopes for their future together. However, Summer's behavior continues to be erratic, and she eventually breaks up with Tom, citing that she never wanted to be in a relationship.

Heartbroken, Tom sets out to understand why Summer ended things between them. He discovers that Summer had been using him as a way to cope with her own emotional baggage, and he realizes that he was the one who was truly invested in their relationship. The film's narrative is presented non-linearly, jumping back and forth between different points in Tom and Summer's relationship.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Tom and Summer's time together, as well as present-day scenes where Tom is struggling to move on from their breakup. Through a series of vignettes and voiceovers, Tom reflects on his experiences with Summer, and he comes to realize that he was in love with her, but she was never truly in love with him.

The film's ending is bittersweet, as Tom finally understands the nature of his relationship with Summer. He realizes that he deserves better than someone who doesn't reciprocate his feelings, and he begins to heal and move on from their breakup. The final shot of the film shows Tom sitting alone in a park, surrounded by the 500 letters he wrote to Summer, as he finally finds closure and acceptance.

Overall, (500) Days of Summer is a poignant and offbeat romantic comedy that explores the complexities of love and relationships. With its unique narrative structure and memorable performances from Joseph Gordon-Levitt and Zooey Deschanel, the film has become a cult classic among rom-com fans.

documents.title: Spread
documents.tagline: It's a business doing pleasure.
documents.overview: In Los Angeles, Nikki is homeless, car-less and closing in on 30, but he's amoral, good-looking, and adept in the sack, moving from one wealthy woman of 35 or 40 to another, a kept boy-toy. His newest gig, with Samantha, an attorney whose house overlooks L.A., is sweet, although it's unclear how long she'll put up with him. Then Nikki meets Heather, a waitress. Is the player being played, or might this be love? What will Nikki discover?
documents.plot:
Spread is a 2009 American comedy film directed by James Washington and written by James Washington and David Gordon Green. The movie stars Ashton Kutcher, Margarita Levieva, and Natasha Lyonne.

The story revolves around Nick (Ashton Kutcher), a young man who has just been dumped by his girlfriend, Amanda (Margarita Levieva). Feeling down and lonely, Nick decides to attend a singles party in Los Angeles. At the party, he meets a beautiful woman named Samantha (Natalie Portman) at a bar, but she leaves before they can talk.

The next day, Nick wakes up with a mysterious tattoo on his backside, which reads "Samantha". He soon discovers that he has been tattooed by Samantha after a wild night together. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Nick and Samantha had an intense and passionate encounter, but their relationship is complicated.

Nick's life begins to spiral out of control as he tries to navigate his feelings for Samantha. He starts to experience strange and unexplained events, including finding himself in various locations around Los Angeles with no memory of how he got there. The tattoo on his backside becomes a recurring motif throughout the film, symbolizing Nick's connection to Samantha.

As Nick delves deeper into his relationship with Samantha, he discovers that she is a free-spirited artist who lives life on her own terms. He begins to question his own identity and sense of purpose, feeling like he is stuck in a rut. Through a series of misadventures and encounters with various characters, including a eccentric tattoo artist (Christopher Walken), Nick slowly starts to come to terms with his feelings for Samantha.

Throughout the film, the tone shifts between humor and drama, as Nick navigates the ups and downs of his relationship with Samantha. The movie features a mix of witty dialogue, quirky characters, and offbeat humor, which adds to its charm.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Nick and Samantha, as they both try to make sense of their complicated feelings for each other. In the end, Nick comes to realize that he has been given a second chance with Samantha, and he must decide whether to take it or let her go.

Overall, Spread is a quirky and offbeat romantic comedy that explores themes of identity, relationships, and self-discovery. With its unique blend of humor and drama, the film offers a fresh take on the traditional rom-com genre.

documents.title: Surrogates
documents.tagline: How do you save humanity when the only thing that's real is you?
documents.overview: Set in a futuristic world where humans live in isolation and interact through surrogate robots, a cop is forced to leave his home for the first time in years in order to investigate the murders of others' surrogates.
documents.plot:
Surrogates is a 2009 science fiction action film directed by Jonathan Mostow and starring Bruce Willis, Radha Mitchell, and Rosamund Pike.

The main themes of Surrogates can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Convenience vs. Humanity**: The movie explores the idea of a society where people use surrogates, or robotic duplicates, to control their lives. On one hand, this technology provides convenience, efficiency, and a sense of security. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that this reliance on surrogates comes at the cost of genuine human connections and emotions.

2. **Free Will vs. Control**: The film raises questions about the nature of free will and control in a world where people can manipulate their surrogates to do their bidding. As the protagonist, Detective Greer (Bruce Willis), delves deeper into the mystery, he begins to realize that his own life is not as under his control as he thought.

3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The movie explores the theme of identity and self-discovery through the character of Greer, who must confront the possibility that his surrogate may be a copycat killer. As he navigates this complex web of identities, Greer is forced to re-examine his own sense of self and purpose.

4. **The Dangers of Unchecked Technological Advancement**: Surrogates serves as a cautionary tale about the potential risks of unchecked technological advancement. The film highlights the dangers of relying too heavily on technology to solve our problems, rather than addressing the underlying issues that drive human behavior.

5. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Ultimately, the movie suggests that true human connection and empathy are essential for a fulfilling life. As Greer forms connections with those around him, including his wife (Radha Mitchell) and a young girl named Verity (Pike), he begins to realize that these relationships are what truly make us human.

Overall, Surrogates is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human nature in a world where technology is increasingly integrated into our lives.

documents.title: The Exterminating Angels
documents.overview: A filmmaker holds a series of boundary-pushing auditions for his latest project: a thriller on the subject of female pleasure.
documents.plot:
The Exterminating Angels (French: Les Anges exterminateurs) is a 2006 French erotic drama written and directed by Jean-Claude Brisseau, with music by Jean Musy and cinematography by Wilfrid Sempé. Together with Secret Things (2002) and À l'aventure (2009), it forms a trilogy about female sexuality. The film is semi-autobiographical: in 2002 Brisseau was arrested and later convicted of harassing actresses who had performed sexual acts in front of him during auditions for Secret Things, and he based the film on his book of the same name, a fictionalized account of his working methods and his version of those events. Frédéric van den Driessche plays the filmmaker François, while the young actresses are played by Maroussia Dubreuil (Charlotte), Lise Bellynck (Julie) and Marie Allan (Stéphanie), with Raphaële Godin and Margaret Zenou as two apparitions, and Jeanne Cellard as François's grandmother.

In a dream, the ghost of François's grandmother warns him not to let his curiosity take control of him, while two black-clad fallen angels hover over him as he sleeps, conspiring to set events in motion. François plans a film about the moment when women transgress sexual taboos. Without a producer or casting director, he holds auditions himself, and after many candidates refuse, two young actresses show promise. In a restaurant he guides Charlotte through an improvisation in which she pleasures herself among the diners, joined by Julie, as the waitress Stéphanie looks on; the trio continues the experiment in a hotel. The next day Stéphanie comes to his office and asks to take part. François insists he is only gathering material for his script and remains a detached observer, but the encounters become increasingly intense. Charlotte grows obsessive, wrecking her apartment and calling him at all hours, and his wife warns him about her ego, while the women's rivalries and obsessions, apparently steered by the spirits, turn against him with tragic consequences.

The film premiered at the Cannes Film Festival on 20 May 2006 and opened in limited release in the United States through IFC First Take on 7 March 2007. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reports 49% positive reviews and Metacritic a score of 54. The Hollywood Reporter called it provocative and sexy but pretentious, redeemed by its glossy visual style and humor, while Film-Forward saw it as an unpersuasive mea culpa.

documents.title: Jennifer's Body
documents.tagline: She's evil... and not just high school evil.
documents.overview: Jennifer, a gorgeous, seductive cheerleader takes evil to a whole new level after she's possessed by a sinister demon. Now it's up to her best friend to stop Jennifer's reign of terror before it's too late.
documents.plot:
Jennifer's Body is a 2009 American horror-comedy film directed by Karyn Kusama and written by Diablo Cody. The movie stars Megan Fox, Amanda Seyfried, Adam Brody, and Jake Abel.

The story begins with Jennifer Check (Megan Fox), a popular high school student who is part of the "popular crowd" in the small town of Devil's Kettle, Minnesota. She is known for her beauty, charm, and popularity among her peers. However, Jennifer has a dark secret: she is a Satanist who makes a pact with the devil to become more beautiful and popular.

One night, Jennifer meets Anita (Amanda Seyfried), a new student in town who is an outcast due to her goth appearance and interests. Despite their initial differences, the two girls quickly form a bond, and Anita becomes Jennifer's confidant. However, things take a dark turn when Jennifer invites Anita to join her for a party at a local bar, where they are both brutally attacked by a group of men.

In the aftermath of the attack, Jennifer discovers that she has developed supernatural powers after being bitten by one of the attackers. She can now transform into a demon and possess others, using their bodies as vessels to carry out her evil deeds.

As Jennifer's powers grow stronger, she begins to use them to terrorize Anita and the rest of the town, turning her friends against each other and wreaking havoc on Devil's Kettle. Meanwhile, Anita becomes increasingly obsessed with stopping Jennifer and saving the town from her demonic wrath.

Anita teams up with Neil (Adam Brody), a local musician who is initially oblivious to Jennifer's true nature. As Anita delves deeper into Jennifer's past, she discovers that Jennifer's pact with the devil has made her a vessel for an ancient evil spirit.

In the climactic final act, Anita and Neil concoct a plan to stop Jennifer and break the curse that has taken over her body. They perform a ritual to exorcise the demon from Jennifer's body, but not before she unleashes a devastating attack on Anita.

In the end, Anita manages to defeat Jennifer by using a sacred artifact to banish the demon back to hell. However, in a shocking twist, it is revealed that Jennifer had become pregnant with Anita's child during her possession, leaving Anita to grapple with the moral implications of having killed an innocent being.

The movie ends with Anita reflecting on the events that transpired and the true cost of saving Devil's Kettle from Jennifer's demonic wrath. Despite its dark themes and graphic content, Jennifer's Body is a commentary on female friendship, peer pressure, and the dangers of toxic relationships.

documents.title: Avatar
documents.tagline: Enter the world of Pandora.
documents.overview: In the 22nd century, a paraplegic Marine is dispatched to the moon Pandora on a unique mission, but becomes torn between following orders and protecting an alien civilization.
documents.plot:
Avatar (2009) is a science fiction epic film directed by James Cameron, set in the mid-22nd century on the planet Pandora, inhabited by the Na'vi people. The story follows Jake Sully, a paraplegic marine who is recruited to participate in the Avatar Program, which allows humans to control genetically engineered Na'vi bodies called "avatars."

Jake's twin brother, also a marine, had previously participated in the program and was killed during a clash with the Na'vi. The program's goal is to convince the Na'vi to leave their homes so that a mining corporation can extract valuable minerals from Pandora.

Upon arrival on Pandora, Jake is fitted with an avatar body and begins his training as an avatar driver. He soon becomes immersed in Na'vi culture and forms a bond with Neytiri, a Na'vi warrior who teaches him about the natural world and the spiritual connection between humans and nature.

As Jake becomes more deeply involved with the Na'vi, he begins to question the true intentions of the human corporation and the motivations of his own brother's death. He also starts to experience strange visions and sensations that suggest a deeper connection to the natural world.

The conflict escalates when the human corporation threatens to destroy the Na'vi's sacred Tree of Souls, which is connected to their spiritual energy source. Jake must choose between his loyalty to humanity and his growing allegiance to the Na'vi people.

The film culminates in an epic battle between the humans and the Na'vi, with Jake ultimately siding with the Na'vi and helping them defeat the human forces. The movie ends with Jake permanently transferring his consciousness into his avatar body, allowing him to live among the Na'vi as one of their own.

Throughout the film, Cameron explores themes of colonialism, imperialism, and the clash between technology and nature. The film's stunning visuals and groundbreaking use of motion capture technology brought the world of Pandora to life in a way that was both breathtaking and thought-provoking.

Overall, Avatar is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of human actions on the natural world.

documents.title: The Prince & Me: A Royal Honeymoon
documents.original_title: The Prince & Me: A Royal Honeymoon
documents.overview: At last! The newly crowned King of Denmark, Edward, and his wife and Queen, Dr. Paige Morgan, find time to fly to Belavia for their secret honeymoon. What better way to spend the Christmas holidays than at a fabulous ski resort? But as they take a tour of Belavia's natural beauty, Eddie and Paige discover that the evil Prime Minister Polonius has given orders to bulldoze the precious forests - to drill for oil. Then, the couple bump into Paige's ex-boyfriend, Scott. Eddie immediately becomes jealous - furthermore he suspects Scott cannot be trusted. Paige and Eddie must do everything they can to save the forest, even if it means putting aside their honeymoon.
documents.plot:
The Prince & Me: A Royal Honeymoon is a romantic comedy film that explores the challenges and joys of royal life, love, and identity. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of self-discovery, as Princess Charlotte's journey from being a sheltered princess to becoming a confident individual is put to the test.

The film also touches on the idea of cultural differences and the importance of understanding and respecting each other's backgrounds. The contrast between Charlotte's traditional Danish upbringing and her American fiancé Prince Edward's more modern approach to royal life serves as a catalyst for growth and learning.

Furthermore, the movie examines the complexities of love and relationships, particularly in the context of royal duties and expectations. As Charlotte navigates her feelings for Prince Edward, she must also confront the pressures of royal protocol and the scrutiny that comes with being part of the royal family.

Ultimately, The Prince & Me: A Royal Honeymoon is a heartwarming tale about embracing one's true self, finding love, and learning to balance individuality with responsibility.

documents.title: Royal Space Force - The Wings Of Honneamise
documents.original_title: 王立宇宙軍 オネアミスの翼
documents.overview: On a future Earth, war between the Kingdom of Honneamise and its rival, The Republic, is inevitable. As evolving technology creates new ways to wage war, a small group seeks to propel mankind into space in their world’s first spaceflight program. For astronaut candidate Shirotsugh Lhadatt, it’s a personal odyssey as he grows from an aimless young man into a leader willing to put everything on the line in order to move the human race forward and away from the brink of Armageddon.
documents.plot:
Royal Space Force - The Wings Of Honneamise is a thought-provoking anime film that explores several profound themes, including existentialism, pacifism, and the human condition. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of war, peace, and the nature of humanity.

The story follows Claude, a young man who joins the Royal Space Force to fight against an alien threat, only to discover that the true enemy is not the aliens, but rather the militaristic society he lives in. As Claude navigates this moral quagmire, he begins to question the very fabric of his existence and the values he was taught.

One of the primary themes of Royal Space Force is the exploration of pacifism versus militarism. The film presents a nuanced portrayal of both sides, highlighting the devastating consequences of war and the importance of seeking peaceful solutions. Through Claude's journey, the movie encourages viewers to consider alternative perspectives and challenge their own assumptions about conflict resolution.

Existentialism also plays a significant role in Royal Space Force, as Claude grapples with the meaning of his life and the purpose of his actions. The film raises profound questions about the nature of humanity, encouraging viewers to reflect on their own values and motivations.

Ultimately, Royal Space Force is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of war, peace, and existence. Through its thought-provoking themes and nuanced characters, the movie offers a rich and rewarding viewing experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Confessions of a Shopaholic
documents.tagline: A new job? Hopefully. A new man? Possibly. A new handbag? Absolutely!
documents.overview: In the glamorous world of New York City, Rebecca Bloomwood is a fun-loving girl who is really good at shopping-a little too good, perhaps. She dreams of working for her favorite fashion magazine, but can't quite get her foot in the door-until ironically, she snags a job as an advice columnist for a financial magazine published by the same company.
documents.plot:
Confessions of a Shopaholic is a 2009 American romantic comedy directed by P. J. Hogan, based on the first two novels in Sophie Kinsella's Shopaholic series, The Secret Dreamworld of a Shopaholic and Shopaholic Abroad, known in the United States as Confessions of a Shopaholic and Shopaholic Takes Manhattan. The film recasts the English heroine as an American. It was shot in New York, Connecticut and Florida in 2008, with reshoots late that year to make the ending more sympathetic during the recession, and Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures released it on February 13, 2009.

Shopping addict Rebecca Bloomwood shares a New York apartment with her best friend, Suze, writes for a gardening magazine and dreams of working at the fashion magazine Alette. On her way to an interview there, her credit card is declined as she tries to buy a green scarf, and a stranger lends her $20. The Alette job has been filled, so she interviews instead at the financial magazine Successful Saving, whose editor, Luke Brandon, turns out to be the stranger. That night, drunk, she mails her letters to the two magazines in the wrong envelopes, and Luke, impressed by the one meant for Alette, hires her. Her column, published under the pen name "The Girl in the Green Scarf", becomes a hit.

As her success grows, so do her debts, and she dodges her debt collector, Derek Smeath, while Suze sends her to Shopaholics Anonymous. When Smeath confronts her during a television interview, Luke is humiliated and the magazine drops her column. Refusing her father's offer to sell his camper for her, Rebecca takes responsibility, turns down a job at Alette that would require lying to readers, and with help from her support group auctions her clothes to clear her debt, paying Smeath entirely in coins. She reconciles with Suze at her wedding, resists a shop window, and discovers that Luke, now running his own firm, had his agent buy her scarf. They kiss, and she joins his company as a columnist.

Isla Fisher plays Rebecca and Hugh Dancy plays Luke, with John Lithgow as Edgar West. Critics were largely negative, with 26% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though Fisher was widely praised, and Roger Ebert called her a joy. It grossed about $106.9 million worldwide.

documents.title: The Batman vs. Dracula
documents.tagline: There's another bat in Gotham...
documents.overview: Gotham City is terrorized not only by recent escapees Joker and Penguin, but by the original creature of the night, Dracula! Can Batman stop the ruthless vampire before he turns everyone in the city, including The Caped Crusader, Joker and Penguin, into his mindless minions?
documents.plot:
The Batman vs. Dracula is a 2005 American animated superhero horror film based on the television series The Batman and loosely inspired by Bram Stoker's Dracula and the Elseworlds comic Batman & Dracula: Red Rain. Rino Romano voices Batman and Peter Stormare Count Dracula, with Tara Strong, Alastair Duncan, Tom Kenny and Kevin Michael Richardson. It was released on DVD on October 18, 2005, and premiered on Cartoon Network's Toonami block four days later.

The Joker and the Penguin escape from Arkham Asylum in search of treasure hidden in a crypt at Gotham Cemetery. Batman intercepts the Joker, who appears to die in a river after being electrocuted by his own joy buzzer. The Penguin reaches the crypt, cuts his hand, and his blood drips onto a corpse, reviving Count Dracula, whose body had been secretly brought to Gotham. Dracula bites a passing guard instead and hypnotises the Penguin into serving as his daytime guardian.

As people begin vanishing across the city, the media label them the Lost Ones. At a party at Wayne Manor, Bruce Wayne meets a visiting anthropologist calling himself Dr. Alucard, who shows a keen interest in Bruce's girlfriend, the reporter Vicki Vale, and turns a waiter into a vampire. Bruce realises that Alucard is Dracula, turning the missing into vampires, and seeks a cure that will spare the victims. Witnesses' accounts of a bat-like figure lead the police to blame Batman. When Batman confronts Dracula and refuses an offer to join him, only the sunrise saves him.

The Joker, it turns out, survived, and after chasing the Penguin into the crypt he is himself bitten and turned. Batman captures him during a raid on a blood bank and uses his infected cells to develop an antidote, while Alfred discovers that Dracula once had a bride, Carmilla Karnstein, destroyed by sunlight. Dracula kidnaps Vicki, intending to use her soul to bring Carmilla back.

Armed with the mass-produced cure, Batman fights his way through the catacombs beneath the cemetery, restoring the Lost Ones to human form, and interrupts the ritual to free Vicki. He lures Dracula into the Batcave, where Alfred's injection of the vaccine fails, since it cannot cure a born vampire, and Batman finally destroys him with a solar energy device, reducing him to ashes. Freed from Dracula's control, the Penguin finds the treasure and is arrested, and Batman's name is cleared. Retrospective reviews have been mixed, though Stormare's Dracula was praised.

documents.title: Straight from the Barrio
documents.tagline: You can take the man out of the street... but you can't take the street out of the man.
documents.overview: A young drug dealer falls in love while facing disruption among the men in his gang, and being offered a career as a Reggaetón singer.
documents.plot:
Straight from the Barrio (Spanish: Talento de barrio) is a 2008 Puerto Rican crime drama directed by José Iván Santiago from a screenplay by George Rivera and Ángel M. Sanjurjo, and the first feature co-produced by the reggaeton star Daddy Yankee, who makes his screen acting debut in the lead. He plays Edgar "Dinero," a small-time gangster, with Katiria Soto as Soribel, Ángel "Maestro" Rodríguez as Jeico, César Farrait as Wichy, Angélica Alcaide as Natasha, Norma Colón as Edgar's mother and Eddie Dee as Jay. The story is loosely inspired by its star's own life.

Edgar, aptly nicknamed for his devotion to money, runs a drug operation in a housing project in Puerto Rico. His mother disapproves of his trade and refuses to leave the project for the comfortable middle-class house he has bought. Edgar has no musical ambitions of his own, but a record producer pushes him onto the stage of a seedy nightclub and secretly records his rapping, hoping to persuade him to change careers. At the same time he falls for Soribel, a well-off young woman from uptown, and must hide the depth of his feelings and the nature of his life from her.

Meanwhile, his crew begins to unravel. A vicious ex-convict, Jeico, destabilizes the gang from within and gets Edgar's younger sister hooked on drugs without Edgar noticing, while beatings and rivalries escalate into open conflict. A first recording session in New York goes badly because Edgar seems to lack energy, but when Soribel turns up there, his music becomes stronger and more passionate. As he tries to leave the street for the studio, violence follows him in both Puerto Rico and New York, and the film ends on an ambiguous note about whether he survives an attack.

Shot largely in the Barriada Morales community of Caguas, as well as in San Juan and New York, the film was released on 10 October 2008 by Maya Entertainment in a limited run in major U.S. cities, and in Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic, followed by DVD and Blu-ray in November. It made more than $1 million in Puerto Rico and was received well there, but American critics were harsh: reviewers found the script generic, the storytelling clumsy and the film derivative of 8 Mile and Carlito's Way, though some felt Daddy Yankee held his own on screen.

documents.title: World's Greatest Dad
documents.tagline: Lance Clayton is about to get everything he deserves.
documents.overview: In the wake of a freak accident, Lance suffers the worst tragedy and the greatest opportunity of his life. He is suddenly faced with the possibility of fame, fortune and popularity, if he can only live with the knowledge of how he got there.
documents.plot:
World's Greatest Dad is a 2009 American comedy-drama film directed by Gus Van Sant. The movie follows the story of Dignan (played by Jason Biggs), a high school English teacher who becomes embroiled in a series of misadventures after his girlfriend, Trish (played by Mary Lynn Rajskub), leaves him for another man.

The main themes of World's Greatest Dad include:

1. Identity Crisis: The film explores Dignan's struggle to find his place in the world and define himself outside of his relationship with Trish. As he navigates a series of awkward encounters, Dignan begins to question his own identity and sense of purpose.
2. Toxic Masculinity: Dignan's character is often portrayed as a symbol of toxic masculinity, embodying traits such as aggression, entitlement, and emotional repression. The film critiques these masculine norms and explores the consequences of adhering to them.
3. Loneliness and Isolation: Throughout the movie, Dignan finds himself increasingly isolated from others, including his friends, family, and romantic partner. This loneliness serves as a catalyst for his downward spiral into self-destruction.
4. Absurdity and Surrealism: The film features a series of bizarre and surreal events, which serve to underscore the absurdity of Dignan's situation. These moments often feel disconnected from reality, highlighting the protagonist's disconnection from the world around him.

Overall, World's Greatest Dad is a dark comedy that explores themes of identity crisis, toxic masculinity, loneliness, and absurdity. The film features a unique blend of humor, pathos, and surrealism, making it a thought-provoking and unsettling viewing experience.

documents.title: Interstate 60
documents.tagline: It began as a wish, became an adventure, and ended as the ultimate road trip.
documents.overview: An aspiring painter meets various characters and learns valuable lessons while traveling across America.
documents.plot:
Interstate 60 is a 2002 American drama film directed by Tony Bui. The movie follows the story of a young man named Bobby Mercer, played by James Marsden, who embarks on a road trip from New York to Los Angeles.

The main themes of Interstate 60 include:

1. **Self-discovery and personal growth**: Throughout his journey, Bobby encounters various people and experiences that challenge his perceptions and force him to confront his own identity, values, and purpose in life.
2. **Redemption and forgiveness**: As Bobby navigates the complexities of human relationships and experiences, he seeks redemption for past mistakes and learns to forgive himself and others.
3. **The search for meaning and connection**: The film explores Bobby's quest for a sense of belonging and connection with others, as well as his desire to find meaning in life beyond his mundane daily routine.
4. **The power of human relationships**: Interstate 60 highlights the importance of forming meaningful connections with others, including friends, family, and strangers, which can lead to personal growth, healing, and transformation.

Overall, the movie offers a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, encouraging viewers to reflect on their own values, goals, and relationships.

documents.title: L: change the WorLd
documents.tagline: The final death note showdown!
documents.overview: "The human whose name is written in the Death Note shall die." After making the hardest decision ever, another serious case confronts L. There are only 23 days left and without his best partner Watari (Shunji Fujimura), L has to solve the case all by himself for the very first time.
documents.plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "L: Change the World" released in 2008 by Shochiku. 

However, I found that there is a Japanese film titled "L: Change the World" released in 2008, directed by Ryūhei Kitamura and produced by Toho Co., Ltd. not Shochiku.

The movie is based on the manga of the same name written by Tsutomu Nihei. 

"L: Change the World" is a science fiction film that explores themes of existentialism, nihilism, and the human condition. The story follows L, a mysterious figure who is tasked with erasing humans from existence. As L navigates this world, he begins to question his own purpose and the nature of humanity.

Throughout the movie, Kitamura delves into philosophical and psychological themes, exploring the idea that humanity's existence is but a fleeting moment in an infinite universe. The film also touches on the concept of identity and what it means to be human.

The movie features stunning visuals and a haunting score, which complements its thought-provoking narrative. Overall, "L: Change the World" is a visually striking and intellectually stimulating film that challenges viewers to confront their own existence and place in the world.

documents.title: Despicable Me
documents.tagline: Superbad. Superdad.
documents.overview: Villainous Gru lives up to his reputation as a despicable, deplorable and downright unlikable guy when he hatches a plan to steal the moon from the sky. But he has a tough time staying on task after three orphans land in his care.
documents.plot:
Despicable Me is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2010 by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures. The movie follows the story of Gru, a supervillain who adopts three girls to steal the Moon.

The film begins with Gru (voiced by Steve Carell), a brilliant but eccentric supervillain who has been trying to steal the Moon for years. He is aided in his quest by his loyal Minions, small yellow creatures that are obsessed with bananas and causing chaos. However, Gru's plans are constantly thwarted by Vector (voiced by Jason Segel), a rival villain who steals the spotlight.

One day, Gru meets three girls - Margo (voiced by Miranda Cosgrove), Edith (voiced by Dana Gaier), and Agnes (voiced by Elsie Fisher) - who are being neglected by their mother. Gru adopts the girls to use as a distraction while he carries out his Moon-stealing plan, but soon finds himself falling in love with them.

As Gru spends more time with the girls, he begins to question his life of crime and his relationship with Vector. Meanwhile, Vector's true intentions are revealed: he plans to steal the Moon and sell it to a wealthy collector.

The plot thickens as Gru must balance his villainous ways with his newfound love for the girls. He also has to deal with the Minions' antics, which often get out of hand. In the end, Gru's plan is foiled by Vector, but he ultimately finds a way to save the Moon and redeem himself.

The ending of the film shows Gru finally finding happiness as a father figure to the girls, and Vector getting his comeuppance. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Gru and the girls enjoying quality time together.

Throughout the film, there are many humorous moments courtesy of the Minions, who provide plenty of comedic relief. The animation is also noteworthy, bringing the characters to life in a way that is both visually stunning and endearing.

Overall, Despicable Me is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of love, family, and redemption. With its lovable characters and hilarious humor, it's no wonder why this movie became a beloved classic among audiences worldwide.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo and the Alien Invaders
documents.overview: A cosmic case of flying saucers, intergalactic intrigue and out-of-this-world romance launches Scooby-Doo and the Mystery Inc. Gang into their most unearthly adventure ever.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo and the Alien Invaders is a 2000 animated film that combines mystery, adventure, and science fiction elements. The movie follows the Mystery Inc. gang as they travel to the planet Zorgon to solve a mystery involving alien invasions.

At its core, Scooby-Doo and the Alien Invaders explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the power of believing in oneself. The film showcases the strong bond between the members of the Mystery Inc. gang, who work together to overcome obstacles and unravel the mysteries they encounter.

The movie also delves into the idea of skepticism versus blind faith. The gang's leader, Fred, is initially skeptical of the alien invasion claims, but as he witnesses the strange occurrences firsthand, he begins to question his initial doubts. This theme is reflected in Scooby-Doo himself, who often relies on his instincts and intuition to help solve the mystery.

Furthermore, the film touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery. The main antagonist, an alien named Zorgon, is struggling with his own identity and sense of belonging. His actions are motivated by a desire for acceptance and connection, which serves as a commentary on the human experience.

Overall, Scooby-Doo and the Alien Invaders is a lighthearted, entertaining film that balances humor and adventure with deeper themes about friendship, self-discovery, and the power of believing in oneself.

documents.title: Messengers 2: The Scarecrow
documents.tagline: The Beginning Of The End
documents.overview: The family man farmer John Rollins is stressed with his financial situation: the crows and the lack of irrigation are destroying his crop of corn; the bank is near closure of his mortgage; he does not have credit to fix the water pump or to buy seeds; and his marriage is in crisis and his wife Mary is giving too much attention to her friend Tommy. When John accidentally discovers a hidden compartment in the barn, he finds a creepy scarecrow but his son Michael makes him promise to destroy it. However, his neighbor Jude Weatherby visits him, gives a six-pack of beer to the abstemious John and convinces him to put the scarecrow in the cornfield. Out of the blue, the life of John changes: the crows die; the pump works again irrigating the land; and the banker responsible for the closure has an accident and dies. However, he feels that his land is possessed by something evil that is threatening his beloved family.
documents.plot:
Messengers 2: The Scarecrow is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie explores the theme of revenge, as the scarecrow, a malevolent entity created to protect a family from harm, seeks retribution against those who have wronged it.

The story also touches on the idea of isolation and loneliness, highlighting the devastating effects of being cut off from human connection and community. The characters' struggles to form meaningful relationships and find acceptance serve as a stark contrast to the scarecrow's existence, which is rooted in solitude and a desire for revenge.

Furthermore, Messengers 2: The Scarecrow examines the blurred lines between good and evil, raising questions about the nature of morality and the consequences of one's actions. The film's portrayal of a seemingly innocent entity turned malevolent serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of underestimating others and the importance of empathy and understanding.

Ultimately, the movie presents a haunting commentary on the human condition, revealing the darker aspects of our own nature and the devastating consequences that can arise when we fail to acknowledge and address our deepest fears and insecurities.

documents.title: Digimon: The Movie
documents.tagline: New Monsters. New Battles. Now on the Big Screen.
documents.overview: The first story focused on Tai and Kari Kamiya four years before their adventure in the Digital World. It shows their first encounter with Digimon and what happened to them (as well as the other children). Tai and Kari wake one morning to find a Digi-Egg that came out of their computer the night before and the egg soon hatches, revealing a Botamon. The Digimon then evolves into Koromon and then Agumon (not the same one that became friends with Tai in the series, and yet, somehow, both Koromon and Kari remember each other), who then goes out and unintentionally destroys a good part of the neighborhood with Kari riding on his back. A second Digi-Egg appears in the sky to reveal an evil digimon, Parrotmon. Agumon then Digivolves to Greymon but isn't strong enough to beat Parrotmon and is knocked out. Tai grabs Kari's whistle and wakes up Greymon, who defeats Parrotmon and disappears with him.
documents.plot:
Digimon: The Movie is a 2000 animated science fiction adventure film based on the popular Digimon franchise. The movie follows the story of Taichi "Tai" Kamiya, a young boy who partners with a digital creature known as Agumon to save the world from destruction.

The main themes of Digimon: The Movie include:

1. Friendship and Camaraderie: The film highlights the strong bond between Tai and his friends, including Matt Ishida, Sora Takenouchi, and Joe Kido, who all work together to defeat their enemies.
2. Self-Discovery and Growth: Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges that test their courage, loyalty, and determination. As they overcome these obstacles, they learn valuable lessons about themselves and grow as individuals.
3. Good vs. Evil: The film features a clear distinction between good and evil, with the Digimon and their human partners fighting against an evil organization known as the "Digital Monster" that threatens to destroy the world.
4. Sacrifice and Loyalty: Tai and his friends are willing to make sacrifices for each other and for the greater good, demonstrating the importance of loyalty and selflessness in the face of adversity.

The movie's plot is driven by a series of events that unfold as follows:

* The story begins with Tai and Agumon being transported to a digital world where they meet other Digimon and form alliances.
* As they journey through this new world, they discover that an evil Digital Monster known as Devimon is threatening to destroy the digital realm.
* Tai and his friends must work together to defeat Devimon and save their partners from destruction.
* Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and the importance of believing in themselves.

Overall, Digimon: The Movie is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that explores themes of friendship, self-discovery, and good vs. evil.

documents.title: The Book of Eli
documents.tagline: Some will kill to have it. He will kill to protect it.
documents.overview: A post-apocalyptic tale, in which a lone man fights his way across America in order to protect a sacred book that holds the secrets to saving humankind.
documents.plot:
The Book of Eli is a post-apocalyptic drama film directed by the Hughes Brothers and starring Denzel Washington, Gary Oldman, Mila Kunis, and Ray Stevenson. Released in 2010, the movie takes place in a world devastated by nuclear war.

In the year 2035, humanity has been decimated, and society has collapsed. The story follows Eli (Denzel Washington), a lone survivor who embarks on a perilous journey to protect a sacred book known as the "Book of Eli." This book is believed to hold the secrets of the past and potentially the key to rebuilding society.

The movie begins with Eli, a rugged and stoic man, walking through a desolate landscape. He is accompanied by a young girl named Solara (Mila Kunis), who claims that she has been sent to protect him from an unknown threat. As they journey together, it becomes clear that Eli's past is shrouded in mystery, and he is haunted by his own demons.

Their path is fraught with danger, as they encounter various factions vying for control of the remaining resources. One such faction is led by a ruthless leader named Carnegie (Gary Oldman), who seeks to exploit the book's power for his own gain. Eli and Solara must navigate treacherous landscapes, avoid deadly traps, and fight off hostile groups to reach their destination.

As they journey on, Eli begins to open up to Solara about his past, revealing that he was once a member of a community called Zion. He shares with her the story of how he became the guardian of the Book of Eli, which contains the secrets of the pre-war world. The book is said to hold the key to rebuilding society and restoring hope to humanity.

Throughout their journey, Eli and Solara face numerous challenges, including encounters with marauders, radiation zones, and treacherous terrain. Along the way, they form a bond that transcends their differences, and Solara becomes a catalyst for Eli's emotional growth.

As they near their destination, Carnegie and his followers close in on them. In a tense showdown, Eli and Solara fight to protect the book from falling into the wrong hands. In the end, Eli sacrifices himself to ensure the book's safety, allowing it to be taken by a young girl named Irad (Ray Stevenson), who is destined to carry on Eli's mission.

The movie concludes with Eli's sacrifice serving as a symbol of hope and redemption in a world that has lost its way. The Book of Eli serves as a reminder of the past and provides a glimmer of light for humanity's future, setting the stage for Irad's journey to rebuild society.

Overall, The Book of Eli is a gripping post-apocalyptic drama that explores themes of hope, redemption, and the power of human connection in the face of adversity.

documents.title: TRON: Legacy
documents.tagline: The game has changed.
documents.overview: Sam Flynn, the tech-savvy and daring son of Kevin Flynn, investigates his father's disappearance and is pulled into The Grid. With the help of a mysterious program named Quorra, Sam quests to stop evil dictator Clu from crossing into the real world.
documents.plot:
TRON: Legacy is a 2010 science fiction film directed by Joseph Kosinski and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1982 classic TRON, while also introducing new characters and themes.

The story begins with Kevin Flynn (Jeff Bridges), the original creator of the virtual world of Tron, who has been missing for 28 years. His son, Sam Flynn (Garrett Hedlund), is now an adult and a brilliant programmer in his own right. Sam's life takes a dramatic turn when he receives a message from his father, which leads him to a mysterious website that reveals the existence of Clu (Jeff Bridges), Kevin's business partner who has taken over the company.

Clu, played by the same actor as Kevin Flynn, is revealed to be a digital creation of Kevin's own code. He was created to manage and maintain the Grid, but he became self-aware and eventually took control of the system, leading to Kevin's disappearance. Clu sees Sam as a threat to his existence and decides to eliminate him.

Sam soon discovers that he has inherited his father's abilities and is able to enter the virtual world of Tron. He meets Quorra (Olivia Wilde), a program created by Kevin who becomes his ally in the fight against Clu. Together, they embark on a perilous journey through the Grid, navigating treacherous landscapes and battling Clu's army of programs.

As Sam delves deeper into the Grid, he learns more about his father's past and the true nature of Clu's existence. He also discovers that Quorra is not just a program, but a sentient being with her own motivations and desires. The two form a strong bond as they work together to defeat Clu and restore balance to the Grid.

The film features stunning visual effects, showcasing the beauty and danger of the virtual world. The action sequences are intense and thrilling, with Sam and Quorra facing off against Clu's programs in epic battles. The movie also explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the consequences of playing god with technology.

In the end, Sam and Quorra succeed in defeating Clu, but not before he reveals a shocking secret about his own existence. The film concludes with Sam returning to the real world, forever changed by his experience in the Grid. He also discovers that Kevin is still alive, trapped in a digital limbo, and sets out to rescue him.

TRON: Legacy received mixed reviews from critics, but was a commercial success, grossing over $400 million worldwide. The film's visual effects and action sequences were widely praised, while some critics felt that the story was too predictable and lacked the originality of the 1982 classic. Nevertheless, TRON: Legacy remains a beloved sequel in the franchise, offering a fresh take on the world of Tron while honoring the spirit of the original.

documents.title: Something the Lord Made
documents.tagline: A breakthrough that changed the face of medicine. A unique partnership that broke the rules.
documents.overview: A dramatization of the relationship between heart surgery pioneers Alfred Blalock and Vivien Thomas.
documents.plot:
Something the Lord Made is a 2004 American television biographical drama about the partnership between Vivien Thomas (1910–1985), a Black laboratory technician who became a pioneer of cardiac surgery, and the white surgeon Alfred Blalock (1899–1964), known as the "Blue Baby doctor". Directed by Joseph Sargent for HBO, it is based on Katie McCabe's National Magazine Award-winning Washingtonian article "Like Something the Lord Made". Alan Rickman plays Blalock and Yasiin Bey, then known as Mos Def, plays Thomas, with Kyra Sedgwick, Gabrielle Union and Merritt Wever in supporting roles.

The story spans a partnership of more than three decades. In Depression-era Nashville in 1930, Blalock hires Thomas, a carpenter who had hoped to study medicine but lost his savings in the stock market crash, to work in his laboratory at Vanderbilt University, expecting him to do little more than cleaning. Thomas's extraordinary manual skill and quick intelligence soon make him an indispensable research partner, even though he is classified and paid as a janitor.

In 1943, Blalock moves to Johns Hopkins in Baltimore and insists on bringing Thomas with him. At the time, the only Black employees at the institution are custodial staff, and Thomas must use the back entrance. The paediatric cardiologist Helen Taussig challenges Blalock to find a surgical treatment for infants with tetralogy of Fallot, known as blue baby syndrome. Thomas develops the operation in the laboratory on dogs, and when Blalock performs the first procedure on a human patient in 1944, Thomas stands behind him in the operating room, guiding him step by step. The operation launches modern heart surgery, but Blalock receives the public credit while Thomas remains unrecognised, and tensions over race, money and respect strain their relationship over the following years.

The film explores ambition, loyalty and the racial injustice that kept Thomas from the recognition he deserved, ending with his belated honours from Johns Hopkins, including an honorary doctorate and the hanging of his portrait beside Blalock's.

Something the Lord Made received critical acclaim and won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Made for Television Movie, along with other honours including a Peabody Award. Rickman and Bey both earned Emmy nominations for their performances.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! in Where's My Mummy?
documents.overview: Scooby-Doo and the Mystery Inc. gang become involved in a supernatural mystery in Egypt.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo! in Where's My Mummy? is a 2005 animated film that follows the Mystery Inc. gang as they travel to Egypt, where they become embroiled in a mystery surrounding an ancient mummy.

The main themes of Scooby-Doo! in Where's My Mummy? include:

1. Friendship and teamwork: The movie highlights the strong bond between the members of the Mystery Inc. gang, who work together to solve the mystery and uncover the truth behind the mummy's awakening.
2. Cultural sensitivity and appreciation: The film takes a lighthearted approach to exploring Egyptian culture and history, showcasing the gang's curiosity and enthusiasm for learning about ancient civilizations.
3. Deception and misdirection: As with many Scooby-Doo movies, the plot is driven by clever deceptions and misdirection, keeping the audience guessing until the very end.
4. Growing up and change: The movie also touches on themes of growing up and change, as Shaggy and Scooby face new challenges and learn to adapt to their surroundings.

The story begins with the Mystery Inc. gang arriving in Egypt, where they meet a wealthy collector who is searching for his missing mummy. As they explore the ancient ruins and temples, they begin to uncover clues that suggest the mummy may be more than just a simple relic.

As the mystery deepens, the gang encounters various suspects and red herrings, including a rival treasure hunter and a mysterious cult leader. Along the way, Shaggy and Scooby become separated from the rest of the group and must navigate the treacherous jungle terrain to find their way back.

In the end, the Mystery Inc. gang exposes the truth behind the mummy's awakening, revealing a surprising twist that challenges their expectations. The movie concludes with the gang returning home, wiser and more experienced, but also with a newfound appreciation for the wonders of ancient Egypt.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! in Where's My Mummy? is a fun and entertaining mystery film that combines humor, adventure, and cultural exploration, making it a great addition to the Scooby-Doo franchise.

documents.title: Swimfan
documents.tagline: His biggest fan just became his worst nightmare.
documents.overview: Ben Cronin has it all: the admiration of his many friends, a terrific girlfriend, and he's on the fast-track to an athletic scholarship. Ben's rock-solid, promising future and romance are turned upside-down with the arrival of Madison Bell. Madison, the new girl in town, quickly sets her sights on the impressionable Ben. While their first few meetings are innocent enough, the obsessive and seductive Madison wants more ... much more.
documents.plot:
Swimfan is a 2002 American teen drama film directed by Andrew Fleming. The movie revolves around Cassie Wright (played by Jessica Biel), a high school student who becomes obsessed with winning the state swimming championships, and her complicated relationships with those around her.

At its core, Swimfan explores themes of ambition, obsession, and the pressures that come with achieving success in competitive sports. Cassie's relentless drive to win is fueled by a desire for validation and recognition from her peers, as well as her own sense of identity. As she navigates the cutthroat world of high school swimming, she must confront the darker aspects of her own personality and the true cost of her ambition.

The film also delves into the complexities of female relationships, particularly those between women who are perceived as rivals or competitors. Cassie's interactions with her teammates and opponents serve as a catalyst for exploring themes of jealousy, insecurity, and the blurred lines between friendship and rivalry.

Furthermore, Swimfan touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Cassie struggles to reconcile her athletic persona with her personal life and relationships. The movie raises questions about what it means to be oneself, both in and out of competition, and whether the pursuit of success can come at a cost to one's emotional well-being.

Overall, Swimfan is a thought-provoking drama that uses the backdrop of competitive swimming to explore universal themes of ambition, identity, and relationships.

documents.title: Robin Hood
documents.tagline: Rise and rise again, until lambs become lions.
documents.overview: When soldier Robin happens upon the dying Robert of Loxley, he promises to return the man's sword to his family in Nottingham. There, he assumes Robert's identity; romances his widow, Marion; and draws the ire of the town's sheriff and King John's henchman, Godfrey.
documents.plot:
Robin Hood is a 2010 historical action film directed by Ridley Scott and written by Brian Helgeland from a story by Helgeland, Ethan Reiff and Cyrus Voris. Russell Crowe stars as the outlaw of legend, with Cate Blanchett, William Hurt, Mark Strong, Mark Addy, Oscar Isaac, Danny Huston, Eileen Atkins and Max von Sydow. A 2007 spec script centred on the Sheriff of Nottingham was rewritten to tell how Robin Hood became an outlaw.

In 1199 Robin Longstride is a common archer in the army of King Richard the Lionheart at the siege of Chalus Castle. He gives the king a frank assessment of his conduct and is put in the stocks with his comrades Allan A'Dayle, Will Scarlett and Little John. After Richard is killed in the assault, they desert and come across an ambush of the royal guard by Godfrey, an English knight conspiring with King Philip of France. Posing as the dead knights to secure passage home, and Robin promises the dying Sir Robert of Loxley that he will return his sword to his father in Nottingham. Arriving in England, Robin, still posing as Loxley, delivers Richard's crown and witnesses the coronation of King John, who imposes harsh new taxes and sends Godfrey north to collect them, unaware that Godfrey plans to use French troops to stir up unrest ahead of a French invasion. In Nottingham, Loxley's elderly, blind father Sir Walter asks Robin to keep impersonating his son so that the Crown cannot seize the family's lands, and Loxley's widow, Lady Marian, initially cold, warms to him after he recovers grain for the townspeople. When the northern barons rise against John, Robin persuades the king to accept a charter of rights to unite the country against the invasion. French raiders plunder Nottingham and Godfrey kills Sir Walter before Robin and the barons arrive. On the beach below the cliffs of Dover, Robin leads the united English army against the French landing, with Marian joining the fight, and kills Godfrey with an arrow, forcing Philip to abandon the invasion. Seeing the French surrender to Robin rather than to him, John breaks his promise of the charter and declares Robin an outlaw, and Robin, his men and Nottingham's orphans retreat to Sherwood Forest to right the wrongs of the kingdom.

Filmed across England and Wales from March 2009, Robin Hood premiered at the Cannes Film Festival on 12 May 2010, the day of its British release. It received mixed reviews, with a 43% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and grossed $322 million worldwide.

documents.title: Deep Cover
documents.tagline: There's a thin line between catching a criminal... and becoming one.
documents.overview: Black police officer Russell Stevens applies for a special anti-drug squad which targets the highest boss of cocaine delivery to LA—the Colombian foreign minister's nephew. Russell works his way up from the bottom undercover, until he reaches the boss.
documents.plot:
Deep Cover is a crime drama film that delves into the complexities of identity, loyalty, and deception. The story revolves around a deep-cover FBI agent who infiltrates a gang to gather evidence against them, but as he becomes more entrenched in their world, his own moral compass begins to blur.

At its core, Deep Cover explores the theme of identity fragmentation, where an individual's sense of self is torn apart by conflicting loyalties and allegiances. The protagonist's dual existence as both a lawman and a gangster raises questions about the nature of truth and how it can be distorted or manipulated for personal gain.

The film also touches on the idea of loyalty and betrayal, highlighting the difficulties of navigating complex relationships within a world where trust is a luxury few can afford. As the protagonist becomes more embroiled in the gang's activities, he must confront the consequences of his own actions and the true cost of his deception.

Furthermore, Deep Cover critiques the systemic failures that enable organized crime to thrive, particularly in urban communities where poverty, racism, and social inequality create fertile ground for exploitation. The film offers a nuanced portrayal of the cyclical nature of violence and the devastating impact it has on individuals and society as a whole.

Ultimately, Deep Cover presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of their own nature and the world around them.

documents.title: Detective Conan: Captured in Her Eyes
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 瞳の中の暗殺者
documents.overview: Police officers around Tokyo are being murdered by an unknown assailant. When Ran witnesses an attempt on the life of one of her friends in the police, she loses her memory. Now, Conan and Inspector Megure must find the murderer while Ran attempts to regain her lost memories.
documents.plot:
Detective Conan: Captured in Her Eyes is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows Ran's quest to uncover the truth behind her sister's death, which leads her down a rabbit hole of deceit and manipulation.

At its core, the film explores the theme of obsession, as Ran becomes increasingly entangled in a web of lies and half-truths that threaten to consume her. Her fixation on the truth drives her to confront the darker aspects of human psychology, including the capacity for cruelty, deception, and even madness.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and how it can be manipulated and distorted. The main antagonist's ability to create multiple personas and alter their appearance raises questions about the nature of self and how easily it can be changed or fabricated.

Furthermore, the film critiques the societal pressures that can lead individuals to conform to certain expectations or norms, even if it means sacrificing their own desires and autonomy. Ran's journey is a powerful commentary on the constraints placed on women in particular, as she navigates a patriarchal society that seeks to control her every move.

Ultimately, Detective Conan: Captured in Her Eyes is a gripping thriller that probes the depths of human psychology, revealing the complexities and nuances of the human condition.

documents.title: Rugrats Go Wild
documents.tagline: The Family Vacation Goes Overboard.
documents.overview: When the Rugrats find themselves stranded on a deserted island, they meet the Thornberrys, a family who agrees to help them escape.
documents.plot:
Rugrats Go Wild is an animated adventure film that combines the worlds of two beloved Nickelodeon shows: Rugrats and The Wild Thornberrys. At its core, the movie explores the theme of exploration and discovery, as the Rugrats embark on a wild adventure with the Thornberry family.

The film delves into the idea of stepping out of one's comfort zone and embracing the unknown. The Rugrats, led by Tommy Pickles, are initially hesitant to venture into the jungle, but ultimately learn to adapt and thrive in their new surroundings. This theme is mirrored in the Thornberry family's own experiences as they navigate the challenges of exploring the wilderness.

The movie also touches on the importance of friendship and teamwork. As the Rugrats and Thornberries work together to overcome obstacles, they develop a strong bond that helps them succeed in their mission. This theme is particularly evident in the relationships between Tommy and Donnie, who form an unlikely but effective partnership, and between Chuckie and Eliza, who find common ground despite their differences.

Furthermore, the film explores the idea of growing up and letting go of childhood innocence. As the Rugrats face new challenges and experiences, they begin to realize that there's more to life than just playing in the sandbox. This theme is subtly woven throughout the story, as the characters learn valuable lessons about responsibility, courage, and the importance of family.

Overall, Rugrats Go Wild is a heartwarming adventure film that celebrates exploration, friendship, and growth, making it a delightful watch for both children and adults alike.

documents.title: La Maison en Petits Cubes
documents.overview: La Maison en Petits Cubes tells the story of a grandfather's memories as he adds more blocks to his house to stem the flooding waters.
documents.plot:
La Maison en Petits Cubes is a poignant and visually stunning film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, loss, and the passage of time. The movie follows the story of an elderly woman who lives in a small house made up of 109 cubes, each representing a year from her life.

The main theme of the film revolves around the idea of nostalgia and how it shapes our perception of ourselves and our relationships with others. As the woman reminisces about her past, we see flashbacks of her life, filled with moments of joy, love, and heartbreak. The film masterfully interweaves these memories with the present, highlighting the ways in which our experiences shape us into who we are today.

One of the most striking aspects of La Maison en Petits Cubes is its exploration of loneliness and isolation. Despite being surrounded by loved ones, the woman feels deeply disconnected from the world around her. This sense of disconnection serves as a powerful metaphor for the human experience, where we often feel like we're just going through the motions of life without truly connecting with others.

The film also touches on the theme of love and loss, particularly in the context of relationships that have come to an end. The woman's memories are filled with moments of tenderness and intimacy, but these are also tinged with a sense of sadness and longing. This bittersweet quality is a hallmark of the film, leaving the viewer with a sense of melancholy that lingers long after the credits roll.

Ultimately, La Maison en Petits Cubes is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human emotions and relationships. Through its use of nostalgia, loneliness, love, and loss, the movie creates a poignant and thought-provoking portrait of life's fragility and beauty.

documents.title: Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch
documents.original_title: Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch
documents.overview: Now, we find the rowdy extraterrestrial getting used to life with his new ʻohana. However, a malfunction in the ultimate creation of Dr. Jumba soon emerges, which reinstates his destructive programming and threatens to both ruin his friendship with Lilo and to short him out for good!
documents.plot:
Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch is a 2005 American direct-to-video animated science fiction comedy-drama produced by the Australian office of Disneytoon Studios. It was directed by Tony Leondis and Michael LaBash in their directorial debuts, and they co-wrote it with Eddie Guzelian and Alexa Junge. It is a direct sequel to Lilo & Stitch (2002). Chris Sanders voices Stitch and Dakota Fanning voices Lilo, with Tia Carrere as Nani, David Ogden Stiers as Jumba, Kevin McDonald as Pleakley and Jason Scott Lee as David.

Stitch, now part of the Pelekai family on Kauaʻi, dreams of reverting to his destructive programming and attacking Lilo. At hula class, her teacher Moses Puloki announces that each student must create an original dance for the May Day festival. Lilo is inspired to learn her mother won it as a girl. After she lashes out at her taunting rival Mertle, Moses doubts she is ready. As she and Stitch struggle for ideas, Stitch begins suffering seizures that make him act wildly. Jumba never fully charged Stitch's molecules before his arrest, and the defect is reverting Stitch to his old programming and will kill him unless fixed.

Focused on winning, Lilo assumes he is misbehaving on purpose and neglects him. Lilo devises a hula based on the legend of Hiʻiaka, but Stitch's episodes keep ruining rehearsals, while Jumba builds a recharging machine from household objects. On the day of the festival, a seizure causes Stitch to lash out at Lilo just as in his nightmare. Lilo realizes something is wrong, but Stitch, horrified, runs away. Lilo abandons her performance and learns the truth from Jumba. Stitch tries to leave Earth in Jumba's ship but crashes in the mountains after another seizure. Lilo gets him into the finished machine too late, and he appears to die. When she apologizes for putting herself first and tells him she will always love him, Stitch revives. That night the family performs Lilo's hula together, and Nani tells her their mother would be proud.

Fanning replaced Daveigh Chase, who was busy with Lilo & Stitch: The Series. Planned for theaters, it went to video after The Jungle Book 2 disappointed, and it became Disney's only direct-to-video animated film rated PG. It premiered at Turtle Bay Resort on Oahu on August 15, 2005, and was released on DVD and VHS on August 30. Rotten Tomatoes reported 42% approval. Polygon, however, later ranked it the best of Disney's direct-to-video sequels, praising its balance of alien and human stories.

documents.title: The Road
