documents.tagline: In a moment the world changed forever.
documents.overview: A father and his son walk alone through burned America. Nothing moves in the ravaged landscape save the ash on the wind and water. It is cold enough to crack stones, and, when the snow falls it is gray. The sky is dark. Their destination is the warmer south, although they don't know what, if anything, awaits them there.
documents.plot:
The Road is a post-apocalyptic drama film directed by John Hillcoat, based on the Pulitzer Prize-winning novel of the same name by Cormac McCarthy. The movie was produced by 2929 Productions and released in 2009.

The main themes of The Road include:

1. **Survival vs. Humanity**: The story revolves around the struggle to survive in a world ravaged by an unspecified cataclysmic event, while also exploring the human condition and what it means to be alive.
2. **Hope and Despair**: The film's narrative is marked by moments of hope and despair, as the father and son navigate their perilous journey through a desolate landscape, searching for safety and security.
3. **Love and Sacrifice**: The relationship between the father and son serves as a powerful symbol of love and sacrifice, as they risk everything to protect each other in a world devoid of hope.
4. **Existentialism**: The movie raises fundamental questions about the meaning of life, the nature of humanity, and the significance of existence in the face of unimaginable suffering and loss.
5. **Parental Love and Responsibility**: The father's unwavering dedication to his son serves as a testament to the power of parental love and responsibility, even in the most challenging circumstances.

The Road is a haunting and powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the darkest aspects of existence while also celebrating the resilience of the human spirit.

documents.title: Kim Possible: So the Drama
documents.overview: Dr. Drakken has an evil new plot for world domination, but his ultimate success depends upon finding out KP's weakness which may involve a new hottie at Middleton High School named Eric, who suddenly sparks feelings in Ron about Kim that resemble much more than friendship. To make matters worse, Bueno Nacho, Ron's favorite fast food chain has turned sour on him by bombarding him with little Devils
documents.plot:
Kim Possible: So the Drama is an animated film that revolves around the life of Kim Possible, a high school girl who leads a double life as a superhero. The movie delves into themes of identity, self-discovery, and the challenges of growing up.

At its core, the film explores the tension between Kim's secret life as a superhero and her everyday life as a high school student. As she navigates these two worlds, Kim must confront the difficulties of balancing her responsibilities and desires. This struggle is reflective of the universal experience of adolescence, where young people are constantly trying to figure out who they are and where they fit in.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty and friendship. Kim's relationships with her friends and family are put to the test as she navigates the complexities of being a superhero. The film highlights the importance of having a strong support system, particularly during times of uncertainty and self-doubt.

Furthermore, So the Drama explores the idea of embracing one's true nature and not trying to hide or conform to societal expectations. Kim is forced to confront her own insecurities and doubts, ultimately leading her to accept herself for who she is and find a sense of confidence and empowerment.

Overall, Kim Possible: So the Drama is a coming-of-age story that explores the challenges and triumphs of growing up, self-discovery, and finding one's place in the world.

documents.title: The Flyboys
documents.overview: Two boys from a small town find their courage tested when they accidentally stow away aboard an airplane owned by the mob...
documents.plot:
The Flyboys is an action-drama film that revolves around the lives of American fighter pilots during World War I. At its core, the movie explores the themes of camaraderie and brotherhood among the pilots as they navigate the harsh realities of war.

One of the primary themes of The Flyboys is the bond between men in the face of adversity. The film showcases the strong relationships that develop among the pilots, who rely on each other for support and comfort in the midst of chaos. This camaraderie is particularly evident in the way the characters look out for one another, both on and off the battlefield.

The movie also delves into the psychological effects of war on its protagonists. The Flyboys grapples with the trauma and emotional toll that combat can take on individuals, highlighting the struggles of pilots to cope with the loss of friends and the moral complexities of war.

Furthermore, The Flyboys touches on the theme of sacrifice and the true cost of heroism. As the characters face increasingly dire situations, they are forced to confront the ultimate sacrifices they must make for their country and their fellow pilots. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, The Flyboys is a powerful exploration of the human experience during wartime, one that sheds light on the complexities of male relationships, the psychological toll of combat, and the ultimate sacrifices made by those who serve.

documents.title: Funny People
documents.tagline: George Simmons was prepared to die, but then a funny thing happened.
documents.overview: Famous and wealthy funnyman George Simmons doesn't give much thought to how he treats people until a doctor delivers stunning health news, forcing George to reevaluate his priorities with a little help from aspiring stand-up comic Ira.
documents.plot:
Funny People (2009) is a comedy-drama film directed by Judd Apatow, starring Adam Sandler and Seth Rogen. The movie follows the life of George Simmons (played by Adam Sandler), a successful comedian who announces that he has terminal cancer.

The main themes of Funny People include:

1. Mortality and the meaning of life: As George's health deteriorates, he is forced to confront his own mortality and re-evaluate his priorities in life. The film explores the idea that we all have limited time on this earth, and it's up to us to make the most of it.

2. Friendship and relationships: The movie highlights the importance of genuine friendships and relationships in our lives. George's friendship with Ira Wright (played by Seth Rogen) is a central theme, as they navigate their way through life's ups and downs together.

3. Identity and purpose: As George struggles to come to terms with his own mortality, he begins to question the purpose of his life and career. The film explores the idea that our sense of identity and purpose can be shaken by unexpected events, and it's up to us to find new meaning in life.

4. Comedic legacy: The movie also touches on the theme of comedic legacy, as George grapples with the idea of leaving a lasting impact on the world through his comedy. This theme is particularly relevant for Adam Sandler, who has built a career on making people laugh.

5. Existentialism and the search for meaning: Throughout the film, George's existential crisis serves as a catalyst for exploring deeper questions about the human condition. The movie raises questions about the nature of existence, the meaning of life, and our place in the world.

Overall, Funny People is a thought-provoking comedy-drama that explores complex themes through the lens of humor and satire.

documents.title: Aliens in the Attic
documents.tagline: The aliens vs. the Pearsons
documents.overview: A group of kids must protect their vacation home from invading aliens.
documents.plot:
Aliens in the Attic is a 2009 American science fiction comedy directed by John Schultz, from a screenplay by Mark Burton and Adam F. Goldberg based on a story by Burton. The live-action cast includes Carter Jenkins, Austin Butler, Ashley Tisdale, Kevin Nealon, Robert Hoffman, Andy Richter, Doris Roberts and Tim Meadows, while Josh Peck, J. K. Simmons, Thomas Haden Church and Kari Wahlgren voice the computer-animated alien invaders. Released by 20th Century Fox in the summer of 2009, the film was aimed squarely at a family audience.

The story follows the Pearson family from suburban Chicago. Fifteen-year-old Tom is a gifted student who has been deliberately failing his classes to fit in, and after he is caught hacking his school's website to alter his grades, his father Stuart decides that the family needs a holiday at a lakeside house in Michigan. Joining them are Tom's sisters, his immature uncle Nate, his cousins Jake and the gamer twins Art and Lee, and his grandmother Rose. Older sister Bethany's boyfriend Ricky, a smug college student, also turns up uninvited and talks his way into staying.

During a storm, four small aliens, the vanguard of an invasion force, crash-land on the roof and set up a base in the attic. They carry a device that allows them to control human beings by attaching it to their necks like a remote-controlled toy, but the gadget does not work on children, which means only the kids can fight back. While the adults remain oblivious, Tom and his cousins wage a secret war against the invaders using homemade weapons, potato guns and fireworks, eventually finding an unlikely ally in Sparks, a gentle alien engineer who does not share his comrades' ambitions. Comic set pieces include Grandma Rose being turned into a martial-arts fighter and Ricky being forced to perform humiliating stunts under alien control.

Beneath the slapstick, the film is about Tom learning to accept his intelligence rather than hide it, as his knowledge of technology and strategy becomes the key to defeating the aliens and protecting the planet before reinforcements arrive.

Critics gave Aliens in the Attic largely negative reviews, describing it as formulaic, though some found it harmless entertainment for younger viewers. The film achieved moderate box-office returns and is now also remembered as an early screen role for Austin Butler.

documents.title: Innocent Voices
documents.overview: A young boy, in an effort to have a normal childhood in 1980s El Salvador, is caught up in a dramatic fight for his life as he desperately tries to avoid the war which is raging all around him
documents.plot:
Innocent Voices is a 2004 American drama film directed by Mike Binder, not 2005. The movie was produced by A Band Apart.

The main themes of Innocent Voices include:

1. Coming-of-age: The story revolves around the life of a young boy named Jesse, who is struggling to cope with his father's death and navigate the complexities of growing up.
2. Grief and loss: The film explores the emotional impact of losing a loved one on a child, and how it affects their relationships with family members and friends.
3. Identity formation: As Jesse navigates adolescence, he begins to question his own identity and sense of purpose in life.
4. Family dynamics: The movie highlights the complexities of family relationships, particularly between Jesse and his father, who was a Vietnam War veteran struggling with PTSD.

The film received critical acclaim for its nuanced portrayal of these themes, as well as its thoughtful exploration of the human experience during times of war and loss.

documents.title: The Ugly Truth
documents.tagline: The battle of the sexes is on.
documents.overview: A romantically challenged morning show producer is reluctantly embroiled in a series of outrageous tests by her chauvinistic correspondent to prove his theories on relationships and help her find love. His clever ploys, however, lead to an unexpected result.
documents.plot:
The Ugly Truth is a 2009 American romantic comedy film directed by Ron Howard and starring Katherine Heigl and Gerard Butler.

The movie begins with Abby Richter (Katherine Heigl), a television news producer who has just been assigned to work alongside Colton McCauley (Gerard Butler), a chauvinistic and womanizing TV show host. The two have an instant dislike for each other, with Abby finding Colton's sexist behavior and lack of professionalism off-putting.

Despite their initial animosity, the two are forced to work together when they are paired as co-hosts on a local morning news program. As they spend more time together, Abby tries to reform Colton into a more respectable and family-friendly host, while Colton attempts to seduce Abby and break her spirit.

As the days go by, Abby begins to see beyond Colton's rough exterior and discovers that he has a softer side. Meanwhile, Colton starts to develop feelings for Abby, but his past behavior makes it difficult for him to express them. The two engage in a series of witty banter-filled exchanges, with Abby trying to keep Colton in check while also navigating her growing attraction to him.

As the story progresses, Abby's colleagues and friends start to notice the change in her and become concerned about her relationship with Colton. They warn her that he is not good for her, but Abby is determined to give him a chance.

In the end, Abby and Colton's feelings for each other are revealed, and they share a romantic kiss on live television. The movie ends with the two of them working together as co-hosts, with Colton having undergone a significant transformation from his sexist and womanizing days.

Throughout the movie, Katherine Heigl delivers a standout performance as Abby Richter, bringing depth and nuance to her character. Gerard Butler also shines in his role as Colton McCauley, showcasing his range as an actor and adding humor and charm to the film.

Overall, The Ugly Truth is a fun and lighthearted romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and personal growth. With its witty dialogue and strong performances from the leads, it's a movie that will leave audiences smiling and feeling uplifted.

documents.title: Ocean Waves
documents.overview: At Kichijōji Station, Tokyo, Taku Morisaki glimpses a familiar woman on the platform opposite boarding a train. Later, her photo falls from a shelf as he exits his apartment before flying to Kōchi Prefecture. Picking it up, he looks at it briefly before leaving. As the aeroplane takes off, he narrates the events that brought her into his life...
documents.plot:
Ocean Waves is a 1993 Japanese coming-of-age drama film directed by Tomoko Yoshida, based on the novel of the same name by Aiichiro Miyamoto.

The main themes of Ocean Waves revolve around the complexities of adolescence, first love, and self-discovery. The story follows Taku Morisaki, a high school student who returns to his hometown after spending three years abroad with his family. Upon his return, he reunites with his childhood friends, including Rikako Chigira, and becomes involved in a complicated web of relationships.

The film explores the themes of:

1. **First love and heartbreak**: Taku's rekindled romance with Rikako serves as a catalyst for exploring the complexities of first love, desire, and heartbreak.
2. **Identity formation**: As Taku navigates his relationships and personal growth, he grapples with finding his place in the world and defining himself outside of his family's expectations.
3. **Nostalgia and longing**: The film is set against the backdrop of a changing Japan, and the characters' nostalgia for their childhood serves as a reminder of the passing of time and the fragility of youth.
4. **Social hierarchy and class differences**: The story touches on the social stratification in Japan, particularly in the context of Taku's family and his relationships with his peers.

Through its thoughtful portrayal of adolescent struggles and relationships, Ocean Waves offers a poignant exploration of the human experience during this pivotal stage of life.

documents.title: Tom and Jerry Blast Off to Mars!
documents.original_title: Tom and Jerry Blast Off to Mars!
documents.overview: While carrying on their usual hi-jinks, they inadvertantly stow-away on a spaceship bound for Mars. They meet up with the local Martian residents and cause them to invade the Earth, aided by the "Invincitron", a vacuum-wielding giant robot. Tom, Jerry and their Martian ally, Peep, save the day.
documents.plot:
Tom and Jerry Blast Off to Mars is an animated science fiction comedy film that revolves around the eternal cat-and-mouse rivalry between Tom and Jerry, with a space-themed twist. The movie's main theme is the never-ending struggle for dominance and control between two arch-nemesis who find themselves on a mission to Mars.

The story explores the idea of friendship and camaraderie in the face of adversity as Tom and Jerry are forced to put aside their animosity and work together to survive on the hostile Martian terrain. The film's themes also touch upon the concept of teamwork, cooperation, and mutual respect, highlighting that even the most unlikely of adversaries can find common ground when faced with a shared challenge.

The movie also delves into the idea of exploration and discovery, as Tom and Jerry navigate the uncharted territories of Mars and encounter various obstacles and challenges along the way. The film's visuals and animation bring to life the wonders of space travel and the thrill of exploring the unknown, making it an entertaining and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Tom and Jerry Blast Off to Mars is a lighthearted and humorous film that uses its science fiction setting to explore timeless themes of friendship, teamwork, and cooperation.

documents.title: Sin Nombre
documents.tagline: The greatest sin of all is risking nothing.
documents.overview: Sayra, a Honduran teen, hungers for a better life. Her chance for one comes when she is reunited with her long-estranged father, who intends to emigrate to Mexico and then enter the United States. Sayra's life collides with a pair of Mexican gangmembers who have boarded the same American-bound train.
documents.plot:
Sin Nombre is a 2009 American drama film directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga, written by Fukunaga and Eric Warren Singer, and starring Diego Luna, Jeremy Renner, and Woody Harrelson.

The movie follows the story of Elmer Escalante (Diego Luna), a young Guatemalan migrant who is traveling north through Mexico with his cousin, Valentina (Paola Mendoza). They are part of a large group of migrants attempting to reach the United States in search of a better life. The group faces numerous challenges and dangers along the way, including corrupt border patrol agents, ruthless coyotes (human smugglers), and treacherous terrain.

As Elmer navigates this perilous journey, he meets Alejandro (Jeremy Renner), a seasoned migrant who has been traveling for years. Alejandro is initially portrayed as a tough, no-nonsense individual who is driven by a desire to reach the United States and start anew. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that Alejandro's motivations are more complex, and he is haunted by his past.

Throughout the film, Elmer forms a bond with Alejandro, who becomes a sort of mentor to him. As they face various challenges together, Elmer learns valuable lessons about resilience, courage, and the importance of human connection in the face of adversity.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alejandro's past is marked by tragedy and loss. He has been searching for his sister, who disappeared during a previous migration attempt. This personal quest drives much of Alejandro's actions throughout the film, as he hopes to find her and bring closure to his own emotional scars.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Elmer and Alejandro, as they are forced to make a difficult decision about their future. Ultimately, Elmer decides to continue on his journey, while Alejandro chooses to turn back and return to Mexico.

The movie ends with Elmer standing alone at the border, looking out at the vast expanse of the United States. He is filled with a mix of emotions - hope, fear, and uncertainty about what lies ahead. The camera lingers on his face, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of this young migrant's journey.

Throughout Sin Nombre, Fukunaga explores themes of migration, identity, and the human cost of globalization. The film offers a powerful and unflinching portrayal of the challenges faced by migrants, as well as the resilience and determination that defines them.

documents.title: Orphan
documents.tagline: There's something wrong with Esther.
documents.overview: After losing their baby, a married couple adopt 9-year old Esther, who may not be as innocent as she seems.
documents.plot:
Orphan is a 2009 American psychological horror-thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and written by Alex Mace. The movie stars Vera Farmiga, Peter Sarsgaard, and Isabelle Fuhrman.

The story begins with the adoption of Esther (Isabelle Fuhrman), an orphaned girl from Eastern Europe, by the Duncan family - Kate (Vera Farmiga) and John (Peter Sarsgaard) along with their six-year-old son Daniel. The Duncans are struggling to cope with the loss of their previous child, who died in a car accident.

Initially, Esther seems like an ideal addition to the family, but strange occurrences start to happen. She is extremely intelligent, obedient, and eerily mature for her age. As time passes, Kate begins to notice that Esther's behavior is not normal, and she starts to suspect that something is amiss.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Esther has a dark secret: she was born with a rare genetic disorder called "progeria," which causes accelerated aging. However, this condition also makes her extremely intelligent and manipulative. Esther's true intentions are slowly revealed as she begins to manipulate the Duncans, using her intelligence and charm to get what she wants.

As Kate becomes more suspicious of Esther, she starts to investigate her past, only to discover that Esther was actually a 12-year-old girl who had been abandoned by her parents in Eastern Europe. The truth about Esther's age is revealed when Daniel discovers an old photograph of Esther as a young girl, which shows her with a younger brother.

The climax of the movie takes place at a family dinner, where Kate confronts Esther about her true identity and intentions. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Esther had been planning to kill Daniel all along, using her intelligence and manipulation to make him believe she was his sister. The movie ends with Kate being killed by Esther, who then escapes.

The ending scene shows an elderly woman, believed to be Esther's mother, visiting the Duncans' home. She is revealed to be a 60-year-old woman, not the young girl Esther claimed to be. This twist suggests that Esther had been lying about her age and identity from the beginning, and that she had been manipulating the Duncans all along.

Overall, Orphan is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of identity, manipulation, and the dangers of underestimating others. The movie features strong performances from its cast, particularly Vera Farmiga and Isabelle Fuhrman, who bring depth and complexity to their characters.

documents.title: Barbershop 2: Back in Business
documents.tagline: Let your hair down
documents.overview: The continuing adventures of the barbers at Calvin's Barbershop. Gina, a stylist at the beauty shop next door, is now trying to cut in on his business. Calvin is again struggling to keep his father's shop and traditions alive--this time against urban developers looking to replace mom & pop establishments with name-brand chains. The world changes, but some things never go out of style--from current events and politics to relationships and love, you can still say anything you want at the barbershop.
documents.plot:
Barbershop 2: Back in Business is a comedy film that explores the theme of community and the importance of relationships in maintaining social cohesion. The movie delves into the lives of the characters in the barbershop, showcasing their interactions and dynamics as they navigate the challenges of everyday life.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and how it evolves over time. As the main character, Eddie, navigates his way through adulthood, he must confront his own sense of self and find a balance between his personal and professional life. This internal struggle is reflected in his relationships with those around him, particularly his friends and family.

Furthermore, the movie highlights the theme of loyalty and friendship, as the characters come together to support each other through various struggles and triumphs. The barbershop serves as a hub for social interaction, where people from different walks of life can gather, share stories, and find common ground.

Overall, Barbershop 2: Back in Business is a heartwarming film that celebrates the importance of community, relationships, and personal growth, making it a relatable and entertaining watch.

documents.title: Leroy & Stitch
documents.tagline: Here comes trouble!
documents.overview: Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, and Pleakley have finally caught all of Jumba's genetic experiments and found the one true place where each of them belongs. Stitch, Jumba and Pleakley are offered positions in the Galactic Alliance, turning them down so they can stay on Earth with Lilo, but Lilo realizes her alien friends have places where they belong – and it's finally time to say "aloha".
documents.plot:
Leroy & Stitch is a 2006 animated science fiction comedy film produced by Walt Disney Television Animation. The movie revolves around the story of Leroy, an alien who crash-lands on Earth and meets Stitch, a genetically engineered experiment designed to destroy everything in his path.

The main themes of Leroy & Stitch can be broken down into several key elements:

1. **Family and Belonging**: Throughout the film, Leroy struggles to find his place in the world and form meaningful connections with others. He eventually finds acceptance and love from Nani, a young girl who takes him under her wing, and becomes part of her ohana (family). This theme highlights the importance of finding one's family and belonging.

2. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Stitch, initially designed to cause chaos and destruction, undergoes significant character development as he learns about the value of friendship, loyalty, and compassion. His transformation serves as a metaphor for personal growth and redemption, demonstrating that individuals can change and become better versions of themselves.

3. **The Power of Love and Acceptance**: The film showcases the transformative power of love and acceptance. Nani's unwavering kindness and dedication to Leroy help him overcome his initial fears and insecurities, while Stitch's own experiences with love and acceptance lead to a profound shift in his behavior.

4. **Cultural Exchange and Understanding**: The movie celebrates the diversity of cultures and traditions, as seen through the characters' interactions and experiences. The film promotes cross-cultural understanding and appreciation, highlighting the importance of embracing differences and finding common ground.

5. **The Importance of Home and Belonging**: Leroy's journey is also a metaphor for finding one's home and sense of belonging. As he navigates his new surroundings, he comes to realize that home is not just a physical place but also a sense of connection and community.

Overall, Leroy & Stitch explores themes of family, redemption, love, acceptance, cultural exchange, and the importance of finding one's place in the world, making it a heartwarming and engaging animated film.

documents.title: All the Pretty Horses
documents.tagline: Some passions can never be tamed.
documents.overview: The year is 1949. A young Texan named John Grady finds himself without a home after his mother sells the ranch where he has spent his entire life. Lured south of the border by the romance of cowboy life and the promise of a fresh start, Cole and his pal embark on an adventure that will test their resilience, define their maturity, and change their lives forever.
documents.plot:
All the Pretty Horses is a 2000 American Western produced and directed by Billy Bob Thornton, adapted from Cormac McCarthy's 1992 novel of the same name, the first book of his Border Trilogy. Matt Damon leads a cast that includes Henry Thomas, Lucas Black, Penélope Cruz, Rubén Blades, Robert Patrick, Bruce Dern and Sam Shepard. Miramax Films released it in the United States on December 25, 2000, with Columbia Pictures distributing in other territories.

The story is set in 1949. Young Texas cowboy John Grady Cole finds himself without a home after his family's ranch is sold following his grandfather's death. Unwilling to give up the only way of life he knows, he persuades his best friend Lacey Rawlins to leave San Angelo with him and ride on horseback roughly 150 miles south across the border to look for work in Mexico. Along the trail they fall in with Jimmy Blevins, a strange, headstrong teenager riding a fine horse, but after he loses the animal in a storm and causes trouble trying to recover it, the pair part ways with him.

Cole and Rawlins find work as hands on a large hacienda, where the owner, Don Héctor, is impressed by their skill with horses. Cole falls in love with Alejandra Villarreal, the rancher's beautiful daughter, but the romance is firmly opposed by her aunt, Dueña Alfonsa, who guards the family's honor. After Alejandra is sent away, Cole and Rawlins are arrested by Mexican police and reunited with Blevins, who has been accused of horse theft and murder. The boy is executed by a corrupt police captain, and the two friends are thrown into a brutal Mexican prison as accomplices, where they must fight to stay alive. Their eventual release comes at a heavy price, and Cole is left to decide what he owes to Alejandra, to his friend and to the dead Blevins.

The production became known for a protracted dispute between Thornton and the studio over its length. Thornton's original cut ran close to four hours and was considerably shortened for theatrical release, and Daniel Lanois's score was largely replaced. The finished film was poorly received. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 32% approval rating from 100 reviews, with critics describing it as a weak adaptation of the novel and dramatically inert, and it grossed only about $18.1 million worldwide against a much larger budget.

documents.title: Merlin and the Book of Beasts
documents.original_title: Merlin and the Book of Beasts
documents.overview: In the twenty years since the fall of Camelot, Merlin has become a recluse known as "the wild man of the woods." He is now summoned by a charge of young knights as they quest to destroy an evil wizard who rules the land from a throne of a "New Camelot."
documents.plot:
Merlin and the Book of Beasts is a 2009 Canadian fantasy television film directed by Warren P. Sonoda from a screenplay by Brook Durham, made by Front Street Pictures for Syfy. Drawing loosely on Arthurian legend, it stars James Callis as the wizard Merlin and Laura Harris as Avlynn, the daughter of King Arthur and Guinevere. The film was shot in Langley and Maple Ridge, British Columbia, and premiered on American television on 30 May 2009.

Twenty years after the death of Arthur and the fall of Camelot, the castle is ruled by the sorcerer Arkadian, who draws his power from the Book of Beasts, a magical tome that unleashes monstrous creatures. Avlynn sets out with the last of the knights, among them Sir Galahad, his son Lysanor and Tristan, to find Merlin, Arthur's old counsellor, now living as a recluse in an enchanted forest and known as the wild man of the woods. Merlin at first refuses to help, but eventually joins the quest to retake Camelot, which also requires Avlynn to find Excalibur. Arkadian is revealed to be Mordred, Arthur's son by Morgan le Fay and thus Avlynn's half-brother.

Along the way Merlin is struck down, and the company carries him to a legendary healing well, only to find it dry. Galahad urges them to leave him behind, but Avlynn refuses and draws water from the well with her own blood, reviving the wizard, who then dispatches a pack of Medusa-like creatures sent by Arkadian. At the Lake of Destiny Avlynn recovers her father's sword, before the group is captured by giant birds under the sorcerer's control. Arkadian tries to seduce Avlynn by taking on the appearance of Lysanor, with whom she is in love. In the final battle Merlin strips Arkadian of his magic and binds his spirit within Camelot, while Avlynn uses Excalibur to pin the Book of Beasts to a rock, saving Merlin from being consumed by it.

The supporting cast includes Jim Thorburn as Arkadian, Jesse Moss as Lysanor, Donald Adams as Galahad and Patrick Sabongui as Tristan, with Monique Ganderton, Maja Aro, Megan Vincent and Daniel Cudmore. Produced with Starz and Magical Trail Productions, the film was later released on DVD in several countries, including Japan and Germany. Reception was poor, with an audience score of only about 15 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from more than 250 ratings.

documents.title: Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers
documents.original_title: Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers
documents.tagline: All for fun and fun for all
documents.overview: In Disney's take on the Alexander Dumas tale, Mickey Mouse, Donald Duck and Goofy want nothing more than to perform brave deeds on behalf of their queen (Minnie Mouse), but they're stymied by the head Musketeer, Pete. Pete secretly wants to get rid of the queen, so he appoints Mickey and his bumbling friends as guardians to Minnie, thinking such a maneuver will ensure his scheme's success. The score features songs based on familiar classical melodies.
documents.plot:
Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers is an American animated musical adventure of 2004 directed by Donovan Cook and produced by Walt Disney Pictures with the Australian unit of Disneytoon Studios. Loosely drawn from Alexandre Dumas's novel, it was the first feature-length film to star the three friends together. Wayne Allwine voices Mickey Mouse, Tony Anselmo Donald Duck and Bill Farmer both Goofy and Pluto, with Russi Taylor as Minnie, Tress MacNeille as Daisy, Jim Cummings as Pete, April Winchell as Clarabelle Cow and Rob Paulsen as the narrating Troubadour.

The Troubadour, a music-loving French tortoise, tells the tale from his comic book. In 17th-century France, the street urchins Mickey, Donald, Goofy and Pluto are rescued from the bullying Beagle Boys by royal musketeers, who give Mickey a hat and inspire the friends to become musketeers themselves. Years later they are merely janitors at musketeer headquarters, run by Captain Pete, who secretly plans to depose Princess Minnie and crown himself king. After the Beagle Boys, in Pete's pay, nearly assassinate her, Minnie demands musketeer bodyguards, and Pete appoints the three janitors, assuming they will be easy to dispose of.

On a carriage ride the Beagle Boys kidnap Minnie and her lady-in-waiting Daisy. Mickey and Goofy track them to a tower and defeat them while a frightened Donald hangs back, and Mickey and Minnie begin a romance. Pete then targets the heroes one by one: his lieutenant Clarabelle lures Goofy away and tries to drown him in the Seine, only to fall in love with him, while Mickey, warned by Donald of Pete's treachery, is locked in a flooding dungeon at Mont Saint-Michel. Scolded by the Troubadour for his cowardice, Donald joins Goofy and Pluto to free Mickey. At the opera, where a disguised Beagle Boy posing as Minnie proclaims Pete king, the musketeers battle the villains on stage and rescue the princess and Daisy, who declare their love for Mickey and Donald. Minnie then makes the three friends royal musketeers at last.

The songs set new comic lyrics to classical pieces and include a cover of "Three Is a Magic Number". After a limited screening at the El Capitan Theatre, the film was released on DVD and VHS on 17 August 2004, the first Disney DVD with the FastPlay feature. Reviews were mixed, praising the music and action, and it scored 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Collector
documents.tagline: He always takes one
documents.overview: Desperate to repay his debt to his ex-wife, an ex-con plots a heist at his new employer's country home, unaware that a second criminal has also targeted the property, and rigged it with a series of deadly traps.
documents.plot:
The Collector is a 2009 American thriller film directed by Marcus Nispel and starring Josh Stewart and Monica Potter.

The movie follows the story of Arkin, a man who is kidnapped by a serial killer known as "The Collector" (played by Josh Stewart). The Collector is obsessed with collecting rare and unusual items, including human specimens. As Arkin tries to escape from his captor, he discovers that The Collector's true intention is not just to collect him, but also to study and understand the human psyche.

The main themes of The Collector include:

1. Obsession: The film explores the theme of obsession, as embodied by The Collector's fixation on collecting rare items. This obsession leads him to become increasingly unhinged and violent.
2. Trauma: Arkin's past trauma is slowly revealed throughout the movie, and it becomes clear that his experiences have left him with emotional scars. The Collector's actions serve as a catalyst for Arkin's own emotional release.
3. Survival: As Arkin tries to escape from The Collector, he must also confront his own mortality and the possibility of being trapped forever. This theme is closely tied to the idea of survival, both physical and emotional.
4. Psychological manipulation: The Collector uses psychological manipulation to control Arkin, making him question his own sanity and reality. This theme highlights the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

Throughout the movie, these themes are expertly woven together to create a tense and suspenseful narrative that keeps the viewer on the edge of their seat.

documents.title: Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed in at the House of Mouse
documents.original_title: Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed in at the House of Mouse
documents.overview: When a huge snowstorm leaves everyone stranded, Mickey and all of his guests at the House of Mouse, including Pooh, Belle, Snow White, Cinderella, Ariel and many more of his old and new friends, break out the cookies and hot chocolate to help Donald mend his tattered Christmas spirit.
documents.plot:
Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed In At The House Of Mouse is a direct-to-video animated film produced by Disney Television Animation, released in 2001. The movie takes place during the holiday season and revolves around Mickey Mouse and his friends at the House of Mouse.

The story begins with Mickey Mouse excitedly preparing for Christmas at the House of Mouse. However, on Christmas Eve, a severe snowstorm hits Toontown, causing the power to go out and trapping the guests inside the restaurant. As the night progresses, the group starts to get restless, and tensions rise as they realize that they won't be able to leave.

As the hours pass, Mickey tries to keep everyone's spirits high by telling Christmas stories and singing holiday songs. However, things take a turn when Pete, who has been trying to ruin Christmas for the gang all along, reveals his true intentions: he plans to steal Santa's bag of presents meant for Toontown.

Determined to stop Pete, Mickey rallies his friends, including Minnie Mouse, Pluto, and Goofy. Together, they devise a plan to outsmart Pete and save Christmas. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and the true meaning of the holiday season.

As the night wears on, the group faces various obstacles, including a wild goose chase through the House of Mouse and a confrontation with Pete's accomplices. However, in the end, Mickey and his friends successfully thwart Pete's plans, and Christmas is saved.

The movie concludes with a heartwarming celebration of the holiday season, featuring festive music, decorations, and a special appearance by Santa Claus himself. The film ends on a high note, with Mickey and his friends enjoying a joyful Christmas Eve together, surrounded by the magic of the House of Mouse.

Throughout the movie, the characters' personalities shine through, adding to the humor and charm of the story. From Goofy's goofy antics to Pluto's loyal companionship, each character brings their unique voice to the film, making it a delightful holiday treat for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed In At The House Of Mouse is a fun, festive, and heartwarming animated film that captures the spirit of the holiday season. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and catchy music, this movie is sure to become a classic among Disney fans and families alike.

documents.title: Twitches
documents.overview: Twins separated at birth, Camryn and Alex meet by chance for the first time on their 21st birthday and discover they're witches with the power to save their homeland of Coventry from the evil that threatens it. But when Camryn leaves Alex to face the darkness alone, will Coventry be doomed? Or will the sisters multiply their magic by standing together?
documents.plot:
Twitches is an American fantasy comedy-drama of 2005 made as a Disney Channel Original Movie, directed by Stuart Gillard and written by Melissa Gould and Dan Berendsen, based on the Twitches book series by H. B. Gilmour and Randi Reisfeld. Tia and Tamera Mowry star as Alex Fielding and Camryn Barnes, twin witches separated at birth, with Kristen Wilson as their mother Miranda, Patrick Fabian as their uncle Thantos. It premiered on 14 October 2005.

In the magical realm of Coventry, the royal witch Miranda gives birth to identical twin girls on Halloween night. Named Apolla and Artemis, they wear sun and moon amulets. Their father, the powerful warlock Aron DuBaer, dies after pouring all his magic into protecting them from an evil force called the Darkness. The family friends Karsh and Ileana spirit the babies away to Earth and give them up for adoption. Apolla is raised by a wealthy couple as Camryn Barnes, while Artemis is raised by a single mother as Alex Fielding.

Alex grows up a night owl who writes stories about magical twin sisters without knowing they are true. Camryn, an early riser and passionate artist, unknowingly sketches Miranda and Coventry. On their 21st birthday, Karsh and Ileana steer Alex into the shop where Camryn is trying on clothes. Camryn is thrilled, but when she grabs the fleeing Alex's hand, a burst of energy releases their powers. The guardians reveal the sisters' origins and a prophecy that only they can defeat the Darkness and restore Coventry. Alex, whose stories all end in death, wants no part of it, but Camryn persuades her, and the two practice their magic and grow close.

Miranda, now married to Aron's brother Thantos, senses that her daughters are alive. When the Darkness reaches Alex's apartment, the twins escape to Coventry, but the overwhelmed Camryn returns to Earth for her birthday party. Alex stays and meets Thantos, who warns that Camryn is powerless alone. At the party, Camryn learns from the Darkness itself that Thantos controls it, and she escapes to Coventry as Karsh and Ileana sacrifice themselves to help her. Exposed, Thantos admits murdering Aron for wealth and power, seizes Miranda and rampages through the castle until the twins unite their magic of light and love to destroy him, restoring Coventry and reviving Miranda, Karsh and Ileana. The sisters then celebrate their birthday on Earth with their adoptive families.

Shot in Toronto in 2005, the film was followed by a sequel, Twitches Too, in 2007.

documents.title: Possession
documents.tagline: Inhuman ecstasy fulfilled.
documents.overview: A young woman left her family for an unspecified reason. The husband determines to find out the truth and starts following his wife. At first, he suspects that a man is involved. But gradually, he finds out more and more strange behaviors and bizarre incidents that indicate something more than a possessed love affair.
documents.plot:
Possession is a 1981 psychological horror drama written and directed by Andrzej Żuławski, starring Sam Neill as Mark, a spy, and Isabelle Adjani as his wife Anna, with Heinz Bennent as Anna's lover Heinrich. A French and West German co-production, it is Żuławski's only English-language feature. He wrote the screenplay in the emotional aftermath of his divorce from the actress Małgorzata Braunek and his exile from Poland, and the film was shot in West Berlin in 1980, largely near the Berlin Wall, on a budget of about 2.4 million dollars.

Mark returns home to West Berlin after a mission to find that Anna wants to separate from him and is seeing another man. He gives up their apartment and custody of their young son Bob, but after a long drinking binge he returns to find the boy neglected and decides to care for him himself. Bob's teacher, Helen, turns out to look exactly like Anna, except for her lighter hair and green eyes. Mark confronts Heinrich, an eccentric lover who easily overpowers him, but soon realizes that Anna has been seeing someone, or something, else entirely.

As the couple's encounters turn into scenes of hysterical violence and self-harm, Mark hires a private detective to follow Anna, who has been living in a derelict apartment. There the detective discovers a monstrous tentacled creature that Anna has been nurturing, and she kills him. As more people disappear, Mark is drawn into Anna's madness, killing and covering up crimes to protect her, while the creature gradually transforms, leading to an apocalyptic and deeply ambiguous ending.

The film uses horror to depict the disintegration of a marriage, with themes of jealousy, faith, chance and doubles. Adjani's frenzied performance, including a scene in which Anna suffers a violent miscarriage in the subway, is often singled out as the film's most memorable element. The creature effects were created by Carlo Rambaldi.

Possession premiered at the 34th Cannes Film Festival, where Adjani won the award for Best Actress. It received a lukewarm response on its initial release and was released in a heavily cut version in the United States. In later years the film acquired cult status and has been reappraised as a major work of art-house horror; it holds a Metacritic score of 75.

documents.title: Noroi: The Curse
documents.overview: A documentary filmmaker explores seemingly unrelated paranormal incidents connected by the legend of an ancient demon called the "kagutaba."
documents.plot:
Noroi: The Curse is a 2005 Japanese horror film directed by Kōji Shiraishi, who co-wrote the screenplay with Naoyuki Yokota, and produced by Takashige Ichise, whose earlier horror productions included Ring and Ju-On: The Grudge. Presented as a finished documentary assembled from pseudo-documentary and found footage, it stars Jin Muraki as paranormal researcher Masafumi Kobayashi, with actress Marika Matsumoto playing a fictionalized version of herself, alongside Rio Kanno, Tomono Kuga and Satoru Jitsunashi, and cameos from the comedy duo Ungirls, Dankan, Ai Iijima and author Hiroshi Aramata. Shiraishi spent about a year on research and interviews, aiming to heighten the fear by grounding the fiction in apparent reality.

The film explains that Kobayashi, known for his books and documentaries on the supernatural, vanished after his house burned down, leaving his wife dead in the ruins, while he was making a documentary called The Curse. That documentary then plays, largely through the footage of his cameraman, Miyajima. Eighteen months earlier, Kobayashi looks into complaints about the sound of crying babies from the home of a woman named Junko Ishii, who moves away soon after, leaving dead pigeons in her yard; days later her neighbor and the neighbor's daughter die in a mysterious car crash. At the same time, a psychic girl named Kana Yano, who appeared on a television variety show, disappears, and an eccentric psychic named Mitsuo Hori claims she was taken by "ectoplasmic worms". After filming at a shrine, Marika Matsumoto collapses on hearing a strange voice and begins weaving yarn and wire into interlocking loops in her sleep, and a camera records a deep voice uttering the word "kagutaba". A local historian tells Kobayashi that Kagutaba is a demon once summoned and then imprisoned by the villagers of Shimokage in Nagano Prefecture, who held an annual ritual to appease it until the village was abandoned to make way for a dam in 1978. As a string of hangings and disappearances follows, Kobayashi uncovers a link between the last ritual and Ishii, drawing him, Marika and Hori ever closer to the demon's influence.

Distributed by Xanadeux, Noroi: The Curse opened in Japan on 20 August 2005 and received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its presentation, performances, atmosphere and pacing. Despite limited distribution outside Japan it developed a following and became legally available in North America through Shudder in 2017.

documents.title: Love Don't Co$t a Thing
documents.tagline: Love Don't Co$t A Thing but it pays to be yourself.
documents.overview: High school loser (Cannon) pays a cheerleader (Milian) to pose as his girlfriend so he can be considered cool. Remake of 1987's Can't Buy Me Love, starring Patrick Dempsey.
documents.plot:
Love Don't Cost a Thing is a 2003 American romantic comedy film directed by David E. Talbert, produced by Alcon Entertainment, and written by David E. Talbert.

The movie follows the story of Derek Matthews (played by Omarion), a high school student who has just transferred to a new school in Los Angeles. Derek is initially hesitant to fit in with his new classmates but eventually befriends two girls: Deena (played by Gabrielle Union) and Nia (played by Brandy Norwood).

Deena, the popular and beautiful cheerleader, catches Derek's eye, and they start dating. However, their relationship is put to the test when Deena starts to develop feelings for her ex-boyfriend, Darius (played by Simon Baker). Meanwhile, Nia, who is initially portrayed as a nerdy and awkward student, reveals her own romantic interests in Derek.

As the story unfolds, Derek finds himself torn between his growing feelings for both Deena and Nia. He struggles to balance his relationships with these two women while navigating high school life. The movie explores themes of love, friendship, and self-discovery as Derek learns valuable lessons about loyalty, trust, and being true to oneself.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges, including peer pressure, family expectations, and personal growth. The movie features a mix of humor, drama, and romance, making it an entertaining watch for audiences.

Ultimately, Derek must make a choice between his relationships with Deena and Nia. In the end, he decides to pursue a relationship with Nia, who has been a constant source of support and encouragement throughout his high school journey.

Love Don't Cost a Thing received mixed reviews from critics but was a moderate box office success. The movie's blend of humor, romance, and coming-of-age themes resonated with audiences, particularly young viewers.

documents.title: A Prophet
documents.tagline: Escaping the prison of life.
documents.overview: Sentenced to six years in prison, Malik El Djebena is alone in the world and can neither read nor write. On his arrival at the prison, he seems younger and more brittle than the others detained there. At once he falls under the sway of a group of Corsicans who enforce their rule in the prison. As the 'missions' go by, he toughens himself and wins the confidence of the Corsican group.
documents.plot:
A Prophet is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of the human condition, particularly in the context of the French prison system. The movie delves into the struggles of its protagonist, Abel, as he navigates the harsh realities of life behind bars.

At its core, A Prophet is a story about redemption, forgiveness, and the cyclical nature of violence. Abel's journey is marked by his transformation from an innocent young man to a hardened convict, driven by a desire for survival and revenge against those who have wronged him. As he rises through the ranks of the prison hierarchy, Abel must confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of his own actions.

One of the primary themes of A Prophet is the exploration of masculinity and its relationship to violence. The film portrays a world where traditional notions of masculinity are often distorted or corrupted by the harsh realities of life in prison. Abel's character embodies this tension, as he struggles to reconcile his desire for power and respect with his own sense of vulnerability and humanity.

The movie also examines the theme of loyalty and friendship, highlighting the complex web of relationships that exists within the prison system. Abel's bond with his fellow inmates, particularly his mentor and friend, Le Fabre, serves as a source of comfort and support in an otherwise brutal environment.

Furthermore, A Prophet touches on issues of social inequality and the systemic failures that lead to the marginalization of certain groups. The film critiques the French prison system, revealing its flaws and injustices, and highlighting the need for reform and rehabilitation rather than simply punishment.

Ultimately, A Prophet is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of violence, redemption, and forgiveness in a world marked by inequality and social injustice.
production_companies: Conseil Régional de Provence-Alpes Côte d'Azur

documents.title: Cemetery Man
documents.tagline: Zombies, guns and sex, OH MY!!!
documents.overview: A cemetery man has the unusual problem of the dead rising from the grave. Himself and his assistant must end these creatures' lives again after they are reborn. Everything is going well until "She" comes along and stirs things up a bit.
documents.plot:
Cemetery Man is a 1994 Italian horror-comedy film directed by Michele Soavi. The movie follows the story of Emilio Velter, a mortician who works in a cemetery and is forced to confront his own dark past when he becomes involved with a mysterious woman.

The main theme of Cemetery Man revolves around the struggle between good and evil, as embodied by the two main characters: Emilio Velter, a well-meaning but somewhat inept mortal, and the vampire, a symbol of darkness and malevolence. The film explores the idea that even in the most mundane and ordinary-seeming lives, there can be a deep well of darkness and violence lurking beneath the surface.

The movie also delves into the theme of identity and the blurring of boundaries between reality and fantasy. Emilio Velter's character is a complex one, struggling to reconcile his mundane life as a mortician with his own desires and fantasies. The vampire, on the other hand, represents a kind of freedom and release from the constraints of society, but also poses a threat to Emilio's very existence.

Furthermore, Cemetery Man touches on the idea of the power dynamics between men and women, particularly in the context of relationships and intimacy. The mysterious woman who enters Emilio's life is a catalyst for his transformation, forcing him to confront his own desires and vulnerabilities.

Overall, Cemetery Man is a film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, delving into themes of identity, morality, and the complexities of human relationships.
production_companies: Fonds Eurimages du Conseil de l'Europe

documents.title: Batman: Mystery of the Batwoman
documents.tagline: Gotham City's newest hero... or criminal?
documents.overview: As if the Penguin wasn't enough to contend with, a new vigilante has surfaced in Gotham City, and her strong-arm tactics give Batman cause for concern.
documents.plot:
Batman: Mystery of the Batwoman is an animated film that delves into the complex and intriguing world of Bruce Wayne's psyche, exploring the blurred lines between his dual identities as a billionaire philanthropist and the masked vigilante Batman.

At its core, the movie is a thought-provoking examination of identity, loyalty, and the consequences of playing with fire. The story revolves around Barbara Gordon, aka Batgirl, who finds herself entangled in a web of deceit and corruption that threatens to destroy the very fabric of Gotham City's social hierarchy.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Bruce Wayne is not only grappling with his own demons but also struggling to maintain control over those closest to him. The film masterfully weaves together themes of obsession, possession, and the dangers of unchecked power, all while maintaining a sense of intrigue and suspense.

One of the most striking aspects of Batman: Mystery of the Batwoman is its portrayal of Barbara Gordon as a strong-willed and intelligent heroine who refuses to be defined by her circumstances. Her character serves as a powerful counterpoint to Bruce Wayne's brooding intensity, highlighting the importance of female agency and empowerment in the face of adversity.

Throughout the film, the animation is richly detailed, with a vibrant color palette that brings the dark and gritty world of Gotham City to life. The voice acting is also top-notch, with each character bringing their own unique energy to the story.

Ultimately, Batman: Mystery of the Batwoman is a gripping and thought-provoking tale that explores the complexities of human nature and the consequences of our choices. It is a must-see for fans of the Batman franchise and anyone looking for a compelling animated adventure.

documents.title: The Barbie Diaries
documents.overview: This movie stars Barbie as a teenage girl, trying to deal with crushes, rivals and friendship as she tries to achieve her dream of working as a news anchor for her school's TV station. She doesn't always make the right decisions, but she's a nice enough character and considerably less "perfect" than she is portrayed in her other films.
documents.plot:
The Nativity Story is a 2006 American drama film directed by Catherine Hardwicke, produced by New Line Cinema, and written by John Steinbeck IV.

The main themes of The Nativity Story include:

1. **Faith and Spirituality**: The film explores the spiritual journey of Mary, Joseph, and Jesus as they navigate their way to Bethlehem for the census. It highlights the importance of faith, trust, and obedience in the face of uncertainty and adversity.
2. **Love and Sacrifice**: The story showcases the selfless love and sacrifice of Mary, who is willing to give up her own desires and ambitions for the sake of her child. This theme is also reflected in Joseph's willingness to care for Jesus as a father figure.
3. **Identity and Purpose**: As Jesus grows up, he begins to question his purpose and identity. The film explores this theme through his interactions with other characters, including John the Baptist and the Pharisees, who challenge his understanding of himself and his mission.
4. **Human Connection and Community**: The Nativity Story emphasizes the importance of human connection and community in times of need. The film depicts the kindness and generosity of strangers, such as the innkeeper and the shepherds, who provide shelter and support to Mary, Joseph, and Jesus.

The film's narrative is structured around key events from the biblical account of Jesus' birth, including:

* The journey to Bethlehem
* The encounter with the innkeeper
* The visitation by the shepherds
* The birth of Jesus in a manger

Overall, The Nativity Story offers a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of faith, love, identity, and community, set against the backdrop of one of the most significant events in human history.

documents.title: Dance Flick
documents.overview: Street dancer, Thomas Uncles is from the wrong side of the tracks, but his bond with the beautiful Megan White might help the duo realize their dreams as they enter in the mother of all dance battles.
documents.plot:
Dance Flick is a 2009 musical comedy film that satirizes popular dance movies such as Save the Last Dance and Step Up. The movie follows the story of Derek, a white dancer who falls in love with a black ballerina named Lily, and their struggles to overcome racial differences and find acceptance.

The main theme of Dance Flick is the exploration of racial tensions and stereotypes in the context of dance culture. The film uses humor and satire to critique the way African American and white dancers are portrayed in popular media, highlighting the absurdity and superficiality of some dance movies. Through Derek's character, the movie also touches on issues of identity, cultural appropriation, and the complexities of interracial relationships.

The film also explores themes of class and privilege, as Derek's wealth and status create tension with Lily's more humble background. Additionally, Dance Flick pokes fun at the conventions of romantic comedies, using its lighthearted tone to comment on the ways in which love stories can be used to mask deeper social issues.

Overall, Dance Flick is a satirical comedy that uses dance as a metaphor for exploring complex social issues and stereotypes.

documents.title: Cold Prey
documents.tagline: You'll Catch Your Death.
documents.overview: When one of them breaks a leg, 5 friends snowboarding in the Norwegian mountains take shelter in a abandoned ski lodge and soon realize they’re not alone.
documents.plot:
Cold Prey is a Norwegian horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. The movie follows a group of college students who are stalked and terrorized by a mysterious figure while on a skiing trip in the mountains.

At its core, Cold Prey explores the theme of vulnerability and how it can be exploited by those who seek to harm others. The film takes a close look at the dynamics between the characters, particularly the relationships between men and women, and how these interactions can lead to feelings of isolation and disconnection.

The movie also touches on the idea of masculinity and how societal expectations can stifle individuality and creativity. The protagonist, Laila, is a strong-willed and independent character who challenges the traditional norms of femininity, while her male counterparts are often portrayed as shallow and emotionally unavailable.

Furthermore, Cold Prey critiques the notion of "buddy movies" and the way they often perpetuate toxic masculinity. The film's portrayal of the male characters' behavior towards each other is often cruel and dismissive, highlighting the dangers of toxic relationships and the importance of empathy and understanding.

Overall, Cold Prey is a thought-provoking horror film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the darker aspects of human nature.

documents.title: Drop Dead Sexy
documents.tagline: Small time crooks... Big time idiots!
documents.overview: When their money scam runs aground, a group of would-be thieves turn to kidnapping in an attempt to blackmail their target.
documents.plot:
Drop Dead Sexy is a 2005 American romantic comedy film directed by Michael Patrick Jann. The movie follows the story of a woman who wakes up one morning to find herself transformed into a seductive and alluring version of her former self, allowing her to attract men from all over.

The main theme of Drop Dead Sexy revolves around the idea of female empowerment and self-discovery. As the protagonist navigates this new reality, she must confront her own desires, insecurities, and relationships with others. The film explores the complexities of femininity, identity, and the societal expectations placed upon women.

Through its lighthearted and humorous tone, Drop Dead Sexy also touches on themes of self-acceptance, body image, and the objectification of women in society. As the protagonist learns to navigate her newfound confidence and allure, she must also confront the consequences of her actions and the impact they have on those around her.

Ultimately, Drop Dead Sexy is a film about embracing one's true self and finding happiness on one's own terms. It offers a playful and entertaining take on the challenges faced by women in modern society, making it a relatable and engaging watch for audiences.

documents.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death and Rebirth
documents.original_title: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン 劇場版 DEATH & REBIRTH シト新生
documents.tagline: When our HEARTS are melting together, I will be destroyed.
documents.overview: Originally a collection of clips from the Neon Genesis Evangelion TV series, Death was created as a precursor to the re-worked ending of the series. Rebirth was intended as that re-worked ending, but after production overruns Rebirth became only the first half of the first part of The End of Evangelion, with some minor differences.
documents.plot:
Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death and Rebirth is a 1997 Japanese animated film directed by Hideaki Anno, based on the popular anime series Neon Genesis Evangelion. The film serves as a conclusion to the series and provides closure for the characters.

The story begins with Shinji Ikari, the main protagonist, still struggling with his emotional baggage from his past experiences. He is haunted by the guilt of not being able to save his mother, Yui, who died in a catastrophic event known as the "Second Impact." Shinji's relationships with his father, Gendo Ikari, and his friends, Rei Ayanami and Asuka Langley Soryu, are also still unresolved.

The film takes place after the events of the original series, where Shinji has become increasingly isolated and withdrawn. He is visited by a mysterious figure known as "Death," who claims to be an angel from the future. Death reveals that Shinji's existence is tied to the creation of the Evangelion Unit-01, a giant humanoid robot designed to fight against other angels.

As the story unfolds, Shinji discovers that he has the ability to pilot the Evangelion Unit-02, which was created by his father as an alternative to the original unit. However, this new development only serves to further complicate Shinji's emotions and relationships with those around him.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of existentialism, psychological trauma, and the nature of humanity. The story is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between different timelines and perspectives.

Ultimately, the film culminates in a confrontation between Shinji and his father, Gendo, who reveals that he has been manipulating events from behind the scenes to bring about the Second Impact. In a final act of desperation, Shinji sacrifices himself to save humanity by destroying the Evangelion Unit-01, which is revealed to be a vessel for the angel Lilith.

In the end, it is implied that Shinji's sacrifice has created a new timeline, one in which he is no longer trapped by his emotional baggage. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as Shinji's spirit is reborn into a new existence.

Overall, Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death and Rebirth is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged conclusion to the series. It provides closure for the characters while also leaving room for interpretation and speculation about the nature of reality and the human condition.

documents.title: Deep in the Valley
documents.tagline: Where Every Fantasy Comes True
documents.overview: Best friends, Carl and Lester, find themselves magically transported into an alternate universe straight out of a real-life adult movie. Hilarity ensues as they embark upon a journey of adult-themed mayhem while Carl ultimately finds true love in the most unlikely of places.
documents.plot:
Deep in the Valley, released in the United Kingdom as American Hot Babes, is a 2009 American romantic comedy film written and directed by Christian Forte, the son of the 1950s and 1960s teen idol Fabian. It stars Chris Pratt as Lester Watts and Brendan Hines as his best friend Carl, with Scott Caan as the police officer Rod Cannon, Rachel Specter as Bambi Cummings, Christopher McDonald as "Diamond Jim", Denise Richards as Autumn Bliss, Kim Kardashian as Summa Eve, Blanca Soto as Suzi "Diablo" and Tracy Morgan as "Busta Nut".

Lester works in a liquor store, where he cheerfully sells alcohol to minors and spends whatever money he has left on his pornography collection. His best friend since the third grade, Carl, works a corporate job at the family company of his British fiancée, and when he says he wants to quit and find work elsewhere, she angrily tells him that he has no choice but to stay, making it clear that she controls every aspect of their relationship. That night, as the two friends share a beer, a delivery arrives: a vintage porn viewing booth that plays the films of the adult film mogul Diamond Jim. When they step inside, the machine transports them into a world where everyone behaves as if they are in a pornographic movie. They are soon arrested by police officers led by Rod Cannon, but they escape and are hidden from the authorities by Bambi Cummings at her sorority house, Tri-Pi. As the pair evade the police, Carl and Bambi fall in love. Eventually the friends make their way to a pool party at Diamond Jim's mansion, where Carl chooses to be sent home while Lester decides to stay behind, and it is revealed that Lester is in fact Diamond Jim's son. Back in the real world, Carl breaks up with his domineering fiancée, and Bambi is transported to him, reuniting the couple. Meanwhile, Lester takes over his father's adult entertainment empire. In a scene after the closing credits, Rod is revealed to have been transported to the real world, where he has taken over Lester's old job at the liquor store.

The film's soundtrack includes songs by Darius Holbert, Jake Keller and Bang Camaro, whose "Push, Push (Lady Lightning)" is featured.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico
documents.original_title: Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico
documents.overview: A friend of Fred's, Alejo Otero, invites the Scooby gang to Veracruz, Mexico. There they find a monster, El Chupacabra, terrorizing the town.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico is a 2003 animated film that follows the Mystery Inc. gang as they travel to Mexico to solve a mystery surrounding a legendary monster said to be terrorizing a small town.

The main themes of Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico include:

1. Friendship: The movie highlights the strong bond between the members of the Mystery Inc. gang, particularly Shaggy and Scooby, who work together to help their friends and solve the mystery.
2. Cultural Exchange: The film showcases the rich cultural heritage of Mexico, introducing American viewers to traditional Mexican music, food, and customs.
3. Teamwork: The gang must put aside their differences and work together to uncover the truth behind the monster legend, demonstrating the importance of collaboration and communication in solving problems.
4. Skepticism vs. Belief: The movie pokes fun at the idea of believing in monsters and supernatural explanations, encouraging viewers to think critically about the evidence presented.

The plot development revolves around the gang's arrival in Mexico, where they meet a local girl named Lupita who is being terrorized by a legendary monster known as El Chupacabra. As the Mystery Inc. gang investigates, they uncover a series of clues and red herrings that lead them on a wild goose chase through the town.

In the end, the gang exposes the truth behind the monster legend, revealing it to be a human culprit in disguise. The movie concludes with the gang enjoying a festive celebration, highlighting the importance of friendship, teamwork, and cultural understanding.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico is a lighthearted, entertaining film that combines humor, mystery, and adventure, making it a fun watch for both kids and adults.

documents.title: Like Mike
documents.tagline: Think like Mike, Achieve like Mike, Be Like Mike.
documents.overview: Calvin and his friends, who all live in an orphanage, find old shoes with the faded letters MJ connected to a powerline. One stormy night, they go to get the shoes when Calvin and the shoes are struck by lightning. Calvin now has unbelievable basketball powers and has the chance to play for the NBA.
documents.plot:
Like Mike is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores several themes that resonate with audiences of all ages. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of identity, self-discovery, and the transformative power of sports.

The story follows a young boy named Calvin, who discovers he has the ability to step into the shoes of his basketball idol, Michael Jordan, when he wears his lucky red sneakers. As Calvin navigates this newfound phenomenon, he must confront the challenges of being a teenager, including peer pressure, family expectations, and self-doubt.

Through Calvin's journey, the film highlights the importance of staying true to oneself while also embracing one's passions and talents. The movie showcases how sports can be a powerful catalyst for personal growth, teaching valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and the value of hard work.

Moreover, Like Mike explores the theme of family and the impact that loved ones have on our lives. Calvin's relationships with his parents and friends are put to the test as he navigates this extraordinary experience, ultimately learning to appreciate the people who matter most in his life.

The film also touches on the idea of fame and celebrity culture, as Calvin becomes an overnight sensation after his basketball skills are showcased on national television. However, instead of letting fame go to his head, Calvin remains humble and grounded, using his newfound platform to make a positive impact on those around him.

Overall, Like Mike is a feel-good movie that celebrates the power of sports, family, and self-discovery, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Blood and Bone
documents.tagline: Destroy your enemy
documents.overview: In Los Angeles, an ex-con takes the underground fighting world by storm in his quest to fulfill a promise to a dead friend.
documents.plot:
Blood and Bone is a 2009 American martial arts film directed by Ben Ramsey and written by Michael Andrews. Michael Jai White stars as Isaiah Bone, with Julian Sands, Eamonn Walker, Dante Basco, Nona Gaye, Michelle Belegrin and Bob Sapp in supporting roles. The film also features appearances by a number of well-known fighters, including Matt Mullins, Ernest "The Cat" Miller, Kimbo Slice, Maurice Smith and Gina Carano. It was released direct to DVD on 15 September 2009.

Isaiah Bone is a former marine and martial artist who has just been released from prison. He rents a room in a Los Angeles boarding house owned by Tamara, who is raising her young adopted son Jared. After watching an underground fight won by the local champion Hammerman, Bone makes a deal with a promoter named Pinball, played by Basco, to enter the fighting circuit in exchange for a share of his winnings. He wins his first bout with just two kicks, and night after night defeats every opponent he faces, earning thousands of dollars for himself and Pinball. During this time he bonds with Tamara, Jared and an elderly neighbour named Roberto.

Bone's arrival attracts the attention of James, a ruthless local crime boss played by Walker, and his girlfriend Angela, played by Gaye. Pinball explains that James framed Angela's husband Danny for a triple homicide, sending him to prison, and that she has since fallen into drug addiction. After Bone beats the undefeated Hammerman, James proposes that he face Pretty Boy Price, the champion of an international underground fighting circuit run by the arms dealer Franklin McVeigh, played by Sands. Bone privately reveals to Angela that Danny was his cellmate and friend, and that he was murdered in prison. Angela tells him that she had a son after Danny went to prison but lost custody of him, and Bone sends her to a rehabilitation clinic, promising to reunite her with her child. When James tries to force Bone into the fight by threatening the people he cares about, it becomes clear that Bone has a plan of his own.

The film follows the classic pattern of the underground fighting revenge story, with Bone's quiet sense of honour and loyalty driving the narrative and White's martial arts skills showcased in a series of brutal fight sequences.

Although it was released without a theatrical run, Blood and Bone is remembered chiefly for its fight choreography and for White's physical, charismatic lead performance, which became its main selling point.

documents.title: Bionicle: The Legend Reborn
documents.overview: Once the ruler of an entire universe, the Great Spirit Mata Nui finds himself cast out of his own body, his spirit trapped inside the fabled Mask of Life, hurtling through space. After landing on the far-away planet of Bara Magna, the mask creates a new body for Mata Nui, who unwillingly gets caught up in the furious battles of the nearly barren and dangerous planet.
documents.plot:
Bionicle: The Legend Reborn is an animated film that explores several profound themes, primarily centered around identity, self-discovery, and the struggle between light and darkness. 

The story revolves around Gali, a young Toa, who embarks on a perilous journey to reclaim her people's lost city of Metru Nui from the evil Makuta. As she navigates this treacherous world, Gali grapples with her own identity and purpose, questioning whether she is truly destined for greatness or merely a pawn in a larger game.

Throughout her quest, Gali confronts the darkness within herself and the world around her, forcing her to make difficult choices that test her courage, loyalty, and compassion. The film's narrative is replete with symbolism, as Gali's journey serves as a metaphor for the universal human experience of self-discovery and growth.

Ultimately, Bionicle: The Legend Reborn presents a powerful allegory about the importance of embracing one's true nature and finding balance within oneself, while also acknowledging the need to confront and overcome the shadows that threaten to consume us.

documents.title: Minutemen
documents.tagline: It's a short trip from zero... to hero.
documents.overview: When three high-school friends invent a time-machine, they decide to use it to go back in time and prevent other youngsters from making humiliating mistakes.
documents.plot:
Minutemen is a 2008 science fiction Disney Channel Original Movie directed by Lev L. Spiro, with a teleplay by John Killoran from a story by David Diamond and David Weissman. Jason Dolley stars as Virgil Fox, with Luke Benward, Nicholas Braun, Chelsea Staub, Steven R. McQueen and Kara Crane.

On their first day of high school, best friends Virgil, Derek and Stephanie try out different activities. When young genius Charlie disrupts football practice with a homemade rocket-powered vehicle, Virgil tries to help him, and both are publicly humiliated by the jocks. Three years on, Virgil and Charlie are outcasts, while Derek and Stephanie are popular and dating.
