Charlie designs a time machine, and with Virgil and another outcast, the engineering-minded Zeke, he builds it. On their first trip a street performer ends up keeping a winning lottery ticket meant for them.

The trio then decides to use the machine to undo classmates' humiliations, recruiting Jeannette, who has an unrequited crush on Charlie, to monitor their trips; she provides snowsuits against the freezing temperatures of the time stream. Students hail the anonymous heroes as the "Snowsuit Guys" rather than the "Minutemen" they prefer, while Vice Principal Tolkan sees them as troublemakers. Charlie, who hacked NASA's files to finish the machine, urges restraint, but Virgil uses it to save Stephanie from an injury and reveals his identity to her. At her request he helps Derek undo a loss at the state championship, rekindling those friendships while neglecting Charlie and Zeke, and when Stephanie catches Derek cheating, Virgil, now aware of his own feelings for her, hesitates to undo it. The FBI, which has been tracking them, interrogates the trio, and they split up over Virgil's selfishness. Government scientists tell Charlie that their trips have damaged space-time and created a black hole, and the three reunite to fix it. Sent back to their first day of high school, Virgil considers preventing his friendship with Charlie but learns that Charlie treasures that day and that Derek joined in the humiliation to make the team. The trio escapes the closing black hole, and back in the present nobody remembers their exploits. Virgil confronts Derek and tells Stephanie how he feels.

The film premiered on Disney Channel on January 25, 2008 and with 6.48 million viewers was the most watched program on American cable that week. Spiro received a Directors Guild of America nomination for his work.

documents.title: Shaolin Girl
documents.overview: A Shaolin-trainer young woman returns to Japan to resuscitate her grandfather's defunct martial arts school.
documents.plot:
Shaolin Girl (Shōrin Shōjo) is a 2008 Japanese martial arts sports comedy directed by Katsuyuki Motohiro, best known for the Bayside Shakedown series, from a screenplay by Seishi Togawa and Rika Togawa. Inspired by Stephen Chow's Shaolin Soccer, which it transposes to women's lacrosse, the film stars Ko Shibasaki in her first solo leading role in four years, alongside Toru Nakamura, Kitty Zhang, Takashi Okamura and Yosuke Eguchi. Chow is credited as executive producer, and Tin Kai Man and Lam Chi Chung from Shaolin Soccer appear in similar roles. It was released in Japan on April 26, 2008.

Rin Sakurazawa returns to Japan after 3,000 days of training at a Shaolin martial arts school in China, hoping to spread kung fu at home as her late grandfather wished. She finds his dojo in ruins, and her former teacher Iwai, one of her grandfather's pupils, now runs a Chinese restaurant and urges her to give up her plan. Minmin, who works at the restaurant, persuades Rin to join the women's lacrosse team at Seikan International University, where her astonishing physical ability draws the attention of Tamura, the administrator who manages the team, and Iwai becomes its coach. Left out of the starting line-up for her first match, Rin comes on after a teammate is injured but plays only for herself, and the team falls apart. A game of football with local boys teaches her the meaning of teamwork, and as she wins back her teammates and teaches them the basics of kung fu, both the team and the dojo begin to revive. The university's president, Yuichiro Oba, himself a martial arts master, has been watching her and wants to draw out her hidden power. When his men abduct Minmin, Rin comes to understand Iwai's reluctance to fight and heads to the campus for a final battle to protect her friends.

The film was shot largely around Izunokuni and elsewhere in Shizuoka Prefecture. Its score is by Yugo Kanno, and mihimaru GT performed the theme song "Giri Giri Hero". Reported to have cost over one billion yen, it grossed about 1.51 billion yen in Japan. Critical reception was harsh: critic Kiichiro Yanashita derided it, and the magazine Eiga Hiho named it the worst film of 2008 by a wide margin in its annual poll of critics and writers. It was released in Germany as Kung Fu Girl.

documents.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel
documents.original_title: Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel
documents.tagline: Three guys. One pub. Too much time on their hands.
documents.overview: Follows three social outcasts -- two geeks and a cynic -- as they attempt to navigate a time-travel conundrum in the middle of a British pub. Faris plays a girl from the future who sets the adventure in motion.
documents.plot:
Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel, stylized as FAQ About Time Travel, is a 2009 British science fiction comedy directed by Gareth Carrivick from a screenplay by Jamie Mathieson. Chris O'Dowd, Marc Wootton and Dean Lennox Kelly star as three friends who find themselves caught up in a time-travel conundrum in a pub, with Anna Faris as a mysterious woman from the future and Meredith MacNeill. It was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on 24 April 2009.

Ray, a science fiction enthusiast who has just been fired from his job as a theme park guide, spends the evening with his friends Pete, a fellow fan, and Toby, a cynical would-be ladies' man. After a trip to the cinema they settle into their local pub, where they compose a sarcastic "Letter to Hollywood" listing their complaints about bad films, written on a page torn from Toby's notebook. Ray then meets Cassie, a woman who claims to be a time traveler sent to repair "time leaks," and who warns him about the Editors, agents from the future who eliminate creative people at the peak of their careers. Ray assumes his friends have set up a prank, while they believe he has invented the encounter.

Soon Pete has a disturbing vision of a massacre in the pub involving a bearded version of himself, and the friends discover a time leak in the men's toilet that sends them half an hour into the past, where they meet earlier versions of themselves. Although Cassie claims to have repaired the leak, the anomalies multiply. The trio find themselves in a post-apocalyptic version of the pub, and Pete briefly vanishes into the leak, returning disheveled and shaken. Trying desperately to avoid paradoxes, they attend a party in the pub themed around their own future selves and meet Millie, who claims to be Cassie's mentor but is in fact an Editor sent to kill them at the moment of their greatest potential. Suspecting that their Letter to Hollywood is the source of their future fame, the friends race to protect it and escape the Editors.

Critical reception was mixed, with a 35 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Empire called it quirky and engaging, with a script that keeps viewers on the ride, while the Daily Mirror felt it resembled a stretched-out television pilot but praised it as a nicely made comedy with enough laughs.

documents.title: Thirst
documents.tagline: Lusting after sinful pleasures.
documents.overview: A respected priest volunteers for an experimental procedure that may lead to a cure for a deadly virus. He gets infected and dies, but a blood transfusion of unknown origin brings him back to life. Now, he’s torn between faith and bloodlust, and has a newfound desire for the wife of a childhood friend.
documents.plot:
Thirst (Korean: Bakjwi, literally "Bat") is a 2009 horror film written, produced and directed by Park Chan-wook, based on Émile Zola's 1867 novel Thérèse Raquin. Park had first asked Song Kang-ho to star in a vampire film as early as Joint Security Area, and developed the story with co-writer Chung Seo-kyung. A co-production of South Korea and the United States, it was the first Korean feature made with both Korean and American studio funding and distribution, from CJ Entertainment and Focus Features. It opened in South Korea on 30 April 2009.

Sang-hyun, a Catholic priest who ministers to hospital patients, volunteers for an experiment to find a vaccine against the deadly Emmanuel Virus. He is infected but recovers after a blood transfusion, and his parishioners come to believe he has healing powers. Among the new worshippers is his childhood friend Kang-woo, a sickly man who lives with his overbearing mother, Mrs. Ra, and his wife, Tae-ju. When Sang-hyun relapses, he discovers that he has become a vampire: sunlight burns him and only human blood keeps the disease at bay. Trying not to kill, he steals transfusion packs from the hospital, and he begins a passionate affair with Tae-ju. After she tells him that Kang-woo abuses her, Sang-hyun drowns his friend during a fishing trip.

The couple are haunted by visions of Kang-woo, and Mrs. Ra, drinking heavily, sinks into complete paralysis. When Tae-ju admits that Kang-woo never abused her, Sang-hyun is enraged. Distraught, she asks him to kill her, and he does, but unwilling to be alone forever, he revives her with his own blood. As a vampire, Tae-ju kills without restraint while Sang-hyun feeds only when necessary, and their conflicting ethics lead to violent clashes. When Mrs. Ra reveals their crime to Kang-woo's friends, Tae-ju murders two of them. Sang-hyun destroys his followers' faith in him by pretending to attack a girl, then drives Tae-ju and Mrs. Ra to an open field before dawn. Tae-ju tries to hide, but he thwarts every attempt, and the lovers burn to ash in the rising sun as Mrs. Ra looks on.

Song plays Sang-hyun, with Kim Ok-vin as Tae-ju, Shin Ha-kyun as Kang-woo and Kim Hae-sook as Mrs. Ra. Thirst won the Jury Prize at the 2009 Cannes Film Festival, where it competed for the Palme d'Or, and topped the South Korean box office on its opening weekend. Critics were largely positive, with 81% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Roger Ebert called Park the most successful horror director working.
production_companies: Company K Movie Asset Fund No. 1

documents.title: Inuyasha the Movie 2: The Castle Beyond the Looking Glass
documents.original_title: 犬夜叉 鏡の中の夢幻城
documents.overview: With their most formidable foe vanquished, Inuyasha and his comrades begin returning to their everyday lives. But their peace is fleeting as another adversary emerges: Kaguya, the self-proclaimed princess from the Moon of Legend, hatches a plot to plunge the world into an eternal night of the full moon. Inuyasha, Kagome, Miroku, Sango and Shippou must reunite to confront the new menace.
documents.plot:
Inuyasha the Movie 2: The Castle Beyond the Looking Glass is a fantasy adventure film based on the popular manga and anime series of the same name. 

The movie begins with Inuyasha, Kagome, Miroku, Sango, and Shippo searching for the shards of the Shikon Jewel, which have been scattered across Japan. They soon discover that Naraku has created a mirror portal to another world, where they must navigate through a mystical realm filled with illusions and puzzles.

As the group delves deeper into the castle, they encounter various obstacles and challenges that test their courage, wit, and friendship. Along the way, Inuyasha struggles with his own identity and the consequences of his actions as a half-demon.

The plot development is driven by the group's quest to retrieve the shards and close the mirror portal before it's too late. They must also confront their own personal demons and work together to overcome the challenges they face.

In the end, Inuyasha and Kagome successfully retrieve the final shard, but not without sacrifices made by some of the characters. The movie concludes with a sense of closure for the group, as they reflect on what they've learned about themselves and each other.

The main themes of the movie include:

* Friendship and camaraderie: The bonds between Inuyasha, Kagome, Miroku, Sango, and Shippo are put to the test as they work together to overcome challenges.
* Identity and self-discovery: Inuyasha's struggles with his demonic heritage serve as a metaphor for the complexities of identity and the importance of embracing one's true nature.
* Sacrifice and loyalty: The characters must make difficult choices and sacrifices in order to protect each other and achieve their goals.

Overall, Inuyasha the Movie 2: The Castle Beyond the Looking Glass is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of friendship, identity, and sacrifice.

documents.title: Scott Pilgrim vs. the World
documents.tagline: Get the hot girl. Defeat her evil exes. Hit love where it hurts.
documents.overview: As bass guitarist for a garage-rock band, Scott Pilgrim has never had trouble getting a girlfriend; usually, the problem is getting rid of them. But when Ramona Flowers skates into his heart, he finds she has the most troublesome baggage of all: an army of ex-boyfriends who will stop at nothing to eliminate him from her list of suitors.
documents.plot:
Scott Pilgrim vs. the World is a 2010 American action-comedy film directed by Edgar Wright, based on the graphic novel series of the same name by Bryan Lee O'Malley.

The movie follows Scott Pilgrim (played by Michael Cera), a young musician who plays bass guitar in a band called Sex Bob-omb with his friends Stephen Stills (Mark Webber) and Young Neil (Johnny Simmons). Scott is also in a relationship with Knives Chau (Ellen Wong), but he becomes infatuated with Ramona Flowers (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), a mysterious and charismatic girl who has a habit of "dying" and coming back to life.

As Scott tries to win Ramona's heart, he discovers that she is being pursued by seven evil exes, each representing a different aspect of her personality. To defeat these exes and win Ramona's love, Scott must defeat them in a series of musical battles, known as "dance fights."

The first ex, Matthew Patel (Satya Bhabha), is defeated with the help of Ramona's music video. The second ex, Lucas Lee (Chris Evans), is defeated by Scott using his own music video. The third ex, Todd Ingram (Brandon Routh), is a vegan bassist who uses his psychic powers to defeat Scott.

The fourth ex, Roxy Richter (Mae Whitman), is a punk rock singer who is also Ramona's friend. She is defeated with the help of Stephen Stills' music video. The fifth ex, Gideon Graves (Jason Schwartzman), is a successful musician and Ramona's current boyfriend. He is defeated by Scott using his own music video.

The sixth ex, Envy Adams (Brie Larson), is a seductive and manipulative girl who tries to win Scott over. She is defeated with the help of Young Neil's music video. The seventh and final ex, Gideon Graves, is defeated in an epic battle that involves all of Ramona's exes.

Throughout the movie, Scott also has to confront his own personal demons, including his relationship with Knives Chau and his feelings of inadequacy as a musician. In the end, Scott defeats Gideon Graves and wins Ramona's love, but not before realizing that he needs to grow up and become a better person.

The movie features a unique blend of music, action, and comedy, with a distinctive visual style and a memorable soundtrack. The film received widespread critical acclaim for its originality, energy, and performances, and has since become a cult classic among fans of the graphic novel series and action-comedy movies in general.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! The Mystery Begins
documents.tagline: The greatest mystery is how it all began.
documents.overview: Unjustly accused of staging a spooky practical joke complete with ghosts, Daphne, Velma, Fred and Shaggy are suspended from Coolsville High. To clear their names, they team up to solve the supernatural mystery…and head straight into nonstop laughs and adventure.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo! The Mystery Begins is a 2009 animated mystery comedy film that serves as a prequel to the original Scooby-Doo series. The movie follows the adventures of four teenagers, Shaggy Rogers, Fred Jones, Daphne Blake, and Velma Dinkley, who form a detective agency called Mystery Inc.

The main themes of Scooby-Doo! The Mystery Begins include:

1. Friendship: The film highlights the strong bond between the four main characters, showcasing their camaraderie, trust, and loyalty to each other.
2. Teamwork: As they work together to solve mysteries, the gang learns to rely on each other's strengths and weaknesses, demonstrating the importance of collaboration and communication in achieving success.
3. Bravery: The movie encourages viewers to face their fears and stand up for what is right, even if it means confronting the unknown or overcoming personal anxieties.
4. Mystery-solving: The film celebrates the thrill of the chase, as the gang uses their collective skills and ingenuity to unravel the mysteries they encounter.

The plot follows the gang as they travel to Coolsville, where they meet a new friend, Scooby-Doo, who becomes an integral part of their team. Together, they must solve a series of spooky mysteries that threaten the town's reputation and safety.

Throughout the movie, the characters learn valuable lessons about responsibility, empathy, and the importance of using their unique skills to make a positive impact. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic moments add to its appeal, making it an enjoyable watch for both children and adults.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! The Mystery Begins is a heartwarming and entertaining movie that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, bravery, and mystery-solving, setting the stage for the beloved franchise's enduring popularity.

documents.title: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story
documents.original_title: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story
documents.overview: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story is a movie based on the life story of world-renowned neurosurgeon Ben Carson from 1961 to 1987.
documents.plot:
Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story is a 2009 American biographical television film directed by Thomas Carter and written by John Pielmeier, based on the 1990 autobiography of the neurosurgeon Ben Carson, written with Cecil Murphey. Cuba Gooding Jr. stars as Carson, with Kimberly Elise as his mother, Sonya, and Aunjanue Ellis as his wife, Candy. Presented as a Johnson & Johnson Spotlight Presentation, it premiered on TNT on February 7, 2009.

In 1987, Dr. Ben Carson, director of pediatric neurosurgery at Johns Hopkins Hospital, travels to Ulm, West Germany, to meet Peter and Augusta Rausch, whose twin baby boys are joined at the back of the head. He believes the boys could be separated, but warns that the operation risks the lives of one or both. As Carson spends months searching for a way to perform the surgery, the film turns back to his childhood.

In Detroit in 1961, ten-year-old Ben is failing at school and taunted by classmates. His mother, Sonya, a single parent with only a third-grade education, refuses to let her sons fail. She makes Ben and his older brother, Curtis, learn their multiplication tables, limits them to two television programs a week, and requires them to read library books and write reports on them, concealing from the boys that she herself cannot read. Ben discovers a love of books, and within a year he rises from the bottom of his class to the top. As a teenager, however, he struggles with a violent temper, until an incident in which he nearly stabs a friend, whose belt buckle stops the blade. Horrified, Ben prays for forgiveness and finds in his faith the strength to master his anger.

Ben earns a scholarship to Yale University, where he meets his future wife, Candy, and goes on to study medicine. As a neurosurgery resident at Johns Hopkins, he risks his career by operating without supervision to save a dying patient and is rewarded with promotion. In 1985, while Candy suffers the loss of twins in a miscarriage, he performs a hemispherectomy on a young girl suffering from constant seizures, removing half of her brain, and her recovery brings him to public attention.

Back in Germany, Carson finally devises a plan and leads a team through a twenty-two-hour operation that successfully separates the twins, saving both boys' lives, and he faces the press afterward. Gooding was nominated for the Screen Actors Guild Award for his performance, and Carter for a Directors Guild of America Award for his direction.

documents.title: Whiteout
documents.tagline: See Your Last Breath
documents.overview: The only U.S. Marshal assigned to Antarctica, Carrie Stetko will soon leave the harsh environment behind for good – in three days, the sun will set and the Amundsen-Scott Research Station will shut down for the long winter. When a body is discovered out on the open ice, Carrie's investigation into the continent's first homicide plunges her deep into a mystery that may cost her her own life.
documents.plot:
Whiteout is a 2009 crime thriller film directed by Dominic Sena, based on the 1998 comic book series of the same name by Greg Rucka and Steve Lieber. Kate Beckinsale stars as a U.S. Marshal stationed in Antarctica, with Gabriel Macht, Columbus Short and Tom Skerritt. It was produced by Dark Castle Entertainment and distributed by Warner Bros.

In 1957, a Soviet cargo plane flying over Antarctica crashes after a gunfight breaks out aboard over a locked box in its hold. In the present day, Deputy U.S. Marshal Carrie Stetko, who took the post at the Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station two years earlier after a partner's betrayal, is preparing to leave before winter sets in and confides to the station doctor, John Fury, that she intends to resign. Days before the last flight out, a pilot named Delfy reports a body on the ice. The victim, Anton Weiss, one of three scientists searching for meteorites, was murdered with an ice axe, and an autopsy reveals stitches on a leg wound.

Stetko decides to investigate herself. Summoned to the Russian Vostok Station by Weiss's colleague Mooney, she finds him dying and is attacked by a masked man with an ice axe, injuring her hand as she escapes. With Robert Pryce, a United Nations security agent, she comes to suspect the third scientist, Rubin. At the group's search site, Stetko falls through the ice into the wreck of the Soviet plane, where they find the box opened and its canisters missing. Back at the station, Doc amputates two of Stetko's frostbitten fingers. Rubin tells her that he and his colleagues found the plane and took its cargo, but he is killed, and Stetko identifies his murderer as the biologist Russell Haden. As a fierce storm sweeps in and the base is evacuated, Haden escapes and fights Stetko and Pryce outside, until Stetko cuts his safety line and he is carried away by the wind.

Noticing that the stitches on Weiss's leg match those Doc used on her own hand, Stetko opens the wound and finds hidden uncut diamonds, the true cargo of the plane. Doc confesses that he was part of the scientists' scheme to sell them. When he says he wants to see the aurora once more, she lets him walk out into the cold to die. Stetko winters at the station with Pryce and Delfy, and later withdraws her resignation.

Released on September 11, 2009, Whiteout was panned by critics, who found it sluggish and uninspired, and it was a box-office bomb, grossing under $18 million against a $35 million budget.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)

documents.title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs
documents.original_title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs
documents.tagline: Prepare to get served.
documents.overview: Inventor Flint Lockwood creates a machine that makes clouds rain food, enabling the down-and-out citizens of Chewandswallow to feed themselves. But when the falling food reaches gargantuan proportions, Flint must scramble to avert disaster. Can he regain control of the machine and put an end to the wild weather before the town is destroyed?
documents.plot:
Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2009 by Columbia Pictures. The movie was directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, and it follows the story of Flint Lockwood, a young inventor who creates a machine that turns water into food.

The movie begins on Swallow Falls Island, where Flint (voiced by Bill Hader) lives with his mother, Linda (voiced by Anna Faris). Flint is a shy and awkward teenager who dreams of becoming a famous weatherman. However, he's constantly overshadowed by the town's eccentric weatherman, Steve the Monkey (voiced by Andy Samberg).

One day, Flint invents a machine called the FLDSMDFR (Flint Lockwood Diatonic Super Mutating Dynamic Food Replicator), which can turn water into food. The machine is initially met with excitement and curiosity, but it quickly gets out of control when it starts producing massive amounts of food that start falling from the sky.

As the town descends into chaos, Flint teams up with Sam Sparks (voiced by Anna Faris), a weather intern who's sent to Swallow Falls to cover the strange weather phenomenon. Together, they try to shut down the machine and restore order to the town.

However, things take a turn when Flint discovers that his invention has attracted the attention of the evil Chester V (voiced by Will Ferrell), a billionaire inventor who wants to use the FLDSMDFR for his own gain. Chester V is determined to capture Flint and harness the power of the machine to create an army of food-dispensing robots.

As the story unfolds, Flint and Sam must navigate through treacherous weather conditions, avoid Chester V's minions, and find a way to shut down the FLDSMDFR before it's too late. Along the way, Flint learns valuable lessons about responsibility, friendship, and following his dreams.

The movie features a talented voice cast, witty humor, and stunning animation that brings the world of Swallow Falls Island to life. The film's climax features an epic battle between Flint and Chester V, with the fate of the town hanging in the balance.

In the end, Flint is able to outsmart Chester V and shut down the FLDSMDFR, saving the town from destruction. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with Flint and Sam sharing a romantic moment as the town returns to normal.

Overall, Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs is a delightful animated film that combines humor, adventure, and heart. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and stunning animation, it's no wonder why this movie became a beloved classic among both kids and adults alike.

documents.title: Whip It
documents.tagline: Be Your Own Hero
documents.overview: In Bodeen, Texas, Land Of The Dragon, an indie-rock loving misfit finds a way of dealing with her small-town misery after she discovers a roller derby league in nearby Austin.
documents.plot:
Whip It is indeed a 2009 film directed by Drew Barrymore, and it's distributed by Dune Entertainment.

The movie follows Bliss Cavendar, a young woman who discovers her passion for roller derby while feeling suffocated by the expectations of her family and society. As she navigates this new world, Bliss must confront her own identity, independence, and the constraints placed upon her.

At its core, Whip It explores themes of self-discovery, empowerment, and the struggle for individuality in a world that often seeks to conform. The film delves into the complexities of female relationships, particularly those between mothers and daughters, as well as the challenges faced by women who refuse to be bound by societal norms.

Through Bliss's journey, Whip It also touches on the idea of finding one's true passion and purpose, even if it means challenging the status quo. The movie celebrates the spirit of rebellion and nonconformity, highlighting the importance of embracing one's uniqueness and living life on one's own terms.

Overall, Whip It is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores themes of identity, empowerment, and self-expression, making it a relatable and engaging watch for audiences.

documents.title: Law Abiding Citizen
documents.tagline: Justice at any cost.
documents.overview: A frustrated man decides to take justice into his own hands after a plea bargain sets one of his family's killers free. He targets not only the killer but also the district attorney and others involved in the deal.
documents.plot:
Law Abiding Citizen is a 2009 American vigilante action thriller film directed by F. Gary Gray and written by Kurt Wimmer. Set in Philadelphia, it stars Gerard Butler as Clyde Shelton, a man who wages war on the justice system after one of his family's killers receives a lenient plea deal, and Jamie Foxx as the prosecutor Nick Rice, with Bruce McGill, Colm Meaney, Leslie Bibb, Regina Hall, Michael Irby, Christian Stolte and Josh Stewart.

When two burglars, Rupert Ames and Clarence Darby, invade Clyde's home, Darby stabs him and rapes and murders his wife and daughter. Prosecutor Nick Rice, unwilling to risk his high conviction rate on weak evidence, ignores Clyde's pleas and lets Darby plead guilty to third-degree murder for a three-year sentence in exchange for testifying against Ames, who is sentenced to death. Ten years later, Ames's execution goes horribly wrong because the drugs have been replaced. Disguised as a police officer, Clyde paralyzes Darby with a toxin-laced trap and records himself torturing him to death. Arrested, he mails the recording to Nick's daughter and, representing himself, berates the judge who approved Darby's deal, who then denies him bail.

From his cell, Clyde trades confessions for luxuries, and when Nick misses a deadline, Darby's lawyer is found buried alive. Clyde kills his cellmate and is put in solitary confinement. A CIA contact reveals that he was once an agency specialist in unconventional assassinations. Clyde says that he is exposing the failures of the justice system, and the killings continue: the judge dies when her phone explodes, Nick's assistant and colleagues die in car bombings, and the district attorney is killed by an armed robot. Promoted to acting district attorney, Nick learns that Clyde owns a building near the prison, where he and a detective find a tunnel leading to the solitary cells, revealing that Clyde has been slipping out undetected. Clyde plants a napalm bomb beneath a City Hall emergency meeting, but it has been moved under Clyde's bed, and Clyde dies clutching his daughter's bracelet when he triggers it. Nick finally attends his daughter's cello recital.

Released on October 16, 2009, the film opened second at the box office and grossed about $127 million worldwide. Reviews were generally negative; critics praised the premise and central performances but criticized the logic, violence and moral stance, and Rotten Tomatoes gave it 26% approval.

documents.title: Saw VI
documents.tagline: The game has come full circle
documents.overview: Special Agent Strahm is dead, and Detective Hoffman has emerged as the unchallenged successor to Jigsaw's legacy. However, when the FBI draws closer to Hoffman, he is forced to set a game into motion, and Jigsaw's grand scheme is finally understood.
documents.plot:
Saw VI is a 2009 American horror film directed by Kevin Greutert and written by Patrick Melton and Marcus Nispel. The film is the sixth installment in the Saw franchise.

The story begins with Jigsaw's (Tobin Bell) latest game, where four people are chained in a room with no apparent way to escape. They soon discover that they have been chosen for their selfishness and lack of empathy, which will be punished by being forced to kill each other. The main characters include Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), a surgeon who is haunted by his past; Amanda Young (Shawnee Smith), Jigsaw's apprentice; Peter Strickland (Peter Outerbridge), a police officer who has been investigating the Jigsaw murders; and Xavier Chavez (Donnie Wahlberg), a former convict.

As the game progresses, the characters are forced to work together to survive. They soon realize that they have been brought together for a reason, which is revealed through a series of cryptic messages and clues left by Jigsaw. The group discovers that they must find a way to escape the room before time runs out, but their efforts are hindered by their own personal demons.

Throughout the film, the characters' backstories are slowly revealed, adding depth to their motivations and actions. Dr. Gordon is haunted by his past mistakes as a surgeon, while Amanda's troubled history with Jigsaw is explored. Peter's investigation into the Jigsaw murders has led him to this point, where he must confront his own morality.

As the game reaches its climax, the characters are forced to make difficult choices and confront their own mortality. In the end, only one character will survive, but not before they have been forced to confront the true nature of Jigsaw's games.

The film ends with a twist, as Amanda is revealed to be the main antagonist, having manipulated the game from the beginning. The final shot is of Amanda, who has escaped and is now on her own path of revenge against those she perceives as responsible for her past traumas.

Overall, Saw VI is a tense and suspenseful film that explores themes of morality, empathy, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the franchise continue to enjoy the series' unique blend of horror and social commentary.

documents.title: The Fourth Kind
documents.tagline: There are four kinds of alien encounters. The fourth kind is abduction.
documents.overview: Since the 1960s, a disproportionate number of the population in and around Nome, Alaska, have gone missing. Despite FBI investigations, the disappearances remain a mystery. Dr. Abigail Tyler, a psychologist, may be on the verge of blowing the unsolved cases wide open when, during the course of treating her patients, she finds evidence of alien abductions.
documents.plot:
The Fourth Kind is a 2009 science fiction horror thriller written and directed by Olatunde Osunsanmi, starring Milla Jovovich, Elias Koteas, Will Patton and Charlotte Milchard. Its title extends J. Allen Hynek's classification of close encounters, in which the fourth kind denotes alien abduction. Presented as a pseudodocumentary, it claims to dramatize true events in Nome, Alaska, and places supposed archival footage of the "real" psychologist side by side with the re-enactments. Jovovich opens the film by telling viewers that it is real and that she plays a character based on a woman named Abigail Tyler; the "real" Tyler is played by Milchard, with Osunsanmi as her interviewer.

In August 2000, psychologist Abbey Tyler is raising her two children, Ashley and Ronnie, after her husband Will's death, which she believes was a murder. Several of her patients describe the same experience of a white owl staring at them as they sleep before something tries to enter their homes. One night a patient holds his family at gunpoint, asks what the phrase "Zimabu Eter" means and kills them and himself. A tape recorder reveals that Abbey herself was apparently attacked in her home by a being speaking an unknown language, which the linguist Awolowa Odusami identifies as Sumerian. Under hypnosis, another patient, Scott, levitates above his bed while a voice orders Abbey in Sumerian to end her study, and he is left paralyzed.

Sheriff August blames Abbey and places her under guard. A police camera then records a huge saucer-shaped object above her house and people being pulled from it, and Ashley disappears, so August takes Ronnie away from her. Abbey undergoes hypnosis to contact the beings, recalls that she and Ashley were both abducted, and hears a voice calling itself "God" tell her that her daughter will never return. Abbey, her skeptical colleague Abel Campos and Odusami vanish from the footage, and she wakes in hospital with a broken neck, where August reveals that Will actually took his own life. In the closing interview, Abbey insists that Ashley is still alive.

The film premiered at Screamfest in Los Angeles on October 24, 2009, and opened in the United States and United Kingdom on November 6, earning about $49.5 million worldwide. Reviews were mostly negative, with 18% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; Roger Ebert gave it one and a half stars but praised Jovovich, and NPR likened it to a chain e-mail hoax.

documents.title: Ninja Assassin
documents.tagline: Fear not the weapon, but the hand that wields it.
documents.overview: Ninja Assassin follows Raizo, one of the deadliest assassins in the world. Taken from the streets as a child, he was transformed into a trained killer by the Ozunu Clan, a secret society whose very existence is considered a myth. But haunted by the merciless execution of his friend by the Clan, Raizo breaks free from them and vanishes. Now he waits, preparing to exact his revenge.
documents.plot:
Ninja Assassin is a 2009 action-thriller film directed by James McTeigue and written by Justin Marks. The movie stars Rain, Donnie Yen, and Scott Adkins.

The story begins with a young boy named Kai (played by Mika Nakashima), who lives in feudal Japan with his father, a samurai named Kage (played by Kazuki Kitamura). However, their peaceful life is disrupted when Kai's village is attacked by the ruthless Lord Hattori Hanzo (played by Takeshi Kitano) and his men. In an attempt to save his son, Kage sacrifices himself to protect Kai.

Years later, Kai grows up to become a deadly ninja assassin trained by Hanzo, who seeks revenge against those responsible for his father's death. As Kai navigates the treacherous world of ninjas, he begins to question his loyalty to Hanzo and the true nature of his existence as an assassin.

Kai is sent on a mission to kill a young woman named Harima (played by Yuki Morinaga), who has been accused of being a spy. However, Kai soon discovers that Harima is innocent and working for a secret organization known as the "Shadow Syndicate," which seeks to overthrow Hanzo's regime.

As Kai delves deeper into the world of espionage, he meets a mysterious woman named Mika (played by Lucy Liu), who becomes his ally in uncovering the truth about Hanzo's plans. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Hanzo and bring down the Shadow Syndicate.

Throughout the film, Kai struggles with his dual identity as both a ninja assassin and a human being. He grapples with the moral implications of his actions and the consequences of his loyalty to Hanzo. As he navigates this complex web of intrigue, Kai must confront his own demons and make a choice between his duty as an assassin and his growing sense of humanity.

The film's climax features an intense showdown between Kai and Hanzo, with Kai ultimately emerging victorious but not without scars. In the end, Kai has found a new purpose in life, one that allows him to use his skills for good rather than evil. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Kai may have finally found redemption and a chance to forge a new path.

Overall, Ninja Assassin is an action-packed thrill ride with stunning martial arts sequences and a gripping storyline. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has developed a loyal fan base over the years, thanks in part to its unique blend of Eastern and Western influences.

documents.title: Evangelion: 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance
documents.original_title: ヱヴァンゲリヲン新劇場版：破
documents.tagline: In the War Between Heaven and Earth, Salvation is Machine.
documents.overview: Under constant attack by monstrous creatures called Angels that seek to eradicate humankind, U.N. Special Agency NERV introduces two new EVA pilots to help defend the city of Tokyo-3: the mysterious Makinami Mari Illustrous and the intense Asuka Langley Shikinami. Meanwhile, Gendo Ikari and SEELE proceed with a secret project that involves both Rei and Shinji.
documents.plot:
Evangelion: 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance is a 2009 anime film directed by Hideaki Anno, produced by Studio Khara, and written by Masahiro Takuma. The movie serves as the second installment of the Neon Genesis Evangelion Rebuild series, which reimagines the original 1995 anime series.

The story takes place two years after the events of the first film, Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone. Shinji Ikari, the protagonist, is still struggling with his emotional baggage and feelings of inadequacy. He is now a member of NERV's Special Operations Division, where he works alongside Asuka Langley Soryu, a skilled but troubled pilot.

The plot revolves around the appearance of a new Evangelion unit, Unit-02, which is designed to be more powerful than its predecessor. However, during its first test flight, Unit-02 malfunctions and crashes into the city, causing widespread destruction. Shinji is tasked with piloting Unit-01, but he struggles to cope with the pressure and his own emotional demons.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Unit-02's malfunction was not an accident, but rather a deliberate act of sabotage. The true intentions behind this event are slowly revealed, and Shinji discovers that he is not alone in his struggles. Asuka, who has her own share of emotional issues, begins to open up to Shinji, and their bond grows stronger.

Meanwhile, the enigmatic leader of NERV, Gendo Ikari, continues to manipulate events from behind the scenes. His true motives for creating the Evangelion project are slowly revealed, and it becomes clear that he is willing to sacrifice anyone who gets in his way.

The climax of the film takes place at a concert event where Shinji and Asuka confront their inner demons and face off against Gendo's sinister plans. The movie culminates in a dramatic showdown between Shinji and Unit-02, which ultimately leads to a tragic confrontation with Gendo.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of existentialism, psychological trauma, and the consequences of playing god. The animation is stunning, with intricate details and a blend of traditional and computer-generated imagery. The soundtrack, composed by Shirō Sagisu, is equally impressive, featuring haunting melodies that perfectly capture the mood and atmosphere of each scene.

Overall, Evangelion: 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that delves deeper into the complexities of Shinji's character and the world of Evangelion. While it may not be as accessible to new viewers as the original series, fans of the franchise will appreciate the nuanced storytelling and stunning animation.

documents.title: Superman/Batman: Public Enemies
documents.tagline: No one is above the law.
documents.overview: United States President Lex Luthor uses the oncoming trajectory of a Kryptonite meteor to frame Superman and declare a $1 billion bounty on the heads of the Man of Steel and his ‘partner in crime’, Batman. Heroes and villains alike launch a relentless pursuit of Superman and Batman, who must unite—and recruit help—to try and stave off the action-packed onslaught, stop the meteor Luthors plot.
documents.plot:
Superman/Batman: Public Enemies is a 2009 animated superhero film based on the comic book series of the same name by DC Comics. The movie follows the story of Superman and Batman as they team up to take down a corrupt politician, Lex Luthor, who has been elected President of the United States.

The main themes of Superman/Batman: Public Enemies include:

1. **The Dangers of Unchecked Power**: The film highlights the dangers of unchecked power and corruption in government. Lex Luthor's rise to power is facilitated by his ability to manipulate public opinion and use propaganda to sway voters.
2. **The Importance of Accountability**: The movie emphasizes the importance of holding those in power accountable for their actions. Superman and Batman must work together to stop Lex Luthor, who has become a threat to national security and the rule of law.
3. **The Tension between Heroism and Politics**: The film explores the tension between heroism and politics, as Superman and Batman struggle with how to balance their desire to protect the public with the need to respect the democratic process.
4. **The Power of Friendship and Partnership**: The movie showcases the strength of the partnership between Superman and Batman, who put aside their differences to work together towards a common goal.

Overall, Superman/Batman: Public Enemies is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of power, accountability, and the importance of working together to protect the greater good.

documents.title: The Blind Side
documents.tagline: Based on the extraordinary true story
documents.overview: The story of Michael Oher, a homeless and traumatized boy who became an All American football player and first round NFL draft pick with the help of a caring woman and her family.
documents.plot:
The Blind Side is a biographical sports drama film directed by John Lee Hancock, released in 2009 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie is based on the life of Michael Oher, an American football player who was adopted by a wealthy family.

The story begins with Michael Oher (played by Quinton Aaron), a homeless and traumatized teenager living in Memphis, Tennessee. He is forced to live in foster care after his mother's death due to HIV/AIDS. Despite his difficult circumstances, Michael shows exceptional athletic talent, particularly in football.

Enter the Tuohy family - Sean (Tim McGraw), Leigh Anne (Sandra Bullock), and their two children, S.J. (Jae Head) and Collin (Taylor John Smith). The family is wealthy and influential, but they are also kind-hearted and open to helping those in need. When Michael's foster care case comes up for review, the Tuohys decide to take him in.

Initially, Michael struggles to adjust to his new life with the Tuohys. He faces cultural and social challenges as an outsider in their affluent household. However, Leigh Anne, a devoted mother, takes it upon herself to help Michael overcome his emotional scars and develop into a confident individual.

As Michael settles into his new home, he begins to flourish under the Tuohys' care. Sean, a successful businessman, becomes a mentor to Michael, teaching him valuable life lessons about responsibility and hard work. Meanwhile, Leigh Anne forms a close bond with Michael, helping him to heal from his traumatic past.

Throughout the movie, Michael's football talent is showcased, as he joins the Briarcrest Christian School team under Coach Cotton (Ray McKinnon). With the Tuohys' support, Michael becomes an exceptional player, earning college scholarships and eventually being drafted by the Baltimore Ravens in 2009.

The Blind Side explores themes of family, love, and redemption. The movie highlights the transformative power of the Tuohy family's kindness and generosity towards Michael Oher, who was once a lost soul. As Michael navigates his new life, he finds solace in the Tuohys' unwavering support and guidance.

The film culminates with Michael's successful NFL career, as well as his adoption by the Tuohy family. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, showcasing the strong bond between Michael and the Tuohys, who have become like a second family to him.

Overall, The Blind Side is an inspiring true story of hope, resilience, and the impact one family can have on another's life.

documents.title: It's Complicated
documents.tagline: First comes marriage. Then comes divorce. And then...
documents.overview: Ten years after their divorce, Jane and Jake Adler unite for their son's college graduation and unexpectedly end up sleeping together. But Jake is married, and Jane is embarking on a new romance with her architect. Now, she has to sort out her life—just when she thought she had it all figured out.
documents.plot:
It's Complicated is a 2009 romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of relationships, identity, and personal growth. The movie delves into the theme of women navigating their lives after a divorce, particularly in regards to their careers, friendships, and romantic connections.

The main character, Jane Adler, played by Meryl Streep, is a successful architect who has built a life around her marriage and family. However, as she navigates her post-divorce reality, she must confront the choices she made and the person she has become. The film showcases Jane's journey of self-discovery, as she rekindles an old flame with her ex-husband's business partner, Adam, while also reconnecting with her daughter.

Throughout the movie, the theme of complicated relationships is woven throughout. The characters' pasts and present interactions are intertwined, revealing a web of emotions, desires, and unresolved issues. The film expertly portrays how people can be both hurtful and loving towards one another, often simultaneously.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and how it evolves over time. Jane's character is a prime example of this, as she struggles to reconcile her past and present selves. Her relationships with others serve as a catalyst for her growth, forcing her to confront her own desires, fears, and limitations.

Ultimately, It's Complicated presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, highlighting the complexities and intricacies of relationships, personal growth, and self-discovery. The film encourages viewers to reflect on their own lives, acknowledging that relationships are multifaceted and often messy, but ultimately worth navigating.

documents.title: Takers
documents.tagline: Who's Taking Who?
documents.overview: A seasoned team of bank robbers, including Gordon Jennings, John Rahway, A.J., and brothers Jake and Jesse Attica successfully complete their latest heist and lead a life of luxury while planning their next job. When Ghost, a former member of their team, is released from prison he convinces the group to strike an armored car carrying $20 million. As the "Takers" carefully plot out their strategy and draw nearer to exacting the grand heist, a reckless police officer inches closer to apprehending the criminals.
documents.plot:
Takers is a 2010 American heist action thriller film directed by John Luessenhop, who co-wrote it with Peter Allen, Gabriel Casseus and Avery Duff. It stars Idris Elba as Gordon Cozier, leader of a crew of professional bank robbers, Paul Walker as John Rahway, Michael Ealy and Chris Brown as the brothers Jake and Jesse Attica, Hayden Christensen as A.J., Tip "T.I." Harris as their former partner Ghost, and Matt Dillon and Jay Hernandez as the detectives Jack Welles and Eddie Hatcher.

Welles and Hatcher are investigating a daring bank robbery by Gordon's well-organized crew. Ghost, once a member, was caught during a robbery five years earlier; in his absence, Jake has become engaged to Ghost's former girlfriend, Lilli. Released from prison, Ghost reconnects with the crew and proposes a major job: in five days, $25 million will be moved in a convoy of two armored trucks. Disguised as construction workers, the robbers plan to blow a hole beneath the street and drop the trucks into the ground, with Ghost posing as a police officer and John covering him with a sniper rifle in case of a setup. When a cyclist forces the lead truck to stop short, the charges go off early, and a gunfight breaks out with the guards before John rams the lead truck into the crater. The crew bag the cash and escape through sewer tunnels connected to the subway. Deducing their route, the detectives corner Jesse in a station, and he shoots Hatcher, who dies as Welles stops to help him.

The crew regroups at a hotel, unaware that Ghost had made the same deal with a Russian gang and double-crossed it by striking early. Ghost tells the Russians where the crew is hiding and slips out a window before they attack. A.J. sacrifices himself, and the others kill the gangsters and flee. Jake and Jesse return home to find Lilli dead and their money gone, and they die charging out at the police who surround their bar. Ghost kills the crew's fence, Scott, on his private plane and takes their laundered money, but he is confronted by Gordon and Welles and wounds them both before John shoots him dead. Sparing Welles, who calls for help, John and the wounded Gordon drive off with the money and Gordon's sister, Naomi.

The film opened at number one at the U.S. box office with about $20.5 million. Critics were largely negative, with 28% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 45; reviewers found its set pieces gripping but its characters two-dimensional and its plot derivative.

documents.title: Up in the Air
documents.tagline: The story of a man ready to make a connection.
documents.overview: Corporate downsizing expert Ryan Bingham spends his life in planes, airports, and hotels, but just as he’s about to reach a milestone of ten million frequent flyer miles, he meets a woman who causes him to rethink his transient life.
documents.plot:
Up in the Air is a 2009 American comedy-drama film directed by Jason Reitman, produced by Gary Goetzman and Steven Haft, and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

The main themes of Up in the Air revolve around:

1. **Existentialism and Meaning**: The protagonist, Ryan Bingham (played by George Clooney), is a corporate downsizer who travels the country firing people for a living. As he navigates his job and personal life, he begins to question the meaning of his existence and the purpose of his actions.

2. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Ryan's character is portrayed as a loner, who has given up on relationships and intimacy. His interactions with others are often superficial, and he struggles to form genuine connections with people.

3. **The American Dream**: The film critiques the idea of the American Dream, which promises success, happiness, and fulfillment through hard work and material possessions. Ryan's character is a product of this system, but he begins to realize that it may not be as fulfilling as he thought.

4. **Mortality and Impermanence**: As Ryan travels from city to city, he encounters people who are facing their own mortality, whether due to illness, job loss, or personal struggles. This theme serves as a reminder of the impermanence of life and the importance of living in the present.

5. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Through his relationships with Natalie (played by Vera Farmiga) and Alex (played by Anna Kendrick), Ryan begins to develop empathy and understanding for others, which challenges his initial cynicism and loneliness.

The film's themes are expertly woven throughout the narrative, creating a complex and thought-provoking story that explores the human condition.

documents.title: Old Dogs
documents.tagline: Sit. Stay. Play Dad.
documents.overview: Charlie and Dan have been best friends and business partners for thirty years; their Manhattan public relations firm is on the verge of a huge business deal with a Japanese company. With two weeks to sew up the contract, Dan gets a surprise: a woman he married on a drunken impulse nearly nine years before (annulled the next day) shows up to tell him he's the father of her twins, now seven, and she'll be in jail for 14 days for a political protest. Dan volunteers to keep the tykes, although he's up tight and clueless. With Charlie's help is there any way they can be dad and uncle, meet the kids' expectations, and still land the account?
documents.plot:
Old Dogs is a 2009 American comedy film directed by Jake Kasdan and produced by Walt Disney Pictures.

The movie follows two friends, John (Robin Williams) and Charlie (John Travolta), who are high school sweethearts now in their 40s. They have been inseparable since childhood but have drifted apart over the years due to life's responsibilities. When they're forced to take care of a young girl, Emily (Bella Thorne), John and Charlie embark on an adventure to prove that they still have what it takes to be cool.

The main themes of Old Dogs include:

1. Friendship: The movie highlights the importance of male friendships and how they can withstand time and life's challenges.
2. Redemption: John and Charlie try to redeem themselves by proving their worth as friends and fathers, showcasing that age is just a number.
3. Nostalgia: The film takes the audience on a trip down memory lane, revisiting the carefree days of childhood and the importance of holding onto those memories.
4. Family: As John and Charlie take care of Emily, they learn to put their differences aside and work together as a team, demonstrating that family is not just about blood ties but also about the people you choose to be with.

The movie features plenty of humor, heartwarming moments, and entertaining performances from its lead actors.

documents.title: Invictus
documents.tagline: His people needed a leader. He gave them a champion.
documents.overview: Newly elected President Nelson Mandela knows his nation remains racially and economically divided in the wake of apartheid. Believing he can bring his people together through the universal language of sport, Mandela rallies South Africa's rugby team as they make their historic run to the 1995 Rugby World Cup Championship match.
documents.plot:
Invictus is a 2009 historical sports drama film directed by Clint Eastwood. The movie tells the story of Nelson Mandela's efforts to unite South Africa through the sport of rugby during the country's transition from apartheid to democracy.

At its core, Invictus explores themes of hope, redemption, and the power of sports to bring people together in times of conflict and division. The film delves into the complexities of South African history, highlighting the struggles of the black majority under apartheid and Mandela's courageous fight against racial segregation.

Through the character of Francois Pienaar, a white rugby player who becomes the captain of the South African team, the movie examines the challenges of reconciling past injustices with present-day unity. The film also explores the complexities of identity, as Pienaar grapples with his own heritage and loyalties in the face of apartheid's legacy.

Ultimately, Invictus is a story about the human spirit's capacity for resilience, forgiveness, and transformation. As Mandela says to Pienaar, "Invictus means 'unconquered' – it's not about being unbeaten, but about never giving up." The film's themes of hope, redemption, and unity serve as a powerful reminder that even in the darkest of times, there is always the possibility for healing, forgiveness, and a brighter future.

documents.title: The Cabin in the Woods
documents.tagline: You think you know the story.
documents.overview: Five friends go for a break at a remote cabin, where they get more than they bargained for, discovering the truth behind the cabin in the woods.
documents.plot:
The Cabin in the Woods is a 2012 American horror film directed by Drew Goddard and produced by Lionsgate. The movie takes place in a remote cabin in the woods, where five college students go to spend their spring break.

The story begins with Dana Polk (Kristen Connolly), Jules Louden (Frances O'Connor), Curt Vaughan (Chris Hemsworth), Holden McCrea (Jesse Williams), and Marty Mikalski (Richard Jenkins) - who is actually an older man, not a college student - arriving at the cabin. They are all excited to spend their break together, but things take a dark turn when they discover that the cabin has a mind of its own.

As the group settles in, they begin to experience strange occurrences and supernatural events, which seem to be connected to an ancient ritual. The group soon realizes that they are part of a larger experiment, designed by a secret organization known as the Order of the Garter.

The Order, led by Gary Sitterson (Bradley Whitford) and Wendy Linowski (Amy Acker), has been manipulating the students' actions from behind the scenes. They have set up a complex system to control the group's behavior, using a combination of psychological manipulation, technology, and supernatural forces.

As the night wears on, the group is forced to participate in the ritual, which involves sacrificing one of their own to an ancient deity known as the "Tribal Elder." The students are unaware that they are part of a larger experiment, designed to appease the deity and ensure the continuation of human life.

Throughout the movie, the characters' actions are influenced by the Order's manipulation. However, as the night progresses, the group begins to realize what is happening and starts to fight back against their captors. The movie takes a dark and unexpected turn when Marty, who is actually an older man with a hidden agenda, reveals his true intentions.

In the end, the group manages to subvert the Order's plan and sacrifice themselves to the deity, but not in the way that was expected. Instead of sacrificing one of their own, they use the ritual to destroy the cabin and kill the Order members. The movie ends with a twist: Marty is revealed to be an older man who has been manipulating the group all along, and he is actually the one who has been controlling the experiment.

The Cabin in the Woods is a clever subversion of traditional horror movie tropes, using humor, satire, and social commentary to critique the genre. The movie's twist ending adds a layer of complexity to the story, making it a thought-provoking and entertaining watch.

documents.title: Dear John
documents.tagline: Love brought them together. Will fate tear them apart?
documents.overview: While Sergeant John Tyree is home on two weeks leave from Germany, he meets Savannah after he dives into the ocean to retrieve Savannah's purse that had fallen off a pier. John eventually falls in love with Savannah, who promises to write to him until he returns from overseas.
documents.plot:
Dear John is a 2010 American romantic drama film directed by Lasse Hallström and starring Channing Tatum and Amanda Seyfried.

The movie follows the story of John Tyree, a U.S. Army soldier who falls in love with Savannah Lynn Curtis, a college student, while on leave during his deployment to Iraq. The two share a whirlwind romance, but their relationship is put to the test when John is deployed again, and Savannah must navigate her feelings for him from afar.

The main themes of Dear John include:

1. Love vs. Duty: The film explores the conflict between following one's heart and fulfilling one's duty. John is torn between his love for Savannah and his commitment to serving his country.
2. Long-distance relationships: The movie highlights the challenges of maintaining a relationship when physical distance separates the partners. John and Savannah must navigate the difficulties of communication, trust, and intimacy despite being apart.
3. Sacrifice and loyalty: As John prepares to deploy again, he is forced to confront the reality of his situation and make sacrifices for the sake of his country. This theme is echoed in Savannah's own struggles with her feelings for John and her desire to support him.
4. Coming-of-age: The film can also be seen as a coming-of-age story for both John and Savannah, as they navigate their first loves, independence, and adulthood.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $215 million worldwide. Despite its flaws, Dear John remains a romantic drama that explores the complexities of love, duty, and sacrifice in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Green Zone
documents.tagline: Chief Warrant Officer Roy Miller is done following orders
documents.overview: During the U.S.-led occupation of Baghdad in 2003, Chief Warrant Officer Roy Miller and his team of Army inspectors are dispatched to find weapons of mass destruction believed to be stockpiled in the Iraqi desert. Rocketing from one booby-trapped and treacherous site to the next, the men search for deadly chemical agents but stumble instead upon an elaborate cover-up that threatens to invert the purpose of their mission.
documents.plot:
Green Zone is a 2010 American war drama film directed by Paul Greengrass, starring Matt Damon as Chief Warrant Officer Roy Eberhardt, a U.S. Army Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) expert.

The main themes of Green Zone include:

1. **Deception and Corruption**: The movie explores the theme of deception and corruption in the context of war and politics. The protagonist, Roy Eberhardt, uncovers evidence that suggests the Bush administration knew about the existence of WMDs in Iraq but chose to ignore it or cover it up.

2. **Power and Politics**: The film delves into the world of power and politics, highlighting the complexities and moral ambiguities involved in decision-making during wartime. Eberhardt's investigation puts him at odds with his superiors and forces him to confront the consequences of his actions.

3. **Identity and Loyalty**: Throughout the movie, Eberhardt struggles with his own identity and loyalty. As a soldier, he is sworn to follow orders, but as an individual, he begins to question the morality of the war and the actions of those in power.

4. **War's Human Cost**: Green Zone humanizes the effects of war on individuals and communities. The film portrays the devastating consequences of conflict on innocent civilians and the moral toll it takes on those who fight in it.

5. **Government Secrecy and Accountability**: The movie critiques government secrecy and accountability, particularly in the context of wartime decision-making. Eberhardt's investigation exposes a web of deceit and corruption that raises questions about the responsibility of those in power to inform the public.

Overall, Green Zone is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and moral dilemmas, challenging viewers to consider the human cost of war and the importance of accountability in government decision-making.

documents.title: Tooth Fairy
documents.tagline: You can't handle the tooth.
documents.overview: When minor-league hockey player Derek Thompson -- who has a penchant for knocking out his opponents' teeth every time he plays -- disillusions a fan, he is sentenced to a stint for one week as a bona fide, tutu-clad, real-life tooth fairy. Soon, Derek is inspired to rekindle his youthful dreams.
documents.plot:
Tooth Fairy is a family comedy film released in 2010, directed by Tom Shadyac and starring Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, Ashley Judd, and Regan Mitchell.

The movie begins with Derek Thompson (Johnson), a former hockey player who has lost his way in life. He's now working as an airport security guard, but he's unhappy with his job and feels unfulfilled. On Christmas Eve, Derek is involved in a car accident that kills the mother of his young daughter, Maggie (Regan Mitchell).

Feeling guilty and responsible for her mother's death, Derek decides to take care of Maggie on his own. However, he soon realizes that taking care of a child is not as easy as he thought it would be. Maggie's father, Mike (Jon Heder), is nowhere to be found, and Derek must navigate the challenges of single parenthood.

As part of the tradition of exchanging gifts for teeth under their pillow on Christmas Eve, Maggie loses her first tooth, which leads to a series of events that changes Derek's life forever. He discovers that he has the ability to fly by using his "fairy dust," a magical substance that allows him to leave gifts and collect teeth.

As Derek navigates his new role as a single father, he also starts to develop feelings for his colleague, Wendy (Ashley Judd). However, their relationship is complicated, and they must navigate their differences in order to be together.

Throughout the movie, Derek's character undergoes significant development. He learns to let go of his past and find a new sense of purpose as a single father. With the help of Maggie and his fairy dust, he discovers that being a good parent is not just about providing for your child's physical needs but also about being there for them emotionally.

The movie ends with Derek and Wendy finally getting together, and Derek finding a way to balance his life as a single father with his relationship. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, with Derek and Maggie flying off into the sky, ready for their next adventure together.

Overall, Tooth Fairy is a lighthearted and entertaining movie that explores themes of family, love, and redemption. With its blend of humor, action, and heart, it's a fun and engaging film that's suitable for both children and adults.

documents.title: Season of the Witch
documents.tagline: Not all souls can be saved.
documents.overview: A 14th century Crusader returns with his comrade to a homeland devastated by the Black Plague. The Church commands the two knights to transport a witch to a remote abbey, where monks will perform a ritual in hopes of ending the pestilence.
documents.plot:
Season of the Witch is a 2011 American supernatural action-adventure film directed by Dominic Sena and written by Bragi Schut, starring Nicolas Cage and Ron Perlman, with Claire Foy, Stephen Campbell Moore and Christopher Lee. It reunited Sena and Cage after Gone in 60 Seconds. Schut's spec script was purchased in 2000 and passed between several studios before being produced by Relativity Media, with filming mainly in Austria, Hungary and Croatia.

In 13th-century Villach, a priest condemns three women as witches; after their execution, one of them rises in demonic form and kills him. A century later, the Teutonic Knights Behmen von Bleibruck and Felson fight for years in the Crusades, until Behmen is horrified to find he has killed women and children during the capture of Smyrna. The two friends desert and return to Europe, which has been ravaged by the Black Death. In Styria, Behmen's crest exposes them as deserters, and they are brought before the dying Cardinal D'Ambroise, who asks them to escort a young woman accused of causing the plague through witchcraft to a remote monastery, where monks can perform a ritual to destroy her power.

The knights agree on condition that the girl, Anna, receives a fair trial and that the charges against them are dropped. They are joined by the priest Debelzaq, the knight Johann, the young altar boy Kay and Hagamar, a swindler serving as guide. The journey is plagued by strange events. Johann is killed after Anna escapes and he is lured by visions of his dead daughter, Anna rescues Kay with unnatural strength on a crumbling bridge, and wolves seem to answer her call and kill Hagamar.

At the monastery, they find that all the monks have died of the plague. As Debelzaq reads the ritual against witches from the Book of Solomon, Anna speaks in a demonic voice of Behmen's past, and they realize that she is not a witch but is possessed by a demon seeking to destroy the book. The demon escapes, raises the dead monks against the men and kills Debelzaq and Felson. Behmen is mortally wounded fighting it while Kay completes the exorcism, freeing Anna. Behmen asks Kay to protect her, and after burying their friends, Kay and Anna leave together with the book.

Released on January 7, 2011, the film was panned by critics, who found it ponderous and silly, though some enjoyed it as B-movie schlock. Cage received a Golden Raspberry Award nomination for Worst Actor.

documents.title: Hot Tub Time Machine
documents.tagline: Kick some serious past!
documents.overview: Four pals are stuck in a rut in adulthood: Adam has just been dumped, Lou is a hopeless party animal, Craig is a henpecked husband, and Jacob does nothing but play video games in his basement. But they get a chance to brighten their future by changing their past after a night of heavy drinking in a ski-resort hot tub results in their waking up in 1986.
documents.plot:
Hot Tub Time Machine is a 2010 American science fiction comedy film directed by Steve Pink and written by Josh Heald, Sean Anders, and John Morris. The movie stars John Cusack, Craig Robinson, Rob Corddry, Clark Duke, and Chevy Chase.

The main themes of Hot Tub Time Machine revolve around friendship, nostalgia, and the consequences of one's actions. Here's a brief overview:

Beginning: The film follows four friends - Adam (John Cusack), Lou (Rob Corddry), Nick (Craig Robinson), and Jacob (Clark Duke) - who have lost touch over the years due to their individual successes and failures. They reunite for a bachelor party in Las Vegas, where they stumble upon an old hot tub that transports them back to 1986.

Plot Development: As they travel through time, the friends experience different versions of themselves from various points in their lives. They witness how their choices and decisions have led to their current situations, including Adam's failed marriage, Lou's unfulfilling job, Nick's lack of direction, and Jacob's immaturity. Through these experiences, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and the importance of living in the present.

Ending: The film concludes with the friends returning to 2010, but not before they make a pact to stay connected and support each other. Adam realizes that he needs to re-evaluate his life and prioritize his relationships, while Lou finds a new sense of purpose. Nick and Jacob also learn to take responsibility for their actions and become more mature individuals.

Throughout the movie, Hot Tub Time Machine explores themes such as:

* The power of friendship: The film highlights the importance of maintaining strong bonds with others, especially during times of change and uncertainty.
* Nostalgia vs. progress: The movie pokes fun at the idea that nostalgia can be both comforting and limiting. The friends must confront their past mistakes and learn to move forward.
* Personal growth: As the characters navigate different versions of themselves, they gain insight into their own strengths and weaknesses, leading to a greater understanding of who they are and what they want out of life.

Overall, Hot Tub Time Machine is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and science fiction elements to explore deeper themes about friendship, personal growth, and the importance of living in the present.

documents.title: My Life in Ruins
documents.tagline: The most fun you can have without a passport.
documents.overview: A Greek tour guide named Georgia attempts to recapture her kefi (Greek for mojo) by guiding a ragtag group of tourists around Greece and showing them the beauty of her native land. Along the way, she manages to open their eyes to the wonders of an exotic foreign land while beginning to see the world through a new set of eyes in the process.
documents.plot:
My Life in Ruins is a 2009 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of love, family, and self-discovery. The movie follows the story of Rachel White, a young woman who returns to her hometown on the Greek island of Santorini after her mother's passing, only to find herself entangled in a web of relationships and emotions.

At its core, My Life in Ruins is a film about the power of love and connection. The movie delves into the complexities of human relationships, showcasing how people can both hurt and heal each other. Through Rachel's journey, the film highlights the importance of embracing vulnerability and taking risks in order to truly experience life.

The movie also explores themes of identity and self-discovery, as Rachel navigates her way through a series of unexpected encounters and experiences. As she confronts her past and present, Rachel begins to uncover new aspects of herself and her place in the world.

Furthermore, My Life in Ruins touches on the idea of family and legacy, highlighting the ways in which our relationships with others shape us and define us. The film shows how even the most well-intentioned actions can have unintended consequences, and how it's never too late to make amends and start anew.

Overall, My Life in Ruins is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores the complexities of human emotions and relationships, ultimately revealing the transformative power of love and connection.

documents.title: Pinocchio 3000
documents.overview: This is the story of a little robot known as Pinocchio 3000 whose greatest wish is to become a real boy. The year is 3000. Geppetto, with the help of his faithful assistant, Spencer the cyber penguin, and by the holographic fairy Cyberina, creates Pinocchio, a prototype superrobot equipped for emotions. But before he can be given a heart and become a real boy, Cyberina insists that Pinocchio learn the difference between right and wrong.
documents.plot:
Pinocchio 3000, also known as P3K, is a 2004 computer-animated science fantasy film directed by Daniel Robichaud and distributed by Christal Films. A Spanish, French and Canadian co-production, it reimagines Carlo Collodi's 1883 novel The Adventures of Pinocchio as a futuristic story in which Pinocchio is a robot rather than a wooden puppet. The voice cast includes Sonja Ball as Pinocchio, Howard Ryshpan as Geppetto, Howie Mandel as the robotic penguin Spencer, Whoopi Goldberg as the fairy Cyberina and Malcolm McDowell as Mayor Scamboli.

In a futuristic city, the elderly inventor Geppetto builds a robot boy, Pinocchio, to be his son. Meanwhile, the city's ruthless mayor, Scamboli, is building a gleaming technological metropolis called Scamboville and wants to eliminate all traces of nature. He dislikes children, except for his own daughter Marlene. When Marlene complains that there is no place for children to have fun, he builds a children's theme park, Scamboland. On the night of its grand opening, Geppetto diverts the city's electricity to bring Pinocchio to life, causing a blackout in the park.

Cyberina, a robotic fairy, promises to make Geppetto's wish come true and turn Pinocchio into a real boy if he learns the difference between right and wrong. Accompanied by Spencer, who serves as his conscience, Pinocchio goes to school and meets Marlene and other children, but he behaves badly after losing a game to her and runs away. Scamboli's robotic henchmen bring him to the mayor, who is inspired by Pinocchio's remark that life would be better if children were more like robots. Scamboli makes Pinocchio an attraction at Scamboland and uses a roller coaster ride in the park to transform the city's children into robots called Scambobots, while also kidnapping Geppetto. Pinocchio must realize his mistakes, rescue his friends and save Geppetto in order to become a real boy.

The film updates the moral lessons of Collodi's tale, about honesty, responsibility and the value of humanity, for a technological age, with Spencer taking the role of the original story's Talking Cricket.

Pinocchio 3000 was released in 2004 and distributed by Christal Films. Aimed at young children, it combines the familiar story with bright futuristic designs and comic robotic sidekicks.

documents.title: The Invention of Lying
documents.tagline: In a world where everyone can only tell the truth... This guy can lie.
documents.overview: Set in a world where the concept of lying doesn't exist, a loser changes his lot when he invents lying and uses it to get ahead.
documents.plot:
The Invention of Lying is a 2009 British fantasy comedy film directed by Richard Curtis, written by Curtis and Simon Beckerman, and starring Ricky Gervais, Jennifer Garner, and Louis C.K.

The main themes of The Invention of Lying revolve around the concept of truth and its impact on human relationships. The story takes place in an alternate universe where lying is not a natural part of human behavior, and people are forced to be truthful at all times.

At the beginning of the film, we meet Andy (Ricky Gervais), a young man who lives in a world where honesty is the only policy. However, when he meets a woman named Kay (Jennifer Garner) from a parallel universe where lying is acceptable, he begins to question the nature of truth and its consequences.
